# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Fixed (TLS-25: `cdo-speed --rounds` above 5 is refused up front)

- **`scripts/cdo-speed --rounds N` with N above 5 crashed after minutes of timing.** There are 5
  round routines, one per round. `--rounds 6` built and started both servers, timed the warm-up
  and 5 rounds (about 5 minutes on CDO), then stopped with `IndexError` and wrote no
  `speed.json` (found in TLS-09 (b)). It is now a usage error (exit 2) naming the limit, given
  before anything is built or started; so is `--rounds 0`. `--max-rounds` was already capped at
  5. Test: `tests/cli/gate_scripts.rs` `speed_gate_refuses_more_rounds_than_routines`.

### Fixed (ENG-12: record operations the engine did not see, engine limits L35, L36 and B10's left item 1)

- **`GetBySystemId` is a record read (L35).** `R.GetBySystemId(Id)`, a bare `GetBySystemId(Id)`
  in a table and `RR.GetBySystemId(Id)` on a RecordRef answered `query touches --direction down:
  no (every candidate decided)` for the record's own table; they are now read operations (d11/d21
  count them as loading the record; an unchecked one in statement position is an implicit error,
  as `Get`). The performance detectors' retrieval lists (d1, d3, d36, d4) are unchanged.
- **A record array element is a record (L36).** `Recs[1].FindFirst()` and `with Recs[1] do
  FindFirst()` made no record operation and answered `no`; an array of records (or of RecordRef)
  now receives through its elements in both the body walk and the resolver, the table taken from
  the element type, so `Recs[1].Modify(true)` also runs the table's triggers.
- **A record operation on a record no variable names** answered a definite `no`:
  `GetRef().Modify(true)` (a function's returned record) for `may-commit`, `GetRef().FindFirst()`
  for `query touches`. A known table's call result is now a record operation of its own (the
  resolver reads the table from the function's return type; the model builds the operation at the
  call site, `{call site}/callresult`, with its triggers and table-event subscribers, as ENG-06
  does for `FieldRef.Validate`); a RecordRef result is an honest open dispatch; an object global
  through `this` (`this.X.FindSet()`) is a record operation on the global. On CDO, all in
  dependency code: 13 `this.X` sites, and 3 RecordRef call results
  (`CreationFactory.GeteDocumentHeader().Modify()`, `GeteDocumentHeader(): RecordRef`), honest
  dynamic dispatches; no known-table call result. Base Application has 36 array-element writes.
  Probe: `docs/superpowers/notes/2026-11-12-eng12-record-ops-probe.md`.
- Review round 1: a non-record parameter, local or return value shadows a record global of its
  name in both engines (a local `X: array[2] of Codeunit W` under a global `X: Record T` had made
  `X[1].Modify()` a record operation and hidden the codeunit's commit); an element of a
  `temporary` array is temporary; `Recs[ 1 ]` and
  `Recs[1]` are one receiver; `query effects` lists `GetBySystemId` as a read. A record
  operation written without parentheses in expression position (`if R.FindFirst then`, about 96
  sites in CDO) is still not seen: task ENG-25.
- Review round 3: a call result's `CalcFields(F)` reads its FlowFields' source tables and its
  `ModifyAll(F, …)` writes field `F` (`explain --field`); cross-app demand follows the triggers and
  table events a call result's record operation (and a FieldRef's `Validate`) raises, so a
  dependency trigger reached only that way is loaded, and `alsem graph` exports them
  (`implicitTrigger`/`tableEvent` edges, OverApprox when the route is conditioned, as an edge's
  route is), so test selection reaches a trigger through them; a call result's retrieval (a
  shadowed `this.G.FindFirst()`) gets the FlowField reads of `this.G`'s `SetAutoCalcFields`, which
  is scoped as the global whatever local shadows it; a variable whose quoted name holds `[`
  (`"Line [Temp]"`) is looked up by its whole name; `Recs[ 1 ].SetAutoCalcFields(F)` is spelled
  as its retrieval's receiver, and an array element's FlowField setup is shared only as its array
  variable is (another routine's local array no longer supplies it).

### Fixed (ENG-10: a database write inside a used try call is refused on premises, engine limits L23 item 6)

- **`throws-error` answered `no` for `Ok := TryInsert()`** whose try function inserts: it counted
  the insert's error as caught by the TryFunction. On premises with `DisableWriteInsideTryFunctions`
  on (Learn: the default there; no such restriction online), BC refuses the write and raises
  "Call to the function 'INSERT' is not allowed inside the call to '…' when it is used as a
  TryFunction.", which no try call catches. Measured on BC 28 on premises (Linux sidecar and
  Windows 28.0.54946.56477, 21 scenarios; probe note
  `docs/superpowers/notes/2026-11-12-eng10-write-in-try-probe.md`): refused are `Insert`,
  `Modify`, `ModifyAll`, `Delete`, `LockTable` and `Commit()`, in the try function, a callee, an
  unchecked `Codeunit.Run` or the call's arguments; not caught by the try call or an outer one;
  caught by a checked `Codeunit.Run` or `asserterror` between; a temporary record's write is
  allowed; every use of the value makes the call a try call, only a call statement does not.
- Each such call (any resolved callee, any `#if` arm declaring `[TryFunction]`) now carries
  `ERROR (database write refused inside a try call)` at its call site (`error-implicit`, resource
  `write-in-try`), raised, never unconditional, where a refused operation or unknown code may run
  inside it, "not raised" otherwise (trap kind `try-write-refused`; JSON verdict
  `escapes-if-write-refused`). prove (and its `--site/--match/--op` slice, which also rules a
  refused operation inside the try that way, by its route: through a try call with no checked run
  or `asserterror` on it; `--op Commit` and a tested `--op Insert` find the refusal too),
  explain and digest. A symbol-only routine (no body)
  is unknown code inside a try call. A root that is itself such a try function states that its
  answer assumes statement calls (`obligations.assumesStatementCallsOnly`, the header's
  assumptions). `alsem impact` keys the refusal as `error|error-implicit|write-in-try` (summary
  schema 13). CDO: 5 of its 30
  `[TryFunction]` procedures may write (the PDF service's token cache is CDO bug #80680, guarded
  by a token warm-up the engine cannot see).

### Changed (TLS-27: the findings sort builds each sort key once)

- **`alsem analyze` sorts its findings about 11 times faster, in the same order.** The sort
  compared detector names with the natural comparator and formatted each location string on
  every comparison. Now each distinct detector name gets a rank once, and each finding's key
  (rank, location text, root cause) is built once (`sort_by_detector_location_cause` in
  `src/engine/l5/registry.rs`). The same helper serves `role_scope_and_sort` and the r4
  projections in `src/engine/l5/finding.rs`. Measured on CDO (2026-11-12, release-fast,
  `analyze --scope all --format json --deterministic`):
  - the sort's span (`crossapp.role_scope`) median of 3: 250.9 → 22.5 ms;
  - one untraced run each: wall 24.13 → 22.88 s, CPU 129.8 → 124.5 s, peak 3,209 → 3,224 MiB
    (single runs, within noise);
  - all 8 outputs byte-identical.

  Note: `docs/superpowers/notes/2026-11-12-findings-sort.md`.

### Changed (TLS-21: impact's up walk runs roots in parallel)

- **One-shot `alsem impact` (and `--part up`) walks the up part over 8 roots at once instead of
  one.** It uses the same worker count and thread pool as TLS-22's literal pass
  (`AL_SEM_REACH_WORKERS` for measurement). The output is byte-identical at any worker count, and
  equal to master's on a fixture (`tests/fixtures/up-parallel`). The resident engine (`alsem mcp`,
  `engine-host`) still walks one root at a time. A traced CDO `impact --diff` spent 93 % of its
  46 s up part in the per-root walks and 0.2 % in the union walk. Measured on CDO (2026-11-12,
  release-fast, 22 cores, 699 roots):
  - the up part at 8 workers against 1: `impact --diff` 40.0 → 8.4 s, `--base` 44.2 → 7.4 s,
    `--part up` 36.3 → 7.6 s;
  - peak memory against master at 8: +1.4 % (`impact --diff`) and +1.5 % (`--part up`); the walk
    itself adds 39-132 MB;
  - the outputs equal master's, the whole `impact --diff` and `--part up` at every count;
  - the resident engine's `cdo-speed` against master passes: round total ×0.990, memory ×0.988.

  At 16 workers the command is slower, so the count stays 8. Note:
  `docs/superpowers/notes/2026-11-12-parallel-up-walk.md`.
- **`impact-up`'s `cost.scratchBytes` now sums every walk scratch** (one per walk in flight). It
  grows with the worker count and can differ between runs, like `walkMs`. The resident-vs-CLI
  comparison test now blanks it too. `cost.walksUs` is still the sum of each walk's own time, so
  with several workers it is larger than the wall time. Spec:
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-12-parallel-up-walk.md`.
- **Measurement only: `AL_SEM_UP_WALK_WINDOW=1` with `ALSEM_TRACE=1`** makes a one-shot run's up
  walk report its own memory window. The trace counters are `impact.up.rss_start_mb` and
  `impact.up.peak_mb` (Linux). It resets the process's peak-memory mark, so that run's process
  peak is not the command's. The resident engine never does this, because its memory budget reads
  the same mark.

### Changed (TLS-09: the gate's optimized build is `release-fast`)

- **`scripts/ci-steps build` and `perf-bounds` build with `--profile release-fast` instead of
  `--release`** (local `ci-steps all` and GitHub CI's `release` job). Measured on server1
  (master `d887bb47`, after an edit): the `--release` build took 636 s, 62 % of it the library's
  single codegen unit and 38 % the `alsem` fat-LTO link, almost all on one thread; `release-fast`
  took 200 s, and the `perf_bounds` build 24 s against 78 s. In ENG-22's landing gate the
  release build (9 min 41 s) was the critical path by about 6.5 minutes. Every `perf_bounds` row
  keeps at least 2x headroom on `release-fast` (tightest: the `compute_all` scaling ratio, 2.2x
  -> 2.1x). No profile changed; the shipped `release-ship` is still built on every code push to
  master by `build-and-deploy.yml` (Windows, Linux, macOS), so a fat-LTO-only failure shows there,
  after the merge and before any tag. That workflow now also runs on a `rust-toolchain.toml`
  change. Note: `docs/superpowers/notes/2026-11-12-gate-release-build.md`.
- **The shipped profile keeps `codegen-units = 1` (measured, not changed).** With 16 or 4 units
  the `release-ship` build took 297 / 299 s against 511 s, but an A/A control (the same binary
  against itself in `scripts/cdo-speed`) varied about ±10 % per round on this host. That is too
  wide to show the binary is not slower, which the owner's rule for the shipped profile requires.
  The numbers and a better method for next time (instruction counts) are in the note's section 5.

### Changed (TLS-22: the literal pass runs roots in parallel)

- **One-shot `impact`, `digest` and `prove` run the literal pass (`prove.reach_effects`) over 8
  roots at once instead of one.** Measured on CDO (release-fast, 22 cores, 2026-11-12): the
  699-root `impact --diff` pass falls 87.1 -> 29.4 s and its wall 218 -> 162 s; `impact --base`
  147.4 -> 53.0 s and 321 -> 253 s. Peak memory +5 %. Output is byte-identical at any worker count.
  16 workers was slower than 8 and used 15 % more memory, so the count is fixed at 8 (capped by the
  cores; a one-core host runs serially), not taken from the machine. A pass called from inside a
  rayon worker runs serially there.
- **The context server keeps the pass serial** (owner decision 2026-11-12,
  q-20261112T032637-1269d8fc). With 8 workers a resident 699-root impact fell 206 -> 140 s, but two
  in a row (the engine runs heavy asks one at a time) peaked at 8,030-8,089 MiB, 2 % under its 8 GiB
  budget, against 7,929 MiB (3 %) serially. A first design that lowered the count only while two
  passes ran was built, tested and measured, then removed: two passes never run at once in one
  engine child, so it could not fire.
- How: the RecordRef flow's per-evaluation state is a local of each evaluation; its answers, the
  suffix trees (one shared cache, `Arc` trees, searches outside the lock, evicted trees freed
  outside it) and the other memos sit behind short locks that recover from a panicked holder; one
  pool of exactly `n` big-stack threads per worker count. The setting is a parameter on every route
  (`ReachWorkers`); only the binary reads `AL_SEM_REACH_WORKERS` (measurement). `ALSEM_TRACE` counts
  the suffix cache's searches, duplicates and evictions, and passes run serially inside rayon.
- Tests: equality at 1/2/8 workers over the r0 corpus and the dependency fixtures (a suffix tree
  served again asserted); the worker count observed (exactly `n` roots in flight), on every
  resident route; the resident engine serial in both modes; two passes sharing one pool; serial
  inside a rayon worker; the core cap; races forced through test hooks on the evaluator's answers
  (the same key, no timeout) and the suffix cache (a key missing its bindings, a double insert,
  eviction under four workers). Each with a discrimination proof. Spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-parallel-literal-reach.md`
  section 8; note `docs/superpowers/notes/2026-11-12-parallel-literal-pass.md`.

### Added

- **`scripts/seed-target <worktree>`** (TLS-08): makes a new worktree's `target/` a
  copy-on-write copy of the main checkout's, so its first build reuses every compiled
  dependency. Measured 2026-11-11 (master `c498fd98`, 3 rounds): the first
  `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-run` took 94.3 s seeded (+1.6 s copy) against
  146.3 s cold, 3 units compiled against 257. Where a reflink copy fails it removes the
  partial copy and the build runs cold. Note: `docs/superpowers/notes/2026-11-11-warm-deps.md`.

### Fixed (ENG-22: a checked `Codeunit.Run` with a write pending raises an error, engine limits L28)

- **The run's own error.** BC (measured on the BC 28.4 Linux sidecar, confirmed on Windows BC
  28.0.54946.56477 by the owner) refuses a checked `Codeunit.Run` while a write is pending: the run
  itself raises "An error occurred and the transaction is stopped.", the checked form does not
  catch it, and nothing of the caller's is committed. `R.ModifyAll(V, 1); if
  Codeunit.Run(Codeunit::"C") then;` answered `throws-error: no`; each checked run now carries
  that error at its call site, `ERROR (checked Codeunit.Run with a write pending)`, raised (never
  `unconditional`) where a write may be pending at the run on some route from the root, and "not
  raised" where none may, with the callers' entry assumption stated. prove, its `--site/--match`
  slice, explain and digest; impact keys it `error|error-implicit|checked-run`
  (`SUMMARY_SCHEMA` 11 → 12).
- **The "is a write pending at this checked run" search** (it also decides when a checked run
  catches a callee's error) missed two shapes: a run in a `while`/`repeat` condition after an
  earlier pass of a body that writes, and a subscriber entered after another subscriber of the
  same event that writes. Both now count as a write that may be pending. Review round 1 found
  four more: a call in a loop after its own earlier pass wrote; a table-event subscriber or
  trigger (its siblings, and the write operation that fires it); and `LockTable`, which opens a
  write transaction (measured on the BC 28.4 sidecar).
- **`if IsInWriteTransaction() then Commit();` ends the write** (that shape only: the platform's
  call as the whole condition, not negated, no `else`, one `Commit()`), in prove's trap search and
  in the transaction spans. Measured on the BC 28.4 sidecar: `IsInWriteTransaction()` was true
  exactly when a checked run failed, in seven transaction states; confirmed on Windows BC
  28.0.54946.56477 by the owner.
  Before, a branch `Commit()` ended nothing, and d50's one CDO finding (CDOLegacyeDocDispatcher,
  which commits that way before its run) was a false positive.
- **A helper's writes inside its own checked run are not pending after it** (the transaction
  spans' pending walk, which d50 and the explicit-commit spans read). The walk counted a called
  routine's whole write cone, also the writes behind a checked run inside it, which BC commits or
  rolls back with the run. On CDO that made both of d50's findings on the send-on-posting path
  (`CDOSubscribers`: `LogAutoSendFailure`, `RunDocHandleIsolated`) false positives: d50 on CDO
  went from 3 old-meaning findings on master to none (6 checked runs considered, all with no
  write pending), at both scopes. A workspace callee that reaches a checked run is now walked
  with those runs left out, and the result is kept inside its cone (it can only remove a write);
  a run inside dependency code still counts its writes. Whatever a walked routine's cone holds
  that the walk cannot explain (an edge the forward sites lack, a callee with no summary) still
  counts (review round 4), and a routine id with two rows, or one whose cone follows an edge its
  forward sites lack, is not walked (its whole cone counts).

### Changed (ENG-22: d50 reports the error, not an implicit commit)

- **d50 changed meaning** (owner decision q-20261112T025612-62a3ca62, id kept). It reported "a
  checked Codeunit.Run performs an implicit commit … within a posting span", which BC does not do.
  It now reports a checked run at which a physical write may be pending (BC raises an error at the
  run), severity medium, rule `CheckedRunWithPendingWrite` (was `CheckedRunImplicitCommit`). The
  posting-name and three-table "transaction manager" tests and the medium tier for a nearby
  explicit `Commit()` are gone with the old claim. It also sees the variable form
  `Ok := C.Run()`. Finding ids are `d50/pending-write/<site>`, so
  the fingerprints are new: **a suppression or baseline of the old d50 finding does not carry
  over**; review the new findings before suppressing them again. The detector name
  (`d50-checked-run-implicit-commit`) is unchanged so existing `--detector` lists keep working.

### Fixed (ENG-09: a checked `Codeunit.Run` commits, engine limits L16 item 2)

- **`if Codeunit.Run(X) then` no longer answers `may-commit no` when X has no `Commit()`.** It did
  (and `unknown` for a run-time id), re-probed on master `c498fd98`. Measured on the BC 28.4 Linux
  sidecar: after such a run a second checked run succeeds, which BC refuses while a write is
  pending, so the run committed its insert; the same under the caller's `[CommitBehavior(Ignore)]`
  and `(Error)` (no error), and for `Ok := W.Run()` on a codeunit variable. Each checked run (keyword
  form, run-time id included, or a codeunit variable's `.Run()` that starts the codeunit, with or
  without an `OnRun`) now carries a commit at its call site (`PCallSite::checked_run`, set by
  `program_calls`), with the resource id `checked-run` (shown as `detail.resourceId`), so it never
  shares a cone entry with a `Commit()`. No `[CommitBehavior]` rule applies to it (Learn: "the
  implicit commit by `Codeunit.Run` isn't affected by `CommitBehavior`"), it is never
  `unconditional on success` (a failed run commits nothing and the caller carries on), in the
  ordering engine it is `COMMIT_REACHABLE` only (it ends no write of the caller), and it does not
  feed d34/d35's "may commit" flag (their findings do not change).
- Found on the way: `prove throws-error --match` under `[CommitBehavior(Error)]` would have listed
  the run's commit as an error site; the slice applies the same rule as the unfiltered answer.
  Review (astra, Fable): with a witness-shape identity, a root reaching both a `Commit()` and a
  checked run kept one inherited commit for both, so `[CommitBehavior(Ignore)]` over a `Commit()`
  and a deeper run answered `may-commit no`; the resource id fixes it. Round 2 (Fable): beyond a
  dependency crossing the two kinds were still one group row (its key had no resource), and a
  run's group ended its witness on a `Commit()`; now they are two rows (the run's says
  `resourceId: checked-run`), each ending on its own site. `alsem impact` keys a new checked run's
  commit as `commit|checked-run`, the twin of its cone row, so it is listed once.
- Tests: `tests/cli/cli_eng09_checked_run_commit.rs` (6 tests, one cross-app) and
  `impact::delta::tests::a_new_checked_runs_commit_is_one_change`; discrimination proofs: no commit
  fact, no `conditional` floor, the digest's or the slice's `[CommitBehavior]` split applied to the
  run's commit, no variable-form mark, one cone key for both kinds of commit, the run's commit in
  d35's "may commit" flag, one crossing group for both kinds, the run group's witness looked up as
  a `Commit()`'s, and no impact twin each fail them; leaving the ordering exclusion out moves the
  d49 run-boundary goldens. `cli_prove_traps`: a checked run's digest now has a live commit row
  beside its caught error.
- Goldens: `l2_features.snapshot` (the new internal field only, proven by stripping it against the
  old snapshot); `r3a3` `ws-d50-pos` and `ws-txn-d49-neg-run-boundary` gain the run's commit (and
  `ws-d50-pos` its inherited copy), with the manifest matrix (commit 90 -> 93). The policy facts
  oracle is re-recorded: 9 of 454 cases moved, each by its checked runs' commits, no count down.
- `alsem impact`'s summary schema goes 10 -> 11.
- L28 is now measured too: a write followed by a checked run fails at the run.
- Left: a run that always fails still answers `may-commit yes` (an over-statement); `Ok := …; if not
  Ok then Error(…)` answers `commits-on-success-path unknown` (an under-statement); see engine
  limits L16 item 2.

### Fixed (ENG-08: an XmlPort import can raise an error, engine limits L20)

- **A statement that starts an XmlPort import no longer answers `throws-error: no`.** A
  statement `Xmlport.Import(X, IS)`, an `Xmlport.Run` that imports and a variable's `X.Import()`
  answered `no` (re-probed on master `f12bf250`). Measured on the BC 28.4 Linux sidecar: an
  import fails on a key that exists or that the file holds twice (unless `AutoUpdate` or
  `AutoReplace` is true), and on a value that does not evaluate or malformed XML whatever the
  properties; `Ok := Xmlport.Import(…)` returns `false` instead. So a call the resolver decided
  starts an import (`dataset::import_export`; an `Import`, or a `Run` whose `Direction` allows
  one) is marked `PCallSite::start_may_fail` in `program_calls`, and in statement position it is
  an implicit error (`ERROR_IMPLICIT`, as a statement `Evaluate`). A used result catches it, a
  run that only exports raises none, and an import with `AutoSave = false` raises it too.
- **A literal direction no longer overrides `Direction`.** Measured: `Xmlport.Run(X, false,
  false)` on a `Direction = Import` XmlPort fails ("The XMLPort 'X' is designed for import
  only."), and the export case alike, before any trigger runs. The dataset model let the literal
  win, so that run answered `throws-error: no` and claimed a read, and the mirror case claimed
  the import's writes. Now an explicit import or export runs only when `Direction` allows it
  (`dataset::import_export`), and one it refuses runs nothing and is a start that may fail
  (`dataset::direction_refused`).
- Tests: `tests/cli/cli_eng08_xmlport_import_error.rs` (5 tests, keyword and variable forms, a
  run-time id, the default cross-app mode; discrimination proofs: dropping the rule brings the
  old `no` back, dropping its statement-position condition makes `Ok :=` and `if` raise,
  dropping the import check makes an export-only run raise, dropping `direction_refused` makes a
  refused run answer `no`, and letting an explicit import ignore `Direction` makes a refused run
  write).
- `alsem impact`'s summary schema goes 9 -> 10, so a base cached before this change is rebuilt
  (it also covers ENG-06's and ENG-07's summary changes, which did not bump it).
- Left: an export was not measured failing, so a run that only exports raises no error fact; a
  checked import (`Ok := Xmlport.Import(…)`) is not a trap yet, so an error inside the XmlPort
  still reaches the caller (a false `yes`, older than this change).
- The request-page trigger order (ENG-07) is now confirmed on Windows BC 28.0.54946.56477 for
  reports (the owner, q-20261111T144908-3d4d3d0b); the XmlPort request page stays sidecar only.

## [3.0.0] - 2026-11-11

### Highlights

- **Breaking output for programs that read al-sem's JSON (#375).** query 5.0.0 and digest 5.0.0
  rename `entryPoint(s)` to `dependencyCall(s)`, refer to tables and files by id (`t:<n>`,
  `f:<n>`) and are compact by default; `--schema 4` (MCP `schema: 4`) still writes the 4.0.0
  document for one release. See "Schema majors (consumer notice)" and the consumer notices
  under the round-2 and round-3 sections, and "Outside consumers (wave 2)" for every field wave 2
  changed (split subscribers' routine and site ids, impact `summarySchema` 9, `PACK_SCHEMA` 17).
- **The context server** (`alsem mcp`): a resident engine that answers explain, prove, digest and
  query from a kept model and refreshes it per change; the LSP's `al-call-hierarchy/*` methods use
  it too.
- **Agent tasks:** `alsem impact` (on the current revision and against a `--base`), `alsem tests`
  (test selection), field impact, the debugging slice, callers through dependency code.
- **Engine precision** (engine limits waves 0-2): error traps and `[CommitBehavior]`, the record
  operations of report, query and XmlPort datasets, one routine per `#if` arm or subscriber
  declaration, unreadable event subscribers reported as gaps, literal values through interfaces.
- **Grammar:** tree-sitter-al v5.2.0 (`f8c6d8b6`).
- **Speed:** the unresolved cones build their indexes once per read (`digest.unresolved_cones`
  30-42 s to 4 s on CDO); the CDO gate skips its speed check when a diff touches no product code
  and builds the speed check's base right after each landing.

### Changed (GRM-02: tree-sitter-al 5.2.0, main `f8c6d8b6`)

- **Grammar 5.1.0 (`abc77b25`) -> 5.2.0 (`f8c6d8b6`).** The parser has 46.8% fewer states and
  `parser.c` is half the size (70.3 -> 34.7 MB). `gen-syntax`: no new kind (still 513 named
  kinds, 79 fields), only the node-types hash moves. `node-types.json` gains one child type,
  `preproc_pragma_only`, under `preproc_conditional_var_block`, the conditional and split
  procedure and trigger preambles, and itself (an empty `#if` group right after a routine
  header, grammar item 102). `kind_policy` already classes it structural and the lowerer
  descends through it, so a var section after such a group still gives the routine its locals
  (new test `an_empty_group_after_a_routine_header_keeps_the_var_section`; on 5.1.0 the first
  shape is `Recovered` and the test fails). `CACHE_VERSION_GRAMMAR` is
  `tree-sitter-al-v5.2.0-f8c6d8b6-native` (and the two fixture-cache stamps, the kept one's
  content hash recomputed).
- Measured (old = master `f12bf250` on 5.1.0, new = this branch on 5.2.0):
  - Trees: all 12,351 `.al` files (CDO's 10,881 dependency sources, the whole CDO baseline and
    this repo's fixtures) give byte-identical S-expressions, parse status, issue count and
    lowered routines. The grammar's own 61 item-102 inputs: 14 go `Recovered` -> `Clean`, 4 of
    them gain a local the error had swallowed, none regress.
  - Tests: the whole suite passes on 5.2.0 with no golden regenerated (5,812 tests).
  - CDO (`/work/src/cdo-baseline/Cloud`, `cdo` profile): `aldump --program-call-graph-stats`
    is byte-identical (46,426 edges, 0 unknown, the same 2 recovered files).
  - Build: an `al-syntax` rebuild (release, its build script compiles `parser.c`) took
    9.9-12.4 s on 5.1.0 and 8.6-9.9 s on 5.2.0 (3 runs each, machine shared).

### Changed (TLS-19 and TLS-20: the CDO gate's impact lane and speed skip)

- **`scripts/cdo-gate` runs the impact ratchets last again, not beside the other phases** (TLS-23,
  2026-11-11). They stay their own phase, `output_cdo_impact`, now run after every other phase with
  both tests at once. Three gates with the background lane (TLS-19, below) on the shared kraken host:
  test phases 874 s and 1,232 s with both tests at once, the second keeping only 2,836 MiB of the
  owner's 4 GiB headroom (peak 46,315 of 49,152 MiB, no OOM); then 1,641 s with one test at a time
  (8,087 MiB headroom), slower than the 1,170 s the phases took one after another. The timeline
  showed why: `lib_cdo`'s test process alone reaches 25-29 GB and `output_cdo` about 24 GB, so only
  the base test (2 calls, ~5.7 GB) fits beside them, and a lane staged to fit would have saved
  little. The memory sampler stays and now also writes `memory.timeline` (every 2 s: the
  container's unreclaimable MiB, the RSS sum of the gate's own process tree, its three largest
  processes) and `phases.times`; the summary names the gate's own share at the container's peak,
  since the container counts every agent's processes.

- **`scripts/cdo-gate` runs the two impact ratchets as their own lane, also in serial mode**
  (TLS-19, owner approval 2026-11-11). `output_cdo::cdo_impact_ratchets` and
  `cdo_impact_base_ratchets` (one-shot `alsem impact` processes, 4-7 min each on about 3 cores) held
  `output_cdo` open 470-700 s after its other tests. They now run as the phase `output_cdo_impact`,
  started in the background before the test lanes; `output_cdo` runs the rest. Together the two
  phases run every `output_cdo::` test, and each is summarized and counted. The gate now samples the
  container's unreclaimable memory (`memory.stat`: anon + shmem + kernel − slab_reclaimable) while
  its lanes run and prints the peak against `memory.max` with the headroom (the owner's rule: keep
  at least 4 GiB, or go back to serial and say why), plus the `max`/`oom`/`oom_kill` counts of
  `memory.events` the run added. The first version sampled `memory.current`, which counts page
  cache the kernel reclaims: on the first gate (2026-11-11) it read 49151 of 49152 MiB with no OOM.
  Measured on two gates (2026-11-11): the test phases took 874 s and 1,232 s (busy host), against
  1,170-1,174 s (quiet) and 1,594 s (busy) one after another; peak unreclaimable memory 42,822 of
  49,152 MiB (6,329 MiB headroom), no OOM. Details:
  `docs/superpowers/notes/2026-11-11-cdo-gate-time.md`, "TLS-19".
- **`scripts/cdo-gate` skips its speed phase when the diff touches no product code** (TLS-20, owner
  approval 2026-11-11). Against the base the speed check itself would use (the merge base with
  master, or on a clean master HEAD's first parent), every changed path, untracked ones included,
  must be on an allow-list of paths never compiled into `alsem`: `tests/`, `docs/`, `scripts/` (not
  `scripts/cdo-speed`), `.config/nextest.toml`, `CHANGELOG.md`. Any other path, an empty diff or an
  unreadable one keeps the phase. A skipped run says so: `speed: skipped, diff touches no product
  code`, and `PASS (behaviour only: speed skipped, ...)`, never a plain PASS (and `--summary` of that
  run too). `cdo-gate --product-paths` prints the rule's verdict for paths on stdin. Saves the
  7.5-19 min of `speed_build` and `speed` on test-, script- and docs-only branches.

### Changed (TLS-18: the speed check's base is built after a landing, not in the next gate)

- **`scripts/merge-and-push` builds the new master's speed-check binary in the background right
  after it pushes**, so the next branch's `cdo-gate` finds its base (the merge base: this master)
  in `~/.cache/al-sem/cdo-speed/bin/<sha>/` instead of building it inside the gate (304-595 s in
  TLS-16's gates). It runs `scripts/cdo-speed --warm <sha>`, a new mode that only calls the gate's
  own builder (`cached_binary`: the same cache key, lock, `release-fast` profile, `git archive` and
  grammar lookup) and exits, so no comparison changes; a gate that starts while it builds waits on
  the cache lock and then finds the binary. Linux only, at `nice 10`, detached; its log path is
  printed. A failed warm build only means the next gate builds the base itself, as before. Test:
  `gate_scripts::speed_warm_reads_the_gates_own_cache_entry` (a warm on a cached entry builds
  nothing; a warm keyed by any other commit tries to build and fails, its discrimination proof).
  To be measured: `speed_build` in the next two gates after a landing.

### Changed (TLS-17: the unresolved cones build their indexes once per read)

- **A multi-root digest, prove or impact no longer rebuilds the snapshot's indexes for every
  root's unresolved cone.** `unresolved_cone` built four indexes over the whole snapshot (identities,
  the call-site index, the typed edges with sorted buckets, the ledger) before each root's search:
  699 times for a 699-root impact. They are now built once per read (`ConeIndexes`, in a `OnceLock`
  on `FinishCx`) and looked up by every root's search. Output is unchanged byte for byte (every
  golden; the CDO runs below). Measured on CDO (release-fast, TLS-16's note): the
  `digest.unresolved_cones` span 30.4 -> 3.6 s on `impact --diff` and 41.8 -> 4.0 s on
  `impact --base`; peak RSS unchanged within noise. Tests: the old function kept verbatim as a
  test-only oracle, compared through `FinishCx::finish` on every r0 dir and the dependency
  fixtures, a hand-built visit-cap case for the bucket order, and a one-build-per-read counter, each
  with a discrimination proof. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-parallel-literal-reach.md`,
  which also records why a parallel literal reach is not built yet (ENG-18, TLS-22).

### Fixed (ENG-07: a report run follows its request page's triggers, engine limits L20)

- **A write in a report's request-page trigger no longer answers `no` through a run.**
  `run_triggers` listed only a report's `OnInitReport`/`OnPreReport`/`OnPostReport` and its data
  items' triggers, so `prove writes-table` answered a definite `no` for a write in the request
  page's `OnOpenPage` through `Report.Run`, `RunModal`, `Execute` and a report variable's run
  (re-probed on master `a8a6c70a`). A run of a report, or of the report a report extension
  extends, and of an XmlPort, now follows its request page's `OnInit` (`unconditional on
  success`) and its `OnOpenPage`, `OnQueryClosePage`, `OnClosePage` and record triggers
  (`conditional`). The list also feeds the sited graph (`alsem graph`, `impact`) and explain's
  `reachedFrom`: `impact` on a request-page trigger now counts the runs as its code callers, where
  it said "direct code callers: none found" and reached it by UI navigation only. Which trigger
  runs in which run was **measured on the BC 28.4 Linux sidecar, and for reports confirmed on
  Windows BC 28.0.54946.56477** (the XmlPort request page: sidecar only):
  `OnInit` ran in every run; `OnOpenPage`/`OnClosePage` not with `UseRequestPage` false;
  `OnQueryClosePage` not under `Execute` (the order is in `docs/engine-limits.md`, "L20 in
  detail").
- **A run's triggers are triggers.** The resolver matched a run's triggers by name alone, so a
  procedure named like one (a report procedure `OnOpenPage`) was followed as if the run ran it.
  It now takes routines declared as triggers only, for a page, report, XmlPort and query run.
- Left (engine limits, "L20 in detail"): `Report.RunRequestPage` is still not a run (a wrong
  answer left); which request-page triggers one call runs is not read from the call (`RunModal(X,
  false)` still reaches `OnOpenPage`, safe).
- No fixture golden moved: no fixture runs a report that has a request page.
- CDO (`/work/src/cdo-baseline/Cloud`, master `faddbbd4` against the branch, `cdo` profile):
  `aldump --program-call-graph-stats` is byte-identical, and so are `alsem graph`'s 58,609 edges
  and 26,098 nodes: those count call sites and objects, and every run site already resolved. The
  graph header's `dependencyBodies` histogram moves: 3 call sites in the loaded Base App code go
  from `honestEmpty` to `resolvedSource` (report runs that read "runs no AL code" now reach
  their request-page triggers). Two CDO pins moved (the landing gate found them; each was
  attributed by switching off only the request-page names, which reproduces the old value):
  - The compiler audit's program-only `ObjectRun` pairs, 409 -> 415: six `Report.RunModal`s now
    reach a request page's `OnOpenPage` (two `OnAction`s running "CDO Update Customer Setup",
    four warehouse action pages running Base App report 7323). altool has no run edges at all
    (`docs/al-compiler-callgraph-holes.md`, A1).
  - The L4 whole-program digest, `a0ce2366…` -> `f9c5d1e1…`: the two `OnAction`s each gain the
    two `opaque-callee` uncertainties of that request page's `OnOpenPage` cone; no `db_effects`
    change (`tests/l4-summary-baseline/README.md`, re-freeze log).
- Tests: `tests/cli/cli_eng07_request_page.rs` (6 tests; discrimination proofs: dropping the
  report's or the XmlPort's request-page names brings the old `no` back, dropping their
  conditionality or making `OnInit` conditional fails the conditionality pins, dropping the trigger
  filter follows the procedure, and dropping `OnOpenPage` from the sited graph's rule fails the
  `impact` pin).
- Left: a report procedure with a request-page trigger's name and parameters still hides the
  trigger (one routine id; alc accepts the pair), a wrong `no`.

### Fixed (ENG-18: a literal-reach answer no longer depends on what else the read asked)

- **The RecordRef flow evaluates each question from fresh state.** `RecRefFlow` (the
  table-under-inputs evaluation behind literal reach, G35) kept ONE memo, one set of final
  values and one budget of 200,000 evaluations for a whole read, and a value its depth cutoff
  (48 calls) turned into "anything" was folded into its callers' memo and marked final. So a
  root's answer could depend on which roots the same read asked first: `prove` on one root and
  `impact` or a digest over many could answer the same root differently. Each top-level
  evaluation now starts from a fresh state (its own budget, depth, memo and final marks) that is
  dropped afterwards, and its answer is kept by its key (routine, input tables, globals), so an
  answer depends on its key alone. Found by TLS-17's spec review.
- Measured on CDO before the fix (2 of 15 chunks of the workspace's files, one digest read
  each, 362k top-level evaluations): no depth cutoff, no budget cutoff, no unsettled
  evaluation, under 1,000 of the budget used per read; on those two chunks the fixed and the
  old binary give byte-identical digests. Time on the same chunks, alternating which runs
  first: +1.8% and +2% (one earlier pair, fixed second, read +37%; it did not reproduce). Peak
  RSS equal (7.0 and 8.4 GB). Landing gate speed phase: prove x0.99, model build x1.12.
- **The history dependence does fire on CDO, without any cutoff.** In one `prove` of
  `CDO E-Mail Handler::RunReportID` (`writes-table:CDO E-Mail Log`), a probe build of the old
  code that also computed every top-level evaluation's key from fresh state found 1,410 of
  ~4,400 evaluations (11 routines) whose answer differed: every one of the 2,002 differing
  variables was "anything" in the shared state and a precise table set fresh (none the other
  way). The old answer is reproduced asked alone, so it is the read's own earlier evaluations,
  not a batch of questions. With the fix that `prove`'s answer is unchanged and one witness row
  takes another route (`RunReportID.prove-writes-table.human.txt`: 25 → 30 guards, through
  Base App's `Workflow Management::ExecuteResponses`).
- Limits (panel review: gpt-6-astra, Fable): the budget is per top-level key, so the worst
  case per read is no longer bounded by one 200,000 (a shape where many keys share a deep
  sensitive subtree recomputes it per key; CDO shows no such shape); inside one evaluation a key
  reached first past the cutoff and later shallower still answers by call-edge order (stable,
  and sound: it over-approximates); the test pins depth contamination in both orders, not budget
  exhaustion. The old shared `done` marks and the `touched` sets are gone (dead with fresh
  state).

### Fixed (ENG-06: `FieldRef.Validate` and record operations on a table not known, engine limits B9, B10)

- **B9: `FieldRef.Validate` validates its field.** `FR := RR.Field(2); FR.Validate(1);` now
  runs the field's `OnValidate` and reaches the subscribers of that field's
  `OnBefore/OnAfterValidateEvent`, as `Rec.Validate(Field, …)` does. Before, it was a plain
  built-in call and `prove … may-commit` answered a definite `no` for a subscriber that commits.
  The FieldRef is followed to `RecRef.Field(<number>)`, `Field('<name>')` or
  `Field(B.FieldNo(F))` (field `F`'s number in `B`'s table, which need not be the RecordRef's),
  written in place or bound to a local FieldRef only that way, and the RecordRef to its one
  literal table (`Open(Database::X)`, `GetTable` of a known record). The call site gets a
  `Validate` record operation of that table and field (`…/fieldref`, the FieldRef operation id
  B5 introduced, so it takes its call site's context and order). A field number two `#if`
  builds declare under two names is either field: the lookup by number declines it.
- **An undecided FieldRef, and B10: a trigger-capable record operation on a table not known,
  is `unknown` when code may run there.** A FieldRef whose table or field is not provable here (a
  parameter, a global, passed to a call, `FieldIndex`, a computed number, bindings that name
  different fields), and `Insert`/`Modify`/`Delete`/`Rename`/`Validate`/… on a record whose
  table does not resolve, may run code the engine did not follow. They now carry an open edge
  (`UnknownReason::RecordTableUnresolved`) and the call-site-local uncertainty and coverage
  reason `record-table-unresolved`: `prove` answers `unknown` and its `coverage-incomplete`
  blocker says why (it carries no site anchor), `query effects` counts it in its scope, coverage
  lists it (the operation's id, or a FieldRef's call site), and finding confidence is capped by
  `dynamic-dispatch`. Before, all were `no (every candidate decided)`, for the routine
  and every caller. When code may run there (`SiteFacts::record_table_unresolved`):
  - a record of a named table the program does not hold (`Record "G/L Entry"` without its app),
    or a local RecordRef (and a FieldRef on it) whose provable bindings name no one loaded table
    (`RR.Open(Database::X)` with `X` not loaded): whenever the operation fires that table's
    trigger (`Validate` always, `Insert`/`Modify`/`Delete`/`Rename` with RunTrigger), since its
    triggers are code the engine cannot see;
  - a RecordRef that may hold any table (`RR.Modify(true)` with `RR` a parameter) and an
    undecided FieldRef: only when a loaded table has a trigger of that operation's family
    (`On<Op>`, or a table extension's `OnBefore<Op>`/`OnAfter<Op>`), or a readable subscriber to
    its table events, or when a loaded table's code is not loaded (a symbol-only dependency's:
    it may have any trigger or subscriber). With none, nothing loaded can run there, and the
    answer stays `no` within the loaded apps, and says so: its assumptions read "… the triggers
    of a record operation on a table not known, of the loaded tables only" (`RR.Insert(true)`
    with no insert trigger anywhere; `RR.Modify()` with no modify-event subscriber). Owner
    answer q-20261111T044238-cead8f76.
  On the corpus this adds eight gaps, all `Record Customer`/`"G/L Entry"`/a dependency's
  undeclared table in fixtures that do not load it. On CDO (measured 2026-11-11, `aldump`
  release-fast): the call-graph stats are byte-identical (46,426 edges, 0 unknown); 12
  operations gain the gap, all RecordRef `Modify()`/`Modify(false)`/`Insert(false)` in CDO's
  own code (the table events of whatever table they hold; loaded code subscribes and symbol-only
  tables are loaded), five of them `CDOHandledFieldsManagement`'s `FilterRecord.Modify()`; in
  the default cross-app mode 1,628 of 5,479 workspace routines carry the reason through their
  cones, of which 60 (1.1%) go from complete to partial because of it alone. Narrowing such an
  operation by a `FieldExist` guard (G36) is ENG-17.
- `FieldNode` (the program graph's table field) carries the field's number (source `field(<no>;
  …)`, the symbols' `Id`), with a new index lookup by number, recorded for the incremental
  session like the lookup by name. `PACK_SCHEMA` is 18: dependency packs built before are
  rebuilt once.

### Fixed (#363: an absolute path to a workspace file names that file)

Spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-issue-363-absolute-paths.md` (panel-approved).

- **An absolute path below the workspace now names that file**, in every root mode (the git
  top, `--diff-root`, or none): `--file` and `--changed <abs>.al` (digest), the `---`/`+++`
  headers of a diff (digest, `explain --diff`, `tests --diff`, `impact --diff`), the
  malformed-record veto and `Only in` lines. Before, every such path was unmatched
  (`file-unmatched`, `diff-file-unmatched`). The workspace may be written as given or as its
  real path (a symlinked workspace): both are its **anchors**, decided once with the diff root
  and carried to batch workers and the engine child beside it (`pathAnchors` on the wire; the
  protocol stays version 1 and an older peer simply reads no anchors). A path below an anchor
  has exactly one reading, so it is never ambiguous. Folders compare exactly, case included;
  only a Windows disk letter compares in any case. An absolute `Only in` naming the workspace
  or a folder above it follows #353's folder rule (`diff-file-unmatched`) instead of
  `diff-file-not-al`.
- **`impact --base` reads absolute headers on the base side too**: the base run on the
  workspace copy gets the live workspace's anchors (hidden `--path-anchor`). The base cache key
  for a diff now also holds the workspace's path below the root (`rel`), which changes what the
  same text maps to (a pre-existing gap: `--diff-root` and the git top could share an entry),
  and, for a diff holding an absolute path, the anchors. Older entries miss once.
- **impact's malformed-record veto now goes by file, not spelling**, as digest's does (#76):
  a malformed `./src/x.al` record now also vetoes a healthy `src/x.al` record (before, the
  healthy one was accounted), and under the git top a malformed path that reads two ways
  vetoes both files. impact keeps its `old_path` veto, now also by file.
- Limits: an absolute path with `..`, through a symlink that is neither the workspace's
  spelling nor its real path, or with a folder above the workspace in another case; `\\?\`
  and `\\?\UNC\` inputs; a Unix path starting with `//` (read as a network share); the MSYS
  `/c/…` and WSL `/mnt/c/…` spellings of a Windows workspace; `impact --file` and `tests --file` stay workspace-relative (#376);
  `impact --base` still cannot map a record whose original old path lies outside the workspace,
  and drops it silently (#377); the in-process `run_digest_pipeline*` APIs (tests only) have
  no anchors.

### Fixed (#362: `digest --changed path.al` is a file input wherever you run it)

- **A `--changed` value with a `.al` entry is now always read like `--file`.** Before,
  `--changed` first asked whether the value existed as a path relative to the current
  folder, and if it did, parsed the AL source as diff text: no roots, no diagnostic, exit
  2. That happened from the git top (`--changed Cloud/src/posting.al`) and from the
  workspace itself (`--changed src/posting.al`). Now the `.al` test comes first; a value
  with no `.al` entry is still a diff when it exists and routine selectors when it does
  not. An existing `.al` file that is no workspace file is now `file-unmatched`. A batch
  reads it the same way (its pinned existence decision is consulted only for a value
  with no `.al` entry). Limit: a diff file whose name ends in `.al` needs `--diff`.

### Changed

- **`scripts/ci-steps task-affected` builds only the test binaries it runs** (crate split Phase 1,
  ENG-05). It used to pass `--workspace` with an `-E` filter: the filter chose which tests ran, but
  every test binary was still built. It now passes the filter's own targets (the `al-sem` lib tests,
  `--test X` for each `binary(X)`, `-p al-syntax` for `package(al-syntax)`) and keeps `-E` inside
  them. A filter part with no known target falls back to the whole suite. `task` and `all` are
  unchanged. TLS-13 re-check (TLS-12's tree): for every filter `affected_filter` can build, each
  path class alone and all 13 parts together, both forms list the identical tests (3,282 to 5,724).
  Measured (an edit simulated by touching one file, build and test, alternating, 3 each; every run on
  a busy host, 0-69% idle): `src/lsp/handlers.rs` wall 66.3 -> 64.9 s, CPU 556 -> 514 s (every pair
  lower); `src/program/resolve/full.rs` CPU 716 -> 704 s, wall within the noise (73.8 -> 84.7 s,
  pairs -11, +18, -15 s); `src/engine/l5/digest_cli.rs` inconclusive (2 of 3 old runs stopped at a
  load-sensitive test, `mcp_server::faults::status_answers_during_a_heavy_call`, 223-227 ms against
  its 200 ms bound). The saving is the skipped test binaries' linking: real in CPU, small in wall.

- **Grammar: tree-sitter-al v5.1.0, `abc77b25`** (was v5.0.0, `18c988e8`). Seven new `RawKind`s,
  all `Structural`; `NAMED_KIND_COUNT` is 513. `CACHE_VERSION_GRAMMAR` is now
  `tree-sitter-al-v5.1.0-abc77b25-native` (same length, so `dry-run.txt` did not move).
  - The grammar's tree changes on valid input (a caption's trailing `,` before an `#if` group;
    nine or more empty groups after an ML or `Namespaces` value) touch nothing the lowerer reads.
  - Measured on 12,343 files (the CDO baseline's 741, al-sem's 721 test fixtures and the 10,881
    sources inside the CDO baseline's 11 dependency packages): every raw tree is identical, the
    lowered routines are identical, and no file has an `ERROR` or `MISSING` node on either side.
    The whole suite gives the same outcome for every test on both grammars.
- **Grammar: tree-sitter-al v5.0.0, `main` at `18c988e8`** (was v4.5.0, `91a5db62`). Five new
  `RawKind`s, all `Structural`; `NAMED_KIND_COUNT` is 506. `CACHE_VERSION_GRAMMAR` is now
  `tree-sitter-al-v5.0.0-18c988e8-native` (same length, so `dry-run.txt` did not move).
  - **Breaking shape:** a `case`'s `else` is now the last child of `case_body`. The lowerer's
    fallback that read a `case_else_branch` directly under `case_statement` is gone.
  - `preproc_split_procedure_preamble` now has a `body` field, so its bare-child fallback is
    gone too.
  - On real code (the CDO baseline, DO-Next and BC.AL.Runner/BC-on-Linux, 963 files) every
    tree is the old one with only the `else` moved, and there are no `ERROR` or `MISSING` nodes
    on either side. The CDO unknown counts are unchanged.

### Added

- **More `#if` shapes the 5.1.0 grammar parses (they were `ERROR` before).**
  - A nested group of header and `var` section in a split procedure or trigger
    (`preproc_conditional_procedure_preamble`, `preproc_conditional_trigger_preamble`) yields
    one routine per arm, with that arm's own locals and build context, as a nested header
    group does.
  - An attribute in an outer arm before a nested header group belongs to every routine of that
    group, and to no routine of another outer arm.
  - A label whose `Locked` attribute sits in an `#if` group is not a constant
    (`FixedLocal::constant`): it is locked in some builds only. The lowerer reads no other
    grouped label, caption, ML or `Namespaces` content.
- **`#if` shapes the new grammar parses (they were `ERROR` before).** A split trigger header
  (`preproc_split_trigger_preamble`) and a nested header group in a split procedure
  (`preproc_conditional_procedure_header`) yield one routine per arm, with that arm's build
  context. An `#if` group in a parameter list (`preproc_conditional_parameters`) or a return
  clause chosen per arm (`preproc_conditional_return`, `preproc_conditional_return_type`) reads
  the first arm the routine's build does not rule out, with a `SyntaxIssue`, as `#if` in
  attribute arguments does.
- **`extends` and `implements` take a dotted name** (`Contoso.Sales."Base"`), read as its last
  segment because objects carry no namespace. `extends 50101` is kept as the number's text and
  raises a `SyntaxIssue`: targets are looked up by name, so a numeric base is not resolved.

### Fixed (FW2: an ABI ingest failure is pinned all the way to the user)

- **`ProgramGraph::abi_ingest_errors` already had a production reader; now a test pins it.**
  The dependency ledger (`dependency_ledger`, `src/program/resolve/full.rs`) copies each
  failure onto its declared dependency, `FreshCoverage::dependency_diagnostics` reports it
  as a `dependencies` warning ("could not be read: …") and the preflight degrades
  ("unreadable dependency app(s)"). This has worked since S5.2a/#91, but no test covered
  the step from the graph into the ledger, so deleting it left everything green. The new
  test `abi_ingest_error_reaches_the_dependency_diagnostics_and_the_preflight`
  (`src/program/abi_ingest.rs`) fails when that lookup is broken (proof run 2026-11-10).
  No behavior or golden changed. On real input this path is rare: the dependency loader
  parses `SymbolReference.json` first, so a corrupt file usually makes the whole package
  unreadable before ABI ingest runs.

### Outside consumers (wave 2)

One list of every field and value wave 2 changed for a program that reads al-sem's output
(bc-dev-mcp, ConTinAI, saved baselines). The sections below describe each change as it was
made; where they name an older value or mechanism, this list is the current one. Field names
are as they appear in the JSON. "Additive" means the old shape still holds.

- **Effect rows and error answers** (prove, explain, digest):
  - Digest effect `status` has a new value, `caught` (a definite trap catches the error on
    every route), next to `live` and `literal-dead`.
  - `trap` (additive, on effect rows of prove, explain and digest, and on the rows of prove's
    filtered slice): `verdict` (`caught`, `escapes-if-write-pending`,
    `trapped-on-some-routes`), `kind` (`checked-run`, `try-function`, `asserterror`,
    `isolated-event`), `routine`, and `file` and `line` when known.
  - `collectedBy` (additive, same rows): the procedures whose
    `[ErrorBehavior(ErrorBehavior::Collect)]` may collect the error.
  - `caughtErrors` (digest and explain summaries). An error caught on every route leaves the
    summary's `kinds`.
  - prove's filtered slice JSON gains `caught`.
  - `suppressedCommits` (prove `result.suppressedCommits` for a commit question; digest entry
    `suppressedCommits`), present only when some commit is ignored or turned into an error by a
    `[CommitBehavior]`. Each entry has `behavior` and `reason`, and `file` and `line` (1-based)
    when known. `beyond` is the dependency routine for a commit past a call into dependency
    code. It is a routine name, not a flag, and is left out when the commit is not beyond one.
  - An `ERROR_IMPLICIT` row for a commit turned into an error carries `detail.commitBehavior`.
- **Assumptions** (all only when set):
  - prove `obligations.assumesNoPendingWriteAtEntry`, `obligations.assumesNoCommitBehaviorAtEntry`.
  - digest and explain `summary.assumesNoPendingWriteAtEntry`,
    `summary.assumesNoCommitBehaviorAtEntry`.
  - digest and explain `coverage.assumptions` gain the labels `no-pending-write-at-entry`,
    `no-commit-behavior-at-entry`.
- **Platform operations:** `query effects` and `query touches` JSON gain `origin.platform` on a
  row for a platform dataset operation (a report's or query's read, an XmlPort import's
  insert or modify); human output adds `(platform: …)`; explain adds a `platform:` line; such a
  row's evidence `excerpt` is the reason instead of `Var.Op`. No field was removed or renamed.
- **Gaps:** coverage reason `unreadable-event-subscriber` (an `[EventSubscriber]` the engine
  cannot read; prove `unknown`, explain and digest name it); `query touches` adds a count,
  `unreadableEventSubscribers`, only when above 0, and then says `analysis partial`.
- **Digest paths:** `paths[].terminal.operationId` now names the site whose line it prints,
  for any callee with two sites of one kind (it used to name a representative fact's id).
- **Attribute JSON** (the L2 projection's `attributesParsed`, and the model's `AttributeInfo`
  wherever it is serialized): `conditional: true` when only some builds of THIS declaration have
  the attribute, `anotherDeclarationLacks: true` when another declaration of the same routine
  lacks it. Both are left out when false. `conditional` no longer appears for an attribute only
  another declaration lacks.
- **Human lines** (text outputs; each is new or reworded):
  - prove and digest: `commit behavior:` (a commit that is ignored or raises an error, with
    why); explain prints the same line.
  - prove: `no — no error site escapes the routine; N error sites caught on every route by a
    trap`, and the lines `caught on every route by a trap: …; not counted`.
  - prove, explain, digest: the condition words `escapes on a route with no trap; caught on
    others (…)`, `a write may be pending at the checked Codeunit.Run at …`, `escapes only if a
    write is pending when the event is raised, …`; the filtered prove's `escapes on the route
    below (no trap on it); other routes are caught by the …`.
  - explain and digest: `errors caught on every route by a trap (they do not leave the routine
    if its callers have no write pending when they call it …)`; the summary's `; N caught on
    every route by a trap`.
  - prove, explain, digest headers: the longer `assumptions:` sentence
    (`traps::entry_assumption`).
  - explain: the compact card's wording (section "compact explain card" below), including
    `no table-event subscriber loaded` and `lines 351, 623 (…)`.
  - query effects: `[CalcFields] on … through FlowField "…"`.
- **`alsem graph`** (schema `al-sem.callgraph`, major version still 1):
  - additive optional node field `otherDeclarations`, `[{sourcePath, line, endLine}]`: the other
    places of a routine declared more than once with the same subscriptions;
  - a subscriber whose declarations subscribe differently is one node per declaration, each with
    its own lines and subscriptions;
  - a static report save is a resolved `run` edge to the report (it was an `Open` edge into the
    `h:run:report` hub); `Q.Open()` and `Query.SaveAs*` get an edge into the query's
    `OnBeforeOpen` (`entry_trigger`);
  - an importing routine gets `implicitTrigger` and `tableEvent` edges (confidence `OverApprox`)
    to its tables' `OnInsert`/`OnModify` and table events;
  - `hiddenCallers` value `unboundSubscriber` is set on a subscriber with an unreadable
    `[EventSubscriber]` even when another of its subscriptions is bound (the value is not new);
  - a subscriber declared only in a second file gains its subscription edges.
- **Routine and site ids:**
  - A split subscriber (whose declarations subscribe differently) has new routine ids, stable
    ids `{stable}~{8 hex}` and site ids. A name or the routine's base id selects every
    declaration (`prove`, `digest`, `tests`, `impact`); `~hex` selects one; the fingerprint
    query lists them as candidates (`differs_in` says "the file or #if arm"). A change of
    another file's subscription that starts or ends a split moves an unchanged file's ids once.
  - A routine declared in two `#if` arms of one file: the second arm's site ids move (`…/opN`,
    `…/csN`, `loop`, `u`, `rule`).
  - A routine declared in two or more files: each file's site ids are in that file's own block,
    `…/op{block * 100000 + n}`, with the block picked from a hash of the file's own source unit.
    The format is the same; the numbers are large. A file's ids move when a second file starts
    or stops declaring the routine, or when its own path changes.
  - Everything built on site ids moves with them: digest `factId`, `evidenceOperationId`,
    `callsiteId`, snapshot and `diff` operation ids, `explain`/`prove` lines. Fingerprints strip
    site segments, so baselines do not move except where a split changes a routine's id.
    `SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA_VERSION` is unchanged (the snapshot's shape did not change).
  - `alsem query` no longer calls a routine declared in two `#if` arms ambiguous (one candidate
    per stable id).
- **Schema and cache values** (now):
  - Impact JSON `summarySchema`, and the impact-base cache key: **9**
    (`impact::keys::SUMMARY_SCHEMA`; 2 before wave 2). A base cached earlier is not read.
  - `PACK_SCHEMA` **17** (14 before wave 2): dependency packs are rebuilt.
  - `FACADE_VERSION` **2** (1 before; the session dependency recorder, internal).
- **Answers that changed without a new field:** the record operations of a report's, query's or
  XmlPort's platform dataset run; a report's `SaveAs*`/`Execute`/`Print` and a query's
  `Open`/`SaveAs*` now run their triggers; FlowField reads (`query touches`, `query effects`,
  `digest --include-reads`, `fingerprint`'s `R` right); `unknown` where a dynamic object id or an
  unreadable subscriber gave `no`; `conditional` for `#if` arms and per-record triggers; errors
  caught by a trap leave the error answers.

Terms used in the wave-2 sections below:
- **`N`, `I`, `E`, and sets like `N|I` or `N|E`:** the `[CommitBehavior]` value a commit may run
  under (`N` normal, `I` ignored, `E` raises an error); `N|I` means "normal or ignored", because
  the routes or builds differ. `P` and `X` are the same value on a route pinned by a checked
  `Codeunit.Run` (a commit that runs, or an error that the run traps).
- **#160 step 11b, "the 11b rules":** the rules issue #160 added for rows of one routine id that
  share a site id: a reader that looks a site up in such a group must take the row that holds
  it, not any row.
- **Class P:** of the 11b rules, the case where such a reader keeps the LAST row that holds the
  site.
- **Least fixpoint:** the result of repeating a rule over the reachable routines until no
  routine changes; used for "may a write be pending at this run".
- **Per-value transfer function** (`commit_scope::Transfer`): one result per `[CommitBehavior]`
  value a routine may be entered under, so a "may" deep in the graph combines exactly with a
  declaration above it.

### Changed (TLS-14: the prove parity test builds each model once)

- **`no_dependency_parity_prove` runs each dir's cases as one in-process batch**, TLS-12's reviewed
  design (one model per universe instead of one per case), and every root of every 5th dir also
  runs each job alone through `standalone_output`, the path `alsem prove` runs. It now also compares
  the stderr. Limit: a fault only a one-job view shows is compared on the sampled dirs only.
  Discrimination: B1 fails both halves; B2, a cross-app-only change made only in a one-demand view,
  fails the standalone half alone (362 cases, 0 batch). Measured (3 alternating pairs): CPU per run
  -26 s (-1.6%), wall -1.3 s, the test 46 -> 41 s; prove's per-root work, not its model build, is
  most of the test's cost. See `docs/superpowers/notes/2026-11-10-task-gate-test-time.md`.

### Fixed (TLS-15: a status test that failed under host load)

- **`mcp_server::faults::status_answers_during_a_heavy_call` no longer has a fixed 200 ms bound.**
  It took 223-227 ms on a saturated host (2026-11-11, TLS-13's timing) and stopped the run. What it
  guards is that `alsem_status` answers WHILE a heavy call runs: it still requires the status first
  (before the explain) and naming the running call, and now times the status against the heavy call
  itself in the same run: from the status request, the status must answer in under a quarter of the
  time the explain still takes (about 2.5 s of a 3 s sleep). Host load stretches both alike.
  Discrimination: a status that waits for the running call fails at "answered first"; a status
  slowed by 1.5 s but still answered first fails the new ratio (1.50 s against 2.51 s).
- Other fixed wall-clock bounds in `tests/cli/mcp_server.rs` and `engine_host.rs`: the 10-30 s
  upper bounds are hang guards and the lower bounds cannot fail under load. The one tight upper
  bound, `engine_host::faults::repeated_deaths_back_off_then_fail_until_reset`'s `< 100 ms` for a
  failure "at once", is now `< 800 ms`: `spawns == 3` pins that nothing was spawned, and the bound
  pins that no backoff was waited, the next of which is at least 800 ms (the waits double: 200,
  400). Discrimination: the failed state sleeping its next backoff before failing (1.6 s) fails it;
  a 500 ms sleep would not (a half-of-the-third-wait ratio was tried first and let it through).

### Changed (TLS-12: the slowest tests build each model once)

- **Four `tests_rule_b` corpus tests are one test**, `scoped_reads_equal_unscoped_on_the_corpus`:
  its arms (T3, the streamed read, prove, the fingerprint query) share each target per universe
  and the trees two arms build alike, on 4 threads (about 127 s -> 11.5 s alone). Under nextest
  each test is its own process, so a build is shared only inside one test.
- **`no_dependency_parity_fingerprint_routine` runs each dir's cases as one in-process batch**
  (`batch_in_process` over `engine::batch::run_batch`): one model per universe instead of one per
  case. Every root of every 5th dir also runs each job alone through `standalone_output`, the path
  `alsem fingerprint` runs (87 s -> 21 s alone). `ids_parent_baseline` batches its SARIF and JSON
  analyses the same way.
- Every assertion and failure message is kept; no golden moved. Measured (3 alternating pairs):
  children's CPU per run -200 s (-12%), median wall 154.5 -> 123.0 s. See
  `docs/superpowers/notes/2026-11-10-task-gate-test-time.md`.

### Changed (TLS-11: the long tests start first)

- **`.config/nextest.toml` gives the longest tests a priority.** The task gate's test run was
  limited by its tail: three long tests in the lib and `al-syntax` started 60-90 s into the run,
  and the run waited about 20 s on them (TLS-07,
  `docs/superpowers/notes/2026-11-10-task-gate-test-time.md`). Every test with a median of 15 s
  or more now has priority 60 (14 tests, by name), and the cli fingerprint parity test (70-87 s,
  the longest) priority 70. Priority only reorders; every test still runs. Measured on master
  `761581b3`, 3 alternating pairs: the tail 22.6-27.0 s -> 3.1-3.6 s, the median wall
  149.1 -> 122.6 s (pairs -15.7 to -28.6 s; the host was shared, see the note).
- **Every nextest run writes a JUnit report** (`target/nextest/<profile>/junit.xml`). After the
  full suite, `scripts/ci-steps test` runs `scripts/nextest-priority-check`, which names any test
  of 15 s or more that no priority override selects (asking nextest which tests each override's
  filter selects). It only warns: one run's durations swing with the machine's load.

### Fixed (TLS-10: the CDO gate passed on failed calls)

- **`scripts/cdo-speed` fails when a timed call fails.** Given a wrong workspace, every call
  exited 1 in about 0.01 s on both sides, and the speed phase still printed `PASS` on the
  ratios of those failures (2026-11-10, `/work/src/cdo-baseline` for its `Cloud` folder). A
  call that exits non-zero, or fails in the engine, on either side now stops the run at once
  with exit 1, naming the round, the call, the side, the exit code and the call's first stderr
  lines; nothing is judged on a failed call. Every call exits 0 on CDO (the gate's runs of
  2026-11-10), so a correct run is unchanged.
- **`scripts/cdo-gate` fails a test phase that ran no test.** A phase whose `cargo test`
  filter matches nothing (a renamed member or module) exits 0 on "0 passed"; the summary now
  calls it `FAILED (no test ran)`. Every other phase already failed on a wrong workspace
  (`ENFORCE_CDO_WS=1`): only the speed phase could pass on nothing. `cdo-gate
  --summary=<run folder>` prints a past run's summary from its logs.
- Tests: `tests/cli/gate_scripts.rs` (Linux/Unix), each with a discrimination proof.

### Fixed (engine limits wave 2, B2 final review follow-up 5: the rest of the unreadable `[EventSubscriber]`)

- **An unreadable field of a table's validate event is a gap too** (review of 1dbb302c).
  `[EventSubscriber(ObjectType::Table, Database::"AD T", 'OnAfterValidateEvent', (Amt), …)]`
  read as "no field", so it listened to no field event and `R.Validate(Amt, 1) may-commit`
  said `no` (the same for `5` and `Rec.Amt`). A fourth argument present but not readable, on
  a table's validate event, is now unreadable (`resolve::event::UNREADABLE_ELEMENT`) and the
  gap applies to a `Validate` on that table, any field. On any other event the element is
  not read by the dispatch, so it stays as it was.
- **A readable field narrows the gap:** an unreadable publisher with `'OnAfterValidateEvent',
  'Amt'` is a gap for a `Validate` of `Amt`, and a `Validate` of another field stays
  definite.
- **The publisher now narrows a record operation's gap.** The lookup used the object ids
  while a record operation holds a model table id (`{guid}/table/{n}`), so it found nothing
  and matched every table, and a publisher by number was not read. It now reads the model's
  tables, by name or by number: an `Insert` on an unrelated table stays `no` and complete.
- **An unreadable declaration's readable parts narrow what it borrows.** It takes only the
  sibling subscriptions its own parts allow; when they rule out every readable
  subscription of the routine it does subscribe differently, so the routine splits (probe
  `cw`: `RaiseY` stays `no`, `RaiseX` is the gap). Names are compared with `fold_identifier`
  on both sides.
- `PACK_SCHEMA` 17, `SUMMARY_SCHEMA` 9 (the current values).
- Tests (`tests/cli/cli_b2_alternative_declarations.rs`) with proofs, break with Edit, red,
  revert with Edit, green:
  - Unreadable element left as "no element": `an_unreadable_element…` red (`no`).
  - Table lookup left empty: `a_record_operation_gap…` red (`unknown` on the other table).
  - Publisher number not compared: the same test red, on its by-number pass.
  - Field not compared: `a_readable_element_narrows…` red (`unknown` on `Name`).
  - Borrowing not narrowed: both `an_unreadable_declaration` narrowing tests red (`yes`).
  - No split when the parts rule the routine's subscriptions out: `…ruled_out…` red (`yes`).

### Fixed (engine limits wave 2, B2 final review follow-up 4: an unreadable `[EventSubscriber]` is a gap)

- **An `[EventSubscriber]` the engine cannot read never gives a definite `no`.** Probe u2
  (review of 38738f3b): `a.al` subscribes to `OnX` and is empty, `b.al`'s
  `[EventSubscriber(ObjectType::Codeunit, (Codeunit::"AD Pub"), 'OnX', …)]` commits. The
  parentheses made the attribute unreadable, so the subscription lists differed, the
  routine split, `b.al`'s body was reachable from no dispatch and `RaiseX may-commit` said
  `no` (true answer `yes`). The same for one declaration, older, in
  `parse_event_subscriber_ir`: an integer object type, two arguments, a parenthesised
  publisher, `'On' + 'X'`, `ObjectType::Foo`, a bare identifier as the publisher: each
  dropped the attribute and answered a definite `no` with no gap.
- `resolve::event::read_event_subscriber_ir` keeps the attribute with the parts it could
  read (`ParsedSubscriberArgs::is_unreadable`: an empty object type, publisher or event).
  A part is unreadable for an object type no event is published on, a bare identifier as
  the publisher (AL writes `Codeunit::"X"`), or an argument list longer than the
  attribute's six (the grammar reads `'On' + 'X'` as three items).
- **Split:** a declaration with an unreadable subscription never counts as subscribing
  differently (only the readable copies are compared), so `u2` stays one routine and its
  body stays reachable. When the readable copies differ and it does split, the unreadable
  copy also subscribes to every event its readable siblings do. *(Follow-up 5 above changes
  both halves: it does count as subscribing differently when its readable parts rule out
  every readable subscription of its routine, and it borrows only the sibling subscriptions
  its own parts allow.)*
- **The gap:** `model::events` records one `unreadable` event edge per attribute of any
  app (`unknown/unreadable/…`), and `combined_graph` puts an uncertainty
  (`unreadable-event-subscriber`, a coverage reason) on every publisher routine and every
  record operation (for a table event) it may be for, narrowed by the readable parts: a
  readable event name, object type or publisher leaves the others alone (`RaiseY` stays
  `no` when only `OnX` is named). Prove says `unknown` (the blocker names the attribute),
  `explain` and `digest` report it as the coverage reason, `query effects` and `query
  touches` as `analysis partial`. A subscriber with an unreadable subscription has
  `hiddenCallers: unboundSubscriber` in `alsem graph` even when another subscription of
  its binds, so the callers' questions say `unknown`.
- Real code: **0 of 3,629** `[EventSubscriber]` attributes in the CDO baseline and its
  dependencies are unreadable (`aldump --program-call-graph-stats`, every parsed attribute
  counted, 2026-11-10), so no answer on CDO moved; the guards are for shapes nothing has
  shown yet.
- `PACK_SCHEMA` 16 (entries for unreadable attributes), `SUMMARY_SCHEMA` 8 (at this round; the
  current values are in "Outside consumers (wave 2)" above). `alsem graph` schema unchanged.
- Dependency selectors are scoped to the workspace app (a name finds no dependency
  routine, a stable id does), for every routine, not only a split subscriber; unchanged.
- Tests (`tests/cli/cli_b2_alternative_declarations.rs`) with proofs, break with Edit,
  red, revert with Edit, green:
  - Unreadable copies compared too (`.filter(|&i| true || …)`): not-split test red (two
    nodes). Prove alone stayed green, since the union also makes the body reachable, so the
    test pins the single node.
  - No union on a split: `stays_reachable_when_the_others_split` red (`unknown`).
  - Attributes dropped at extraction: every `an_unreadable…` test red (`no`).
  - No gap at publishers: definite `no`, red.
  - No narrowing by the event: `RaiseY` red (`unknown`).
  - No gap at record operations: table test red (`no`).
  - No `hiddenCallers` for a bound subscriber with an unreadable one: callers test red
    (`no`; the proof first passed because the parenthesised attribute also trips parse
    recovery, so the test uses `ObjectType::Foo`).
  - `query effects` and `query touches` gaps: red (no `analysis partial`).

### Fixed (engine limits wave 2, B2 final review follow-up 3: the program graph splits too)

- **The program graph has one routine node per declaration of a subscriber whose
  declarations subscribe differently** (`program::split_decls`, decided once in
  `build::split_declarations`, before the dedup). Follow-up 2 below split only the MODEL,
  so the walkers that read the program graph still saw one node holding every
  declaration's subscriptions (review of 53d143ef):
  - M1 (a wrong definite answer): `prove . "AD Q::C" callers-intercept-errors
    --no-dependents` said `yes` through a `[TryFunction]` that raises `OnY`, reaching
    `H` from the `a.al` declaration, which subscribes `OnX` and calls `C`. No build has
    that path. Now `no`; and `callers-have-pending-writes`, the same walker.
  - M2: `alsem tests` and `alsem impact` did not find a split subscriber (`"not in
    projection"`, run the whole suite), and the callers' questions could not name one at
    all (`~` id: "not in the call graph"; base id: no routine; name: ambiguous).
  Each declaration node has the routine's id with its `sig_fp` mixed with a hash of its
  place (its source unit and ordinal in the file, as the model's `~hex` suffix now is:
  `split_decls::stable_suffix`), its own subscriptions, its own table-event and out
  edges, its own source lines. Name lookup shows one declaration per routine, so
  overload logic is unchanged (`resolve::reads::RoutineRun`), and the resolver sends a
  direct call to every declaration (`split_decls::expand_call_routes`, one route per
  declaration, each a possible build). The callers' walker, the sited graph, `alsem
  graph`, the LSP call hierarchy and the model agree by construction, and the model's
  own split (`split_subscriber_declarations`, `events::row_declares_subscription`,
  `program_calls::split_declaration_edges`) is gone: its rows take their declaration's
  ids from `node_of` (`workspace::adopt_declaration_ids`), so a demanded dependency
  declaration splits even when it is the only row of its routine.
- **A selector resolves a split subscriber.** A name or the routine's base id names every
  declaration (form 1b of the selector cascade; `prove`/`digest`/`tests`/`impact`, the
  one exception being the fingerprint query, which lists them as candidates, and
  `differs_in` now says "the file or #if arm"); the `~hex` id names one declaration
  (`SitedGraph::nodes_with_stable_id`, which also takes the base id for a split routine).
- **`alsem graph`: every declaration's lines are there.** Split: a node per declaration.
  Not split (an `#if` routine declared twice with no differing subscription): the node's
  `sourcePath`/`line`/`endLine` are one declaration's, and the new optional node field
  `otherDeclarations` (`[{sourcePath,line,endLine}]`) lists the others. Additive: the
  graph's major version stays 1 (spec 2026-10-13 §4.2). bc-dev-mcp's join still falls
  back by name for a place it does not read; it should read this field (outside-consumers
  update).
- **Ids:** `SUMMARY_SCHEMA` 7 at this round (a split declaration's model id and `~hex` suffix
  derive from the place hash, so they move once); the recorder's `FACADE_VERSION` 2 (a new
  query, `DeclarationsOf`, and `routines_of`/`routines_named` now hide the other
  declarations). A split declaration's id stays the declaration's own when other files
  change, but **a change of another file's subscription that starts or ends a split
  does move an unchanged file's ids** (`H` in `a.al` moves between `…~9f0631d4` and its
  base id, since its node is split only while a declaration elsewhere subscribes
  differently), so fingerprints, baselines and diffs move for that routine. Always
  suffixing every routine with a second declaration would stop that one case, at the
  price of splitting every `#if` procedure in real code (model rows, selectors, the
  join's "alternatives" reading) to save one rare, one-time move; not done.
- *(Superseded by follow-ups 4 and 5 above: an unreadable `[EventSubscriber]` now stays on
  its node as a coverage gap, and a copy with one is not compared.)* Limits, as measured
  (engine-limits B2, updated): a subscription whose
  `[EventSubscriber]` attribute the engine cannot read is not on its declaration's node
  (as with any subscriber), and two copies count as subscribing alike or differently from
  the readable ones; no real code has shown one.
- Tests (`tests/cli/cli_b2_alternative_declarations.rs`, every shape and both file
  orders; session refresh-equals-cold through a split starting and ending, both memory
  modes, `program::session::workspace::tests`), with proofs (break with Edit, red, revert
  with Edit, green):
