### Fixed (engine limits wave 2, B7/L23 + L30)

- **An error behind a trap is no longer reported as escaping.** `prove … throws-error` (with
  and without `--match`, `--site`, `--op`, `--table`), explain's and digest's error lines
  counted every error the root's cone can raise, even one that a trap on every route turns
  into `false`. Fixture (`if not Codeunit.Run(Codeunit::Thrower)`): `yes — ERROR_THROW at
  thrower.al:5 (unconditional on success)`; now `no` with `caught on every route by a trap: 1
  error site (… by the checked Codeunit.Run at callers.al:6)`. A definite trap is:
  - a checked run: `if [not] Codeunit.Run(…)`, `Ok := Codeunit.Run(…)`, `exit(Codeunit.Run(…))`,
    `MyCodeunit.Run()` with its result used (Microsoft Learn, "Codeunit.Run(Integer [, var
    Record]) Method",
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/methods-auto/codeunit/codeunit-run-method:
    without the return value "a runtime error will occur"; with it, the run returns false and
    its changes are not committed), **but only where no write may be pending at it**. The same
    page says "If you're already in a transaction you must commit first before calling
    Codeunit.Run": a checked run inside an open write transaction is itself a run-time error,
    raised at the run. So a write that may be pending at the run makes it no definite trap (see
    the review fixes below);
  - a `[TryFunction]` call whose value is the whole right-hand side of `Ok := …` or the whole
    condition of an `if`, `while` or `until` (through parentheses and `not`). Learn ("Handling
    errors using try methods",
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/devenv-handling-errors-using-try-methods):
    "If a try method call doesn't use the return value, the try method operates like an
    ordinary method, and errors are exposed as usual"; "If a try method call uses the return
    value in an `OK:=` statement or a conditional statement such as `if-then`, errors are
    caught". Learn names no other shape (see the review fixes below). A TryFunction does not
    roll back database changes (same page), and nothing says it does;
  - a call or record operation under `asserterror`.
- **An isolated event's subscriber error stays `yes` and states its condition**: `escapes only
  if a write is pending when the event is raised, or during an install or upgrade; otherwise
  caught by the isolated event at …`. Learn ("Isolated events in AL"): a write transaction not
  committed before the event makes it run as a normal event, and install/upgrade runs it
  normally. prove's yes is a may-answer, so the error is kept.
- **A route trapped on some paths and not others says which.** The row keeps escaping and says
  `escapes on a route with no trap; caught on others (the checked Codeunit.Run at …)`; with a
  filter, the printed route is one that crosses no trap.
- **L30, `[ErrorBehavior(ErrorBehavior::Collect)]` forward:** an `Error` whose route passes a
  collecting procedure says it may be collected and raised when that procedure ends, unless the
  code clears it. The error is kept: Learn ("Collecting errors", "Collectible errors API") says
  only a collectible `ErrorInfo` is collected and a collected error is still shown when the
  procedure ends. Whether a given `Error` is collectible is not read (stated as left in
  `docs/engine-limits.md`).
- **One trap rule for both directions:** `src/engine/l5/traps.rs` holds it;
  `callers-intercept-errors` (callers_context), the pending-writes walk and the forward answers
  all read it (the checked-run test was in three copies before). A fourth checked-run test, the
  transaction spans' commit boundary (`transaction_spans::is_checked_codeunit_run`), stays
  apart: it answers where a transaction ends, counts no codeunit variable's `.Run`, and moving
  it would change the commit answers (left, in `docs/engine-limits.md`). The forward search
  (`literal_reach`) marks trap edges once; for a root with a trap in its reach it walks the
  edges again with guards ignored and trap edges not crossed. A site whose routine that walk
  does not reach is caught: ignoring guards reaches at least what any literal arguments and
  any loaded-subscriber assumption reach, so `caught` rests on neither. (A first version ran a
  second guarded search instead; `scripts/cdo-speed` failed it at prove CPU x1.27.) A site
  whose only trap-free route the literal arguments rule out stays escaping.
- **The same applies to the error's dialog (`UI_ERROR`)**: `reaches-ui` no longer counts the
  dialog of an error caught on every route.
- **Output (outside consumers):** digest's per-effect `status` has a new value `caught`;
  effects gain an additive `trap` object (`verdict`: `caught` / `escapes-if-write-pending` /
  `trapped-on-some-routes`, `kind`, `routine`, `file`, `line`) and `collectedBy`; digest and
  explain summaries gain `caughtErrors` (and an error caught on every route leaves `kinds`);
  prove's slice JSON gains `caught`. Human text gains the `caught on every route by a trap`
  lines and the trap words in the condition.
- **Errors beyond a call into dependency code** (a boundary group) are caught when every route
  to the crossing crosses a trap.
- CDO (`SendQueue`, release-fast): `throws-error --site CDOQueueEntry.Table.al:249` answered
  `yes`; the site sits behind `if not Codeunit.Run(…)` at `CDOQueueManagement.Codeunit.al:46`.
  It now answers `unknown` (no matching site reachable; the cone's open-world and unresolved
  calls still block a `no`), and 7,246 of the 7,249 error sites are named as caught. Unfiltered
  `throws-error`: 317 evidence rows before, 3 now (`DOSetup.Get()` at :27 and the two
  `Modify()` at :41 and :49, the only error sites outside the checked run), 314 caught.
  `RunReportID`'s explain: `errors at 296 places` before, 271 and 26 caught now (TryFunctions);
  `IssueReminder`: 289 before, 286 and 4 caught. `scripts/cdo-speed` (load 350-490): PASS,
  prove CPU x0.88, round total x0.89, memory x1.02.
- **Review fixes (two false `no` answers the first version gave):**
  - **A checked run with a write pending is no definite trap.** Fixture `R.ModifyAll(V, 1); if
    Codeunit.Run(Codeunit::Thrower) then;` answered `no … limits: none`; BC raises an error at
    that run. It now answers `yes`, the row's trap verdict is `escapes-if-write-pending` with
    kind `checked-run`, and the condition reads `a write may be pending at the checked
    Codeunit.Run at …: a checked Codeunit.Run inside a write transaction is itself a run-time
    error, raised there; with no write pending it catches the error`. Whether a write may be
    pending is read per root: a write of the run's own routine before the run (the
    pending-writes walk's statement order, so a `Commit()` before the run clears it when it
    runs normally on every route, see round 2 below, and a write to a known-temporary record
    is none), a call before the run into code that may leave
    a write (a callee's write, a call no edge resolves, a callee with no row; not through a
    checked run), or a write pending where a caller in the root's reach called the routine
    (the rule repeated over the root's reach until no routine changes). When the ruling may rest on a checked run with no write
    pending inside the root, the answer states the one thing it cannot see: `assumptions: …
    assumes the routine's callers have no write pending when they call it …` (prove JSON:
    `obligations.assumesNoPendingWriteAtEntry: true`), for the unfiltered and the filtered
    question alike.
  - **A TryFunction traps only where its value is tested.** `Use(TryIt())` answered `no`
    (caught by the TryFunction); Learn names only `OK :=` and a condition, and its one argument
    example (`DoWork(DoInsert(Rec)); // Allowed as the DoWork return value isn't used so it's
    not a try function`) does not establish that a try call used as an argument traps. A new
    call-site fact, `PCallSite::result_tested` (set by the body walk), marks the tested shapes:
    `Ok := …` and the whole condition of `if`, `while` or `until`, through parentheses and
    `not`. Learn names `OK :=` and `if-then`; reading `while`/`until` and `B := not TryIt()`
    the same way goes slightly beyond what Learn names and was not checked on BC. An
    argument, `exit(TryIt())` and `a and TryIt()` are now ordinary calls (the error is
    reported as escaping). `callers-intercept-errors` reads the same rule, and its "not
    intercepted" line now says why for a used-but-unnamed shape. Not modeled, stated in
    `traps.rs`: an error in a try call's arguments is caught too ("Arguments for a try
    function are evaluated inside the try function"), which the answers report as escaping
    (safe); and on premises with `DisableWriteInsideTryFunctions` a write inside a try method
    is itself a run-time error, which the answers do not add. Learn does not say whether the
    try call catches that error, so this one is NOT known to be safe (left, L23).
  - **The pending-writes walk reads a `Commit()` inside a loop.** A target inside a loop counted
    the whole body (an earlier iteration) and stopped there, so a `Commit()` that runs before the
    target in the same iteration ended nothing. CDO's `SendQueue` is exactly that (`repeat …
    Modify(); Commit(); if not Codeunit.Run(…) … until`), and without this the checked run read
    as having a write pending. The walk now also follows the iteration that holds the target, so
    such a `Commit()` ends what came before, earlier iterations included. A `Commit()` after the
    target in the body, or in a loop that does not hold it, still ends nothing. This walk also
    serves the transaction spans and the callers' questions; on CDO `alsem analyze --preset
    transaction-integrity` is byte-identical before and after, and no golden moved.
  - CDO after the review fixes (release-fast): `SendQueue` is unchanged from the first version
    (its run commits first), and its `no`/`unknown` answers now carry the callers' precondition.
    `RunReportID`'s explain: `errors at 281 places; 16 error places caught` (26 caught in the
    first version): the 10 sites behind `exit(TryMergePdf(…))` at
    `CDOContniaOnlinePDFMgt.Codeunit.al:160` are reported as escaping again, since Learn does
    not name `exit(…)` as a try call. `IssueReminder` and `UpdateLastUpload` are unchanged.
  - `scripts/cdo-speed` on the review-fix tree (load average 9.2 at the start, 5.7 at the end):
    PASS. prove CPU x1.06, round total x1.05, model build CPU x1.11 (wall x1.22), warm-tests
    x0.96, peak memory x0.995.
  - New additive JSON: `obligations.assumesNoPendingWriteAtEntry` on prove; the trap verdict
    `escapes-if-write-pending` can now carry kind `checked-run`.
  - A `no` that left errors out as caught says so in its headline: `no — no error site escapes
    the routine; N error sites caught on every route by a trap`.
  - A trap ruling needs a known owner for every operation of the row (before, one known owner
    was enough).
  - When no trap-free route can be printed for a site trapped on some routes (its search
    stopped at the cap, or literal arguments rule it out), the filtered answer no longer says
    `escapes on the route below (no trap on it)`; it says the escaping route could not be
    printed and the route below is a trapped one.
- **Second review fixes (round 2, `fix/w2r2-b7`):**
  - **A `Commit()` that `[CommitBehavior]` stops no longer ends the write before a checked
    run.** Fixture: `[CommitBehavior(CommitBehavior::Ignore)] procedure IgnoredCommitRun …
    R.ModifyAll(V, 1); Commit(); if Codeunit.Run(Codeunit::Thrower) then;` answered `no — no
    error site escapes the routine; 1 error site caught … by the checked Codeunit.Run`, while
    `prove may-commit` on the same routine said the commit is ignored. Microsoft Learn
    ("CommitBehavior attribute",
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/attributes/devenv-commitbehavior-attribute):
    under `Ignore` "this commit is ignored", so the write stays pending and the checked run is
    itself a run-time error; under `Error` "this commit causes an error", so it commits nothing
    either. It now answers `yes` with the `escapes-if-write-pending` verdict, with and without
    `--match`, and so does a scope the caller sets (`[CommitBehavior(Ignore)] IgnoreOuter`
    calling the same shape) and `[CommitBehavior(Error)]`. The pending-writes search reads the
    behavior from B4's rule rather than a copy of it: `commit_scope::CbGraph` gains
    `commit_surely_runs(root, routine)`, which is true only when every route from the root runs
    the routine's commits normally. For this question it reads a checked run as a run the
    scope MAY follow into (B4 pins it to normal, which stands for the run's implicit commit;
    whether a caller's scope reaches an explicit commit inside the run is not on Learn). No
    current answer depends on that choice: an error inside a clean checked run is caught by the
    run anyway. `pending_writes::sites_before_where` takes whether the commits end anything.
  - **When a run is clean only because a `Commit()` before it ends the write, the answer
    states a second assumption.** The root is read as entered with no behavior set; a caller
    that calls it under `Ignore` or `Error` would stop that commit. prove's assumptions line
    reads `assumes the routine's callers have no write pending when they call it and do not
    call it under [CommitBehavior(Ignore)] or [CommitBehavior(Error)]: …`, and its JSON adds
    `obligations.assumesNoCommitBehaviorAtEntry: true` (the search runs a second time with no
    commit ending anything; the flag is set when that makes more runs unsafe). A ruling that
    needs no commit (a helper that only runs) keeps the shorter sentence.
  - **explain and digest state the assumption too.** They dropped a caught error with a
    definite "they do not leave the routine" and only `assumptions: loaded program …`. Now
    their header assumptions line carries the same sentence as prove
    (`traps::entry_assumption`, one source), the caught line reads `errors caught on every
    route by a trap (they do not leave the routine if its callers have no write pending when
    they call it …)`, the JSON summary gains `assumesNoPendingWriteAtEntry` and
    `assumesNoCommitBehaviorAtEntry` (present only when set, as prove's), and
    `coverage.assumptions` gains `no-pending-write-at-entry` and `no-commit-behavior-at-entry`.
    A caught dialog row (`UI_ERROR`) counts too, since it is left out on the same ruling. A
    caught error behind no checked run (a used TryFunction) keeps the plain wording.
  - `LiteralReach::new` now takes the snapshot (it needs the tree's `[CommitBehavior]`
    scopes); every caller passed the snapshot's edges and facts already.
  - Docs corrected: `traps.rs`, this entry and `docs/engine-limits.md` no longer call the
    unmodeled `DisableWriteInsideTryFunctions` case safe (Learn does not say whether the try
    catches that error), and no longer say the TryFunction rule keeps to "the shapes Learn
    names" (`while`/`until` and `not` go slightly beyond them).
  - **Discrimination proofs, round 2** (each break made with Edit, the narrowest test run,
    then reverted and run green):

### Changed (engine limits wave 1, L14 review fixes)

- **The speed gate now catches a change that loses parallelism.** The entry below said
  wall time was judged so that "a change that loses parallelism still shows". It did not:
  wall time was judged only in the rounds, whose calls run on about one thread, while the
  parallel work (the model build, the test universe) is in the warm-up, which was judged
  on CPU time only. `scripts/cdo-speed` now also judges the warm-up's wall time for those
  two calls, at most x1.60 (the worst single sample against the same binary was x1.32).
  Proof (2026-11-09, load 3-6): master `4129eb52` against itself with the head server
  pinned to 2 of 22 cores (`taskset -c 0,1`): model build wall x2.03, test universe wall
  x2.77, so the gate FAILS (exit 1) on exactly those two lines. Their CPU ratios were
  x0.63 and x0.56 (a pinned run spends less CPU), and every round and memory passed, so
  the earlier rule passed this run.
- **The warm-up's side order flips per call**, not only per round: going second always cost
  the test universe up to x1.13 CPU in three earlier runs, eating into its 1.30 limit.
- **On master with no edits** the default base was the merge base, which is HEAD itself:
  the phase timed the tree against itself (200-500 s for nothing; a scheduled run, or the
  agentflow post-merge check). It now times HEAD against its first parent and says so in a
  banner.
- **A tool call that exits non-zero is timed, not a "cannot run" (exit 2).** Its exit code
  is recorded with the answer's hash, so a changed verdict shows as `[outputs or exit codes
  differ]`.
- **Peak memory counts engine children that exit mid-run:** every process's VmHWM is read
  after each call and its highest value kept, instead of read once at the end.
- **`scripts/cdo-gate`:** `--no-speed` works in any position, and an unknown option or a
  second workspace stops the gate (exit 2) instead of being ignored. On a test-build
  failure it now stops the whole speed build (its own process group: cdo-speed and its
  cargo builds), not just the subshell, so no orphaned base build holds the cache lock;
  a Ctrl-C during the test build stops it too.
- **Docs:** the speed phase is Linux only (it reads `/proc`); CLAUDE.md now says that on
  Windows every `cdo-gate` run fails unless given `--no-speed`. The timing range is one
  number everywhere (CLAUDE.md, the L14 row, the `cdo-gate` header): 178-301 s, with this
  change's own run as the low end. The must-catch and must-pass proofs below were run with
  an earlier warm-up rule; their round verdicts do not depend on it.
- **The whole `cdo-gate` on this tree** (2026-11-09, Linux, 22 cores, test build already
  fresh): PASS in ~935 s. `speed` 178 s against the merge base `4129eb52` (model build CPU
  x1.003 and wall x0.998, test universe x0.999 and x0.989, prove x0.946, round total
  x0.961, peak memory 9,530 → 9,545 MiB x1.002), then the lanes: output_cdo 756 s;
  program_resolve_harness 143 s, lsp 19 s, l4_summary_differential 57 s, lib_cdo 391 s.

### Changed (engine limits wave 1, L14: a CDO speed and memory gate)

- **`scripts/cdo-gate` now fails a branch that makes CDO answers slower or larger.** Its
  new first phase, `speed`, runs `scripts/cdo-speed`: the working tree's `alsem`
  (`release-fast`) against the merge base's, on the CDO baseline. Before this nothing
  timed anything on CDO; round 4's slowdown (the c25 assumption-records fix made prove
  and explain ~45% slower, RunReportID `prove … may-commit` 28 s → 41 s, until
  `df5c8fe7`) was noticed only because a golden run took three times as long.
  `--no-speed` (or `CDO_GATE_NO_SPEED=1`) skips the phase for a machine where timing is
  impossible; the gate then prints a banner at the start and in its summary, and its
  last line says `PASS (behaviour only: SPEED AND MEMORY NOT CHECKED)`.
- **What it runs.** One `alsem mcp` server per side (the resident path agents use), both
  alive for the whole run and asked the same calls in turn. Round 0 warms up: the first
  ask builds the CDO model (`build`), then one call of each tool (on `CDO Telemetry::
  UpdateLastUpload`) builds the per-revision artifacts and the test universe. Then
  3 rounds, each on a new routine (RunReportID, IssueReminder, DocEMailSend; DocSave and
  RunReport when more rounds are needed): prove `may-commit`, explain, digest, query
  effects, tests and impact. A new routine each round, because the engine keeps answers:
  asking RunReportID twice measured ~1 s the second time, nothing of the search that
  regressed. The side order flips every round.
- **Why A/B against the merge base, and why CPU time.** Measured first: on this shared
  machine (other agents' load 10-70) one-shot `prove RunReportID` of ONE binary took
  39.0 s and 66.3 s in two runs, so stored per-host budgets would need a margin wider
  than the slowdown they are to catch. Comparing two binaries interleaved cancels most
  load; CPU time (user + system of the server and its engine children, from `/proc`)
  cancels more, since a single-threaded answer's CPU time does not grow while it waits
  for a core. Wall time is judged too, with wider limits. The rounds' calls run on about
  one thread (prove 12.56 s CPU in 12.63 s wall), so a change that loses parallelism
  (same CPU, more wall) shows in the warm-up's wall time: the model build (~160 s CPU in
  ~36 s wall) and the test universe (~135 s in ~18 s) are the parallel parts. The base binary is built from
  `git archive <sha>` once per commit and cached under `~/.cache/al-sem/cdo-speed/`
  (every worktree shares it), beside the test build.
- **Measured noise: the same binary against itself** (master `4129eb52`, release-fast,
  2026-11-09; the median of the per-round ratios of the rounds' prove, which is ~11-20 s
  per routine; and the single-sample warm-up):
  - quiet (load 7-9), two runs: prove CPU x0.94 and x1.06 (single rounds 0.92-1.19),
    round total x1.01 and x1.03; model build CPU x1.01 and x0.96; test universe CPU x1.02 and x1.07;
    peak memory x1.006 and x0.976.
  - beside a release-fast build of master (all 22 cores; this run `58d0c94e` against
    itself): prove x0.97 (single rounds 0.78-1.07); model build CPU x1.09 but its wall x1.32; a 4 s warm-up prove x1.19.
  - beside 22 busy loops (load ~45 on 22 cores): prove x1.12 (5 rounds: 1.12, 1.12, 1.68,
    1.25, 0.98), round total x1.07, model build CPU x0.95, test universe CPU x1.08,
    wall x1.31; the timing took 505 s instead of 220-300 s.
- **The limits that follow** (head over base): the rounds' median CPU ratio at most 1.20
  and wall ratio at most 1.30, per call whose base CPU is at least 2 s (prove) and for the
  round total; the warm-up's model build and test universe (single samples, base CPU at
  least 20 s) at most 1.30 in CPU and 1.60 in wall time; the 1-5 s calls are reported only (single samples
  of them swung to x1.19 under load), and count in the round total; peak memory (every
  server process's VmHWM, summed: ~9.1-9.8 GB, the base engine, the test universe and the
  front end) at most 1.10. When the rounds disagree about a call (some ratios over its
  limit, some not), up to 5 rounds run and the median decides.
- **The must-catch proof.** `1127e74e` (the c25 fix without `df5c8fe7`) against
  `58d0c94e` (with it), an earlier draft of the script that ran 5 rounds: prove x1.77
  (rounds 2.52, 2.25, 1.77, 1.45, 1.09; median 14.8 s → 33.3 s), round total x1.62, FAIL.
  Against master `4129eb52` with the final routines and round limits (the warm-up rule
  was still an earlier one that judged the 4 s warm-up prove too; the round verdicts
  below do not depend on it): prove x2.13 CPU and
  x2.12 wall (RunReportID 14.4 → 30.6 s, IssueReminder 13.7 → 32.8 s, DocEMailSend
  19.2 → 34.2 s), round total x1.88, exit 1, 301 s. Master against itself, same script:
  prove x1.06, round total x1.03, memory x0.98, PASS, 231 s.
- **What it adds to the branch gate:** the timing, 178-301 s on a quiet machine; the
  working tree's release-fast build (a cold one took 233 s; after an edit, the al-sem
  crates only); the base build, ~245 s once per master commit, beside the test build.
  Peak memory: two engines and two test universes, ~19 GB, before the test lanes start.
  The whole `cdo-gate` on this branch's final tree: PASS in ~1,300 s (test build 243 s,
  its release-fast build already fresh, `speed` 203 s with prove x0.96 and round total
  x0.98 against master, then the lanes 853 s), against 834-910 s before.

### Changed (engine limits wave 1, cdo-gate faster)

- **`scripts/cdo-gate` builds once and runs in two lanes; the lib phase runs only the
  CDO tests.** Measured first (2026-11-09, Linux, 22 cores, 93 GB, `cdo` profile, warm
  build; other agents shared the machine, their load alone 10-30 and at times over 100,
  so read each number as a range):
  - Before: 1,184 s and 1,164 s in two runs, peak 39.5 GB. Phases in a row:
    `program_resolve_harness` 41-45 s (210 tests), `lsp` 8 s (2), `l4_summary_differential`
    17-18 s (25), `cli output_cdo` 780-808 s (24), `--lib` 290-317 s (3,214).
  - Where the time went: `output_cdo`'s two impact ratchets. They ran their one-shot
    `alsem impact` calls one after another, each building the CDO model and computing
    the 699-routine change: measured alone, `impact --diff` JSON 275 s, human 263 s,
    `--routine` 65 s (603 s in a row); `impact --base` JSON 428 s, then human 275 s (703 s).
    Every other `output_cdo` test was done by 205-240 s; the impact tests ran on for
    another ~550 s using about 5 of the 22 cores. Inside one `impact --diff` run (traced),
    127 s of its 215 s is the main part, 120 s of that the digest's stream batches over
    the 699 roots. The shared MCP server's 42 calls (`cdo_answers`) took ~205 s with the
    model build; the engine child answers explain, prove and digest on one heavy worker,
    so asking it concurrently would not help. Of the lib's 3,214 tests, 15 read `CDO_WS`;
    alone (nextest `-j 1`) they take 594 s summed, the longest 137 s
    (`cdo_crossing_census`), 118 s, 111 s.
  - After: 834 s and 880 s in two runs of the two-lane version, peak 57-58 GB (each in
    its own cgroup); the final tree (lib phase at 4 threads) 886 s, peak 55.4 GB, and
    910 s, peak 50.6 GB, started at a load average of 178. That is 22-29% shorter. In the final run `output_cdo` was the gate's length (886 s): its
    other 22 tests ended by 404 s, `cdo_impact_ratchets` at 768 s,
    `cdo_impact_base_ratchets` at 886 s; lane 2 took 736 s at `nice 10` (harness 159 s,
    lsp 31 s, l4 46 s, lib 500 s). The gate is CPU-bound on this shared machine (11,000
    CPU-seconds against 9,400 before, at load averages up to 150 in its first 5
    minutes), so the impact calls run slower side by side than alone (275 s alone, up to

    `l4_summary_differential` 25, `output_cdo` 24 — unchanged; the lib phase 17 (the 15

### Fixed (engine limits wave 0, B1)

- **`alsem_prove` with a filter no longer kills the resident engine.** `prove` with
  `--match`, `--table`, `--op`, `--site` or `--routes` reads each routine's guard arms
  (the conditions around a site). The resident engine (`alsem mcp`, `engine-host`, the
  LSP's `al-call-hierarchy/prove`) builds its revision with explain's needs, which leave
  the guard arms out, and nothing widened them: the first filtered ask panicked in the
  engine child ("site guards not built") and the engine died with signal 6. The
  one-shot CLI was right. Now a revision refuses any job whose demand reads model rows
  it was not built with (`PrepareError::Needs`, checked against the job's own demand,
  so it covers every job kind, not just prove), and the engine host then pins with
  `ResidentSession::pin_needs`: the session's needs widen, the model is rebuilt once
  (build class `needs`), and every later build keeps the guard arms. An audit of every
  served command's demand found prove with a filter is the only one that needed more
  than the revision's needs today. New tests: a resident contract test asks every
  filter in both universes after an unfiltered prove and checks each answer equals the
  CLI's bytes, with one rebuild and no engine death; a revision test checks the refusal
  and the widened answer. Cost, measured on the `ws-explain` fixture (release-fast,
  `alsem mcp`, warm): the first filtered prove took 48 ms (the rebuild and the new
  revision's fills), later ones 4 ms; RSS 52.0 MB before, 52.8 MB after. Not measured
  on CDO: there the first filtered ask pays one model rebuild of class `needs` (every
  row projected again, the parses reused) and the new revision's fills, and the session
  then keeps the guard arms (5.6 MB on CDO by the E1 measurement). A session that never
  gets a filtered prove pays nothing.

### Fixed (engine limits wave 0, B3)

- **`prove … callers-intercept-errors` no longer answers a wrong `no` for a subscriber of
  an isolated event.** An isolated event (`[IntegrationEvent(_, _, true)]`,
  `[BusinessEvent(_, true)]`, `[InternalEvent(_, true)]`) runs each subscriber in a
  transaction of its own. When a subscriber fails, the platform rolls back that
  subscriber's database changes and goes on with the next subscriber and then the
  publisher. This does not hold when the raising transaction has a write pending, or
  while an extension is installed, uninstalled or upgraded: then the event runs as a
  normal event and the error fails the whole operation (Microsoft Learn, "Isolated
  events in AL",
  <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/devenv-events-isolated>).
  The question ignored isolation, so the fixture subscriber `HandleIso` got `no (every
  candidate decided) — every path propagates an error to its entry`. Now the dispatch
  from an isolated publisher is a new witness kind, `isolated-event`, which names the
  publisher and the condition; the answer is `yes`. Since the trap does not hold with a
  write pending, the walk still goes on above the publisher. Isolated witnesses are
  listed after the traps that always hold, as `collectible` ones are.
- **The isolated flag now reaches the program graph for every publisher.** A new
  `RoutineNode::publisher_isolated` is read from source attributes
  (`resolve::event::publisher_isolated`) and from a symbol-only dependency's
  `SymbolReference.json` attributes (the rule of `model::events::parse_isolated`:
  isolated when any reading passes `true` or a value that is not a literal). `#if` arms
  of one publisher merge it (isolated in any arm). The sited graph keeps the isolated
  publishers (`SitedGraph::is_isolated_publisher`). The event graph's symbol for a
  dependency publisher that is not a model row (`--single-app`) now carries it too; it
  was always `None` ("not read from dependency attributes yet"). Dependencies on the
  CDO baseline declare 12 isolated events (Base App 5, System Application 5, System 1,
  Continia Core 1). The dependency pack schema moves to 14.
- **An event dispatch no longer needs the publisher's body facts in
  `callers-intercept-errors`.** Whether an error crosses the dispatch depends only on
  the publisher's declaration, but a symbol-only publisher (such as System's
  `Company Triggers::OnCompanyOpenCompleted`) blocked `no` with `order-unknown` ("no
  body facts in the model"). On CDO, `CDO Telemetry`'s `OnCompanyOpenCompleted`
  subscriber got `unknown`; the answer is now `yes`.
- **`prove … throws-error` on a subscriber of an isolated event says whether the error
  escapes** (r3 §7 R5): `whether it escapes <publisher>: no, unless the raising
  transaction has a write pending or an extension is being installed or upgraded`, with
  the reason. A normal event keeps `not established`, because the forward answer does
  not yet apply the traps inside the subscriber (B7).
- Tests: `tests/fixtures/isolated-events` (a workspace and a symbol-only dependency,
  each with an isolated and a normal event) and five tests in
  `engine::l5::callers_context::tests`: four pin the rules (each rule with a
  discrimination proof), the fifth is the normal-event control.

### Fixed (engine limits wave 0, B8 first half)

Five small wrong outputs from `docs/engine-limits.md` §1, B8.

- **`alsem fingerprint` prints AL's own TableData rights.** The human answer and the query
  JSON (`--witness`) printed `W` for an insert; AL's rights are `R`, `I`, `M`, `D`. The full
  snapshot's `permissionFacts` already said `I`. Both now read one mapping
  (`src/engine/l5/table_rights.rs`), and a table's rights print in AL's order (`RM`, not
  `MR`). Fingerprint goldens moved: `W` → `I`, `MR` → `RM`, `RW` → `RI`.
- **A follow-up runs as printed in single-app mode.** A single-app `throws-error` answer
  suggested `alsem prove … callers-intercept-errors --single-app`, and a single-app explain
  card suggested `alsem explain --callers-context … --single-app`; the CLI refuses both
  (they walk the cross-app program). The shared follow-up table
  (`src/engine/follow_up.rs`, `FollowUp::cross_app_only`) now leaves `--single-app`
  (`singleApp`) off them. A new test runs every follow-up that single-app and cross-app
  answers print and checks that none is refused.
- **The `--memory-budget` help of `alsem mcp` and `alsem engine-host` states the real
  defaults** (`8G cross-app, 6G cross-app with --low-mem, 2G single-app`). It said `6G
  cross-app`. The text is now built from the constants in `budget.rs`.
- **`query effects` blames dependency depth only when the cone enters dependency code.**
  `locks: none observed (one dependency routine deep; …)`, the same `reads:` line and the
  header limit `reads, locks and validations one dependency routine deep` printed even
  for a cone with no dependency code. When the cone enters none (the cone was read, not
  cut short, visits no dependency routine, and no operation is dependency code's), the
  lines say `none observed (searched: the whole cone)`, the header says `limits: none`,
  and each operation family's JSON scope is `depth: wholeCone` (`exhaustive` unless a
  call was not resolved).
- **An interface call with no implementer is a gap in workspace code, in the count and
  in the list alike.** The snapshot keeps no call-site evidence for a call with no target,
  so its unresolved-cone item had no position: the explain card counted it `not placed`
  while listing it under `gaps in workspace code`. Such an item now takes its model call
  site's position (`unresolved_cone::place_items`), for every reader of the cone. The same
  holds for a single-app call into a dependency that is not loaded: prove's blocker is now
  placed at its call site and counted `1 in this workspace`.

### Fixed (engine limits wave 0, B8 second half)

- **An MCP answer that may be stale no longer says plainly `served: fresh`.** A file
  rewritten with the same size and modification time is not seen by the default check
  until a `verify` (the context-server spec's stated residual, §5.3), but the answer's
  header said `served: fresh`; only `alsem_status` named the residual. The header's
  `freshness` block is now `{requested, served, residual}`: `served` is
  `fresh-by-size-and-time`, `verified` (every input hashed) or `latest-built` (stale),
  and `residual` says what that check cannot see. `alsem_tests` and `alsem_impact`, which
  run in parts, said `stale: false` and `served: fresh` whatever their parts said; they
  now take `stale`, the changed paths and `served` from their parts.
- **explain and digest no longer repeat the same dependency routine names once per
  place.** A kind line (`errors at N places`, `background tasks at N places`, …) listed
  each dependency call as `TYPE beyond <routines>`, so calls into the same routines from
  many sites printed the same names many times, and never the sites. On CDO
  `CDO Update Handled Sales::SetHandled` (an event with five subscribers, raised at 10
  sites) that was about 5 KB. Calls into the same routines are now one item, named
  once, with their place count and the call sites (`… beyond <routines> (10 places,
  entered at …)`). Every place and every count is kept; a folded group counts all of
  its places in `+N places`. CDO's `IssueReminder` explain golden is expected to move
  (`HTTP beyond Codeunit "CSC Core"::IsAppActiveOrAskToActivate` appears twice there).
- **Test-app discovery no longer stops at 64 `app.json` files for a workspace inside a
  repository with fixture folders.** The walk from the git top level entered folders
  marked as project collections (`.al-sem-projects`, such as this repository's
  `tests/r0-corpus/`) and nested repositories, read 64 unrelated `app.json` files and
  answered "test app discovery incomplete" (seen for workspaces under `target/tmp`).
  It now does not enter a folder holding `.al-sem-projects` or its own `.git` unless the
  workspace is inside it; a folder that is itself an app is still read first, so a
  test app that is its own repository is still found. The 64 cap stays as a safety net.

### Fixed (performance: finding the keeps an assumption record needs)

- **Naming every publisher a ruled-out row needs no longer reruns the whole search per
  keep.** The fix that names every publisher keep a literal-dead row relies on (r3 §7 R1)
  ran one full guarded search per keep the root's search used, plus one more for the
  whole set. On the CDO baseline `CDO E-Mail Handler::RunReportID` uses 88 keeps, so
  `prove … may-commit` and `explain` spent 13 s in 91 searches (each ~140 ms, as each
  keep choice also missed the flow-evaluation cache). Now the search with every keep
  followed is kept as a graph, and each keep choice replays it: a state whose flow
  evaluation asked about no dropped keep keeps its recorded successors and rulings, and
  only the states that did, and the new states they lead to, are stepped again; only
  the rows being explained are judged, over those states only. A flow evaluation now
  records every keep verdict it asked about (`FlowEval::consulted`), which is what
  makes the reuse exact. The answers are the same byte for byte. Measured on the CDO
  baseline (release-fast, one shot): `prove RunReportID may-commit` 40.6 s → 28.4 s
  (before the R1 fix: 28.4 s), `explain RunReportID` 39.5 s → 27.1 s (27.3 s),
  `prove "CDO Issue Document"::IssueReminder may-commit` 39.2 s → 27.6 s (27.3 s).
  A lib test (`a_replayed_search_rules_out_what_the_search_does`) checks the replay
  against the real search for every keep choice.

### Fixed (output validation round 4 final, c05: route guard counts)

- **"N guards on the route" is the route's full count, the one `prove --site` uses.**
  Explain printed `CDOTableFieldArrayMgt.Codeunit.al:278 (8 guards on the route, 0
  evaluated)` where `prove --site …:278` lists "8 of 11 enclosing conditions". The 8 was
  no display cap: it was a different population. The words counted the `if`/`case`/
  `while` conditions plus the earlier `if … then exit` checks, but no `for`, `foreach`
  or `repeat`, and they lost the guards of the effect's own site when that site is a
  call (`Evaluate`, `Message`, `Commit`) or an `Error` statement. prove's listing counts
  every enclosing `if`/`case`/loop and no exit. Now:
  - The witness route's guards include the loops a site sits in (`for i := 1 to 10:
    loop body`, `repeat … until X: continuation`), and the guards of the effect's own
    site for a call-site effect (the evidence call site) and for an `Error` statement
    (the call at the operation's position).
  - `N guards on the route, k evaluated` counts the enclosing conditions only, the
    population of prove's "of M enclosing conditions"; the earlier exits are counted
    apart: `(11 guards on the route, 0 evaluated; 6 earlier exits, 0 evaluated)`. One
    function (`literal_reach::route_guard_counts`) counts for explain, digest and prove.
  - A `condition:` line that lists only some guards says how many, in prove's words:
    `… shown (4 of 18 enclosing conditions and 10 earlier exits)` (was `… +21 guards
    (25 guards in all)`). An exit reads `earlier exit if <condition>: must be false`.
  - JSON `routeGuards`: a loop's `kind` is `for`, `foreach` or `repeat`; an earlier exit's
    is `exit` (was `if` with `mustBe: false`).
  - Rows whose route has only loops or exits now print the guard form instead of the
    class label (`(in a loop)`, `(error-path)`, `(IsHandled pattern, not evaluated)`).

### Fixed (round-4 final m02, c15, c25: an interface call a literal enum value fixes is not open world)

- **An interface call whose implementation every route fixes is no open-world gap.** The
  literal reach already followed `ModuleLicense := ModuleType; ModuleLicense.X()` only
  into the implementation of the enum value the route binds (an enum extension cannot
  change an existing value's implementation), but the call itself stayed in the
  unresolved cone as a polymorphic, open-world site. On CDO, m02's
  `CDOModuleManager.Codeunit.al:16` is reached only through `IsSecurityActivated`
  (`"CDO Module Type"::Security`), and c15/c25's `:16` and `:42` only through
  `LogUsage("CDO Module Type"::Essential, …)`; each was still counted in "N interface calls
  open world", listed as a blocker and as a workspace gap.
  - The literal reach now returns, next to the sites no route can reach, the unresolved
    interface calls whose receiver holds known enum values in every reached state where
    the call can run, each value's implementation a loaded codeunit
    (`LiteralReach::narrowed_sites`). The unresolved cone leaves them out, so they are no
    blocker, no gap and no open-world count.
  - A single route with the enum not known (a parameter its caller does not bind, a
    `foreach` over the ordinals, a value read from a table) keeps the call open world. On
    CDO, `CDOCoreEventHandler.Codeunit.al:39` and `:117` and `CDOUsageManagement.Codeunit.al:27`
    route the enum variably, so a cone that holds them keeps the call.
  - They are counted apart, additively: prove's `obligations.literalNarrowedSites` and the
    line `fixed by literal arguments: N interface calls whose implementation every route's
    enum value selects (not open world, not counted as blockers)`; digest's entry
    `unresolvedLiteralNarrowed`; explain's, digest's and impact's `gaps.literalNarrowed`
    and `; N interface calls fixed by literal arguments (…)` on the uncertainty line. A
    coverage that is partial only through such calls (or literal-dead sites) counts as
    complete for prove, as before for literal-dead sites.
  - Known limit, unchanged: a literal is carried only as deep as the literal reach
    carries it today (m10's literal three frames above the dispatch is not).
  - On CDO: m02 "6 interface calls open world" is now 5 (0 in workspace code); c15's
    `scope.reasons` 9 → 7 and its `CDO File` answer loses the `:16`/`:42` blockers;
    IssueReminder's and RunReportID's cones (c08, c12) 262 → 260. The CDO rendering
    goldens moved by exactly these sites, and three human prove ratchets grew by the new
    line (RunReportID may-commit 2,650 B, RunReportID writes-table data-exch 22 lines,
    IssueReminder writes-table data-exch 3,700 B).

### Fixed (output validation round 4: assumption records name every publisher a site needs)

- **A site ruled out only by several publishers' keeps names all of them (r3 §7 R1).**
  Round-4 c25: the commit at `CDOUsageManagement.Codeunit.al:35` is reached from
  `StartEvents` after `OnBeforeSendMailV2` AND after `OnBeforeSendMailExtV2`, both taking
  `SendHandled` by `var`, yet its assumption record named `OnBeforeSendMailV2` alone. The
  engine read the deciding keep off ONE route (the first the strict search found), so a
  publisher guarding another route to the same site was dropped.
  - The literal reach now judges which keeps a ruling depends on over the whole search:
    it reruns the search following only some keeps (a new keep mask beside "all" and
    "none") and keeps a smallest set that still rules the row out, every member needed.
    The searches are shared by the rows of one root. Measured on the five affected CDO
    calls: no slowdown.
  - Every consumer reads the same set: the rows' `assumes` / `literalAssumes` strings,
    prove's `assumptionRecords` and `subscriberAssumptions`, digest 5.x
    `entries[].assumptionRecords` and `summary.commits.literalDead`, explain and the
    routine totals. On CDO, `StartEvents`' 43 literal-dead rows now all name both
    publishers (40 named `OnBeforeSendMailV2` alone).
  - The sentence names every publisher a site needs: `assumes <A> and <B> have no loaded
    subscriber, so <parameter> keeps its value (…); rules out <site>` (was one sentence
    per publisher, each reading as if it alone ruled the site out). Records stay one per
    publisher; a site listed in several records needs all of them. `--schema 4` is
    unchanged (records stripped).

### Changed (output validation r3 §7: B1 completed, R2 lookup failures, R6 write order)

- **Tests: a test's relation is a property of its path set, in every count and line
  (§7 B1).** The round-4 fix made a test `code` when any of its reaches is code. Now also:
  - A code test whose code path was not kept (its code path lies outside the tier pick)
    stays `code`; its printed path carries its own tag, `path [UI navigation; the test's
    code path is not kept]: …` in the human text and `pathRelation: "UI navigation"` in
    JSON (as before). Among code tests, one whose code path is shown ranks before one
    whose path is such a tagged UI path, so a codeunit's first path is its shortest code
    path when it has one.
  - An incomplete reach inventory (`reachesComplete: false`, changed routines past the
    reach limit) is never reported as "navigation only": the headline says `N more by UI
    navigation on the reaches computed (reach incomplete: k changed routines not
    expanded, which a code path may reach)`. The counts stay the rows' own.
  - A test pins that the headline numbers, `by relation:`, `byRelation`, the summary rows
    and the per-codeunit tags each equal the sum over the rows' `relation`.
- **Lookup failures give the ready call again (§7 R2).** A digest answered inline because
  its selector is ambiguous or not found (r3 H5) dropped the envelope's summary, so
  `summary.next` was gone (round-4 n08, m01, p02).
  - The inline lookup failure keeps the envelope's summary (`outcome`, `next`).
  - Ambiguous: the digest JSON document carries the complete call in
    `payload.summary.next` too (5.0.0, additive; the 4.0.0 adapter drops it), and the
    human text ends with `complete call: …` and `differs in: …`.
  - Not found: a near name is labelled `did you mean: <name> — corrected call: …` in
    explain, prove and digest (was `corrected call (the nearest name): …`); digest also
    puts the corrected call in `summary.next`. No correction when nothing is near; with
    several selectors, a call only when every one has a near name (a call that drops a
    selector is no correction); never a call with an empty target.
- **Touches lead with the writes the task asks about (§7 R6).** With `opFamily: "write"`
  (`--op-family write`, the write follow-up the answers offer) the record-write sites are
  ordered persistent → caller-dependent → temp state not resolved → temporary, Insert
  before Modify before Delete, and the heading states the split (`record writes: 7 sites
  in 4 routines — persistent 3, caller-dependent 1, not resolved 1, temporary 2; by op:
  …`). `writeSites` follows the same order. Without the mode the neutral sampler and
  heading stay; the key-relevant order is unchanged.
  - Field mode (`--field`): a `ModifyAll` that names the field writes it to the database,
    so its row and the counts say `record write (ModifyAll)`, apart from the in-memory
    `field assignment`s and `validate`s (it was counted as a field assignment). JSON keeps
    `uses: ["write"]` with `source: "ModifyAll"`.
- **Consumer notice (additive fields):** digest 5.0.0 `payload.summary.next` on a lookup
  failure (the same `{tool, arguments, why, kind}` object as the envelope's
  `summary.next`); query touches `payload.up.writeSitesByTempState` (`persistent`,
  `callerDependent`, `notResolved`, `temporary`) under `opFamily: "write"`, and
  `writeSites` in the new order. No consumer reads either today.

### Changed (r3 §7 R1, R4, R5: assumptions in words, `starts by:`, error boundaries)

- **R1: a publisher assumption is one sentence, never the bare `loaded-subscribers` token**
  (spec `2026-11-08-output-validation-r3.md` §7; round-4 p05, n01, p09, c25). Wherever the
  literal flow's publisher keep decides a route, prove's assumptions line, explain's and
  digest's `commits:` line and the `--writes-table` answer line print the same template:
  `assumes <publisher> has no loaded subscriber, so <parameter> keeps its value (<universe>;
  no additional subscribers assumed)`, or with subscribers `assumes no subscribers beyond
  those considered in <universe> (<names>), none of which changes <parameter>`, then
  `rules out <site>` or `rules out <n> sites (first: <site>)`. The universe is the
  primary app with its loaded dependencies (`Continia Document Output with its loaded
  dependencies` on CDO), or the app alone. A `no` that rests on the loaded subscribers of
  the events its cone raises (p05, which printed only `assumptions: loaded-subscribers`)
  says which events (`the table events of its record operations, 1 event publication`);
  a `commits: no` that an assumption decided now says so too. The JSON labels
  (`assumptions: ["loaded-subscribers"]`), `subscriberAssumptions`, `literalAssumes`,
  `commits.literalDead.assumes` and the digest rows' `assumes` strings are unchanged;
  prove's `scope.assumptions` mirrors the human line, as before.
- **R4: `starts by:` ends at a statement boundary and keeps literal arguments** (n10, p09,
  c06, m07). A statement prints whole up to about 200 characters
  (`RunReport(false, VariantRec, LanguageCodeFieldNo, TableView, OutputAction::SaveAsPDF,
  false)`, where it was cut at 80 characters inside `OutputAction::SaveA`); a longer one is
  cut at an argument boundary of its first call with `… (+k arguments)`, never inside an
  argument (a quoted string's comma included), and a long `if`/`case`/loop prints its head
  up to the statement inside it. Up to four statements are named while their text stays
  within about 200 characters (m07 now shows three of four). It is never omitted: no
  other line of the card carries a statement's literal arguments.
- **R5: error answers state their boundary** (m04, n04, p08, n01). A witness that ends in
  dependency code counts the guards of the route the analysis replayed through the
  dependency entry to the operation, with their expressions and polarity (m04: `4 guards
  on the route, 0 evaluated`, with `InsertDefaultCustomerSetup`'s two guards; it printed
  `condition not resolved`). When the guards beyond the entry were not analyzed (a routine
  on the route without a statement tree, or no witness through the entry), it says `N
  guards on the analyzed route, k evaluated; guards beyond the dependency entry: not
  analyzed`. A `throws-error` answer about an event subscriber adds `whether it escapes
  <publisher>: not established` before the caller-interception follow-up. prove, explain
  and digest print a row's condition alike: the replayed route's guard count when a route
  was replayed (prove's folded `also` rows and explain's and digest's `COMMIT at` and
  kind-family places included), the class label (`conditional`, `in a loop`, …) only
  where none was; a replayed route with no guard whose class was `condition not resolved`
  says `no guard on the route`. Two evidence rows whose routes share their guards print
  the guards once (`condition: the same guards as the row above (2 rows with them)`).

### Fixed (r3 §7 R3: a pending write in dependency code names its own site)

- **A callers'-context pending-write witness names the write's own site when the write is
  reached through an event, a trigger or an object run** (round-4 p09). The site search
  followed resolved calls only, so p09's `Insert on "My Notifications" (1518)` printed no
  location; it now also searches the sited graph's may-execute edges, entering only
  routines whose cone performs the write (unguided, the search passed 20,000 nodes on
  CDO): `Insert on "My Notifications" (1518) at dep:Base Application:src/Modules/System/
  Notifications/MyNotifications.Table.al:160, inside the call CreateInventoryPick at …:70,
  before the call at …:76`. c06's witness is unchanged. A prove witness ending in
  dependency code named its terminal operation and site before `entered at` only for a
  group's own witness (m04); a `writes-table` answer printed `DB_MODIFY beyond …,
  entered at …` with no site. It now names the asked table's witness's site (`DB_MODIFY
  at dep:Out Base:src/BasePoster.Codeunit.al:68, beyond …`), and its condition is that
  route's guards, never another resource's.

### Added (r3 §7 R1: `assumptionRecords`, additive)

- **Consumer notice: a new structured field, `assumptionRecords`**, a list of
  `{publisher, parameter, universe, subscribersConsidered: [names], rulesOut: [sites]}`
  (sites `file:line`, 1-based, in file then line order). It appears in prove's
  `payload.result` (beside `subscriberAssumptions`), in digest 5.x's
  `entries[].assumptionRecords` (every literal-dead row's assumption) and in the routine
  summary's `commits.literalDead.assumptionRecords` (explain JSON, digest 5.x, impact's
  routine totals). Digest
  `--schema 4` and `--schema 3` documents do not carry it, and `digest_v5::to_v4` drops it
  (`strip_assumption_records`), so a 4.0.0 rebuild of a 5.x document stays exact.
  Consumers reading the existing strings need no change.

### Fixed (context server: a reclaim could free only one artifact kind)

- **An ask is no longer refused as "impossible" while other asks' trees fill the memory
  budget.** Round 4 of output validation ran 60 calls through one `alsem mcp` on CDO;
  call 59 (an `explain` with `callersContext`) failed with `the witness fill needs about
  89 MiB; budget 8192 MiB, resident 8220 MiB, ... retained floor 8220 MiB`. It was not a
  regression of the r3 work: a binary built from `275bdb2d` fails at the same call
  (round 3 ran only the first 50). Each ask keeps the tree of its own roots (one per
  distinct root set, about 40 MiB, up to 290 MiB for a large one); after 58 calls the
  cross-app child held 33 trees, 2.5 GB of measured, evictable bytes. A request held
  its whole store snapshot while it reserved memory for a fill (and its ready snapshot
  while it reserved for its trees). The reclaim that reservation ran evicts by owner
  count, and its first eviction (the witnesses) published a new snapshot, so the held
  one became a second owner of every other value: no tree could go, the retained floor
  read the whole RSS, and the reservation was refused as impossible. The store now
  reserves before it loads the snapshot a fill reads, and a request lets its ready
  snapshot go before its trees' reservation (its needs stay pinned and it loads the
  snapshot again). Measured (release-fast, the 60 calls on one server): before, the
  cross-app child rose to 8.24 GB and call 59 was refused; after, every call answers,
  call 59's reclaim evicts 50 entries (2.3 GB measured) and the RSS falls from 8.30 GB
  to 5.89 GB; the peak after a call is 8.02 GB, the end 5.89 GB. Answers are
  byte-identical to before (every call, `generatedAt` aside). The child's
  `status.memory` now also reports `stored`: the published revision's artifacts by
  kind, with their entries and measured bytes.

### Fixed (round-4 fact check: a test's relation follows its own reaches)

- **A test is a code test when any of its paths reaches the change by code calls**
  (round-4 c28, c21; spec `2026-11-08-output-validation-r3.md` §2 T1). T1 made each
  `reaches` entry `code` when any code path reaches that routine, but a `runFirst` row's
  own `relation`, the ranking ("code paths first"), `result.selection.byRelation`, the
  summary rows and the human headline ("N tests by code calls; M more by UI navigation
  only") still took the relation of the test's shortest path. A test whose shortest path
  opens a page was counted as UI-navigation-only even when its own `reaches` said code.
  On CDO, c28 (the WaitForMailLimit diff, `--tier dependency`) said 107 by code and 337
  by UI navigation only; it now says 365 and 79. c21 (`--tier local`) said 85 and 59, now
  88 and 56. The fact check counted 388/56 and 94/50 from the old `reaches`, which also
  called a test `code` when its only code path went through a hub (`Codeunit.Run` of a
  variable, a record trigger behind `Validate`), a path outside the tier the answer picks.
  - One rule now classifies a test everywhere: `code` when any of its reaches is code,
    `UI navigation` only when every one is (a part with no `reachesAll` keeps its printed
    path's relation). Schemas 1 and 2 take the same rule (their `reachesByNavigationOnly`
    already did).
  - A reach is judged on the answer's tier pick: when a routine's best code path lies
    outside it (via-hub under `--tier local` or `dependency`, via-dependency under
    `--tier local`) and a UI-navigation path inside it reaches the routine, the reach (and
    schema 3's `reaches` entry) is that UI-navigation one. The select part carries the
    best UI-navigation reach beside each code reach (`navigation`) for this. A test outside
    the pick (a via-dependency test counted apart) is judged on its own tier. Without
    this, n02 (a field trigger reached from tests only by opening pages on a local path)
    turned into "6 tests by code calls" whose code paths all ran through hubs.
  - `path` stays the test's shortest. When it opens a page while the test counts as code,
    the row says so (`pathRelation: "UI navigation"`) and carries the code path the
    per-root walk found (`codePath`, `codePathHops`, `codePathTier`; additive, all
    schemas). The human group line prints that code path with its own tier and hops, so
    `first [local, code] …` is never followed by a path that opens a page.
  - Code tests rank by the tier and hops of that code path, the path the answer shows.

### Fixed (round-4 fact check: literal arguments through interfaces, Variants and unresolved sites)

- **An interface variable assigned from a known enum value now reaches only
  that value's implementation** (c15). `ModuleLicense := ModuleType` with
  `ModuleType` bound to `"CDO Module Type"::Essential` dispatched to every
  implementation, so a digest listed a witness through `"CDO Security Module
  License"` that cannot run. The literal reach now tracks interface locals in
  the within-routine flow; at an interface call it keeps only the
  implementation each known enum value names (its `Implementation`, else the
  enum's `DefaultImplementation`; an enum extension value its own). An
  unknown value, or an implementation that names no loaded codeunit, keeps
  every implementation, as before. Enum extensions' values are now lowered
  (`ObjectDecl::enum_values`), and a label written `"Enum Name"::Value`
  (without `Enum::`) binds like `Enum::"Enum Name"::Value` when no variable
  or field has that name.
- **An unresolved call site no route can reach is no longer a gap or a
  blocker** (c15). The interface call at `CDOModuleManager.Codeunit.al:55`,
  reached only under `if ShowError` with every caller passing `false`, was a
  table-answer blocker while the same routine's `Error` was marked
  literal-dead. The unresolved cone now leaves out the sites the literal
  reach rules out from the root, and says once how many: `prove` adds
  `obligations.literalDeadSites` and a `ruled out by literal arguments` line;
  digest and explain add `gaps.literalDead` and the count on the
  `uncertainty:` line. Coverage partial only through such sites counts as
  complete for that root.
- **A `Variant` type test is decided by the argument's static type** (p01).
  `RecordIsTemporary(Rec)` behind `if not VariantRecord.IsRecord then
  Error(…)` was listed as an inherited rule, a caller rule and an
  `ERROR_THROW`. A `Variant` parameter now holds the static type of the
  caller's variable (`Record`, `RecordRef`, `Codeunit`, …; the implicit `Rec`
  included), and `IsRecord`, `IsCodeunit` and the other type tests evaluate
  on it, in the literal reach and in the rules across calls
  (`ConditionAtom::ParamVariantTest`). Text, Code and number types stay
  unknown.
- **A dead row no longer shows a route** (p09). `explain`'s JSON kept a
  `via` for `literalUnreachable` rows that went through a branch the literal
  arguments rule out; it is now left out, as the human text shows none, and a
  crossing's `prefix` is taken only from a row that can run.

### Fixed (round-4 n10: commit entries counted per routine)

- **"dependency routines entered that commit" now counts routines, not crossings**
  (round-4 fact check n10). On CDO, `explain` of `Codeunit "CDO E-Mail Handler"::DocSave`
  said "3 dependency routines entered that commit" for `Sales-Calc. Discount`::OnRun
  (entered once) and `CSC Core`::IsAppActiveOrAskToActivate (entered twice): 2 routines
  at 3 call sites. The ruled-out part ("… dependency routines entered more under literal
  arguments that cannot run") was worse: it counted COMMIT rows, so one crossing with two
  ruled-out COMMIT rows counted twice. Both now count distinct routines and add the call
  sites when there are more of them than routines: `commits: may (1 site; 2 dependency
  routines that commit, entered at 3 call sites; …)`. The parts of that clause are now
  separated by `; `, because a part can hold a comma. A crossing with a live COMMIT row is
  a live entry only, never also a ruled-out one. A count can also go UP: one crossing
  into two routines (CDO `RunReportID`'s insert into `Incoming Document Attachment`
  enters both `Graph Mgt - Inc Doc Attachment`::HandleOnAfterInsert and the table's
  OnInsert) is two routines, so `RunReportID` now says 9 where it said 8 (8 crossings).
  `IssueReminder` now says 6 routines at 7 call sites where it said 7, and 4 ruled-out
  routines where it counted 3 rows. The `commits:` section header of
  `explain` and `digest` uses the same words. JSON: `commits.entryPoints` (shown as
  `commits.dependencyCalls` in schema 5) now counts entry points grouped by target, as
  `entryPoints.count` already did, and `commits.routines` and `commits.callSites` are new;
  `commits.literalDead` gets the same three fields. Every other line that says
  "dependency routines entered" (impact, query effects, the writes-beyond sections, the
  scope line) already counted distinct routines; checked, unchanged.
- **Checked, no change: "owned by this app" already means the table's declaring app.**
  The same fact check read "250 tables (6 owned by this app, …)" as counting Base App
  `Incoming Document Attachment` as owned. It does not: the 6 are the workspace's own
  tables (`CDO E-Mail Log`, `CDO E-Mail Template Header`, `CDO File`, `CDO Queue Entry`,
  `CDO Template Recipient Setup` and `CDO Output Profile Conflict`, the last written only
  beyond `Sales-Calc. Discount`::OnRun). `Incoming Document Attachment` is listed under
  "writes in workspace code" because workspace code inserts it
  (`CDOElectronicDocumentMgt.Codeunit.al:182`), and counts under dependencies. A new
  test pins that ownership follows the table's app id, not where the write runs.

### Fixed (round-4 E2: values inside a routine and publisher `var` parameters)

- **A value computed inside a routine now prunes the branches it cannot take**
  (spec `2026-11-08-output-validation-r3.md` §1 E2, n01). On DO, `CreateAndSendMail`
  takes `UseSMTP` by value, may set it (`if UseHandleDoc then UseSMTP := true`), passes
  it `var` to the publisher `OnBeforeCreateAndSendMailV2` and derives `IsEmailPreview :=
  not UseSMTP`; the COMMIT in `OpenDOMail` runs only under `if IsEmailPreview`. E1 binds
  only parameters that never change, so `prove … may-commit` on the Print/Email All
  action led with that COMMIT, a route the action's arguments (`UseSMTP = true`) cannot
  run. The literal reach has a new flow pass (`engine::l5::literal_flow`):
  - Tracked: locals (starting at their type's default: `false`, `0`, the first Option
    member; an Enum local starts unknown), by-value parameters (from their bound entry
    value), and `var` parameters from their first assignment. Two `var` formals can name
    one actual and a `var` formal can name a global, so a tracked `var` formal becomes
    unknown at a write to another `var` formal, to a global of a compatible type (or a
    name that may be one, or a member), and at any call or database operation. Globals
    are never tracked. A routine with a `with` statement is not tracked.
  - Each statement is evaluated with its incoming state, then its writes apply; a
    condition or assigned value is read after the calls inside it. Values: literals,
    labels (as E1 reads them), other tracked variables, `not`/`and`/`or`, `=`/`<>`/`in`.
    A variable passed to a `var` parameter, to `Evaluate`, `Clear` (and `Get`, `Read`,
    `StartSession`, `SelectToken` and kin), or to a call not resolved is written.
    Feasible branches join; a variable written anywhere in a loop (its counter included)
    is unknown at every read in the loop and after it.
  - A `var` pass to an event publisher keeps the value only when every loaded subscriber
    of the event in this universe is proven unable to change the matching parameter (it
    does not assign it, pass it on `var`, to a call not resolved, or to
    `Evaluate`/`Clear`). A subscriber whose body is not available, a subscription not
    bound to a publisher object, or a model subscriber the event graph could not read
    prevents keeping it.
  - E1's last binding rule is wired: a caller's tracked local (or a parameter it
    changed) binds a callee's Integer, Option, Enum or Boolean parameter.
  On CDO the n01 answer now leads with `CDOLegacyeDocDispatcher.Codeunit.al:229`, a
  COMMIT the action can reach, and says which assumption ruled the `:123` route out.
  The statement tree carries the new in-memory fact `PCFNNode::flow` (never serialized).
- **Answers state the loaded-subscriber assumption where it decides a route.** A row
  ruled out only because a publisher's loaded subscribers keep a value counts in
  prove's strict world, so a `no` that rests on it is labelled `loaded-subscribers`;
  a `yes` whose evidence it changed says so in the `assumptions:` header (`a route is
  ruled out because Codeunit "CDO Events"::OnBeforeCreateAndSendMailV2 has no loaded
  subscriber, so UseSMTP keeps its value`). Explain's commits line adds `assuming …` to
  its literal-dead count.
- **A witness's condition lists the guards on its route.** Prove's `condition:` line
  names each `if`, `case` arm and earlier `if … then exit;` on the printed route, with
  the value the route needs, `evaluated` when the flow knows the guard's value on that
  route and `not evaluated` otherwise (never a class label presented as a guard); the
  headline says how many guards there are and how many were evaluated. A long route
  names its evaluated guards and the innermost others (4 at most) with the full count;
  a route with no guard keeps the effect's class (`in a loop`). A COMMIT row whose
  listed paths all cannot run now gets a searched witness, as a write row did (a COMMIT
  in the root itself now prints `path: <root> (in the routine itself)`).

**Consumer notice (additive JSON, no schema bump):** prove evidence rows gain
`routeGuards` (`routine`, `line`, `condition`, `kind` `if`/`case-arm`/`case-else`,
`mustBe` or `arm`, `evaluated`); prove's `payload.result` gains
`subscriberAssumptions` (`publisher`, `parameter`, `subscribers`, `statement`); explain
rows gain `literalAssumes`, explain's `commits.literalDead` gains `assumes`, and digest
3.x effect rows gain `assumes` on a literal-dead row.

### Fixed (round-4 E1: Integer, Option and Enum literal values)

- **A literal Integer, Option or Enum argument now prunes the branches it cannot take**
  (spec `2026-11-08-output-validation-r3.md` §1 E1, n10). The literal reach
  (`engine::l5::literal_reach`, new submodule `literal_values.rs`) followed only
  Boolean parameters and record tables. On DO, `DocSave` passes
  `OutputAction::SaveAsPDF` (a member of a global `Option` variable) into `RunReport`'s
  Integer parameter, and `RunReportID` reads it in `case OutputActionInt of
  OutputAction::Print: … OutputAction::SaveAsPDF: …`, so `DocSave` was charged with the
  tables and commits that only the Print, e-mail and electronic-document arms reach.
  Now:
  - A parameter is usable when it is by value, of type Integer, BigInteger, Option or
    Enum, never assigned (compound assignment included), never a `for`/`foreach`
    variable, and passed only by value to known routines or to platform methods other
    than `Evaluate` and `Clear`. A call the resolver did not resolve makes it unusable.
  - A call binds it from an integer literal, an option or enum label (`Enum::"X"::Y`,
    `V::Y` on an Option- or Enum-typed parameter, local or global, `Rec.Field::Y` on an
    Enum field), or the caller's own bound parameter. Option labels are ordinals that
    count blank members (`Print,EMailOpen,,,SaveAsPDF`: SaveAsPDF is 4).
  - Each route keeps its own binding; an effect is ruled out only when no route can
    run it.
  - `case P of` arms, the `else`, `if P = L`, `if P <> L`, `if P in [..]` and an `if …
    then exit;` of those prune. An arm is dead only when every label in it resolved and
    none matches. One unresolved label (a range, an expression, another enum's label)
    keeps its arm and the `else` live. A `case` with no `else` guards nothing after it.
  - Enum values compare by (enum name, value name): the syntax tree carries no enum
    value numbers. So an Enum label against an Integer or Option parameter is a
    conversion this does not model, and the label stays unresolved.
  The statement tree carries the new in-memory fact `PCFNNode::value_fact` (never
  serialized). No output schema changes.
- **Explain no longer lists an event as an extension point when its listed paths were
  dropped.** An event row whose every listed path cannot run under the literal
  arguments keeps no path, and explain read that empty path as "raised by the routine
  itself". With E1 this added 60 false `extension point … 0 subscriber(s)` lines to the
  CDO `IssueReminder` explain. A row whose paths were all dropped is no longer one.

### Changed (output validation r3, milestone X3: answers lead with what decides them)

Spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-08-output-validation-r3.md` §3 (H1-H7) and the §5.1 and
§5.2 items that are not about the tests tool.

- **Impact folds the UI-navigation census (H1).** `entries by kind` and `by context` under
  `reached by UI navigation` print only with `detail: true`, for one routine and for each
  routine of several alike (diff mode with `detail: true` used to print none); the population
  line keeps its count, share and nearest entry. The code census is unchanged.
- **Prove's `yes` leads with what decides it (H2).** No `top callees not resolved` / `top
  interface dispatch` lists on a `yes` (the header keeps `analysis partial` and its counts).
  Witnesses rank workspace first, then the least restrictive condition (unconditional before
  conditional, a condition not resolved last), then the shortest path; a witness the literal
  analysis rules out is never one. A group row names its terminal operation and site before
  the boundary (`Insert (implicit error) at dep:…:514, beyond …, entered at …`, `[COMMIT] at
  dep:…, beyond …`), folded rows included. The IsHandled class prints `condition: not
  evaluated (IsHandled pattern)` (in parentheses `IsHandled pattern, not evaluated`), never `guarded-by-IsHandled` (now a replaced word).
- **One negative form for effect questions (H3).** An existing-effects `no` reads `no — no
  <effect> site in the analyzed cone (every candidate decided; static candidates, not an
  observed trace)` (`COMMIT site`, `UI site`, `error site`, `write site on T`, `site raising
  E`; a filtered question names its filter, c27). The must question and the callers' context
  questions keep their own subject; an answer with blockers stays `unknown`.
- **Same-object callees read `this object: Name` (H4)** in explain and impact (was `::Name`).
  A pending-write witness inside a call names the write's own site (found in the callee's
  cone), the call it is inside with that call's location, and the call to the routine with
  its own (c06: `Modify on … at …CDORecipientMgt.Codeunit.al:86, inside the call
  DocOutput.GetRecipientsDescription at …:264, before the call at …:276`).
- **A small digest lookup failure comes back inline (H5).** In the MCP server, a digest whose
  outcome is `ambiguous` or `not-found` and whose whole stdout fits the inline cap is answered
  inline (the CLI's bytes, in the requested format); an `out` still writes a file. The human
  header says `answer: ambiguous — names 2 routines` / `answer: not found` and drops `more:
  … for every effect row`.
- **Lock-edit answers lead with the limit (H7).** With `callersContext`, the `answer:` line
  ends `caller-held locks and their order: not analyzed`, and the callers' block's first line
  is `locks held by callers: not analyzed (no lock facts)`. Above that block the header names
  what `analysis complete` qualifies: `analysis complete (the routine's own cone)` (§5.2, c06).
- **Shorter callers' context cards (A P5).** Above a callers' context block the card's
  `callers:` line and caller rules keep their counts and the rule; names fold behind
  `detail: true`; `through dependency code` names one witness (the JSON keeps three).
- **`starts by:` (A P6, m07).** An explain card of a workspace routine names its first two
  top-level statements, read from its statement tree and its own file, labelled `a start, not
  a summary` (not with `showSource`, whose excerpt shows the first statement).
- **Touches offer the complete write-only call (A P3)** when the record writes are folded:
  `every record-write site (16): alsem_query_touches {"table": "…", "opFamily": "write"}`.
- **Vocabulary (§5.2).** A field's write is a `field assignment` in touches field mode; the
  table-mode read family is `other reads` (`Get` counts under key-relevant); a digest summary
  row's commits say `none observed` / `no (every candidate decided)` (never `no observed`).
- **Typo recovery (§5.2, n06, m08).** An explain or prove `not found` ends with `corrected
  call (the nearest name): …`, the complete call for the first nearest name.
- **query effects envelope summary (A P1).** The MCP summary and its index row carry
  `analysis`, `reasons` and `scopes` (`operations`: one dependency routine deep; `deepWrites`:
  the whole cone), and `beyondWrites.dependencyCalls` (was `entryPoints`).
- **digest index (A P10, §5.2, F top-9).** The tests hand-off is once per index (the index
  file's `testsNext`, `testsNextFor`), not on every row; an index row's `answer` is its
  overall effect (every family) with the writes-only line as `writesAnswer`; `effectsByType`
  leaves the index rows (`effectCounts` is the same map); the envelope summary states the
  test status most rows share once (`testStatus`) and a listed row only where it differs;
  index rows' `summary` names `dependencyCalls`.

**Consumer notice (query 5.0.0 and digest 5.0.0, both unreleased; bc-dev-mcp, ConTinAI):**
- `dependencyClosure` is renamed `dependencyFingerprint` (H6). Its value is unchanged:

- query 5.0.0: `summary.scope` reads `operations-one-routine-deep;
  writes-beyond-dependency-calls-full-cone`; an answer with no operation keeps `summary` as

- digest 5.0.0: an effect's `detail.tempState` uses the §8.1 words (`temporary`, `not

  `entries[].tableAnswers` lists two entries or more carry alike are kept once in

- `--schema 4` and the 5→4 adapters rebuild 4.0.0 exactly (rebuild tests cover each change).

### Changed (output validation r3, X4: tests schema 3 and the round-3 leftovers)

Spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-08-output-validation-r3.md` §2 (T1), §4 (L1–L4),
§5.1 (F top-9's c28 headline) and §5.2 (selectors in tests).

- **Consumer notice — `al-sem.tests` version 3 is the default JSON** (bc-dev-mcp reads
  it). `--schema 2` / MCP `schema: 2` keeps the version 2 document for one release
  (`schema: 1` the version 1 one); `render::v2_of_v3` is the exact rebuild. What
  moves:
  - `changed[]` entries carry `key` (`"c:1"`, `"c:2"`, … in `changed[]` order; unique
    within one document, not stable across calls). `changed[].display` is the routine's
    selector; an entry whose display is not one (a display another routine shares, a
    dependency routine) also carries `selector`. `changed[].nearest.candidate` is new
    (below).
  - A `runFirst` row's `reaches` is one object per reached changed routine, in
    `changed[]` order: `{"changed": "c:3", "hops": 8, "relation": "code"}`, plus
    `"candidate": "runtime-editable"` when the only path is a candidate page path. Each
    object prints on one line. `reachesHops` and `reachesByNavigationOnly` are gone
    (version 2 rebuilds them: the ids in the same order, the hops beside them, the ids
    whose relation is `UI navigation`, absent when none). Each row carries `selector`
    (the test's own display); the envelope summary's test and routine rows do too.
  - `result.selection` carries `reachLimit` and, when some changed routine was past
    it, `notExpanded` (their keys).
  - The relation of a reach changed meaning in every version: `code` when **any** path
    from the test to that changed routine is code (its hops are that path's), `UI
    navigation` only when every path opens a page. Before, it was the shortest path's
    relation, so a test with a short UI path and a longer code path counted as
    navigation-only (schema 2's `reachesByNavigationOnly` now means what its name says).
- **The reach walk is complete for up to 128 changed routines, and says so past it**
  (L4). Each of the first 128 changed routines gets a walk of its own (was 32); the
  rest are named as not expanded (`notExpanded`, a human line `reach per changed
  routine: limit 128 routines; not expanded: …`, and the header's `limits:`), their
  tests counted only where they are the nearest changed routine, and their status still
  comes from a walk of their own, so "not expanded" never reads as "no modeled path".
  Measured on CDO (warm, `release-fast`, the select phase alone, median of 3): before,
  32 roots took 2,116 ms, 64 4,466 ms and 128 7,275 ms (about 65 ms per root walk, and
  each dependency entry's forward cone measured again for every root); now the per-root
  walks run on up to 8 threads and each cone is measured once per call: 32 roots 830
  ms, 64 568 ms, 128 1,083 ms (a shared, loaded machine; noisy). `ALSEM_SELECT_TIMING=1`
  prints the select phase's own time to stderr.
- **c21 on schema 3: 40,297 bytes** (was 52,390), selectors included (the spec's 38.8 KB
  target was measured without them; selectors win). It is under the 40 KiB inline cap,
  so it comes back inline.
- **Candidate page paths are marked** (L3). A test whose every UI path to a changed
  routine takes a page lifecycle into a record trigger the page declares
  non-editable while code may make it editable at runtime keeps relation `UI
  navigation` and carries `candidate: "runtime-editable"` (on the reach and on
  `changed[].nearest`); an established route wins when one exists, and a nearest test
  prefers it. Human text: `UI navigation (candidate)`. `explain`'s potential UI
  surfaces mark such pages `(may be read-only at runtime)` and list them in JSON
  (`mayBeReadOnlyAtRuntime`, additive). Impact already never promoted the edge (it is
  `overRule`).
- **c28's headline counts the UI-navigation codeunits** (F top-9): `337 more by UI
  navigation only in 36 codeunits (…)` instead of 36 codeunit numbers; `groups` and
  `runFirst` in the JSON still list them.

### Fixed (output validation r3, X4: table-extension keys and `runs:`)
