  on the extension's own stub only, so `query touches` table mode left them out of the

  follow the table's own keys, named by the extension (`("No.", "Ext Code"; from
  tableextension "Cust Ext")`, JSON `declaredBy`), resolved against the base table's

### Fixed (round-3 recheck: impact's tests line)

- **The tests left out of the pick are not "not in this filter".** Impact's `tests:`
  line said the tests with a modeled path only via dependency code or a hub "are not
  in this filter", but the filter runs whole codeunits, so a left-out test in the
  same codeunit as a picked one runs too (c20: both nearest tests are in "CDO ABS
  Setup Tests"). It now says they are `outside this pick` and, when there is a
  codeunit filter, `the whole-codeunit filter may still run some of them`. The
  block lists the left-out tests by count only, so the overlap is stated, not
  counted. Reviewer astra's last round-3 item.

### Changed (gates: no second task gate on a tree that already passed)

- **`scripts/merge-and-push` skips its task gate when the merged tree already
  passed.** A whole `scripts/ci-steps task` or `scripts/ci-steps all` that passes on a
  clean work tree (no tracked change, no untracked file outside `.gitignore`, before
  and after the run) writes `<git common dir>/gate-passed/<tree hash>`; the directory is
  shared by every worktree. `merge-and-push` looks up the merged commit's tree there and
  runs the task gate only when no record exists, which is the case whenever master
  moved since the branch gate. Owner decision 2026-11-07: one landing ran the whole
  suite 4-6 times on identical trees.

### Fixed (round-3 fact check: a page's permissions decide what a user runs through it)

Round-3 fact check n09 and m03. A page's lifecycle site into its source table's record
triggers and table events (a user inserting, modifying, renaming, deleting or editing a field
in the page) was added whatever the page declared. So `Page "CDO E-Mail/Print Statement"`
(`DeleteAllowed = false`) was an established UI route to the Customer `OnAfterDeleteEvent`
subscriber (n09's nearest UI entry, `established: true`), and a `TestPage` on `Page "CDO Key
Field Value Part"` (`InsertAllowed = false`) selected 7 tests for the variant entry's
`OnInsert` (m03). New module `program::page_ui`:

- `InsertAllowed = false` blocks insert; `ModifyAllowed = false` modify and rename;
  `DeleteAllowed = false` delete; a field edit (`OnValidate` and the validate events) needs
  insert or modify. No AL method sets these at runtime, so the site is not added.
- `Editable = false` blocks insert, modify, rename and field edits, **not delete** (Microsoft
  Learn: "Do not use `CurrPage.Editable` to prevent users from deleting entries"; Base
  Application's `Customer List` is `Editable = false` and users delete customers there).
  `Page.Editable(true)` can undo it at runtime: a page some code may make editable (a
  `CurrPage.Editable(…)` in the page or an extension of it, a `Page X` variable's
  `Editable(…)`, a part's `CurrPage.<part>.Page.Editable(…)`) keeps the site as a candidate,
  in impact's `overRule` population (relation not established, the path also needs UI
  navigation). A setter whose receiver the declarations do not type makes every
  `Editable = false` block a candidate.
- A property counts only when every `#if` arm writes it literally `false`. A page extension
  cannot declare these properties (they apply to Page and request page only). A
  symbol-only page carries them from its symbols.
- `SourceTableTemporary = true` is unchanged: the table's own triggers still run (on
  temporary records), and its table events carry the temporary record (round 2's guard).
- One answer for every consumer: the facts live on `ObjectNode::page_ui` (pack schema 13),
  `page_ui::page_ui_blocks` reads them from the program graph, and the sited graph (impact,
  tests, the call-graph export, explain's callers' context) and the model
  (`Model::page_ui_blocked`, explain's potential UI surfaces of a table trigger or a field's
  `OnValidate`) both call it.
- Measured on CDO (`bc3ccb18`): n09's nearest UI entry is now `Page "CDO E-Mail/Print
  Statement".action(Action10Action)` (its `RunObject` opens Base Application's `Customer
  Card`, where a user can delete); the UI-navigation population is unchanged (14,528
  ancestors, 11,230 entries: Customer List and Card allow delete), over a hub 5,654 -> 5,649.
  m03 selects 134 tests in 15 codeunits (was 141 in 16): 68943 is gone, 68984 stays (its
  wizard's `Insert(true)`). The call-graph export loses 3,224 edges and gains none: 3,211
  page lifecycle edges from 303 pages (2,632 into `OnValidate`), and 13 edges of the 9
  nodes it now prunes. Every runtime `Editable(…)` setter in the CDO program resolves to a
  page, so `Editable = false` blocks stay certain everywhere else (`Customer List` loses
  its insert, modify, rename and validate edges and keeps delete).

### Fixed (round-3 fact check: witnesses on paths that cannot run)

- **An `Error(..)` behind a literal Boolean argument is no error on that path (m04).**
  `alsem prove 'Codeunit "CDO Subscribers"::OnAfterCreateCustomerFromTemplate' throws-error`
  listed an ERROR_THROW at Continia Core's `CredentialManagement.Codeunit.al:148`, which
  fires only under `if ShowError and not IsClientCredentialValid then Error(..)`, while
  its one route calls `HasValidCredentials(false)`. Two defects stacked:
  - an `Error(..)` statement's statement-tree leaf carries its call-site id, while its
    `error-throw` fact names its `error-call` operation id, so no parameter guard ever
    reached an explicit error, not even `if ShowError then Error(..)`. Each `error-call`
    operation now takes the guard of the call site at the same place
    (`param_guard::alias_error_ops`, the pairing `control_context` already used);
  - only a whole-condition guard (`P`, `not P`, `P = false`) was read. Now the simple
    guards among the operands of an `and` chain guard its THEN branch, and those of an
    `or` chain guard (negated) its ELSE branch and what follows `if … then exit;`
    (`PCFNNode::junction_guards`, in memory only; L2 output unchanged).
  Both the cone's guard (singleton SCCs) and the per-root literal reach (recursive SCCs,
  dependency code included) read these frames, so every reader of literal-dead effects
  (prove, digest, explain, query) moves together. On CDO the answer stays `yes` on the
  two ERROR_IMPLICIT rows; the ERROR_THROW row is gone. `explain DocSave` now counts
  412 tables written (was 415) and errors at 305 places (was 308).
- **A record operation that runs no trigger is no "hub record trigger" (c02).** A
  `RecordRef.Modify();` on a RecordRef opened from a table-number parameter
  (`UpgradeBaseApp.Codeunit.al:2022`) became the hub `h:record:modify`, which expands to
  every table's `OnModify`, so `prove … callers-may-run-noninteractive` printed `[hub
  record trigger (Modify) at …:2022]` and a path into `Table "CAL Test Line"::OnModify`.
  An `Insert`/`Modify`/`Delete`/`DeleteAll`/`ModifyAll` whose RunTrigger is left out or a
  literal `false` runs no trigger of any table. Such a site on a table not resolved now
  gets the bound `OpenBound::RecordEvents` and the hub `h:record-events:<op>` (node
  `hub: "record-events"`, shown as `table events (Modify, no trigger)`), which expands to
  the platform table events only (`OnBefore/OnAfter<Op>Event`, raised whatever the
  RunTrigger). `Rename` and `Validate` take no RunTrigger and keep the trigger hub. Spec
  row added to `2026-10-13-callgraph-export-design.md` §4.5; the `alsem graph` export
  gains the new hub class (additive; a consumer that switches on the hub class, such as
  bc-dev-mcp's parser, should learn `record-events`: not checked from here).

### Fixed (round-3 output validation: test selection)

- **Every changed routine a test reaches (c21).** `runFirst[].reaches` named only the
  changed routine at the end of the test's shortest path, so with 20 changed routines every
  row named `SetSendUsingBCEmailAccount` while its tests also reach 12 more (BCSendMail,
  WaitForMailLimit, …). With up to 32 changed routines (one walk each) `reaches` now lists
  every changed routine the test reaches, in `changed[]` order, with `reachesHops` beside it
  (same order) and `reachesByNavigationOnly` (the ones it reaches only by UI navigation,
  left out when none). Over 32 it stays the shortest path's routine, and
  `result.selection.reachesComplete` says which (`true`/`false`). The select part carries
  `reachesAll` (each root with tier, hops and relation) and `reachesComplete`.
- **Nearest test is relation-aware (c21).** A changed routine's nearest test is the first
  code test (tier, hops), and a UI-navigation test only when no code test reaches it.
  `changed[].nearest.relation` is new (additive), the human `nearest [via-dependency, UI
  navigation]` label and impact's `tests:` line (`nearest … (local, code, 1 hop)`) say it.
  Under `maxTests` each routine takes its nearest test by that test's own path to the
  routine (code before navigation, then tier, hops), so for BCSendMail a code test is
  returned instead of `AttachmentsAssistEdit_OpensAttachmentsPage` (UI navigation only).
- **The capped run target is the returned tests' (round-3 B1).** The envelope summary's
  `runTarget.codeunits` listed the full selection's codeunits (15 on c21) while the 10
  returned tests come from 4. It now lists the returned tests' codeunits, with
  `runTarget.supersetOf: "returnedTests"` (whole codeunits: a superset of them); under a cap
  the full selection's codeunits move to `selectionRunTarget` (`supersetOf:
  "selectedTests"`, with `tests`). **Consumer notice** (bc-dev-mcp and any reader of
  `summary.runTarget`): under a cap the field's meaning changes from "the selection" to "the
  returned tests"; read `selectionRunTarget` for the old value. Uncapped answers are
  unchanged.
- **"Effectively the suite's posting tests" (c07, n02, m03)** came from a cone-size rule,
  not from the tests: on c07 only 28 of the 444 are in posting codeunits. The line now says
  what the rule measured: `[via-dependency] 444 tests in 40 codeunits of the suite's 1,844,
  not listed at this tier — a broad set: each one's path enters dependency code that may run
  more than half of the program; nearest: … ; tier: "dependency" lists them`. The MCP tool
  description no longer promises "not specific to this change".
- **"Each opens a page on the field's table" (n02)** was not computed: the 37 tests open
  Template Card, CDO Setup and Setup Wizard, on other tables. The navigation caveat now names
  the first page each path opens (at most three, then counted) and the step still needed:
  `the first page each path opens: Page "CDO E-Mail Template Card", Page "CDO Setup", Page
  "CDO Setup Wizard"; whether a test edits the field is not established`.

### Fixed (counts and labels the round-3 fact check found)

- **n03, a key on a system field.** A table key may name a system field (Base
  Application's Customer: `key(Key17; SystemModifiedAt)`), which no table declares as a
  `field`. The model dropped that member, so the key had no fields and `query touches`'
  `keys:` line left it out ("+13" for 14 hidden keys). Key members now resolve the five
  system fields to their fixed numbers (SystemId 2000000000 … SystemModifiedBy
  2000000004), the keys line counts every declared key and prints the system field by
  name, and the key-relevant test and `--field` mode's key names read the same names.
  The keys line also stopped adding the keys of a tableextension stub whose id collides
  with the table (G-5).
- **c17, touches callers.** "first touch not the shared one" listed callers whose first
  touch was the shared one, reached through an event subscriber. The callers are now
  grouped by the touch's site; one that reaches the shared touch another way is on its
  own line, `the shared first touch, reached another way (3 callers): … (through an
  event subscriber)`.
- **c18, the reason of an unresolved RecordRef.** The reason named the first `Open` or
  `GetTable` anywhere in the routine. It now names the origins that reach the operation
  (a reaching-definitions walk over the statement tree): `copied by Duplicate() from the
  global RecRefFilter, which SetRecRefFilter sets` at `CDOEMailHandler.Codeunit.al:450`;
  both branches where both reach (`…; or set by GetTable from a record whose table is
  not resolved`).
- **m10, a page run.** explain's `calls:` line showed `Page.RunModal(Page::"X")` as one
  of the page's trigger edges (`Page "X"::OnClosePage`). Object runs are now on their
  own line, `runs: Page "CDO E-Mail Recipients" (RunModal at :105)` (impact's
  `runsLine` beside `callsLine`).
- **m04, prove's headline on a dependency group** names the operation the witness ends
  at and where (`Insert (implicit error) at dep:…:514, beyond Codeunit "CTS-CDN DO Page
  Helpers"::InsertDefaultCustomerSetup, entered at …`); a group's boundary is printed in
  the one display (`Codeunit "CSC Core"::…`).
- **n08/m01, digest on an ambiguous selector** gives the complete follow-up over the
  candidates (`complete call: alsem_digest {"routines": [...]}`, and `summary.next`),
  and a lookup failure's summary carries no effect totals; its payload has no routine
  table or path cap.
- **c02 wording.** "unknown because of 9545 callers that reach it only over a hub"; the
  callers' answer line says "unknown because of"; a fold note says what `detail` adds
  (`--detail lists 2 more; 12 only counted`).
- **c10, explain `--field`'s scope** names whose cone the depth clause is about (`the
  writer card's effects: dependency code: none reached`); the field search itself reads
  dependency bodies and says so on its `searched:` line.

### Changed (round-2 output validation, W4: consistency)

Milestone W4 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-07-output-validation-r2.md` (§4.5 G39–G45,
§4.6). Output only: no engine fact, digest payload fact or resolution changes.

- **"writes" means a record write** (G39, c10, c25): a field's writers are named by the new
  words — `answer: the field is assigned or validated by 1 routine`, `confirmed field writers
  (assignment or validation): 1` (was `confirmed writers`). A caller-dependent write prints
  its operation's own verb: `may delete persistent … records (Delete at …)`, `may insert`,
  `may modify`, `may rename`, and `may change` when the kinds mix (was always `may modify`).
- **not-found and ambiguous answers** (G40, c03, c26, n06, n08): a lookup miss prints its
  failure sentence once, on the `answer:` line (was three copies), with no analysis,
  assumptions, limits, scope or `more:` line; the nearest names or the candidates follow.
  A member-form selector (`Page X.action(SendEMailActio)::OnAction`) is near by its
  member's name, so n06 offers `SendEMailAction` first (it ranked by the trigger name
  every action shares). An ambiguity lists its candidates in source order, says what tells
  them apart (`differs in: a trailing Boolean`, `parameter 3 (Integer or Text)`, `the
  object`, `the number of parameters (7, 9, 11)`) and ends with a complete call in the
  surface's words (`complete call: alsem_explain {"routines": [<both selectors>]}`; prove
  and query effects, which take one routine, print `call 1:`, `call 2:` …), in place of the
  `both: routines: [...]` value. Ambiguity never picks a routine (exit 2, `outcome:
  ambiguous`, unchanged).
- **names residue** (G41): every object name in renderer-owned text and JSON display fields
  goes through r1 §2.1's formatter (AL quoting): the by-object lists of query touches (c18,
  c30, n03) and field mode (c22), explain's `most actions` and `by publisher` (n10), the
  routines' JSON `objectDisplay` (c16, c18, n05), test coverage's `uncovered[].objectDisplay`
  (c25), digest effects' `detail.boundary` (now the crossing's own display, `Codeunit
  "CTS-SYS Azure Blob" (6225924)::Put`, c15, c25), the query touches header (`Table "CDO
  Queue Entry"`, c22, c30), prove's routine line (c27), explain's pending-write witness
  (`may write Table "CDO E-Mail Template Header"`, was `Table 6175283 (app f4b69b55-…)`,
  c06), impact's action entry (`Page "CDO Unhandled".action(StatementsAction)::OnAction`,
  was `Page "CDO Unhandled" action StatementsAction`, n09), the tests JSON root `display`,
  and the `calls:` line (`calls: Codeunit "X"::A (called at :184); ::B (called at :190)`,
  was `Codeunit "X": A (:184); this object: B (:190)`, c05, n09). A query document's
  `firstHop` routine carries its `selector` (c08's two routines without one). Selector
  matching still reads the unquoted owner key, so an unquoted selector resolves as before.
- **one JSON shape per field** (G42, c15, c16): digest `tableAnswers[].tableRef` is prove's
  table object (`{id, name, number, app, appId}`, `null` when the name is no table), in the
  document and in the summary rows; a summary row that shares its answer says
  `sharedWith: "s1"` (was `shared`); summary and index rows carry `effectCounts` (always a
  map) beside `effectsByType`. A blocker with no source site keeps its kind and `site:
  null` (unchanged).
- **legacy words in JSON** (G43, c08, c15): the query envelope summary's `byTempState` keys
  are `temporary` / `not temporary` / `caller-dependent` / `not resolved` (were
  `known(true)` / `known(false)` / `parameter-dependent(…)` / `unknown`); the documents'
  `entryPoints` keys move in query 5.0.0 and digest 5.0.0 (below).
- **`volatile`** (G44, c16): prove and digest documents carry `volatile: ["generatedAt"]`
  beside `deterministic` (`[]` under `--deterministic`, which pins it). Prove 2.11.0
  (filtered 2.12.0), additive.
- **a location says its role** (G45, c29, c30): a witness path's hop location reads
  `(called at …:345)` (`raised at` for an event hop, `operation at` for a table trigger
  hop), was `(…:345)`; query touches' transitive list and `callers: true` list read
  `(defined at …:243)`, was `— …:243`.

#### Schema majors (consumer notice)

Each major keeps the previous document for one release behind `--schema 4` (MCP `schema:
4`); `--schema 3` still writes the 3.x document. `schema: 4` is rebuilt exactly from the 5.0.0
document (`query_v5::to_v4`, `digest_v5::to_v4`, tested on every shape and through the
binary on the fixture).

- **query 5.0.0** (G43, G41): `summary.beyondEntryPoints` → `summary.beyondDependencyCalls`,
  each item's `entryPoint` → `dependencyCall`; `summary.beyondWrites.entryPoints` →
  `dependencyCalls`; `summary.byTable[].beyond[].entryPoint` → `dependencyCall`;
  `down.beyond[].entryPoint` → `dependencyCall`; `down.absence.reasons[].entryPoints` →
  `dependencyCalls` (`result.scope.families.beyondDependencyCalls` is unchanged). Every
  `origin` gains `fileDisplay` (`dep:Base Application:src/…`); `origin.file` keeps its guid
  form. Additive: a `firstHop` routine's `selector`.
- **digest 5.0.0** (G40, G42, G43): `entries[].tableAnswers[]`: `table` (the asked string)
  → `asked`, plus `tableRef` (prove's table object). A `selector-ambiguous` entry of
  `changedRootsDiagnostics` has one `candidates` array of `{selector, display, signature,
  stableId, definedAt}` in source order, in place of the string lists `candidates`,
  `candidateRoutines` and `candidateSelectors`. `entryPoints` → `dependencyCalls` (in
  `entries[].summary` and `summary.commits`, `commits.literalDead`), `entryPoint` →
  `dependencyCall` (`summary.mayWriteTables.mostBeyond`), `throughEntryPoint` →
  `throughDependencyCall` (`effects[].paths[]`). `volatile` (G44). The 4.x document gains
  `tableRef` and `candidateRows` additively, from which 5.0.0 is built.
- **W5 additions to 5.0.0** (G34, G35, G38): query `effects[].tableId` / `tableName` →
  `table: "t:<n>"` into `payload.tables`; every `origin.file` → `"f:<n>"` into
  `payload.files` (`{file, display}`; W4's `origin.fileDisplay` is `display` there);
  `routines[].qualifiedDisplay` left out when derivable (`""`: none);
  `summary.beyondDependencyCalls[].tables[]` → `["t:<n>", <op>…]`;
  `result.scope.families.{reads,locks,validate,writes}.reasons` (constant) left out.
  Digest: hops `[edge, line, to, file?]` and a tail reference `"t:<n>"`; the default JSON is
  one compact line. Both: `dependencies.apps` → `dependencyCount` + `dependencyClosure`.
  `to_v4` rebuilds every 4.0.0 field but `dependencies.apps` (no reconstruction, §4.6);
  `--schema 4` still writes the exact 4.0.0 document.
- **Envelope summaries** (not versioned): query effects `byTempState` keys (above); digest
  rows `asked` + `tableRef` in place of `table: {name}`, `sharedWith` in place of `shared`,
  `effectCounts` beside `effectsByType`.
- **Unchanged**: prove's shapes (2.11.0 / 2.12.0 add `volatile` only), explain
  `al-sem.explain/4`, impact version 1, `al-sem.tests/2`, `alsem graph`.
- **Who must move**: ConTinAI `work/scripts/effects.py` (query rows): read
  `summary.beyondDependencyCalls[].dependencyCall` and `summary.beyondWrites.dependencyCalls`
  (were `beyondEntryPoints[].entryPoint`, `beyondWrites.entryPoints`), resolve
  `effects[].table` and `origin.file` through `payload.tables` / `payload.files` (W5), and
  read beyond table rows as `["t:<n>", <op>…]`; or pass `schema: 4` for one release.
  bc-dev-mcp `risk.ts` / `alsem-writes.ts` (digest and query JSON): `tableAnswers[].asked`
  / `tableRef` (was `table`), `dependencyCalls` / `throughDependencyCall` for the entry-point
  keys, an ambiguity's `candidates[].selector` (was `candidateSelectors`), hop arrays and
  `dependencyCount` in place of `dependencies.apps` (W5); the
  envelope summary's `byTempState` words. al-lsp-for-agents: display strings quote object
  names as AL needs (`Codeunit "CDO Log Management"`), and the `calls:` line reads
  `Object::Routine (called at :N)`; nothing parses them today.

### Changed (round-2 output validation, W3: missing information)

Milestone W3 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-07-output-validation-r2.md` (§3, §2.4's
W3 rows). Output only, except a lazily built index of each record operation's trigger and
table-event edges for the write lines (no engine fact changes).

- **impact names the tables, fields and company context** (G7, c20, n09): when a changed
  routine may write 1 to 3 tables, its effects line names them with explain's evidence —
  `effects: may write CDO Setup (Modify at …:60; the routine assigns "Azure Blob Folder",
  …)` (a table written only beyond a dependency call says so) — and a cone that calls
  `ChangeCompany` adds `target company: not established by this analysis (ChangeCompany at
  …)`. One shared function (`explain::effect_evidence`, its index built once per impact
  run); JSON `effects.evidence` (`tables`, `changeCompany`). Impact's reach and entries are
  unchanged.
- **touches on a table shows each operation family, writes first** (G8, n03, c18, c30):
  the workspace sites print by family — `record writes: 16 sites in 14 routines — Modify 13,
  DeleteAll 1, Insert 1, ModifyAll 1 (temporary records: 2)`, `validations: 5 sites (a
  validation may lead to a write; it is not one)`, `locks:`, `key-relevant`, `reads:`,
  `other operations:` — each with its own count and a share of the 12 samples (record
  writes at most 6; each kind of a family once before a second site of any; key-field
  filters before Gets). JSON `directSites.byFamily`. New input `opFamily: "write"` (CLI
  `--op-family write`, workspace-global list only): every record-write site (Insert,
  Modify, ModifyAll, Delete, DeleteAll, Rename), temporary records included and tagged
  (`up.writeSites[].tempState`). No other value is accepted.
- **touches, smaller items** (G21, G22, G19): an unresolved table names its receiver and
  why (`table: not resolved (RecordRef RecRef: opened from a variable)`; also `set by
  GetTable …`, `passed by the caller`, `not opened in this routine`); the table's keys
  print before the key-relevant line (`keys: primary key "Code"; other keys: …`), which
  says what it does not search (key uses in page and report declarations); an answer from
  a routine says where it is (`defined at …`, so `showSource` shows its first statements).
- **digest hands tests over to the tests tool** (G9, c25): with no test code here and a
  sibling test app found, the human line is `tests: not analyzed here (test app "…" is not
  loaded in this engine) — alsem_tests {"files": […]} selects them`; the summary's
  `testScope.next` and each `not loaded` index row (`testsNext`) carry the call.
- **digest summary rows fit** (G10, c25): each summary row is compact — `index` (its row in
  the result index), `selector`, `analysis`, `testStatus`, `tableAnswers`,
  `observedWrites` and a short `answer`, one clause per effect family with its qualifiers
  (`may write 15 tables (4 owned by this app, 11 by dependencies), 1 write on a table not
  resolved, caller-dependent writes on 1 table (only when the caller's record is not
  temporary); commits: may; UI 2; …; analysis partial (…)`); an answer two rows share is in
  `shared`. Signature, stable id, the full answer and the totals are in the index row. c25's
  20 rows now all fit (7.9 KB of 8 KiB, was 6 of 20); the overflow contract
  (`summaryTruncated`, the complete index) stays.
- **a capped test selection spreads over the changed routines** (G11, c21): under
  `maxTests` each changed routine takes its nearest test first (a test counts once), then
  the global rank fills the rest; the run line describes the returned tests (`codeunits … —
  for the 10 returned tests (144 selected in all)`), the totals stay the full selection's.
- **large inline JSON gets the summary too** (G12, c21): an inline JSON answer over 8 KiB
  carries the envelope `summary` a file answer carries (no index file: the result is
  inline).
- **blockers** (G13, c15, c19): `coverage incomplete` is dropped from the blocker list and
  count when each of its reasons is a listed blocker (interface open world, a call not
  resolved); otherwise it stays. A table answer's `firstBlocker` is the first blocker with a
  site (`site: "file:line"`), else the first with `site: null`. A digest row names its
  written tables when there are 3 or fewer (`observedWrites`).
- **limits agree with the body** (G14, c01, c11, c23): query effects' header `limits:`
  collects the families inventoried one dependency routine deep (`limits: reads, locks and
  validations one dependency routine deep`). A write line in digest and explain says what
  its table events ran: `runs: no OnModify trigger run; table-event subscribers: none in the
  loaded program` (or the triggers and the count of followed subscribers).
- **what runs a table or page trigger** (G4's W3 rows, c10-style cards): a table's
  `OnInsert`/`OnModify`/`OnDelete`/`OnRename` prints `run by: record operations that run it:
  N sites (Insert at … in …)` (the resolver's implicit-trigger edges, so `Insert()` without
  RunTrigger is not listed) and the pages on the table as potential UI surfaces; a page
  trigger a run runs prints the code runs of the page and the actions that open it; any
  other page trigger says it runs while a user works in the page. The `callers:` line stays
  beside it.
- **prove** (G16, G17, n01, n04): a `yes` names its first witness on the answer line (`yes —
  COMMIT at …:229 (in a loop), and 10 more`), workspace sites before dependency ones; an
  implicit error names its operation (`Get (implicit error) at …:50 (in a loop)`); on
  `throws-error` a TryFunction root says `declared TryFunction; interception depends on how
  the caller invokes it`, and every such answer gives `whether a caller traps it: alsem_prove
  {…, "question": "callers-intercept-errors"}`.
- **tests and explain follow-ups** (G18, G20, G23, G60, G62): `then the whole suite: app "…",
  1,844 tests`; the posting-tests line says which input gives their codeunit filter; prove's
  callers'-context answers print `to narrow it:` (the unrecognized guard's site, the
  roots.config.json) before the other blockers; explain's field answer is the field card
  only (`field 60 declared at …`, reference candidates counted per kind, no `no rule`
  lines, complete calls for the field's OnValidate, the writers' cards and the touches
  query); explain's tests line gives the complete `alsem_tests {"routines": […]}` call; a
  query effects answer with no operation says `scope: record operations only; not
  page-context restrictions or non-record effects` (JSON `result.scope.covers`).

### Changed (round-2 output validation, W2: impact records the relation)

Milestone W2 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-07-output-validation-r2.md` (§2.1 engine
part). Replaces W1's interim "relation not recorded" population.

- **impact's reverse walk classifies every path** (G1, c12, c20, n09): impact's visitor sets
  three bits on each walk state from the sites it crosses (`NAV`: a page's lifecycle into a
  trigger a user starts, or an action's `RunObject`; `RULE`: a `TestPage` declaration;
  `CONFIGURED`: a configured-dispatch site). A background start, a test runner or handler,
  an event dispatch and a dispatching builtin on a receiver typed as one object stay code.
  Each node takes its best state in one total order (established code, established UI
  navigation, candidates over configuration, over a rule edge, over a hub; then the better
  tier, then fewer hops), and its witness is that state's. The tier is R0's (`via-hub`,
  then `via-configuration`, `via-dependency`, `local`).
- **impact prints populations, code first**: `reached by code: …` (with `none — no code
  path reaches it` when empty), `reached by UI navigation: …`, `candidates over
  configuration (depends on configuration data not read): …`, `candidates (relation not
  established): over a rule edge <r>, over a hub <b>`. Each established population names
  its tiers, its nearest witness as `[<tier>, <relation>]`, its entries by kind and its
  share of the program's entries; from 90% it says `program-wide: <p>% …` and folds the
  counts; when only the populations together pass 90%, one line says so. `external:` is
  back, for the code population only. A limited walk claims no share and no absence.
  Measured on CDO: c12 reaches no code and 14,527 ancestors by UI navigation (25% of the
  program's 43,793 entries, so not program-wide); c20's subscriber is reached by code from
  Report "Copy Company" and Page Companies' action, and by navigation from the role
  centers; its second routine has 1 code ancestor and no entry. n09's subscriber exits when
  `RunTrigger` is false, and no code deletes a Customer with `RunTrigger` true: its code
  population is the publisher alone, and the deletes come from pages (UI navigation).
- **Cost** (§2.1 targets, the up walk alone, release-fast, CDO): states 1.96× on c12,
  2.60× on c20, 2.61× on n09 (target 2×); walk time 2.6×, 3.3×, 3.5× (target 1.5×; 52 →
  134 ms on c12); scratch and visitor memory about 2.4× (a few MB); process peak memory
  roughly stable. The review (§R2.4, option A) accepted the cost and replaced the relative
  targets with an absolute bar: the whole up part (`walkMs`) at most 250 ms per changed
  routine on c12. Pruning is a later register item.
- **Review landing changes (§R2.4):** a background target codeunit and the `OnRun` it runs
  are one entry (a target with no `OnRun` is counted apart and noted); a page whose
  `RunObject` actions are not named is one entry per page, and the totals say so (JSON
  `entryNotes`, human `entry totals include …`); the scope line says test code is not in
  these callers, the `roots.config` overlay is not applied, and (when there is one) that
  `local` includes dependencies loaded from source folders; `direct code callers: none
  found (test code is not counted; see tests:)`; the ancestor-publishers block leaves the
  human text (JSON keeps `eventPublishers`); JSON `programEntries` is the canonical
  program total (the legacy mask count is gone); a changed routine that is an entry says
  `the changed routine is a page action (an entry itself)`; the `population` label sits
  on the legacy `ancestors` object only; `reached by code: none — no established
  code-path witness in the analyzed graph`.
- **Canonical entries** (§2.1 steps 3-4): one identity per entry for numerator and
  denominator (a routine's `#if` arms as one; a page action as `(object, action)`, whether
  it runs through `OnAction` or `RunObject`; static background targets and action-run
  actions included; one kind per entry by a fixed priority). The program's inventory is
  built once per sited graph. This replaces W1's root-kind mask share.
- **JSON** (`al-sem.impact-up`, additive): `relationRecorded: true`, `byRelation`
  (ancestors and entries), `entriesByKind`, `entriesByContext`, `programEntriesByKind`,
  `programShare`, `nearest`, `firstByKind`, `externalCode`; W1's `declaredEntries` goes
  (it never shipped). The legacy `ancestors` tiers and entry buckets stay. The envelope
  summary's routine rows carry `relationRecorded: true`. The impact base cache moves to
  `cache/impact-base/v2`.
- **R0's visited set is a dense `u64` per node** (Cost (a)): states with consumer bits
  0-7 stay out of the hash set (48 of 64 bits); bits 8 and above keep the hash fallback.
  The r0 goldens do not move.

### Changed (round-2 output validation, W1: what misled)

Milestone W1 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-07-output-validation-r2.md` (§2.1 interim,
§2.2-2.4, §3.9). Output only: no engine walk changes.

- **impact's reach has no relation, and says so** (G1, c12, c20, n09): the reverse walk
  does not record whether a path is a code call, UI navigation, configuration or a hub, but
  the reach printed under tier brackets that read like code paths (`via-dependency 16,749`).
  It now prints as one population: `reached beyond it: 22,378 ancestors by code calls, UI
  navigation, configuration or a hub (relation not recorded by this walk): within the
  workspace 0, through a dependency 16,749, over a hub 5,629`. No bracketed tier on that
  population (the first entry per kind moves behind `detail`, tagged `[relation not
  recorded]`; the ancestor publishers print the plain words). JSON adds
  `relationRecorded: false` and `population` per walk, and the envelope summary's routine
  rows carry `relationRecorded: false`.
- **impact's share of the program** (G1): the fold share divided a bucket sum by a
  distinct count. It now counts the reached nodes whose root kinds hold an entry kind
  against the program's nodes passing the same test, the changed routines left out of both
  (JSON `declaredEntries`: `reached <= program` by construction). From 90% it prints
  `these ancestors hold 99% of the program's declared entries (n of N; pages run by an
  action's RunObject, background targets and roots.config entries are counted on neither
  side); counts by kind folded`; from 50% `broad reach (…; list folded)`; below 50% the
  same `these ancestors hold …` line without the fold (c12, c20 and n09 measure 30% on
  CDO, so the share would otherwise never print there). A limited walk prints no share.
- **impact, smaller W1 items** (G1, G15): the changed routine is no longer listed as its
  own entry (JSON `rootEntryKinds`, `rootUserOrJob` keep its kinds for the ranking); the
  hubs line prints once per answer (the whole change's, with several routines); `external:`
  is not printed (it belongs to a code population this walk does not record; JSON keeps
  it); `reached by code callers: no …` becomes the computed `direct code callers: none
  found`; each routine prints explain's `calls:` line (JSON `callsLine`).
- **tests on a navigation-only selection** (G2, n02): 37 tests whose every witness needs UI
  navigation were headlined `run first`. The headline now says `no modeled code-call
  witness in the selected scope; 37 tests reach this trigger by UI navigation only (each
  opens a page on the field's table; whether the page shows or edits the field is not
  established) — candidates: codeunits …`; with some code paths, `run first: n tests by code
  calls (…); m more by UI navigation only (…)`. Items print both axes (`[local, UI
  navigation]`), the count line adds `by relation: code 0, UI navigation 37`, and JSON
  `result.selection.byRelation` is added.
- **explain's callers are one set** (G3, c06, n10): `callers: 13` left out the page actions
  whose trigger calls the routine directly, while the caller-rule line counted them. Now
  `callers: 43 direct (13 routines and page triggers, 30 page actions); 118 page actions
  reach it in all`, the same set as the caller rules. JSON adds `callers` (`direct`,
  `directRoutines`, `directPageActions`, `pageActionsInAll`); `summary.callers` and
  `reachedFromSummary.actions` keep their meaning.
- **explain says what runs a trigger** (G4's W1 rows, n07, c10, c05): `callers: none` on a
  trigger becomes `run by:`: a field's `OnValidate` by its `Validate` calls (searched and not
  searched stated) and the pages on its table as potential UI surfaces; `OnLookup` and
  `OnAssistEdit` by no code call; a page action `entry point: this action (no code caller)`
  (no longer "reached from" itself); a subscriber by its publisher plus any direct code
  caller. Other table and page triggers print `direct code callers: none found (what runs a
  trigger is not listed for this kind yet)` (W3 lists them). JSON adds `runBy`.

### Fixed (counts and labels the round-2 fact check found)

The round-2 fact check of the output validation (calls c06, c11, c12, c20, n07, n08,
n09) found answers whose count or label did not match their own facts.

- **impact, first entry per kind** (c12, c20): a kind's count adds every legacy bucket of
  that kind (codeunit OnRun = `onrun-codeunit` + `background-start` + …), but its "first"
  witness was the first bucket's first witness: `first codeunit OnRun: Codeunit "Check Gen.
  Jnl. Line. Backgr." (9081) (21 hops)` beside an OnRun bucket that held one at 3 hops. The
  witness is now the nearest over the same buckets (no open site first, then hops).
- **impact, run first** (c20): `codeunits 69000 — a superset: whole codeunits, for the 678
  tests with a modeled path` claimed the codeunits cover every test with a modeled path.
  They cover the tests `runFirst` picked (local paths by default). The line now says
  `a superset of the 1 test picked on a local path; 677 tests have a modeled path only via
  dependency code (446) or via a hub (231) and are not in this filter`. With no local test
  it no longer says "no test with a modeled path" when some reach it through dependency
  code or a hub.
- **"dependency routines entered" counts routines** (c11): one entry point that raises an
  event into three subscribers printed `through 1 dependency routine entered` beside the
  three routines' names. Every line that says "dependency routines entered" (explain,
  digest and query's `writes beyond dependency calls`, the scope line, the header's depth,
  query's answer and touches) now counts distinct routines; JSON adds
  `entryPoints.routines` / `withWritesRoutines` (digest, explain, impact) and
  `beyondWrites.routinesEntered` (query). `entryPoints.count` keeps counting entry points.
- **impact, raised by** (n09): `raised by: 368 event publishers` counted publishers anywhere
  among the routine's ancestors. `raised by:` now lists only the events that raise the
  routine itself (JSON `eventPublishers.direct`, additive), and the ancestor count prints as
  `event publishers among its ancestors: 368`.
- **impact, completeness** (n09): impact said `analysis complete` where explain on the same
  routine said `analysis partial (interface-open-world; … 8 interface calls open world)`.
  Impact's header read only whether the reverse walk ran. Each root's effects now carry
  their digest entry's completeness (`effects.analysis`, the same function explain and
  digest use), the routine's effects line names it, and the header is partial when any
  root's effects are.
- **explain and digest, dependency depth** (n07): `dependency code: none reached` was decided
  from the entry points, which exist only for dependency calls that carry an effect. A cone
  that enters dependency code with no effect beyond it (`CDO File::SetFilename → File
  Management::GetFileName`) said "none reached". The cone walk now counts the dependency
  routines it visits, and the line says `dependency code followed through every resolved
  call (N dependency routines reached; no effect beyond them)`.
- **digest, rootsRequested** (n08): a request naming one ambiguous routine printed
  `rootsRequested: 0`; each routine selector that resolved to none or to several now counts.
- **MCP outcome from the resolution, not the words** (n08, c26): the envelope said `outcome:
  not-found` for an ambiguous selector whose answer went to a file, because the outcome was
  read from the answer's text and a filed answer had none. explain, digest, prove and query
  now put `outcome` in their summary from their structured resolution diagnostics
  (`…-ambiguous` → `ambiguous`, `…-not-found` / `…-unmatched` → `not-found`;
  `result_header::outcome_of_kinds`), impact already did, and the envelope takes it from
  there (`outcome_of_answer`); the words stay only for an answer with no structured outcome.
- **query effects, completeness from its families** (astra M1, c08): `result.scope.analysis`
  said `complete` beside `families.beyondDependencyCalls.blockers {callNotResolved: 21,
  interfaceDispatchOpenWorld: 267}`. A document that reports families is now `partial`
  whenever one has an unresolved call or an open-world dispatch, with one reason per blocker
  set naming its families (`Analysis::of_families`, applied in the shared
  `Header::scope_json`); the human header says the same. The per-family fields stay.
- **explain, caller rules** (c06): `checked by 2 callers; no equivalent check recognized in
  41` missed four callers that run the same `VariantRec.IsRecord` check through
  `HasRecipients → FindEMailTemplateLine`. The walk already looks through calls (unbounded
  but for its 512-deep chain limit); what it missed was the caller side: only a top-level
  call counted before the call site, and those four callers make both calls inside `if
  DOActiveInCompany … if ActionsEnabled`. A step now counts when it runs on every path to
  the site by the routine's statement tree: before it in the same block or a block around
  it, or in the condition of a branch around it. The same rule applies to the rules in force
  at a write. Fixture `tests/fixtures/caller-rule-paths/`.

### Fixed (a Temp Blob stream is not file access)

`TempBlob.CreateOutStream` was a FILE effect (`fileOp: "write-blob"`, ported from al-sem's
`file-blob.ts`). A `Temp Blob` stream is in memory, so `explain`, `digest`, `query
effects`, `prove` and the ordering engine reported memory streams as file I/O. Round-2
fact check n10: `explain --callers-context` on `CDO E-Mail Handler::DocSave` printed "FILE
at …CDOeDocumentsDispatcher.Codeunit.al:286" for `PdfTempBlob.CreateOutStream(WriteStream)`;
c25: digest counted `CDOUniversigneSealService.Codeunit.al:218` `TempBlob.CreateOutStream`
under `kinds.file`.

- One rule, `capability::io::is_file_write_call`, shared by the body's capability
  extractor and the capability cone's (two hand copies before). A FILE write is a method
  of the AL `File` type that writes the server's file system (`Create`, `Copy`,
  `WriteAllText`). Not file I/O: a `Temp Blob` (or the old `TempBlob` table), a BLOB
  field, an `InStream` / `OutStream`; `UploadIntoStream` / `DownloadFromStream` stay
  client file dialogs (`UI_FILE_DIALOG`, G26); a `File Management` call is a call into
  Base Application, whose loaded body reaches the `File` methods. No consumer needs a
  separate in-memory-stream label, so none was added.
- Population (static count): `Temp Blob` `CreateOutStream` calls on the CDO baseline,
  3 in the workspace, 159 in dependency source (Base Application 91, System Application
  57, Continia Delivery Network 11); each was a FILE effect. The CDO renderings moved
  only where a Temp Blob was the whole FILE story: `IssueReminder` FILE effects 6 → 3
  (`file at 4 places` → 1), `RunReportID` 4 → 2 (the `Data Compression` and Temp Blob
  `SendNetworkDocument` entries drop out; entry points 44 → 42). On the fact-check calls,
  n10's `file at 5 places` is now 2 (both real `File` I/O in Base Application's
  `IC Outbox Export`), and c25 holds no FILE effect (total effects 1,788 → 1,780).
- Tests: `tests/cli/cli_temp_blob_not_file.rs` (explain and digest through the binary,
  a `File.Create` as the positive control); `r4_cross_app_program::temp_blob_is_not_file_io`
  now asserts the workspace's own `Temp Blob` call has no FILE fact either.

### Fixed (a named return value of a record type is a record variable)

A procedure's named return value (`procedure P() Ret: Record T`) is a variable of that
routine, scoped like a local. The body walk took only globals, parameters and locals as
record receivers, so `Ret.Get(…)`, `Ret.Insert()` and `Ret."Field" := …` were not record
operations or field accesses: `query touches` left them out, and `explain`, `digest`,
`query effects` and `prove` saw no write on the returned record. Round-2 fact check c30:
`query touches --table "CDO E-Mail Template Header"` answered 199 sites in 121 routines
without `CDOEMailTemplateManagement.Codeunit.al:259` `EMailTemplateHeader.Get(…)` (in
`GetEmailTemplateFromRecord`, `:243`); CDO Send Code missed
`CDOeDocsSendCodeMigration.Codeunit.al:207` and `CDOSetupData.Codeunit.al:650`, and
`CreateDefaulteDocsSendCode`'s `SendCode.Insert()` (`:663`) was no write at all.

- One definition, `ir_walk::named_return_var`, read by the body walk's receiver sets
  (record operations, field accesses, RecordRef receivers), its record variables (a row
  typed to the return type's table, temporary when declared `temporary`) and the
  resolver's site extraction (`extract::routine_rvars`), so the two engines classify the
  same calls as record operations (a named return's `Insert` now raises the table's
  `OnAfterInsertEvent` like a local's). A bare name that is the return value is no longer
  an implicit field access of a same-named field. A return value that shares a parameter's
  or local's name (a compile error) is declined, as `receiver::caller_scope_symbol`
  declines it; a `Rec` return in an object with an implicit `Rec` keeps the implicit row
  (#299).
- Population (static count over the CDO baseline `bc3ccb18` and its dependency source):
  4 workspace routines have a record-typed named return; 3 of them hold 4 operations on it
  (Get 3, Insert 1), and the fourth (`GetSendCode`) only passes it as a `var` receiver; in
  dependency code, 36 routines hold 49 (Continia Delivery Network 28 / 39,
  System Application 6 / 5, Base Application 2 / 5). `aldump --program-call-graph-stats`
  on CDO: edges unchanged (whole program 46,426, primary 21,014), `unknown` 0 → 0.
- The CDO L4 frozen digests moved (re-frozen on `integrate/r2-fixes`, see
  `tests/l4-summary-baseline/README.md`). This fix's part: 136 routines gain the new
  operations through their cones (`GetEmailTemplateFromRecord`'s Get in 117,
  `CreateDefaulteDocsSendCode`'s Get and Insert in 18, `GetOrCreateDefaulteDocsSendCode`'s
  Get in 6), and `CDO Send Code::GetSendCode`'s two `Get`s go from temp state unknown to
  not temporary in 6, where a named return is passed as the `var` receiver. The Temp Blob
  fix moves no DB effect, and the round-2 count fixes move neither digest.
- Tests: `tests/cli/cli_named_return_record.rs` through the binary (query touches counts,
  explain's write and its table-event subscriber write, digest's persistent and temporary
  writes, the scalar return named like a field, the RecordRef return);
  `ir_walk::…::named_return_record_variable_rows` (the clash and `Rec` rules).

### Fixed (table events a temporary record or `RunTrigger = false` cannot run; RecordRef on a literal table)

Found by the round-2 fact check of the 2026-11-06 output validation (calls c02, c12, c20,
n09, n10; `target/tmp/output-validation/round2/factcheck/`).

- **A table-event subscriber that exits first thing no longer runs where the raising site
  proves its guard** (`src/program/table_event_guard.rs`). Business Central raises the
  database trigger events for temporary records and for `RunTrigger = false` too (the
  evidence: 151 of 515 such subscribers in Base Application test `Rec.IsTemporary`, and
  subscribers branch on `RunTrigger`; Microsoft Learn "Event types" and "Performance
  articles for developers": `DeleteAll`/`ModifyAll` raise them once per row). So the edge
  stays, but a subscriber whose leading statements are `if Rec.IsTemporary() then exit;`
  or `if not RunTrigger then exit;` (or an `or` of those two tests, nothing else) runs only
  its guard from a record operation on a record declared `temporary` (a local, a parameter,
  a global, the `Rec` of a page with `SourceTableTemporary = true`, or a record the model
  knows is temporary such as a `TableType = Temporary` table), or one that passes
  `RunTrigger = false` (a literal, or left out). Effects no longer count it (the model's
  table-event edges, so `prove`, `explain`, `digest`, `query`), and paths no longer use it
  (the reverse walk carries the subscriber's guard to its publisher and does not cross a
  raising site that proves it, so `impact`, `tests` and callers' context). Where the site
  does not decide (the caller's record, a computed RunTrigger), the edge stays and is
  marked conditional (the subscription may be skipped). A guard beside a call
  (`if Rec.IsTemporary or Mgt.Disabled() then exit;`) still runs the call (AL evaluates
  every operand) and keeps its edge; `#if` arms count as dead only when every arm has the
  guard. On CDO this removes the impossible `Codeunit "Check Gen. Jnl. Line. Backgr."`
  witness (c12, c20: `TempGenJnlLine.Insert()` into `RunWorkflowOnAfterInsertGeneralJournalLine`),
  n09's paths through `CustomerTemp.DeleteAll()` (its first page trigger was `Page "CDO
  E-Mail/Print Statement"::OnOpenPage`; its first page action, `Page "CDO Unhandled"`, now
  stays only through a user's delete on that `SourceTableTemporary` page, which the page
  lifecycle still allows although the page says `DeleteAllowed = false`), and n10's Office
  Document Handler commit witness. The CDO renderings move with it:
  `IssueReminder`'s `writes-table:Data Exch.` was a false `yes` through `Reminder-Issue`'s
  `TempGenJnlLine` insert into the same Workflow subscriber and is now `unknown` (its
  ratchet rises to 3,400 B for the folded blockers), and its cone loses 6 tables only
  that path wrote. The call-graph JSONL (`alsem graph`)
  keeps the may-execute edge: one publisher node serves every raising site.
- **A local RecordRef bound only to one literal table is that table**
  (`src/program/recordref_table.rs`). `R.Open(Database::"T")` / `R.GetTable(<record of
  T>)`, with `R` a local never assigned, passed on, copied or re-opened on another table:
  `R.Modify()` is T's operation, firing T's triggers by its RunTrigger and T's table
  events, and writing T, instead of the open record hub that reached every table's
  `OnModify` (c02: `UpgradeBaseApp.Codeunit.al:2100` was printed as a hub into `Table "CAL
  Test Line"::OnModify`). CDO: 3 more resolved dependency obligations (table events of
  RecordRef operations now typed), `unknown` stays 0. `derived_only_matches_raw_fold_on_cdo`'s
  pinned recursive-member count 1,027 → 972 (the raw-fold oracle agrees; subscriber self-loops
  65 → 31, recursive SCCs 106 → 71): a guarded subscriber no longer re-raises its own table's
  event for a temporary record.
- **The CDO L4 frozen digests moved** with this fix and the named-return fix above
  (whole program `b696264e…` → `46c002a2…`, reverse index `9576f2c0…` → `ce2b1abf…`;
  attributed per branch in `tests/l4-summary-baseline/README.md`). This fix's part: 1,068
  routines; `CDO File::GetNextEntryNo`'s `RecRef.FindLast()` is typed to CDO File instead
  of `unknown` in the 1,058 routines that reach it, and the 10 routines under `Page "CDO
  E-Mail/Print Statement"`'s `CustomerTemp.DeleteAll()` lose the 10 effects of the two
  guarded Customer `OnAfterDeleteEvent` subscribers.

### Changed (size and dedup: query 4.0.0, digest 4.0.0, tests version 2; output validation V5)

Output validation round 1, milestone V5 (spec
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-output-validation-r1.md` §7, §8.3, §12.1; findings F38,
F40, F41, F44–F47, F83, F84). Large answers repeated the same witness, routine, effect or
path many times. Each shared thing is now stated once and referred to by id; nothing a
reader needs is dropped.

- **Path segments** (§7.5, §7.7, F45; `src/engine/path_segments.rs`): when several printed
  paths share a run of three or more hops, the run prints once. The first path that uses it
  prints `[segment S1: 7 hops]`, a later one `[S1]`, and the hops are listed once under
  `path segments (each [Sn] in a path above stands for these hops):`. A path keeps its own
  last hop, and a hub, guard or location stays on the hop that has it. explain's card,
  digest's per-root card, query effects' `writes beyond` section and both prove renderers
  use it. It replaces the per-section `(in <section>, a path that begins with `… →` begins
  with: …)` line.
- **prove, callers' context** (§7.5, F45, F83): `blocked by:` is one line of counts, the
  kinds that carry an action first, each with its first example (`guard not recognized 1
  (… at …:1433)`, `publication data not loaded 1 (no roots.config.json …)`); `detail`
  lists examples of each kind below it. A hop that enters a hub no longer prints the site
  the hub's `at` already names. The `coverage: the reverse cone, N states over M nodes`
  line left the human text (JSON `states`, `nodes` keep it).
- **`through` only when it names another routine** (F84): query effects and touches drop
  `, through X` when X is the `in` routine.
- **query touches, callers** (§7.1, F38, F39): the first touch the callers share and their
  touch class print once (`shared first touch (952 of 952 callers): …`); then every caller
  once, grouped by object (nearest object first), each with its definition line and hop
  distance, and its own first touch or class only when it differs. The through-dependency
  line says how its populations relate (`the three are disjoint`: the transitive callers,
  the via-dependency callers and the via-configuration candidates). The
  `callers` input and the tool description say exactly that.
- **explain caller rules** (§7.7, F47): more than three callers without the equivalent check
  print as counts by object kind (`no equivalent check recognized in 41 analyzed callers:
  14 page extensions, 5 pages — detail: true lists them`). In `most actions`, a tie the fold
  would cut prints as one count (`6 page objects with 5 each`).
- **impact detail** (§7.6, F46): `detail` is an evidence budget per routine, not ten items
  per list: the direct callers and event publishers with call sites (three each), and the
  nearest entry per tier, each on its own line. The hubs stay three, counted. The
  whole-change block is left out when the change has one routine. "No base given" prints
  once, in the header's assumptions (no longer in the comparison, input and block lines).
- **MCP default inline cap back to 40 KiB** (`MCP_DEFAULT_INLINE_BYTES`; 48 KiB from V3 until
  now): the path segments bring RunReportID's CDO explain card under it (45,374 bytes
  before; the CDO renderings are re-minted in their own commit, which states the sizes).

#### Schema majors (consumer notice)

Each major keeps the previous document for one release behind `--schema` (MCP `schema`),
as digest 2.x did (owner decision 5). §8.3: the word renames of §8.1 that touch these
documents ship in the same major, so a reader sees one break.

- **query 4.0.0** (§7.1, §7.2, F40): every routine a row names is one entry of
  `payload.routines` (`r:<n>` → display, objectDisplay, qualifiedDisplay, signature,
  selector, stableId, definition anchor); rows carry `firstHop: "r:<n>"` and `origin:
  {routine: "r:<n>", file, line, column, role}` (the operation's own place stays on the
  row). `via` is `payload.defaults.via` (its most common value) and a row carries it only
  when it differs. A touches caller's first touch is `"w:<n>"` into `payload.witnesses`.
  Words: `tempState` on an operation row is `temporary` / `not temporary` /
  `caller-dependent (Rec)` / `caller-dependent (parameter N)` (1-based) / `not resolved`;
  `tier` is `via-dependency` / `via-hub` / `via-configuration`; a row on a table not
  resolved has no `tableId` and carries `tableNotResolved` (`RecordRef` or `Record`);
  `isUnknownBucket` is gone. `--schema 3` writes 3.10.0.
- **digest 4.0.0** (§7.3, F41): an effect's intrinsic facts (type, site, table, boundary,
  resources, class, events, crossing) are one entry of `payload.effects` (`e:<n>`); each
  root lists `{effect: "e:<n>", …}` with its own annotations: `status` (literal liveness),
  `detail.tempState` and `detail.resourceCount`, `conditionality`, `provenance`, the paths
  and their counts, `factId`, `guarantees`, `scopedGuarantees`, `refutableGuarantees`. A
  root's liveness and temp state come from its reference, never from the shared row.
  Crossings' boundary, sites and targets are in `payload.crossings` (each root keeps its
  `prefix`); a path's hops may end with `{"tail": "t:<n>"}` into `payload.pathTails`;
  `entries[].unresolved` holds `u:<n>` ids into `payload.unresolvedSites`;
  `payload.defaults.effect` holds the most common `conditionality` and `provenance`.
  `--schema 3` writes 3.3.0; `--schema 2` still writes 2.3.0.
- **`al-sem.tests` version 2** (§7.4, F44): `hidden` is `{"<class>": {reason, channel,
  selectionRelevant, nodes: [{node, nodeId}]}}` (a node whose own value differs keeps it);
  `changed[].nearestTestedCaller` is left out when null; `changed[].status` and
  `runFirst[].tier` are gone (`testStatus`, `pathTier` stay); `byTier` keys and
  `nearest.tier` are the §8.1 tier words; `productionTier: "localApproximate"` is `"local"`
  with `productionApproximate: true`. `--schema 1` writes version 1. impact keeps the
  version 1 tests block inside `al-sem.impact/1` until impact's next major.
- **Unchanged**: `alsem graph` JSONL (`al-sem.callgraph`), prove 2.10.0 / 2.11.0, explain
  `al-sem.explain/4`, impact version 1, the result index `al-sem.result-index/1`.
- **Who must move**: ConTinAI `work/scripts/effects.py` reads query rows' `via`,
  `origin.routine.{stableId, objectDisplay, display}`, `origin.anchor.{file, line}`,
  `tableName`, `isUnknownBucket`, `tempState == "known(true)"`: in 4.0.0 read
  `origin.{file, line}`, join `origin.routine` with `payload.routines`, take `via` from the
  row or `payload.defaults.via`, `tableNotResolved` for the unknown bucket and the new temp
  words (or pass `--schema 3` for one release). bc-dev-mcp reads digest 2.x (pinned to
  1.7.1, `satisfiesPin` refuses another major): when its pin moves, `risk.ts` and
  `alsem-writes.ts` read each root's references and annotations and join them with
  `payload.effects`, `crossings` and `pathTails` (or ask `--schema 3`/`2`); it reads `alsem
  graph`, which is unchanged. al-lsp-for-agents relays engine answers and parses none of
  these documents: no change.
- **Semantic gate** (§12.1): `tests/cli/output_shared_evidence.rs` checks, through the
  binary, that every digest root's entry, every query row's operation location and routine
  and every touches caller's first touch read back through the shared tables equal the 3.x
  document of the same input; `callers_context_tests::shared_witness_tails_print_once_and_
  expand_to_every_hop` checks a prove witness's hops through its segment. Each has a
  discrimination proof.

§7 size targets on CDO (`bc3ccb18`, release-fast, round-1 argv; before → after). Met:
RunReportID's explain card 45,374 → 37,461 B (inline under 40 KiB); IssueReminder's digest
1,347,484 / 798,800 → 1,238,334 / 734,734 B (budget 1,380,000 / 820,000 kept); c21 `hidden`
by class; c23 no repeated `through`; c29 no traversal statistic. Missed, open for the
round-2 reviewers: c17 348,928 → 72,599 B (target 60 KB, all 952 callers listed); c08
1,306,333 → 728,567 B (200 KB); c25 1,259,622 → 643,176 B (300 KB); c02 10,502 → 6,711 B
(3 KB); c20 14,246 → 6,964 B (4 KB). The explain line ratchets rose to 145 / 160 and the byte
ratchets fell to 34,000 / 39,000 (owner decision 2026-11-06: the segment listing adds lines
while removing bytes).
