### Fixed (tests no longer fill /tmp: a cached temp folder was never deleted)

`output_cdo::cdo_answers` kept its CDO dependency-source dump (~12,000 files) in a
`tempfile::TempDir` inside a `static OnceLock`. A `static` is never dropped, so the folder
was never deleted: every `scripts/cdo-gate` run left one in the system temp folder. On
2026-11-06 85 of them had used all of /tmp's inodes (a tmpfs, 1,048,576), and every gate
that created a temp file failed with "No space left on device". `cli_implicit_trigger_cone`
leaked a small fixture the same way (1,284 left). Both now use `process_scratch` (the `cli`
test crate's `main.rs`): a folder per process under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR`, which removes
earlier processes' folders older than six hours. Measured: the CDO anchor check now leaves
/tmp's entry count unchanged and its dump under `target/tmp/process-scratch/`.

### Fixed (explain and prove callers: every caller counted, page runs followed, entries and guard lines right)

Four defects found by fact-checking real tool answers on the CDO baseline (output
validation round 1, calls c06 and c02):

- **`explain` counted page triggers nowhere.** The F16j rule moves a page action's
  `OnAction` trigger from "callers" to "reached from page actions", but it dropped
  every Page/PageExtension trigger, so a page's `OnOpenPage`, `OnAfterGetCurrRecord`,
  `OnAfterGetRecord` or a field's `OnAssistEdit` was in neither number (c06:
  `SetReportSelectionUsage` showed "callers: 2" against 13 non-action callers). Only an
  action's trigger (a row that is some action's `OnAction`) is moved now; every other
  direct caller is a routine caller. `impact`'s `up.callers` (`select::direct_callers`,
  explain's definition, pinned equal by R0-3) changes the same way.
- **`explain`'s "reached from page actions" followed `RunObject` into codeunits only.**
  An action with `RunObject = page X` runs X, so when a run of X reaches the routine (X's
  `OnOpenPage` or another lifecycle trigger, or that of an extension of X), the action
  is counted now (c06: 8 role-center "Customer Statement Journal" actions and
  `CDOUnhandled`'s "Statements" were missing). The trigger set is the resolver's own
  (`run_triggers`), shared through `impact_graph::reverse::run_reaches_trigger`, the
  rule the sited graph's `object_run_reaches` already used. An action reached through
  several triggers counts once. On CDO, `SetReportSelectionUsage` now reads "callers: 13,
  reached from 118 page actions" (was 2 and 38): the 80 new actions are the 9 above, 1
  opening `CDO Customer Card`, and 70 Base App actions (role centers, Customer Card/List)
  opening `Sales Order (List)` / `Sales Invoice (List)`, whose CDO page extensions'
  `OnAfterGetCurrRecord` call it.
- **Every routine of an Install or Upgrade codeunit was an entry.** Only the triggers the
  platform runs are now: `OnInstallAppPerCompany`/`PerDatabase`, and
  `OnCheckPreconditions…`, `OnUpgrade…`, `OnValidateUpgrade…` (per company and per
  database). A helper procedure is reached through the trigger that calls it (c02: a
  `local procedure` was reported as an "upgrade-codeunit entry"; its only call is
  commented out, so it never runs. c02's witnesses go from 47 to 14, upgrade entries from
  35 to 4, install from 3 to 1; the answer stays `unknown`). `analyze` on CDO, both
  scopes, and `--program-call-graph-stats` are unchanged.
- **`prove`'s unrecognized GuiAllowed guard printed the guarded call's line** with wording
  that names the condition (c02: `:1434`, the condition is at `:1433`). It prints the
  condition's own line now.

### Fixed (impact reach and test selection: four over-claims from output-validation round 1)

Measured on the CDO baseline (`bc3ccb18`, release-fast, before = master `6e577c24`).

- **A declared `Page`/`Report`/`XmlPort`/`Query` variable no longer runs its object (c12).**
  The may-execute graph's rule 2 gave every routine of an object a `declaredRunnable` run
  edge to every runnable type its globals (or its own locals) declared. `Document Errors
  Mgt.` declares `Page "Sales Invoice"` and only calls `RunBackgroundCheck()` on it, so its
  empty `OnRun` and `GetNothingToPostErrorMsg` were shown as impossible "first" witnesses.
  Now only a `TestPage`/`TestRequestPage` declaration counts; for the other four kinds the run
  is a site: a typed `.Run()`/`.RunModal()` was already an engine `run` edge, and a call whose
  route is a dispatching builtin that runs an object of kind K (`ReportVar.SaveAsPdf()`,
  `QueryVar.Open()`) on a receiver typed as object X of kind K gets the `declaredRunnable`
  edge to X, from that routine, at that line (`project::Builder::receiver_run`). c12's
  ancestors: 27,718 → 21,088; its first codeunit OnRun is now `CDO Open Unhandled Sales
  Inv.::OnRun`, not `Codeunit 9070::onrun`. `alsem graph` on CDO: 31,099 → 24,872 nodes,
  78,678 → 56,780 edges, `declaredRunnable` 4,690 → 6 (the rest leave by pruning).
  **bc-dev-mcp:** no schema change; fewer edges.
- **An open-site (hub) witness says so in impact's human answer (c20).** `reached from`
  printed `Report.RunModal(<id from Report Selections>)` → `run:report` hub witnesses (JSON
  tier `onlyOpen`) beside real paths. Each list now puts witnesses with a real path first
  (a node reached first over a hub and later by a real path shows the real one), every
  non-local witness carries its tier in the words `tests` uses (`5 hops, only over open
  sites`, `through dependency code`), each entry kind counts its open-only nodes
  (`5,657 page actions (1,046 only over open sites)`), and the JSON entry, external and
  publisher rows gain `onlyOpen` (additive). c20's `"Print" on Page CDO Customer Card`
  witness is no longer among the first ten.
- **A control add-in's event trigger is not reachable from a test (c21).** A page's
  lifecycle edge into a `usercontrol` event trigger (`EditorInitialized`) now has
  `via: "clientEvent"`: only the add-in's JavaScript raises it, so `alsem tests` (and
  impact's test part) does not walk it, while impact keeps it (a real client fires it).
  c21's ten run-first tests no longer go through `EditorInitialized` (now through the page's
  Send action, the labelled over-approximation c28 accepted); c28: 369 → 351 tests in
  34 codeunits. **bc-dev-mcp:** a new, additive `via` value; a test walk over the export
  should skip it (spec 2026-10-13 rule 1).
- **`digest --tests` no longer says "complete" / "no-path" with no test considered (c25).**
  With 0 `[Test]` procedures the block is `partial` (reason `no-test-code`) and each routine
  reads `no-test-code`. The coverage graph still holds the workspace app's own tests only
  (the agent-tasks spec names no single test universe for digest); the sibling test apps the
  same discovery as `alsem tests` finds are named in `testAppsNotLoaded` and add reason
  `test-apps-not-loaded`, in JSON and in the human line. c25 on CDO: `complete` / 20 ×
  `no-path` → `partial: no-test-code, test-apps-not-loaded`, naming `Continia Document
  Output 365 - Test` (1,844 `[Test]` lines).

### Fixed (output validation V1: wrong statements in tool outputs)

Spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-output-validation-r1.md` §1. Each fix has a test
on a hand-stated fixture and a discrimination proof.

- **`query effects` counted reads as writes (F15).** `bucket()` sent every row of a
  caller-dependent temp state to "caller-dependent writes", and every row on a temporary
  record to "temporary records", before it looked at the operation. A `Get` on the
  caller's record was counted as a write (c11: `caller-dependent writes 2 on 1 table` for
  one `Get` and one `Modify`). Both classes are now split by operation family the way the
  physical class is: only a write is a caller-dependent or temporary-record write; a read
  joins `reads` with a note (`Get 2; 1 caller-dependent, 1 on temporary records`), a lock
  joins `locks`, and so on. JSON: those rows leave `summary.callerDependent`,
  `summary.temporary` and `byTable`; query schema 3.6.0.
- **`query effects` numbered one parameter two ways (F16).** The table rows said
  `caller-dependent: parameter 3` (1-based) while the `--all` rows said
  `temp parameter-dependent(2)` (the raw 0-based index). Both now print
  `caller-dependent: parameter 3 (ToPurchaseHeader)`, 1-based with the parameter's name;
  each JSON row adds `parameterPosition` (1-based) and `parameterName`, and `tempState`
  keeps its 0-based form.
- **`impact` exited 2 on a complete answer (F24).** A change that touched no routine
  (c13: 25 object headers) got a full, complete accounting, "0 changed routines", and
  exit code 2, which agents and the MCP envelope read as a failure. It now exits 0. Exit
  2 stays for no answer: a `--routine` selector or `--file` that matched nothing or more
  than one thing, a diff file naming two workspace files, or a diff that does not parse.
- **`impact` without a base called an added routine "signature changed" (F25).** The
  status came from "a changed line falls on the signature", so a routine the diff adds
  (c20) read as a changed signature. Without a base the status now says only what the diff
  shows: `new in this diff` (JSON `addedInDiff`) when the routine's header line is a `+`
  line and no `-` line sits in or at the edges of its span, else `signature lines changed
  in the diff` (`signatureLinesChanged`). The rule is not "every line is a `+` line": git
  aligns a new routine's closing `end;` with the previous routine's old one as context, as
  in c20. `added` and `signature changed` still come from a base comparison's pairing. The
  accounting's per-routine row gains its added-line count and the two facts.
- **`prove`'s callers' context answers printed dependency guids (F5).** Their human text
  named a dependency location `dep:<guid>:path` (c02); the rule is `dep:<app name>:path`,
  which the effects path already applied. The callers' context path now applies the same
  `readable_locations`; the JSON keeps the guid.
- **Test-selection paths printed two overloads alike (F9).** A path passing two
  overloads read `Codeunit CDO E-Mail::Send → Codeunit CDO E-Mail::Send` (c28); agent-tasks
  §12.1 requires each to carry its handle. The sited graph now keeps each local overload's
  short handle (`/1`, `/2[1: Integer]`, `/0#2`), computed by the rule `RollupCx::handle`
  uses (factored into `routine_rollup::overload_short`, which both call), and every
  `alsem tests` / impact test path prints it (`Send/1 → Send/0`), in JSON `path` too.
- **The touches `callers` input was described wrongly (F39).** Its MCP descriptions said
  "without their witnesses", but a caller that touches the table through another branch
  prints its first touch (operation, location, first hop; c17). Both texts now say so.

### Fixed (field writers count bare writes through the implicit record)

`alsem explain --table T --field F` (and d65's writer index, which reads the same
`l5::field_writers::field_writes`) read only qualified writes (`R.F := …`), `Validate` and
`ModifyAll`. A bare `F := …` inside the table's own code, a table extension, a page with
that source table or a `with` body was never a writer, although the body walk records it
(`implicit_field_accesses`) and `alsem query touches --field` already listed it as an
`implicit-access` write. On the CDO baseline (`bc3ccb18`), `CDO Setup."Document Folder"`
answered "0 writer(s)" while its own OnValidate assigns
`"Document Folder" := "Document Folder" + '\'` (`CDOSetup.Table.al:97`); it now answers
1 writer, `Table CDO Setup::OnValidate`, assign at `:97`. `CDO E-Mail Template Header."Document
Folder"` gains its OnValidate (`:363`) beside the two writers it had.

- One definition: `ModelRoutine::field_access_sites()` (qualified then bare accesses) is what
  both `query touches --field` and `field_writes` iterate, so explain's writers and the
  touches' `write` sites are the same sites.
- d65 (opt-in) on CDO: 0 → 2 findings at both `--scope primary` and `--scope all`, both at
  `CDO Merge Table Field::ImportFromXmlNode` (`CDOMergeTableField.Table.al:611`, a bare
  `Table := …`): the other five writers set `Table` through `Validate`, whose OnValidate
  `TestField` rules the import skips. Triaged against source: the skip is real and
  deliberate (the XML import restores exported values field by field without validation),
  an exception d65 is meant to surface, not a bug. The default `alsem analyze` findings did
  not move (2,238 primary, 31,311 all).
- Test: `tests/cli/cli_field_writers.rs` on the new fixture `tests/fixtures/field-writers-implicit`
  (a table trigger, a table procedure, a table extension, a page action, a qualified write;
  a bare read, a shadowing local and another field as controls), through the binary; it also
  checks explain's writer lines equal `query touches`' write lines (the new fixture dir
  bumps `FIXTURE_ROOTS`' `fixtures` count, 58 → 59). Discrimination: reading
  only `field_accesses` again in `field_writes` fails both tests (only `Qualified` is left).

### Fixed (a statement `Insert` / `Modify` / `Delete` / `Rename` / `Find` raises an implicit error)

AL raises a runtime error when a record method declared `[Ok :=] Rec.M(…)` fails and its
Boolean is not consumed. G20's rule (`implicit_error_record_op`) knew this only for
`Get` / `FindFirst` / `FindLast` / `FindSet` and `TestField`, so a bare `Modify();` raised
nothing. On CDO, the digest of a one-line edit adding `Modify();` to `CDO E-Mail Job`'s
"Table No." OnValidate said "UI and errors: none observed"; it now says "errors at 1 place"
(`ERROR_IMPLICIT` at `CDOEMailJob.Table.al:24`). The rule now also covers `Find`, `Insert`,
`Modify`, `Delete` and `Rename` in statement position; `CalcFields` / `CalcSums` stay out
(they fail only on a non-FlowField, a coding error no data state causes), and `DeleteAll`,
`ModifyAll`, `Next`, `Count`, `IsEmpty` return no "ok" Boolean. Consumers: digest and
explain's errors, `prove … throws-error`, impact's error counts, snapshots and
fingerprints. The detectors read `error-throw`, not `error-implicit`: CDO's default
`analyze` findings are unchanged at both scopes, and `--program-call-graph-stats` is
byte-identical.

- **Latent bug fixed with it:** the snapshot's pd arena found a producer's row by
  `(owner, operation id)` alone, first match. One operation can witness two facts (a
  statement `Modify();` is a `modify` table fact and an `error-implicit` fact), and the
  sorted rows put `error-implicit` first, so a parameter-dependent write's states pointed
  at the error fact and its digest effect lost its proof paths, evidence and ordering
  labels (`cli_digest_temp_state`, `cli_implicit_trigger_cone`,
  `cli_event_dispatch_first_hop`, `r3_temp_class_parity_arena` all failed). The same held
  for a statement `Get` on a parameter record since G20. `snapshot_view::is_producer_row`
  (a direct TABLE fact witnessing the operation) is now the one rule for
  `derive_pd_arena` and both view lookups. Discrimination: dropping its `resource_kind ==
  "table"` test fails `r3_temp_class_parity_arena` and `cli_digest_temp_state::a1a`.
- Test: `cli_prove_throws_error::throws_error_sees_statement_record_writes` (a table
  trigger's bare `Modify();`, the c01 shape, and qualified `Insert` / `Modify(true)` /
  `Delete` / `Rename` / `Find`; `exit(T.Insert())`, `if not T.Modify()`, `Ok := T.Delete()`
  and statement `DeleteAll` / `ModifyAll` / `Init` as controls). Discrimination: removing
  the `Modify` arm makes `OnValidate` answer "no" and the test fails.
- Goldens: 300+ digest, fingerprint, snapshot, explain, output, r1a, r3a3, r4f and batch
  goldens gain `error-implicit` facts / `ERROR_IMPLICIT` effects and the counts and hashes
  that follow; where the one-row-per-kind outputs list one site, the new site can become
  the representative and the old one moves to `moreSites`, and an inherited error's
  shortest witness can change. The CDO rendering goldens (`tests/cli-output-goldens/cdo/`,
  re-minted with `CDO_WS` + `REGEN_TEMP_GOLDENS=1`) move the same way: IssueReminder's errors
  194 → 301 places, `UpdateLastUpload` (a statement `Modify` at `CDOTelemetry.Codeunit.al:48`)
  "UI and errors: none observed" → "errors at 1 place"; a dependency entry point can gain a
  real call site its write group had folded into "at least" (`CreateEDocumentLog` at
  `CDOeDocumentsDispatcher.Codeunit.al:308`), and explain's write lines gain "fields … assigns"
  from the field-writers fix. Hand-held oracles moved with them: the l2cap vectors (+4
  facts), the r3a3 vectors (+13), the R3a-3 manifest matrix (+130 direct, +46 inherited),
  the R3a-5 matrix (`totalCrossAppInheritedFacts` 1 → 2) and the split records
  (`REMINT_SPLIT_RECORDS=1`, RECORD explains) and the policy facts oracle
  (`REMINT_POLICY_FACTS_ORACLE=1`: 175 of 455 cases gain facts, none loses one). Hand-written
  tests whose fixtures have a statement write now expect the new error, or filter to table
  effects where the test is about tables (`cli_digest_query_dependencies`,
  `cli_escaped_object_names`, `cli_object_display`, `cli_impact_base`, `cli_prove_cross_app`,
  `no_path_tests`, `wave2_index_tests`, `digest_rule_b_tests`). Where the extra fact would
  break a test's stated precondition, its fixture consumes the Boolean instead
  (`if … then;`): `cli_commit_sites_up_chain` (a crossing with no row), the cone's T3b
  (the set's one entry is the commit) and T7 (G has one fact).
- Observed, not changed: in a dependency group, a resource-less kind (now also this
  error) gets a row at every crossing, also one whose literal argument makes the
  operation unreachable (`wave2_index_tests`' `PostWith(false)` around `if Flag then
  L.Insert();`), because `literal_reach` judges a group by its crossing and resources,
  and a resource-less group has none.

### Fixed (record operations raise their table's platform events: F1)

A record operation raises its table's database trigger events and their subscribers run in
the caller's transaction: `Insert` (`OnBefore/OnAfterInsertEvent`), `Modify`/`ModifyAll`
(`…ModifyEvent`), `Delete`/`DeleteAll` (`…DeleteEvent`), `Rename` (`…RenameEvent`) and
`Validate(F)` (`…ValidateEvent` of `F`), whatever the RunTrigger argument says and on
temporary records too. The engine never followed them: a record operation reached only the
table's own triggers, and none at all for `RunTrigger = false`. So on the CDO baseline
`alsem prove OnAfterCopyPurchaseDocument writes-table:"Purch. Inv. Entity Aggregate"`
answered `no` with complete coverage, though its `Modify(false)` raises Purchase Header
`OnAfterModifyEvent` and the Base Application subscriber `PurchInvAggregator` locks and
writes that table (output validation 2026-11-06, call c11). It was the known gap F1 of the
call-graph export spec, flagged `unraisedPublisher`, not a choice for cost; `prove`'s
`loaded-subscribers` label already claimed the cone followed these subscribers. Design note:
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-db-event-subscribers.md`.

- **Program engine**: a record operation on a resolved table gets a second edge at its site,
  `EdgeKind::TableEvent` under `ObligationId::TableEvent`, to the table's synthetic platform
  publishers of the events it raises (`resolver::resolve_table_events`); their `EventFlow`
  edges carry the subscribers. No site rule applies. A table no loaded app subscribes to gets
  no edge. `Validate` reaches the publisher, which collapses fields; the detector model
  narrows it to the validated field's subscribers.
- **Detector model**: one `DispatchKind::TableEvent` (`table-event`) call edge per model
  subscriber, keyed by the record operation, with the event id and whether the subscription
  may be skipped. The cone, prove, explain, digest and `query effects/touches` follow it
  (facts inherited `via: event-dispatch`); a subscriber's `Rec`/`xRec` take the raising
  operation's temp state. Witness paths show it as an `[event]` hop; a fact's first hop names
  both the operation and the event, so the operation's trigger edges never pass for it.
- **Walkers that leave event fan-out to another detector** (d1, d2's evidence walk, d46,
  d48, d54) skip it as they skip `event-dispatch`; explain's callers and rules do not count a
  table event's subscriber as called (as for integration events).
- **Demand** follows it forward; a dependency routine whose record op raises an event a
  primary routine subscribes to is not a "raiser" for the reverse rule.
- **`alsem graph`**: an `Event` edge with the new `via: "tableEvent"` (additive). A synthetic
  table publisher is flagged `unraisedPublisher` only when no non-hub edge raises it, so test
  selection prints the `platform-table-event` hidden channel only for such a publisher. Holes
  doc row A12: table events now better than altool.
- Not done (design note §6): the global triggers (`OnDatabaseInsert`, `OnGlobalModify`, gap
  F8), table-extension `OnBefore/OnAfter<Op>` triggers (F5), d2/d7 rules for table events, and
  dependency subscribers in a single-app model (no edge, as for dependency triggers).

**Measured on CDO** (`bc3ccb18`, release-fast, before = master `6e577c24`):

- `aldump --program-call-graph-stats`: 98 new `TableEvent` edges, all `resolvedSource`
  (primary 20,916 → 21,014; whole program 46,328 → 46,426); `unknown` 0 → 0.
  `--dependency-bodies-stats`: 431,379 → 437,511 (+6,132, Base Application +5,859);
  `unknown` 0 → 0.
- c11 (`query effects OnAfterCopyPurchaseDocument --all`) now lists writes beyond the
  dependency entry point on 3 tables (Purch. Cr. Memo Entity Buffer, Purch. Inv. Entity
  Aggregate, Purchase Order Entity Buffer) through the three `OnAfterModifyPurchaseHeader`
  subscribers entered at `CDOSubscribers.Codeunit.al:953`. `prove … writes-table:"Purch. Inv.
  Entity Aggregate"`: `yes` (Insert at `PurchInvAggregator.Codeunit.al:519`, Modify at `:517`).
  `prove --closed-world SetCustomerOutputProfile writes-table:"CDO Output Profile
  Conflict"`: `yes` through `OnAfterModifyCustomer_SyncConflict` (`:578`); its coverage is now
  incomplete (the cone reaches Customer's other subscribers and their open calls).
- `alsem analyze --scope primary`: 2,238 → 2,253. d44 20 → 35 (+15): 14 on `CDO
  Telemetry::Company Triggers_OnCompanyOpenCompleted`, whose `JobQueueEntry.Restart()` raises
  Job Queue Entry `OnBeforeModifyEvent`, whose CRM subscriber may start a full sync writing
  the integration tables another `OnCompanyOpenCompleted` subscriber writes (path checked,
  true may-path); 1 on Customer `OnAfterModifyEvent` (`OnAfterModifyCustomer_SyncConflict`
  and Workflow's `RunWorkflowOnCustomerChanged` "both" write CDO Output Profile Conflict,
  but the workflow side reaches it only by modifying Customer again, which re-enters the CDO
  subscriber: a false positive for d44's intent, 1 of 15). d9: the same 24 findings with more
  tables (e.g. `PostAndHandle` 399 → 413 tables before its Commit).
- `alsem analyze --scope all`: 31,311 → 32,454 (1,189 new, 46 gone). All new findings but the
  primary ones above are in dependency code the cross-app model now demands (the subscribers
  of table events the workspace raises and their cones): d14 +615, d44 +186, d43 +171, d35
  +68, d3 +37, d1 +34, smaller others. The 16 d44 findings gone are displaced by the
  per-event cap of 32 (`onafterlogin` 26 → 32, `apisetup` 5 → 32, `oncompanyinitialize`
  2 → 32 findings).
- One `explain` and one `prove` (OnAfterCopyPurchaseDocument), three alternating rounds on a
  host at load 30-340 on 22 cores: user CPU median explain 133 → 131 s, prove 141 → 142 s
  (unchanged within the noise); peak RSS median explain 3.14 → 3.20 GB, prove 2.99 → 3.16 GB;
  wall times too noisy to compare (explain 38-99 s before, 29-49 s after).
- **A new `Witness::Platform`**: the route to a synthetic publisher has no declaration to
  cite; the route-applicability contract (CDO: `route_applicability_zero_violations`, 124
  violations with `Witness::None`) accepts it with `Source`/`Abi` evidence and a `Routine`

- **CDO ratchets moved, re-minted through their documented `REGEN_TEMP_GOLDENS=1` path**:
  the L4 frozen digests (`tests/l4-summary-baseline/cdo-*-digest.txt`: the cone now holds the
  subscribers' effects); the CDO rendering goldens (`tests/cli-output-goldens/cdo/`: e.g.
  `IssueReminder` `writes-table:Data Exch.` goes from `unknown` to `yes` through Reminder-Issue
  → Gen. Journal Line `OnAfterInsertEvent` → Workflow's subscriber → its responses, a may-path
  through the workflow engine; `RunReportID` may-commit gains a 14th effect through Incoming

  `derived_only_matches_raw_fold_on_cdo`'s pinned recursive-member count 784 → 1,027 (the

  1,310,000 / 760,000 bytes (IssueReminder measured 1,293,230 / 744,546), confirmed by the

### Fixed (the macOS build compiles again)

`OutputDir::create` (`src/engine/host/output.rs`) compared `fstat`'s mode, a `u32`, with
`libc::S_IFMT`/`S_IFDIR`, which are `u16` on macOS (`mode_t`). The crate did not compile
there, so the "Build and Deploy Binaries" workflow failed its `build-macos` job on every
master merge from at least 2026-11-03 on and deployed nothing. The constants are now widened
to `u32`. Linux and Windows were unaffected (CI builds only Linux).

### Fixed (a commit's hook no longer lets tests write into the committer's repository)

Git hands its hooks `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and `GIT_PREFIX` (from a worktree,
`GIT_DIR` is absolute), and they beat `git -C <dir>`. The pre-commit hook ran
`check-goldens` with them set, so the impact tests' scratch repositories
(`git -C <tmp> init/add/commit`) became the committer's own: a commit from a worktree
recorded the tests' "fixture"/"base" commits on the branch, replaced its index and set
`core.bare=true` in the shared `.git/config`, which broke the main checkout. Fixed on
both sides:

- `scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit` runs everything it starts (`ci-steps fmt`,
  `check-goldens`) with every variable `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` names removed;
  its own `git` calls keep them. It blocks the commit if it cannot list them.
  `scripts/check-goldens`, `scripts/ci-steps` and `scripts/cdo-gate` drop the same
  variables themselves, for any other caller.
- Every `git` the crate and its tests spawn goes through the new `al_sem::git_env`:
  `git_command()` (the variables removed; used by `alsem impact`'s base and comparison
  code and the golden stamps' `workspace_git_info`) and `scratch_git_command()` (also no
  system or user config, the hook's `GIT_AUTHOR_*` dropped and a fixed identity given
  with `-c`, for a repository the test made). The integration tests reach them through
  `tests/common/git.rs` (`cli_impact`, `cli_impact_base`, `output_cdo`), the lib tests
  directly (`impact::compare_tests`).
- `tests/cli/cli_git_env_isolation.rs` re-runs the test binary with the three variables
  pointing at a sentinel repository and checks its HEAD, commit count, index and config
  are unchanged. With the variable removal deleted it fails (the sentinel's config gains
  the child's write); `git_env`'s own test checks the list covers what the installed git
  names.

### Added (callers through dependency code, v1: the configured-dispatch label)

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-dependency-callers-design.md` (revision 2).

- **Configured dispatch, a site condition.** A catalogued `case` whose arms the engine resolves as
  ordinary static calls, but whose arm runs only when configuration rows select it, now carries
  the site condition `configuredDispatch` (`impact_graph::configured_dispatch`, `sited::CONDITIONS`)
  on the sites of its arm labels, arm bodies and `else` body. The catalog is engine-owned and
  versioned (version 1); its one entry is Base Application's `Workflow Response
  Handling::ExecuteResponse` and its `case WorkflowResponse."Function Name"`, matched on the app id,
  the object, the routine's full signature (each parameter's `var` and type) and the scrutinee
  folded and unquoted. A matched routine with no such case, two of them, or a case sharing a
  source line with other code is a mismatch: nothing is labelled (never the whole body) and the
  reason is reported. The condition is a label: the site's boundary, `via`, confidence and
  `is_code_call_site` are unchanged, and no R0 walk, detector, summary or prove answer reads it.
- **`alsem graph`** exports the condition on the catalogued edges' `conditions` (additive under
  `al-sem.callgraph` v1; documented in the callgraph spec). A consumer may rank a test found only
  through such edges lower; it must not exclude one.
- **`aldump --configured-dispatch-candidates <ws> [--min-arms K]`**, the discovery probe for
  whoever extends the catalog: the catalog's version and status, then every `case` in dependency
  code with at least K (default 12) arms making a code call, with its scrutinee, arm count,
  distinct callees and whether the catalog labels it.
- Fixture `tests/fixtures/dependency-callers` (a dependency carrying Base Application's id, loaded
  from a source folder; its README states each case).

### Added (callers through dependency code, v1: `query touches` up)

- **`query touches --from R --direction up` (or `both`) lists the workspace callers that reach R
  only through dependency code** (`up.throughDependency`, query schema 3.5.0, additive;
  `impact_graph::dep_callers`). Not a new structure: R0's reverse walk over the cross-app sited
  graph restricted to code-call sites (`reverse::CodeCalls`), with a visitor that marks the states
  whose path passed dependency code (an app other than the workspace's, the line `ExecRelation`
  draws, not R0's trust tier: a source-folder dependency counts) and records each state's parent.
  Callers compose across any number of crossings between workspace and dependency code (a caller
  whose path enters the workspace six hops before the root is still listed). The first hop into
  dependency code is any code-call site (a call, an object run, a record operation firing a
  dependency trigger, event dispatch). Each caller has its tier (`code`; or `configured`: reachable
  only through a configured-dispatch site, listed after the others with the catalog entry and
  arm), its hop count, where it enters the workspace, and its witness from the caller to R with
  every dependency routine, every event and each hop's kind and site. The list is disjoint from
  `up.transitiveCallers` and labelled "potential callers by code calls, path feasibility not
  checked"; single-app, and cross-app with no dependency loaded (the no-dependency contract),
  answer `notApplicable: "no dependency code loaded"`; a walk that hits its budget says `limited`. Human
  output: one count line (configured callers' arms by frequency) and the 3 nearest callers, each
  witness folded around where it enters the workspace; `--callers` every caller with a path of
  at most 12 hops plus the 3 nearest whatever their length (the rest counted); `--all`
  everything. The `callers:` line now says "paths through dependency code are listed apart below".
  The job declares the sited graph for this question (the engine host's `reads_sited` pins it).
  `up.relation`, `transitiveCallers` and every other field are unchanged; no detector, summary,
  solver or prove answer reads the walk.
- The MCP `alsem_query_touches` description says so (no parameter changed).
- CDO: the three rendering goldens of `query touches` (human) gain the block; RunReportID's lists
  its 2 code callers, so its size ratchet in `output_cdo` rises from 3,000 to 4,100 bytes (3,683
  measured; still 16 of 20 lines).

### Fixed (impact follow-ups: a warm large range, the `--base` answer's size, overload names)

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-agent-tasks-design.md` §8.12.

- **A warm repeat of a large impact range was refused by the memory budget.** The main part read
  every root's effects at once: a root's witnesses are 5.6-7.9 MiB on CDO, so the 94-file range
  (`bc3ccb18~5..bc3ccb18`, 699 roots) peaked at 4.1 GB of trees over a 5.6 GB resident child,
  past the 8 GiB budget. The main part now STREAMS its effects read (`TreeDemand::stream`,
  `EffectsStream`, `digest_effects_chunks`) above 64 roots, in batches of 32 (`ROOT_BATCH`): one
  batch's witnesses alive at a time, each root's totals and summary kept, its entry dropped. The
  tree's indexes, carrier cache, literal reach with its suffix trees and the finishing sets are
  built once and shared by every batch (`QueryCx`, `LiteralPass`, `FinishCx`). A resident
  revision reserves the trees for one batch and holds that reservation through compute, where the
  batches are read; a one-shot run keeps the tree until compute. Each root's effects equal the
  whole read's (`streamed_effects_equal_one_read`, every r0 dir and the dependency fixtures). CDO
  (`release-fast`, load 25-60): before, the warm repeat was refused (`the trees needs about 4123
  MiB … resident 5549 MiB`); after, cold 238 s, warm 123 s twice (main part 100 s), the window
  peak during the warm range 6.74-6.78 GB (+0.75 GB over the resident child), RSS after 5.99-6.04
  GB, nothing evicted, the one-routine impact 1.1 s and a digest 0.25 s after it.
- **The retained floor counted a request's own artifacts as room.** `update_floor` read every
  evictable artifact (`evictable_bytes`); now only what a reclaim could evict now
  (`Revision::reclaimable_bytes`: not pinned by a request, held by no older snapshot). The
  refused range above held 2.1 GB of its own tree and raw facts, read a floor of 3.5 GB, so the
  reservation was "possible": the reclaim evicted the session's dependency rows (10,881 entries,
  unmeasured, which the next build makes again), the RSS fell only 0.18 GB, and it was refused
  anyway. That was the "eviction does not lower the RSS" of the warm fix: not the allocator, but a
  reclaim that could reach nothing the request did not hold. Such a reservation is now
  impossible at once and evicts nothing.
- **A reclaim hands freed memory back** (`release_alloc::collect_freed`: a forced `mi_collect` on
  every global rayon thread and the caller's, after each artifact kind it evicts;
  `ALSEM_RECLAIM_COLLECT=0` turns it off). Measured on CDO under `--memory-budget 6.5G`: a reclaim
  evicting 871 MB (measured) of unheld artifacts lowered the RSS 0.86 GB by itself and 0.13 GB more
  with the collect (259 ms); without it 861 MB → 0.856 GB. `status` reports the last reclaim
  (`lastReclaim`: entries, measured bytes, RSS before, after the evictions, after the collect).
- **The human answer with `--base` was not bounded** (46.5 KB on CDO with `--no-tests`, over the
  MCP tool's 40 KiB inline cap; one before/after clause alone listed 7 KB of added sites). A
  count change lists its first two sites and counts the rest (`… +N`; every one with `--detail`),
  and the default answer is kept under 38 KiB (`HUMAN_BUDGET`): fewer than `--max-roots`
  routines are shown when their blocks would pass it, the fold saying `… +N routines (the answer
  is kept under 38 KiB: …)`. An explicit `--max-roots` or `--detail` turns the budget off. The
  untracked-file list is capped at five. CDO-gated: the default `--base` answer (tests on) is at
  most 40 KiB.
- **Overloaded callees printed only their name** (`+ calls … CreateSkipLogEntries; - calls …
  CreateSkipLogEntries` on CDO: two overloads). Impact's labels, callers, root lines and deleted
  routines name a routine by the short handle the rest of the output uses (`Name/n`,
  `Name/n[position: type]`, ` [<app>]`, `RollupCx::handle`); summaries carry `handle`, and their
  schema is 2 (a cached base of schema 1 is rebuilt).

### Added (agent tasks, milestone B2: impact before/after against a base)

`alsem impact --base REV` (and `--base REV --diff P`; MCP `alsem_impact` `base`, `base` with
`diff`) builds the comparison base and prints, per changed routine, what its behavior gained and
lost. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-agent-tasks-design.md` §10 (as built: §10.11).

- **The base, materialized** (`engine::impact::base`): `git archive <merge base>:<workspace
  folder>` into a private folder (git is only read), analyzed under TODAY's packages (the base
  part reads the current workspace's package discovery, `--package-root`; a `.git` marker at the
  copy's top stops the ancestor walk). Every answer says `base … analyzed under the current
  dependency environment` with each package file's blake3, the package files both sides read and
  the source dependencies; a change to `app.json`'s dependencies is named and every
  dependency-reaching change is marked unreliable.
- **Semantic effect keys** (`engine::impact::keys`): per routine, a multiset of its own sites by
  key (writes by table, operation and class; commits; errors by label name or static text hash;
  UI; HTTP; files; background tasks; object runs; calls; raised events) from the engine's direct
  capability facts and resolved calls, plus the SET of its cone's effect keys from its digest
  entry, plus its coverage (status, unresolved calls, depth-bounded searches, literal-dead rows,
  undecided write classes). Never positions: a comment above an unchanged `Commit()` is no
  change; a count-preserving table swap shows both tables; sites of one key are paired by
  operation identity in source order, `ambiguous` when that cannot say which.
- **The delta** (`engine::impact::delta`), reusing `alsem diff`'s engine: routine pairing by id,
  else `renames::pair_signature_changes` over both sides' complete inventories (a changed
  parameter list pairs; two overloads changed at once stay deleted + added, with the reason);
  the loss wording through the diff policy's `policy::loss_kind` (a key only the base has is
  "no longer observed", not "removed", when the new side's coverage of that routine is
  incomplete or it writes the table under an undecided class; a call the analyzed body no longer
  makes is removed, and a call to a routine paired by signature is the same call);
  `run_diff_engine` over both sides'
  contract snapshots (`snapshot_full::contract_snapshot`) for the preflight and the schema and
  ABI findings. Deleted routines come with their callers in the base. A `--diff` whose
  pre-images do not match the base is refused with the files named; the current side stands.
- **Lazy per-root base summaries and a bounded cache** (`engine::impact::cache`,
  `engine::impact::before`): the base computes summaries only for the change's roots (both
  sides'); entries live in `~/.al-sem/cache/impact-base/v1/` (`AL_SEM_IMPACT_BASE_CACHE`
  overrides), keyed by the base tree id, the package files' digest, source dependencies, options,
  engine version, grammar commit and summary schema; a header with the payload's blake3, atomic
  publication by rename, at most 10 entries, 64 MB compressed / 256 MB decoded per entry, 256 MB
  in all, 30 days, least recently read first; a bad entry is deleted and rebuilt. `cache prune`
  does not touch it. `--no-base-cache`, `--no-delta` (MCP `delta: false`).
- **Admission for the base child** (`mcp::pool`): over MCP the base part runs in a one-shot child
  that takes a place of the children bound (`--max-children`, so `--total-budget` is never
  oversubscribed): a free place, else the least recently used idle engine child ends (a test
  universe's first), else it waits up to 60 s and the answer says `base not built: …` with the
  rest of the answer intact. While it holds the place, a call for another engine is refused.
- **`al-sem.impact/1`, additive**: `roots[].delta` (pairing, own and cone changes, both sides'
  coverage, `unreliable`), `deleted`, `behavior`, `schemaChanges` (findings, preflight
  diagnostics, what is not computed), `base` (commit, tree, environment, packages read, cache
  status, timings, or `notComputed`). The human answer adds the base line, a `before/after:` line
  per routine (changed behavior ranked first), the deleted routines and the schema findings.

### Added (diff: table key passes)

- `alsem diff` (and impact's schema findings) gains `table-key-added` (info),
  `table-key-removed` (high) and `table-key-fields-changed` (medium), from the schema facts' key
  rows (a key is identified by its position, `<table>#K<n>`, as those rows identify it).

### Added (agent tasks, milestone E2: the debugging slice, several routes)

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-agent-tasks-design.md` §11 (revision 2; review item a15).

- **`alsem prove … --routes N`** (MCP `routes`; 1 to 10, default 1; only with `--match`, `--site`,
  `--op` or `--table`): up to N distinct routes per matching site (the first 20 matching sites),
  fewest hops first, each with its selected guards as in E1. `--routes 1` is E1's answer byte
  for byte. The routes are enumerated over the literal search's **state-transition graph**
  (`engine::l5::literal_reach::routes`: the same search, the same states, every transition it
  examined kept), not over its tree, which keeps one parent per `(routine, known values)` state
  and so loses paths that reconverge. Definitions: a route is a simple path over those states
  (recursion is followed while it changes the known values; a transition back to a state on the
  route is counted, not followed), ending at the first state where the site can run; routes are
  told apart by their sequence of (site, callee); order is fewest hops, then site ids
  (best-first search with the exact distance to the site as its estimate). Caps: the routes
  asked, and 50,000 candidate edges examined per site; cancellation is checked at the first
  edge and every 1,024. Each site says whether the enumeration completed (then every route is
  listed) or which cap fired (`route-cap`, `edge-budget`, `cancelled`, with the partial routes
  left), and the candidate edges it examined and rejected: by literal arguments at the edge's
  own site, by literal arguments further on (no live way on, although the callee reaches the
  site's routine with guards ignored), back to a state on the route, or with a callee that
  cannot reach the site at all. These are counts of edges; no count of ruled-out routes is
  given. An enumeration that listed none falls back to E1's route, labelled so.
- Prove JSON (2.5.0, additive): per matching site `routes` (E1's route shape each) and
  `routeSearch` (`requested`, `listed`, `complete`, `limit`, `edgeBudget`, `edgesExamined`,
  `edgesRejected`, `duplicatePaths`, `partialRoutesLeft`, the definitions); `payload.filter.routes`
  when above 1. E1's `route` stays.
- A resident tree read passes the request's cancellation to the slice and is checked again
  after it, so a stopped enumeration is never answered (`session::read_tree_shared`).

### Added (agent tasks, milestone E1: the debugging slice, narrow)

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-agent-tasks-design.md` §9 (revision 2; astra 15's
honesty parts). Multiple routes (E2) are not in this milestone.

- **Prove filters** (`engine::l5::prove_slice`): `alsem prove … --match <text>` (throws-error),
  `--site <file:line>` (throws-error, writes-table, may-commit, reaches-ui), `--op <kind>`
  (throws-error, writes-table) and `--table <table>` (throws-error); MCP `match`, `site`, `op`,
  `table` on `alsem_prove`. A filter on another question is refused with one text, before the
  workspace is read. The answer is about the matching SITES: each direct fact of the question's
  kinds whose routine the root's guarded search (literal arguments followed) reaches where the
  site can run. Each matching site prints its location, its operation, the error message text
  (a literal, a Label's or TextConst's value, `%1` kept, with the Label's name; "message not
  known" for a variable, an expression, an ErrorInfo or the platform's own message), one
  representative route from the root (shortest first) and, per site on the route, the 2 innermost
  enclosing conditions with their polarity (then/else, case arm, case else), labelled "selected
  context, not all necessary conditions" with the count left out (`guards shown: k of n`). A
  `while`/`for`/`foreach` condition is a loop-entry condition, a `repeat … until` condition a
  continuation condition. Every answer says "static candidates, not an observed trace".
- **Filtered verdicts.** `yes`: a matching site is reachable. `no`: none matches, every reachable
  site is decided against the filter, the root's search completed and the cone's obligations are
  clear. `unknown` otherwise, with one blocker per reason: `message-unknown` (no static text: an
  unknown message never supports "no error matching this text"), `message-placeholders` (a text
  that did not match but has `%1` values that may hold it), `message-platform-wrapped` (a
  `FieldError` text, which the platform wraps), `temp-state-depends-on-caller`,
  `unknown-table-write`, `position-unknown`, `operation-unknown`, `table-unknown`, `no-site`,
  `slice-search-capped`, `slice-found-no-site`. An implicit error (TestField, an unguarded Get, …)
  matches `--match` only by its kind word, and says so.
- **A new gated fact: the sites' guard arms** (`program::body::site_guards`,
  `ModelRoutine::site_guards`): per routine, each `if`/`case`/loop block with its condition text
  (whitespace folded, at most 120 characters). Built at assembly behind
  `AssemblyNeeds::site_guards` / `ViewNeeds::site_guards`; only `alsem prove` with a filter
  declares it (`ViewNeeds::PROVE_SLICE`, with the rules for the message text). Every other
  command, and an unfiltered prove, builds none; reading it unbuilt panics "site guards not
  built: declare ViewNeeds::site_guards". The resident session widens its needs for it as for
  the rules. The slice is a level-3 read of prove's tree (`TreeDemand::slice`,
  `session::prove_slice_plan`).
- Prove JSON: a filtered document is schema **2.5.0** (additive: `payload.filter`,
  `payload.slice` with counts and the first 10 undecided sites per kind, evidence rows that are
  the matching sites with `message`, `route` (hops, witness, per-site `guards`,
  `enclosingTotal`, `guardsShown`, `guardsTotal`, `guardsAre`) and `evidence.{file, line}` as
  before). An unfiltered document is byte-identical (2.4.0). The MCP instructions' "which tool"
  line names the filters.

### Fixed (F3, the effect side: every background start, named)

- **`CurrPage.EnqueueBackgroundTask` is a `BACKGROUND_TASK` effect.** The `start` capability fact
  (both extractors: the cone's `direct_facts_for_routine` and the L2 `extract_background`) now reads
  `program::resolve::background::STARTERS`, the table F3's edges use, instead of its own list of
  three; the page task had no fact, so explain, digest and prove never saw it.
- **explain's and digest's `BACKGROUND_TASK` line names what the start starts**: `BACKGROUND_TASK at
  ws:src/a.al:12 (unconditional-on-success), starts Codeunit BS Job`, and for a task with a failure
  codeunit `…, starts Codeunit BS Job, on failure Codeunit BS Fail`. A literal is named by the object
  the program engine resolved it to (a number by its declared name); a codeunit that is not a
  literal is `a codeunit decided at run time`; a literal the start's edge reaches no routine of (an
  id no object declares, a codeunit without `OnRun`) keeps its spelling (`Codeunit 59999`); a
  failure codeunit of `0` is none. The model keeps the names in a side table,
  `ResolvedCalls::background_starts` (call-site id → `BackgroundStart`), filled by the adapter from
  each start's `ObligationId::Background` edge; the model's edges still never follow a start. The
  digest JSON carries it as the effect's `detail.starts` (CLI layer only, like `tempState`: no
  `factId`, dedupe key or fingerprint moves).
- **CDO** (release-fast, 2026-11-05): the workspace has no background start; `alsem analyze` findings
  identical at `--scope primary` (2,240) and `--scope all` (31,313), call-graph statistics as above.

### Fixed (an integer object id runs its object)

- **`Codeunit.Run(50000)` resolves as `Codeunit.Run(Codeunit::50000)` does.** A positive integer
  literal as a run's first argument is the object's id: `Codeunit.Run(N)` and `Codeunit.Run(N,
  Rec)`, `Page.Run`/`RunModal(N…)`, `Report.Run`/`RunModal(N…)`, `XmlPort.Run`/`Import`/`Export(N…)`
  now reach the entry triggers of the object the caller's app sees with that id
  (`ResolveIndex::object_by_number`, the same app-scoped lookup `Codeunit::N` uses). Before, the
  extractor read only a `Codeunit::…` reference as static and left an integer `DynamicOpen`
  (`honestDynamic`). An id no object declares is `ObjectNotInGraph` (unknown, with its reason), as
  a missing `Codeunit::N` is; `0`, a variable and an expression stay dynamic, and `Page.Run(0, Rec)`
  still opens the table's lookup page. The body facts' `ObjectRun` target (`ir_walk`) reads the
  same shapes, so the model names the same object. Transpiled dependency bodies write runs this
  way. (`Query` has no run method, so these four kinds are every run.)
- **CDO** (`/home/sshadows/Projects/DO-cdo-baseline/Cloud`, release-fast, 2026-11-05): the workspace
  has no integer run (`--program-call-graph-stats` unchanged: 46,328 edges, 16 `honestDynamic`, 0

  unknown before and after; all five are Continia Delivery Network's
  `CTS-CDN Document Output Mgt.` (`Codeunit.Run(6086250, SalesHeader)` and four more, each now the

### Added (callgraph gap F3: static background starts are edges)

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-callgraph-export-design.md` §9 (F3) and §16.1.

- **A static background start gets its own engine edge.** `StartSession(S, Codeunit::X)`,
  `Session.StartSession(S, 50100)`, `TaskScheduler.CreateTask(Codeunit::X, Codeunit::F)` and
  `CurrPage.EnqueueBackgroundTask(T, Codeunit::X)` keep their catalog `Call` edge and get an
  `EdgeKind::BackgroundStart` edge (own obligation, `ObligationId::Background`) to each literal
  codeunit's `OnRun`, resolved as `Codeunit.Run(Codeunit::X)` is. A literal is `Codeunit::X`,
  `Codeunit::"X"` or a positive integer (the transpiled bodies of symbol packages spell every start
  that way). The site is classified by the catalog id its call resolved to
  (`program::resolve::background`), so a procedure named `StartSession` is no start. The failure
  codeunit's route carries the new `Condition::OnTaskFailure` (does not fire by default; a failure
  codeunit of `0` is none). A non-literal codeunit gets no edge and keeps the open `Run{codeunit}`
  bound with its reason; a literal-only site drops that bound. The bare `StartSession(S, Id)` had
  no bound at all (its catalog id was not a dispatching builtin) and now has one.
- **An execution boundary in the sited graph and the export.** The edge projects to a `Run` of the
  started codeunit's object with the additive `via: "backgroundStart"` (and `conditions:
  ["onTaskFailure"]`, `OverApprox`, for a failure codeunit), at a new `Boundary::Background` site:
  a new session or task, no shared transaction, no UI, errors do not come back. Schema stays
  `al-sem.callgraph` v1 (new `via` and condition values are additive, spec §4.2).
- **R0: the started codeunit is a `background-start` entry, from the graph** (the node a
  `Background` site enters). The walk itself does not stop there; consumers decide.
- **Milestone A's background-start stop is now reachable.** `callers-*` questions get the
  `background-start` entry from R0 (placed at the start site) instead of their own body-fact
  lookup; a start whose codeunit is not a literal still blocks `no`
  (`unresolved-background-target`). The stop's discrimination proof now fails when the stop is
  removed (`a_trap_above_a_background_start_does_not_intercept`).
- **LSP**: the started `OnRun`'s incoming calls list the starter.

### Changed (F3)

- **Effects beyond a background start are never the starter's.** The model's calls (and so the
  cone, `prove`, `explain`, `digest` and every detector) do not carry the start's edge: the start
  stays one `BACKGROUND_TASK` effect at its site, and the started codeunit's commits, UI and errors
  are not counted as the caller's (pinned by
  `a_started_codeunits_commit_ui_and_error_are_not_the_starters`). Cross-app demand does not follow
  the edge either. explain's `callers:` line does not count a starter (`direct_callers`); the
  reverse walks (tests and page actions that reach a routine) do pass through it.
- The compiler-graph oracle leaves the start's edge out (altool has none, holes doc A21).
- **CDO** (`/home/sshadows/Projects/DO-cdo-baseline/Cloud`, release-fast, 2026-11-05): the workspace
  has no background start, so `--program-call-graph-stats` is unchanged (46,328 edges, 0 unknown,
  coverage holds). Dependency bodies: 431,321 → 431,379 edges (+58, all `resolvedSource`), 0
  unknown before and after. `alsem analyze`: 2,240 findings at `--scope primary` and 31,313 at
  `--scope all`, the same fingerprints before and after. `alsem graph`: 125 → 82 callers of
  `h:run:codeunit`, 21 `backgroundStart` edges after pruning; 31,265 → 31,095 nodes and 78,936 →
  78,665 edges (the hub no longer keeps every codeunit on a path).

### Added (agent tasks, milestone A: adding an effect)

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-agent-tasks-design.md` §6 (revision 2; astra 3/4/5, Fable
2/14; owner decisions §13.2).

- **Three prove questions about a routine's callers' context** (`engine::l5::callers_context`),
  for an agent about to ADD a `Commit()`, an `Error(...)` or UI to routine R. Each walks R's reverse
  cone over the sited graph (R0's `walk_multi`) with its own visitor, whose `step` evaluates every
  reverse edge `caller C --site s--> R'` against C's body facts in the model (the site found by its
  anchor). Answers are `yes` (a path exists), `no` (the whole cone seen, nothing blocks it) or
  `unknown` with the blocking reasons; never "safe".
  - `callers-have-pending-writes`: may a caller have a database write pending (written, not yet
    committed) when R runs? Per edge, `pending_writes::pending_before_report` (the same tree walk
    the transaction spans use, now also reporting whether it fell back to the whole body and
    whether a `Commit()` statement on the way cleared what came before) gives the sites of C that
    may run before s: earlier statements, conditions, only the branch holding s, a loop's whole
    body. A physical write among them (its own, or a callee's cone write, a `Codeunit.Run` target's
    lifecycle routines included) is a `pending-write` witness. A `Commit()` before s, a checked
    `Codeunit.Run` (its own transaction) and a background start (a new session) stop the walk
    above C. A trigger of a write on a physical record is an `inside-write` witness; on a temporary
    record it proves nothing. Above a publisher, the other subscribers' cone writes count (they run
    in an unknown order). A commit inside a callee does not clear. A TryFunction caller blocks `no`
    on its own row (`tryfunction-caller`; owner decision). A caller whose order is not known (no
    tree, s not found, no body facts in the model) blocks `no` (`order-unknown`); an unresolved
    call before s gives `effects-incomplete`. `CommitBehavior` attributes and
    `InherentCommitBehavior` objects on the paths are printed.
  - `callers-intercept-errors`: may a caller turn an error raised in R into something else? The
    edge into a TryFunction whose result is used, or a checked `Codeunit.Run`, is
    `catch-and-return-false` (the text says a TryFunction does not roll back database changes,
    and that a checked run's own transaction is rolled back); a TryFunction called as a statement
    is an ordinary call and is listed as not intercepted; an error raised in a call's arguments is
    the caller's (a different edge). `asserterror` intercepts; `[ErrorBehavior(ErrorBehavior::
    Collect)]` is `collectible` (collectible errors only; the walk goes on). A background start
    ends a path. The entries reached with no trap are counted by kind.
  - `callers-may-run-noninteractive`: may R run where no user answers UI, whatever the UI kind?
    Witnesses are entries no user answers: API pages, web-service and job-queue roots
    (`roots.config.json`), install and upgrade codeunits, and the OnRun of a codeunit a literal
    `StartSession`/`TaskScheduler.CreateTask`/`CurrPage.EnqueueBackgroundTask` starts (the
    capability `start` facts' call sites, not an edge; the run below a start is non-interactive
    whatever started it). A call in the then-branch of `if GuiAllowed` (or a conjunction with it)
    is not followed, the else branch is; any other condition that mentions GuiAllowed keeps the
    witness and is listed (`unrecognized-guard`). Guards come from M0-3's guard enrichment
    (re-parsing the revision's pinned bytes, only for callers that mention GuiAllowed), so the
    model gains no per-site fact (A-15: 0 bytes). A missing `roots.config.json`
    (`publication-unknown`), a `WebServicePublish.xml` in the workspace (`unread-publication-
    file`) and any background start with a non-literal codeunit (`unresolved-background-target`)
    block `no`. Tests are counted apart, never witnesses.
  - Every question: hidden callers, `OnlyOpen` ancestors (hubs), external ancestors (public,
    protected, or internal with `internalsVisibleTo` friends) and a walk limit block `no`. **A
    witness whose path uses an open site** (a hub's stand-in for "any page run", "any call of this
    name") is listed (`evidenceThroughOpenSites`) but makes no `yes` alone: the answer is then
    `unknown — witnesses only through open sites`. **The walk stops at a page's lifecycle edge**
    (`stopped: page-event`): an open page runs its actions and triggers on later user events,
    after the code that opened it finished, so the opener's pending writes and error traps are not
    around them (found on CDO: `IssueReminder`'s first witness was a write before
    `Contact::ShowResultForCustomer` opened the Customer Card that holds the reminder action).
  - Known limit: the sited graph has no edge from a `StartSession`/`CreateTask` site to its
    target yet (callgraph F3), so the walk's stop at a background start is not reachable on
    today's graphs; its discrimination proof stayed green and the fixture pins the outcome
    instead (no trap above the start; the target is a `background-start` entry).
    `--no-dependents` (MCP `assumeNoDependents`) turns external callers off and says so under
    `assumptions`; it is its own flag, not `--closed-world`. The questions read the cross-app
    program and refuse `--single-app`.
- **`alsem explain --callers-context`** (MCP `callersContext: true`): each card gains a "callers'
  context" section with the three answers in one line each (before `next:`), and its JSON a
  `callersContext` object. **Only when asked**: the section needs the sited graph, which M0 made
  lazy (about a second per refresh on CDO cross-app), and the detector run's summaries, which a
  default explain does not run; printing it whenever a resident revision happens to hold the graph
  would make a resident answer differ from the CLI's.
- `engine::resident::guards::site_guards_cached` with a `GuardCache`: the units' pinned texts and
  parses, and the packages' embedded sources listed once per answer, not once per site. Before
  it, `callers-may-run-noninteractive` on CDO `RunReportID` took 229 s (every Base Application
  caller that mentions GuiAllowed re-listed every package's sources); after, 20.5 s cold CLI.
- A model job can now walk the sited graph beside the model (`ViewNeeds::MODEL_SITED`,
  `ViewCx::sited`): one-shot, the graph is built off the lent program and kept for the compute;
  resident, the revision's `ArtifactKey::Sited` is served, and the engine host pins with
  `pin_sited` for a command that reads it.

- **Measured on the CDO baseline** (`bc3ccb18`, cross-app, `release-fast`, 2026-11-05; the
  machine was shared, so upper bounds).
  - Cold CLI, each question alone: 18.8-20.7 s and 3.16-3.21 GB peak for `RunReportID`,
    `IssueReminder`, `UpdateLastUpload`, `TryRunReport`, `RunEMailJobs` (one outlier, 32 s), against
    28.3 s / 3.14 GB for `prove RunReportID may-commit` (the callers' questions run no digest
    tree; they add the sited graph and the walk). `explain RunReportID`: 27.2 s; with
    `--callers-context` 32.2 s (+5 s: the detector run, the sited graph, three walks).
  - Resident (`alsem mcp`, one session): `may-commit` cold 29.9 s; the first callers' question
    8.2 s (`pin_sited` rebuilds the revision once with its sited graph); then 0.09-0.14 s for
    pending writes and intercepted errors, 1.26 s for non-interactive (its GuiAllowed guards parse
    the callers' files); `explain --callers-context` 4.3 s after a plain explain. Under
    `--low-mem`: 34.3 s for the first callers' question (the rebuild parses the dependency trees
    again), then 0.18-0.29 s, and 2.45 s for non-interactive.
  - Answers, hand-checked against source: `RunReportID callers-have-pending-writes` **yes** (local,
    1 hop: `RunReport` calls `Core.IsAppActiveOrAskToActivate`, which may write Continia Core table
    6192807, at `CDOEMailHandler.Codeunit.al:240`, before its calls at :251/:268); `RunReportID
    callers-intercept-errors` **yes** (`RunDocHandleIsolated`'s `exit(AutoSendRunner.Run())` at
    `CDOSubscribers.Codeunit.al:1239`, a checked run, 5 hops); `UpdateLastUpload
    callers-have-pending-writes` **yes** with `QueueUpload` as the witness (its unchecked
    `Codeunit.Run(Codeunit::"Job Queue - Enqueue", …)` at `CDOTelemetry.Codeunit.al:41` inserts a
    Job Queue Entry before the call at :42); `TryRunReport callers-intercept-errors` **yes** (`if not
    TryRunReport(…) then` at `CDOLegacyeDocDispatcher.Codeunit.al:231`); `IssueReminder` all three
    **unknown**, blocked only by its public access for pending writes (its one caller, the
    `Issue and send/print` action at `CDOReminderActions.Page.al:142`, writes nothing before the
    call). Non-interactive is `unknown` on CDO for every routine: no `roots.config.json`, an unread
    `WebServicePublish.xml`, two background starts with a variable codeunit, and the background
    entries found are reached only through hubs.

### Changed (agent tasks, milestone A)

- **prove 2.4.0** (additive): the callers' context questions' documents carry
  `payload.questionScope: "callers-context"` and a `result` with `answer`, `evidence[]` (`kind`,
  `detail`, `evidence.{file,line}`, `entry`, `hops`, `tier`, `path[]`), `blockedBy[]` (at most 5
  per kind) with `blockedByCounts`, `assumptions`, `entries`, `stopped`, `commitBehavior`,
  `tryFunctionCallers`, `notIntercepted`, `testEntries`, `unrecognizedGuards` and `cone`. The six
  existing questions' JSON is unchanged except `schemaVersion`.
- **The six existing prove questions say "existing effects"**: their human `question:` line ends
  `— existing effects (what the routine and its callees already do)`; the new ones end `— callers'
  context (not about the routine's own effects)`. The prove tool's description, its `question`
  argument and the server instructions say which is which; a contract test keeps the word "safe"
  out of every tool description, argument description and the instructions.
- **explain JSON `al-sem.explain/4`** (additive: `callersContext` with `--callers-context`).

### Added (agent tasks, milestone D: field impact)

- **`alsem query touches --table T --field F`: every code consumer of one field** (agent-tasks
  milestone D, narrowed v1; MCP: `field` on `alsem_query_touches`). Each site is listed once
  with its uses: read, write (a `R.F += 1` is one site with uses read and write), validate,
  filter (`SetRange`, `SetFilter`, `GetFilter`, `GetRangeMin/Max`, `CopyFilter`), key-use,
  load, calc (`CalcFields`, `CalcSums`, `SetAutoCalcFields`), rule (`TestField`,
  `FieldError`), metadata (`FieldNo`, `FieldCaption`, `FieldName`, `FieldActive`),
  copy-candidate (`TransferFields`, when the other table has a field with F's number, or its
  table is not resolved), and by-number (`RecordRef.Field(<literal>)`, a match only when the
  routine decides the RecordRef's table). Extraction is per operation: `Next(2)`, `Get('X')`
  and `FieldIndex(n)` never name a field. Temporary consumers are counted beside persistent
  ones; a record of an unresolved table is a candidate. Workspace and loaded dependency bodies
  are searched, and the answer says so; CalcFormula, TableRelation and page/report/query/XMLport
  columns are stated as not searched, so an answer with no site is "no indexed consumer
  observed", never no. With `--from R`, only R's cone (the solve graph, as `query touches` down)
  and R's callers, named by R0's reverse walk over the sited graph as `alsem tests` names them
  (each up site with its tier; `--single-app` walks the workspace program's graph). It reads
  the graph through milestone A's one mechanism (`ViewNeeds::MODEL_SITED`, `ViewCx::sited`,
  the engine host's `reads_sited` pin rule), extended for D: single-app, `build_view_model`
  lends the workspace program for the graph, and `ViewCx::sited` panics when read without
  the declaration and says when the graph's build did not finish. The query schema is
  **3.3.0** (additive: `field`, `searched`, `fieldSummary`, `fieldTouches[]`, `declaredKeys[]`,
  `reasons[]`, `absence`); every other query document changes only its version.
- **Two field facts for field impact (agent-tasks milestone D, the D1 probe).** A bare field in
  a table or page trigger (`Amount := Amount + 1`, through the implicit `Rec` or a `with`
  record) was no field access at all: only the `X.F` member form was recorded. The body walk
  now records it as `ModelRoutine::implicit_field_accesses`, with its read / write kind, apart
  from `field_accesses` so no detector input and no serialized feature moves. A record method's
  field-naming argument (`TestField(F)`, `SetRange(F, …)`'s first) is not one. A
  `TransferFields`' source record is kept as `ModelRecordOperation::transfer_fields_source`.
  `aldump --field-census <ws> [--single-app]` counts the field facts by role (on CDO, cross-app:
  22,707 implicit accesses, 5.3 MB, against 16.9 MB for the existing field accesses). The
  findings and scope decisions are in the agent-tasks design §7.3a.

### Added (caller relations)

- **Two caller relations, named and pinned.** The solve graph (`query touches` up,
  `DbEffectQuery::ancestors`, the detectors' caller walks) and R0's reverse walk (`alsem tests`,
  impact, `query touches --field --from` up) disagreed on CDO (`WaitForMailLimit`: 967 transitive
  callers against 4,827 with a body, 1,030 of them local). Diffed exactly: every local difference
  (66 routines) is a routine that opens a page whose user-started trigger (an action, a field's
  `OnDrillDown`/`OnLookup`, a part, a page it opens) reaches the root. The program engine does
  not follow those on purpose (`run_triggers`: platform entry points are not modelled); R0's
  may-execute graph does. Not a bug on either side. New in `program::impact_graph::reverse`:
  `is_code_call_site` (the code-call relation over the sited graph: calls, object runs and the
  triggers a run runs, record triggers, event dispatch; no user-started lifecycle, rule edge or
  open site), `object_run_reaches` (the resolver's run rule, page and report extensions
  included) and the `CodeCalls` visitor adapter. R0 over code-call sites equals the solve graph's
  local callers exactly on CDO (`WaitForMailLimit` 964 = 964, `RunReportID` 880 = 880).
  The rest of the gap is the solve graph's documented cut at dependency code (it holds workspace
  callers' calls only): 86 workspace routines reach `WaitForMailLimit` by code calls only through
  Base Application code (84 by `Sales-Post`'s `OnAfterFinalizePosting`), plus open sites and
  bodiless dependency routines.
- **`query touches` up names its relation**: JSON `up.relation: "code-calls"` and a human
  `callers:` line saying what it follows and what it does not (a page a caller opens, a path
  through dependency code). Query schema **3.4.0** (additive; milestone D's `touches --field`
  fields are 3.3.0, and this branch's `up.relation`, minted as 3.3.0 in parallel, is the next
  step on top of them).
- Fixture `tests/fixtures/caller-relations` and the agreement test
  `reverse::caller_agreement_tests::solve_callers_equal_the_reverse_walk_over_code_call_sites`.
- `aldump --caller-diff <ws> "<Object>::<Routine>" [--code-calls]`: the probe that measured the
  above (both caller sets, every local difference with a witness path).

### Fixed (caller relations)

- **R0-3's `select::direct_callers` missed page extensions.** A run of a page runs its
  extensions' lifecycle triggers too (the resolver's `dispatch_entry_trigger`), so explain counted
  the page's runners as callers of an extension's `OnOpenPage` while `direct_callers` (which
  looked up `run_triggers` by the extension's own kind) counted none; and an extension's triggers
  were counted as routine callers where explain counts them apart as page actions (F16j: an
  `object_type` starting with `Page`). It now reads `reverse::object_run_reaches`, and a page
  extension's trigger is a page trigger. `explain_callers_equal_the_cones_direct_callers` runs
  over `caller-relations` as well (breaks: the old run rule -> `explain 1, cone 0` on the
  extension's `OnOpenPage`; page triggers only -> `explain 4, cone 6` on `Target`). No shipped
  output read `direct_callers` on master.
- The code-call relation (`is_code_call_site`) leaves out F3's background-start sites, as the
  model's calls do (integration of the two branches).

### Fixed (warm MCP calls slow once `alsem_impact` / `alsem_tests` had run)

Measured on CDO through one long-lived `alsem mcp` session (digest, impact, digest, impact,
tests, digest, explain twice, impact, digest; then the 94-file range). Root causes, each with
its own test and discrimination proof:

- **`alsem impact`'s parts never used the resident engine.** `impact --part main` and
  `--part up` were not in `SERVED_COMMANDS`, so the engine child ran each through the one-shot
  job path over its inputs: a whole program build per part on every call, warm or not (CDO
  before: main 34-50 s, up 13-43 s per call, no fill and no eviction counted). They are now
  answered off the revision: the main part from its retained artifacts (digest's plan), the up
  part from its sited graph.
- **The first question that read the sited graph threw the revision's artifacts away.**
  `pin_sited` rebuilt the session to add the graph, publishing a new revision with an empty
  store, so the next digest or explain filled everything again (CDO: 9.1 s of fills for the
  digest after the first impact). The graph is now added to the published revision, built from
  a program over that revision's own read (the workspace session's, reusing every parse;
  single-app, the cold builder's): no workspace read, no new revision, every filled artifact
  kept. A cancelled request leaves the revision without the graph and is answered `stopped`.
- **A request's witness batch reserved once per root.** The first witness fill computes every
  witness of the request; the later ones are lookups, but each reserved the case's estimate
  again (the batch's observed peak once observed): a 699-root diff was refused at 2042 MiB per
  root over a 7.4 GB RSS. A witness fill whose batch has run reserves nothing.
- **Large reads memoized every root's witness.** A witness is 5.6-7.9 MiB per root on CDO and
  the tree read clones the ones it reads, so a 699-root impact held them twice and its trees'
  reservation was refused. A read over more than `WITNESS_MEMO_MAX_ROOTS` (64) roots computes
  its entries itself, as a one-shot run does, and publishes none.
- **One large request's peak became every request's estimate.** The budget's estimate of a
  case was the largest of its last three observed peaks whatever the work's size, so after the
  range (trees peak 4174 MiB) every one-routine ask was refused over a 5.7 GB RSS. Estimates
  and observations are now kept per size class (the work's roots, one class per factor of 4:
  `budget::size_class`); a small request reads its own class, or the table.

After (CDO, `release-fast`, machine load 25-110, so upper bounds): a repeated `alsem_impact`
on one routine 0.44-0.53 s (before 47-63 s), `alsem_digest` 0.27-0.34 s after impact and tests
(before 9.5 s once, then 0.3-0.4 s), `alsem_explain` 0.46-0.81 s, `alsem_tests` 0.07 s; the
first impact of a session 17.4 s (its up part 2.3 s adds the sited graph; the test engine's
cold start 14.4 s). After the 94-file range the one-routine calls stay there (digest 1.2-1.3 s
with a refill of what the range's reclaim evicted, impact 0.44-0.46 s). Production child 5.4-
5.6 GB, test child 2.2 GB. **Still open, measured:** the range itself answers cold (152 s;
before 314-319 s, warm or cold) but a warm repeat is refused by the budget: its main part's
trees peak at 4.1 GB over a 5.6 GB resident child (9.7 GB against 8 GiB), and an eviction does
not lower the RSS the admission reads (10,882 entries evicted, RSS 5.79 → 5.62 GB, the retained
floor 3.5 GB). Not fixed by raising the budget; computing the per-root totals in chunks would
bound that peak.

### Added (agent tasks, milestone B1: impact on the current revision)

The blast radius of a change, current effects only. Spec:
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-agent-tasks-design.md` §8.

- **Every changed line accounted** (`engine::impact::accounting`, B-1b): each added or removed
  line of a diff lands in exactly one bucket: a routine's body or signature (split at the body's
  first `var` or `begin` line; the attributes and header above are the signature), an
  object-level declaration by kind (field, key, field group, global variable, property, action,
  layout, trigger declaration, enum value, object header, comment or blank, other), outside any
  object, removed routine text (removed lines that held a routine no new-side span holds: named
  from their header lines, never called deleted without a base), routine text the model holds no
  span for, or unmapped with the reason (not in the workspace, two workspace files, not AL, a
  deleted file, a rejected hunk header, a line past the end of the analyzed file). Per file the
  buckets sum to the file's changed lines, and a hunk that touches a global and a routine reports
  both (digest's `hunk-outside-routines` names only hunks that hit no routine). The declaration
  kinds come from a line scanner (`engine::impact::scan`) over the analyzed text: braces outside
  comments and strings, the head before each `{`, `var` sections and routine headers; a removed
  run is scanned from the scanner's state at its gap, so it is classified by what it was.
- **The diff is checked against the analyzed text**: each new-side line a hunk shows (context and
  added) must be the analyzed file's line at that number; a file that fails is reported with its
  first differing line, and its routines' positions are uncertain.
- The unified-diff parser keeps each deletion run's text (`DiffHunk::deleted`) and the new-side
  lines a hunk shows (`DiffHunk::new_side`); digest's output does not change.
- **The comparison tuple** (`engine::impact::compare`, B-3): `requestedRef`, `resolvedCommit`,
  `mergeBase`, `comparisonBase`, `head` (commit and the revision's `inputsStamp`) and `diffHash`
  (blake3 of the diff text used), resolved once and printed. `--base REV` alone compares the
  MERGE BASE of `REV` and `HEAD` with the working tree: committed, staged and unstaged changes
  (each layer's files listed) and every untracked `.al` file under the workspace (listed, and read
  as a new file so its routines resolve). Git is only read; a diff alone names no base, and says
  so.
- **`alsem impact <ws> (--routine R… | --file F… | --diff P [--diff-root D] | --base REV)`**
  (`engine::impact::{jobs,up,run,render}`, B-1, B-2, B-3b): the input accounting first (the
  tuple, every bucket with counts, the hunks outside routines with what each touched, unmapped
  files, removed routine headers, diff/working-tree mismatches, every root diagnostic), then per
  changed routine, ranked "reached from a user or a job first, then by ancestors": its CURRENT
  effects (digest's own plan and the per-routine rollup: writes, caller-dependent tables, commits,
  UI, errors, events), who reaches it (R0's reverse walk over the sited graph, one streaming walk
  per root with one reused scratch and a counting visitor, never a cone per root: direct callers
  by explain's definition with each first call site, ancestors by tier, entries by kind with page
  actions by caption, event publishers, external callers by reason), and its tests (milestone C's
  select parts, unchanged, with the production-stamp retry). Then the whole change's reach (one
  `walk_multi` over every root), schema lines, the tests line (`selectionComplete` and its
  reasons, the codeunit filter), and the walks' limits. "Current effects; no before/after" is
  said plainly; nothing is called added or deleted. **Nearest tested caller** (C left it null): a
  root no test universe has is answered with the nearest production ancestor a test universe has
  and a test reaches (the up walk's nearest ancestors, probed in each test universe with
  `tests --part select --probe-id`, which never joins the selection). Human by default, the first
  20 routines (`--max-roots`), more per list with `--detail`; `--format json` is
  `al-sem.impact/1` (`comparison`, `input`, `roots[]` with `up`, `effects`, `tests`, `delta:
  null`; `union`, `tests`, `assumptions`, `limits`, `base: null`). `--no-tests` skips the test
  universes, `--no-dependents` the external callers. Spec §12.1's refusals: exactly one mode;
  `--base` with `--diff` is B2's delta; `--diff-root` goes with `--diff`. Goldens:
  `tests/cli-output-goldens/impact/`.
- The diff check ignores a byte-order mark (found on CDO: 54 files of the 94-file range added
  one, and read as mismatched before).
- **MCP tool `alsem_impact`** (B-8, B-10): `routines` | `files` | `diff` (+ `diffRoot`) | `base`,
  with `testApps`, `tests` (default true), `maxRoots`, `detail`, `assumeNoDependents`, `format`
  (human by default). The front end resolves the comparison tuple (`base`: git, read only) before
  it sends anything, then runs the parts as a composite request, one at a time (the main and up
  parts on the production engine, which builds its sited graph on the first up part; the select
  parts on the test engines, as `alsem_tests`). The stdout is `alsem impact`'s bytes except the
  tuple's inputs stamp, which is the main part's revision (a one-shot CLI run has none); the
  envelope's `revisions` names every part's revision, wall time (`ms`) and engine timing. Over the inline cap (40 KiB) or the client's
  50,000-character budget the answer goes to a file with a `summary` (the comparison, the
  accounting line, the first five routines, the tests line). The LSP front end refuses it, as it
  refuses `alsem_tests`. The server instructions name it for reviewing a diff or a PR.

### Fixed (transaction spans read statement order)

- **A transaction span now ends at its Commit and the next one starts after it.** The spans
  behind d9, d8, d50 and digest's transaction context (`engine::l5::transaction_spans`) read
  the statement order only for the pending writes. Three other parts ignored it:
  - **coverage**: `coverage_complete` was the AND of every member's whole-cone coverage, so a
    gap in a callee called AFTER the Commit (or in a checked `Codeunit.Run`, its own
    transaction) made the span "effect scope unknown". It now reads what each member may run
    before its call toward the Commit (the Commit routine: before the Commit), with the same
    site set as the pending writes: no gap of the member's own and complete cones for the
