    routines it may call first. A member whose whole cone is complete stays complete.
  - **an earlier Commit of the Commit routine**: `w1; Commit; X(); Commit` gave the second
    Commit's span the routine's callers and their writes, which the first Commit had already
    ended. That span is now the routine alone, from the first Commit on (its span root).
  - **a caller that commits**: the walk stopped at every caller with a Commit anywhere in its
    body. It now stops only when a Commit statement runs on the way to the caller's call
    toward the Commit (`Before::committed`, read by `pending_writes::sites_before`); a caller
    that commits only after (or beside, or in a branch before) its call does not end the
    transaction its callers opened, so they are in the span. With the order unknown (no tree,
    or a site the tree does not hold) the old stop rule holds.
- digest's transaction context names a Commit's span `span-has-known-writes` from the physical
  writes pending at it (`pending_physical_tables`), not from everything the span can reach.
- On CDO (`bc3ccb18`, `--scope primary` and `--scope all` alike) 12 d9 findings move and no
  other detector's: 2 drop (SendQueue, whose only gap is in the checked `Codeunit.Run` after its
  Commit; StampBlankSendCodeBatched, whose gaps are in `RunMigration`'s phase 2, after its call),
  10 change their routine count (callers past `HandleEntry`, `PrintDocuments`,
  `PrintOrEMailAll` and `RunMigration`, which commit after their call) and 2 of those lose one
  pending table (`CDO Print document`, written after `PrintDocuments`' call toward the Commit).
- Known precision gap, not fixed here: a literal argument is not followed through a function
  return and an event `var` parameter. `EnableeDocsFeature` passes `GetCDNeDocsFeatureCode()` to
  `CSC Feature Management.EnableFeature`, whose `OnAfterEnableFeature` reaches
  `OnAfterEnableCDOFeature`'s `case FeatureCode of ... ESealFeatureCodeLbl: RunESealServiceSetup`,
  so the eSeal arm counts as reachable from the CDN eDocs feature. This was found while checking
  the proto/dep-callers d9 report: its RunESealServiceSetup growth (5 → 18 routines) comes from
  these callers, not from statement order.
- Tests: `transaction_spans::order_tests` (7 inline-AL fixtures) and
  `pending_writes::tests::a_commit_on_the_way_clears_and_a_branch_or_loop_commit_does_not`,
  `digest_cli::tests::tx_context_reads_the_writes_pending_at_the_commit`.
- Milestone A's callers' context questions read the same order: `pending_before_report` is now
  `sites_before` + `pending_of` (its `committed` is `Before::committed`, a Commit on the way to
  every target; the questions pass one target, so their answers do not change).

### Added (agent tasks, milestone C: test selection)

Which tests to run first for a change, as a first-class answer. Spec:
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-agent-tasks-design.md` §4.

- **Test universes** (`engine::test_select::universe::TestUniverse`): a sibling test app's
  program with the workspace (production) app loaded as an **injected** source dependency and the
  production root's `.alpackages` (and ancestors) as an extra package root. Nothing is written into
  the user's test app: `WorkspaceInputs::read_scoped` takes the injected inputs
  (`program::inputs::Injected`), `source_deps::read_with` / `walk_with` read the injected folders
  after the configured ones (one the configuration already names by app id is left out), and
  `dependencies::discover_app_files_with` searches the extra roots after the workspace's. The
  descriptor's key is `tests:<16 hex>`. A **production stamp** (blake3 over the sorted relative
  path and content hash of the production app's `.al` files and its `app.json`, the same function
  on both sides) tells whether the two universes were built from the same production bytes. On
  the fixture every production routine keeps its StableRoutineId and its resolved out-edges in the
  test universe (C-2, C-2b).
- **The manifest names a test universe's injected inputs** (`inj:sources`, `inj:pkg-roots`;
  `Manifest::observe_scoped`, `Manifest::injected`), so a resident test universe sees a production
  edit as its own change, and the freshness check (`check_against`) observes the injected inputs
  from the published manifest alone (F-7). `Manifest::changes` names them by category:
  `injected-source` (an injected folder's files, app.json and listing) and `injected-packages` (a
  package found under an injected package root); both are refresh class `Package`.
  `ResidentSession::with_injected` / `with_universe_label` (the descriptor's universe is
  `tests:<key>`); `WorkspaceReader::read_scoped`.
- **`alsem tests <ws> (--routine R… | --file F… | --diff P [--diff-root D]) [--test-app DIR…]
  [--tier local|dependency|all] [--max-tests N] [--format human|json]`**: the test scope first
  (the workspace's own `[Test]` procedures and the sibling test apps, with how each was found and
  what was skipped), each changed routine's status (`reached`, `no-known-path`,
  `analysis-incomplete`, `not-loaded`, `not-in-projection`), the tests to run first ranked by tier
  (local, through dependency code, over open sites), then hops, then codeunit, grouped per
  codeunit with the first test's path, `selection complete: yes|no` with every reason the whole
  suite must run as well (`requiredFallback`), and a codeunit filter. JSON schema
  `al-sem.tests/1` (`runFirst`, `requiredFallback`, `selectionComplete`, `byTier`, `hidden`,
  `next`). The answer is made of parts: `tests --part roots` (digest's root resolution in the
  production universe, the production stamp, the scope) and `tests --part select` per test
  universe (the reverse walk over its sited graph); `test_select::run::orchestrate` runs them,
  retries once when the production stamps differ and then refuses that test app, and renders.
- **Scope discovery** (`engine::test_select::scope`): `--test-app`, else `testApps` in
  `.al-sem.json` (`"testApps": []` turns sibling discovery off), else auto-discovery under the git
  top level (the workspace's parent when there is none): sorted, 3 levels deep, at most 64
  `app.json` files, skipping hidden folders, `node_modules`, `target`, `target-*` and the
  workspace itself. An app qualifies when it depends on the workspace app and holds a `Subtype =
  Test` codeunit; one with no `.al` is skipped `no-source`, one with no test codeunit
  `no-test-codeunit`. A cap that fires is "discovery incomplete", never "no app depends on this
  one". The test-codeunit scan is cached by every file's stat.
- **Honesty rules**: a selection-relevant hidden channel in a cone keeps the selection incomplete
  (an unreached root is then `analysis-incomplete`, never `no-known-path`). A platform-raised
  table event would be covered when every write of its table is an edge into it; the sited graph
  has no such edge, so it is never shown covered and counts. When a root's through-dependency
  tests come only via dependency nodes that may execute over half of the graph, the answer says
  they are "effectively the suite's posting tests, not specific to this change". When the test
  app declares Microsoft test libraries that are not loaded, a `next:` line says how to get their
  symbols. Static reachability is not coverage, said once at the end.
- **MCP tool `alsem_tests`** (`routines` | `files` | `diff` [`diffRoot`], `testApps`, `tier`,
  `maxTests`, `format`, and the common properties): a **composite request** (`Pool::run_tests`,
  on a coordinator thread off the reader loop). The roots part runs on the production engine;
  each test app's select part on a **test-universe engine** of its own (pool key: the test app's
  folder, universe `tests`; the child opens a graph-only session with the descriptor's injected
  inputs, `session/open {universe: "tests", testUniverse}`), started on its first part and kept;
  the workspace's own tests' part on the production engine (`pin_sited` turns its sited graph
  on). One part at a time, so a part never holds one child while waiting for another;
  `--max-children 2` stays (with a third universe the least recently used idle child is evicted).
  The stdout is `alsem tests`' bytes (the same `orchestrate` and render); the envelope carries
  the revision vector `revisions: {production, tests: [{workspace, universe: "tests:<key>",
  revision}]}`. explain starts no test engine (a test pins the engine count). The LSP front end
  refuses `alsem_tests` with the reason. `tests` and `tests-select` join the commands a resident
  revision serves. Measured on CDO 2026-11-05 through `alsem mcp` (release-fast; load average
  ~170 on 22 cores from other builds, so cold times are upper bounds): cold (both engines build,
  one after the other) 24.7-52 s; warm 0.1 s (UpdateLastUpload), 0.2 s (RunReportID,
  IssueReminder); after a single-app explain (a third universe) the next `alsem_tests` took 11.3 s
  (one engine rebuilt). After a cold RunReportID call: the production child 3.65 GB RSS, the test
  child 2.31 GB (each under its 8 GiB budget).
- **`alsem graph --keep-local-sources[=true|false]`** and **`meta.apps[].sourceRoot`** (§4.8,
  C-8): every routine of an app loaded from local source (a source-folder dependency, such as a
  test app's production app) survives pruning, so a consumer can join changed production files on
  `(appId, sourcePath)`; the default is on exactly when such an app is loaded, so an export with
  none is byte-identical (the `cli_graph_export` golden). `sourceRoot` names the folder.
- **explain's `tests:` line reads the test scope** (C-7) without analyzing it: "no [Test]
  procedure in the workspace app; 1 test app discovered (…); not analyzed in this call — alsem
  tests (MCP: alsem_tests) selects them", or "no test code found (0 [Test] procedures in the
  workspace app; <why no sibling was found>)", and with workspace tests an `also …` line. JSON
  cards carry `testScope` (`analyzed: false`). Explain never builds a test universe. **Explain
  goldens move** by that line. A workspace with no git top level searches no sibling and says so.
- **A project-collection marker bounds discovery** (`.al-sem-projects`,
  `scope::PROJECTS_MARKER`): a folder holding that file says each of its subfolders is a project
  of its own, so for a workspace under it the search root is the subfolder that holds the
  workspace, when that is nearer than the git top level; the "none found" wording then says
  "under the project folder". This repository marks `tests/r0-corpus/` and `tests/fixtures/`.
  Before, a fixture searched from the repository's git top level, met the 64-`app.json` cap among
  the other fixtures and read "test app discovery incomplete", so every explain golden depended on
  how many `app.json` files the repository held. The fixture goldens (cli-explain, cli-output,
  `tests/selection-graph.applydecay`) now show each fixture's own scope: searched 0 `app.json`
  files, complete. The cap's "incomplete" wording is unchanged and still tested on a hand-built
  tree over the cap (`the_app_json_cap_makes_discovery_incomplete`); the marker by
  `a_projects_marker_bounds_the_search_to_the_project`.
- **explain's summary agrees with that line.** Its `callers and tests:` clause said `tests: none
  (no test code loaded)` while the `tests:` line below named the discovered test app. It now
  reads the same scope: `tests: none in the workspace; 1 test app discovered (not analyzed here;
  alsem tests)`, `tests: none in the workspace; test app discovery incomplete`, or (with
  workspace tests) `tests: none of N loaded; also …`; "no test code loaded" stays only when the
  discovery finished and found none (or `testApps: []`). JSON cards: `summary.testApps
  {discovered, discoveryComplete}`. The three CDO explain rendering goldens move by that clause.
- **A client's cancel of `alsem_tests` reaches every part.** Its parts are sub-requests with ids
  of their own, so `notifications/cancelled` for the call's id found no flag: the running part ran
  to its end and the next parts still ran. `Pool::run_tests` now registers the call's cancel flag
  and `run_composite` queues each part with it: a queued part is dropped, the running one is sent
  `session/cancel`, no later part runs, and the call is not answered (MCP). Pinned by
  `mcp_tests::a_cancelled_tests_call_stops_its_parts_and_is_not_answered` (the cancelled roots
  part publishes no revision; no test engine starts).
- **`alsem_status` shows a `testApps` change (`test-config`).** The roots part of a tests answer
  records the `.al-sem.json` `testApps` its scope was discovered under (`scope.testConfig`;
  `scope::read_test_config_identity`, one function on both sides), and the pool keeps it per
  production workspace. The status check of that workspace's production engine compares it with
  the file (`check.testScope {atLastTestsAnswer, now, changed}`); a difference is listed as
  category `test-config` (`.al-sem.json`, counted in `changeCount`) and the headline adds "Test
  scope changed: … the next alsem_tests rediscovers it." It is no input of the engine's revision
  (discovery runs on every tests answer), so `fresh` and the refresh class keep the engine's own
  verdict (`refreshClass.class: null`, "not a refresh of this engine", when nothing else moved).
  **The earlier discovery is invalidated** when the next answer's scope no longer holds a test
  app: its registered test-universe descriptor is dropped and its idle test engine retired, so it
  no longer holds a child slot.
- **The CDO ratchet pins the sameness wording** (C-12 on CDO): `alsem tests Cloud --routine
  "CDO E-Mail Handler::RunReportID"` prints exactly `through dependency code: 301 tests —
  effectively the suite's posting tests, not specific to this change`
  (`output_cdo::cdo_test_selection_ratchets`, run by `cdo-gate`).
- **Measured on CDO through `alsem mcp`** (release-fast, a scratch copy; load average 25-230, so
  cold times are upper bounds; spec appendix "Milestone C's open items"): `alsem_tests` for
  RunReportID cold 23.0 s / 6.0 GB peak (default) and 24.0 s / 4.6 GB (`--low-mem`), warm
  0.17-0.20 s in both; after a B edit of a production file 13.2-14.3 s (default) and 14.2 s
  (`--low-mem`): the test universe sees the injected file as a `Package`-class change and
  rebuilds. Resident after: 3.85 + 2.16 GB (default), 2.80 + 1.21 GB (`--low-mem`). A cancel
  during the cold build does not interrupt the build (it is one phase): the engine was idle
  10.0 s later, the call unanswered, no test engine started, and the revision kept. The spec now
  says `--base` (B1/B2) and "nearest tested caller" (with B1's up-walk) come in later milestones.
- **R0-3: explain's callers and the reverse cone agree.** `select::direct_callers` defines a
  direct caller over the sited graph the way the model's calls count it: a call, interface call,
  object run or record operation site (`via` call/interface/run/implicitTrigger, never a rule's
  edge such as a TestPage variable's `declaredRunnable`), and for a trigger a run of its object
  runs (the resolver's `run_triggers`: a codeunit's `OnRun`, a page's or report's lifecycle
  triggers) every routine that runs that object; not an event's publisher, a test's handler list,
  a hub or a page's triggers. A test checks every workspace routine of `test-selection-graph`:
  explain's `callers` count equals the cone's. **explain keeps reading the model's adjacency**
  (M0's lazy-graph decision: the sited graph costs each edit 0.93-1.19 s and 45 MiB on CDO; only
  `alsem tests` builds a graph, and only in its test universes).
- **The sited graph names local routines** in their source spelling (`SitedGraph::local_name`:
  object, routine, file) and lists the platform table-event publishers
  (`is_platform_publisher`); `SitedGraph::apps`.
- Measured on CDO 2026-11-05 (release-fast; the machine was under heavy load from other builds,
  so wall times are upper bounds): `tests Cloud --routine "CDO Telemetry::UpdateLastUpload"` lists
  exactly the 3 `CDO Telemetry Tests` tests at 1 hop, local; RunReportID: 68 local-path tests in
  7 codeunits at 3-7 hops, 301 through dependency code with the sameness line, 253 over open sites;
  IssueReminder: 0 local, nearest `CDO Setup Tests::HideStandardMailActions_WhenDisabled_…` at 6
  hops through dependency code. `selectionComplete: false` on CDO: 48 selection-relevant hidden
  nodes (47 platform table events, 1 unbound subscriber) and 4,702 unresolved test calls. One-shot
  cost: the roots part 15.1 s / 3.10 GB peak, the select part 10.2-10.4 s / 2.53 GB, the whole
  command 20.7-30.5 s / 3.13 GB peak (the parts run one after the other in one process).

### Security

- **The private output folders no longer trust a reused inode number.** The engine child's
  output namespace (`src/engine/host/output.rs`) and the MCP server's output folder
  (`src/mcp/output.rs`) allowed an overwrite when the name's (device, inode) equalled the pair
  recorded at creation. A freed inode number is handed out again, and ext4 does it at once, so
  a file or a symlink planted after the server's own file was removed carried the same pair and
  was accepted as the server's file (the rename then replaced the planted entry; nothing was
  written through a link). Each overwritable file is now **pinned** by the descriptor it was
  written through, which keeps its inode allocated, and an overwrite needs the name to be a
  regular file with the pinned descriptor's device and inode while the pinned file still has a
  link. At most 256 entries are pinned per folder; an older one is unpinned and its overwrite is
  refused from then on. Spills are never overwritten and take no pin. CI (ubuntu-24.04, ext4)
  had failed on this since 2026-11-02 (`the_private_namespace_contract`; nextest's fail-fast hid
  the same failure in `overwrite_only_what_the_server_wrote`); it passed locally because btrfs
  and tmpfs do not reuse inode numbers at once. Reproduced and verified on a real ext4 mount.

### Fixed (event subscriptions to events declared in an extension)

- **An event declared in a table, page or report extension now binds the subscribers that name
  the base object.** AL publishes such an event on the object the extension extends, so a
  subscriber writes `[EventSubscriber(ObjectType::Table, Database::"Error Message",
  'OnDrillDownSource', …)]`, not the extension. `SubscriberIndex::build` searched only the named
  object's own routines, so the subscription was `Orphaned` and the publisher's event-flow edge
  had no route. The candidates now also include the publishers of the base object's extensions
  (`index::PublisherExtensions`): an extension counts when its `extends_target` resolves, from its
  own app, to that object, and when it is in the subscriber's dependency closure. Found on CDO,
  where three Base Application subscribers of events in its own extensions were orphaned
  (`OnDrillDownSource` in `tableextension "Error Message Extension"`, `OnOpenRelatedRecord` in
  `pageextension "Error Messages Extension"`, `OnAfterSetIsDocumentArchiveTable` in
  `pageextension "Reten. Pol. Setup Lines Ext."`). On CDO `--program-call-graph-stats`
  `wholeProgram` moves 3 edges from `honestEmpty` to `resolvedSource` (28256 → 28253, 11639 →
  11642); `primaryScoped`, `--dependency-bodies-stats`, `alsem analyze` at both scopes and every
  `--switch-dump` file (event graph and findings included) are unchanged. The IncludeSender
  preflight diagnostic and the semantic-golden event check read the same extension facts (the
  check accepts the declaring object or its base as the named publisher).
- Not changed, and honest: Continia Core's four subscriptions to codeunit `"Hybrid Cloud
  Management"` and page `"Cloud Migration Management"` stay `ObjectUnresolved` ("target object
  not in indexed source"). Both objects are in Microsoft's Intelligent Cloud Base app, which is
  in no loaded package, and all four attributes sit under `#if BCONLINE`, a symbol the shipped
  Core build does not define (its manifest lists `BC21`–`BC26` and `CLOUD`). The engine reads
  every `#if` arm (the union read of `al-syntax`'s lowerer), so it still sees them.

### Fixed

- `release_alloc::tests::freed_large_blocks_are_released_only_when_on` no longer depends on how
  the kernel backs the test's heap. It measured residency (`mincore`) on memory that mimalloc
  marks for transparent huge pages, and wrote only the requested 256 KiB of a block whose usable
  size (and released interior) is 320 KiB, so its precondition held only while a huge page
  covered the unwritten tail. On CI (Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 7.0 azure) the old block of the
  moving `realloc` read as all 79 interior pages resident after its release, 16 of them never
  written since the first huge-page fault. It is intermittent: reproduced once in two full
  nextest runs in an Ubuntu 26.04 VM on `7.0.0-1019-azure` (4 vCPUs, 16 GB), never alone (0 of
  360) nor on `7.0.0-38-generic` or the dev machine. With huge pages off (`never`) the
  precondition failed instead. The test now turns huge pages off for its
  process (`PR_SET_THP_DISABLE`), writes every usable byte, checks the precondition before each
  release, and also pins each release by its counters (one release, exactly the interior's
  bytes). The allocator itself is unchanged.
- An unused `mut` in `mcp::freshness::CheckOptions::new` warned in builds without the test hooks
  (the shipped release build; CI's clippy runs with `--all-features`, so it never saw it).

### Changed (MCP output step 2: shorter, task-shaped output)

- **Paths name overloads by a short handle.** A path printed every overloaded routine with its
  whole parameter list (`CreateLogEntries(DocumentTemplateLine, FilterRecord, …)`, 20 names, twice
  per path; 35–48 % of a large explain card). explain, digest (human) and prove now print
  `Name/n` (its arity) when no other overload of the routine has that arity, `Name/n[position:
  type]` (the parameter types it differs in) when one does, and `Name/n#k` (k in source order) when
  only the place tells them apart (two field triggers); a `#k` handle's signature and declaration
  are printed once under the card (`overload … = (…) at …`), every handle's with `--detail`.
  `query effects` paths use the same handles (its `writes beyond` section is explain's own); it
  prints no legend.
- **A section's shared path start prints once.** Within one section, the start (the root and at
  least two more hops) that saves the most text over its `path:`, `prefix path:` and
  `representative path` lines prints once, `(in <section>, a path that begins with \`… →\` begins
  with: …)`, and those paths print `… → <rest>`. An entry point's prefix and its representative path now
  print as one line (`--detail` keeps both).
- **Commit and kind rows print paths for the first few only.** The `commits:` section prints a path
  for the first 3 sites and the first 3 commit-bearing entry points; the others share one `and N
  more (--detail prints their paths): …` line with their places. A kind family line lists its first
  6 places and counts the rest. prove prints one witnessed row per effect type (its shortest path)
  and lists up to 3 more as places on one `also [TYPE]:` line, then counts the rest; `--detail`
  prints every row with its path. The digest JSON keeps one row of each site-enumerated type whole
  (its shortest witness) and lists the type's other rows as places in a new
  `entries[].moreSites[<type>]` (`file:line conditionality`, `beyond <crossing key> …`,
  `literal-dead` when it cannot run); `--detail` keeps every row in `effects`.
- **The summary is a short risk block.** explain's and digest's `summary` line is now `summary —
  writes: …` followed by `transaction, UI and errors: …`, `other effects: …`, `callers and tests:
  …` and `uncertainty: …`, the same clauses as before. The writes line names the entry point behind
  most of the tables when one is behind more than half of 10 or more (RunReportID on CDO: "357 of
  them beyond Codeunit Sales-Calc. Discount::OnRun (entered at
  ws:src/Foundation/CDOFile.Table.al:125)"); JSON `summary.mayWriteTables.mostBeyond`.
- **The CDO output budgets hold at their existing limits** (re-measured on `bc3ccb18` with the
  commit-site fixes in): explain IssueReminder 136 lines / 31,467 B (limit 140 / 35,500),
  RunReportID 147 / 34,495 (150 / 39,936; inline with 6.4 KiB to spare); prove may-commit 10–11
  lines, at most 1,514 B (20 / 2,000); digest JSON IssueReminder 1,224,146 B, core 712,169
  (1,250,000 / 720,000), RunReportID 1,198,204 / 692,325. The CDO rendering goldens are
  regenerated. The output checks read the new shapes: a folded `and N more …` / `also [TYPE]: …`
  line's anchors are checked item by item, and an entry-point count may be "at least".

### Fixed (`Database.Commit()` is a commit, #155)

- **`Database.Commit()` now gives the same commit fact as `Commit()`.** AL's `Commit` is a
  method of the `Database` type that may be called without its receiver, but the body walk
  recognised only a bare `Commit` callee. `Database.Commit()` (and `Database.Commit`, in any
  case) became a call site to the `Database::commit` builtin, so a routine committing that way
  was invisible to every tool: `prove may-commit` answered `no`, `explain` and `digest` listed no
  COMMIT, and d34, d35, the transaction spans (d9 and the span detectors) and pending writes
  missed it. Every spelling is now a `commit` operation site. A declared `Database` (a
  parameter, local, named return value, global, dataitem or table field) shadows the platform's,
  as the compiler does, so its `Database.Commit()` stays an ordinary call. The key join now pairs
  a commit by the resolver's verdict (`ProgramSite::commit`: the `Commit` shape or a route to a
  commit builtin, `member_catalog::is_commit_builtin`) instead of the callee text `Commit`, so a
  disagreement between the walk and the resolver (a `Database` field of another object that only
  the resolver sees) is a census loss, never silent. Tests: `cli_database_commit` and the adapter
  test `every_commit_spelling_is_an_operation_site_and_a_shadowed_database_is_not`. The CDO
  baseline has no `Database.Commit` in workspace or dependency source, so no CDO answer moves.

### Fixed (commit sites dropped up the call chain)

- **A routine's COMMIT rows now list every commit it reaches, not only the nearest.** On CDO,
  `prove RunReportID writes-table:"Sales Header"` was `yes` through `CDO File::CalcSalesDisc`,
  yet `prove RunReportID may-commit` and `explain RunReportID` listed only the COMMIT at
  `CDOEMailTemplateManagement.Codeunit.al:1241` ("1 site in workspace code; 0 commit-bearing entry
  points"): `CalcSalesDisc`'s own `Commit()` (`CDOFile.Table.al:128`) and the COMMIT beyond
  `Sales-Calc. Discount::OnRun` were gone. Root cause: the capability cone keeps one inherited fact
  per key, which for a COMMIT is one per routine, and its witness followed only that fact's first
  hop to the nearest carriers. For COMMIT the digest now searches every site itself
  (`digest::reconstruct_site_witnesses`): one shortest-path DAG from the root over all its first
  hops, entered only where a commit may be reached, one row per site in workspace code and one per
  crossing into dependency code behind which a commit lies. `explain RunReportID` now reports 6
  sites in workspace code and 7 commit-bearing entry points (8 sites are reached; the 2 in
  `CDO E-Mail Log::MoveEMailToFile`/`MoveEmalToAzureBlob` are reached only from the table's
  `OnInsert`, which passes `OnInsert = true` to their `if OnInsert then exit;`, so the literal pass
  rules them out). This feeds explain, digest, `prove may-commit`, `commits-on-success-path` and the
  ordering engine. A site's conditionality is that of its paths from the asked root, so it can
  differ between roots (`conditional` from `CalcSalesDisc`, `guarded-by-IsHandled` from the
  callers behind `if IsHandled then exit`).
- **A commit site is judged by itself under literal arguments.** With one row per site, the literal
  pass decides a COMMIT row by its own operation, not by "some COMMIT of the routine can run".
- **`commits-on-success-path` ignores a COMMIT the root cannot reach under literal arguments**, as
  the MAY questions already did (G23): such a commit made the answer `unknown` (or could make it
  `yes`).
- **Every other resource-less effect kind is listed per site too, and entry-point totals say when
  they are a lower bound.** The same one-fact-per-key cone hid UI, error, HTTP, file, background
  task, isolated storage and telemetry sites behind the nearest one: on CDO `explain RunReportID`
  printed "UI at 5 places", "HTTP at 2 places", "errors at 5 places"; it now prints 16, 20 and 196.
  These kinds go through the same site search as COMMIT; a row's detail (an HTTP method, a storage
  or file operation) is the site's own, so two representatives of one kind that reach one site
  give one row. A table write or an event keeps one row per table or event, so a second crossing
  that leads only to a table already written nearer had no row and the entry-point counts were
  silently low: digest now checks every crossing the root can take toward any effect, and when one
  has no row (or the search stops at its depth bound) explain and digest print "at least N entry
  points at at least M sites" and `summary.entryPoints.atLeast` is `true`; a kind family's count
  from a search cut at the depth bound is "at least" too (`summary.kindsAtLeast`). In the
  `ws-explain-calls` fixture, `PostOrder` now lists 9 error places (was 2), each a real `Error`/
  `TestField` it reaches; `QuickPost` does not list `CheckOrder`'s `TestField`, which its literal
  `Strict = false` rules out.
- **A commit count the search could not finish says "at least".** A site search that stops at its
  depth bound (64 calls) with a commit possibly beyond it records a `sites-partial` entry
  diagnostic; explain and digest then print "at least N sites … at least M commit-bearing entry
  points", and `summary.commits.atLeast` is `true`.

### Added (agent tasks, milestone R0: the reverse cone)

The shared up-walker ("who reaches this routine") that test selection, "what context does R run
in" and impact build on. A library API and a measurement probe; the agent-facing tools come with
milestones C, A and B1. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-agent-tasks-design.md` §3.

- **`program::impact_graph::reverse`**: `walk_one` (one root, streaming, its scratch reused across
  roots) and `walk_multi` (all roots in one breadth-first walk, each state labelled with its
  nearest root). The walk keeps the shortest hop count per **state** `(node, tier, crossedEvent,
  ext)`, not per node, so a node reached locally and, shorter, through dependency code keeps both.
  Tiers: `Local` (every node in the workspace or an app loaded from local source),
  `ThroughDependency`, `OnlyOpen` (the path uses a hub). The universal hub `h:any` is walked once,
  one hop from the roots, as `OnlyOpen`, and reported once as a hidden channel; its callers are
  never dropped. `hiddenCallers` flags are reported per node. A state budget (2,000,000) and the
  cancellation are reported as limits. The visitor (`ConeVisitor`) gets each state once with the
  site and state it came from; `ConeVisitor::step` is the hook where a consumer sets its own state
  bits per site and refines a `Run` or `TriggerOf` site by its anchor (checked or unchecked
  `Codeunit.Run`, background starts, a trigger's temporary state: body facts the sited graph does
  not carry). The walk keeps no path and nothing per root.
- **Entry kinds from source**, not from the graph having no caller: the model's root classifier
  is now one shape-based function (`root_classification::root_kind_mask`) that the model and the
  sited graph's source facts both call, so they classify alike (a test checks the fixture's every
  routine). A page action reached by a lifecycle edge is still a `page-action` entry; a page whose
  action's `RunObject` runs the cone is one too. Graph sources are reported apart. The
  roots.config kinds come from a model (`reverse::config_entries`) or not at all (graph-only).
- **External callers**: a workspace (or local-source) procedure that apps outside the program may
  call: `public` (public access, object not internal), `protected`, or `friend` (internal, and the
  app's manifest names an `internalsVisibleTo` friend, loaded or not). `assumeNoDependents` is its
  own walk option.
- **The sited graph's node table** now holds each source routine's StableRoutineId (interned;
  `SitedGraph::nodes_with_stable_id` is the test universe's lookup of a production routine), its
  root kinds, flag bits and a reverse index. On CDO cross-app the graph is 57.0 MB by its own
  estimate (`bytes()`), up from about 48 MB.
- `aldump --reverse-cone <ws> (--routine <Object::Routine|stableId>)... [--roots-file F] [--multi]
  [--no-dependents]` measures walks. Measured 2026-11-05 (release-fast):
  - **Test universe** (the design's scratch `TestApp`, CDO as a source dependency): RunReportID
    is reached by 68 tests in 7 codeunits by a local path at 3-7 hops, 369 tests without hubs and
    622 with them; IssueReminder by 0 locally, nearest `CDO Setup Tests` at 6 hops through Base
    Application; UpdateLastUpload by the 3 `CDO Telemetry Tests` tests at 1 hop (the pruned export
    has no such routine). These equal the design's walks over the export, except one hidden node
    more in RunReportID's resolved cone (48, not 47): `Check Dimensions::OnErrorMessageDrillDown`,
    whose every out-edge the export prunes.
  - **CDO cross-app**: 134,385 nodes, 318,084 sites. RunReportID's cone 27,957 nodes, 98,504
    states, 68 ms with the probe's summarizing visitor. The 699 roots of the 94-file range as one
    `walk_multi`: 100,090 states, 25 ms bare (48 ms with the visitor), 1.6 MB of scratch, no RSS
    change. The same roots as 699 `walk_one` calls with one scratch: 33 s in all, most of it the
    probe's per-root summaries; the scratch stays 1.6 MB.

### Added (agent tasks, milestone F: freshness)

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-agent-tasks-design.md` §2.

- **Source dependencies are stat-cached inputs** (`engine::resident::manifest`). The input
  manifest records each configured source folder (`al-sem.dependencies.json`) as its own entries:
  its `app.json` (`srcapp:`), its `.al` listing (`srcwalk:`) and every `.al` file with its stat
  (`src:<spelled>\0<rel>`), through the same walk and checks the read makes
  (`program::source_deps::walk`, which `read` now uses too). A stat-cached freshness check now
  reads and hashes only the dependency files whose length or modification time moved; before, it
  read and hashed every file of every source dependency on every check. A workspace without
  source dependencies has the same entries and the same stamp as before.
- **Input categories** (`Manifest::changes`): every input that differs between two manifests, with
  its category (`al-file`, `al-walk`, `app-json`, `app-json-paths`, `roots-config`,
  `coverage-config`, `source-dependency`, `package`, `package-list`, `unreadable-package-folder`,
  `meta`), its path when it is one file, and what changed when the path does not say it (a file
  on one side only is `added` or `removed`). `Manifest::hashed` lists the files an observation
  actually read. The spec's `injected-source` / `injected-packages` categories wait for the test
  universes (milestone C), which are the only builds with injected inputs.

### Changed (agent tasks, milestone F)

- **`alsem_status` checks the disk** (`statusVersion: 2`, `mcp::freshness`). Before, it returned the
  workers' snapshots and never looked at a file, so `revision` and `lastBuild` read as "current"
  when nothing was checked. Now each engine's row has a `check`: the disk compared with the input
  descriptor its worker published for the revision (stat-cached, or every input hashed with the new
  `verify: true` argument), bound to `checkedRevision` (`generation`, `inputsStamp`) with start and
  end times, `complete`/`incompleteReasons` (a check past its deadline, 5 s cached and 30 s verify,
  or one that meets an unreadable input is never `fresh`), `fresh`, the `changes` by category with
  their paths, `filesHashed`, and the `refreshClass` from the session's own classes (`Package` for
  a package, the root `app.json` or a source dependency; `Declaration` for a `.al` file added,
  removed or renamed; `BodyOnly` for `roots.config.json`, the coverage config or a nested
  `app.json` alone; `BodyOnly|Declaration`, not certain, for `.al` edits). A `headline` per engine
  and one for the whole answer say FRESH, STALE (what changed, the class, the next action), not
  checked (no engine for the workspace: `noEngine`, `check: null`), or that the check did not
  finish. The check runs on a checker thread in the MCP process: the reader loop keeps answering,
  and a busy engine child, worker or build never delays it, since it never goes through the
  engine's front end; it builds nothing and leaves the child's session alone. The old per-engine
  fields move under `details`. `refresh` gives the last `alsem_refresh`'s state (`idle`, `queued`,
  `running`, `completed`, `failed`) with what it did, its class and generation; an unwaited refresh
  is `queued` until a later call shows its outcome.
- **Measured on a copy of the CDO baseline** (cross-app, 582 `.al` files, 11 packages,
  `release-fast`, 2026-11-05; the machine was shared, load average 187-215, so these are upper
  bounds). Idle: a cached check took 2.6-4.7 ms, and the status answer arrived 4.0-6.5 ms after the
  call (10 runs; the spec's bar is 10 ms). A `verify` check hashed 594 files in 38-40 ms (answer
  40-42 ms). While a heavy `alsem_explain` ran on the same engine: 3.2-4.2 ms cached, 36 ms verify,
  and a `ping` sent during the check answered in 0.05-0.16 ms. After a body edit: STALE, 1 file
  hashed, category `al-file`, class `BodyOnly|Declaration`. With one source dependency of 579
  `.al` files: a cached check took 10-46 ms (it stats 1,173 files) and hashed 0 of them; the edit
  of one dependency file hashed exactly that file and was reported as `source-dependency` with its
  path and class `Package`; `verify` hashed 1,173 files in 190-330 ms. Before this milestone every
  cached check read and hashed all 579 dependency files.
- **`alsem_refresh` says what it did**: `did` is `rebuilt` (with `class`, `files`, `durationMs`,
  `generation`), `already-fresh`, or `queued` (`wait: false`). The child's `session/refresh`
  answer carries `built`, `class` and `changedFiles`.
- `changedPaths` (a `latest-built` answer's stale inputs) now also names a changed source
  dependency file and `al-sem.dependencies.json`; before, a source-dependency change gave no path
  at all. It is computed from `Manifest::changes`.

### Fixed (agent tasks, milestone F)

- **The `freshness: verify` description** said "answer from the built revision and report whether
  it is stale", but `verify` hashes every input and rebuilds first when anything changed. It now
  says so: "verify: like fresh, but hashes every input instead of trusting size and modification
  time; rebuilds first when anything changed." `fresh`'s text now says it trusts an unchanged size
  and modification time. A contract test pins the text and the behavior (a same-size,
  same-mtime rewrite: `fresh` keeps generation 1, `verify` rebuilds to generation 2).

### Added (agent tasks, milestone M0: resident groundwork)

Nothing an agent sees changes yet; these are the pieces the later milestones (the reverse cone,
test selection, adding an effect, impact) build on. Spec:
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-agent-tasks-design.md` §1.

- **The sited graph** (`program::impact_graph::sited`). The may-execute graph behind `alsem graph`,
  with one edge per site instead of one per `(caller, callee, kind)`: each site keeps its own id
  (its index), its source anchor (unit and span), its kind, confidence, `via`, conditions and an
  execution boundary (`Sync`, `Run`, `EventDispatch`, `TriggerOf{op}`, `Lifecycle`,
  `TestHandler`, `TestRunner`, `Open`). Nodes, sites and units are interned to `u32`. `alsem
  graph`'s edges are now computed by collapsing the sited graph with the old merge rule, folded in
  site order (strongest confidence wins, equal confidences keep the first `via` and union their
  conditions, the line is the minimum), so the export is byte-identical. The finer boundaries the
  spec names (checked against unchecked `Codeunit.Run`, background sessions and tasks, a
  trigger's temporary state) are body facts the program edges do not carry; R0 and A refine a
  `Run` or `TriggerOf` site by its anchor. Measured on CDO cross-app: 134,385 nodes, 318,084 sites,
  48 MB resident.
- **The sited graph as a revision artifact** (`ArtifactKey::Sited`). It can only be built where the
  program exists, so it is built inside the revision's build (the workspace session lends the
  program between its build and the model's, `refresh_lending`; single-app through
  `build_single_app_model_lending`) and seeded into the store before the revision publishes; it is
  never filled afterwards and never evicted. Under `--low-mem` its source facts parse the
  dependency trees again, as the model assembly does. **Built only when a question needs it**
  (owner decision, agent-tasks §13.3 answer 1): on CDO cross-app its build costs 0.93-1.19 s per
  body or declaration edit (CPU time equal to wall time: one thread), 0.84 s cold, and 45 MiB
  resident (`aldump --session-refresh --sited`, 2026-11-05), over the 300 ms bar. Under
  `--low-mem` it costs 2.1-2.4 s wall (about 26 s of CPU) per B or S edit, because its source facts
  parse the 10,881 dependency files again. `alsem graph` on CDO is byte-identical before and after
  (27.4 MB). `ResidentSession::pin_sited` pins as usual; when the revision has no graph it turns
  the graph on for every later revision and rebuilds once for this request
  (`Pinned::rebuilt_for: "sited"`). `alsem engine-host --graph` turns it on from the start. The
  request's cancellation stops that graph's build (polled every 4,096 sites): the revision is then
  published without it, and the next question builds it. `session/status` counts `sitedBuilds`,
  `lastSitedMs`, `lastSitedBytes`.
- **Graph-only sessions** (`ResidentSession::graph_only`, engine universe `graphOnly`): each build
  makes the cross-app program and its sited graph and no model (no L4, fold or trees), and
  publishes a `Built::Graph` revision. The workspace session still keeps what its next refresh
  reuses. It answers only jobs that read the sited graph (`ViewNeeds::sited`, `Job::sited`; the
  one-shot driver builds the graph off its lent program, so a resident answer equals the CLI's);
  any other command is refused with `this engine is graph-only (…): '<command>' needs a model`. A
  model revision built with its sited graph answers sited jobs too. The test universe and the
  impact base child will be of this kind.
- **Guard enrichment from pinned inputs** (`engine::resident::guards`, `Revision::site_guards`,
  `GraphRevision::site_guards`): the enclosing `if`/`else`/`case`/loop conditions of one site of
  the sited graph, outermost first, with their source text. The site's file is read from the
  revision's own read (a workspace file's pinned text, a source-folder dependency's, or a
  package's embedded source when the package's bytes are still the ones the read acquired), parsed
  again and walked down to the site's anchor, so the text is the revision's even after the disk
  moved. Nothing is kept per site; it works the same under `--low-mem`.
- **Needs-aware resident rows** (`ResidentSession::with_needs`, `pin_needs`). A published state
  records the assembly needs its model's rows were built with. A request that needs more pins with
  `pin_needs`: the session widens its needs and rebuilds once (`rebuilt_for: "needs"`, class
  `needs`, `session/status` `needsRebuilds`); the row cache misses every file whose recorded needs
  differ, so the rows are projected again; a rebuild the budget refuses is a `budget` refusal with
  its reason. No command needs more than the default (`ViewNeeds::EXPLAIN`) today; this makes the
  next gated need safe.
- **Admission for the sited graph.** A build that makes the sited graph reserves its estimate
  (`Case::Fill("sited")`, 120 MiB: 46 MiB measured resident on CDO plus its build's working set,
  not measured apart) on top of the build's own.
- **The input descriptor** (`session/descriptor`, `ResidentSession::descriptor`,
  `Pool::descriptor`): a published state's generation, inputs stamp, universe and manifest, every
  file entry with the stat its hash was taken at (`Manifest::descriptor_entries` /
  `from_descriptor_entries` round-trip it). After each call the pool's worker asks its child for
  it once per revision and keeps it in its snapshot, so a later freshness check can observe the
  disk against it without asking a busy engine.
- **Composite requests** (`Pool::run_composite`): a request that needs several engine children
  runs as a sequence of plain sub-requests, each part's outcome in order. A part is admitted only
  after the previous one is answered (its child released), and admission never waits: a part
  that cannot get a child says why (`the crossApp engine could not start: 2 engine children are
  running (--max-children) and none is idle (max-children 2)`) and the rest still run. The
  pool's own `busy` message gains the `(max-children N)` suffix.
- `aldump --session-refresh --sited` builds and keeps the sited graph at every step and prints its
  wall and CPU time, nodes, sites and bytes.

### Fixed (test infrastructure: a clock-dependent package fixture)

- **`an_in_place_overwrite_and_restore_during_consumption_is_refused` no longer fails on a
  slow machine.** The test fixture `write_minimal_app` (`src/snapshot/snapshot.rs`) built its
  `.app` with the `zip` crate's default entry time, which is the wall clock in 2-second steps.
  So "restore A" wrote bytes that differed from the first A whenever the two writes fell on
  different 2-second ticks: same length, another blake3. The test's precondition "the disk
  reads A both times" then failed. It happened once at a load average of 100–900, where the
  test's few milliseconds can stretch past a tick. Forcing the clock across a tick between
  the writes failed it every time; with the fix it passes. The fixture now stamps every entry
  with a fixed time, so its bytes depend on its arguments alone. Not a product bug: the
  consistency check compares content hashes only, never times, and still refuses the
  overwrite-and-restore.

### Fixed (test infrastructure: golden regeneration raced its readers)

- **A golden regen no longer rewrites committed files in place.** Under `scripts/check-goldens
  --regen`, cargo-nextest runs every test in its own process at once, and
  `output_fixture::fixture_app_matches_its_sources` rewrote
  `tests/fixtures/mcp-output/ws/.alpackages/probe_Out Base_1.0.0.0.app` with a truncate-then-fill
  write while other tests read it. One regen run loaded the dependency as symbol-only and wrote a
  wrong `tests/cli-output-goldens/explain.issuedoc.json`; the same race once failed
  `output_invariants::a_commit_beyond_an_entry_point_has_its_own_terminal_witness`. Every write
  into the tree during a test run (about 55 golden, fixture and record writers, including the
  `r3a*` goldens their `*_oracles` read and the `emit.policy-pins.yaml` golden `cli_policy_pins`
  uses as a policy) now goes through one helper, `tests/common/regen.rs::write_golden`: it writes
  nothing when the file already holds the bytes, and otherwise writes a temp file in the same
  directory and renames it over the target, so a reader sees the old file or the new one, never a
  part. The two shard regens (`cli_b_snapshot`, `cli_b_fingerprint`) no longer delete their
  directory before rewriting it; they drop stale files afterwards (`regen::remove_stale`). The
  dependency `.app` builder gained `symbol_app::source_app_bytes`, so the fixture test builds
  bytes instead of writing a file. A new `cli` member, `regen_atomic_writes`, pins the helper (a
  reader thread never sees a partial file while a writer swaps it 200 times; equal bytes keep the
  file's modification time) and the use: it scans every test source and fails when a function
  that consults the regen switch writes any other way, directly or through a same-file helper.

### Fixed (MCP output, step 1b: correctness and wording of agent answers)

- **`query touches` turned an index miss into a whole-cone "no".** `down` printed `no — this
  routine's cone does not touch the table` whenever the per-operation index (one routine into
  dependency code) held no operation on the table, and then warned on the next line that
  operations on a RecordRef may be that table. On CDO, IssueReminder vs `Data Exch.` said `no`
  beside 69 RecordRef operations, a cone that enters Base Application and calls not resolved. Now
  the answer is `no` only when nothing leaves room for an unseen touch (no operation on a table
  not resolved, no dependency code entered, every call resolved, the cone read and complete);
  otherwise `unknown — no indexed touch observed`, with each reason on its own line. JSON:
  `down.absence {answer: no | unknown | beyond, index, reasons[]}` (query schema 3.2.0,
  additive). The workspace-global list states the depth it stands on (`index` in JSON).
- **`query touches` called a hub's callers "not a finding".** RunReportID vs `CDO File` said `883
  transitive callers … not a finding`. Those callers inherit the touch and are its consumers: the
  line now says `883 transitive callers inherit this touch through this routine`, and the new
  `--callers` (MCP `callers: true`) names every caller with its depth and location without
  building `--all`'s caller × witness product (JSON `up.callers[]` with each caller's outcome).
- **`query effects` showed routes the root's literal arguments rule out, unmarked.** IssueReminder
  listed `CDO Queue Entry` through `DocHandle`, while explain shows that route cannot run with
  IssueReminder's literal arguments and the only live one re-enters from Base Application. Rows
  are still all kept and `via` is unchanged (ConTinAI reads them); each row the cone can judge now
  carries `literalRoute` (`ruledOut`: an effect it originates from is literal-dead; `notInCone`:
  the cone keeps no live write of that kind on that table; `otherRoute`: the cone keeps no live
  route through the row's first hop, and names the first hop its live route takes; `coneRoute`),
  and the human table line says so on the row it qualifies, with how many of the table's rows
  are ruled out. `summary.literalRoutes` counts them (query schema 3.2.0, additive).
- **An overloaded routine could not be selected.** `prove <ws> "CDO File::CreateDocumentFromReport"
  …` answered `routine-ambiguous … names 4 routines (Table CDO File::CreateDocumentFromReport, x4)`
  and told the agent to pass a stable id it never printed. Each candidate is now printed as the
  selector that picks it, with its location and stable id (`Table CDO
  File::CreateDocumentFromReport(Integer, Integer, Code[20], Text, Text, var RecordRef) at
  ws:src/Foundation/CDOFile.Table.al:132 (stable id …)`; JSON `candidateRoutines`), and the one
  selector grammar of explain, prove, digest and query takes a parameter list:
  `Owner::Routine(Integer, Text)`, by types (a length, `var` and AL quotes optional, or the type
  word alone) or by parameter names (`name: type` too). The tool descriptions and the server
  instructions say so.
- **"tests: none reach it" read the same with and without test code.** CDO holds no `[Test]`
  procedure, yet every explain said `tests: none reach it`, as if the routine were untested in a
  tested app. Explain now says `tests: no test code loaded (0 [Test] procedures in the workspace
  app); that is not a reason to skip tests` or `tests: N [Test] procedures loaded; none reaches it
  (not a reason to skip tests)`; the summary says `tests: none (no test code loaded)` or `tests:
  none of N loaded`, and JSON `summary.testsLoaded` gives N. Digest's `--tests` line says the same
  (`test coverage: no test code loaded …`, or `… loaded and considered; an unreached routine is
  not a reason to skip tests`).
- **Touch counts read as if the operation persisted.** `[CalcFields] read` rows were listed under
  "possibly persistent". The classes are the record's temp state, so they now read `on persistent
  records`, `on possibly persistent records` and `on temporary records`.

### Fixed (MCP output, the final hands-on CDO review)

- **`prove`'s human `unknown` no longer lists every blocker.** IssueReminder's
  `writes-table:Data Exch.` on CDO printed `blockedBy: 287 blocker(s)` and one line each: 294 lines
  and 47,875 bytes, over the 40 KiB inline cap, so the MCP answer went to a file. The blockers are
  now grouped by kind (in the order the kinds first appear), each kind with its count split by
  where the call site is (this workspace, dependency code, not placed) and its first 3 items,
  workspace ones first, since those are the ones the user can act on; the rest are counted on one
  line. `--detail` (MCP `detail: true`, new on `prove`) lists every blocker. The case is now 22
  lines and 2,076 bytes. The JSON `blockedBy` is unchanged and always complete. The coverage,
  assumptions and limits lines stay always visible.
- **A write in workspace code printed no path and no reason.** IssueReminder's `CDO Queue Entry`
  Insert (`CDODocumentTemplateLine.Table.al:1713`) printed its anchor and nothing else. Root cause:
  the cone listed three paths for it, all through `RunReportID → QueueMail`, which IssueReminder's
  literal arguments rule out; the literal pass dropped all three, while the write stayed live
  through a route the cone had not listed. The literal pass now searches the root's guarded search
  for such a row (the first live state owning one of the row's own operations, its evidence
  operation first) and keeps the witness; the line prints that real path, here one that re-enters
  workspace code beyond `Codeunit Reminder-Issue::OnRun` (and says so), or `no path kept:
  <reason>` (search cap reached; none of the row's operations can run in any reached state; no
  operation id). A write in the routine's own body prints `path: <routine> (in the routine
  itself)`, the zero-hop witness of design §3.4.2, where it printed nothing. Digest JSON carries
  the searched witness as `paths[0]` with `searched: true` (or `pathUnavailable`), prove's human
  evidence prints it, and explain JSON's `via` names it.
- **explain's entry-point counts disagreed with its sections.** The scope line counted the
  crossings with a may-persist write and summed their sites ("14 entry points at 14 sites" on
  IssueReminder), while the sections counted entry points ("12 … at 14 sites" with writes, "15 …
  at 17 sites" temporary only). Every line now counts entry points (crossings grouped by target, a
  multi-target crossing its own) at DISTINCT sites, and the scope line is the union of the two
  sections by identity: IssueReminder 27 entry points at 31 sites. The same counts in digest and
  query effects. `summary.entryPoints` gains `withWrites` and `withWritesSites`; `count` and
  `sites` are now every entry point and its distinct sites.
- **Tests**: the blocker fold (`prove::tests::human_blockers_fold_by_kind_workspace_first`), the
  searched witness on a hand-stated row whose listed path cannot run
  (`wave2_index_tests::an_own_row_whose_listed_paths_cannot_run_gets_a_searched_witness`), the
  entry-point unions (`routine_rollup::tests::entry_point_counts_are_unions_by_identity`), each
  with a discrimination proof; on the fixture and on CDO, every workspace-code write record has a
  path or a reason and the scope's entry-point counts equal the sections' union read off the
  `--detail` card (`output_invariants_w3::write_lines_have_a_path_and_entry_point_counts_agree`,
  `output_cdo::cdo_write_lines_have_a_path_or_a_reason`, `cdo_entry_point_counts_agree`); a CDO
  size ratchet and rendering golden for the Data Exch. case.

### Added (MCP output item T, the remaining output tests)

- **The invariants of item T and spec §8.3 not pinned before**, in the new `cli` member
  `output_invariants_w3` (fixture, every `cargo test`) and in `output_cdo` (CDO, `scripts/cdo-gate`):
  human-output hygiene (no blank name, `(no anchor)` row, `%20` or two identical lines; B1, B5,
  B6) and size budgets in lines AND bytes of the whole output with every line ≤ 2,000 characters
  (T-W2-15; on CDO per-routine ratchets pinned to the input stamps); every effect kind digest
  reports is on its line of explain's card (M2); every prove evidence row names its place or says
  `unavailable` (T-W2-17); every crossing prints its target's qualified display (T-W2-18);
  explain's groups list what they count and event groups carry only their count (T-W2-7); the
  fields the ConTinAI pipeline reads (T-W2-21); page actions folded to at most 3 lines, the
  grouped counts adding up to the listed actions (T-W2-14); every folded `… +N <unit>` line
  states its full count (T-W2-3, CDO); two budgets per `tools/call` result, the client's
  `structuredContent` and the whole wire (T-W2-23), with a hand-stated workspace whose card
  escapes to more than 50,000 characters while under the 40 KiB byte cap; IssueReminder's and
  RunReportID's default explain cards stay inline with at least 1 KiB of the cap to spare
  (RunReportID 37,671 bytes, a 3,289-byte margin, on `bc3ccb18`).
- **CDO rendering goldens** (`tests/cli-output-goldens/cdo/`, `output_cdo::cdo_rendering_goldens`):
  the explain card, query effects, query touches, prove may-commit and writes-table (human) and the
  digest summary of IssueReminder, RunReportID and UpdateLastUpload, byte-compared under
  `scripts/cdo-gate`, with `STAMP.json` holding the workspace's git sha, dirty flag and dependency
  closure (drift fails under `ENFORCE_CDO_WS=1`). Regenerate with `REGEN_TEMP_GOLDENS=1` and
  `CDO_WS` set for that one command.

### Fixed (MCP output item T)

- **An inline MCP answer could exceed the client's limit once escaped.** The 40 KiB inline cap
  counts raw bytes; a stdout of quotes and backslashes doubles in `structuredContent`, which Claude
  Code files past 50,000 characters. When the call leaves `maxInlineBytes` to the server, the pool
  now also sends an answer whose escaped form plus a 4 KiB envelope room exceeds 50,000 UTF-16
  units to a file, with its summary (`tools::MCP_CLIENT_BUDGET_CHARS`). A call that sets its own
  `maxInlineBytes` (the LSP front end does) keeps that cap exactly.
- **Three folded lists did not state their full count** (T-W2-3): the fields an owner assigns on a
  table (`(not operation-specific; N fields)`), events by publisher (`by publisher (N
  publishers)`) and the top dependency callees (`top callees (N callees)`) now state it when
  folded (`Folded::count_note`). Only CDO-sized outputs fold there; no fixture golden moves.
- **Two entry points into overloads of one routine printed one name** (T-W2-18 with T-W2-24).
  A crossing's name (explain's and query's `writes beyond dependency entry points` lines, the
  `crossings` records of explain `/3` and digest 3.x) is now its targets' qualified displays, an
  overload with its parameters, as the routine table prints it (`Codeunit CTS-CDN Network Doc.
  Mgt.::SendNetworkDocument(RecordVariant, eDocVariant, XMLDoc)` and its five-parameter twin, on
  CDO); a group row's raw `detail.boundary` is unchanged.

### Changed (MCP output wave 3b)

- **The MCP tool descriptions and server instructions are written around an agent's decisions**
  (plan 3b; E7, P6, D7, X10). The instructions say which tool answers which question, the one
  selector grammar, the line base and location forms (`ws:`, `dep:<app name>:`), the inline cap
  and the summary beside a file, each tool's dependency depth, the common inputs, and what `yes`,
  `no`, `unknown`, "no matching effect observed", `coverage`, `assumptions`, `limits`, temporary
  records and caller-dependent writes mean. Each command tool's description says what its default
  prints, how to ask for more (every input it takes, in backticks), the line base, typical sizes
  (measured on CDO: explain human 30-40 KB, query effects human 20-25 KB, digest JSON up to
  ~1 MB), its dependency depth and one next step; digest names `files`/`diff` as the change modes.
  `alsem_refresh` says when to use it. A test pins that every input a description names is in the
  tool's schema and every schema input is named
  (`output_invariants_w3::descriptions_name_exactly_the_inputs_the_schemas_take`).
- **One routine selector grammar for every tool.** `explain`, `prove` and `digest` now also take
  `Object.Routine` (read as `Object::Routine` at the last unquoted dot, only when no other form
  matched: `selector_index` form 6); `query effects --routine` and `query touches --from` now
  also take `Owner::Routine` and the owner's type word or AL quotes in either spelling
  (`selector_index::split_qualified`). No selector that resolved before resolves differently.
  Pinned by `output_invariants_w3::one_selector_grammar_for_every_tool` (seven spellings, five
  tools, byte-identical answers).

### Added (MCP output wave 3c)

- **`alsem_status` answers "is this current, and what is the engine doing?"** (plan 3c, S2).
  Each engine gains a `freshness` block: the answering revision (`generation`, `inputsStamp`,
  `engineInstanceId`, as every answer's envelope names it), the last build (`class`,
  `startedAtUnixMs`, `durationMs`, `builds`, `discardedBuilds`), the freshness checks
  (`freshHits`, `lastCheckUs`), `activity` (`idle`, `asking`, `pin`, `prepare`, `compute`,
  `refresh`) with `activityMs`, `building` (true in the `pin` phase or a refresh; `null` after an
  unwaited refresh until the next call), and the child's memory (`rssBytes`, `peakRssBytes`,
  `rssSource`: `live` from `/proc/<pid>/status` on Linux, else the child's last report) with
  `countersAgeMs`. The pool now asks every call's progress phases from the engine child (they
  were sent only for a client's progress token) and reads the child's counters after a waited
  `alsem_refresh`. The session stamps each build's start (`lastBuildStartedUnixMs`). A new
  engine test hook, `sleep-in-phase:<phase>:<ms>`, lets a test watch a call mid-phase
  (`mcp_server::faults::status_shows_a_build_in_progress`).

### Changed (MCP output wave 3a)

- **3a: query reads the whole cone for writes beyond dependency entry points.** `alsem query
  effects` (and `query touches --from` asked down) now declares a tree over its root
  (`session::query_cone_plan`) and reads the root's digest entry after the L4 temp-state join and
  the literal pass, exactly as `alsem explain` does. Its human output gains explain's own `writes
  beyond dependency entry points` section (the same function, `routine_rollup::beyond_lines`), a
  summary part `writes beyond dependency entry points on N tables through M entry points (K only
  there)`, and coverage/scope lines that say `dependency code: full cone for physical writes,
  grouped per entry point; per-operation detail one routine deep`. `query touches` lists the entry
  points beyond which the cone may write the table, and says `down: no operation one routine into
  dependency code touches the table` when only the cone does. Query JSON 3.1.0 (additive): the
  reserved `summary.byTable[].beyond` and touches' `down.beyond` are filled (`{entryPoint, sites,
  ops}`), `summary.beyondEntryPoints` and `summary.beyondWrites` are new, `summary.scope` reads
  `operations-one-routine-deep; writes-beyond-entry-points-full-cone`, and the MCP summary counts
  the writes beyond. Every per-operation row, `via` and L4 count is unchanged (ConTinAI reads
  them). On CDO (`bc3ccb18`): IssueReminder 131 tables beyond 12 entry points (was invisible to
  query), RunReportID 396. Cost: cold CLI `query effects` ~13 s → ~21 s at the same peak RSS
  (~3.1 GB); on the resident engine the first query builds what the first explain did, and a
  query and an explain on one root share the root's witness entry. The cross-tool agreement's
  query leg is per table (design §12.2): every table the cone names is in query's writes, query's
  beyond equals explain's, and the `CDO Log Attachment` `Modify` operations (literal-dead in the
  cone) are pinned by id (`output_cdo::cdo_query_effects_writes_agree_with_the_cone`). Goldens:
  `cli-query-goldens` and `cli-output-goldens` query files and `gate-goldens/batch/one-job` (the
  new lines and fields); `cli_build_counters::query_effects_cross_app` now expects the cone row.
- **Q4: "RecordRef" only where the receiver is one.** The body walk now records, per record
  operation, whether its receiver resolves lexically (parameters and locals before the object's
  globals) to a variable declared `RecordRef` (`PRecordOperation::receiver_is_record_ref`,
  forwarded to `ModelRecordOperation`; serde-skipped, read only by `alsem query`, so no detector
  input moved). `alsem query effects` splits its "table not resolved" bucket: `on a RecordRef
  (table decided at run time): N operations in M routines` and `table not resolved: …` for the
  rest, in the summary line, the bucket lines, the locks line and each `--all` row (was one
  `table not resolved (determined at run time or not resolved)` line for both). `query touches`
  says how many of the unresolved operations in the cone are on a RecordRef. Query JSON
  **3.1.0** (additive): such a row carries `receiver: "RecordRef"`;
  `summary.tableNotResolved.recordRef {operations, routines}` and
  `down.counts.tableNotResolvedRecordRef` count them. Goldens: `cli-query-goldens`,
  `cli-output-goldens` and `gate-goldens/batch/one-job` query files (version line, the new
  counts, the split wording); `ir-l2-goldens/l2_features.snapshot` (its `Debug` digest of every
  routine with a record operation shows the new field).

### Changed (MCP output wave 2, W2-4 … W2-8)

- **Digest size budgets decided (owner, 2026-11-04):** the default digest JSON (pretty) of `CDO
  Issue Document::IssueReminder` and `CDO E-Mail Handler::RunReportID` on the CDO baseline is at
  most 1,250,000 bytes whole and 720,000 bytes without event names; a CDO-gated ratchet
  (`output_cdo::cdo_digest_json_fits_its_size_budgets`, run by `scripts/cdo-gate`) pins both.

- **W2-4 (2d): a write states fields by its original operation kind.** `alsem explain`'s table
  writes print `fields X assigns on this table (not operation-specific): …` only for `Insert` and
  `Modify` (one clause per owning routine), `ModifyAll sets: F (in …)` for a `ModifyAll` (the
  operation's own field), `renames (primary key) in …` for a `Rename`, and nothing for `Delete`,
  `DeleteAll` and `LockTable` (before, every write listed every field its routine assigned on the
  table, a `DeleteAll` too). Explain JSON (`/3`, no outside reader): `fields` is now an object keyed
  by the owning routine's qualified display, beside `fieldOps` (`{op, field, in}`) and `renames`.
  A `Validate` is no digest write type; its field stays in its routine's assignments.
- **W2-5 (2e): every effect kind has its own bucket.** `alsem query effects`' locks line says
  `not writes`, marks a locked table that is also written `(also written)`, prints a lock-only
  table's first `LockTable` at its own anchor with its owner, and counts the locks on a table not
  resolved. The `--all` row of such an operation reads `table not resolved: determined at run time
  or not resolved` (was `target table unresolved — not a table`). Explain and digest put an effect
  type no kind family names into an explicit `other effect kinds` bucket (JSON `otherKinds`, only
  when used) instead of dropping it; today every digest effect type has a family. `Validate` is
  no operation of either substrate (a trigger-class op: its effects are its `OnValidate`'s), so
  query's `validate` bucket stays empty on real code.
- **W2-6 (2f): every group gets a real witness, COMMIT and resource-less groups included.** The
  literal pass gives a resource-less group (COMMIT, HTTP, UI, …) its own terminal witness through
  its crossing to a live state owning a direct fact of its type (W2-0b's suffix search), or the
  reason it has none. Prove JSON **2.3.0** (additive): such evidence carries `groupPath`,
  `crossing`, `throughEntryPoint` and `groupWitness` (or `groupPathUnavailable`). Prove human
  prints where each effect sits (`[COMMIT] beyond Codeunit X::OnRun, entered at …`, `[DB_INSERT]
  at …`) and its path, ending `(<Kind> at <terminal anchor>)`; `evidence: N effects`. Explain and
  digest human print a commit-bearing entry point's own COMMIT path, and per entry point one
  `representative path (<table>, the nearest of N tables)` (it names the site it passes when the
  entry point has several); `--detail` prints every table's witness, or why it has none. Digest
  JSON 3.x: a COMMIT / HTTP / UI / ERROR group row carries its representative witness in `paths`
  (or `pathUnavailable`); explain JSON's resource-less group rows carry `paths` and `pathOutcome`.
- **W2-7 (2g): readable dependency locations and `--show-source`.** Every human output of
  explain, digest, prove and query prints a dependency location as `dep:<app name>:<path>:<line>`
  (`dep:Base Application:src/Sales/Reminder/ReminderIssue.Codeunit.al:182`), the name followed by
  ` (<first 8 of the guid>)` when two loaded apps share it, and `%20` as a space. JSON keeps
  `dep:<guid>:` (the `aldump --dump-dependency-source` citation contract). `alsem explain` and
  `alsem query effects` / `touches` take `--show-source` (MCP `showSource`): the cited line ±2,
  marked `>`, under each location, from the same text the dump command writes.
- **W2-8 (2h): prove states its coverage, assumptions and limits.** The human answer's
  `obligations:` line is replaced by three always-visible lines: `coverage: complete` or
  `incomplete — N calls not resolved (K in this workspace), M interface calls open world (L in
  this workspace); top: <callee> ×n, …`; `assumptions:` with the answer's world label
  (`loaded-subscribers`, `closed-world`) or `none (default world; …)`; `limits:` (analysis gaps,
  cone truncation) or `none`. An absence the obligations block reads `answer: unknown — no
  matching effect observed; coverage incomplete`; `yes` and `no` print bare (prove's answer is
  authoritative; the JSON `answer` is unchanged). Prove JSON 2.3.0 (additive): `obligations`
  gains `unresolvedInWorkspace {notResolved, openWorld}` and `topUnresolvedCallees` (3).
- **One answer to "does R write T" across explain, digest and prove, by construction.** `alsem
  explain --routine R --writes-table T` and `alsem digest … --writes-table T` (repeatable; MCP
  `writesTables`) print prove's own answer per table (`cards[].tableAnswers`,
  `entries[].tableAnswers`: `answer`, `evidence`, `blockedBy`, `assumptions`; a human line per
  table): all three call one evaluation, `prove::TableQuestions::answer` (classification,
  field-guarded matches, caller resolution, the obligation rules, the loaded-subscribers label).
  Such a run counts the cones' analysis gaps, as prove's plan does. Not with `digest --schema 2`.
- **Routines that share a display print apart** (T-W2-24): an overload in the same app prints its
  parameter names (`Note(Msg, Level)`; the typed list when two overloads share the names), a
  routine of another app with the same
  qualified display gets ` [<app name>]`, in path lines and every qualified display (digest's
  `payload.routines[].display` included).
- **Workspace-code write lines count operations**: `Out Item: Insert 1, ModifyAll 1, Rename 1`,
  the section header saying these are the cone's retained representative operations (at least
  that many). Exact counts need the per-root reach of the terminal-fact index, which the passed
  entry does not keep (left open).
- **Entry-point table names are nearest first**: by each table's witness length through the
  entry point, then by name (was alphabetical).

### Fixed (#369: dependency writes with no witness path, and colliding `factId`s)

- **A write deep in dependency code through a `var` record parameter now gets its witness.** Such
  a write takes its temp class from the caller, so only the proof walk (`enumerate_proofs`) can
  witness it. Past the crossing into dependency code the walk listed every simple path until one
  reached the write, which grows exponentially with depth; on the CDO baseline every one of the 78
  facts behind the 77 no-path rows of `CDO Issue Document::IssueReminder` (57) and `CDO E-Mail
  Handler::RunReportID` (20) spent the 25 000-state limit first (the writes sat 13–35 calls deep).
  The crossing already fixes the candidate's key, so the walk now asks only whether the write is
  reachable below it: one breadth-first search over states, each visited once (`seed_reach`). The
  rows become members of the group of their crossing. None of the issue's hypotheses H1–H4 held.
- **An unresolved write is never witnessed by a typed one.** The witness's carrier test let a
  typed insert carry an insert whose table is not known (`fact_equivalent` compares tables only
  when both name one), so an unresolved RecordRef insert in Continia Delivery Network was shown at
  a workspace `CDO Queue Entry` / `CDO E-Mail Log` insert, with that row's path and `factId`. A
  carrier now names a table exactly when the fact does (as the proof walk already required); the
  write is counted in its crossing's group as unresolved.
- **A digest row with no terminal id is keyed by its first originating operation and its
  resource** (`build_canonical_key`'s terminal id, and the resource beside the effect type as
  `DB_READ` already had), so no-path rows no longer share one `factId` per effect type. A row
  with no originating operation either (an `EVENT_PUBLISH`, which has no operation id) is keyed by
  its resource alone, so two such publishes of different events on one path cannot share an id.
  Goldens moved for this alone, each an `EVENT_PUBLISH` row's `factId` (and `canonicalKey`):
  `tests/cli-b-goldens/digest/ws-d8-commit-in-tx{.json,.v3.json,.diff.json}`,
  `tests/cli-b-goldens/prove/ws-d8-commit-in-tx.publishes-event-onafterpostsalesdoc.json`,
  `tests/cli-output-goldens/digest.issuedoc{,.detail}.json`,
  `tests/r4f-goldens/ws-txn-d47-event-pos.digest.golden.json`. No consumer keyed on the old collision: `ordering_facts` and the ordering engine key by
  `factId` within one entry (a collision merged two rows' data there), and `alsem diff` keys its
  capabilities `op|resourceKind|resourceId`.
- CDO baseline `bc3ccb18`, before → after: IssueReminder 275 rows (222 distinct `factId`s, 57
  no-path rows over 5 ids) → 220 rows, all distinct, 0 no-path; RunReportID 227 (210, 20 over 4) →
  206, all distinct, 0 no-path. Pinned by `cdo_i369_no_path_rows_and_fact_ids`.
- **One prove verdict moves:** IssueReminder `writes-table:Data Exch.` goes from `yes` to
  `unknown`. The `yes` rested only on a no-path row. Its write is now in five groups (one
  DB_DELETE, two DB_INSERT, two DB_MODIFY) on two crossings, both `literal-dead`, checked by hand
  in the source: `Incoming Document Attachment.Insert(true)` at
  `CDOElectronicDocumentMgt.Codeunit.al:182` (into `Table Incoming Document Attachment::OnInsert`)
  runs only after `if not (RecordFilter.Number in [Database::"Sales Invoice Header",
  Database::"Sales Cr.Memo Header"]) then exit;` (line 170), and `Codeunit.Run(Codeunit::"Sales-Calc.
  Discount", SalesLine)` at `CDOFile.Table.al:125` only after `if RecRef.Number <> Database::"Sales
  Header" then exit;` (line 115). IssueReminder passes an `Issued Reminder Header` (table 297), and
  its kept paths enter through `RunReportID`'s `OutputAction::CreateElectronicDoc` and `::SaveAsPDF`
  branches while `DocHandle` passes `OutputAction::Handle`. The other 72 prove questions checked on
  both roots keep their verdict.

### Changed (MCP output wave 2, W2-2 part 4: `query effects` summary first; first hops)

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-mcp-output-wave2-design.md` (revision 3) §4.5, §4.6.

- **`query effects` human is summary first.** One `summary:` line puts every operation in exactly
  one bucket, in this precedence: table not resolved, then the write class of its temp state
  (temporary records; caller-dependent writes), then the op family (writes that may persist,
  locks, validate — never a read —, reads, unclassified). Then `coverage:` and `scope:` lines
  (the `dependencies:` first line moves into the scope line as a count; `--all` names the apps),
  writes that may persist and caller-dependent writes per table (operation counts, `+ LockTable`
  on a table also written, the first operation's location and owner, and `through <first hop>`),
  locks, validate, reads, temporary records and table-not-resolved as counts, and `next:`.
  `--all` (new; MCP `all`) adds one line per operation, the old layout.
- **JSON (query 3.0.0, additive):** `payload.summary` (`writes {operations, tables,
  knownPersistent, tempStateUnknown}`, `callerDependent`, `locks`, `validate`, `reads`,
  `unclassified`, `temporary {operations, tables, routines}`, `tableNotResolved {operations,
  routines}`, `byTable[{table, tableId, ops, class, first, beyond: []}]`, `scope`), and on every
  row that is not the routine's own, `firstHop` (the routine) or `firstHop: null` with
  `firstHopUnavailable`. Every existing row field is unchanged (`via`, `origin`, …).
- **`firstHop` is a real association**: the first direct callee, in sorted order, whose summary
  holds a row equal to the row's complete contribution (operation id, table, op kind and its
  temp state here); otherwise none, with the reason. `query touches` prints the same
  `through <first hop>` on its witness lines, and its scope line carries the dependencies count
  (W2-3's leftovers).

### Changed (MCP output wave 2, W2-2 part 3: digest human, digest JSON 3.0.0, `--schema 2`)

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-mcp-output-wave2-design.md` (revision 3) §4.3, §4.4,
§4.7, §5.

- **Digest human** prints, per root, explain's effect sections through the same functions
  (summary, coverage, assumptions, limits, scope, commits, writes in workspace code,
  caller-dependent writes, writes beyond entry points, writes with no path kept, literal-dead
  tables, temporary records, events, kind families, gaps), then its diagnostics as counts by
  kind and reason (each with its operation under `--detail`). The old per-row
  `[TYPE] direct / evidence / detail / via` blocks are gone.
- **Digest JSON 3.0.0** (major) is the default: every effect row kept (multiplicity included),
  with `status` (`live` / `literal-dead`) and `class` / `classReason` on table writes; paths as
  `paths: [{hops: [{edge, to, line, file?}], terminal}]` whose `to` is a key of the new
  `payload.routines` table (`r:` + 12 hex of the stable id's SHA-256, extended on a collision),
  one path on a decision effect by default (may-persist and caller-dependent writes, COMMIT,
  HTTP, FILE, BACKGROUND_TASK, ISOLATED_STORAGE, TELEMETRY, UI_*, ERROR_*), none on events,
  reads and temporary rows, with `pathsKept`, `pathsOmitted` and `pathsProducerTruncated` (the
  old `viaPaths` / `viaPathsTruncated`); group rows name their `crossing` (a key of the new
  `entries[].crossings`, which holds the id, boundary, targets, sites and prefix once) instead
