  of the "enters X" evidence, list every table as `resources[{id, display}]` and every event
  as `eventsByPublisher[{publisher, events}]`, and a may-persist group row carries one
  representative terminal witness (`paths[0].representative`); `detail.resources` (the
  first-ten string) is dropped; only non-trivial `scopedGuarantees` (`scopedGuaranteesFolded`
  counts the rest); `entryDiagnosticCounts` instead of `entryDiagnostics`; `unresolved` holds
  workspace and not-placed call sites (`candidateCount` for `candidates`) and
  `unresolvedInDependencies` the dependency ones as counts and top callees; new
  `entries[].summary` (`RollupTotals`), `coverage.assumptions` / `coverage.limits`,
  `payload.pathCap`. `entries[].routine` (anchor and anchors), `factId`, `detail.tempState`,
  `provenance`, `conditionality`, `transactionContext` and `guarantees` are unchanged.
- **New flags**: `--detail` (unfolded 3.x: every path up to 3, every scoped guarantee,
  diagnostic, unresolved item and per-resource group witness), `--compact` (no indentation),
  `--max-paths N` (now honoured: paths per effect, at most 3), `--schema 2` (the 2.2.0 document,
  the old shape over the current analysis, for one release window; with `--detail`,
  `--max-paths` or `--compact` it exits 2). MCP `alsem_digest` takes `detail`, `maxPaths`,
  `compact` and `schema`. `run_digest_pipeline` (the in-process API) keeps the 2.x document;
  `run_digest_pipeline_render` renders either.
- **Prove's evidence serializer is its own** (`prove::evidence_value`, a copy of the 2.x effect
  shape), so the digest redesign never moves prove's JSON; prove output is unchanged.

### Changed (MCP output wave 2, W2-2 part 2: the explain card, human and `al-sem.explain/3`)

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-mcp-output-wave2-design.md` (revision 3) §4.1, §4.2, §5.

- **Explain reads the L4 temp-state join.** `explain_plan` now declares `l4` with its tree, and
  the card reads the root's digest entry after the join and the literal pass, so every write has
  the class digest and prove give it (physical, caller-dependent, temporary). Explain now pays the
  L4 build that `digest` and `query` already pay (measured in the W2-2 commits).
- **The human card is summary first.** One `summary:` line (tables it may write, owned by the app
  and by dependencies, and writes on a table not resolved; caller-dependent tables; commits;
  events; each present kind family; callers and page actions; tests; gaps by where), then
  `coverage:`, `assumptions:`, `limits:`, `notes:` (when present) and `scope:`, then rules,
  callers (page actions grouped by caption and page object past 3), commits with their sites and
  commit-bearing entry points, writes in workspace code (one block per table: kinds, class, the
  representative witness's anchor and path, the fields each owner assigns), caller-dependent
  writes, writes beyond dependency entry points (one line per entry point: sites, tables per kind,
  names folded at 12, other kinds, events), writes with no path kept (by the owner's app, with the
  owner and location the operation index recovers), literal-dead tables, temporary records (never
  writes), events by publisher, extension points (never a group), one line per kind family (UI,
  HTTP, file, background tasks, isolated storage, telemetry, errors), tests, gaps in workspace
  code, gaps in dependency code as counts and top callees, and `next:`. A group row never prints
  with an empty name and never becomes an extension point.
- **`al-sem.explain/3`** (major): `cards[].summary` (`RollupTotals` plus `callers`,
  `pageActions`, `tests`), `coverage {status, reasons, assumptions, limits, notes}`; each write
  carries `class`, `classReason`, `opKinds` and its `tempState`; a group row carries `crossing`
  (listed once in `effects.crossings` with its targets, target ids, sites and prefix),
  `resourceCount` and every `resources[]` entry instead of `table: ""` / `tableId: ""` and the
  "enters X" anchor; an event group carries its count (`resourcesListed: false`; the names with
  `--detail`); a write with no witness carries `noPathKept` and the recovered `owner`;
  `effects.{http, file, backgroundTasks, isolatedStorage, telemetry, errors}` beside `ui`;
  `reachedFromSummary`, `gapsInDependencies`; `effects.commits` is `yes`, `may`, `none` (complete
  coverage, no limit) or `no observed` (was `no`). Folded by default and complete with `--detail`: a page action's `via` and
  `tooltip`, dependency gaps, event-group names. `fields` and `via` keep their names. No outside
  reader: the editor extension uses only the call-hierarchy and property requests (plan §4.1).
- **New flags** `explain --detail` (every list, no fold) and `--max-paths N` (paths per item:
  default 1, 3 with `--detail`, at most 3); MCP `alsem_explain` takes `detail` and `maxPaths`
  (passed only when set, so `detail` alone gives 3).

### Changed (MCP output wave 2, W2-2 part 1: one rollup and one summary for every effects output)

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-mcp-output-wave2-design.md` (revision 3) §3.1, §3.6,
§3.8 rule 4.

- **New `engine::l5::routine_rollup`.** One root's digest entry (after the L4 temp-state join and
  the literal pass) is sorted once into sections: writes in workspace code (one record per table),
  caller-dependent writes, crossings into dependency code (by the crossing's identity, with the
  refined resource lists), writes with no path kept (with the owner the operation index
  recovers), temporary records, literal-dead tables, commits, events, the other kind families and
  the gaps by where the call site is. `RollupTotals` is the one summary every output prints;
  every total is a union by identity, never a sum of section counts.
- **The digest MCP summary (1b) prints `RollupTotals`.** Per root: `summary` (`mayWriteTables
  {count, ownedByApp, byDependencies}`, `unresolvedTableWrites`, `callerDependentTables`,
  `commits {answer, ownSites, entryPoints}`, `events`, `kinds`, `gaps {workspace, dependency,
  notPlaced}`, `temporaryOnlyTables`, `literalDeadTables`, `noPathKept`, `entryPoints`) and
  `names` (first tables owned by the app and by dependencies, entry points, top callees). The
  old `physicalTablesWritten`, `temporaryTablesWritten`, `commits`, `boundariesEntered`,
  `unresolved`, `writesWithoutTable` and `callerDependentTablesWritten` fields are gone.
  Literal-dead resources count nowhere; temporary contributions never count as writes.
- **One fold helper.** `routine_rollup::fold` (the cap, or every item when at most a quarter
  more; tables 12, all when 15 or fewer) replaces `query touches`' local `fold_len`.

### Changed (MCP output wave 2, W2-1b: the literal pass memoized per revision; schema bumps)

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-mcp-output-wave2-design.md` (revision 3) §3.1, §11.10.

- **The context server memoizes each root's effects AFTER the literal pass.** The pass now runs
  where a root's entry is made (`digest_cli::passed_root_entries`, one `LiteralReach` per batch of
  roots), and the revision's `Witness` artifact keeps that passed entry, so a second ask on the
  same root and revision (digest, explain or prove) pays nothing for the pass. The CLI builds it
  per read as before. Answers are unchanged: the pass was already run by every effects reader on
  its own copy, and it is idempotent.
- **Digest JSON 2.1.0 → 2.2.0** for W2-1's additive `literalUnreachable` and W2-0c's
  `resourcesOriginalCount`. **Explain JSON `al-sem.explain/2` → `al-sem.explain/2.1`** for its
  additive `literalUnreachable` (`/3` stays the redesign's). Goldens: the version line only.

### Changed (MCP output wave 2, W2-3: `query touches` computes less and says more)

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-mcp-output-wave2-design.md` (revision 3) §4.6, T-W2-10.

- **The `up` answer no longer builds every caller's witnesses.** Before, `query touches --from R`
  read every witness of every transitive caller that touches the table and printed one line per
  witness. On the CDO baseline, `RunReportID` vs `CDO File` was 180,340 human lines (36.8 MB) and
  a 257 MB JSON document; `IssueReminder` vs `CDO File` 412 lines (74 KB). Now, when R touches the
  table itself (the trivial case: every caller then touches it through R), each caller is only
  probed — "has a summary row?" first, then "touches the table?" — and `up` is one line:
  `883 transitive callers: 883 touch it, 0 do not, 0 unknown — through this routine; not a
  finding`. A caller with no summary row is counted as unknown, never as "does not touch", and
  the callers that do not touch or are unknown are named. When R does not touch the table (the
  informative case), each touching caller's witnesses are streamed into its first witness, its
  count and its class counts; one line per caller. `--all` (MCP `all: true`) gives every caller
  witness as before.
- **`down` counts touches by class.** Each touch is known persistent (`known(false)`), possibly
  persistent (temp state unknown, or caller-dependent through a parameter) or on a temporary
  record. Temporary-record touches persist nothing, but they use the table's schema and run its
  triggers and table-event subscribers, so they are counted and listed under `--all`, never
  dropped; the default human form folds them into one line naming the routines that own them.
  Operations on a table that was not resolved are counted apart ("they may be this table"):
  `tableNotResolved` is outside the three class counts, except for `--table unknown`, where those
  operations are the witnesses themselves and `tableNotResolved` equals `witnessCount`.
  Human lines name the operation family (read, write, lock, validate, unclassified) and the
  owning routine: `[Insert] write at <file>:<line> in <routine> (temp state unknown)`. Lists are
  folded in the default human form (8, or all when there are at most 10; the workspace-global
  list 12, or all up to 15).
- On CDO (release-fast, one batch per binary, model built once): `RunReportID` vs `CDO File` is
  now 12 human lines (2,099 B) and 202,063 B of JSON; `IssueReminder` vs `CDO File` 12 lines
  (2,136 B) and 202,070 B of JSON. The four answers (human and JSON, both routines) cost 5.9 s
  and 285 MB of peak RSS on top of the model before; now under 0.1 s and no measurable RSS.
- **Query JSON 3.0.0** (`query touches` and `query effects`; the spec gives W2-2's `query
  effects` changes the same major). `query touches`: `up` drops `witnesses` by default (only
  `--all` has it) and gains `callersNotTouching`, `callersUnknown`, `notTouching[]`, `unknown[]`
  (with `reason`), and in the informative case `callers[]` (`depth`, `routine`, `witnessCount`,
  `counts`, `firstWitness`); `down` gains `counts` (`knownPersistent`, `possiblyPersistent`
  {`tempStateUnknown`, `callerDependent`}, `temporary`, `tableNotResolved`, `byOp`), the
  reserved wave-3 `beyond: []`, and a `touchClass` on each witness. `query effects` changes only
  its `schemaVersion`.
- Not yet (they wait on W2-2): the `through <first hop>` on an inherited touch (the shared
  `firstHop` rule of §4.5) and moving the `dependencies:` line into the scope line.

### Changed (MCP output wave 2, W2-1: one classifier and one literal pass for every reader)

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-mcp-output-wave2-design.md` (revision 3) §3.1, §3.2,
§3.2.1, §11.8.

- **One write classifier** (`engine::l5::rollup::classify`): `Physical` (known persistent, temp
  state unknown, or not joined), `CallerDependent` (a record parameter, or the implicit `Rec`) or
  `Temporary`, from a row's joined `tempState`. Prove's G17/G17b tests call it; every prove
  verdict is byte-stable.
- **`evaluate_writes_table`** (`engine::l5::prove`) is the one implementation of "does the root
  write table T": the classification plus field-guarded matches, caller resolution and the
  obligation rules. Prove's `writes-table` calls it; explain and digest are to call it when they
  state a table answer (W2-2).
- **Digest and explain read their effects after prove's literal pass** (literal reach, G33 and
  W2-0c's crossing-local status), so the three tools judge the same facts. Raw versus refined: a
  row the root cannot reach under literal arguments stays, marked — digest JSON
  `literalUnreachable: true`, digest human `(ruled out by literal arguments)`, explain JSON
  `literalUnreachable: true` and explain human `, ruled out by literal arguments`; a literal-dead
  COMMIT no longer makes explain's commit unconditional; a group's refined list and counts follow
  W2-0c's rules; a listed path that cannot run is dropped, as prove already did. Only table
  writes are judged beyond a crossing (`DB_READ` and event groups are never pruned).
- **The digest MCP summary (1b) uses the three classes**: a caller-dependent table is no longer a
  `physicalTablesWritten` table and is counted as `callerDependentTablesWritten` (present only
  when non-zero); a literal-dead write counts nowhere. On the MCP fixture `Out Doc` (a `Modify`
  on `IssueDoc`'s `var` record parameter) moves out of `physicalTablesWritten.workspaceNames`.
- No golden file moved: no fixture has a literal-dead row, a dead path or a disproved resource.
  One test expectation moved (`output_invariants::digest_summary_through_mcp_on_the_fixture`, the
  1b change above).

### Fixed (MCP output wave 2, W2-0c step 2: prove drops a group resource its crossing cannot reach)

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-mcp-output-wave2-design.md` (revision 3) §3.3.1, §11.7.

- **A dependency group no longer lists, for prove, a table its own crossing cannot write.** A
  resource whose status is `Disproved` (step 1) leaves the group's refined list; the raw list is
  kept, and the group prints `resourcesOriginalCount`. A resource not established is never
  dropped. Before, the literal pass judged a resource at the root only: a write live through one
  crossing (or any other route) kept it in every group that listed it.
- **One CDO verdict moves**, checked by hand: `prove "CDO Issue Document::IssueReminder"
  writes-table:"Email Connector Logo"` goes from `yes` to `unknown`. Its only evidence was the
  `DB_INSERT` group beyond `Codeunit Email Account::IsAnyAccountRegistered` (called at
  `ws:src/Features/Email/Sending/CDOEMail.Codeunit.al:254`); System Application's
  `IsAnyAccountRegistered` calls `GetAllAccounts(false, …)`, which inserts the logo only `if
  LoadLogos then`, so the write cannot run there. With no evidence left, prove's open-world
  obligations (interface calls in that code) block an absence proof, so the answer is `unknown`,
  not `no`. RunReportID `writes-table:"CDO E-Mail Log"`, IssueReminder `writes-table:"Issued
  Reminder Header"` and `may-commit`, and both digests are byte-identical to step 1. No fixture
  golden moved.

### Added (MCP output wave 2, W2-0c step 1: a group resource's status beyond its own crossing)

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-mcp-output-wave2-design.md` (revision 3) §3.3.1, §11.6.

- **Prove's read now judges every table resource of a dependency group from that group's own
  crossing** (`LiteralReach::resource_status`): from each entry state of the crossing (the W2-0b
  prefix phase), the suffix search either reaches a live state of an operation that could write
  the table (`Reachable`), or completes having reached a candidate's owner with guards ignored
  and no state where it can run (`Disproved`), or concludes nothing (`NotEstablished`, with its
  reason: no entry, no operation, a search stopped early, an owner not reached even with guards
  ignored, or not a table write). The candidates are every direct fact of the table and kind in
  the group's class (the terminal-fact index), parameter-dependent producers always included, not
  only the group's representative operations. Recorded on `DigestEffectResult::
  group_resource_status`; this step drops nothing.
- **The group path reads the same candidates** (W2-0b used the representatives only). On CDO,
  RunReportID's `CDO E-Mail Log` group beyond `Codeunit Sales-Calc. Discount::OnRun` had
  `groupPathUnavailable: "no-witness"`; it now has a 27-hop path that passes the crossing: `…
  Sales-Calc. Discount.CalculateInvoiceDiscount → Sales Line.OnDelete → … Workflow Response
  Handling.PostDocument → Sales-Post.OnRun → … event-dispatch → CDO Subscribers.
  OnRunOnBeforeFinalizePostingSalesPost → MoveLogsForSalesDocs → MoveEmailLog` (checked in the
  CDO source: the subscriber of `Sales-Post`'s `OnRunOnBeforeFinalizePosting` moves the log
  entries). Verdicts and evidence rows are unchanged.
- **Raw versus refined (design §3.1).** A prove group whose refined membership is shorter than its
  raw one (today: G33's literal-dead resources) now describes the list it prints:
  `detail.resourceCount` counts it, `detail.resources` names its first ten, and
  `detail.resourcesOriginalCount` keeps the raw count. Before, the count was the raw one beside a
  shorter list.

### Fixed (MCP output wave 2, W2-0b: G1, a group's path now passes its entry point)

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-mcp-output-wave2-design.md` (revision 3) §3.4.3, §11.5.

- **`prove writes-table:T`'s `groupPath` on a dependency group now traverses that group's
  crossing.** Before, the path was the first state of the root's guarded search that owned one
  of the resource's operations, so a shorter workspace route to the same operation won: on the
  CDO baseline, `RunReportID`'s `CDO E-Mail Log` group "beyond `Codeunit Sales-Calc.
  Discount::OnRun`" was shown a 10-hop path through workspace code only. Now the path is the
  root's search up to one of the crossing's typed edges (matched by source, target and site),
  then a search from that entry with the bindings the prefix established, so a literal argument
  at the crossing still decides what runs beyond it. Verdicts, evidence rows and the resources a
  group lists are unchanged. On CDO that group now has no path through `Sales-Calc.
  Discount::OnRun` at all (`groupPathUnavailable: "no-witness"`): no live route through the
  crossing reaches that `Modify`, which W2-0c's crossing-local resource status will decide on.
  `IssueReminder`'s `Issued Reminder Header` paths were already through `Reminder-Issue::OnRun`
  and are unchanged.
- When a writes-table group match has no path, prove now says why instead of printing nothing:
  `groupPathUnavailable` (`no-witness`, `search-cap`, `cancelled` or `no-operation-id`) and the
  `crossing` searched.
- **Prove JSON 2.2.0 (additive).** A writes-table group match keeps `groupPath` (`resource`, and
  `hops` as the same strings) and gains beside it `crossing` (the boundary identity),
  `throughEntryPoint`, `throughEntryPointReason` (only when false: `search-cap` or `cancelled`)
  and `groupWitness`: `hops` (`edge`, `edgeId`, `to` stable id, qualified `display`, `file` and
  1-based `line` of the edge in its calling routine) and `terminal` (`operationId`, `file`,
  `line`). Every prove document's `schemaVersion` moves to 2.2.0.
- The suffix searches are cached per entry state (target, bindings) for the whole read: at most
  400,000 states per tree and 1,600,000 over all trees, the oldest tree evicted first. A suffix
  search that stops early falls back to the root's own path, which is checked for crossing
  membership: through the crossing it is an ordinary witness, otherwise it is labelled
  `throughEntryPoint: false`. Cancellation is checked every 4,096 states (production reads pass
  "never": a shared fill is not cancelled by a request).
- Event crossings: the CDO baseline has none (813 call-site and 15 operation crossings;
  `cdo_crossing_census`); they are handled by the same code, fixtured only by hand.
- Cost on CDO (`release-fast`; the machine was under heavy outside load, load average 100–400, so
  wall times are not comparable and the in-process spans are quoted): prove's group-path work
  (`prove.reach_effects`) RunReportID `writes-table:CDO E-Mail Log` 16.26 s → 3.45 s,
  IssueReminder `writes-table:Issued Reminder Header` 3.14 s → 0.17 s, IssueReminder `may-commit`
  0.66 s → 0.65 s (the old search scanned the root tree per resource; the new one looks a
  resource's owner up in an index per tree). Peak RSS 3.10–3.13 GB before and after. Over every
  group resource of IR and RR (16,776) the cache built 30 suffix trees, peak 48,840 states,
  nothing evicted.

### Fixed (the context-server store refilled a key that was already published)

- **`Store::ensure_prepared` no longer fills a published key a second time.** A request read
  the published snapshot BEFORE it took the registry lock, then claimed every key that
  snapshot lacked. A key another request published in between was `Published` in the
  registry (so nothing to join) but missing from the stale snapshot, so the request claimed
  it and filled it again: a duplicate L4 solve or fold for nothing, and the same stale read
  behind b41a3b01's witness failure. Now the snapshot is read under the registry lock. Every
  writer of the snapshot (publish, evict, tombstone) holds that lock, so there a `Published`
  key is always in the snapshot read. Test:
  `a_request_never_claims_a_key_published_after_it_read_the_snapshot`: a test-only hook
  (`Store::before_claim`, absent outside `cfg(test)`) holds request 1 at the top of its claim
  section while request 2 fills and publishes `X`; request 1 must fill nothing. The window is
  between two of the store's own statements with no callback in it, so only a hook can hold a
  request there. Discrimination: the snapshot read moved back above the hook fails it (2
  fills of `X`); reverted, it passes. `a_request_publishes_its_claims_before_it_waits_for_a_joined_key`
  now asserts `X` is filled once (it allowed two): under the break it fails 6 of 60 runs; with
  the fix 0 of 200. Stress: 200 runs of the `engine::resident` tests with every core busy
  (22 busy loops, machine load average ~150): 200 passed, none hung.
- **Checked, not changed: the `TreeBase` fill builds a fresh `big_stack_pool()` each time.**
  Building the 22-worker pool costs ~0.9 ms against a ~1.5 s `tree.base` on CDO (~0.06%),
  and a dropped pool's threads end within 50 ms, so an idle engine holds none. A
  process-wide pool would keep 22 big-stack threads for the process's life for a saving
  below the noise. The reason is now written on `big_stack_pool`.

### Changed (#368: `analyze --with-evidence` and `policy check` lines are 1-based)

The rest of the engine-query surface became 1-based with `lineBase: 1` in wave 1a; these two
analyze-side documents still printed the model's 0-based rows. Both now convert once, where a
line leaves the engine (`src/engine/line_base.rs`, after every sort and hash). Columns stay
0-based, except in SARIF, which is 1-based by its own standard.

- **`alsem analyze --with-evidence`**: every `evidencePath[].sourceAnchor.range.startLine` /
  `endLine` is 1-based (it was one line early), the payload states `lineBase: 1`, and the
  envelope `schemaVersion` moves `1.1.0` → `2.0.0` (a value's meaning changed: major). It now
  agrees with the finding's own `primaryLocation.line` and with the fingerprint inventory's
  `rootClassifications[].sourceAnchor`. The default document (no flag) is unchanged: still
  `1.0.0`, no `lineBase`, and its `primaryLocation.line` was already 1-based. SARIF, the HTML
  report, the PR summary and the terminal output already printed 1-based lines and do not move
  (checked, not converted twice).
- **`alsem policy check`**: the JSON's `primaryLocation` and `evidencePath[].sourceAnchor`
  lines are 1-based and the document states `lineBase: 1` (it has no schema version to move).
  Its SARIF wrote the region's `startLine` and `startColumn` 0-based, which SARIF forbids
  (both start at 1); now both are 1-based, as `analyze`'s SARIF writes them.
- Golden diff, checked mechanically (a value-by-value walk of every moved golden against HEAD;
  allowed: a line value exactly +1, an added `lineBase: 1`, a version string, a SARIF region
  `startColumn` exactly +1). Result over 24 files (`tests/cli-c-policy-goldens/` and
  `tests/gate-goldens/batch/one-job/policy.stdout.golden`): 127 line values +1, 14 `lineBase`
  keys added, 17 SARIF `startColumn` values +1, zero other differences. No golden holds
  `analyze --with-evidence` output, so the same walk compared it before and after (the HEAD
  binary against this one, `--scope all --deterministic`) on all 220 `tests/r0-corpus/`
  workspaces plus the `tests/fixtures/mcp-output/` workspace (113 with findings): 1278
  evidence line values +1, 221 `lineBase` keys added, 221 `schemaVersion` 1.1.0 → 2.0.0,
  373 `primaryLocation`/`terminalLocation` lines unchanged (already 1-based), zero other
  differences; every exit code equal.
- Test: `output_invariants::evidence_anchors_open_to_what_they_describe` opens every evidence
  anchor of `analyze --with-evidence` (the cross-app fixture with `dep:` anchors, five corpus
  workspaces covering every loop kind and call, member and identifier steps) and of
  `policy check` at its line, and checks that both documents state `lineBase: 1` (149 anchors
  matched). Discrimination: printing the raw row again in
  `format_json::evidence_path_to_value` fails it (143 of 146 analyze anchors one line early);
  doing so in `format_policy::anchor_to_jv` fails it at the policy run (3 of 3); each passes
  restored. Tests whose 0-based expectations moved with the base: `cli_a_with_evidence`
  (schema 2.0.0, `lineBase`), `cli_events_policy_dependencies`, `cli_implicit_trigger_cone`,
  `cli_policy_pins` (compares policy check with d65's r4 projection, which keeps 0-based rows,
  through each document's base), `cli_split_object_readers`, `cli_step5_coverage_fold`,
  `gap_issue100_testfield_capability`.
- **Readers outside this repo** (not changed here): bc-dev-mcp
  `src/core/hotspot-explain.ts:171-172` adds 1 to these evidence ranges and must drop the `+ 1`
  (better: read `payload.lineBase`) when its al-sem pin moves; it should accept analyze
  evidence `schemaVersion` 2.x then. al-perf `engine-runner.ts:582` passes the evidence
  `startLine` through raw, so its step lines (`views.ts:558,568`) were one line early; this
  change fixes them with no edit there (check its schema-version gate, if any, accepts 2.0.0).
  Any reader of `policy check` JSON or SARIF lines gets 1-based lines now.

### Added (MCP output wave 2, W2-0a: read-side indexes; no output change)

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-mcp-output-wave2-design.md` (revision 3), §3.3,
§3.4.1, §3.5, §11. Every golden is byte-identical; nothing serialized reads the new records yet.

- **Crossing records.** Every rule-B boundary group (`DigestEffectResult`) now carries its
  `Crossing`: the boundary identity, its typed site (`Callsite`, `Operation` or `Event`), its typed
  edge set (each edge's source, dependency target, edge kind and site), its distinct targets by
  stable id, and its distinct source anchors (several for an `ev:` crossing, one per publish
  site). Membership is `(from, to, site)`, so a workspace edge that shares a crossing's call site
  (an interface call with a workspace and a dependency implementer) is not in it. The crossings
  are built once per tree read; the multi-target boundary display and the literal pass's
  "crossing cannot run" check now read them.
- **Event ids on the literal search's event edges.** `LiteralReach`'s adjacency carries an event
  edge's `event_id` as a typed site that is never guarded, so a later crossing-constrained search
  can match an event crossing by identity. Search results are unchanged.
- **Terminal-fact index** (`engine::l5::terminal_facts`). One lossless record per direct
  capability fact with an effect type, resource-less ones (COMMIT, UI, HTTP, …) included: the
  source fact's index, effect type, resource, owner, exact terminal (operation or call site),
  original operation kind (`opSubtype`: `Insert`, `ModifyAll`, …) and temp state in the owner's
  frame, with raw producers (parameter-dependent) marked. `LiteralReach` holds it and its
  "is this kind dead in the root's reach" test reads it, in place of its private map.
- **Operation index** (`engine::l4::operation_index`). Operation id and call-site id → every
  routine row that claims it, in row order; `lookup` reports `Found`, `Ambiguous` or `Missing`,
  so a collided id is never silently one owner. `query effects`' `origin` keeps its LAST-row pick
  and explain its FIRST-row pick, now read through the index (built over record operations only
  for those two, so they build no more than before).
- Tests (in-process workspaces, so no golden moves): two calls of one entry point with different
  literal arguments, with and without a shorter workspace route (today the shorter route hides
  both crossings from the digest rows: the G1 shape W2-0b fixes); the mixed workspace/dependency
  interface dispatch sharing one call site; an event crossing with two publishers and a
  workspace subscriber; a temporary and a persistent insert on one table with the temporary route
  shorter; one parameterized writer called with a temporary and a persistent record; two overloads
  with one display; collided rows for the operation index. Each has a recorded discrimination
  proof (spec §11).
- Cost on the CDO baseline (`release-fast`, two runs each, before → after): digest IR 20.3–20.8 s
  / 3.10–3.11 GB → 20.9–21.0 s / 3.12–3.13 GB; digest RR 20.2–20.7 s / 3.14–3.17 GB → 20.6–20.8 s /
  3.12–3.15 GB; prove IR `writes-table` 21.5–22.0 s → 21.4–21.6 s; query effects IR 11.1–11.4 s →
  11.3 s. Within run-to-run noise; outputs byte-identical (timestamps aside).

### Fixed (a context-server store deadlock, and the flaky test that hid it)

- **Two requests could wait on each other forever in `Store::ensure_prepared`.** A request
  claimed the keys nobody was filling, joined the keys another request was filling, and then
  WAITED for the joined keys while still holding its claims. When a joined key's fill ended, a
  third request that had read the snapshot just before that key was published could claim the
  key again, and then join one of the waiter's claims: each waited on the other. Now a request
  computes and publishes its claims first and waits for the joined keys holding nothing, so a
  wait is never on a waiter and no cycle can form. Found by stress: the reworked test below hung
  in 2 of 300 runs under heavy CPU load, both heavy requests stuck in `wait_for` (gdb stack
  dumps). Test: `a_request_publishes_its_claims_before_it_waits_for_a_joined_key` (one request
  holds `Y` at a gate; another claims `X` and joins `Y`; a third that needs only `X` must answer
  while `Y` is still filled). Discrimination: waiting before the fills fails it with its
  watchdog's `Deadline`; restored, it passes.
- **`concurrent_requests_and_evictions_answer_the_cold_bytes` forces the refill it asserts.**
  Under machine load it failed "l4 refilled after eviction" (one l4 fill), and once ran for
  over 200 s. Its only evictions came from a concurrent thread, and `Store::evict` rightly skips
  every key a request in flight pins, so a run whose eviction bursts never met a gap between
  requests refilled nothing. Now each round starts only once the last round's requests
  returned, every evictable artifact is evicted then (nothing is pinned, and the test states
  that none is left), and the concurrent bursts last exactly as long as the round's requests.
  The test asserts at least one fill per round that reads a kind. A thread that panics ends
  every wait at once (one result channel per thread). Discrimination: no between-rounds
  eviction fails it (35 to 37 l4 fills of 40); no pins fails it; the explain indexes' kind name
  drifting fails it.

### Changed (MCP output plan 1f: tool descriptions, first pass)

- **The MCP tool descriptions and server instructions state what an agent needs before it
  calls** (plan item 1f; review S1, E5, E7): every command tool says its lines are 1-based, its
  typical size and when the answer goes to a file with a summary, when `format: json` is worth
  it, and its dependency depth in one sentence (explain/digest: summarized per entry point;
  prove: the whole cone; query: one routine deep, until the plan's item 3a). `query effects` no
  longer claims a "complete" list; digest names `files`/`diff` as the change modes;
  `alsem_refresh` no longer says there is no built revision to update. The full rewrite is the
  plan's item 3b.

### Added (MCP output plan 1e: a summary on every spilled answer)

- **An explain, query or prove answer that goes to a file carries a summary** (plan item 1e;
  review E2). Only digest had one; an 80 KB explain card arrived as `{path, bytes, sha256}`. The
  renderer builds it from its own data (`ExplainRunResult`, `QueryRunResult`, `ProveRunResult`
  gain `summary`): explain, each card's header line and the length of its lists (own rules,
  writes, events, UI, callers, tests, gaps) and its commit verdict; query effects, the effects
  by operation, by temp state, the tables and the not-known-temporary writes; query touches, the
  `down`/`up` headlines with every list as a count; prove, the answer, the evidence and blocker
  counts and the obligations. Capped at 8 KiB (`capped_summary`), sent only beside a file.

### Fixed (MCP output plan 1d: boundary groups)

- **A dependency boundary group names its boundary owner-qualified, lists every resource, and
  claims no unresolved resource it cannot have** (plan item 1d; review B2, D4, P2). Digest and
  prove printed `<App>.<Routine>` (`Base Application.OnRun` for both Reminder-Issue and
  Sales-Calc. Discount); now `Codeunit Reminder-Issue::OnRun`, as `query` names a routine. The
  JSON gains `resources[]` ({id, display}, every resource in resource-id order;
  `detail.resourceCount` is its length) beside `detail.resources`, which still names the first
  ten, so "Issued Reminder Header" is never lost by omission. `unresolvedResources` counts only
  database writes (every COMMIT, UI, ERROR, HTTP, FILE or background group claimed one), and such
  a resource-less group no longer states `resourceCount: "0"` / `resources: ""`. Digest schema
  2.1.0, prove 2.1.0. Fact ids and canonical keys are unchanged.

### Changed (MCP output plan 1c: one copy of each answer)

- **An MCP answer carries its stdout once in what the client reads** (plan item 1c; review P3,
  E1, E6). Measured through Claude Code first, as the plan asked: with `structuredContent`
  present the client reads and size-checks that field alone (a result with 46,167 characters of
  text blocks and 83,840 of `structuredContent` was reported as 82,195 characters and filed). So
  `structuredContent` now holds the answer exactly once: the parsed `output` without
  `stdoutText` for an inline JSON stdout, else `stdoutText`; before, a JSON answer was there
  twice (and three times counting the text block). The first text block drops the
  `"<the next content block>"` placeholder key; the text blocks keep the byte contract.
  `alsem_prove` answers `human` by default (owner decision 3; `format: json` for the full
  evidence). A call naming no `maxInlineBytes` gets 40 KiB, not 64 KiB, so an inline answer's
  `structuredContent` stays under Claude Code's 50,000-character limit. The LSP relay keeps the
  CLI's defaults (prove `json`, 64 KiB).

### Fixed (MCP output plan 1b: the digest summary)

- **`alsem_digest`'s summary no longer embeds every unresolved call site, says what decides
  whether to open the file, and is bounded** (plan item 1b; review D1, D2, E3). The server built
  it by parsing the stdout and copied each root's whole `unresolved` array into it: 270,781
  characters for `IssueReminder`, which Claude Code moved out of the conversation, and it was
  added after the frame bound. Now the renderer builds it from its own data
  (`digest_cli::digest_summary`, carried as `WriteAction::Summary` → the wire's
  `Outcome::Cli.summary` → the envelope) before the frame is bounded: per root the effects by
  type, the physical tables written (workspace and dependency, a boundary group's whole set, up
  to ten names each), temporary tables, commits, the boundaries entered, coverage and its
  reasons, and the unresolved call sites as `{total, polymorphic, dynamicTarget, inWorkspace,
  topCallees[3]}`. Capped at 8 KiB (`SUMMARY_CAP_BYTES`): past it the names go, then routines
  from the end; never a spill. The server keeps a summary only beside a file (an inline answer
  holds the answer itself), and replaces one over the cap by its size. The server no longer
  parses any stdout for it.

### Changed (MCP output plan 1a: every line 1-based)

- **explain, prove, digest, query, fingerprint and the snapshots print and serialize 1-based
  lines, and every document says so with `lineBase: 1`** (plan
  `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-04-mcp-output-fixes.md`, item 1a, owner decision 1). They
  printed the model's 0-based rows as `file:line`, so an agent's `Read`, `grep -n` or editor
  landed one statement early; `alsem graph`, `alsem analyze`, SARIF and the HTML report were
  1-based already. The model stays 0-based; `src/engine/line_base.rs` converts once, where a line
  leaves the engine, after every sort and hash. Columns stay 0-based. Schema bumps (a value's
  meaning changed, so major): digest 1.8.0 → 2.0.0, prove 1.4.0 → 2.0.0, query 1.1.0 → 2.0.0,
  fingerprint-query 1.3.0 → 2.0.0, routine inventory 1.2.0 → 2.0.0, explain `al-sem.explain/1`
  → `/2`, snapshot schema 4 → 5 (with a `lineBase` header key; old snapshots are refused, as
  every schema bump does, and `alsem fingerprint` re-creates them). The MCP envelope of every
  command answer carries `lineBase: 1`. The aldump R4-F projections keep the model's rows,
  except the snapshot projection, which is the snapshot's own serializer.
  **Readers to update with this change:** bc-dev-mcp's risk join (`src/core/risk.ts:99-110`,
  `:158-169`) adds 1 to a digest routine anchor and must drop the `+ 1`; the ConTinAI citation
  consumer and the editor extension (file:line links relayed by the LSP) read the new base.

### Added (MCP output plan 1a: output invariants)

- **`tests/cli/output_invariants.rs`** (always on, the wave-0 fixture) and
  **`tests/cli/output_cdo.rs`** (the first CDO-gated `cli` member, now run by `scripts/cdo-gate`
  on `IssueReminder`, `RunReportID` and `UpdateLastUpload` off one `alsem mcp` server): every
  `file:line` a human output prints opens to the line it describes (the anchor source-check;
  `dep:` anchors through `aldump --dump-dependency-source`; a sample of 50 on CDO), and every
  JSON document and MCP envelope states `lineBase: 1`.

### Added (MCP output plan, wave 0: the cross-app output fixture)

- **A cross-app fixture whose dependency ships bodies, and its golden family** (plan
  `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-04-mcp-output-fixes.md`, item 0b). Every explain/query golden
  before it was single-app, so the shapes an agent meets on a real workspace never reached a
  golden. `tests/fixtures/mcp-output/` (the workspace `ws/` and the dependency's sources `dep/`,
  packed into `ws/.alpackages/` by `write_source_app`; `output_fixture::fixture_app_matches_its_sources`
  keeps the two equal) has: a workspace routine that runs a dependency codeunit whose callee
  writes twelve tables, modifies a thirteenth, raises a dependency event, runs a dynamic codeunit
  and commits (boundary groups with a commit, more than ten resources, an event group and a
  dependency gap), a second dependency `OnRun` (two boundaries with one routine name), temporary
  and physical writes on one table in the workspace and in the dependency, a `RecordRef.Next()`
  loop, a dynamic `Codeunit.Run`, an interface call, an HTTP call, a background task, an own

### Changed (the finer dependency re-resolution rule for S)

- **An S edit re-resolves only the dependency files whose recorded answers changed** (plan
  `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-03-context-server-remaining.md`, item S, step 2;
  `src/program/session/dep_record.rs`). The workspace session resolves every dependency file
  through a reads-facade recorder and keeps, per file, its edge range and the queries it made,
  and per query a digest of its answer (blake3 over the declaration projection's encoding of
  everything handed out: ids by value, nodes and runs of nodes by their whole content, so a read
  through a returned node is covered; a shared dependency-tier node by its position, pinned by
  the tier's identity). Under S every kept query is asked again against the new revision; a file
  with a changed answer is resolved again, the others keep their edges, site facts and parens-less
  calls (sites re-stamped with the current `FileIx`, source witnesses re-materialized as under B).
  When no file changes and none is renumbered, the old resolution is shared outright. The record
  is not trusted, and everything is resolved, on another tier or facade version, a changed file
  list, a kept witness with no declaration, or two files' site facts sharing an obligation id. P
  and B are unchanged. On CDO (`aldump --session-refresh --verify`, every step equal to the cold
  build): 10,881 dependency files, 499,011 recorded queries, record ~68 MB; adding a procedure, a
  signature change and adding a file each re-resolve 0 files (no answer changed); a new
  implementer of a dependency interface (`CTS-CDN ISenderProfileRetriever`) re-resolves 2. The
  query check costs ~30 ms and the digests ~40 ms per S. Timed on CDO (release-fast, quiet
  machine, two rounds each, master `7b97a134` beside it): the resident S refresh
  (`census-probe incr`, uncounted, a procedure added) 7.2-8.0 s → 3.09-3.16 s; the model refresh
  (`aldump --session-refresh`) for a procedure added 6.65-7.21 s → 2.43-2.70 s, a signature change
  2.47-2.67 s, a file added 6.97-7.31 s → 3.50-3.81 s (every dependency file renumbered, so the
  kept edges are copied to re-stamp them), the new implementer 3.67-3.85 s. The recording's cost
  on a cold build: program 7.27-7.56 s → 7.80-8.20 s, resident cold refresh 11.5-12.0 s →
  12.1-12.6 s, P unchanged within noise (12.9 s); peak RSS of the cold step 3.48 → 3.71 GB.
  New session tests (both memory modes):
  a first workspace implementer of a dependency interface (a negative lookup), an implementer's
  method arity and access changed under an unchanged `implements` list (a read through a returned
  id), a procedure added above that method (witness moved, nothing re-resolved), a workspace
  table extension of a dependency table added and removed, a name collision, a workspace closed
  enum implementing the dependency interface. Discrimination: recording `implementers_of` only
  when non-empty fails the first-implementer test; not recording `routines_named` fails the
  implementer test; comparing by query alone fails 13 tests; skipping the fast path's witness
  re-materialization fails the implementer test.

### Changed (the resolution reads facade and its tripwire)

- **Call-site resolution reads the whole-program state only through a facade** (plan
  `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-03-context-server-remaining.md`, item S, step 1;
  `src/program/resolve/reads.rs`). `resolve_file_obligations` and everything it reaches in
  `resolver`, `receiver`, `arg_dispatch`, `closed_enum`, `interface_holder` and
  `applicability` take `&dyn GraphReads`, `&dyn IndexReads` and `&dyn SurfaceReads` instead
  of the concrete graph, index and surface, so they cannot name a graph field or an index map:
  every read is a semantic query (29 kinds, `reads::Query`). A `Recorder` answers the same
  queries and logs them per file. The six `graph.objects.iter().find(..)` scans and one
  `graph.routines.iter().filter(..)` scan in that code became the equal run lookups. No output
  changes (every golden and test unchanged). The tripwire: a counting hook (tests only) on the
  raw state (node sets, index accessors, surface, topology) counts a raw read made inside a
  recording scope but outside a recorder method; `reads::tests` resolves every file of every
  r0-corpus workspace and two dependency fixtures through recorders and asserts zero such
  reads and an unchanged resolution, and a CDO-gated test does the same over every CDO
  dependency file. Passing the plain graph instead of the recorder fails it (13,313 bypassing
  reads in 292 files), and so does one recorder method reading without its guard (8,364).

### Changed (context server: raw facts emitted on demand for every view)

- **The resident fold no longer emits raw inherited facts for every primary routine** (plan
  `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-03-context-server-remaining.md`, item L6; an owner-approved
  amendment to the context-server design's §6.10 eager emission; `src/engine/l4/capability_cone.rs`,
  `src/engine/l4/pd_solve.rs`, `src/engine/resident/revision.rs`). Measured first: the eager
  emission was 6.7-7.5 s of the 11.3-13.1 s cold fold. The fold's cone store now keeps what a
  subject's emission reads (the typed-edge graph, its SCCs and successors, the non-root fact cones
  by SCC index, the guard frames, the members it re-folded), and every view's `Raw(scope)`
  artifact, primary or dependency, is emitted from it (`ConeStore::emit_raw`; the producer
  entries are read back from the arena by `finalize`'s rule). A subject another view already
  emitted is adopted, and so is one the previous revision emitted when the fold did not re-fold
  its rows (stage 5b's rule). The one-shot CLI path is unchanged; no golden moves. Measured on
  CDO (release-fast probe, mimalloc, uncounted, master beside it): cold fold 11.3-13.1 s →
  5.0-5.3 s, P fold 12.2-12.5 s → 5.2-5.5 s, cold refresh to first explain 29.2 s → 22.4-23.3 s,
  B and S folds unchanged (1.45-1.51 s); the first answer on a never-emitted primary root pays
  13.6 ms of emission (2.7 ms when adopted after B). Memory: the fold's raw map (77.7 MiB) is gone,
  the cone store grew 52.7 MiB; RSS 5.89 → 5.84-5.86 GB cold, peak unchanged. T-order fill counts
  amended (one `raw` fill per view, primary roots included); the raw fill's budget estimate is
  60 MiB (was 600, sized for the former raw-only composition). Tests: the retained emission equals
  a composition for every routine of every r0 app and three fixtures, and on CDO (every primary
  routine, 200 dependency routines); on-demand, eviction, adoption and cross-revision
  re-emission tests, each with a discrimination proof; a `--verify` run after cold, B, S and P
  gave every answer equal to cold.

### Changed (context server: the producer solve's fresh producers in parallel)

- **Fresh producers are solved in parallel** (plan
  `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-03-context-server-remaining.md`, item L2;
  `src/engine/l4/pd_solve.rs`). Each producer the producer-dependent solve has to solve (every
  producer cold and after a P change; the re-solved ones after B or S) runs its BFS on a rayon
  worker into its own states, links and edges; the results are concatenated in producer order
  (state indices shifted, edges deduplicated by address) and finalized. A producer's states
  never meet another's (the state key holds the producer, a link joins two states of one
  producer, the step is a pure function of shared read-only inputs), so the result is the
  serial walk's. `finalize` also runs its sorts, link pass and first hops on rayon and files
  `by_routine` and the resolved entries per routine rank instead of hashing a routine string per
  state. Measured on CDO (cross-app, release-fast probe, mimalloc, uncounted, three rounds each,
  same machine and day): `pd.solve` cold 3.31-3.42 s → 0.76-0.83 s, after P 3.51-3.78 s →
  0.77-0.83 s, after B 1.07-1.15 s → 0.70-0.78 s, after S 1.07-1.11 s → 0.72-0.74 s (the walk
  alone 2.5-2.6 s → 0.23-0.25 s; the concatenation 0.13-0.14 s; `pd.finalize` 0.77-0.82 s →
  0.37-0.41 s). The fold: cold 13.7-14.0 s → 11.1-11.7 s, after P 15.0-15.6 s → 12.6-12.7 s,
  after B 1.81-1.92 s → 1.46-1.56 s, after S 1.84-1.93 s → 1.51-1.53 s. Peak RSS unchanged
  (counted run: cold high-water 5.92 → 6.00 GB, whole run 6.24 → 6.30 GB). Proof: under
  `cfg(test)` a `test_serial` guard makes every solve also run the pre-L2 walk and finalize and
  assert `==` (the arena types now derive `PartialEq`), on every r0 app and the eight dependency
  fixtures (each also with its producers permuted), the seeded and hand-stated solves, and the
  cross-app CDO model (`parallel_solve_equals_the_serial_walk_on_cdo`); the CDO arena dump
  (`aldump --snapshot-memory --pd-dump`, 2,851,161 lines) is byte-identical to master's; a
  `--verify` run after cold, B, S and P gave every answer equal to its cold run. Discrimination:
  mis-offsetting a producer's local indices fails the fixture test; dropping the edge dedup
  fires `finalize`'s new debug assertion (without it the arena stays equal, since `finalize`
  merges edges of one identity, so the plan's "the arena differs" does not hold); filing a state
  under the wrong routine rank fails the permuted fixture run; a highest-ranked first hop fails
  `solve_keeps_all_links`.

### Fixed

- **A witness fill no longer fails when its key was published meanwhile**
  (`src/engine/resident/revision.rs`). A request that read the snapshot before a concurrent
  request published a `Witness` key claims the key once that fill is over and fills off the
  newer snapshot; the batch skipped every key the snapshot held, this one too, and the request
  failed with "is not a witness of the request's plan". Exposed by L2's timing
  (`concurrent_requests_and_evictions_answer_the_cold_bytes` failed 2 runs in 6, master 0 in 12;
  0 in 20 after). Test: `a_witness_fill_returns_the_entry_its_snapshot_already_holds`
  (hand-stated); without the check it fails with that error.

### Changed (context server: a view's tree splices over its revision's base; shared sections)

- **A view's tree no longer re-derives what every view of the revision shares** (plan
  `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-03-context-server-remaining.md`, item L4a). The tree base now
  also holds the evidence candidates (`compute_routine_order` once per row, not three times per
  view), every covered routine's direct facts interned and sorted per subject, and the pd
  arena's edge and producer maps; a view adds only its subjects' raw rows and walks only their
  state closure (`src/engine/l5/snapshot_view.rs`). Measured on CDO (release-fast probe,
  mimalloc, uncounted): per-view tree (`snapshot.derive`) 1.32-1.48 s → 0.18-0.24 s; the tree
  base 1.15-1.29 s → 1.28-1.46 s; the first heavy answer on a root (explain) 5.0-5.8 s →
  4.1-4.6 s; explain over three roots 4.5-4.7 s → 3.4-3.7 s. Proof: the whole per-view derivation
  was kept as a test-only oracle until 1,508 fixture views and six cross-app CDO views were equal
  section by section, then deleted; a `--verify` run after cold, B, S and P gave every answer
  equal to its cold run. Tests: `a_site_only_a_subjects_inherited_fact_names_is_in_its_view`
  (hand-stated: no real view adds an evidence id beyond the base); discrimination: dropping a
  subject's inherited call sites from the view's filter loses the call-site row and changes the
  digest answer; restored, green. The equality test's breaks (no run shift: pd states differ in
  54 comparisons; no re-sort of rebuilt runs: facts differ in 800) failed it before deletion.
- **A view's tree shares its base's whole sections** (item L3). `CapabilitySnapshot`'s typed
  edges, call-site resolutions, analysis gaps, event declarations, root classifications and
  routine order frames are `Arc`s, as identities and coverage were; writers go through
  `Arc::make_mut`. Memory on CDO (counted, four views per revision, `PROBE_TREE_BYTES=1`, a new
  `census-probe` measure): the trees 1,607 → 992 MiB, the base 185 → 286 MiB (L4a's tables), so
  1,792 → 1,278 MiB per revision; RSS 7.12-7.27 → 6.60-6.78 GB, peak 7.51-7.62 → 6.99-7.13 GB.
  With one view per revision the RSS is unchanged (default peak 6.27 GB, `--low-mem` 5.89-5.90
  GB). Test: `views_over_one_base_share_its_whole_sections`; discrimination: deep-cloning the
  typed edges for a shared base fails it; restored, green.
- **L4b is not recommended**: what a view still pays is mostly the pd projection (~0.15 s over
  ~916,000 kept states), which per-key carry does not touch.

### Changed (context server: direct facts in parallel; the finalize split measured)

- **The fold's direct facts are extracted in parallel** (plan
  `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-03-context-server-remaining.md`, item L5 step 1).
  `det_cone_inputs_over` computed every routine's direct facts in a serial loop on every fold
  and on cold start. Each row's extraction is a pure function of the row, its publisher events
  and its uncertainty reasons, so the rows now run on rayon with an order-preserving collect;
  the per-id merge is unchanged. Measured on CDO (release-fast probe, mimalloc, uncounted):
  `cone.direct` 0.28-0.31 s → 0.058-0.068 s on every fold; the fold after a body edit 2.03-2.07
  s → 1.79-1.92 s; "analysis prepared" after a body edit 3.88-3.91 s → 3.59-3.69 s. Step 2 (a
  per-routine memo) is not built: step 1 leaves well under the plan's 0.1 s bar. A `--verify`
  run after cold, B, S and P: every answer equal to its cold run. Tests: `direct_full` and
  `coverage_in` equal (as maps and as a key-ordered digest) to a serial oracle on all 274
  fixture app dirs and on CDO, single-app and cross-app. Discrimination: reversing the
  parallel collect's order moves both digests on CDO and on the fixtures and fails both tests;
  restored, both pass.
- **`pd.finalize` now has two spans, `pd.finalize.sort` and `pd.finalize.build`** (item L1's
  measurement). On CDO the sort half is 0.20-0.24 s (cold, B, S and P alike) and the build
  pass 0.45-0.61 s, so L1's per-producer merge (gate: sort ≥ 0.3 s) is not built; the build
  pass is the larger half.
- **`census-probe`: `PROBE_NO_COUNT=1` turns the counting allocator off.** Its three shared
  atomics per allocation serialize parallel passes: the parallel `cone.direct` measured 0.55 s
  counted against 0.06 s uncounted. Time parallel code uncounted.

### Added (context server: explain's indexes kept per revision)

- **A resident explain no longer rebuilds its model indexes on every request** (plan
  `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-03-context-server-remaining.md`, item W2). The indexes every
  explain card reads (`Indexes`) and the cross-call rules' index (`CrossRules`) depend only on
  the model, but borrowed it; they now have an owned form, `ExplainIndexes` (row, object and
  action indexes, owned id strings; `DeclaringRows`, `CrossRulesIndex`), which a revision keeps
  as `ArtifactKey::ExplainIndexes` (kind `explain_indexes`, phase 0), built once and read by
  every explain over it. `CrossRules` is split: the immutable index is shared, while the memo,
  the expansion budget and the stop flag belong to one walk per run, so an answer never depends
  on earlier requests. `explain --table/--field` reuses the index
  (`RulesIndex::build_where_over`). The one-shot CLI builds the same owned form per run, so no
  output moves. The artifact is evicted after the det, freed at a refresh, and budgeted at 30
  MiB. Tests: explain over a too-deep call chain then over a plain routine (and back) equals
  cold; one fill for several explains; evict and refill equal cold; explain after B, S, a file
  added and removed, and P equals cold. Discrimination proofs (each seen to fail, then pass):
  a stop flag shared across requests; the artifact not retained; the served view without it; a
  stale cross-revision artifact; a kind-name drift. Measured on CDO (release-fast): an explain
  whose root witness is warm takes 0.20-0.22 s instead of 1.16-1.17 s, explain over three roots
  5.2-5.4 s instead of 6.3-6.4 s; the artifact holds 25.7 MiB; resident memory is unchanged.
  `census-probe incr --witness` now also measures the indexes. Design note: §6.11 of
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-01-context-server-design.md`.

### Added (context server: a per-revision memo of root witnesses)

- **Explain, prove and digest asked about the same routine in one resident revision now
  share one computed root entry** (plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-03-context-server-remaining.md`,
  item W). A root's `DigestEntryResult` (its witnesses, the `digest.roots` pass) depends only
  on the root and `--include-reads`, so the revision's store keeps it as an
  `ArtifactKey::Witness { root, include_reads }` artifact (kind `witness`, phase 3), filled off
  the request's own `Tree(scope)` and never carried to the next revision. A request's first
  witness fill computes every absent root of the request in one pass over its tree (one index
  build, the roots in parallel); the read finishes owned clones, because prove's literal-reach
  pass mutates its entries. `digest_effects_each` is split into the pure `root_entries` and the
  per-read `finish_effects`; the one-shot path calls both, so no output moves. Witnesses are
  evicted first under memory pressure and dropped at a refresh with the trees. `status` reports
  `fills.witness` (`hit`, `miss`, `batches`); `census-probe incr … --witness R2,R3` measures a
  command's answer with and without its root's witness, the witness bytes, and the cross-view
  case. Tests: every order of explain/prove/digest on one root plus
  `[digest, digest --include-reads, digest]` (five fixtures), digest after prove reads the
  unpruned entry (G23's dead path), a three-root explain computes in one pass and a later prove
  finds the witness, a witness without its tree fails loudly, and the concurrency test now runs
  two heavy requests on one root while witnesses are evicted. Discrimination proofs (each seen
  to fail, then pass): the key without `include_reads`; memoizing the post-prove entry; no
  `Tree` prerequisite; no batch. Measured on CDO (release-fast, quiet machine): explain, then
  prove and digest on the same root now take 5.8-6.1 s, 2.55-2.63 s and 0.15-0.16 s, against
  5.9-6.1 s, 5.6-6.0 s and 3.2-3.6 s on master; with the view's tree warm, a hit against a miss
  is explain 1.1-1.2 s against 4.3-4.5 s, prove 0.86-0.92 s against 3.8-4.2 s, digest 0.15 s
  against 3.1-3.4 s. A witness holds 5.6-7.9 MiB; resident memory is unchanged (5.8-6.0 GB).
  What an explain hit still pays is `explain.indexes` (0.87-1.14 s), above the 0.4 s bar for
  the plan's W2. Design note: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-01-context-server-design.md` §6.11.

### Added (a guard on the ordering cell, #367)

- **Test `served_plans_never_demand_the_ordering_cell`** (`engine::session`): the plans of
  the commands the resident host serves (prove, digest, explain, query, built with the
  default detectors) never ask for `substrate::ORDERING_FACTS`. The ordering cell
  (`detector_context::fill_ordering`, read by the opt-in d47/d49/d51) composes its own
  snapshot of the whole model; its doc now says a served command that needs it must first
  get a fill over the revision's fold and a tree of the kept roots. Discrimination: giving
  `digest_plan` `own: ORDERING_FACTS` fails the test; reverting passes.
- **#367 closed as not worth it, with numbers** (cross-app CDO, `alsem analyze --detector
  d47,d49,d51`, release-fast, both scopes): the cell's private snapshot holds 246,708
  facts (207,279 inherited), not the 17.0 M of the cross-app cone graph, because it is
  composed over the cut graph. It costs ~2.4 s and ~30 MB of peak in a ~45–50 s, 5.1–6.0 GB
  run. The 1,456 kept roots (of 5,479) already hold 187,102 of the inherited facts (90 %),
  and event-publish facts are 66,645 of those. The cell's real cost is the per-root witness
  work (`digest.roots`, ~30 s, ~2.1 GB of peak), which neither a subject nor a fact-kind
  restriction of the snapshot touches.

### Changed (the default cross-app memory budget is 8 GiB)

- **`--memory-budget` now defaults to 8 GiB for a cross-app engine child (was 6 GiB).**
  Stage 5b's cone and tree stores raised the default mode's resident set on CDO to about
  6.0 GB after a body edit (peak 6.34 GB), right at the old 6 GiB, so a revision's trees
  were evicted under normal use. `--low-mem` keeps its 6 GiB and single-app its 2 GiB
  (`engine::resident::budget::DEFAULT_BUDGET_CROSS_APP`). Owner decision, 2026-11-03.

### Added (context server stage 5: incremental analysis)

- **The resident revision's L4 solve is seeded from the previous
  revision's** (design §6.9). A new revision keeps the complete seed triple of
  the last published solve (its `SolveBaseline`, its bundle inside
  `L4Analysis`, its core summaries) until its own `L4` fill publishes, then
  releases it; the fill runs the L4 host's seeded solve (`L4Reuse`), which
  compares the baseline's digests with the current inputs' and re-solves only
  the SCCs they leave dirty. A seed is used only when the revision's
  `seed_key` (universe, the packages consumed, the root `app.json` bytes, the
  model-instance id, the source dependencies, the engine version) equals the
  seed's; a P change is a full solve. Test
  `seeded_l4_after_b_s_and_p_equals_a_cold_solve` (rule-B fixture: B, S and P
  edits; every served answer and the solve's projection equal cold).
- `census-probe incr <ws-copy> [routine] [--verify] [--steps B,S,P]`: the
  resident session after each change type: refresh, the fold and the L4 fill
  timed apart ("analysis prepared"), each served ask timed, and with
  `--verify` each ask compared with a cold standalone run.

- **The resident fold re-solves only the producers an edit can reach**
  (design §6.10 "Producers", the first part of the cone store). Each fold
  keeps its producer solve's per-routine input digests (every model row of
  the id, its guard frame, its typed out-edges); the next revision's fold
  computes Δ (the routines whose digest changed, appeared or vanished) and
  re-solves a producer only when its owner is reachable from Δ in the new
  graph, when it held a state at a routine of Δ in the old arena, or when its
  fact changed; every other producer's states, links and distances are
  copied from the previous arena and the whole is finalized in the canonical
  order (stage 1b), so the arena equals a full solve's. On CDO after a body
  edit: 2,590 of 2,634 producers copied (2.73 M states), `pd.solve`
  **4.0 s -> 1.4 s** (copy 0.37 s, canonical finalize 0.86 s). Tests
  `reused_producer_states_equal_a_full_solve` (hand-stated graphs: a caller's
  argument from physical to temporary, a new caller, a removed edge, no
  edit) and `fold_reuses_untouched_producers_and_equals_cold` (the rule-B
  workspace through the resident session, every answer cold-equal).

- **The per-SCC cone store: a resident fold re-folds only the SCCs an edit
  reaches** (design §6.10). Each resident fold keeps, per SCC (keyed by its
  member set), an input digest, a product fingerprint and its non-root fact
  and coverage cones. The next revision's fold re-folds an SCC only when its
  input digest differs: a member's raw direct facts, direct coverage input,
  rows, guard frame, typed out-edges or scope mode; an out-edge's
  **transfer digest** (the callee's parameters, read by the publisher ↔
  subscriber guard mapping, and the callee's frame; never subject to
  cut-off); its member order; or a successor's product fingerprint (every
  cone entry's representative by full content hash, distance and guard,
  plus the coverage cone). A re-folded SCC with an equal fingerprint leaves
  its predecessors clean (cut-off). Every other SCC's cones are shared by
  `Arc` and its members' rows copied: derived rows by window (the new
  builder continues the previous interner), raw entries adopted with their
  table set (`InheritedFacts` now has segments), coverage records cloned.
  **Δ_pd_output**: a member whose own producer-solve entries changed (states
  of re-solved or vanished producers, compared per routine) has its derived
  row and raw entry re-folded even inside a reused SCC. CDO, body edit:
  11 of 32,571 SCCs re-folded (all 11 cut off), 33,274 rows copied; the fold
  is **12.0 s -> 2.2 s** and every answer equals its cold run (`census-probe
  incr --verify`, B, B, S). The store holds 4.73 M cone entries: resident
  RSS after a B edit 4.8 -> 5.4 GB, peak 5.6 -> 6.2 GB (default; `--low-mem`
  4.3 / 5.1 GB). A cold or P fold pays about +0.4 s for the digests and
  fingerprints. Tests in `resident::session::cone_tests` (hand-stated, each
  cold-equal on every step, with discrimination proofs): the renamed
  subscriber parameter behind an event guard (transfer digest), an equal
  dedup key with a new representative, cut-off, a removed edge and an
  alternate-path deletion, an SCC split and merge, a moved subscriber, the
  A→C→P producer chain (Δ_pd_output) and an object-only table rename.
- Fold timers: `cone.direct`, `cone.graph`, `cone.tarjan`, `cone.dedup`,
  `cone.frames`, `cone.member_digests`, `pd.output_delta`, `cone.walk`,
  `cone.finish`, `revision.fold`, `revision.seed_release`, and one
  `tree.*` span per tree section (`tree.base` for the whole sections,
  `snapshot.derive` for a view). They account for the whole fold: the
  "untimed remainder" was the SCC walk itself (10.1 s of the 12.0 s fold
  after a body edit). `census-probe incr` prints the cone report and the
  census per step.
- **The tree store: heavy answers share their revision's trees** (design
  §6.11). A resident revision derives the trees' whole sections once
  (`TreeBase`: identities, typed edges and the skipped-edge keys, call-site
  resolutions, analysis gaps, coverage, event declarations, root
  classifications, routine order frames, rule B's boundary; rebuilt whole
  every revision, never carried over) and one tree per distinct view (its
  subjects: `Tree(subjects)`, the view's evidence indexes, capability facts
  and pd arena over the shared sections). Both are artifacts of the
  revision's store, so concurrent requests join one fill, a request's tree
  stays pinned through its reads, and eviction drops trees first
  (`EVICTION_ORDER`: raw, tree, run, det, tree_base, fold, ...); a refresh
  frees the published revision's trees before it builds. A one-shot tree is
  unchanged (`compose_tree` = the base derived and moved into one view).
  CDO after a body edit, explain then prove then digest on one routine:
  explain **7.8 s -> 6.1 s** (its view's tree 1.6 s instead of a whole tree
  2.9-3.0 s), prove **9.1 s -> 5.8 s** and digest **6.5 s -> 3.5 s** (they
  read explain's tree); the whole sections cost 1.4-1.5 s once per revision.
  Every answer equals its cold run (`census-probe incr --verify`, B and S).
  `census-probe incr` prepares and times the tree base apart. Tests:
  `heavy_answers_share_trees_that_equal_cold_trees_after_each_edit` (one
  tree per view and one base per revision, every served tree equal to a cold
  one-shot tree after a new call, a call to no routine and an object-only
  table rename), and the concurrent request/eviction test now evicts trees
  and bases too.

### Fixed (context server stage 5)

- **An eviction that evicted nothing republished the snapshot.** Every
  value then had a second owner while a request held the old snapshot, so a
  reclaim that first tried a pinned key could free nothing after it (found
  when the tree store put a request's own pinned tree ahead of the runs in
  the eviction order). `Store::evict` now publishes nothing when every key
  is pinned. Test `an_empty_eviction_publishes_nothing`.

### Changed (context server stage 5)

- **The L4 solve's row digests are hashed in parallel.** Every resident `L4`
  fill (seeded or not) digested the `Debug` text of every routine row
  serially; on CDO that was about 1.8 s of a 2.2-2.4 s fill. Hashed per id on
  the rayon pool (each id reads only its own rows): the fill is **0.57-0.60 s**
  (cold and seeded; the seeded solve itself re-solves 115 of 33,285 SCCs after
  a body edit). Same digests, so the same seeding decisions.

### Added (context server: the LSP front end)

- **The editor's LSP server answers explain / prove / digest / query
  through the resident engine** (context-server design §9, the last stage-3
  item). New custom requests under the frozen `al-call-hierarchy/` prefix:
  `explain`, `prove`, `digest`, `queryEffects`, `queryTouches`,
  `engineStatus`, `engineRefresh`. Params are the arguments of the matching
  MCP tools (`alsem_explain`, ...; validated by the same code, so flags and
  defaults are the CLI's), plus an optional `uri` (its workspace root
  answers; default the first root) and `workDoneToken` (`$/progress`). The
  result is the MCP envelope (`kind`, `revision`, `exitCode`, `stdoutText` /
  `stdoutFile`, ...): the stdout is the CLI's byte for byte. The server is a
  CLIENT of an `alsem engine-host` child, never a second in-process engine:
  requests run on the engine pool's worker threads, so call hierarchy is
  answered while one runs; the child starts on the first engine request
  (never at server start), ends on its idle timeout and with the server.
  `$/cancelRequest` sends the running request `session/cancel` (answered
  `RequestCancelled`, the engine's `cancelled` answer as `data`); `didSave`
  and the root's file watcher send `session/notifyChanged`, so an edit that
  keeps a file's size and time is still seen.
- **The engine executable** is the `alsem` binary next to `al-call-hierarchy`
  (the packages ship both), or `engine.executable`. The server binary cannot
  host the engine itself: the engine decodes each command line with the
  `alsem` CLI's clap and planning, which live in that binary. A command that
  reads paths (`--diff`, `--file`) has its file-system decisions made on the
  server's side by the same binary (`alsem engine-ask --params`).
- **Config**: an `engine` section in `~/.al-sem/config.json` and the
  workspace's `.al-sem.json` (pre-rename spellings read too): `enabled`
  (default true), `executable`, `memoryBudget`, `lowMem`, `idleTimeoutSecs`,
  `maxChildren`; read at the first engine request. Output files go to
  `~/.al-sem/lsp-out/<instance>/`.
- **Measured on CDO** (release-fast, `IssueReminder`, a heavily loaded shared
  machine): the LSP's RSS 6.0 MiB idle, 8.2 MiB after the first engine
  request, 8.5 MiB after nine (the engine's memory is the child's: 3.96 GB
  after the first explain, 4.1–4.3 GB after the warm asks). First explain
  37–40 s (cold child and build), warm explain 7.7–8.5 s, warm query
  0.04–0.16 s. Tests `tests/lsp/lsp_engine.rs`: transcript equal to the CLI
  byte for byte; call hierarchy answered while a 4 s engine request runs;
  `$/cancelRequest` reaches the engine; `didSave` and the watcher make an
  answer fresh after a size- and time-preserving edit; the engine starts on
  the first engine request only. Each with a recorded discrimination proof.

### Changed (context server)

- **`alsem mcp`'s engine workers moved to `src/mcp/pool.rs`**, shared by the
  MCP and LSP front ends behind a small `Transport` trait (how a response is
  wrapped, how a cancelled request ends, how progress is sent). MCP behaviour
  and bytes unchanged (`tests/cli/mcp_server.rs` green). `EngineFront` gains
  `notify_changed_if_running`, which never starts a child.

### Fixed (context server: Windows)

Everything in the context server was built and measured on Linux. Checked here:
`cargo check` (dev and release) and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` for
`x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` of the lib, both binaries and every test target
(cross-compiled with clang and the mingw-w64 headers; one Windows-only
`clippy::result_large_err` allowed on `app_image::check_consistent`, whose
error is a word larger there); the
fixes below; the rest needs a real Windows run, scripted in
`scripts/windows-ctxsrv-check.ps1`. Linux behaviour is unchanged.

- **The Windows build had four warnings; now it has none**: dead helpers of the
  child's output namespace (`leaf`, `refused`, `quota`) are Unix-only, and
  `release_alloc::set_resident`'s `thp_off` is read off Linux too.
  `child_tests`'s two instance-directory tests are Unix-only (they used
  `std::os::unix` and expect a directory Windows never makes).
- **A stray print could corrupt the protocol stream on Windows.** The child's
  and `alsem mcp`'s protocol stream was plain stdout off Unix. It is now a
  duplicate of the standard output handle, and the process's standard output
  is pointed at its stderr (`SetStdHandle`), as `dup2` does on Unix. New hook
  `stray-stdout-on-ask` and test `a_stray_print_never_reaches_the_protocol_stream`
  (Linux: dropping the `dup2` fails it with a `protocol` answer).
- **Windows answers over 64 KiB failed.** With no output directory (Windows
  fails closed, design §10), a stdout over the ask's inline cap was a
  `protocol` failure, so a CDO digest larger than 64 KiB could not be
  delivered at all. The child now answers inline-only: the cap rises to
  4 MiB, and a larger stdout is answered `refusedPath` as §10 states. New
  hook `no-output-dir` takes this path on any platform, in the child and in
  `alsem mcp`'s output folder. Tests `without_an_output_directory_answers_stay_inline`
  and `the_inline_only_path_delivers_inline` (digest inline with its summary,
  an over-cap stdout inline, `out` refused, nothing written) and
  `inline_only_refuses_an_undeliverable_answer`, each with a recorded break.
- **The memory budget read 0 on Windows**, so admission ignored the real RSS.
  The child's meter now reads the working set (`K32GetProcessMemoryInfo`).
  Windows cannot reset the peak, so a peak window reports the lifetime peak
  only when it rose in that window, and otherwise records no observation
  (`window_peak`, test `an_unknown_window_peak_records_no_observation`).
- The engine child is started with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` on Windows (a front end
  with no console would otherwise give it a console window), and a Windows
  NTSTATUS exit (a `release-ship` panic is 0xC0000409) is described in hex.
- The interior release of freed blocks is now disabled outside Linux (it
  was a no-op there, but still sent `realloc` down the copy path).
- `app_image`'s sealed copy on Windows: `tempfile` opens it with share mode
  0 and delete-on-close, which §5.2 requires; documented, with a
  Windows-only test.

### Fixed (context server: the resident refresh)

- **The default mode no longer extracts the dependency source text again on
  every refresh.** The workspace session now keeps each source-bearing
  dependency's extracted file list in both memory modes (before, only
  `--low-mem` did), so the next snapshot shares that text through the
  session's `DepCache` at the same `.app` stamp (size, time and the image's
  blake3) instead of extracting it again; a changed package is a new stamp
  and a P refresh, which extracts the new text. The tier's trees hold the same
  `Arc<str>` texts, so only the lists are extra. Measured on CDO
  (release-fast, `IssueReminder`, one `alsem engine-host` child through
  `census-probe front-seq`, six B refreshes per run, two runs interleaved with
  the old binary): B refresh median **2.76 s -> 2.61 s** (2.67-2.81 s before,
  2.50-2.70 s after); S unchanged within noise (6.9-7.5 s). Test
  `dependency_text_is_extracted_once_per_package` (both modes, every step
  cold-equal): one extraction for the cold refresh, none for a B or an S,
  one for a changed package, none for the B after it. Discrimination:
  keeping the list only under `--low-mem` again fails the default-mode test
  at the first B (1 extraction, expected 0); reverted, green.
- **The resident child's per-refresh RSS creep: what it was, and the fix.**
  *Measured first* (`census-probe refresh-seq`: the child's code in process,
  a counting allocator over mimalloc; and `front-seq`: a real `alsem
  engine-host` child; CDO copy, `IssueReminder`, each refresh followed by
  query, explain, prove and digest). **Not a leak:** the live heap after the
  asks stays within 2 MiB over 20 B and 10 S refreshes in both modes (default
  3,701-3,703 MiB, `--low-mem` 2,894-2,895 MiB, flat after ten refreshes).
  Not glibc (C code holds 2.9 MiB), not freed pages a thread keeps (a
  `mi_collect(true)` on every thread frees nothing), not the per-call
  big-stack pools (one persistent pool creeps the same). **It is mimalloc
  page fragmentation**, made worse by transparent huge pages: each refresh
  builds the next revision while the published one is alive and then frees
  the old one, and a freed block stays resident inside any page that still
  holds a live block (mimalloc's bytes beyond its blocks in use: 451 MiB after
  the cold build, 835 MiB after 3 B and 3 S refreshes; pages 39.1 K -> 42.3 K).
  It converges: before the fix, over 40 B then 20 S refreshes, the child's
  RSS went 4.81 GB cold, 5.06 GB after the first refresh, then flattened at
  5.22-5.25 GB (B, by about the 30th) and 5.44-5.46 GB (S, by about the
  12th): a band of 0.40 GB over the first refresh.
  *The fix* (`al_sem::release_alloc`, the `alsem` binary's allocator):
  `alsem engine-host` hands the interior of every freed block of 16-512 KiB
  back to the OS (`madvise(MADV_DONTNEED)` on the whole 4 KiB pages after its
  first; mimalloc 3 has no option for freed memory inside a live page), and
  a `--low-mem` child also turns transparent huge pages off for itself
  (`PR_SET_THP_DISABLE`: with them on, `khugepaged` collapses part of the
  released pages back into huge pages). Every other command keeps plain
  mimalloc. Linux only. Same 60 refreshes (RSS cold / after the first
  refresh / at most / band over the first):
  default mode **4.58 / 4.78 / 5.07 GB, band 0.29 GB** (before 4.81 / 5.06 /
  5.46, band 0.40), flat after about ten refreshes of each kind, 0.39 GB less
  at the end; with huge pages off as well, 4.24 / 4.44 / 4.66 GB, band
  0.22 GB (retained floor at the end 3.93 against 4.72 GB). `--low-mem` (20 B
  then 10 S, huge pages off): **3.50 / 3.73 / 3.95 GB, band 0.22 GB** (before
  3.81 / 4.03 / 4.37, band 0.34). Speed (two interleaved runs of 6 B and
  2 S each, one child): the four asks 36.0 s before, 36.6 s with the release
  (+1.7 %), 38.2 s with huge pages off as well (+6 %); B refresh 2.74 s
  before, 2.67 s with the release (the dependency-text fix above included),
  2.84 s with huge pages off as well. So the default mode, kept the fastest
  by the owner's decision, releases with huge pages on; `--low-mem` trades
  about 4 % on the asks for about 0.4 GB. `status.memory` reports `releaseFromBytes`,
  `releasedBlocks`, `releasedBytes` and `thpDisabled`; `ALSEM_RELEASE_MIN`
  (bytes, `0` = both off) is for measurement. Threshold by measurement (6 B
  + 2 S, huge pages on): RSS 4.86 GB at 16 KiB, 5.00 GB at 64 KiB, 5.15 GB
  off; 8 KiB released no more than 16 KiB with twice the calls (about 50,000
  per B refresh at 16 KiB).
- Tests: `release_alloc::tests::freed_large_blocks_are_released_only_when_on`
  (mincore: a freed block's interior stays resident when off, is discarded
  on `dealloc` and on a moving `realloc` when on; contents kept, zeroed
  allocation still zero); `tests/resident_memory_bound.rs` (own binary, a
  counting allocator: a `ResidentSession` over a fixture with a source
  dependency, 24 B and 6 S refreshes each with the four asks, both modes, live
  heap within 2 MiB of the first refresh's; the fixture's live heap moves by
  up to 0.7 MB between refreshes with nothing kept, crossbeam-epoch's
  deferred queue garbage); `engine_host::the_child_releases_freed_large_blocks`
  (the child turns the release on, releases blocks after a refresh, turns
  huge pages off under `--low-mem` only, answers the CLI's bytes;
  `ALSEM_RELEASE_MIN=0` turns both off).
  Discrimination (each broken with Edit, run, reverted, run green): no
