  release in `dealloc` fails the mincore test (79 of 79 pages resident); none
  in the moving `realloc` fails it (63 of 63); the session keeping every
  previous revision fails the bound at B9 (3.1 MB over 1.0 MB, about 230 KB
  per kept revision); `engine-host` not turning the release on fails the e2e
  test (`releaseFromBytes` 0); not turning huge pages off fails it
  (`thpDisabled` false), and so do turning them off in the default mode and
  never turning them off (the `--low-mem` child).
- `census-probe`: `refresh-seq` and `front-seq` (the sequences above),
  `--features mimalloc`, and the `PROBE_RELEASE`, `PROBE_COLLECT`,
  `PROBE_MI_AREAS`, `PROBE_MI_STATS` diagnostics (`tools/census-probe/README.md`).

### Added (context server: `--low-mem`, no dependency syntax trees kept between revisions)

- **Owner decision (2026-11-02):** the default keeps everything (fastest); about
  4.6 GB resident on CDO is the accepted default target, replacing the design's
  3 GB. `--low-mem` is the opt-in for less memory.
- `alsem engine-host --low-mem` and `alsem mcp --low-mem` (passed to each
  child): the cross-app workspace session builds with the new profile
  `BuildProfile::ON_DEMAND` (`DependencyBodies::OnDemand`). The dependency tier
  keeps no syntax tree (it is the `Summary` tier and shares its `DepKey`); a
  build's own context holds the trees only when it parsed them, and they die
  with it. The session keeps each source-bearing dependency's extracted text
  instead (the list the snapshot shares, so the next snapshot reads the same
  text from the session's `DepCache` at the same `.app` stamp).
  What is parsed when: **P** parses every dependency file (the tier is built
  from that parse, as before); **S** parses every one again
  (`ProgramContext::ensure_dep_bodies`), because every dependency body is
  re-resolved; **B** parses none, except the files whose kept rows or routine
  ids miss in the model assembly (a demand expansion, changed assembly needs,
  rows evicted), which are parsed in parallel and only those. Single-app
  children hold no dependency tree either way. `status` reports `lowMem`.
- The row cache keys a file's rows and a dependency file's routine ids on the
  **text** (a tree is `al_syntax::parse` of its text and nothing else) instead
  of the tree's identity, so it holds no tree; equal answers in both modes.
  On-demand file numbering (`FileTable::build_from`) comes from the
  snapshot's file lists, in `parse_dep_bodies`' order.
- `aldump --session-refresh --low-mem`; `census-probe resident <ws> [routine]
  --low-mem`; `RefreshReport.dependency_files_parsed` and
  `RowCacheStats.dependency_parsed` count the re-parses.
- Measured on CDO (release-fast, `IssueReminder`, one child over the protocol):
  RSS after query, explain, prove, digest **3.72 GB** low-mem against **4.70 GB**
  default (retained floor 2.95-2.97 against 3.90-3.91 GB), peak 4.56 against
  5.56 GB; live heap (census-probe) 2,903 against 3,711 MiB (the dependency
  trees were 925 MiB, of which 117 MiB text, now kept alone). Warm asks
  unchanged (query 0.04 s, explain 6.3-6.4 s, prove 6.1-6.4 s, digest
  5.4-5.7 s, both modes). Refresh per change type (`aldump --session-refresh
  --verify` on a copy, every step equal to cold): B **2.29-2.37 s** low-mem
  against 2.52-2.86 s default (low-mem extracts no dependency text again);
  S/F **8.0-8.5 s** against 6.8-7.2 s (+1.2-1.4 s: 10,881 dependency files
  parsed); P 11.9-12.5 s against 12.3-13.1 s. After a B, an S and an S edit,
  each followed by the four asks: RSS 4.39 GB low-mem against 5.36 GB default.
- The low-mem default budget stays **6 GiB**, by measurement: at 4.5 GiB the
  asks after the first S were refused, at 5 GiB the second S was refused as
  impossible (the floor creeps 0.2-0.3 GB per refresh in both modes); at 6 GiB
  nothing was refused or evicted.
- Tests: every session cold-oracle test runs in both modes
  (`program::session::workspace::tests::{default_mode,low_mem}`);
  `low_mem_retains_no_dependency_tree` (a `Weak` probe on every dependency tree
  a refresh builds or parses: none alive after P, B, a demand expansion, S and
  an eviction, with the model held; exact parse counts 0 / 1 / all / all); the
  `ON_DEMAND` profile against `FULL` (report, numbering, dependency body
  resolution, miss and hit; and on CDO under `cdo-gate`); the resident session
  answers cold-equal after B and S in both modes; an end-to-end `--low-mem`
  child. Discrimination: keeping the trees despite the flag fails the probe
  (6 alive); skipping the demand-expansion re-parse fails three low-mem tests;
  dropping the text from the row key fails 25 tests in both modes; numbering
  dependency files in another order fails 21 low-mem tests; skipping the S
  re-parse fails the resident test. The text check on kept routine ids stays
  green when broken (a dependency text changes only with a P, which drops the
  cache): a stated limit.

### Added (context-server stage 3: admission, eviction, idle children, MCP wiring)

- **Reservation before work** (`engine::resident::budget`): every build, fill and
  request's trees reserve their estimated peak; `rss + reserved + estimate <= budget`
  or the child reclaims (admission closed, in-flight releasers waited for, unheld
  artifacts evicted in the design's order: dependency raw, the session's dependency
  rows, runs, det, fold, ordering, rules; never the model, relation, tier or L4 seed)
  and tries once more, else answers `budget` with `estimateKiB`, `budgetKiB`,
  `retainedFloorKiB`. An estimate that cannot fit above the retained floor
  (`status.memory.retainedBytes`: RSS less the measured bytes of every evictable
  artifact) fails at once. A first build is estimated from the manifest's `.al` and
  package bytes (floor 1.5 GiB cross-app, 0.5 GiB single-app) and refused before
  anything is read; observed peaks (`/proc` peak windows) replace the table.
  A request's artifacts stay pinned through its compute, so a reclaim never evicts
  what a request reads (found on CDO: a request's own fold was evicted by its trees'
  reservation).
- `alsem engine-host --memory-budget` (default **6 GiB** cross-app, 2 GiB
  single-app: the design's 4 GiB is below what CDO retains after one build) and
  `--idle-timeout` (600 s: the child announces `engine/idleExit` and ends after a
  grace; the front end starts a new child on its next call, no death counted).
  `status.memory` reports the budget's counters.
- Lanes: one heavy worker and four light workers (queries) in the child; a panic in
  a request ends the child in every profile (the front end restarts it).
- `alsem mcp`: `notifications/cancelled` drops a queued call or sends the running one
  `session/cancel`, and the call is not answered; `alsem_refresh` is `session/refresh
  {wait}`; `--memory-budget`, `--idle-timeout`, `--max-children` (default 2: a call
  for another workspace ends the least recently used idle child) and
  `--total-budget`. `alsem_status` shows each child's memory, idle timeout and
  retirements.
- Measured on CDO (release-fast, cross-app, `IssueReminder`): with the default
  budget no refusal, RSS after query+explain+prove+digest 4.59 GB, retained floor
  3.90 GB; with `--memory-budget 5G` the explain's trees reclaimed the dependency
  rows (10,881 files) and every answer was given, RSS 4.34 GB, peak 5.10 GB; with
  4.5G explain is refused `budget` (the floor 3.75 GB plus the trees' 0.9 GB).

### Changed (context-server stage 3: the resident engine keeps less)

- **Where the resident child's memory goes, measured.** A new `census-probe
  resident <ws> [routine]` mode (counting allocator, drop deltas) builds a
  workspace session and a revision as `alsem engine-host` does, asks query,
  explain, prove and digest twice, then drops every retained part in order.
  On CDO (master `e5b515be`), live heap after the build 3,522 MiB and after
  the four asks 4,441 MiB: the workspace session 2,635 MiB (dependency body
  parses 1,121, dependency rows 691, dependency resolution 595, workspace rows
  70, the rest 158), the model and cross-app base 888 MiB (routine rows 576),
  the artifacts 918 MiB (fold 602, det 191, l4 79, run 46). The child's RSS is
  about 0.7 GB above its live heap (28 M live allocations); `mi_collect`
  after each ask frees none of it.
- **Spare capacity is no longer retained.** Each parse's arenas
  (`al_syntax::ir::exact_size`, a move into an exact allocation: mimalloc
  keeps a block a `shrink_to_fit` still fills by half), the dependency edges
  and their route vectors, and the session's kept dependency rows (a clone
  is kept, not the push-built original) are exactly sized; a routine's
  `statement_tree` is behind an `Arc`, one exact copy shared by the kept rows
  and every revision's model. CDO live heap after the build 2,792 MiB (was
  3,522), after the four asks 3,711 MiB (was 4,441); child RSS after the
  build 3.69 GB (was 4.26), after the four asks 4.55 GB (was 5.14), peak
  5.37 GB (was 5.98). Answers unchanged (every golden and T-order test).

### Fixed (`alsem mcp` help and README described the engine as not yet resident)

- **`alsem mcp --help` and the README said each call builds the model afresh and that
  every answer is fresh whatever is asked.** Both stopped being true when the resident
  engine landed (stage 2 completion). They now say the engine keeps the built model,
  refreshes incrementally on an edit, and describe the three freshness modes. Also
  silenced the release-only `unused_mut` warning on `hello` in
  `engine::host::child::serve` (it is mutated only under the test hooks).

### Measured (context-server stage 2: sequential warm asks through the resident child)

- CDO baseline, release-fast, one `alsem engine-host` driven over the
  protocol, cross-app, `IssueReminder`; every stdout byte-equal to the CLI's
  (sha256 compared). Wall per ask, child RSS after it, against a cold CLI run:
  first ask `query effects` **16.2 s** (build 13.6 s + solve 2.5 s; RSS
  4.28 GB) vs CLI 12.0 s; warm `query effects` **0.04 s**; `explain
  --routine --format json` **21.8 s** (the first composition with every
  primary routine's raw facts 14.9 s, then the tree and card 6.9 s; RSS
  4.95 GB) vs 25.9 s; `prove may-commit` **7.4 s** (det 0.8 s, tree + prove
  6.6 s) vs 27.2 s; `digest --routine` **5.9 s** vs 26.8 s. Resident RSS
  after all five **5.16 GB**, peak 5.98 GB (CLI peaks 3.35–3.40 GB): above
  the design's 3 GB resident target, which stage 3's T-mem owns. The
  per-ask freshness check took 1.4 ms.
- One body edit on a temp copy (a statement added to `IssueReminder`): the
  next ask refreshed the revision (class B, 3.0 s, 1 file parsed and
  resolved, dependency bodies reused) and answered `query` in **5.5 s** in all
  (the L4 solve is not seeded yet: 2.2 s); the following `digest` took
  21.5 s (the composition is refolded whole until stage 5's cone store:
  15.4 s) vs CLI 26.6 s. Both byte-equal to the CLI on the edited copy.

### Added (context-server stage 2: the resident engine child and the completed protocol)

- **`alsem engine-host` is resident**: the first ask builds a revision of the
  workspace (cross-app through the stage-4 incremental model), later asks
  are answered off it after a per-ask freshness check, and an edit
  refreshes it. `explain`, `prove`, `digest` and `query` are answered off
  the revision's retained artifacts (`ensure_prepared`); every other command
  runs the one-shot job path over the revision's acquired read. Answers stay
  the CLI's exact bytes and now name their revision (`engineInstanceId`,
  `generation`, `inputsStamp`).
- **Protocol** (still version 1; every new field optional on the wire):
  `session/open` takes `universe` (`crossApp` | `singleApp`, enforced: an ask
  of the other universe or another workspace is `notThisWorkspace`; the
  workspace must be a folder) and answers `outputDir`; `session/ask` takes
  `requestFiles` (the bytes of every file the command's planning reads, as
  the front end read them; the child never reads a request file),
  `freshness` (`fresh` | `latest-built` | `verify`), `deadlineMs` and
  `progress`; `decisions` (the diff root and `--changed`'s file-or-list) are
  mandatory when the command reads paths, and an ask without them is
  refused `protocol` (the child never probes the file system).
  `session/cancel {id}`, `session/notifyChanged {paths}` (notifications or
  requests) and `session/refresh {wait}` are new. Answers carry `stale`,
  `universe`, `timing {queuedMs, waitedForBuildMs, sharedFillMs, computeMs}`
  and, for a stopped ask, `workDoneMs` and `skippedPhases`. `session/status`
  adds the universe, the published revision, the session's builds, the fill
  counters, the queue and the output directory.
- The child reads requests on its own thread and answers asks on one worker:
  status, cancel and change notifications are answered while an ask runs;
  at most 16 heavy and 64 light asks (16 MiB of parameters) wait, beyond is
  `busy`; a cancelled queued ask answers `cancelled` at once, an expired one
  `deadline`, both with no work; an ask in flight stops between phases and
  tree groups. A shutdown is answered after every queued ask.
- `Answer::terminal`, the one terminal constructor at both hops (the
  child's frame fallback, every failure of `EngineFront`).
- **Private output namespace** (design §10, `engine::host::output`): the
  child creates `<outputRoot>/<engineInstanceId>/` relative to an opened
  root handle, owner-only, refused if it exists; every spill is created
  there `O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW` and recorded with its identity; an overwrite is
  permitted only for a recorded entry whose identity still matches (temp
  leaf + `renameat`); quota 1 GB. Non-Unix platforms fail closed
  (inline-only).
- `EngineFront`: `FrontConfig.universe`, `ask_with` (cancel flag, progress
  callback), `notify_changed`, `refresh`. `alsem engine-ask` ships the
  request's files and takes `--freshness` and `--params` (print the ask's
  params and exit). The MCP front end opens its child in the call's universe,
  passes its freshness, and reports the engine's `stale`, `waitedForBuildMs`
  and `sharedFillMs`.
- Tests: the child over stub engines (frames, queue order, cancel queued and
  in flight, deadlines, busy, notifications, the instance directory), T-paths,
  T-terminal, and end to end through `EngineFront`: T-order over one
  revision, an edit between asks (fresh, latest-built, verify), T-exit3,
  mandatory decisions with shipped request files, the universe refusal,
  deadline and cancel.

### Added (context-server stage 2: the resident session core)

- **`engine::resident`** (design §4-§5): the session core a resident engine
  child answers from. `store`: artifact snapshots and `ensure_prepared`
  (§4.2) — dependency-aware phases, a fill registry with per-key monotonic
  generations, one publication transaction per phase that merges into the
  current snapshot and discards a value whose key was tombstoned since its
  claim (refilled, at most 3 times, then "artifact churn"), keys pinned for
  assembly that eviction skips, and claims released and waiters woken on
  every failure path (cancel, deadline, failed reservation, failed or
  panicking fill); a request gets a ready snapshot or an error, never a
  partial one. `revision`: one built target over one acquired read, its
  artifacts (`Ordering`, `Rules`, `Fold` = the one composition with the
  primary raw facts and pd arena, `L4` with its never-drained core
  summaries, `Raw(subjects)` for dependency roots, `Det` at a mask, `Run`),
  and `answer(job)`: resolve, `ensure_prepared`, the request's trees off the
  ready snapshot, the job's compute over a served `View` — the CLI's exact
  output. `manifest`: every input a build reads (each `.al` text, the walk,
  `app.json`, `roots.config.json`, the coverage yaml, the nested `app.json`
  list, the source-dependency config, package discovery and each `.app`,
  universe, engine, grammar), `M_consumed` from the acquired read, stat-cached
  or fully hashed observations, the `al-sem-manifest-v1:` stamp, and the
  three-way check over every entry. `session`: the published revision (or
  failed build), the per-request pin by freshness mode (`fresh`, `verify`,
  `latest-built` with `stale`, changed paths and a background refresh),
  change notifications, and the build (cross-app through the stage-4
  `WorkspaceSession`) discarded and retried when its three observations
  disagree (3 attempts, then `inputsUnstable`).
- `View` holds its target owned or shared (`View::served` is no longer
  test-only); `capability_cone::cross_app_base_of` builds the base over a
  cross-app model built already (the session's).
- Tests (each with a recorded discrimination proof): T-prepared on the store
  (empty snapshot, eviction, disjoint concurrent publication, tombstoned
  publication refilled, joined prerequisite before dependent, failed
  reservation wakes its waiter, cancelled waiter, failed fill, churn, pinned
  keys); T-order on real artifacts (mixed orders single-app and cross-app,
  dependency root, det evict and refill, seeded L4 over the retained core,
  T-pin, cancel between phases); T-manifest; T-fresh, latest-built, verify
  and notify, T-acquire-during, T-acquire-after, unstable inputs,
  T-failed-build. The stage-1 test-only `Prepared` driver is gone (its tests
  moved to the revision).

### Added (context server: `alsem mcp`, the MCP front end)

- **`alsem mcp`** serves the Model Context Protocol on stdin/stdout for AI
  agents (design `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-01-context-server-design.md`
  §8, §10). A small hand-written JSON-RPC 2.0 layer (`src/mcp/`; no new
  dependency): NDJSON lines, logs on stderr only (fd 1 is moved to the
  protocol stream), protocol versions 2025-06-18 / 2025-03-26 / 2024-11-05
  (the client's echoed when supported, else 2025-06-18), `server/discover`
  answered `-32601` in every state, `-32002` before `initialize`, `-32600`
  for a second `initialize`, a `null` or non-scalar id, or an id still in
  flight; progress notifications only for a call with `_meta.progressToken`.
- Tools `alsem_explain` (`routines` | `diff` text with `diffRoot` |
  `table` + `field`; default format human), `alsem_prove`, `alsem_digest`
  (always a file plus a summary: roots requested and resolved, effect
  counts, per-root coverage), `alsem_query_effects`, `alsem_query_touches`,
  `alsem_status` (per-engine counters, starts nothing) and `alsem_refresh`.
  Common inputs `workspace`, `freshness`, `singleApp`, `out`,
  `maxInlineBytes`. Each call becomes the CLI's argv (`--flag=value`, then
  `--` and the positionals), parsed by the engine child with the binary's
  own clap; the front end decides the diff root and `digest --changed`
  with the CLI's own `decide` and sends a diff's text in the protocol.
  Exclusive modes and non-empty selector arrays are enforced as `-32602`
  (the schemas carry no top-level `oneOf`, which the Anthropic tool API
  refuses).
- Results are the r7 §8.3 envelope: `kind: "cli"` (a semantic build failure
  included, `isError: false`) with `exitCode`, `stdoutText` XOR
  `stdoutFile`, lossless stderr, `stale`, `changedPaths`, `universe`,
  `freshness`, `timing`, `revision` (always present); `kind: "failed"`
  (`isError: true`) for infrastructure outcomes (`engineError`,
  `refusedPath`, `busy`, ...). The envelope is the first text block, the
  inline stdout the second (exactly), and with 2025-06-18 also
  `structuredContent` (plus `output`, the CLI's JSON parsed). Answers are
  bounded to one 16 MiB line with the wire codec's `bound_frame`.
- One engine child per (workspace, universe), each on its own worker thread
  with a queue of 16 (`busy` beyond), so a long build never blocks `ping`
  or another workspace. A child killed mid-call is reported and the next
  call respawns it (the existing `EngineFront` backoff).
- Output policy (§10): every file goes into a private instance folder
  `<output root>/<id>/` (mode 0700, refused if it exists), reached by
  handle-relative `openat`/`mkdirat`/`renameat` with `O_NOFOLLOW`; a
  tool's `out` must be inside it (`..`, other absolute paths and planted
  symlinks are `refusedPath`); only files the server wrote, identity
  unchanged, are overwritten; 1 GB quota; folders older than 24 h removed
  at start. Off Unix the sink fails closed (answers stay inline).
- Tests: `tests/cli/mcp_server.rs` (a full transcript, each answer equal to
  the CLI's stdout byte for byte, version negotiation, invalid and
  duplicate ids, a semantic build failure, refused paths, progress, a
  killed engine respawned) and unit tests in `src/mcp/`; each with a
  recorded discrimination proof.
- Measured on the CDO baseline (release-fast, cross-app, one `tools/call`
  per tool through one `alsem mcp` vs the CLI run right after it; one
  shared machine): every stdout, stderr and exit equal. Wall, MCP / CLI:
  explain 27.7 / 28.0 s (81 KB human card, to a file over 64 KiB), prove
  26.2 / 27.8 s, digest 26.5 / 22.7 s (35 KB, file), query effects
  13.2 / 13.6 s, query touches 13.5 / 13.8 s. One engine child served all
  five (5 asks, 5 workspace reads): the child is still one-shot, so every
  call is a cold build and the front end adds no measurable cost; a
  resident child will make the later calls warm with no front-end change.

### Measured (context-server stage 4: refresh per change type)

- On a temp copy of the CDO baseline (release-fast, `aldump --session-refresh
  --verify`, the same shared machine, run back to back): every step's model
  equals the cold build's. `revision.refresh` before (master 6c463893) →
  after: **B 5.7–6.0 s → 2.43–2.53 s** (program 1.6–2.1 → 0.70–0.76 s;
  model assembly ~2.5–3.0 → ~0.65 s; attach ~0.9–1.0 s unchanged, whole by
  design); **S/F 10.1–11.4 s → 7.0–7.35 s** (dependency re-resolution
  4.1–4.7 s of it, unchanged); P 13.9–14.1 s → 12.2–13.6 s (the cold model
  build 11.7–12.4 s on the same binary). What remains of a B refresh, by
  span: `preflight.snapshot_build` 0.35–0.39 s, `preflight.resolve_full`
  0.19 s (`resolve.event_flow` 64–88 ms), `crossapp.demand` 0.17 s,
  `l3.dependency_rows` 0.25 s (cloning the kept rows), `l3.finish_resolved`
  0.27–0.30 s, `l3.row_nodes` 0.08 s, `crossapp.attach_program_calls`
  0.90–1.0 s. `model.copied_bytes` per B unchanged at 15.5 MB (it counts
  the program's reused resolutions, not the row copies). Peak RSS of the
  whole driver run (session plus verifying cold builds) 5.46 → 6.50 GB:
  the kept raw rows.

### Fixed (graph assembly: platform publisher injection; stage-4 follow-ups)

- **`inject_platform_event_publishers` scanned every routine of the graph
  once per platform-event subscriber** to decide whether the table already
  has a real publisher of that name (0.31–0.33 s of the 0.33–0.35 s
  `preflight.assemble_graph` on CDO, every build and every session
  revision; `graph.platform_publishers`). It now reads the run of
  `(table, event)` in the sorted routine list (`NodeSet::run_by`; the id's
  order starts with the object and the name), the same set the scan
  filtered. Behaviour-preserving: every golden unchanged. New test
  `platform_publisher_is_not_injected_over_a_real_one` states the rule
  literally (a real publisher suppresses the synthetic, a same-named
  non-publisher does not, a publisher on another table does not); break:
  key the run on the table alone → it fails ("not a publisher").
  With this the graph reassembly the design's `DeclSemantics` /
  `DeclLocations` split was to avoid costs ~20 ms per revision
  (`graph.extract` 8–12 ms, `graph.layer_index` 3–5 ms), so the split is
  not built: rebuilding is exact and cheaper than keeping the parts.
- **The session keeps each dependency file's routine ids**
  (`RowCache::dependency_ids`, a pure function of the app and the parse,
  checked by parse identity): the demanded slice and the rows' nodes are
  looked up instead of hashing every dependency routine's id again each
  revision (10,881 files on CDO). The cold assembly is unchanged. Break:
  the slice from the ids ignores the demand → 10 session tests fail on
  model equality.
- **The event-flow edges stay whole** (design §6.5), now that they cost
  64–75 ms per revision on CDO (they were 0.73–0.94 s, see the subscriber
  tier fix below). No finer rule: a body-only edit above a workspace
  subscriber changes the edge of an unchanged DEPENDENCY publisher (its
  route witness is the subscriber's span), so neither reusing the edges
  under B nor recomputing only the publishers in changed files is correct.
  Counterexample test `event_flow_edge_of_an_unchanged_publisher_moves_under_b`
  (its precondition shows the cold edge moving; the session equals cold).

### Added (context-server stage 4: retained raw model rows)

- **The workspace session keeps each file's raw model rows** (context-server
  design §6.8 L3/L4, `program::model::row_cache`). The model assembly
  projects every workspace file, every source-bearing dependency file (its
  demanded slice) and every symbol-only dependency's ABI into rows; all are
  pure functions of their inputs. A session's assembly
  (`WorkspaceSession::refresh_model`, now what `refresh` runs) takes a
  file's rows from the previous revision exactly when every input is equal:
  the parse (by identity: a tree is reused only for byte-equal text, and a
  dependency tree belongs to the tier), the text, the population (physical
  rows / demanded slice), the parens-less calls, the needs, the app guid and
  the source unit. The `FileIx` is kept symbolically: `project_ir` writes it
  only into each routine row's `file`, so a reused copy is re-stamped with
  the current index (a file add shifts every later file's, the dependency
  files' included, which would otherwise reproject all 10,881 CDO dependency
  files). The ABI block is kept with the
  required-dependency list, the apps' `AppRef`s and the needs; the session
  drops all kept rows on a P change, so a block never outlives its packages.
  Row order, `RowNodes`, `finish_resolved`, the adapter, the event graph and
  the three final passes are the cold pipeline's, run whole; each row's
  program node is recomputed every revision. The cold assembly is unchanged
  (no cache: it projects straight into the model, as before).
  `RefreshReport.rows` (`RowCacheStats`) and `aldump --session-refresh`'s
  `rows` field say what was projected and reused.
- New spans: `l3.dependency_rows` (the dependency part of the assembly),
  `graph.extract`, `graph.layer_index`, `graph.lookup_and_internal`,
  `graph.platform_publishers` (inside `preflight.assemble_graph`).
- Tests (T-rows): a body edit projects only its own file (the other
  workspace files and every dependency file reused); the ABI block of a
  symbol-only dependency is reused across B and S and rebuilt when the needs
  change or its package changes (P); a file whose text is unchanged is
  projected again when its parens-less calls change (a renamed callee, S),
  and re-stamped, not projected, when an added file shifts its `FileIx`.
  Discrimination (each break seen failing on model equality, then
  reverted): key without the parens-less calls (the parens-less test
  fails), reuse without the re-stamp (the file-add and `FileIx`-shift tests
  fail), without the population (the demand W → D1 → D2
  test fails), the ABI key without the needs and the file key without the
  needs (the ABI-block test fails), keep the rows across P (the symbol-only
  package test fails).

### Fixed (event-flow edges: subscriber tier lookup)

- `emit_event_flow_edges` found each subscriber route's tier by scanning
  every routine of the graph from the front, once per route (0.7–0.9 s per
  build on CDO; `resolve.event_flow`). It now takes the head of the
  subscriber id's run in the sorted routine list (`NodeSet::run_by`), the
  same routine the scan found (on an aliased id, the first in merged order).
  Behaviour-preserving: every golden unchanged.

### Changed (the ABI-integrity check is a declared need)

- **Only the readers of the ABI-integrity check compute it.** It re-reads
  every dependency's SymbolReference after the resolve (0.85 s on the CDO
  baseline), and every cold cross-app command paid for it in
  `ResolvedProgram::build`, which then dropped it. Now
  `full::resolve_full_program_with` takes `abi_check::AbiIntegrity::{Check,
  Skip}` with no default. Its readers declare `Check`: `aldump
  --program-call-graph-stats` (through `resolve_full_program`, the stats
  entry) and the CDO ratchet `cdo_full_program_coverage_and_self_reported_metric`.
  The command builders (`fresh_program_from_snapshot_with`, behind
  `ResolvedProgram::build`) and the workspace session declare `Skip`. The
  session used to fill the report with zeros, which read like "no ABI routes".
  `ProgramReport::abi_integrity` is now an `Option`, read through
  `abi_integrity()`, which panics "ABI integrity not computed: resolve with
  AbiIntegrity::Check". `ResolvedProgram::from_parts` asserts in debug builds
  that nothing computed it. The applicability check and
  `abi_ingestion_integrity_cdo_gate` run their own check and are unchanged.
- Tests: `the_program_builders_skip_the_abi_integrity_check` and
  `reading_an_unchecked_abi_integrity_panics` (`program::resolved`), and
  `program_call_graph_stats_report_the_abi_integrity_check`
  (`tests/cli/cli_parameterless_symbol_method.rs`, 3 routes, all mapped).
  Discrimination: the stats entry with `Skip` fails the stats test (aldump
  panics with the message); the command builder with `Check` fails the
  builder test and 3 other `resolved` tests through the `from_parts` assert;
  an accessor that returns an empty report fails the panic test; the session
  with `Check` fails 15 session tests. Each passes again after the revert.
- **Measured on CDO** (release-fast, `/usr/bin/time -v`, 3 alternating
  rounds, shared machine with load around 7): the `resolve.abi_integrity`
  span (0.85 s) is gone and `preflight.resolve_full` drops from 1.87 s to
  1.00 s (`ALSEM_TRACE`, `analyze`). Wall time, before / after (median of 3):
  `analyze` 23.5 / 21.7 s, `prove IssueReminder may-commit` 30.5 / 29.1 s,
  `explain --routine IssueReminder` 31.5 / 26.0 s. These are noisy (one
  before round ran 5 s slow on every command); the span is the exact saving.
  Peak RSS is unchanged within noise (3.42–3.49 GB on both sides; `explain`
  about 20 MB lower). Every command's stdout is byte-identical before and
  after.

### Fixed (flaky `engine_ask_prints_what_the_cli_prints`: a broken pipe in the test)

- **The test, not the product, raced.** For its `--no-such-flag` case both
  `alsem` and `alsem engine-ask` exit on the clap error without reading stdin
  (`engine-ask` exits before it starts an engine child). The test wrote its
  diff to their stdin with `.unwrap()`; when the process had already exited,
  the write failed with a broken pipe (EPIPE) and the test panicked. It failed
  only when the process won the race. The test helper (`run_with_stdin` in
  `tests/cli/engine_host.rs`) now treats a broken pipe as the process's
  outcome and compares exit and streams as usual; any other write error still
  fails, as in `cli_batch_*`.
- **The race is now pinned deterministically.**
  `a_process_that_exits_before_reading_its_stdin_is_compared` writes 4 MiB,
  far over any pipe buffer, so the write always meets the closed pipe. With
  the broken-pipe arm removed it failed 3/3 (`write stdin: Broken pipe (os
  error 32)`); restored, it passes.
- **The product side was already correct, and is now pinned.** The front
  end's failed request write (`EngineFront::call`) becomes an `engineError`
  answer with the death recorded. No test reached that path. A new child test
  hook, `exit-after-open` (`ALSEM_ENGINE_TEST_HOOK`), exits right after
  answering `session/open`; `a_child_gone_before_the_request_write_fails_the_ask`
  sends a 4 MiB ask to it and asserts the answer names the failed write. With
  that path changed to a panic the test failed and every other `engine_host`
  test still passed; restored, it passes.

### Added (context-server stage 4: `aldump --session-refresh`)

- **`aldump --session-refresh <workspace-copy> [--file <rel>] [--verify]`**
  measures the workspace session per change type on a real workspace: cold,
  no-op, body edit, prepended newlines, an added procedure, an added file and
  an `app.json` byte, each followed by its restore, one JSON line per refresh
  (class, files parsed/resolved, dependency bodies resolved again,
  `copiedBytes`, `programMs`, `refreshMs`, resident set). `--verify` builds
  each step's model cold and compares the two `write_model` fingerprints. It
  edits the workspace, so it refuses one inside a git checkout (the pinned
  CDO baseline is). `session::workspace::{write_program, write_model,
  model_fingerprint}` are the equality projections the tests and the driver
  share; `RefreshReport` gains `program_ms`.
- **The dependency resolution is shared, not copied, across B.**
  `DependencyBodyResolution.edges` and `.site_facts` are `Arc`s;
  `ProgramBody` holds the dependency edges by `Arc` and its site facts as a
  two-layer `SiteFactsMap` (workspace facts over the shared dependency facts;
  reads answer what the merged map answered, the dependency entry winning a
  common key) read through the `Copy` view `SiteFactsRef`, which `EdgeView`
  and the adapter now carry. A session copies the reused dependency edges
  only when a witness into a moved workspace declaration must change
  (`full::witnesses_current`, then `Arc::make_mut` + re-materialization);
  `RefreshReport.dependency_edges_copied` says which. On CDO
  `model.copied_bytes` per B revision drops from 310 MB to 15.5 MB.
- The session skips the ABI-integrity check, whose one consumer on its path
  (`ResolvedProgram::from_parts`) drops it, as the cold `ResolvedProgram::build`
  does (0.8–1.0 s on CDO); every other caller computes it as before.
- New spans inside the resolve: `resolve.decl_surface`, `resolve.index`,
  `resolve.files`, `resolve.event_flow`, `resolve.abi_integrity`.
- **Measured on a temp copy of the CDO baseline** (release-fast,
  `aldump --session-refresh --verify`, shared machine): every one of the 12
  steps' models equals the cold build's (`equalToCold: true`). `revision.refresh`
  per class: P (first build) 14.0 s, P (`app.json`) 12.5–12.7 s against a cold
  model build of 13.3–15.8 s; S/F 9.5–10.8 s (dependency re-resolution
  4.1–4.6 s of it); B 5.1–5.9 s (program 1.6–1.8 s; model assembly 2.4–2.9 s,
  attach 0.9–1.0 s, demand 0.15–0.2 s; one noisy 9.1 s no-op). Per-file
  resolution under B is 20–40 ms; `resolve.event_flow` is 0.73–0.94 s every
  revision (the design assumed milliseconds). `model.copied_bytes`: 15.5 MB
  per B, 0 for S/P. Peak RSS of the whole driver run (session plus the
  verifying cold builds) 5.55 GB.

### Added (context-server stage 4: the workspace session, retained parse and resolutions)

- **`program::session::WorkspaceSession`**: the incremental cross-app model
  (context-server design §6, a stage-4 prefix). `refresh(inputs, …)` turns
  the state retained from the previous revision plus the next revision's
  inputs into the next `CrossAppProgram`, under a `revision.refresh` span and
  a `model.copied_bytes` counter; `refresh_program` stops at the program.
  Retained: the dependency tier (held strongly, so the session's `DepCache`
  keeps hitting it), each workspace file's parse (reused for byte-equal
  text), its declaration projection and its pre-refinement `FileResolution`,
  and the dependency bodies' resolution. Classes: **P** (first refresh,
  `DepKey` changed, any root `app.json` byte changed, or a source
  dependency's content hash changed) rebuilds; **S** (a projection changed,
  or a file added, removed or renamed) re-resolves every workspace file and
  every dependency body; **B** re-resolves only the changed files and reuses
  the rest, re-materializing each reused route's `SourceSpan` witness through
  the current declaration surface (`rematerialize_witnesses`: only a routine
  route's `SourceSpan`; `AbiSymbol`, `None` and catalog witnesses untouched; a
  routine the surface lacks is an invariant failure — debug panics, release
  resolves the file again — never a zero-span witness). Every whole-program
  step reruns whole, as the cold build runs it: graph assembly,
  `close_holder_sites`, the event-flow edges, the demand, the model assembly,
  the adapter, the event graph and the three final passes
  (`cross_app_program_from`, unchanged).
- Plumbing, behaviour-preserving for every cold caller:
  `snapshot::parse::parse_unit_reusing` / `ParseReuse`,
  `dep_summary::parse_for_build_reusing`,
  `full::build_context_from_snapshot_reusing`,
  `full::resolve_full_program_reusing` (with `KeptResolutions`),
  `ResolvedProgram::from_parts` (now also what `ResolvedProgram::build`
  assembles through). `ClassifiedEdge` derives `Clone, Debug`;
  `FileResolution` and `DependencyBodyResolution` derive `Clone`.
- Tests (`program::session::workspace::tests`, 16): after every edit the
  session's program (every edge with its witnesses, site facts, parens-less
  calls, meta) and model (rows, calls, bindings, events, diagnostics) equal a
  cold build's, as text — body edits (callee and caller), newlines before a
  callee (a workspace caller's and a DEPENDENCY caller's witness move),
  declaration reorder, signature, return type and arity changes, file add /
  rename / remove and a second implementer of a dependency interface, demand
  W → D1 → D2 and contraction, a dependency raiser and subscriber edits,
  duplicate ids across `#if` arms, the setter-argument holder refinement
  X → Y → unprovable → back with the holder's file unchanged, a temp-proof
  revocation and restoration in an unchanged subscriber, `[MethodId]` /
  `[TryFunction]` through a `__alsem_mid_<n>` dispatch, enum extensibility
  and implementation map, a package change (P), a `roots.config.json`-only
  change (B, nothing re-resolved), `app.json` changes (P), including an
  `internalsVisibleTo` friend that reopens an unchanged caller's G28 dispatch,
  and the re-materialization guard itself. Discrimination (each break seen
  failing, then reverted): skip workspace re-materialization (3 fail); skip
  dependency re-materialization (the T-loc test fails); a zero-span fallback
  on a miss, and a target-keyed rewrite of `AbiSymbol`/`None` (the guard test
  fails); skip `close_holder_sites` when anything is reused (T-refine fails);
  drop `method_id`/`try_function` from the projection (T-methodid fails);
  reuse dependency resolutions across S (2 fail, one through the file-table
  shift a file add causes); ignore the `app.json` identity (both `app.json`
  tests fail, the G28 one on equality); reuse a parse by path alone (10 fail).

### Added (context-server stage 4: the change-type classifier)

- **`program::session::classify`**: the declaration projection of one
  workspace file (context-server design §6.1) — blake3 over every
  `ObjectNode`, `RoutineNode` and `RoutineMeta` the build's own extraction
  (`summarize_file`) yields, in document order with multiplicity, every field
  of every nested type, except the positional origins and
  `RoutineNode.source_unit` (`EXCLUDED`). The encoding is the `Classify`
  trait, implemented by exhaustive destructuring with no `..`, so a new field
  does not compile until it is hashed or excluded (`DECL_PROJECTION_VERSION`).
  `classify_files` gives B (every projection equal on the same paths) or S
  (a projection changed, or a file was added, removed or renamed). Tests
  (T-class, T-proj-guard): body edit and inserted newlines keep the
  projection; a reorder, a parameter/return/`var`/name change, a duplicate,
  `[MethodId]`, `[TryFunction]`, enum extensibility and implementation map,
  a subscriber's target and the path each change it; origins and the
  source-unit stamp do not reach the hash, every other field does.

### Changed (context-server stage 4: the `complete(p)` index)

- **`prove_event_param_temps` scans each publisher's own object only.** Rule 2
  (`complete(p)`: no unresolved call in the publisher's object could name it)
  scanned every row of the model once per local publisher; it now reads an
  `object_id → rows` index built once (context-server design §6.8 L8).
  Behaviour-preserving: same rows, pure predicate; every golden unchanged.
  Measured on the CDO baseline (release-fast, `query touches`, three runs
  each, interleaved): `attach.event_param_temps` 1,160–1,514 ms before (one
  noisy 5,120 ms outlier) → 356–388 ms after; `crossapp.attach_program_calls`
  1,984–2,583 → 1,148–1,393 ms. Output bytes identical. New test
  `complete_reads_only_the_publishers_object` pins the per-object scope
  (break: one bucket for all rows → fails); the existing
  `event_param_temp_unresolved_sibling_raise_is_not_proven` fails when the
  index holds no rows.

### Changed (the producer solve's arena is canonical: context-server stage 1b)

- **`pd_solve::solve` returns its arena in rank order** (design r6 §6.10), so
  its order no longer follows the order of its inputs. A finalization pass
  (`pd_solve::finalize`) ranks producers by `(owner internal id, operation
  id)`, edges by the whole `TypedOutEdge` identity in internal ids (`from`
  and `sort_key` first, so a state's links stay in `sort_key` order), states
  by `(producer rank, dist, routine internal id, t, reqs)` and links by
  `(edge rank, callee state rank)`; it remaps every index (`ConeState.producer`,
  `ConeLink.callee_state`, `ConeLink.edge`, link ranges), rebuilds
  `by_routine` and the resolved entries, and merges two graph edges with one
  identity. Ranks use internal ids, never stable ids: two routines with one
  stable id stay two states. Operation ids rank by their ordinal (`op8` before
  `op10`), the solve's old input order.
- **One witness selection moves on CDO, none on the fixtures.** Of a
  routine's own entries that tie for one fact (one key, `dist` and first hop),
  the cone keeps the first; it is now the most precise `t` rather than the
  first discovered. On CDO (`bc3ccb18`) 12 of 581,584 tie groups now keep
  `Known(false)` instead of `Unknown` of the same producer (the
  `capabilityFacts` section moves; 224 more groups change to a state with the
  same rep, which moves nothing). Ranking that last tie by discovery instead
  reproduces every snapshot section byte for byte, so the rest of the change
  is a pure reordering: on every `r0-corpus` fixture and on CDO the arena's
  logical lines are the same multiset (402 fixture arenas byte-identical, 20
  reordered), and no golden moved (`check-goldens --regen` writes nothing).
- **`aldump --snapshot-memory --pd-dump <file>`** writes the cone arena as
  `ConeArena::logical_lines` (every index replaced by its identity), the
  before/after evidence for an order change.
- Tests: `solve_is_independent_of_input_order` and
  `corpus_arena_and_witnesses_are_independent_of_producer_order` (24 and 6
  permutations; arena bytes and rendered digests identical),
  `solve_keeps_two_routines_that_share_a_stable_id`, `op_id_cmp_orders_by_ordinal_and_stays_total`.

### Fixed (CI: the parent-baseline tests overflowed their stack)

- **CI has been red since the routine-id merge (`212e5f82`): both
  `ids_parent_baseline` tests aborted with "has overflowed its stack" on
  GitHub's runners**, while they passed locally. They analyze every fixture in
  parallel on rayon's default worker threads, whose stack is too small there for
  the recursive AL lowerer. They now run on the big-stack pool
  (`al_sem::big_stack::big_stack_pool`), as every engine call site that lowers AL
  source already does. Reproduced locally by shrinking the default thread stack
  with `RUST_MIN_STACK=1048576` (the test binary built first, at the normal
  stack): with the old direct call both tests abort with CI's exact error
  (SIGABRT, "has overflowed its stack"); with the fix both pass (2 passed).

### Fixed (engine protocol: three stage-2 review findings, review r6 NEW 3-5)

- **A CLI answer's stderr is exact (NEW 3).** The wire used to turn stderr
  into lines with `String::from_utf8_lossy` and rebuild "line + `\n`" from
  them, and `bound_frame` spilled that rebuilt text: `b"warning"` arrived as
  `b"warning\n"` and `[0xff, b'\n']` as a replacement character, even in
  the "exact bytes" `stderrFile`. Now `Stderr::Lines` holds a
  `wire::StderrLines`, which keeps the ORIGINAL bytes and exists only for
  bytes the line form carries exactly (empty, or UTF-8 ending in `\n`);
  lines are derived only to encode. Any other stderr goes to `stderrFile`
  as its original bytes (`Stderr::exact`; design r7 §3, no `stderrBytes`
  inline form), and a frame-limit spill writes the held bytes. The lossy
  `wire::stderr_lines` and `wire::stderr_bytes` are gone; `cli_outcome`
  takes the kind-aware `Spill`. Test
  `wire::tests::stderr_is_exact_against_standalone_replay_inline_and_spilled`
  compares with standalone `replay_on`, through `bound_frame` and the real
  decoder, inline and spilled: no final newline, blank lines, non-UTF-8,
  a UTF-8 character split across actions, several actions. Discrimination:
  with the old lossy conversion restored it fails (`b"warning"` delivered
  as `b"warning\n"`); restored, it passes.
- **An oversized request ending exactly at the read bound no longer eats
  the next request (NEW 4).** `read_frame` reads at most the limit plus one
  byte; for a line of exactly that length INCLUDING its newline, the
  newline was already consumed, and the child's unconditional `skip_line`
  then discarded the following valid request. `read_frame` now returns
  `ReadFrame::{Frame, Eof, Oversized}`, where `Oversized` records
  `delimiter_consumed`, and recovery is only `Oversized::skip_rest` (which
  skips nothing when the newline was read); `skip_line` is private. The
  front end's reader stops at an oversized frame (it kills the child and
  never recovers past it), so it had no such boundary. Tests
  `engine::host::child::tests::serve_recovers_at_every_oversize_boundary`
  (exact limit served; limit + 1 with newline, longer, and at EOF refused,
  each followed by a request that is answered) and
  `wire::tests::read_frame_reports_whether_the_refused_line_ended`.
  Discrimination: with `skip_rest` skipping unconditionally both fail
  (request 11 is swallowed); restored, both pass.
- **The front end's queue of child output is bounded (NEW 5).** The stdout
  reader pushed every frame into an unbounded channel and only `call`
  decoded them, so a faulty child could exhaust the front end's memory.
  The reader now checks each frame's shape (a JSON-RPC 2.0 response with
  exactly one of result and error, or a notification) before queueing;
  `engine/progress` notifications are coalesced per request; and past
  `QUEUE_FRAMES` (1,024) frames or `QUEUE_BYTES` (64 MiB) the reader kills
  the child at once, with no ask needed, and records why. The pending ask,
  or the next ask or `status`, fails `protocol` with that reason
  (`EngineFront::last_failure`, `queue_stats`, `ensure_started`,
  `child_exited` expose it). New test hook
  `ALSEM_ENGINE_TEST_HOOK=flood-after-open:<response|notify|progress|garbage>:<n>`.
  Tests: `engine_host::faults::a_flooding_child_is_ended_with_no_ask_waiting`
  (200,000 small frames while nothing reads: the queue peaks at exactly
  1,024 frames, the child is ended, `status` fails with the reason),
  `a_progress_flood_is_coalesced_and_the_child_lives`, and four unit tests
  in `engine::host::front::tests`. Discrimination: with the bound check
  disabled, the integration test times out with 200,000 frames (7.4 MB)
  queued and the two bound unit tests fail; with coalescing disabled, the
  progress tests fail (the child is killed at 1,025 frames); restored, all
  pass.

### Changed (the wire answer: outcome taxonomy and frame bounding)

- **`wire::Answer` is the closed schema of context-server design r5 §8.3.**
  `kind: "cli"` is a CLI outcome (the command ran, failed its planning, or its
  model did not build: a semantic build failure is the job's own text and
  exit); `kind: "failed"` is an infrastructure outcome with a
  `FailedOutcome` (`cancelled`, `deadline`, `budget`, `busy`, `engineError`,
  `refusedPath`, `notThisWorkspace`, `inputsUnstable`, `protocol`), a
  `message` of at most 4 KiB inline and the whole text in `diagnosticFile`
  (review r4 #11). A CLI answer's stderr is `stderr` lines xor `stderrFile`;
  `changedPaths`/`changedPathsTruncated` are in the schema (empty until
  freshness exists). `StdoutFile` is now `SpillFile` (alias kept).
- **`wire::bound_frame`** makes every answer fit one frame (r5 §3): over the
  limit it spills, in order, stdout to `stdoutFile`, stderr to `stderrFile`
  (exact bytes), cuts `changedPaths` to 256, and ends in a minimal terminal
  frame (`failed`, `protocol`, "answer exceeded the frame limit", the whole
  encoded answer in `diagnosticFile`); a failed spill ends in that frame with
  the write error. Recovery from a line `read_frame` refused discards its
  rest without holding it (since the NEW 4 fix: `Oversized::skip_rest`).

### Added (the engine child process: context-server stage 2 plumbing)

- **`alsem engine-host`** (hidden): the engine child a front end owns, speaking
  line-framed JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdin/stdout (`engine::host`): `engine/hello`
  first (protocol version, engine instance id, version, grammar sha, pid),
  then `session/open`, `session/ask`, `session/status`, `session/shutdown`.
  Each ask runs the one-shot job path a standalone `alsem <command>` runs and
  answers its exact bytes (`stdoutText`, or `stdoutFile` over the request's
  inline cap); no resident revision yet (`revision: null`). Order per r5 §4.3:
  decode (clap) → validate through the CLI's own `Planned::Failed | Ready`
  split with no workspace read bound (a planning failure answers its CLI text
  and exit and reads nothing) → acquire the workspace read (each package once,
  `M_before == M_consumed == M_after`, three attempts, then `inputsUnstable`)
  → run. A request for another workspace is `notThisWorkspace`; `--out` is
  `refusedPath` (the output sink is a later step). The child bounds its own
  response frame, refuses an id over 1 KiB, answers an oversized request line
  with a parse error after skipping it unheld, and moves fd 1 to its protocol
  stream with fd 1 pointed at stderr, so a stray print cannot break framing.
- **`engine::host::front::EngineFront`**: the front end's supervision. Hello
  within 10 s with a supported protocol, else kill; a child frame over 16 MiB
  is refused after reading the limit plus one byte, and a frame that does not
  parse kills the child (`protocol`); stderr drained continuously, the newest
  64 KiB kept; end of output or a failed write fails the ask with the exit
  status and stderr tail (`engineError`); restart on the next ask after a
  backoff of 1 s doubling to 30 s that resets only after a completed ask or
  60 s stable (never on a hello); three deaths in 60 s fail every ask for five
  minutes or until `reset`; `shutdown` waits 10 s, then kills; dropping it
  kills and reaps the child and removes its spill folder.
- **`alsem engine-ask -- <command line>`** (hidden): a front end of one ask as
  a process. It decodes the line, decides the diff root and `--changed` itself
  (the child probes nothing for them), reads a `--diff -` from its own stdin,
  and prints the answer's exact stdout and stderr with its exit code.
- **Test hooks** (`ALSEM_ENGINE_TEST_HOOK`: `no-hello`, `protocol:<n>`,
  `abort-on-ask`, `abort-on-ask-once:<marker>`, `oversized-frame-on-ask`,
  `garbage-frame-on-ask`), compiled into debug builds and, through the new
  `engine-test-hooks` feature, into an abort-on-panic build; never in a
  shipped one.
- Tests (`tests/cli/engine_host.rs`, `engine::host::child::tests`,
  `wire::tests`): explain/prove/digest/query through the child byte-identical
  to the CLI, inline and as `stdoutFile`; `engine-ask` equal to the CLI for a
  `--diff -` request and a clap error; planning failures keep their CLI
  outcomes with zero workspace reads; a broken workspace answers the job's own
  failure text; oversized and malformed child frames, a missing hello, an
  unknown protocol, a crash mid-request with respawn, repeated deaths with
  doubling backoff and the failed state; the child's own frame rules.
  Discrimination: reading the workspace before planning, trimming the inline
  stdout, an unbounded frame read, a backoff reset on hello, an ignored hello
  deadline and a child that does not skip an oversized line each fail their
  test.
- Measured on CDO (release-fast, `/usr/bin/time -v`, the peak includes the
  child): one `digest --routine IssueReminder --routine DocHandle --routine
  VendorLedgerSendToQueue --include-reads --deterministic` (22.7 MB of JSON,
  delivered as `stdoutFile`) through `engine-ask` → `engine-host`: 29.27 /
  29.44 s, 3.44 / 3.46 GB, against the CLI's 30.15 / 29.83 s, 3.43 / 3.43 GB
  in interleaved runs; `prove IssueReminder may-commit` 28.77 s against
  28.48 s. The process boundary, framing and spill are inside run-to-run noise;
  outputs are byte-identical to the CLI's.

### Changed (dependency packages are read once, into owned images)

- **Every product of a dependency `.app` is now built from one owned copy of
  its bytes** (context-server design r5 §5.2, review r4 #9). The loader used
  to open a package once per product: the manifest probe, the symbol read, the
  source-cache hash, the extraction, the graph build's ABI read, the
  cross-app model's symbol rows and the fingerprint row each opened the path
  again (`snapshot/cache.rs` hashed the path, then reopened it to extract), so
  a file rewritten in place between two opens gave products of two different
  byte images under one identity. `WorkspaceInputs::read` now acquires each
  package once (`app_image::AppImage`: one open, the whole file read and
  blake3-hashed from the buffer); `extract_app_metadata`, `extract_app_symbols`,
  `extract_app_package`, `extract_embedded_source`, `cached_source`,
  `open_app_image` and the ABI readers take the image, never a path. No
  read-only mapping of a user's `.app` is made (a mapping is not immutable).
- **The identity of a package is its bytes.** `AppFileStamp` gains `content`,
  the image's blake3, so the dependency tier, package and source caches
  (`program::dep_cache`) hit only for the same bytes, not for the same size
  and modification time.
- **Where the bytes live.** The graph build and the cross-app model read a
  package's symbols long after the loader, so an image lives as long as the
  snapshot. Held on the heap the images sat on top of the build's peak
  (CDO `prove IssueReminder may-commit`: +48 MB in a sampled run). An image of
  1 MiB or more therefore moves, once hashed, into a **sealed private copy**:
  an anonymous temp file (unlinked at creation on Unix), written once, read by
  positional reads (design r5 §5.2 allows exactly this). A temp-disk failure
  keeps the bytes in memory. The workspace read hands each image to the build
  that consumes it and keeps only its identity; a second build of the same
  read re-reads the file and accepts it only if the bytes are the same.
- **`M_consumed`.** `ClosureEntries::consumed` lists the identities a read
  acquired, and `app_image::check_consistent` compares them with stat-and-hash
  passes before and after (`M_before == M_consumed == M_after`, r5 §5.1). An
  in-place overwrite with B and restore to A during consumption reads A before
  and after but is refused, because the consumed hash is B's (T-acquire-inplace).
- Tests: `snapshot::tests::package_products_are_built_from_the_acquired_image`
  (an in-place rewrite and a deletion after the read: the build still sees the
  acquired bytes), `..::an_in_place_overwrite_and_restore_during_consumption_is_refused`,
  `..::a_second_build_of_one_read_gets_the_same_bytes_or_none`,
  `app_image::tests::*` (the private copy reads back exactly, by range and by
  two readers at once). Discrimination: an `open_app_image` that re-reads the
  path fails the first two; a check of before against after alone fails the
  in-place test; a second build that skips the hash check fails the third.
- Measured on CDO (`DO-cdo-baseline/Cloud`, release-fast, `/usr/bin/time -v`,
  interleaved runs): `prove IssueReminder may-commit` 28.08–28.58 s, peak
  3.44–3.46 GB (master `f009afc7`: 28.49–29.57 s, 3.43–3.47 GB); `digest
  --routine IssueReminder --routine DocHandle --routine VendorLedgerSendToQueue
  --include-reads --deterministic` (22.7 MB of JSON) 28.80–29.95 s, 3.44 GB
  (master: 28.53–30.03 s, 3.43–3.44 GB). Output byte-identical (prove apart
  from its `generatedAt`).

### Fixed (`Cu.Run(x)` reaches a declared procedure `Run`)

- **A typed-receiver `Run` call with an argument binds to the procedure the
  object declares, not to the built-in run.** The resolver sent every
  `Codeunit`/`Page`/`Report`/`XmlPort` variable call to `Run` (and `RunModal`,
  `Import`, `Export`) with zero or one argument to the object's entry trigger.
  When the object declares a procedure of that name, AL binds a call with
  arguments to it (probed with alc 18.1.43.24897: `procedure Run()` with no
  parameter is AL0440, so a call with no argument is always the built-in; once
  any `Run(…)` is declared, `Cu.Run(DateRec)` against `Run(var R: Record
  "Integer")` is AL0133 and `Cu.Run(IntRec)` against `Run(A; C: Integer)` is
  AL0135 — the built-in is never a fallback; a `pageextension`'s `Run(G: Guid)`
  counts for `PageVar.Run(G)`). For a codeunit with no `OnRun` the old route
  was an empty run, classified `honestEmpty` ("provably no callee"), so
  `alsem prove … may-commit` answered `no` for a routine whose callee commits;
  with an `OnRun` the edge went to the wrong routine. Microsoft's System
  Application declares such procedures (`"Azure AD User Mgmt.
  Impl.".Run(ForUserSecurityId: Guid)`). `resolver::declares_entry_method_overload`
  now sends such a call to the general dispatch.
- This was first reported as a cross-app demand gap (workspace → dependency
  `Start` → dependency `Helper.Run`, missing from the model). It is not: the
  demand closure is transitive, and the same chain with the routine named
  `DoWork` resolves and proves `yes`. The probe's `procedure Run()` had no
  parameter, which alc rejects (AL0440); the engine's built-in reading of that
  call was right. `tests/cli/cli_typed_run_declared_procedure.rs` pins the use
  (prove and the dependency-body histogram, with the dependency as a source
  folder and as a source `.app`, single-app, a page extension, and the
  no-argument call staying on `OnRun`).
- CDO (`DO-cdo-baseline/Cloud`, master `212e5f82` vs this fix): unchanged.
  `--program-call-graph-stats` is byte-identical (wholeProgram 46328 edges:
  resolvedSource 11639, resolvedCatalog 6151, conditionalResolved 266,
  honestDynamic 16, honestEmpty 28256, unknown 0; primaryScoped 20916:
  resolvedSource 9530, resolvedCatalog 6151, honestDynamic 16, honestEmpty
  5219, unknown 0), `--dependency-bodies-stats` is byte-identical (431321
  sites, honestEmpty 125067, unknown 0), and the `alsem graph` export of the
  cross-app model is byte-identical (110202 lines), so no demanded dependency
  routine changes. No CDO call site has the shape: the System Application
  procedures above are not called with one argument in source the build reads.

### Changed (routine ids no longer depend on the file list)

- **Internal routine ids are scoped per app** (context-server design r3 §6.7).
  An internal id is still `{prefix}/{64 lowercase hex}`, but the prefix is now
  the routine's own app scope, `ids::routine_app_scope(app_guid)` = the first
  16 lowercase hex of sha256 over the lowercase app guid, instead of the
  workspace `modelInstanceId`, which hashes the sorted `.al` file list. Adding,
  removing or renaming an `.al` file no longer changes every id of every app in
  the model; the same routine has the same id in every model holding its app.
  The 64-hex hash part is unchanged. Uniqueness across apps does not rest on the
  prefix: the app guid is the first hashed key part, and the loader keys apps by
  guid. The `model_instance_id` parameter is gone from `encode_routine_id`,
  `compute_routine_id`, `project_abi_to_index`, the model assembly entries
  (`assemble_and_resolve_*`, `build_cross_app_base*`, `project_r3a5_cross_app`,
  `project_r4_findings_cross_app`) and the L2 single-routine analyzers;
  `MODEL_INSTANCE_ID_DEFAULT` and `R3A4_MODEL_INSTANCE_ID` are removed.
- **Consumer audit** (every reader of the id shape or of `modelInstanceId`):
  - finding fingerprints (`l5::fingerprint`): swap every internal id for its
    stable id before hashing, scanning `{prefix}/{64 hex}` for each distinct
    prefix. A cross-app model now carries one prefix per app; all are 16 hex, so
    at most one id matches at any position. Unchanged code; the scan oracle test
    gained a two-scope map, and `fingerprint_index_substitutes_ids_of_two_app_scopes`
    pins the production `build`. No fingerprint moved (below).
  - `stable_sub_id` (`l4::summary`, `capability_cone`, `combined_graph`,
    `r3a4_projection`, `program::model::coverage`): split at the second (or
    last) `/`. Unchanged: the scope never holds a `/`.
  - `modelInstanceId` itself stays a workspace input. It is still the commands'
    presence check (no root `app.json` `id` → `NoModelInstanceId`, as before)
    and part of the L4 host key (`engine::incremental`'s `host_global`), so a
    file-list change still invalidates the retained L4 host: the one consumer
    that relied on the id changing with the file list keeps its own key.
  - outputs that print internal ids, or 16-hex ids hashed over them (snapshot
    `edgeId`, digest `factId` and occurrence ids, the policy SARIF message text
    `on routine <id>`): moved once, regenerated. These were already per-run
    handles that changed with every file add.
  - `--baseline` files, SARIF `fingerprints`, stable routine ids and stable
    sub-ids: unchanged.
  - caches: the snapshot source cache holds `.app` text only, the dependency
    cache constants have no on-disk reader, the LSP reads no model ids. CDO
    provenance stamps (git state, dependency closure) are inputs, untouched.
- **Proof.** `tests/ids-parent-baseline/record.json` was minted from the parent
  engine (004f0ee4) over 229 fixture apps: 472 SARIF fingerprints, 1531 stable
  ids and stable sub-ids from analyze `--with-evidence` and digest output, and
  148 `--update-baseline` files. After the change the fingerprints and stable
  ids are equal and every parent-minted baseline still suppresses every finding
  (`tests/cli/ids_parent_baseline.rs`; `REGEN_TEMP_GOLDENS` never rewrites the
  record). `tests/cli/ids_file_list_independence.rs`: ids survive adding,
  removing and renaming an unrelated file (while `modelInstanceId` moves each
  time), and two apps declaring the same `codeunit 50100 Helper` with the same
  `Run()` get distinct ids under their own scopes. Discrimination: a `/` in the
  scope fails the parent-baseline test (124 fixtures' fingerprints moved and the
  parent baselines stopped suppressing); a guid-blind scope fails both id tests;
  the file-list hash mixed back into the id fails the stability test; collecting
  one prefix only fails the two-scope fingerprint test and 3 fixtures of the
  record. The 684 regenerated or re-minted goldens differ from the parent's only
  in internal ids and in 16-hex ids hashed over them (a one-to-one remap per
  file), or in key order (3 `r3a3` goldens); the 6 hand-edited vector files
  (`r0`, `r1a`, `r1d`, `r2-5a` ×2, `r3a3`) swap the old prefix for the app scope
  and drop the `modelInstanceId` inputs. No gate SARIF, `r0`, `r2c`, `r2d`, `r3a1`,
  `r3a2`, `r3a4`, `l4-summary-baseline` or semantic-edges golden moved.
- **CDO** (the pinned `bc3ccb18` baseline). The two frozen L4 digests
  (`tests/l4-summary-baseline/cdo-*-digest.txt`) moved and are re-pinned: with
  the scope temporarily forced back to the old `"r0"` prefix, both tests
  reproduce the old digests byte for byte (README re-freeze log). A
  `--baseline` file minted with the parent binary (2233 fingerprints, 2240
  findings) suppresses every finding of the new binary, and both runs give the
  same multiset of `(ruleId, fingerprint)`. The CDO SARIF is not byte-identical:
  6 d43/d44 messages print internal ids, and 12 d44 results list the same
  code-flow locations in another order. That order follows internal ids, and a
  cross-app model now has one prefix per app instead of one shared prefix. CDO
  provenance stamps are untouched.

### Changed (context-server stage 1: phase split)

- **`View::prepare` is a sequence of phase functions.** `relation_of`,
  `compose_cone` (the one composition), `emit_raw` (a raw-only scoped
  composition for subjects a retained composition did not emit), `tree_apps`,
  `tree_groups`, `read_tree` and `run_once` (`engine::session`) are called by the
  one-shot view with its drain-and-release discipline unchanged, and by a
  borrowed path that keeps what it fills (context-server design r3 §4.2; the
  resident revision is stage 2). The det harvest is split out of
  `build_detector_artifacts`: `harvest_detector_artifacts` takes
  `CapsInput::Owned | Borrowed` (owned moves each routine's direct facts and
  coverage, borrowed clones them) and `L4Input::None | Solve | Solved` (the
  one-shot solve still runs inside the harvest, after the payloads moved and
  the pd arena dropped, so its peak never holds them; `Solved` lends a retained
  solve with `CoreInput::Owned | Borrowed`). `ConeDerivedStore`
  (`CapabilityAnalysis::derived`, `DetectorArtifacts::cone_derived`), the
  cross-app base's `dependency_calls`, the view's `l4` and `det` cells and the
  incremental host's `CoreSummaries` are behind `Arc`. No CLI output moves.
- **Cost of the one-shot path, measured.** A digest `prepare` on ws-d37
  allocates exactly three blocks more than before (the det, l4 and derived
  `Arc`s: 5,984 → 5,987 allocations, +2,128 bytes = the three `ArcInner` sizes)
  and copies no payload. CDO cross-app (`DO-cdo-baseline/Cloud`, release-fast,
  `/usr/bin/time -v`, a shared machine): analyze, explain `--routine
  IssueReminder`, prove `IssueReminder may-commit` and digest `--routine
  IssueReminder` print byte-identical stdout before and after; peak RSS is
  unchanged within noise (3.41–3.49 GB both); wall times overlap once the
  machine's load is low (explain 34.1/34.6 s base, 34.1/41.0 s after).
- **New measurement spans** (design r4 §12 stage 1, r3 §14):
  `attach.settle_dead_marks`, `attach.settle_rules`, `attach.event_param_temps`,
  `l3.finish_resolved`, `pd.solve`, `resolve.close_holder_sites`,
  `deps.layer_consume`, `deps.extract` (on the parsed-tree path) and the counter
  `deps.extract_cpu_ns` (inside the build-time parallel parse, where no
  wall-clock span can hold the extraction alone). On CDO (cross-app explain,
  load ≈ 20): `pd.solve` 3.7–4.2 s of a 6.3–9.0 s composition,
  `attach.event_param_temps` 1.2–1.4 s, `l3.finish_resolved` 0.30–0.40 s,
  `deps.layer_consume` 0.21–0.42 s, `attach.settle_dead_marks` 0.013 s,
  `attach.settle_rules` 0.010 s (0 without rules), `resolve.close_holder_sites`
  under 1 ms, extraction 0.36–0.43 s CPU.
- **Tests** (`engine::session::phase_tests`): mixed-order sequences over one
  prepared state (query→digest, digest→query, explain→prove, prove→explain;
  ws-d37 single-app, rule B cross-app) answer byte-equal to cold standalone
  runs, composing and solving once; the det cell is evicted and refilled twice
  from the retained `CoreSummaries`; a seeded L4 solve after a digest seeds
  every SCC from the retained core and equals a cold solve; a dependency root
  borrows a scoped emission; the owned harvest arm copies no payload (a
  thread-gated counting allocator for the lib tests, `src/test_alloc.rs`: the
  lent harvest allocates at least the measured payload clone more, in bytes and
  count, and the derived `Arc` is moved, not re-wrapped). Discrimination
  proofs, each run and seen to fail, then reverted: the lent arm handing an
  empty derived store → digest on `DepWriteThenCommit` differs; the served
  trees lent an empty pd arena → digest differs; draining the retained core
  into the harvest → the refill's parameter roles vanish and the seeded solve
  panics ("no baseline core summary"); no scoped emission for the dependency
  root → its effects differ; cloning `direct_full` in the owned arm → owned
  bytes 35,773 → 48,498, below the payload margin.

### Changed (context-server stage 0: request-scoped planning)

- **Planning reads no process state.** The `alsem` binary's three planning
  globals (the `STDIN` `OnceLock`, `PLAN_FILES`, `PLAN_TOUCHED`) are gone. A
  request's planning context `engine::batch::plan_cx::PlanCx` holds its
  touched paths, its diff-root decision (`diff_root_decided`) and, when the
  caller has one, the workspace read its job uses (`inputs`); `PlanReads` holds
  what the requests of one run share (the one stdin read, each file read once).
  Every file-system question goes through a `PlanFs` (`ProcessFs` for the CLI).
  The order is the one of context-server design r3 §4.3: decode the argv (clap),
  decide the request's file-system questions in the caller (`decide`: the diff
  root via `decide_diff_root`, `digest --changed`), build the `PlanCx`, then plan
  (`plan`, the design's `make_job`), which probes nothing. The `#[arg(skip)]`
  `diff_root_decided` fields left `DigestCli`/`ExplainCli`; a batch worker's
  shipped decisions go through the same `decide`. A request given a workspace
  read (`PlanCx::inputs`, served by `WorkspaceReader::give`) reads no workspace
  itself; an argv naming another workspace, or needing more than the read holds
  (`WorkspaceInputs::holds`), is refused with exit 3. New
  `engine::batch::standalone_output` returns a job's writes without replaying
  them. No CLI output moves. Tests (bin `alsem`): two sequential `--diff -`
  requests answer their own bytes, each equal to the same diff read from a file;
  a request with no diff text fails `--diff -` with exit 3 and never reads the
  process's stdin (`PROCESS_STDIN_READS`); two threads planning requests of one
  run keep their own touched paths; the diff-root probes are asked of the
  request's file system; planning over a file system that panics on every
  question succeeds; a given workspace read answers after the disk changed, and
  another workspace or a larger need is refused. Discrimination proofs, each
  run and seen to fail, then reverted: a process-global `OnceLock` in
  `stdin_text` → "two diffs, two answers" fails; `PlanReads::request(None)`
  leaving stdin unset → exit 0 instead of 3; one shared touched list → the
  concurrent test fails 3 of 3 runs; `std::fs::canonicalize` back in
  `decide_diff_root` → `Workspace` instead of `GitTop("apps/ws")`;
  `plan_explain` deciding its own diff root → "planning canonicalized" panic;
  `reader_for` ignoring `inputs` → exit 2 instead of 0.

### Added (context-server stage 0: `explain --routine` repeatable; spans)

- **`alsem explain --routine` may be given more than once** (context-server
  design r3 §6.12; review r1 #16). Each selector resolves alone as one
  `--routine` always did (prove's code and `routine-not-found` /
  `routine-ambiguous` wording); one tree serves every routine; the cards are
  the union, sorted by anchor, each routine once (a selector given twice is one
  selector; a name and its stable id give one card); the diagnostics are per
  selector in input order; exit 0 when any card, 2 when none (mixed → 0 with
  the diagnostics). One distinct selector writes the single-routine document
  byte for byte as before (`"selector"`; every existing golden unchanged); two
  or more write `"selectors": [..]` in its place, the rest of the document as
  `--diff` writes it. Human mode: the cards, then the diagnostics. `--help`
  states it. Tests (`cli_explain_differential`): two selectors give the single
  runs' cards in anchor order, JSON and human; a repeated selector writes the
  single run's bytes in both formats, a name plus its stable id one card; mixed
  found/unknown/ambiguous → exit 0, one card, both diagnostics in order; none
  found → exit 2. Discrimination proofs, run and seen to fail, then reverted:
  rendering without collapsing repeated selectors → "a repeated selector is the
  single document" fails; exit 2 whenever any selector is unmatched → the mixed
  case's exit 0 fails.
- **Spans** for prove's post-root work (r3 §13 item 6): `prove.literal_reach`,
  `prove.group_paths`, `prove.reach_effects`, and `digest.unresolved_cones`,
  `digest.coverage_graph`; for explain's render: `explain.indexes` (the
  `Indexes` and `CrossRules` builds), `explain.reaching_tests`, `explain.cards`.
- **Measured on CDO** (`DO-cdo-baseline/Cloud` `bc3ccb18`, cross-app,
  release-fast, `/usr/bin/time -v`, shared 22-core machine), ten routines
  (`IssueReminder`, `DocHandle`, `VendorLedgerSendToQueue`,
  `BackgroundPdfWithFP`, `PurchaseHeaderGetLogInfo`, `ComputeAffectedCount`,
  `GetPayload`, `SetInfo`, `SendToQueue`, `FindFirstViableOutputProfileCode`):
  ten separate runs of the parent binary 243.3 s in total (22.7–28.1 s each,
  peak 3.43–3.48 GB); ONE multi-root call 27.06 s, peak 3.47 GB; a batch of the
  ten single-routine jobs 60.70 s before (ten `snapshot.derive`, 19.2 s) and
  34.74 s after (one derive, 2.5 s; one coverage graph), peak 3.47 → 3.44 GB.
  The multi-root call's per-request work past the composition: derive 2.55 s
  + roots 3.26 s + unresolved cones 0.35 s + coverage graph 0.10 s + render
  0.78 s ≈ 7.0 s, inside the design's 7–8 s hypothesis (one tree ~2.1 s +
  slowest root ≤ 4.2 s); the composition (5.5 s) and model (≈14 s) are per
  view. Equality: the multi-root document's ten cards equal the ten separate
  runs' cards, and every job's stdout of both batches equals its separate run
  byte for byte. In the new batch each job still pays its own
  `explain.indexes` (10 × 0.8 s).
- **Card render is not parallelized** (a deviation from r3 §6.12's "renders in
  parallel", measured): on CDO cross-app, 9 cards cost `explain.cards` 28.6 ms
  in total, while the per-job `explain.indexes` (one `Indexes::new` plus one
  `CrossRules::new`) cost 792 ms. The "≈0.85 s per card" the design read from
  the spec's traces is that per-job build, paid once per explain job, not per
  card; a multi-root explain pays it once. `CrossRules` also carries a run-wide
  expansion budget and memo shared by the cards, so a parallel render would
  need per-card walk state for no measurable gain.

### Changed (context-server stage 0: one tree for grouped explain; pure tree reads)

- **Consecutive `explain` jobs on one view share ONE tree and ONE test-coverage
  graph** (context-server design r3 §6.12). G16's grouping in `View::prepare`
  excluded every reader with `tests` (every explain, and `digest --tests`);
  `tests` is now a read parameter: readers group when their flags are equal,
  and `digest_effects_each` builds the `CoverageGraph` once per tree and hands
  every reader an `Arc` (`DigestEffects::coverage_graph:
  Option<Arc<CoverageGraph>>`). The graph reads only the tree's whole-program
  sections, so it is the same over any subject set; every job's bytes equal its
  standalone run. New trace counter `build.coverage_graph`.
- **A tree read never mutates the tree** (r3 §13 item 3). `digest_effects_each`
  takes `&CapabilitySnapshot` and a `BoundaryMode` (`On`: the tree's rule B,
  a dependency root still read with it off as G31 says; `Off`: none), threaded
  as a parameter to the fingerprint indexes (`compute_digest_effects_cli_in`)
  instead of taking and restoring `tree.boundary`. `CapabilitySnapshot::coverage`
  and `::identities` are `Arc` fields handed out as `Arc` clones instead of
  `std::mem::take` (the inventory read, which owns its tree, edits them through
  `Arc::make_mut` on a unique `Arc`: no copy). No CLI output moves.
- Tests: `cli_batch_plan::batch_explain_jobs_share_one_tree` (five explain jobs:
  two routines, one named by two jobs, a test routine, a `--diff`, both formats
  → `build.snapshot` 1 and `build.coverage_graph` 1, each job equal to its
  standalone run); `tests_rule_b::a_tree_read_is_a_pure_read` (two reads of one
  tree answer the same and share its coverage and identities by pointer; an
  `Off` read gives the cut's per-resource effect and leaves the tree's rule).
  Discrimination proofs, run and seen to fail, then reverted: the old predicate
  (`!a.tests && !b.tests`) → counters (5, 5); `BoundaryMode::Off` answering the
  tree's rule → the grouped effect instead of `DB_MODIFY - Customer`; copying
  the coverage instead of an `Arc` clone → the pointer check fails.

### Added (context-server stage 0: the wire codec and the output sink)

- **`al_sem::wire`, the exact-output codec** (context-server design r3 §3.2,
  §4.3, §13 item 2; a library, no process yet). NDJSON frames (compact JSON,
  one line, at most 16 MiB: `encode_frame`, `decode_frame`, `read_frame`). An
  answer (`Answer`) is `kind: "cli"` (exit code, stdout, stderr lines) or
  `kind: "failed"`, with `revision` always present and `null` allowed. A CLI's
  stdout travels as `stdoutText` — a JSON string whose value is the stdout byte
  for byte, embedded and trailing newlines included — **xor** `stdoutFile`
  (path, length, SHA-256) when it is not UTF-8, over the request's inline cap
  (`clamp_inline`: default 64 KiB, at most 4 MiB), or too large once escaped
  for one frame; a frame with both or neither is refused on decode. Tests: the
  exact bytes of a pretty document round-trip and the frame is one line;
  three frames read back by real line framing; the xor rule; over-cap,
  non-UTF-8 and escape-heavy (control characters) stdout go to a file with
  their exact bytes and hash; frame limits on both sides. Discrimination
  proofs, run and seen to fail, then reverted: trimming the stdout's trailing
  newline → "exact bytes" fails; dropping the escaped-length check → the
  control-character stdout is inlined and the file test fails; pretty-printed
  frames → both framing tests fail (the encoder's own one-newline assertion).
- **`output::Sink`**: `replay_on` writes through a sink (r3 §10, §13 item 4),
  and the first failed write's `al-sem: write error:` line goes through the sink
  too. `Streams` is the CLI's and a batch job's (real streams or the job's two
  files, the file system, the error line on the process's stderr, as before);
  `Captured` keeps everything in memory, the error line in its stderr. Test:
  a failed file write's line is captured and the later writes are not made.
  Discrimination proof: calling `write_error` directly instead of the sink →
  the captured stderr lacks the line, the test fails; reverted.

### Added (`aldump --snapshot-memory`)

- **`aldump --snapshot-memory <workspace> [--single-app] [--hash]` re-measures
  the cone-memory targets**, replacing the throwaway probe the cone-memory work
  used (the spec's planned `tools/cone-probe`). It builds the model a default
  `analyze` builds (cross-app by default; `AssemblyNeeds::BASE`), times the cone
  base and `compose_snapshot_from_base`, and prints JSON: per-phase wall time and
  `VmRSS`/`VmHWM`, census marks, the counts (inherited/direct facts, the
  inherited and snapshot rep/hop tables, snapshot rows, the pd arena) and row
  sizes. `--hash` adds BLAKE3 per serialized snapshot section, of the whole
  document and of the pd arena. Live heap is left to `tools/census-probe`: a
  counting allocator would have been the global allocator of every `aldump` run.
