  New public accessor `SnapshotCapabilityFact::table_lens`. Measured on CDO
  (`bc3ccb18`, release-fast): cross-app peak RSS 5.29 GB (the step-2 probe:
  5.28 GB), document BLAKE3 `3b480fbf…2ddaf` and pd arena `76fd29ac…8c98`, both
  equal to the step-2 probe's; single-app 0.82 GB. Command and reference values:
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-31-cone-memory-design.md` §13. Tests:
  `tests/cli/cli_snapshot_memory.rs` (the JSON shape, rows = inherited + direct,
  `--hash` equal across two processes).

### Changed (docs: a run's lifecycle is may-run)

- **`resolver::run_triggers` now says its trigger set is may-run, and why
  `OnNewRecord` is in it.** The 2026-10-28 entry below described the set as the
  triggers a run reaches "with no user acting on a control". That holds for
  `OnNewRecord` only sometimes: it runs when a new record is initialized, which
  a run does by itself when an insertable card, document or worksheet opens on an
  empty set (Base App journals rely on it for `SetUpNewLine`), and otherwise on
  the user's New. It stays in the set: other members already depend on the data
  (`OnAfterGetRecord` needs a record), leaving it out would let `prove` say `no`
  about a write in it, and `alsem graph`'s lifecycle rule and d39 already treat
  it as a page trigger. On CDO it accounts for 9 of the 409 object-run audit
  pairs. Doc comment only; no behaviour change.

### Removed (cone-memory step 3, the frozen emission oracle)

- **The T3(b) frozen-emission oracle is deleted, as the design's step 3
  plans, now that the CDO comparisons for steps 1 and 2 are recorded** (the
  snapshot document and pd-arena hashes and the byte-equal command outputs
  under steps 1 and 2 above). Gone from `capability_cone`: the test-only hook
  in `compose_inherited_cones` that ran a verbatim copy of the pre-step-1
  selection (`inherited_facts_for_singleton`, `inherited_facts_by_bfs`,
  `emit_picks`, `candidate_wins`, the string-key sort) beside the production
  emission, its stats, `t3_raw_equals_the_frozen_emission_on_fixtures` and
  `t3_oracle_audit_names_only_frozen_code`. Kept: the frozen `retag` (T1's
  oracle, `legacy_raw_oracle::frozen::retag`); T7 (i)'s guarded-entry
  precondition now reads the production raw (N's `G(false)` gets nothing).
  Raw equality stays pinned by the byte-compared r3a3/r3a5/r4f goldens, the
  snapshot corpus test (T3(c)) and T3b. The step-3 census rewrite is in step 2
  (`snapshot.capability_facts`) and step 1 (`witness.raw_bytes`);
  `cone_census::facts_tally` reads only owned direct facts and fixture-supplied
  inherited ones, so it needed no change.

### Changed (16-byte capability snapshot rows, cone-memory step 2)

- **A row of `CapabilitySnapshot::capability_facts` is a 16-byte handle into
  shared tables, not an owned copy of the fact; every output is
  byte-identical.** Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-31-cone-memory-design.md`
  revision 2, step 2 (§4.3). `SnapshotCapabilityFact` is now `{ Arc<SnapTables>,
  rep: u32, hop: u32 }` (a `const` assert pins 16 bytes); `hop == NO_HOP` marks a
  direct row. `SnapTables` holds the stable subjects (one per emission group,
  interned), one `SnapRep` per direct fact and per distinct raw rep (projected
  once, memoised by raw index) and one `SnapHop` per raw first hop. The subject
  contract: every row's subject comes from its emission group; a hop row takes
  the subject of the group that projects it (debug builds check the raw hop's
  own subject maps to it), and a second group emitting the same raw hop is a bug
  (asserted). Readers call accessors (`subject()`, `op()`, ... `extra()`,
  `fields()`) that borrow from the handle's tables; `Vec<&Fact>`, indexing,
  `clone()` (one refcount bump), `retain` and the table-order scans are
  unchanged. The rows are written in output order into one exact-size Vec
  (sequentially: every row clones the one table `Arc`) and each subject's slice
  is sorted as in step 0. Migrated: digest (and prove/fingerprint through it),
  `fingerprint_query`, the CBOR fact serializer, `key_classes::retain`,
  `ordering_engine`'s last-wins HTTP scan, `literal_reach` (borrowed strings
  straight from the accessors), `derive_pd_arena`, `ordering_kept_roots`.
  `SnapshotFactFields` is the old owned layout: hand-built rows convert from it
  with `.into()` (a one-row private table), and mutation-style tests edit
  `fields()` and convert back, never touching shared tables. The
  `snapshot.capability_facts` census bucket now counts the rows plus each table
  set once (it counted only the row buffer before: 456 B per row).
- Measured on the pinned CDO baseline (`bc3ccb18`, Linux, 22 cores, 93 GB,
  `release-fast`, `/usr/bin/time -v`; before = step 1 `bf2de5ad`): the
  full-model cross-app `compose_snapshot` probe peak RSS **20.4 GB -> 5.28 GB**
  (target <= 6 GB), live-heap peak 16.1 GiB -> **3.41 GiB** (target <= 4.5 GiB),
  `snapshot.capability_facts` 13.0 GiB -> 342 MiB for 17,057,037 rows (21 B per
  row with the tables), compose phase 17.6 s -> 7.7 s, whole probe 72 s -> 67 s;
  single-app probe 0.80 GB -> 0.78 GB (target <= 0.95 GB). Commands, before ->
  after: cross-app `alsem policy check` 3.44 GB -> 3.44 GB (33.6 s -> 29.3 s; the
  ordinary policy reads raw facts, not snapshot rows), single-app 0.77 -> 0.77
  GB; `alsem analyze --preset transaction-integrity` cross-app 6.46 / 5.39 GB ->
  5.85 / 6.39 GB (two runs each, 56-58 s both; the production cut builds few
  rows), single-app 4.44 / 4.32 GB -> 3.99 / 5.24 GB. That RSS spread is the
  allocator's, so the live heap was measured too (a scratch `alsem` build whose
  global allocator counts the bytes requested from mimalloc; not committed):
  analyze single-app peak live heap 4.17 GB -> **3.10 GB**, cross-app 5.20 GB ->
  **4.64 GB**, outputs byte-equal.
- Equality: no golden regenerated; `scripts/check-goldens` green. On CDO the
  full-model snapshot document hashes as in steps 0 and 1 (BLAKE3
  `3b480fbf53066d4d071422ee4b9390f768da655687600860937e95c2c2a2ddaf`,
  9,463,055,195 bytes) and so does the pd arena (`76fd29ac…c98`, 2,822,661
  states). Byte-equal (`cmp`, `--deterministic`) with step 1's recorded outputs:
  `policy check` cross-app and `--single-app` with the bundled policy and with
  the inherited-facts policy (cross-app output 8,059,019,869 bytes), `analyze
  --preset transaction-integrity` both modes (two runs each), `digest` over three
  files and the two `prove` questions, cross-app; the bundled-policy and analyze
  runs also against fresh `bf2de5ad` runs.
- Tests (each break made with Edit, run, reverted with Edit, run green):
  `snapshot::cone_memory_step2_tests` T0 (16 bytes; direct rows report
  `NO_HOP`, inherited rows a hop; a stated row is direct-form: direct rows built
  with hop 0 -> fails), T1 on snapshot rows (a rep with its own call site and
  stale first-hop ids through a call, a trigger and an event hop, plus a direct
  fact, against the old owned rows from the materialized facts, fields and
  serialized JSON: `witness_callsite_id()` returning the rep's on an inherited
  row -> fails, and T3(c) on 190 corpus models; `provenance()` returning the
  rep's -> fails, T3(c) on 204), T7 (i) one rep row per raw rep (a rep per row ->
  3 rep rows, fails; every output test stays green), T7 (ii) identical hop
  content of two subjects, now observable in the rows (interning raw hops
  without the subject -> step 1's subject-contract assertion fires; with it
  disabled, the snapshot's "raw first hop's subject is not its emitting
  group's" assertion fires; with that and the shared-hop assertion disabled too,
  B's row reads subject `a#` and the row-subject assertion fails), row edits
  never touch shared tables. T3(c) (`step0_sort_tests::t6_every_corpus_app_*`,
  every `tests/r0-corpus` and `tests/fixtures` app, single-app and cross-app):
  the handle table equals the old owned rows built from the materialized raw,
  field by field and as serialized JSON, and gives the same pd-arena producer
  indexes and digest `facts_by_routine` buckets (`via()` returning the rep's ->
  fails on 204 models). T6 still discriminates on the handle rows
  (`sort_unstable_by` in the slice sort -> `t6_split_*` fails). T5, new test
  crate `tests/cone_memory_bound.rs` with a counting global allocator: 400
  callers of one shared routine writing 40 tables (48,000 inherited facts) cost
  13.0 B per raw inherited fact (bound 16) and 22.4 B per snapshot row (bound
  32), measured as what dropping each frees; breaks: a raw rep interned per fact
  as its own owned copy -> 723 B/fact, fails; a snapshot rep row per row -> 845
  B/row, fails.

### Changed (compact inherited facts in the cone, cone-memory step 1)

- **The cone stores each inherited capability fact as an 8-byte ref into shared
  tables, not as an owned copy; every output is byte-identical.** Design:
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-31-cone-memory-design.md` revision 2, step 1. New
  `engine::l4::inherited_facts`: `InheritedRef { rep: u32, hop: u32 }` indexes
  `InheritedTables` (reps interned by `Arc` identity, the table holding a strong
  `Arc` per entry; first hops interned by content `(subject, via, callsite,
  operation_id, event_id)`, `None` kept apart from `Some("")`; indexes are checked
  `u32` and never `NO_HOP = u32::MAX`). `InheritedFacts` keeps one entry per composed
  subject, empty ones included (missing and empty stay different); drains move owned
  keys and clone the tables' `Arc`. Readers see a fact through the borrowed
  `InheritedFactRef` / `FactRef` (direct or inherited), whose accessors restate
  `retag`'s rules; `materialize()` is the one owned builder (the old `retag`).
  `dedup_direct` mints each direct rep's `Arc` once, and the selection walks carry
  `&Arc` reps; the selection itself is unchanged (singleton min-distance through
  `candidate_wins`, recursive first-seen BFS, producer entries replacing a pick in
  place). Readers moved to the borrowed view: `View::raw`, `TreeRaw::{Drain,
  Borrow}`, `SubjectRaw`, policy (`FieldEvalContext.fact: Option<FactRef>`, the fact
  sort, `emit_match_finding`; nothing in policy materializes), the snapshot's
  capability rows and both evidence indexes, `derive_permissions` /
  `make_required_perm`, the `witness.raw_bytes` census (now refs + tables: on CDO
  cross-app policy 6,966,269,866 -> 90,300,386 bytes); `project_r3a3` /
  `project_r3a5_from_parts` materialize per subject. The snapshot row type is
  unchanged (that is step 2); its rows are built from the accessors, not from a
  materialized fact.
- Measured on the pinned CDO baseline (`bc3ccb18`, Linux, 22 cores, 93 GB,
  `release-fast`, `/usr/bin/time -v`, quiet machine; before = step 0 `cb280c58`):
  cross-app `alsem policy check` (bundled policy) peak RSS **9.49 GB -> 3.44 GB**
  (target <= 3.5 GB; 32 s -> 30 s); single-app policy 0.78 GB -> 0.78 GB; `alsem
  analyze --preset transaction-integrity` cross-app 6.01 / 5.92 GB -> 5.30 / 5.58 GB
  (two runs each, no regression), single-app 4.01-4.46 GB -> 4.18-4.62 GB over four
  runs each (glibc noise; this path builds no raw). The full-model
  `compose_snapshot` probe: peak RSS 33.4 GB -> 20.4 GB, the base phase's retained
  heap 12.70 GiB -> 1.29 GiB (17,017,608 inherited facts: raw freed 163 MiB, about
  10 B per fact with the tables: 27,477 reps, 38,081 hops, 33,285 subjects, exactly
  the design's census); the snapshot rows (13.3 GiB) are step 2's. Single-app probe
  0.80 GB (target <= 0.95 GB).
- Equality proofs: no golden regenerated, `scripts/check-goldens` green (forced
  run). On CDO the full-model snapshot document hashes the same as step 0 (BLAKE3
  `3b480fbf53066d4d071422ee4b9390f768da655687600860937e95c2c2a2ddaf`, 9,463,055,195
  bytes), and so does the pd arena (`76fd29ac…c98`, 2,822,661 states). Byte-equal
  (`cmp`) before/after with `--deterministic`: `policy check` cross-app and
  `--single-app` with the bundled policy and with a policy whose four rules read
  inherited facts (cross-app output 8,059,019,869 bytes, 9,261 findings, 9,014,611
  evidence steps), `analyze --preset transaction-integrity` both modes, `digest`
  over three files, and two `prove` questions, all cross-app.
- Tests (each break made with Edit, run, reverted with Edit, run green):
  `capability_cone::cone_memory_step1_tests` T0 (index sentinel: drop the `NO_HOP`
  assert -> fails), T1 (`materialize` = the frozen `retag` over call / trigger /
  event hops with a rep carrying stale first-hop ids and its own call site;
  accessors = `materialize`: keep the rep's first-hop op in `materialize` -> fails;
  `witness_callsite_id()` returns the rep's -> fails, and T4a in both T4 tests),
  T3(b) (every `tests/r0-corpus` and `tests/fixtures` app, single-app and cross-app
  FULL model, plus one literal model for the producer-replacement class the fixtures
  lack: 543 models, 2,927 subjects, 1,118 facts compared field by field with a
  frozen `legacy_raw_oracle` that carries its own `candidate_wins`, `retag` and
  string-key sort, audited by a grep test; production `candidate_wins` preferring
  the larger distance -> 4 models fail; emitting the previous pick's hop -> 12
  models fail; content interning without the subject -> 2; `None` call site
  interned as `Some("")` -> 92), T3b (first-seen pick kept at distance 3 over a
  later distance-2 candidate: compare on distance -> fails, while T3(b) stays green
  on the fixtures; producer replacement keeps the pick's slot: push instead -> fails),
  T7 (one rep across subjects and a guarded/unguarded entry; identical hop content of
  two subjects -> two hops: intern without the subject -> the subject-contract
  assertion fires; one call site with two targets -> one hop: intern by edge
  address -> fails, T3(b) green; `None` vs `Some("")` -> two hops: merge them ->
  fails); T4 (`snapshot_full::cone_memory_t4_tests` and policy's
  `t4_policy_evidence_carries_the_first_hop_witnesses`: call / trigger / event hop
  witnesses in the snapshot row, the permission row and the finding evidence;
  first-hop op or event accessor returning the rep's -> fails); T8
  (`inherited_facts::tests`, `step6_tree_tests::t8_*`, policy's `t8_*`: drains and
  borrows keep empty entries, share the tables, subjects borrow from the tables, an
  empty subject keeps its pd states in a tree; drop empty entries at emission ->
  policy's "summary but no raw inherited facts" panic fires and the tree loses the
  subject's pd states). T5 (a counting-allocator test crate) is not added in this
  step; the probe numbers above stand in for it.

### Changed (capability snapshot sort, cone-memory step 0)

- **The capability snapshot's sort no longer builds a key `String` per row or a
  flattened copy of the rows; the output is byte-identical.** Cross-app CDO
  `compose_snapshot` (the CDO baseline at `bc3ccb18`, clean; Linux, 22 cores, 93 GB,
  `release`-thin-LTO probe = `release-fast`, `/usr/bin/time -v`, one run each, quiet
  machine): peak RSS **46.8 GB -> 33.4 GB**, whole run 101 s -> 79 s; the
  `compose_snapshot_from_base` phase 32.8 s -> 18.0 s, its live-heap peak
  37.6 GiB -> 27.9 GiB (transient over the result 8.8 GiB -> 0.09 GiB).
  `derive_capability_facts` (`src/engine/l5/snapshot.rs`) now orders the emitted
  routines by `subject + "|"`, projects each one's rows straight into its slice of
  ONE pre-sized Vec (in parallel; a drained raw Vec drops as its slice is written),
  and stable-sorts each subject's slice in parallel on the seven remaining key fields.
  This is exact because `subject + "|"` is prefix-free when no subject contains `|`;
  the check reads the EMITTED subjects (`stable_routine_id` passes unmapped ids
  through), and any `|` falls back to one global stable sort. New
  `engine::joined_key::cmp_joined` compares field lists as their `|`-join, byte for
  byte, without allocating (comparing fields one by one is a different order:
  `a`/`ab` join to `a|…`/`ab|…`, and `ab` sorts first). The cone's `sort_inherited`
  and policy's fact sort use it too, still stable.
  Proof: the whole serialized snapshot document of the cross-app FULL model on CDO
  (9,463,055,195 bytes of JSON, every field of the `project_r4f_snapshot` envelope)
  hashes the same with BLAKE3 before and after
  (`3b480fbf53066d4d071422ee4b9390f768da655687600860937e95c2c2a2ddaf`), and so does the
  pd arena `derive_pd_arena` builds on it (2,822,661 states, 3,928,044 links, producer
  indexes included). No golden was regenerated.
  Tests: `joined_key::tests::t2_*` (named cases and all 46,656 pairs of three-field
  keys over `{"", a, ab, |, a|, b}` against `join("|")`); `snapshot::step0_sort_tests`
  against a verbatim copy of the old derivation: hand-stated rows with 16-way complete
  8-field ties of distinct payloads, subjects `a`/`ab`, field values `x`/`xy`, two
  internal ids on one stable id, a duplicated internal id, the `derive_pd_arena`
  producer among tied direct rows, an unmapped `a|b` subject that interleaves with `a`
  (the fallback), and every `tests/r0-corpus` + `tests/fixtures` app single- and
  cross-app (table and pd arena). Discrimination, each break made and reverted with
  Edit: `sort_unstable_by` in the slice sort -> the tie test fails (pass after
  revert); a field-wise compare -> the tie test fails, and the corpus test fails on
  `ws-r2a-record-types` and `ws-rules` (both modes); grouping by the bare subject ->
  fails (`a` before `ab`); no delimiter fallback -> the `a|b` test fails; in
  `cmp_joined`, a field-wise answer at a prefix -> both T2 tests fail; dropping the
  virtual `|` -> both T2 tests fail. All pass after each revert.

### Changed (cdo-gate memory)

- **`scripts/cdo-gate` peaks at 10.5 GB, not 46.9 GB, and runs in ~3 min instead of
  ~4.7.** Measured 2026-10-31 on Linux (22 cores, 93 GB), `cdo` profile, warm, as the
  summed RSS of the processes (the whole gate after: 10.5 GB, 184 s, exit 0). The whole 46.9 GB came from one test,
  `cdo_i264_closed_interface_site_census` (`program_resolve_harness`): it composed a
  whole capability snapshot of the cross-app CDO model (`compose_snapshot`, whose
  cone keeps every routine's raw inherited facts: 45.8 GB and 83 s with the test
  alone) to read only the snapshot's call-site rows. New
  `engine::l5::snapshot::compose_callsite_resolutions` derives those rows without
  the cone (the test: 3.1 GB, 19 s). The typed-edge and call-site derivers now take
  a cone-free `Ledger`, so the compiler keeps the two paths the same; the lib test
  `callsite_resolutions_alone_equal_the_snapshot_rows` checks it on every
  `tests/r0-corpus` and `tests/fixtures` app, single-app and cross-app.
  `dependency_body_unknown_ceiling_on_cdo` reads the harness's shared CDO context
  instead of building the same one again. Per phase, before -> after: harness
  46.9 GB / 123 s -> 8.6 GB / 42 s; lsp 2.6 GB / 7 s -> 2.6 GB / 6 s;
  l4_summary_differential 1.9 GB / 19 s -> 1.8 GB / 16 s; `--lib` 10.4 GB / 131 s ->
  9.9 GB / 121 s. No assertion changed; the counts are the same (lib +1, the new test).

### Added (intent evidence)

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-29-intent-evidence-design.md` (rev 3).

- **Step 1: label attributes and `TextConst` text are lowered.** `VarDecl::label`
  (`LabelValue`) now also keeps a label's `Comment = '…'`, `MaxLength = n` and every
  other `name = value` attribute (as written, in `other`), and a `TextConst`'s text
  (the `ENU` value, else the first) with its other languages in `translations`. A
  `TextConst` is never locked, so it is never a constant for G52's `Evaluate` rule.
  No golden moves. Tests `label_attributes_and_text_consts_are_kept` (new) and
  `label_declarations_carry_text_and_locked` (G52; now compares text and locked only).
- **Step 2: captions, tooltips, page actions and comments are lowered.** `FieldDecl`
  gains `caption`, `tooltip`, `option_caption` (one text per `#if` arm: the
  property's first string literal, `''` unescaped, so `Caption = 'x', Comment = 'c'`
  gives `x`), `doc` and `origin`; table extension fields included. New
  `ObjectDecl::actions` (`ActionDecl`: name, keyword, caption, tooltip, raw
  `RunObject` values, and `triggers`, the indexes of its `OnAction` routines) holds
  every `action` / `systemaction` / `fileuploadaction` / `customaction` of a page,
  page extension or request page, nested in `area` / `group` / `add*` / `#if`.
  `lookup_symbol_properties` (the LSP's `actionProperties`) now uses the same
  action test, so it also finds the three other action kinds. `RoutineDecl::doc`,
  `FieldDecl::doc` and `ActionDecl::doc` hold the run of lone `//` / `///` lines
  directly above the declaration (by line number, since comments are grammar
  extras; a blank line ends the run, a `#region` line does not), and new
  `AlFile::comments` keeps every comment of the file as written, with trailing and
  own-line comments told apart, for step 3's check comments. Plain IR facts in
  every profile: measured +4.3 % peak memory on the DO workspace (comments alone
  +2.0 %), +2.2 % on the 1000-file LSP corpus, so no gate (spec 4.1b). No golden
  moves.
- **Step 3: rules are built at model assembly, when a view asks for them.**
  `ViewNeeds` gains `rules` (joined by `union`, kept out of `ViewKey`); no demand
  sets it yet. `build_view_model` hands it to the assembly as the new
  `AssemblyNeeds` (no default; `BASE` or `RULES`), which every assembly entry now
  takes: `assemble_and_resolve_workspace_program`,
  `assemble_and_resolve_cross_app_program`, `build_cross_app_base_from` and the
  workspace.rs entries. The new body pass `program::body::rules` turns each
  routine's IR into `PRule` rows (`Error`, `TestField`, `FieldError`,
  `ConfirmError`, `ConfirmExit`): the condition as atoms (`FieldCompare`,
  `FieldEmpty`, `ParamBool`, `CallResult`, `RecordFound`, `NoneOf`, `Other`) from
  enclosing `if` (negated on `else`), `case` arms and `else` (`NoneOf`), earlier
  `if C then exit;` and earlier `if C then <check>;`; the message (literal, label,
  `TextConst`, `ErrorInfo`, platform or dynamic, with args, the label's comment and,
  for a name the routine sees declared more than once, every candidate text); and
  the check's comment. `stops` is settled after resolution, next to #288's dead-mark
  trust and by the same per-site test: a bare `Error` that may bind to an own
  `procedure Error`, or an `ErrorInfo` message, may not stop, and then adds no
  `not C` to later checks. `ModelRoutine::rules` is `None` until built;
  `ModelRoutine::rules()` panics on `None`. A default `analyze` builds none. #288's
  one-argument `Error` proof now also accepts a `TextConst` (it is Text). The
  lowerer now lowers date, time and datetime literals (`0D`) to their `Literal`
  variants instead of `Unknown`. New fixture `tests/r0-corpus/ws-rules` (compiles
  with alc 29); it adds its routines to the l2 snapshot and the r4f root-class
  summary, and no other golden line moves.
- **Step 4: `alsem explain`, the evidence card.** New command
  `alsem explain <ws> --routine <name> | --diff <patch> | --table <T> --field <F>`
  (`--format human|json`, `--out`, `--single-app`, `--diff-root`). Each card
  (JSON schema `al-sem.explain/1`) holds the routine (id, object, object caption,
  doc comment, anchor), its own rules (kind, whether it stops, condition atoms and
  text, message with label text, args, label comment and candidates, comment,
  anchor), its effects (table writes with the fields written and their captions,
  conditionality and call path; `commits` no / may / yes with each commit site;
  events raised; interactive UI), the page actions that reach it (caption,
  tooltip, path), the events it raises itself with their subscriber count and
  `IsHandled` (extension points), the tests that reach it (with each test's own
  assert count), and its gaps (symbol-only calls, unresolved calls, unparsed
  bodies, a cut cone, a text that differs by `#if` arm, a dependency field
  caption that is not read). Every list is always present. Inherited and caller
  rules are step 5: each card has `"inherited": []`, `"callers": []` and a
  `cross-call-rules-not-computed` gap. `--routine` resolves as `prove` does
  (not found or ambiguous: exit 2, with a diagnostic naming the candidates);
  `--diff` resolves the same routines as `digest --diff` (same code, same diff
  root; no routine: exit 2); `--table/--field` lists every workspace routine
  that writes the field by assignment or `Validate` (new
  `engine::l5::field_writers`; an unknown table or field exits 2). Cards are
  sorted by anchor. Usage errors exit 1 (bad `--format`, no mode) or 3 (two
  modes, `--table` without `--field`, `--diff-root` without `--diff`). It runs
  as a batch job too. Wiring: `ViewNeeds` gains `card_text` and the `EXPLAIN`
  preset (rules and card text); `AssemblyNeeds` gains `card_text` and
  `EXPLAIN`; `ModelRoutine::card_text` (doc, object caption, the page actions
  the routine is the trigger of, a test's own asserts) is built at assembly only
  for it and its accessor panics when not built. `ModelField::captions` is a
  plain fact (empty for a symbol-only dependency's field). New `explain_plan`:
  one tree with the test-coverage graph, no detector run, no `l4`.
  `test_coverage::reaching_tests` lists every test that reaches a routine.
  `al_syntax::lower::leading_literal_text` is public. Limit: a `ModifyAll` is
  not yet found as a field writer (its argument is not kept by the body walk).
  New fixture `tests/r0-corpus/ws-explain` (it adds lines to the l2 snapshot,
  the r4f root-class summary, a new r2c event-graph golden and two policy-facts
  oracle cases); new golden family `tests/cli-explain-goldens/` under
  `--test cli`, listed in `scripts/check-goldens`.
- **Step 5: rules across calls in `alsem explain`.** New
  `engine::l5::cross_rules`. `rules.inherited` now lists the rules of the
  routines a card's routine calls, when the call is `unconditional-on-success`
  (not under `asserterror`) and ends, in the source, before the routine's first
  write (a callee that is itself the first write gives only the rules it runs
  before its own first write); transitively, with the call path (`via`) and the
  routine that holds the check (`in`). A write counts when it assigns a record
  field or mutates a record (not a known-temporary one), or calls a routine that
  may write (or has no body). A callee's `ParamBool` atom is rewritten across the
  call: a contradicting literal drops the rule, a matching one drops the atom, a
  forwarded parameter re-anchors it, any other argument becomes an `Other` atom;
  a callee parameter that is assigned (or passed to a `var`) keeps its atom as
  written (`param_guard`'s usability). A call to a `[TryFunction]` whose result is
  used, a `Codeunit.Run`, an interface call with several implementers and an
  unresolved call give no inheritance. Table triggers that a `Validate`, a
  `Rename` or an `Insert`/`Modify`/`Delete(true)` runs (the resolver's
  `implicit-trigger` edges with `fires: always`) are inherited with the write
  named (`trigger`). `rules.callers` lists the rules each known caller runs
  before every call into the routine, with `presentIn`, `appliedBy` (never for a
  `MayNotStop` rule) and `skippedBy`; `rules.knownCallers` counts the callers.
  The `cross-call-rules-not-computed` gap is gone. New gaps:
  `table-trigger-rules-skipped` (a plain field assignment, `Modify()` /
  `Modify(false)` or a non-literal RunTrigger, with the skipped triggers and
  their rules), `error-collector` (a call to a `Log…` procedure of
  `Error Message Management` / `Error Message`, a stated list), and
  `cross-call-rules-truncated` (the walk's budget of 200,000 routine
  expansions, or a chain of calls 512 deep, the walk's recursion limit; cycles
  are cut, results memoised). Each extension point lists its
  subscribers' own rules (`subscriberRoutines`, `conditionalOnAppSet`), never
  merged into `inherited`. `reachedFrom` follows a page action's
  `RunObject = Codeunit X` into that codeunit's `OnRun` (`runObject`). Wiring:
  `PRule::when_texts` (each atom's text); `CardAction::run_object`;
  `ModelObject::run_actions` (the `RunObject` actions, built at assembly behind
  `ViewNeeds::card_text`, accessor panics when not built). Statement order comes
  from the sites' control context and source anchors, so `RULES` does not need
  `ORDERING_FACTS` (spec §4.1b, §4.3 updated). New fixture
  `tests/r0-corpus/ws-explain-calls` (adds lines to the l2 snapshot, the r4f
  root-class summary, a new r2c golden and two policy-facts oracle cases); 12
  new goldens in `tests/cli-explain-goldens/`, and the step-4 goldens show the
  computed lists.
- **Step 6: `d65-guard-bypass` (opt-in) and the rules index behind it.**
  - *A check counts only on the path.* Step 5 counted a caller's own check as
    applied when it sat anywhere before the call, even in the other branch of an
    `if` or in a loop body that may not run; d65 drops conditions that are not on
    the written table, so that hid a real bypass. Each `PRule` now records where
    it is on the path (`on_path`, `PRule::guards`): after the check to the end of
    its block, in the `else` of an `if` whose `then` it directly is (only for a
    check with no condition of its own: `Error`, `FieldError`, a `Confirm` exit;
    a `TestField` is not evaluated there), and wherever its statement lifts out
    of an `if`/`case` branch, `begin..end`, `repeat` or `with`, never out of a
    `while`/`for`/`foreach` body, `try`, `asserterror` or `#if` arm.
    `cross_rules` uses it for caller rules and "before the first write", and a
    callee's `all` keeps only the checks passed on every path to its end
    (`at_exit`). `explain`'s `appliedBy`/`skippedBy` follow it. `PRule` also gains
    `when_earlier` (which atoms are an earlier check's `not C`).
  - *`ModifyAll` writes a field.* `ModelRecordOperation::modify_all_field` holds a
    `ModifyAll`'s first argument, read at assembly from the IR (never serialized),
    so `fieldArguments` and every detector input stay as they were;
    `explain --table/--field` and d65 list `ModifyAll` writers.
  - *`substrate::RULES` (`1 << 7`)*: the per-field writer index
    (`l5::rules_index`): each primary-app writer of each field with the rules in
    force at each write (own on the path, the calls before it, the table triggers
    it runs, and per known caller the rules it applies), `MayNotStop` rules left
    out. Outside `ALL`; filled once before the detector loop (`fill_rules`, also a
    `View` cell, `Cell::Rules`); `get_rules_index()` panics "declare
    substrate::RULES"; filling it from a model without rules panics.
    `registry::assembly_needs(detectors)` says what model a detector list needs;
    `alsem analyze` builds the rules only when a selected detector requires
    `RULES` (`ViewNeeds::analyze_for`), so a default run builds none.
    `project_r4_findings[_cross_app]` now run only the named detectors, and every
    builder that runs a detector list (aldump's `--r4-findings*`, the switch dump,
    `build_analysis_model`) builds with its needs.
  - *`d65-guard-bypass`*: rule key = kind plus the atoms on the written table
    (record variable dropped, enum values by member; `Other`, parameter and call
    atoms, and an earlier check's `not C`, form none); a key applied by at
    least 3 writers and 75 % of them is a majority rule, and each writer without it
    is a finding (`possible`, low) at its first write, with the rule, the follower
    count and two examples. Opt-in: `--detector d65-guard-bypass` or the new
    `--preset business-rules`. Suppress with `// al-sem-ignore d65-guard-bypass:
    <reason>` above the write.
  - `explain --table/--field` lists each write's effective rules (`sites[].rules`)
    and each writer's `callerRules` / `knownCallers`, from the same index.
  - Goldens: new `ws-d65` fixture and r4 golden (5 findings); the d65 row in every
    `all`-slot detector-stats golden (cli-a json/stats) and its SARIF rule in the
    gate goldens; new `ws-explain-calls` callers (`ReleaseBranch`, `ReleaseLoop`,
    `ReleaseGuarded`, `ReleaseElse`, `CheckLines`) move the l2 snapshot, the r4f
    root-class summary and the `calls.*` explain goldens (line shifts and the new
    caller rules); `explain.field-status` gains `ReopenAll` (its `ModifyAll`) and
    the rules per write. `FIXTURE_ROOTS` r0-corpus 220 -> 221.
  - Triage (`docs/detector-audit.md`): on the Continia DO workspace d65 gives 0
    findings at `--scope primary` and `--scope all` (722 written fields; 166 with
    at least 3 writers, none with a majority rule that a writer skips). At looser
    thresholds (N = 2, p = 0.5) it would give 5, all deliberate import/upgrade
    writes, so N = 3, p = 0.75 stay. The CDO-baseline triage is still owed; d65
    stays opt-in.
- **Step 7: pin a rule in the policy** (spec
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-rules-to-policy-design.md`).
  - *`alsem explain --emit-policy`* writes the majority rules of
    `--table T --field F` (or, alone, of every field the workspace writes) as
    `al-sem.policy.yaml` entries. Each entry is one d65 rule key (d65's own
    `rule_key`, `applied` and bar, N = 3 and p = 0.75; d65's `majorities` was
    split so both read `key_counts`), kept even when every writer applies it.
    Its id hangs on the key alone, so fixing a bypass keeps the ids; the counts
    and examples go in a comment. With `--table/--field`, each key below the bar
    is written commented out, ready to confirm by hand. Unknown table or field
    exits 2; `--routine`/`--diff`/`--format` with it exit 3. It builds the rules
    and no card text, and no plan.
  - *Policy format version 2.* A rule may have `requires:`, a predicate over one
    rule key a writer applies. Such a rule (a pin) selects write facts (a writer
    and one field it writes) with `when`, and a writer violates it when no key it
    applies satisfies `requires`. New predicate fields `write.table`,
    `write.field` (glob), `rule.kind` (enum) and `rule.atoms` (exact text, as d65
    forms it: a rule with one more atom is a weaker rule). The loader reads
    versions 1 and 2 (the error is now "policy version must be 1 or 2"), refuses a
    pin or a write/rule field in version 1, and checks a pin's shape; `facts` and
    `requireCoverage` do not apply to a pin. Version 1 files load as before, so no
    existing golden moved.
  - *`policy check`* runs a pin over the same writer index d65 reads (so a
    `MayNotStop` rule is never applied), anchoring a finding at the writer's first
    violating write. A truncated cross-call walk makes a missing key unknown
    (`onUnknown`). `policy explain` prints a `Requires:` block.
  - *Declared needs.* `PolicyJob` asks `ViewNeeds::rules` and the writer index
    only for a policy with a pin: `Plan` gains `own` (substrate bits a command
    reads itself, outside any run; `prepare` fills them before the runs) and
    `View::rules()` (panics "declare substrate::RULES"). A policy without a pin
    costs what it did before.
  - Tests and goldens: `cli_policy_pins` (new); `tests/cli-explain-goldens/emit.*`
    (3) and `tests/cli-c-policy-goldens/pins.*` (4); new fixtures
    `tests/fixtures/policy-pins/{bypass,fixed}` (`FIXTURE_ROOTS` fixtures 48 -> 50).
    On `ws-d65` the emitted pins flag exactly d65's five writes.
- **`scripts/intent-cdo-check <cdo-workspace> [out-dir]`** runs the two checks
  that need the pinned CDO baseline (spec section 6): `scripts/cdo-gate`, and
  d65 at `--scope primary` and `--scope all` (JSON and terminal). It writes
  logs, reports and a `summary.txt` into one folder (default
  `target/intent-cdo-check/`) and exits 1 only when the gate fails or a d65 run
  gives no report. Trial-run on Continia DO: d65 0 findings at both scopes.

### Fixed (G52)

- **A statement `Evaluate` that provably cannot fail is no implicit error**
  (G52, refines G50). `Evaluate(Target, Source)` with two arguments raises
  nothing when `Source` is a constant no translation changes (a string
  literal, or a label declared `Locked = true`) and its text parses for
  `Target`'s declared type: a `Guid` in braced `{8-4-4-4-12}` form, or an
  `Integer` of plain digits (optional leading `-`) in AL's Integer range
  (±2,147,483,647). Both variables must be LOCALS declared exactly once in
  the routine, with no parameter or global of the same name: the IR keeps
  both arms of an `#if`, so a global, a local declared twice, or a local
  declared in one arm only (the other arm then sees the global) may have
  another type or text in the compiled arm. Anything else stays a possible
  error: an unlocked label, a global label, a computed text, another type,
  a target that is no plain variable, or a third (format) argument. Continia DO
  reads notification ids this way (`CDO Conflict Notific. Handler`,
  `CDO DO-eDocs Notific. Handler`): claim OPRF-CORE-007.c4 (throws-error,
  expect no) now answers `no`; PLAT-SET-009.c1 (an `Evaluate` of computed
  text) still answers `yes`. To know a label's text, the lowerer now records
  it on `VarDecl.label` (`LabelValue`: text, locked), and the variable
  symbol carries `fixed_local` (set only for such a local, with a locked
  label's text).

### Fixed (G51)

- **AL synthesized from transpiled C# keeps simple `if` conditions** (G51).
  The translator used to replace every condition with the opaque local
  `"alsem branch"`, so a guard in Continia Core (which ships only C#) could
  never be pruned by a caller's literal argument. An `if` whose condition is
  built only from Boolean parameters and locals the C# never writes, with `!`,
  `&`/`&&`, `|`/`||` and parentheses, is now written out as AL (`if not
  ShowError or ShowMessage then`), with every compound operand parenthesized.
  This is exact: BC's `CStmtHit(n)` prefix returns `true`, and reads of
  non-null `bool` variables cannot fail or have side effects, so C#'s
  short-circuit operators and AL's `and`/`or` give the same value. A variable
  qualifies only when the method never writes it (a parameter's prologue copy
  and a local's `= default(bool)` aside): an assignment, a compound
  assignment, `out`/`ref`, a by-reference `ByRef<bool>` wrapper (a `var`
  argument) or a tuple deconstruction keeps it opaque, because the translator
  drops assignments and the synthesized body would otherwise read a value the
  C# does not have. `var` parameters, globals, comparisons, `^`, loop
  conditions and `case` arms stay opaque. Such a Boolean is also passed bare
  as an argument, so the requirement follows a forwarded flag (al-sem binds
  only a bare identifier argument to the caller's parameter). Extraction
  scheme 7. On Continia DO, Core's synthesized `if`s go from 3618 opaque to
  3458 opaque and 160 written out; `Notification Mgt.MessageHandler`'s
  `if ShowMessage then Message` is now pruned along `HasAccessToModule(…,
  false)`, so EDOC-SEAL-005.c6 and PLAT-UPG-007.c6 (`reaches-ui`, expect `no`)
  move from a wrong `yes` to `unknown` (coverage partial: two open-world
  dispatches in the Continia System Application's HTTP code). Tests
  `cli_prove_transpiled_guard` (a literal `false` through a forwarding routine
  answers `no`; a reassigned flag stays `yes`) and the translator's
  `writes_out_conditions_on_never_written_booleans_only` (every shape).

### Fixed (G49)

- **A temp state that depends on the routine's own `Rec` now reads
  `parameter-dependent(rec)`, not `parameter-dependent(4294967295)`.** The
  receiver index (`RECEIVER_PARAM_INDEX`, `u32::MAX`) means "the implicit `Rec`
  a table procedure or trigger runs on"; the raw number leaked into every text
  rendering of a temp state: `query effects` (JSON and human),
  `digest`'s and `prove`'s `detail.tempState`. On DO it showed for the
  `CDO Setup` `Modify` calls in `CDO Setup.AssignUniqueFolder`. The one
  renderer, `effect_query_cli::temp_state_str`, now names the receiver; the
  internal representation, structured JSON (`parameterIndex`) and effect keys
  are unchanged. `prove`'s `temp-state-depends-on-caller` blocker now says
  "on the implicit Rec: a table write only if the record the routine runs on
  is not temporary" when the write's only caller-dependent state is the
  receiver, instead of "on a record parameter". Pinned by
  `tests/cli/cli_receiver_temp_state.rs` on the new fixture
  `tests/fixtures/g49-receiver` (compiled clean with alc 18.0).

### Fixed (soundness of the guarded search; G47)

- **The guarded search (G23/G33/G48) no longer drops an effect on the strength
  of one representative fact.** The cone keeps one fact per kind (op,
  resource, confidence, temp class) per root, so an effect's and a boundary
  group resource's merged origin operations are that representative's. A dead
  representative dropped the effect even when another write of the same kind
  could run: a root writing a table through a nearer routine guarded by a
  literal `false` and a farther unguarded one answered a false `no`. An
  effect kind (effect type, resource) is now unreachable only when EVERY direct
  fact of that kind in the root's reach has no state where its site can run
  (`LiteralReach::kind_dead`, read off the snapshot's direct facts). Also
  removed: the short-lived rule that dropped a whole group when its merged
  facts were dead (same flaw); it cut real COMMITs on Continia DO (nine
  `may-commit` claims, DPUR-DOC-001…007.c4, DSRV-OPEN-001…004, proven again).
  The crossing rule (a group whose crossing cannot run is dropped) stays.
- **`publishes-event:` an event no publisher or subscriber of the program
  names is refused** (G47; exit 1, `prove: unknown event …`), as an unknown
  table is (G40). The cli-b golden `ws-d34 publishes-event:OnAfterPost`
  answered it; it is now a refusal test.

### Fixed (G50)

- **`Evaluate(X, Text)` used as a statement may throw** (G50), as `Get` does:
  its discarded Boolean result means a failed parse raises a runtime error.
  So does `ReadFrom` on a JSON or XML value used as a statement. `throws-error`
  answered a decided `no` for Continia DO's `CDO Functions.GetCDOVerAsInteger`
  (three statement-form `Evaluate`s, PLAT-SET-009.c1, expect `yes`); it now
  answers `yes`. `if Evaluate(…) then` stays error-free. Test
  `cli_prove_throws_error` (statement and checked forms, `JsonObject.ReadFrom`).

### Fixed (G48, part of G44/G46)

- **A boundary group whose crossing into the dependency cannot run is
  dropped whole**, its UI, event and COMMIT facts too (G48). The guarded
  search (`literal_reach`) cut a group only per table resource, so non-table
  facts behind a dead guard stayed. A group is one crossing (its boundary
  identity is that call site), so when every reached state of its routine
  rules the crossing out, none of it runs. A group is also dropped when every
  merged fact's origin (operation, or call site for a call-borne fact) is
  dead. Continia DO: PRNT-QUEU-006.c8 (`publishes-event:
  OnBeforeAutoSendOnPostingSalesInvoice`, expect `no`) moves from a
  contradicted `yes` to `unknown`. Not yet enough for G46/G44: their facts
  are inside the dependency, and a call-borne fact names the root's first hop
  rather than its origin there. Test
  `cli_prove_table_branches::a_boundary_group_behind_a_dead_crossing_is_dropped_whole`.

### Fixed (G42/G43)

- **The G34 exit guard reads the set form `if not (R.Number in [Database::"A",
  Database::"B"]) then exit;`** (G43). Only `R.Number <> Database::"T"` was
  modelled. Continia DO's `CDO Electronic Document Mgt..CreateSalesSourceDocs`
  exits unless the RecordRef holds a Sales Invoice or Credit Memo Header, so
  from a Service Shipment Header its boundary group (Sales/Purchase/Service
  Header writes) cannot run. Three contradicted claims that expect `no`

  Header`) now answer `unknown`; DSRV-OPEN-006.c5 (expect `yes`) still proves
  `yes`. Test `cli_prove_recref_guard` (set guard, a live and a dead table).
- **`prove` on a routine selector that matches nothing says so** (G42). Its
  `unknown` answer had no blocker and no message, so a mistyped id or a
  missing app-guid prefix read like an answer. The result now carries
  `blockedBy: [{kind: "routine-not-found"}]`, or `routine-ambiguous` with the
  candidates. Exit 2 stays the no-root code `digest` and `fingerprint` share
  (a refused question, like an unknown `writes-table:` table, is exit 1). The
  cli-b `dummy-doc` goldens gain the blocker.

### Fixed (G40/G41, not yet re-verified on the DO claim set)

- **`prove … writes-table:<name>` matched no write of a table numbered like a

- **A bare `Modify(true)` / `Validate(…)` in a report dataitem trigger operates

- **G36's field guard reads a `writes-table:` table asked by number too**

### Added

- **The RecordRef value flow reads a `case R.Number` branch under the tables
  passed in** (G35, extending G34's `recref_flow`). Base Application's
  workflow loop (`Workflow Management.ExecuteResponses`) passes one Variant by
  `var` to every response. `ReleaseDocument`/`OpenDocument` swap it for
  `RecordRef.Get("Record ID to Approve")` only in their `Database::"Approval
  Entry"` branch, and `PostDocument` runs Sales-Post only for a Sales Header.
  - A fact inside a `case R.Number` branch (or past an `if R.Number <> … then
    exit;`) now records that condition. A routine with such facts, or one
    that passes a RecordRef or Variant into one, is evaluated under its actual
    input tables: a least fixpoint over its facts and its callees, memoized
    and bounded (`EVAL_BUDGET`, `EVAL_DEPTH`; giving up means "anything").
    It is used only where the summary alone answers "anything".
  - A by-value Variant parameter is the callee's own copy, so reassigning it
    does not reach the caller. The exception is a callee that rebinds a
    RecordRef the Variant holds through an alias, directly or further down
    (`alias_shared`).
  On Continia DO the requisition-batch route the HandledState triage traced
  for HAND-SALE-009.c2 and EMAIL-TPLM-011.c9 is now cut. Both claims still
  answer `yes`, through the customer-credit-limit workflow event, which hands
  `PostDocument` the Sales Header itself. Whether that runs depends on
  workflow setup data and on Sales-Post refusing a quote: a stated limit.
  Test `cli_prove_recref_guard::a_branch_on_the_variants_table_rebinds_it_only_for_that_table`.

- **`prove` follows the table a RecordRef holds into `if R.Number <>
  Database::"T" then exit;`** (G34), through `GetTable`, `Duplicate()`,
  parameters and a codeunit global. Continia DO's `VendorLedgerPrint` puts a
  Vendor Ledger Entry in a RecordRef, stores it in the e-mail handler's global
  (`SetRecRefFilter`) and prints. The print path copies the global and reaches
  `CDO File.CalcSalesDisc`, which exits unless the RecordRef holds a Sales
  Header, so its `Sales-Calc. Discount` run cannot happen from there. `prove …
  writes-table:Vendor` still answered `yes` through it (contradicted claim
  HAND-PSV-004.c5); it now answers `unknown` (open interface calls remain).
  Re-proving the 584 DO claims moved exactly 4, every one a contradicted `yes`
  through this route, now `unknown`: HAND-PSV-004.c5 and EMAIL-OPEN-001.c1, c3,
  c7. Nothing else moved.
  How it works (`engine::l5::recref_flow`):
  - Each routine gets a flow-insensitive summary of what each RecordRef and
    Variant may hold: a parameter's entry value, no table for a local, a
    record's table by `GetTable`, another variable by `:=` or `Duplicate()`,
    or anything. A call reads what the callee may leave in the parameter; an
    event reads its loaded subscribers, an interface call its loaded
    implementers (`prove` already lists an open interface as a blocker).
  - `A := B` shares the RecordRef: a rebinding (`Open`, `GetTable`, `Close`…)
    of either that can run after it rebinds both. Separate branches of one
    `if`/`case` outside a loop do not count.
  - A codeunit global is read per instance. A codeunit the caller declares as
    a local (not `SingleInstance`, never passed on) holds only what the calls
    made on it assign. A self-call carries the instance along.
  - The guarded search (`literal_reach`) binds the parameters and globals a
    guard depends on, and now binds arguments across interface calls too.
  - `R.GetTable(Rec)` past a guard that `R` already held `Rec`'s table adds
    no table (`CalcSalesDisc` puts its own Sales Header back).
  Test `cli_prove_recref_guard` (a `no`, and four `yes` cases: the guard's own
  table, a rebinding callee, an alias rebinding, a rebinding subscriber).

- **`aldump --dump-dependency-source <workspace> <out-dir>`** writes the AL the
  engine reads from inside each dependency `.app` to `<out-dir>/<app guid>/<virtual
  path>`. That is the path a dependency citation `dep:<guid>:<path>` names, with the
  same text and lines. It includes the AL synthesized for a runtime package that
  ships no AL; each of its statements ends in `// cs <line>`, the transpiled C# line.
  Source from a folder on disk is not written; it is already a file. Asked by the
  CONtinAI pipeline so citations into Continia Core resolve to a file and line. On
  Continia DO: 9 apps, Core 291 files. Test `cli_dump_dependency_source`.

- **`prove` shows how a dependency boundary group reaches the asked table**
  (G35). A `writes-table` evidence entry on a group now carries `groupPath`:
  `{resource, hops}`, the routines from the root to one where a write of that
  table can run, each hop `<edge kind> → Object.Routine`. Under rule B a
  witness ends where it enters dependency code, so Continia DO's
  `writes-table:CDO E-Mail Log` answer through `Base
  Application.CalcInvDiscForHeader` had no path to check. The path is read off
  the guarded search G23/G33 already run (`LiteralReach::live_tree`), so a
  branch G33 proves dead is never shown; it is one example, not checked further
  for feasibility (`engine::l5::group_path`). Test `cli_prove_group_path`.

- **`prove` follows the table a record argument holds into `case RecRef.Number`**
  (G33). A routine that takes a record as a `Variant`, reads its table with
  `RecRef.GetTable(Variant)` and branches on `case RecRef.Number of
  Database::"T": …` runs a branch only for the table its caller passes. G23's
  per-root reachability (`literal_reach`) now carries, next to literal Booleans, the
  table of each such parameter: a call binds it from a record variable of known table
  (the implicit `Rec` included) or forwards the caller's own, and a branch (an `else`
  for a table no branch names) whose table contradicts it cannot run. The `case` and
  its branches are marked in the control-flow tree (`PCFNNode::table_case`). Sound
  limits: a local RecordRef only, bound by one `GetTable` of a by-value `Variant`
  nothing assigns; a call passing either on must sit inside that `case`, which must
  be in no loop. Dependency writes grouped at a boundary drop a resource whose every
  originating operation cannot run (`dead_group_resources`). On Continia DO,
  `ApprovalsMgmt.PreventDeletingRecordWithOpenApprovalEntry`'s `Gen. Journal Batch`
  branch no longer reaches the workflow engine from a Requisition Line delete; its
  `Requisition Wksh. Name` branch, which that caller does pass, still does, so the
  claims' answers do not move. Test `cli_prove_table_branches`.
- **`prove` and `digest` start inside a dependency** (G31). A dependency routine named
  by its StableRoutineId is a root (a display name still selects only the
  workspace's). Rule B (spec 2026-10-23 §14.3.5) ends a workspace root's witness at
  the first dependency routine and groups what lies beyond, which bounds digest's
  cost; a dependency root starts past that boundary, so it is read with rule B off,
  and its witness paths follow the code to each effect of every kind (writes,
  commits, events, …) in every app. It got no effect at all: the reportable roots
  leave every dependency routine out (`digest::reportable_roots`), and rule B ended
  every fact at the root. On Continia DO, from `Sales-Calc. Discount.OnRun`, the
  `Cust. Ledger Entry` write runs through `ApprovalsMgmt` → the workflow engine's
  `ExecuteResponse` (every response) → `GenJournalLine.ClearCustVendApplnEntry`.
  Test `cli_dependency_roots`.
- **An interface held in a codeunit global, set only from codeunit variables, is a
  closed dispatch site** (G30). An interface call on an object global of a workspace
  codeunit dispatches over the codeunits the global can hold when the codeunit itself
  is the only writer: every write, in every routine, stores a `Codeunit X` variable
  or a parameter of a `local`/`internal` routine (not an event subscriber, and the
  workspace names no `internalsVisibleTo` friend), and every call of that routine
  passes a `Codeunit X` variable there. The site is then `Complete`, its routes
  narrowed to those codeunits, with no assumption label. Phase 1 records both facts
  per call site (`SiteFacts::interface_holder`, `argument_codeunits`); a post-pass
  (`resolve::interface_holder::close_holder_sites`) closes the site once every call
  edge is known. Every doubt keeps the site open: a `protected var`, a codeunit that
  implements an interface, a parse issue, any other read or write of the global
  (passing it on, `Clear`), a public setter, one caller passing anything else. On
  Continia DO this is `CDO Template Variant Mgt`'s `FieldChainEvaluator`
  (`SetFieldChainEvaluator`): 348 → 359 proven. Test `cli_prove_interface_holder`.
- **`prove` labels the answers that assume no subscriber beyond the loaded ones**
  (Q6, G29). The cone follows the LOADED subscribers of every event, so events are
  closed over them while interfaces are open; that was unlabelled. prove now has
  three worlds, weakest first (`prove::World`): strict (nothing assumed) <
  loaded-subscribers (the default) < closed-world (`--closed-world`). An answer
  carries ONE label, the weakest world that gives it:
  - `assumptions: ["loaded-subscribers"]` on a `no` whose cone raises an event any
    app may subscribe to: a table write or `Validate` (the platform table events,
    raised for temporary records too; read off the cone's record operations,
    `UnresolvedCone::fires_table_events`), an explicit event publication, or a page
    opened. A `yes` stands on its witness and carries none. Over-approximates: an
    internal publisher only friends can subscribe to counts too.
  - System Application's `Telemetry Logger` falls under the same assumption: its
    loggers exist only through `OnRegisterTelemetryLogger` subscribers that register
    them, so an unloaded app's logger is an unloaded subscriber. In the default world
    a call on it reaches only the loaded implementations, and its open-world row
    stops blocking when the cone already follows them all (counted in
    `obligations.loadedSubscribersRows`). The catalog
    (`calls::PUBLISHER_SCOPED_INTERFACES`) keys on the declaring app's GUID, not the
    name.

  On Continia DO: 340 → 348 proven (the 8 claims the Telemetry Logger alone
  blocked); 57 of the 148 proven `no` answers carry the label, 91 raise no
  subscribable event. Tests `cli_prove_loaded_subscribers`, `cli_prove_publisher_scoped`.
- **An internal interface with every friend loaded is a closed dispatch site** (G28).
  Only the declaring app and the apps its manifest lists in `internalsVisibleTo` can
  implement an interface declared `Access = Internal`. When every such friend is a
  loaded app, a call on the interface reaches only the implementers the program holds,
  so the site is closed in the open world, with no assumption label (the model marks it
  as #264 marks a closed-enum site, `DispatchMeta::closed_over`). On Continia DO this
  covers `CDO Module License`. A public interface, a name two objects share, a route
  that does not resolve, or a declared friend that is not loaded keeps the site open.
  `ProgramGraph::closed_internal_interfaces`; test `cli_prove_internal_interface`.

- **AL synthesized for runtime packages that ship no AL** (phases 2–4 of transpiled
  runtime bodies, spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-28-transpiled-runtime-bodies-design.md`,
  route A). A `.app` with no `.al` but with BC's transpiled C# (`bin/*.cs`) and its
  `SymbolReference.json` used to be symbol-only: every routine bodyless, its cones
  `opaque-dependency`, the app a `symbol-only-boundary` analysis gap. Extraction now
  synthesizes AL for it (`snapshot::transpiled`), one file per object at
  `transpiled/<KIND><id>.al`, read like any embedded source:
  - declarations come from the symbols: ids, names, namespaces, table fields (type,
    class, `CalcFormula`, option members) and keys, enum values and implementations,
    page source tables, extension targets, routine signatures and event attributes;
  - bodies come from the C# (`cs`: a reader for the transpiler's output; `translate`):
    each AL-runtime call becomes the AL call it came from, on a variable of the matching
    AL type, so the existing extractors classify it as real AL. `rec.Target.ALModifyAsync`
    is `"rec".Modify()`, `TrapError` keeps the Boolean consumed, and a record's table
    and temporariness come from its `new NavRecordHandle(…)`. Calls into AL code are
    bound by method id, and record arguments pass through. Control flow is kept, every
    condition an opaque Boolean, so an effect is conditional where the AL was;
  - triggers are placed by `NavName` (`OnRun`, `<Field> - OnValidate`,
    `<Action> - OnAction`), and event subscribers are declared from the C#
    `[NavEventSubscriber]`;
  - every statement carries `// cs <line>`, its C# line. Soundness: a C# call the
    translator cannot place becomes `"__alsem_untranslated"('<shape>')`, an unresolved
    call naming its shape, and a symbol routine with no C# body gets one such call,
    never an empty body.

  A table method called by id on a record variable binds too
  (`resolve_in_extendable_scope`, by id across the table and its extensions). The
  embedded-source cache file is now `<hash>.s<EXTRACTION_SCHEME>.json` (scheme 2), so
  an earlier "no source" entry is not reused. On Continia's Core 29.0 (230 C# files,
  1727 symbol routines): 291 files, 3293 routines, all parse clean, 3 statements
  untranslated. On Continia DO: `unknown` edges 19 → 7 (`realUnknownRate` 0.091% →
  0.033%); the 84 calls into Core's ABI now resolve to its synthesized source; prove
  claims 318 → 321 proven, and 336 of 408 with `--closed-world` (15 labelled), with no
  new contradiction. Tests: the `cs`, `translate` and `synth` units (hand-written C# in
  the transpiler's shape), the extraction hook (`a_package_with_only_transpiled_cs_
  yields_synthesized_al`, which fails with the hook off; shipped `.al` wins), and the
  table-method case of `synthesized_calls_bind_by_method_id` (which failed before the
  fix). Real-package checks are gated on `TRANSPILED_CS_DIR` / `TRANSPILED_SYMBOLS`
  (a package's own files are never committed).
- **AL method ids, and calls bound by them** (phase 1 of transpiled runtime bodies,
  spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-28-transpiled-runtime-bodies-design.md`). The
  new `program::resolve::method_id` computes the id the AL compiler gives a routine
  (`[MethodId(n)]` in BC's transpiled C#, `Id` in `SymbolReference.json`) from its
  signature: FNV-1a of the upper-cased name, combined with the return type's and each
  parameter's type kind, `var` flag and, for an overloadable routine with an object
  parameter, each parameter's subtype. It matches 16 of 16 ids alc 18.0.43 gave a
  probe app and all 1715 computable methods of Continia's Core 29.0. A signature with a
  generic (`List`, `Dictionary`) or `DotNet` parameter whose subtype counts has no id,
  so a call to it stays unresolved. The resolver binds a member call named
  `__alsem_mid_<n>` (what synthesized source will emit for a call the C# names only by
  id) to the one routine of the receiver's object with that id, source or ABI. Limit:
  ABI type text drops array dimensions, so an ABI routine with an array parameter does
  not match. Tests: `method_id` unit tests (the alc ids);
  `synthesized_calls_bind_by_method_id` (an id picks the overload the argument types
  would not, a `Record` parameter folds in its table id, an unknown id stays
  unresolved), failing with the rule off or the subtype id wrong.
- **`prove --closed-world`** (G24): assume the loaded world is all there is. An
  interface call then dispatches only to the loaded implementations, which the cone
  already follows, so its open-world row stops blocking (`obligations.closedWorldRows`
  counts them), and coverage that is partial only through `interface-open-world` counts
  as complete. A site a closed world cannot follow still blocks: one with no
  implementer in the model, a dependency implementer whose body is not loaded (a
  to-less route), or a closed enum that maps a value to a codeunit outside the
  program. That last one is now listed in the site's `unresolvedCandidates`
  (`enum-implementation-not-found`, from the new `ResolveIndex::
  unmapped_enum_implementers`). An answer that holds only under the assumption (the
  open world answers differently) carries `assumptions: ["closed-world"]`. A decided
  answer both worlds give is the open-world result, unlabelled. When both stay
  `unknown`, the result is the closed world's, so its blockers are what remains after
  the assumption. Without the flag nothing changes. On Continia DO it waives
  interface sites in 41 of the 88 undecided claims (`TelemetryLogger.LogMessage`,
  `FieldChainEvaluator.EvaluateFieldChain` and others) but decides none of them yet:
  each still has blockers outside interface dispatch, mostly calls into Continia's
  `Core`, which ships no AL. Limit: an extensible enum's value mappings are not
  extracted, so a mapping of one into an app missing from the package closure is not
  seen. Test: `cli_prove_closed_world`, with discrimination proofs on each guard.
- **Dependencies given as source folders** (G4). A workspace can name dependency
  apps that exist only as source, a folder with its own `app.json` and `.al` files
  and no `.app` (e.g. a BC.History checkout of Base Application), in
  `al-sem.dependencies.json` at its root: `{ "sources": ["../deps/Base Application"] }`,
  relative to the workspace or absolute. Each folder's `.al` files are all read,
  including folders under it with an `app.json` of their own: in BC.History those
  are the app's modules (110 in System Application, 39 in Base Application), and its
  test apps live beside the app's folder (`System Application/Test/…`), so naming the
  app's folder leaves them out. An app with no `.al` file (BC's umbrella
  `Application`) still counts through its `app.json`. A configured folder
  always supplies its app: a `.app` of the same id is not loaded. The folders are
  read once into `WorkspaceInputs` (`program::source_deps`), become dependency units
  of tier `LocalSourceApproximate` (dependency listings: `localApproximate`), and are
  inputs wherever inputs matter: a `dep-source` fingerprint row per folder (hashed
  over its `app.json`, file paths and texts), the incremental L4 host's reuse key,
  `alsem batch`'s write check (a job writing into a folder is refused), and the LSP
  watcher (an edit there, or to the list, rebuilds the dependencies; a changed list
  is watched from the next start). A config that cannot be honoured (unreadable or
  unknown keys, a missing folder, no or invalid `app.json`, a folder inside the
  workspace, two folders with one app id, the workspace app itself) fails the build
  with the reason. Measured on Continia DO 29.0 with BC.History w1-29 (Base
  Application, System Application, Business Foundation, Application):
  `primaryScoped` unknown edges 726 → 283 (real-unknown rate 3.46 % → 1.35 %);
  `alsem analyze` 1.9 s / 0.7 GB peak → 21.5 s / 3.5 GB peak. Their tiers are not
  shared through the dependency cache (no `.app` stamp), so an LSP root rebuild parses
  them again.

- **Runtime (`.NEA`) `.app` packages are read, not reported as encrypted** (branch
  `continai-gaps`, Continia's public 29.0 release as the sample set). These are BC
  runtime packages — the same `.NEA` form BC has shipped for years, scrambled with a
  fixed, public RC4 key (community-documented: hougaard.com, `SimonOfHH/D365BCAppHelper`,
  `businessdev.ALbuild`), not encrypted. `engine::deps::app_package_zip` now detects the
  mark, descrambles the stream (`capped_io::RUNTIME_APP_STREAM_CAP`, a new 512 MB cap on
  the declared stream length), and opens the plain zip: manifest, `SymbolReference.json`
  and embedded source read through the same public readers as a plain package, so the
  dependency loader, ABI ingest, LSP embedded-source and L4 artifacts get the real app
  (measured end-to-end on the 36-file CDN workspace: coverage holds, 22,188 classified
  edges, unknown 542/2.4%, ABI 383/383 mapped). `EncryptedApp` remains as the failure
  channel: a `.NEA` package whose stream cannot be descrambled (truncated, over the cap,
  not a zip) is named in `payload.summary.encryptedPackages` and counted unreadable for
  that stated reason — a future key or format change surfaces loudly, not as silent
  absence. Format notes: `docs/encrypted-app-packages.md` (rewritten: layout, scramble,
  trailer now identified as an `NXSB` + PKCS#7/CMS code-signing signature, per-package
  contents).
- **`subscriber_arity_bound` saturates on the `UNKNOWN_ARITY` sentinel** (`usize::MAX`,
  the ABI arity sentinel) instead of overflowing: debug panicked
  (`attempt to add with overflow`), release would wrap to 0 and admit every subscriber
  as a Sender match. The two `params_count + 1` comparisons in `resolve::index` use
  `checked_add` for the same reason. Exposed by the runtime-package read (dep routines
  with `parameters_known == false` now reach the event wiring); measured on the 10
  Continia packages, zero real occurrences of the panicking shape (an unknown-arity
  publisher with `IncludeSender: true`), so behavior changes nowhere real.

- **The test runners refuse a zero `RLIMIT_RTTIME`** (`scripts/require-rttime`, called by
  `ci-steps` test/task-affected/perf-bounds, `check-goldens` (so the pre-commit hook)
  and `cdo-gate`). Under a zero realtime timeout the kernel SIGKILLs ordinary test
  processes at random and logs nothing; on 2026-10-27 that read as flaky tests (6 of 8
  full nextest runs lost one to five tests, a different set each time). Cause on that
  Omarchy desktop: rtkit was not installed, so the portal gave PipeWire's `module-rt`
  in the desktop shell a zero budget, applied as a hard limit to everything launched
  from it. Confirmed by bpftrace (`SI_KERNEL` from `posix_cpu_timers_work`) and by
  raising the limit: 0 kills in 9 runs. The script names the cause and the fix. A
  system without `/proc/self/limits` is not checked.

### Changed

- **Grammar: tree-sitter-al v4.5.0** (`91a5db62`, the release tag and `main`; was `main` at
  `940ba71b`). A release-only bump: `grammar.js` and `node-types.json` are unchanged, and
  `src/parser.c` differs only in its version metadata (4.4.1 → 4.5.0), so
  `node-types.sha256`, `kind_policy` and the lowerer did not move.
  `CACHE_VERSION_GRAMMAR` is now `tree-sitter-al-v4.5.0-91a5db62-native` (same length, so
  `dry-run.txt` did not move); `cache_version_grammar_tracks_the_linked_grammar` requires
  the package version in it. The two hand-made cache fixtures carry the new string.
- **Digest `schemaVersion` is 1.8.0** (#353). It adds the `diff-file-not-al` kind and
  narrows `diff-file-unmatched` and `diff-file-deleted` to AL paths (see Fixed). Consumers
  that pin 1.7.0, such as CentralGauge's `ALSEM_SCHEMAS`, must add 1.8.0 before a release
  ships it. Merging this releases nothing: v2.1.1 still ships 1.7.0.
  The 21 cli-b digest JSON goldens and the `one-job` batch golden change only in that line.
  Still unreleased, 1.8.0 also gains the `file-ambiguous` kind (#339, see Fixed). It is
  not purely additive on the file side either: a `--file` that resolved as written can
  now be `file-ambiguous` and give no roots.
- **Digest `--diff-root` now reads file inputs too** (#339). With `--diff-root`, a plain
  `--file` path is read relative to that folder only, as a diff path is. So
  `--diff d --diff-root <repo> --file src/x.al`, with the workspace at `<repo>/Cloud`,
  used to resolve and is now `file-unmatched`; write `Cloud/src/x.al` or `ws:src/x.al`.
  `--diff-root` with only file inputs used to fail (exit 3) and now works. A
  `--diff-root` with no diff and no file input (alone, or with `--routine` only) is still
  exit 3, now with `--diff-root needs a diff or file inputs (--diff, --file or --changed)`.
- **`prove … reaches-ui` asks about interactive UI only** (G18). An `Error` counted as
  UI, which overlapped `throws-error` and was wrong where the error never surfaces:
  Continia DO's `TryGetTerminalField`, a `[TryFunction]`, raises `Error('')` to fail
  softly, and its callers answered `reaches-ui = yes`. `reaches-ui` now means a dialog
  or window a user must see or answer (`Message`, `Confirm`, `StrMenu`, a page or
  report `Run`/`RunModal`, `Hyperlink`); errors are `throws-error`'s question. Stated
  in `alsem prove --help` and the module doc. Test: `cli_prove_reaches_ui` (an
  `Error`-only routine and a `[TryFunction]` answer `no`; `throws-error` still sees
  the error). No golden moved.

### Fixed

- **A table extension's method shadows a same-signature base-table method for
  calls from the extension's own app.** The engine reported such a call as
  `overloadAmbiguous`. The compiler binds it to the extension (alc 18.0.43,
  measured: warning AL0523 "already defines a method … with the same parameter
  types"; with both methods `internal`, the same binding with or without
  `internalsVisibleTo`). From a third app that sees both, it is error AL0196
  "The call is ambiguous", which stays ambiguous. Tables only; page and report
  extensions are unchanged (not measured). Found by loading Continia Approvals
  (29.2.0.242622, from the Continia catalogue with `continia deps download`)
  next to Continia DO: its page extensions call `Rec.GetSalesPurchName()`,
  which both Continia Business Foundation's `CTS-CBF Continia User Setup` and
  Approvals' own table extension declare. With Approvals loaded, DO's
  dependency code resolves completely: 432,906 call edges, 0 unknown, 0
  ambiguous (the one unknown left before, Online Connector calling into
  Approvals, resolves). Test `cli_own_table_extension_method`.

- **An object declared `ObsoleteState = Moved` (or `Removed`) binds no reference
  while another of its name or number is visible.** Base Application keeps
  `table 308 "No. Series"` (and `No. Series Line`, `Source Code Setup`,
  `Reason Code`, …: 8 tables) as `Moved` stubs pointing to Business Foundation,
  under `#if not CLEANSCHEMA27`. For every app seeing both, the name resolved
  to two tables, ambiguous, so `Record "No. Series"` had no table; and Base
  Application's own references bound to its stub through the own-app shadow.
  The index now drops such an object wherever an alternative exists
  (`ObjectNode::obsolete_gone`, pack schema 12; a symbol-only object's state is
  not read yet). Continia DO's dependency-body `ambiguousResolved`: 17 → 15
  (CDN's `InvalidCharsInNoSeries(NoSeriesRec)`). Test
  `cli_moved_table_resolution`.

- **Overload selection: a DotNet argument picks the DotNet `var` overload, and
  framework methods' Integer results type.** Every DotNet type canonicalizes to
  `dotnet`, and the `var` exact-text rule called a `DotNet XmlElement` against
  `var DotNet XmlNode` incompatible, so Base Application's
  `XMLDOMMgt.AddAttribute(DocumentElement, …)` over `(var DotNet XmlNode; …)` /
  `(var XmlNode; …)` lost both candidates (a `var` DotNet parameter takes a
  derived class; two aliases are now undecided). `RecordId.TableNo()`,
  `Count()` of a List/Dictionary/JsonArray and `Text.IndexOf`/`LastIndexOf`
  now type as Integer (`GetIntegrationTableMapping(Mapping,
  RecordID.TableNo())`). An untyped argument no longer stops the pick when
  the typed ones prove every other candidate unable (rule (B) holds without
  it): `XMLDOMMgt.FindNode(DotNetDoc.DocumentElement, Path, Found)`, whose
  first argument is an untyped DotNet member. An object-id reference
  (`Database::Contact`, `Page::"…"`, `Codeunit::"…"`) and an enum value's
  `AsInteger()` type as Integer (`GetIntegrationTableMapping(Mapping,
  DATABASE::Contact)`, `IsValidConnector(Connector.AsInteger())`). Continia DO's
  dependency-body `ambiguousResolved`: 59 → 21. Tests
  `cli_dotnet_var_overload`, `cli_record_integer_builtin_arg`,
  `cli_object_ref_integer_arg`.

- **A Text argument is no proof against a `SecretText` parameter.** Text, Code
  and Label convert into SecretText, but overload selection called the pair
  incompatible. That lost both candidates of `SignedXmlImpl.SetSigningKey(Text)`
  over `(SecretText)` / `(Codeunit "Signature Key")` (now bound to the
  SecretText one), and it picked `AddHeader(Label, Label)`'s `(Text, Text)`
  overload over `(Text, SecretText)` on that false proof (now ambiguous: which
  conversion the compiler prefers is not proven). A `Dictionary`'s / `List`'s
  `Get(..)` argument now types as its declared value type
  (`HttpContent.SetHeader(Key, Headers.Get(Key))` over `(Text, Text)` / `(Text,
  SecretText)`), and an element of a declared array as the element type
  (Continia's `Http.AddRequestHeader(RequestHeaders[i, 1], RequestHeaders[i,
  2])`), and a field-qualified enum value `Rec."Field"::Value` as the field's
  enum (Base Application's `CheckBlockedCustOnJnls(Customer,
  GenJournalLine."Document Type"::Payment, true)` over `(…; Enum …; …)` /
  `(…; var Record …; …)`), and an enum type's `FromInteger(i)` as that enum
  (`ShowComments("Service Comment Line Type".FromInteger(Type))` over `(Option
  …)` / `(Enum …)`), and a report's dataitem passed by name as a record of
  its source table (`ReservMgt.SetReservSource("Prod. Order Component")` over
  `(Variant)` / `(RecordRef)`), and a `+` with a Text literal operand as a
  Text (`AddHeader('Authorization', 'Bearer ' + AccessToken)` over `(Text,
  Text)` / `(Text, SecretText)`). Continia DO's dependency-body
  `ambiguousResolved`: 21 → 17 (→ 11 with the Moved-object fix). Tests
  `cli_secrettext_arg`, `cli_array_param_overload`,
  `cli_object_ref_integer_arg`, `cli_dataitem_name_arg`.

- **The last 11 overload ambiguities in Continia DO's dependency code bind,
  each checked with the AL compiler (alc 18.0.43).** A Text-family argument
  (Text, Code, Label, a text literal) binds an unbounded `Text` parameter over a
  `SecretText` one. This is the one conversion ranking the engine now applies:
  probes whose overloads return different types, with a control assignment
  failing (AL0122), prove it. It settles `AddHeader(Label, Label)` ×2,
  `UrlEncode(Label)` and `VerifyData(Text, Text, …)` over `(Text; SecretText;
  …)` / `(SecretText; SecretText; …)`. Six more fixes:
  - A Variant argument is never proven incompatible (it converts into every
    parameter type probed, by value and `var`). A Variant next to typed
    arguments now decides by elimination instead of declining:
    `WordTemplates.Merge(DataVariant, SplitDocuments, …)` ×2. Before, a Variant
    into a `Dictionary` parameter counted as incompatible, which was wrong.
  - A DotNet value is proven apart, both ways, only from AL objects (Record,
    Codeunit, Interface) and AL's wrapper types (Xml*, Json*, Http*, List,
    TextBuilder, RecordRef). Simple values and streams stay undecided:
    `DotNet MemoryStream` converts into OutStream, `DotNet String` with Text.
    That binds `SaveZipArchive(MemoryStream)` over `(OutStream)` / `(var
    Codeunit "Temp Blob")`.
  - The Integer-literal guard ignores a candidate another position already
    rules out: `AddBlobPutContentHeaders(…, BlobType::AppendBlob, 0, …)`.
  - A member call whose same-arity overloads all return one type is that type:
    `CreateFile(…, Helper.GetContentLength(InStream), …)`.
  - An interface method's result is its declared return type:
    `SetFunctionAsToolChoice(Function.GetName())`.
  - `CreateGuid()` is a Guid: `Convert.ToBase64(CreateGuid())`.
  Continia DO's dependency-body `ambiguousResolved`: 11 → 0, `resolvedSource`
  +11, no other count moved. Test `cli_overload_last_ambiguities`.

- **A RecordRef write behind `if not R.FieldExist(N) then exit;` writes only a
  table that has field `N`** (G36). Continia DO's `UpdateHandledFields(var
  FilterRecord: RecordRef)` modifies whatever table it holds, so `prove …
  writes-table` had an `unknown-table-write` for every table. Past its
  `FieldExist(6175274)` guard, only tables a DO extension gives that field
  (Sales Header and the other documents) can be written: such a table's
  question now answers `yes`, and a table the workspace declares without the
  field `no` (a dependency's table keeps the blocker: an extension of it in
  another loaded app may not be in the model). The guard must be a top-level
  statement and the RecordRef not rebound after it (`GetTable`, `Open`,
  `Copy`, `Close`, passed on, assigned). 15 of the HandledState slice's
  unknowns decide (`engine::l5::field_guard`). Test
  `cli_prove_field_guarded_write`.

- **A table extension's fields reach its base table when a table shares the
  extension's number.** The model's extension-field merge looked the
  extension's stub up by its id (`app/table/<extension number>`) and took the
  LAST row of that id: a real table of the same number when it came later.
  Continia DO's `CDOSalesHeaderExt` (6175275) and its table 6175275 `CDO
  E-Mail Template Merge Field`: Sales Header got that table's fields and lost
  the extension's (G-5). The merge now takes the stub, and a base is a real
  table. Pinned by `cli_prove_field_guarded_write`.

- **`Page.Run(0, Rec)` on a dependency's table runs that table's lookup page**
  (G37). Only a workspace table's `LookupPageId` was known, so Continia DO's
  `Page.Run(0, TempServDocLog)` on Base Application's `Service Document Log`
  (`LookupPageID = "Service Document Log"`) was a dynamic run and `prove`'s
  `unresolved-callsite`. Every table with source now carries its
  `LookupPageId` (`ObjectNode::lookup_pages`, pack schema 11), joined with the
  loaded table extensions of it; a symbol-only table's is not read yet. Test
  `cli_dependency_lookup_page_run`.

- **An array parameter takes part in overload selection.** Argument typing read
  `array[8] of Text[100]` as a malformed generic clause (`of` with no `[..]`),
  so an array parameter was untyped and degraded every overload pick of its
  name: Base Application's `VendorRemitToAddress(Rec, array[8] of Text[100])` /
  `(Rec, Record "Remit Address Buffer")` stayed `ambiguousResolved` for both
  argument kinds. An array now types as its dimensions plus element type; it
  never binds a non-array (nor the other way round), and two different arrays
  stay undecided. A symbol parameter's `ArrayDimensions` were dropped too (its
  text is the element type), so a symbol array parameter looked scalar; they are
  now read (`AbiParamRetained::array_dims`, pack schema 10). Argument types
  never choose between two `#if` alternatives (candidates that exist in no
  common build): only one is compiled, and the other build binds the other one
  (`overload_candidates_are_narrowed_to_the_call_sites_build`, which array
  typing would otherwise have broken). Test `cli_array_param_overload`.

- **A record's `FieldNo(..)` / `Count()` argument is an Integer in overload
  selection.** Base Application's `AddAllowedTable(Database::"…",
  Log.FieldNo(SystemCreatedAt))` over `(Integer, Integer)` / `(Integer,
  JsonArray)` stayed ambiguous. Test `cli_record_integer_builtin_arg`. With the
