  array fix, Continia DO's dependency-body `ambiguousResolved`: 86 → 59.

- **A dependency page's `CurrPage.<usercontrol>` call resolves against an add-in
  its package declares only in symbols.** Continia's CDN embeds
  `usercontrol(RefreshTimer; "CTS-CDN Refresh Timer")` and calls
  `CurrPage.RefreshTimer.Schedule(..)`, but ships no `controladdin` `.al`. A
  dependency with source took no objects from its symbols, so the add-in was
  missing (`compoundReceiver`). It now takes the control add-ins its source
  lacks (an add-in has no AL body, so its symbols say all source would). And a
  symbol add-in was read with no procedures at all, so every call to one was
  `memberNotFound`; its `Methods` are now its procedures (its `Events`, as in
  source, are none). Test `cli_dependency_symbol_control_addin`.

- **A symbol-only method with no parameters is called with none.** The compiler
  leaves an empty array out of `SymbolReference.json`, so such a method has no
  `Parameters` key (BC 29's Base Application: 7211 methods so, one
  `"Parameters": []`). Ingestion read the missing key as an unknown arity, which
  no call matches: every 0-argument call into a symbol-only package was an
  `arityMismatch` unknown, and those methods had no symbol method id. Continia
  DO's dependency-body unknowns: 41 → 2 (the 38 `arityMismatch` calls into
  Microsoft's `System` package, e.g. `AgentUtilities.
  BlockPageFromBeingOpenedByAgent()`, and the `compoundReceiver` `.Get` on
  `IndexManagement.GetSupportedOptimizedTextSearchLanguages()`). Earlier notes
  called these 38 a platform version skew; the symbols declare every one. Test
  `cli_parameterless_symbol_method`.

- **A write with no known table is never hidden in a dependency group, nor shown
  at another write.** Digest's producer-proof search matched facts with
  `fact_equivalent`, which treats a missing resource as equal to any, so an
  unresolved table write was proved by a typed parameter-bound producer's path:
  `prove`'s `unknown-table-write` blockers pointed at a typed insert (Continia DO:
  three anchored at a `CDO File` insert). Proved at its own operation, such a
  write inside a dependency is a boundary group's, and a group listed only the
  resources its facts name, so the write vanished and `prove` could answer `no`
  past it. A group now counts them (`detail.unresolvedResources`), and `prove`
  blocks on such a group. Test
  `an_unknown_table_write_is_never_witnessed_by_a_typed_producer`.
- **`ModuleInfo.Id()`/`PackageId()` return `Guid`, `Name()`/`Publisher()` `Text`**
  (`framework_returns`). System Application's
  `IsCapabilityRegistered(Capability, CallerModuleInfo.Id())` and
  `IsCapabilityActive(…, CallerModuleInfo.Id())` stayed ambiguous between their
  `ModuleInfo` and `Guid` overloads. Test
  `record_builtin_and_enum_list_results_pick_overloads`.
- **Framework and RecordRef call results type an argument.** A framework method's
  call result (`Token.AsValue()`) types as the kind it returns, and so does a
  framework call on one (`Token.AsValue().AsText()`); a `RecordRef`/`FieldRef`
  method with parentheses (`RecRef.Number()`) as its parens-less form. Continia
  CDN's `SetSeverity(SeverityToken.AsValue().AsText())` and
  `IsSalesDocument(RecordRef.Number())` no longer stay `ambiguousResolved`. Test
  `record_builtin_and_enum_list_results_pick_overloads`.
- **An XmlPort's `Export`/`Import`/`Run` is a multicast over every trigger it
  reaches.** With no extension mechanism, the entry dispatch was `Exact` whenever
  it had any route, so an xmlport run reaching `OnPreXmlPort` and its elements'
  triggers read as an ambiguous overload set and `prove` blocked on it (Base
  Application's `ICOutboxImpExpXML.Export()`). Test
  `an_xmlport_export_reaches_all_its_triggers`.
- **Two more call results type an argument.** A record's platform method
  (`Line.RecordId()`) types as its documented return, and an enum value's
  `Names.Get(i)`/`Ordinals.Get(i)` as `Text`/`Integer`: Business Foundation's
  `AddAction(ErrorInfo, NoSeriesLine.RecordId(), …)` and System Application's
  `SetHttpMethod(Method.Names.Get(…))` no longer stay `ambiguousResolved`. Test
  `record_builtin_and_enum_list_results_pick_overloads`.
- **A report dataitem or xmlport table element named as a receiver is a record
  operation.** The body pass took only globals, parameters and locals as record
  receivers, so `"Job Ledger Entry".Modify()` from a nested dataitem's trigger, or
  `ICOutboxTrans.Insert()` on a table element, became a call the model could not
  type: `digest` listed it `unresolved-receiver-type` and `prove` blocked on it
  (Base Application's Update Job Item Cost; IC Outbox Imp/Exp: 25 such rows on one
  Continia DO claim, now 0). A dataitem's `UseTemporary = true` is now read
  (`ObjectDecl::temporary_dataitems`), so its record is temporary. A quoted
  receiver (`"My Rec".Insert()`) missed its record variable in the record typing,
  which compared the raw text with the logical name, so its table and temp state
  stayed unknown. Test `dataitem_record_ops_are_record_operations`.
- **A synthesized global the C# exposes as a property is declared and called by
  its AL name.** The runtime stores such a global in a backing field `δx` and
  reads it as `this.x`, so the global was declared `"δx"` and every call on it
  stayed `__alsem_untranslated('untyped …')` (98 Continia Core files; its
  `processingWindow.Open`). `ALFieldExists` is `RecordRef.FieldExist`. Extraction
  scheme 6. Continia DO's dependency-body unknown call edges: 44 → 41 (Continia
  Core: 0). Test `keeps_generic_types_and_member_paths`.
- **G28 closes a dependency's internal interfaces too.** An interface declared
  `Access = Internal` in any app with source closes its dispatch when every friend
  that app's manifest lists is loaded; before, only the workspace's own did.
  Continia CDN's internal `IEndpointCreator`, `IPartyIdentificationCreator` and
  `IPartyTaxSchemeCreator`, held in locals filled from factory getters, were
  dispatched open-world from CDN's own code (the `CTS-CDN Party Type` path of
  `IPartyInformationCreator` stays open: that enum is extensible). An object's
  `Access = Internal` is now `ObjectNode::internal`; `PACK_SCHEMA` 9. Test
  `a_dependencys_internal_interface_with_every_friend_loaded_is_closed`.
- **Three more argument shapes pick an overload.** The C6 literal gate degraded a
  call whenever a `Code` candidate faced a text literal, even when the rival took
  an `Integer` that cannot take the literal at all; it now guards only a choice
  still open (Continia DO's `EMailLog.InitNewEntry(…, '', …)`). A table's own
  field named bare types as the field (Base Application's
  `Cust.CheckBlockedCustOnJnls(Cust, "Document Type", false)`). A `RecordRef`/
  `FieldRef` member without parentheses (`Number`, `Name`, `Caption`, …) types as
  its documented return, on a variable or a call result (Continia CDN's
  `IsPurchaseDocument(RecRef.Number)`). Test
  `literals_own_fields_and_ref_members_pick_overloads`.
- **Calls by method id reach dependency routines whose id a signature cannot
  give.** A dependency's source routine now takes the id its app's
  `SymbolReference.json` declares (`RoutineNode::abi_method_id`), matched by
  object, name and arity, then by parameter types among overloads. A
  `Dictionary`/`List` parameter's part of the id cannot be computed (Continia
  Core's calls to Continia System Application's
  `GetDictionary(var Dictionary of [Text, Text])`). A `[TryFunction]` that declares
  no return value hashes a `Boolean` return, as the compiler does (System
  Application's `Uri.IsValidUri(Text)`, `TryInitializeFromCurrentApp()`).
  `PACK_SCHEMA` 8. Tests `dependency_source_routines_take_their_symbol_method_ids`,
  `synthesized_calls_bind_by_method_id`.
- **AL synthesized from transpiled C# keeps a call's member path and generic
  types.** `webResponse.ALContent.ALReadAs(…)` was written `"webResponse".ReadAs(…)`
  (no such method) and `client.ALDefaultRequestHeaders.ALAdd` became
  `"client".Add`; they now read `.Content().ReadAs(…)` and
  `.DefaultRequestHeaders().Add(…)`. A comma inside a generic type
  (`NavDictionary<NavText, NavText>`) split the scope's locals and the call's
  arguments, so a Dictionary local was declared `Text`. `ALLoadFrom` is
  `HttpContent.WriteFrom`, and an option's `Names()`/`Ordinals()` chain reads only
  metadata. Extraction scheme 5. Continia DO's dependency-body unknown call edges:
  91 → 44 (with the method-id fix above; 38 of the 44 are the System Application
  source/symbols version gap). Test `keeps_generic_types_and_member_paths`.
- **Two more argument shapes pick an overload.** A value of a built-in option type
  (`TextEncoding::UTF8`, `Verbosity::Normal`; `arg_dispatch::BUILTIN_OPTION_TYPES`)
  types as that type, so System Application's
  `TempBlob.CreateInStream(TextEncoding::UTF8)` no longer stays `ambiguousResolved`
  with `CreateInStream(var InStream)`. A framework variable's member without
  parentheses (`Response.Content`) types as the kind it returns, when that kind's
  name is an AL type. Test `builtin_option_values_and_framework_members_type_arguments`.
- **A negative synthesized method id no longer breaks the file's parse.** The
  grammar takes no negative number as an attribute argument, so `[MethodId(-5)]`
  made the whole synthesized file `Recovered` and every object in it
  parse-incomplete. Half of all method ids are negative. A parse-incomplete object
  is not read as loaded source, so a run of a codeunit with no `OnRun` stayed
  `external` instead of running nothing (Continia Core: `"databaseReader".Run()` on
  `CSC DB Reader`). The id is now written quoted, `[MethodId('-5')]`, and read either
  way. Extraction scheme 4. Tests `a_negative_method_id_keeps_the_file_clean`,
  `method_id_attribute_is_the_declared_id`, `synthesized_calls_bind_by_method_id`.
- **Synthesized runtime code binds by the runtime's own method ids.** AL synthesized
  from a transpiled package (`snapshot::transpiled`) now writes `[MethodId(n)]` on
  every routine whose id the symbols or the C# give, and the resolver takes a
  declared id over the one it computes from the signature
  (`RoutineMeta::method_id`). A routine only the C# declares (a `local procedure`)
  got its signature from C# types, where an enum parameter shows as `NavOption`
  (declared `Integer`), so its computed id was wrong and every `"__alsem_mid_<n>"`
  call to it stayed unresolved (Continia Core: `CSC Licensing.GetLicenseState`,
  `__alsem_mid_1859663910`). Extraction scheme 3 (`EXTRACTION_SCHEME`). Continia DO's
  dependency-body unknown call edges: 214 → 91. Tests
  `synthesized_calls_bind_by_method_id`, `method_id_attribute_is_the_declared_id`.
- **`Page.Run(0, Rec)` runs the lookup page of `Rec`'s table.** Page `0` is the
  table's `LookupPageId` (or one a table extension sets); with none, the platform
  shows a page of its own, which runs no AL code. The run was dynamic
  (`Page.Run(<dynamic>)`), which `prove` and every cone blocked on. For a record of a
  workspace table it now reaches that page's lifecycle triggers, or nothing (the
  model's `Builtin` run); `Partial`, since a table extension outside the program may
  set another page (`ProgramGraph::lookup_pages`, `resolve::full::zero_page_table`).
  Continia DO: `CDO E-Mail Log.ShowLog`. Test `cli_lookup_page_run`.
- **A Variant's type tests resolve.** `V.IsRecord()`, `V.IsGuid()` and the other `Is…`
  methods of the AL `Variant` type are platform built-ins with no AL code behind
  them, whatever the Variant holds; a Variant receiver made every member call an open
  dynamic site, so `prove` blocked on them (Continia DO: `RecVariant.IsRecord`,
  `ReferenceVariant.IsGuid`, … across 7 claims). They are now catalog members
  (`resolver::VARIANT_TYPE_TESTS`); any other member stays dynamic. Test
  `cli_variant_type_tests`.
- **`publishes-event` evidence cites the publish call** (G32). An event publication is
  the publisher routine's own fact, with no operation to cite, so its evidence read
  `sourceKind: unavailable` (35 proven answers on Continia DO had no file or line).
  Its anchor is now the call into the publisher, the last hop of its shortest witness
  path. Test `cli_prove_event_anchor`.
- **A known-temporary write the root's L4 summary has no row for says so.** A DB
  effect's `tempState` is joined from the root's L4 rows; with none (a dependency
  root, a write inside a dependency boundary group) it was absent, so `prove` counted
  a temporary record as a table write (from `Sales-Calc. Discount.OnRun`:
  `TempCustLedgEntry.DeleteAll` as a `Cust. Ledger Entry` write). The cone fact's own
  class is frame-correct (#69 D1), so a known-temporary one is now `known(true)`;
  any other class stays absent. Test `cli_dependency_roots`.
- **A record of a namespace-qualified type writes its table, and a write to a table
  that is not known rules out `writes-table`'s `no`.** The model's record-type parse
  (`record_types::record_table_name_of`) took a qualified type's whole dotted path as
  the table name (`Record Microsoft.Manufacturing.Capacity."Capacity Ledger Entry"`,
  as Base Application 29 declares records throughout), so no table resolved and the
  record's writes named none; receiver typing already read the last segment. And a
  write that names no table was no match for any table, so `writes-table:T` answered
  `no` past it: unsound for the qualified record and for a RecordRef opened on a
  computed number. Such a write now blocks `no` (`unknown-table-write`), unless it is
  known to write a temporary record. Test `cli_prove_table_writes`.
- **A page, report or XMLport run reaches its whole lifecycle, and a run with none
  runs no AL code.** A run followed one entry trigger (`OnOpenPage`, `OnPreReport`,
  `OnPreXmlPort`), so a `no` could miss a write or Commit in `OnAfterGetRecord`,
  `OnQueryClosePage` or a report's dataitem triggers (d35's filed limit D3a). It now
  reaches every trigger a run runs with no user acting on a control
  (`resolver::run_triggers`): a page's `OnInit`, `OnOpenPage`, `OnFindRecord`,
  `OnNextRecord`, `OnAfterGetRecord`, `OnAfterGetCurrRecord`, `OnNewRecord`,
  `OnQueryClosePage`, `OnClosePage` and background-task triggers; a report's
  `OnInitReport`/`OnPreReport`/`OnPostReport` and its dataitems'
  `OnPreDataItem`/`OnAfterGetRecord`/`OnPostDataItem`; an XMLport's object and
  element triggers. A user's action (`OnAction`, a field's `OnValidate`, record
  edits) stays under `platformEntryPointsNotModelled`, as do page parts. A run of an
  object whose source is loaded and declares none of these runs no AL code: the
  model's edge is `Builtin`, still naming the object (it was `Opaque`, an unresolved
  run that `prove` and every cone blocked on). Continia DO: `ImportLines.RunModal`,
  `DialogLanguage.RunModal` (a PromptDialog declaring only `OnQueryClosePage`).
- **A computed `Page.RunModal(<n>)` (keyword member form) makes the cone partial.**
  The combined graph turned only the `Codeunit.Run(<n>)` callee shape into an
  unresolved object run; `Page.RunModal(<n>)`, `Report.Run(<n>)` were skipped, so a
  cone through one counted as complete and d35 reported nothing
  (`combined_graph::keyword_run_kind`). `prove` already blocked on it. Tests
  `cli_d35_unknown_commit` V6, V7.
- **An operation on a table of no known resource is no witness of a table's effect.**
  The digest's witness search (`digest::is_bfs_carrier`) accepted any direct fact of
  the same operation whose resource is unknown as the carrier of an inherited fact
  that names a table (`fact_equivalent`'s one-sided leniency). Such an ordinary fact
  never becomes one naming a table at a caller (only the producer solve binds one),
  so it was a false witness: on Continia DO a temporary `RecRef.Insert` was shown
  writing 156 tables, among them `Cust. Ledger Entry`, that dependency boundaries
  below it write. Each effect is now witnessed by its own producer or boundary.
  Test `cli_digest_include_reads` (its G-1 fixture had relied on the shared witness).
- **A local RecordRef opened only temporary is temporary in a routine that branches.**
  The RecordRef temp-state pass (`record_types`) needed a routine with no branching.
  A LOCAL RecordRef whose every `Open` is `Open(_, true)`, with no `GetTable`/`Copy`,
  no assignment to it and never passed on, holds a temporary table on every path (an
  op before any `Open` is a runtime error, not a write), so its ops are now
  `known(true)`. Continia DO: `TryMatchTypedFilter`'s `RecRef.Insert` on `CDO Typed
  Value Buffer`. Test `cli_recordref_open_temporary`.
- **An implicit `Rec`/`xRec` argument is typed, so the overload it picks resolves.**
  An undeclared `Rec`/`xRec` passed to a call was untyped, so an overload set over
  record types stayed ambiguous: Continia DO's `LineAttachment.SetTemplateFilter(xRec)`
  in a table's `OnDelete`. It is now the object's implicit record, as the `Rec.Field`
  argument arm already typed it (`receiver::infer_implicit_rec`). Test
  `cli_implicit_rec_argument`.
- **A `this.Global` argument is typed, so the overload it picks resolves.** Argument
  typing (`arg_dispatch::type_one_arg`) read a bare identifier, a literal and
  `Rec.Field`, but not `this.X`, which names an object global only. A call
  overloaded on that argument stayed an ambiguous pair: Continia CDN's
  `this.Utilities.IsPurchaseDocument(this.CreationFactory)` (overloaded on
  `Codeunit` against `Integer`) blocked 30 cone rows of DO claims. Several `#if`
  declarations of the global leave it untyped. Test `cli_this_argument`.
- **One routine id and declared line bases across `graph`, `fingerprint` and
  `prove`** (G13), so a consumer can join their outputs.
  - `alsem graph` nodes carry `stableRoutineId`, the id the other commands use, on
    every routine with source. It is minted from the graph's own declaration data
    (the same `RoutineDecl` fields the model mints it from), so the export builds no
    model. It matches the model's id for all 5488 routines of Continia DO. Omitted on
    symbol-only and synthetic nodes; the 5 `OnOpenPageEvent` nodes with no
    `sourcePath` are platform publishers the engine synthesizes (`synthetic: true`),
    so they have no declaration and no location by design.
  - `routineInventory` rows carry `arity` and `sourceAnchor`, the same anchor `prove`
    reports as `routine.anchor`.
  - Each document states its line base: graph `meta.lineBase: 1` (as its schema
    always said), prove and fingerprint-inventory `payload.lineBase: 0`. A graph
    node's `line` is the inventory anchor's line + 1.

  These are additive; the graph schema doc lists the new fields. The three
  base-minted goldens that are never regenerated (`single-app/inventory.dd.json`,
  `cross-app/inventory.two-onruns.json`, `single-app/prove.dd.CallChain.may-commit
  .json`) were updated after checking that each differs from its old content only by
  these keys. Test: `cli_ids_and_line_bases` (overloads and a field trigger; it fails
  with the graph's member discriminator off).
  - `events fanout` entries carry `publisherStableRoutineId` next to `publisher`
    (the event graph's own `<16 hex>/<64 hex>` routine id), the last output G13
    named. The `cli-c-events` fanout goldens gain only that key (19 entries, all
    filled). Test: `cli_ids_and_line_bases::events_fanout_names_publishers_by_the_
    shared_id`.
- **`fingerprint --inventory-only` without `--format` emits json** (G12). Its help
  says it implies `--format=json`, but an omitted format resolved to `human`, and the
  command failed with "--inventory-only requires --format=json (got Human)".
  `default_format` now takes `inventory_only`: omitted means json, while an explicit
  non-json format is still refused. Test: `cli_fingerprint_inventory_format` (the real
  binary, both cases).
- **`prove` evidence lists no witness path that cannot run** (G23 follow-up). The
  witness search took the shortest path to an effect. Through a recursive SCC that
  could be one dead under a literal argument (Continia DO's `DocSave` →
  `RunReport(false)` → `if UseQueue then QueueMail`), although the effect is reached
  by a longer live path. Each listed path is now replayed with `literal_reach`'s
  rules (`path_live`) and dropped when a hop's guard contradicts what the call chain
  binds. When that leaves an effect with no listed path, `viaPathsTruncated` is set,
  because a live path exists that was not listed. Test: `cli_prove_dead_paths`
  `DocBoth` (fails with the replay off, and with the truncation flag off).
- **Calls into Microsoft's `Base64Convert` platform codeunit have known behaviour.**
  `Base64Convert` (codeunit 2000000024 of the `System` symbol package) is `[Native]`:
  there is no AL body, so a call was an `unfetched-dependency`, an opaque cone. The
  package also made its app a `symbol-only-boundary` analysis gap. Together they kept
  `prove … no` at `unknown` (35 call sites in Continia DO's claim cones, reached through
  System Application's `Base64 Convert Impl.`). `program::model::platform_natives` is
  now a curated catalog. `[Native]` alone is not enough: `Agent Utilities.
  DeleteCustomAgent` or `Index Management.DisableKey` have effects, so only methods
  whose behaviour is known are listed. A cataloged routine has no database, UI or commit
  effect; `FromBase64` keeps an implicit error (a malformed string). The same predicate
  serves all four places that saw the routine as opaque: its direct facts in the cone,
  its call sites (`resolved`, not `unfetched-dependency`), the gap derivation, and the
  gap count's app-prefix match. On DO with BC 29's `System` symbols added to
  `.alpackages`, 19 of the 39 claims a Base64 call blocked now answer `no`, all as
  expected. Test: `cli_prove_platform_natives` (an uncataloged native stays opaque; it
  fails with an empty catalog, and with the gap exemption off).
- **`prove` follows literal Boolean arguments through recursive SCCs** (G23). The
  cone's `param_guard` drops a fact behind `if P then` when every path binds `P` to the
  opposite literal, but only through a non-recursive singleton SCC: a recursive SCC
  shares one cone, so its members' requirements were dropped and a write behind
  `if UseQueue then` counted for a caller passing `false`. On Continia DO, `RunReport`
  and `RunReportID` sit in a 489-routine recursive SCC. `literal_reach` now runs, for
  `prove`'s read, a per-root reachability over the snapshot's own edges. Its state is a
  routine plus the known literal values of its usable guard parameters (the cone's own
  frames). A direct call binds a literal or forwards a known parameter; every other edge
  kind binds nothing. An effect counts as unreachable only when every origin operation's
  routine is reached with guards ignored but never with its own requirements met. A
  graph or id mismatch never drops an effect, and the search gives up (drops nothing)
  past 400,000 states. The two DO claims the peer named stay `yes`, correctly as a MAY:
  `DocSave` also reaches `DocHandle(true)` through `Codeunit.Run("Sales-Calc. Discount")`
  → a Sales Line `OnDelete` → the approval workflow's `ExecuteResponses` →
  `Sales-Post` → DO's `OnAfterFinalizePosting` subscriber. Test: `cli_prove_dead_paths`
  (the recursive case answered `yes` before; it fails with the mark ignored; controls
  for a literal `true`, the root's own parameter, a reassigned parameter and one passed
  to a `var`).
- **An enum value qualified by an enum VARIABLE, or written `Enum::"X"::V`, types as
  the enum** (G27), so an overloaded call binds the Enum overload, as the compiler does
  (alc/altool 18.0.43.1464, `graph extract`: `EI(K::Open)` with `K: Enum "SV Kind"`
  and `EI(Enum::"SV Kind"::Open)` both bind `EI(Enum)` over `EI(Integer)`). Only an
  unshadowed `"X"::V` was typed, so BaseApp's
  `PriceSourceList.Add(SourceType::"All Customers")` (`SourceType: Enum "Price Source
  Type"`, overloads `Add(Enum)` / `Add(Record "Price Source")`) stayed
  `ambiguous`. That was 65 unresolved rows in 5 of Continia DO's prove claims, all gone
  (the claims still have other blockers). The same `K::V` shape now also closes an
  interface site over a closed enum (`closed_enum::value_enum`). An Option variable's
  `K::A` stays an option value (untyped), as before. Tests: the S9.5c enum-value
  harness test and closed-enum T3, each failing with its arm removed.
- **`prove … reaches-ui` counts client file dialogs and progress windows** (G26, a
  regression G18 exposed). `UploadIntoStream`, `DownloadFromStream`, `Upload` and
  `Download` (bare, or on `File` as a keyword or a `File` variable) and `Open` /
  `Update` on a `Dialog` variable produced no effect at all. Routines reaching one
  answered `yes` only through an `Error` on the same path, which G18 stopped counting
  as UI, so they turned into a confident wrong `no`. They are now the capability ops
  `ui-file-dialog` / `ui-progress`, effects `UI_FILE_DIALOG` / `UI_PROGRESS`. One
  classifier (`ui_dialog_call`) serves the body extractor and the capability cone. They
  are their own types, so the ordering engine's `UI_WINDOW_OPEN` grading does not
  change. On Continia DO, 1 of 73 `reaches-ui` claims moved
  (EMAIL-TPLM-010.c2, `no` → `yes` through `UploadIntoStream`) and none contradicts
  its expectation. Test: `cli_prove_reaches_ui` (bare, `File.`, `Dialog`, transitive,
  and an `Update` on a codeunit variable as control). It fails when the cone drops the
  facts, and when the `Dialog` receiver check is dropped.
- **`prove … writes-table` resolves a caller-dependent write through the callers**
  (G25). A write to a `var` record parameter, or a table method's own `Rec`, whose
  temporariness is the caller's (G17b) answered `unknown`. It is now asked in the
  frames of the routine's callers in the loaded world (the same L4 temp-state join,
  for the caller's id), climbing up to 6 levels while it stays caller-dependent: a
  caller that passes a record not known temporary makes it `yes`, and the evidence
  names that caller (`viaCaller: {stableId, display}`). With no caller, or when every
  caller passes a temporary record, it stays `unknown` with
  `temp-state-depends-on-caller`: the routine may still be called from outside the
  world. On Continia DO, 5 of the 14 claims this blocked are now `yes` via a named
  caller; the other 9 are three methods of obsolete tables that nothing calls and a
  `ZipFiles` whose only caller passes a temporary record. Test:
  `cli_prove_temp_writes` (a `var` parameter, a table method on its own `Rec`, a
  callee only ever given a temporary record), which fails with the walk off.
- **A truncated witness no longer blocks a decided `prove` answer** (G22). Any effect
  whose via paths were capped (or whose evidence anchor was unavailable) made every
  question `unknown` with `witness-truncated`. Truncation caps how many paths an
  effect lists; the effect stays listed, so it cannot hide a match: a MAY question's
  `no` now stands. The MUST question (`commits-on-success-path`) judges
  "unconditional" over a COMMIT's paths, so it still blocks, but only on a COMMIT whose
  own paths were cut short. On Continia DO, all 18 claims whose only blocker this was
  are now decided (`no`). Tests: `prove` unit tests
  `a_truncated_witness_does_not_block_a_may_no`,
  `a_truncated_commit_still_blocks_the_must_question`,
  `evidence_unavailable_does_not_block_a_may_no` (the two old tests pinned the
  blocker on `may-commit`).
- **`prove … throws-error` sees implicit runtime errors** (G20). Only an explicit
  `Error` counted, so Continia DO's `CDO E-Mail.Init`, whose unguarded `DOSetup.Get();`
  raises an error when the setup record is missing, answered `no`. A record lookup
  whose Boolean is discarded (`Get`, `FindFirst`, `FindLast`, `FindSet` in statement
  position), `TestField` and `FieldError` on a record now give an `error-implicit` fact
  (`ERROR_IMPLICIT` effect), from one shared rule in both extractors
  (`implicit_error_record_op`, `implicit_error_call`); record operations carry
  `in_statement_position` as call sites do. Their own op, not `error-throw`: the
  ordering engine and the detectors read `error-throw` as an explicit `Error`, and DO's
  findings did not move (2,203). Only `throws-error` counts both. `if X.Get(...)`, an
  `HttpClient.Get` statement and other non-record calls give none; `Codeunit.Run` is
  left to the run codeunit's own errors (a caught `if Codeunit.Run` is not modelled).
  Goldens: 192 files gain the facts (an r3a3 HTTP fact's `extra` keys were also
  re-ordered, values unchanged); the `l2cap` vectors gain two expected facts; the
  never-regenerated split record `full-snapshot.r5b.cross-app` was re-minted through the
  new explicit `REMINT_SPLIT_RECORDS=1` (its `RECORD` says why; the diff is the one new
  fact); the R3a-3 manifest gains the 146 facts (127 direct, 19 inherited); the policy
  facts oracle, whose recorder is gone, was re-recorded through the new
  `REMINT_POLICY_FACTS_ORACLE=1` (118 of 446 cases gain facts, none loses one).
  DO: all four claims now `yes`, with the lookup or `TestField` as evidence. Test:
  `cli_prove_throws_error::throws_error_sees_implicit_runtime_errors` (guarded lookups
  and `HttpClient.Get` are controls).
- **`Rename` is a table write in the digest and `prove`** (G19). The capability
  facts had it (op `rename`), but the digest's effect taxonomy had no entry for it,
  so it was no effect at all and `writes-table` answered a confident `no` for
  Continia DO's `CDO Document Template Line.OnRename` (`MovedLineAttachment.Rename(...)`).
  It is now a `DB_MODIFY` (a rename rewrites the row's key; the evidence keeps the
  `.Rename`), so it also gets the temp-state rule (G17) and the ordering engine's
  write handling. No golden moved; both DO claims now `yes` with the rename as
  evidence. Test: `cli_prove_temp_writes` (a persistent and a temporary rename).
- **`prove … writes-table` does not count temporary records** (G17, G17b). It matched
  every DB write by table, so a write to a record declared `temporary` or on a
  `SourceTableTemporary` page answered `yes`. It now reads each write's `tempState`
  (#65, joined in the asked routine's own frame): a write that is `known(true)` on
  every path is no table write; a write to a `var` record parameter whose state is the
  caller's (`parameter-dependent`, nothing known persistent) answers `unknown` with
  the new blocker `temp-state-depends-on-caller` when nothing else decides it, while
  a caller passing a temporary record sees `known(true)` and gets `no`. On Continia
  DO, the 8 claims this contradicted: 2 are now `no` as claimed, 6 `unknown` (other
  open blockers), none `yes`. Tests: `cli_prove_temp_writes::writes_table_skips_temporary_records`
  (each rule removed alone fails it); `cli_implicit_trigger_cone::a3_temporary_receiver_stays_non_physical`
  now pins `no` (it pinned `yes` with the temporary write as evidence).
- **A source-folder dependency includes its module folders** (G21). G4 first read a
  folder without the folders under it that hold their own `app.json`, to keep nested
  test apps out. In BC.History those are the app's modules, so most of Base and System
  Application was missing: calls such as `ConfirmManagement.GetResponseOrDefault`,
  `NoSeries.GetNextNo` and `FeatureTelemetry.LogUsage` stayed `objectNotInGraph`. The
  folder is now walked whole, like the workspace; test apps sit beside the app's
  folder. On Continia DO with the four BC.History roots, `primaryScoped` unknown edges
  283 → 19 (real-unknown rate 1.35 % → 0.09 %; 726 with no sources). Test:
  `cli_source_dependencies::a_source_folder_dependency_resolves_with_its_modules_not_its_tests`
  (BC.History's layout: a module inside the app folder, a test app beside it), which
  fails with the old walk.
- **`alsem batch` with many `prove`/`digest` jobs no longer grows per job** (G16).
  Every tree job on a view composed its own tree in the view's one `prepare`, and
  each tree is a whole-program snapshot: a derive per job, and each job's result
  kept its own copy of the tree's identity table and coverage until the job ran.
  Over Continia DO with Base Application's source (G4), 408 `prove` jobs passed 40 GB
  with no output after ten minutes. Now consecutive `Effects` readers with the same
  flags (not `--tests`) share ONE tree over the union of their roots, answered by ONE
  digest query (`digest_effects_each`), and share the two tables (`DigestEffects`
  holds them by `Arc`). A root's entries and cones are those of its own tree
  (`prove_scoped_equals_unscoped`). Measured on that workspace (release-fast,
  `reaches-ui` jobs): 10 jobs 45 s / 4.4 GB → 28 s / 3.5 GB, 40 jobs 175 s / 10.1 GB →
  33 s / 4.2 GB peak, every output byte-identical to the old binary's. Test:
  `cli_batch_plan::batch_prove_jobs_share_one_tree` (one tree, each job equal to its
  standalone run; without the grouping it builds two). `batch_counters_one_per_view`'s
  second digest now shares the first's tree (snap 2 → 1).
- **`prove … reaches-ui` sees pages and reports opening, and `Hyperlink`** (G15). It
  counted only `UI_MESSAGE`, `UI_CONFIRM` and `UI_ERROR`, so the `UI_WINDOW_OPEN` the
  digest already had for `Page.Run`/`RunModal`, `Report.Run`/`RunModal` and `StrMenu`
  was ignored: Continia DO's `CDO Signature FactBox` field trigger `OnDrillDown`
  (`Page.Run(Page::"CDO E-Mail Signature List", Signature)`) answered `no` with
  complete coverage claimed. `Run()` on a Page- or Report-typed variable produced no
  UI fact at all (only `RunModal` did), in both the cone's and the body's extractor.
  And `Hyperlink(url)` (op `open`, resource kind `ui`) was typed `FILE` by op alone,
  so it read as file I/O; it is now `UI_HYPERLINK`, which `reaches-ui` counts and the
  ordering engine does not grade (the ordering prefilter `ordering_kept_roots` reads
  the same type). No golden and no DO finding moved. Test:
  `cli_prove_reaches_ui::every_ui_opening_call_reaches_ui` (a no-UI control keeps
  `no`); each of the three fixes, removed alone, fails it.
- **`[InternalEvent]` routines are event publishers** (G10). Both routine-kind rules
  (`ir_walk::ir_routine_kind`, which the model uses, and `engine::snapshot`'s
  `classify_kind_ir`) and the `.app`-symbols side (`symbol_reference::parse_method`,
  a new `AbiEventKind::Internal`) left an internal event a plain "procedure", after
  the retired al-sem reference. The program engine's own event binding already knew
  better, but the model's event graph, `events fanout` and every detector that reads
  the kind did not: on Continia DO 29.0 `events fanout` reported 208 publishers where
  the source has 217 (DO's three `[InternalEvent(false)]` events and six of CDN's), and
  d19 reported all 8 parameters of DO's three internal events as unused (8 of 8 false
  positives, triaged against the source; no other finding moved). The event graph now
  gives them event kind `internal` and reads `[InternalEvent(IncludeSender, Isolated)]`'s
  `Isolated` (index 1). Goldens: `ws-r0-canon-stress`'s internal event (its fixture
  comment said the old rule) moves in five families; the R2c coverage matrix gains an
  `internalPublishers` axis (the event was counted as an unknown kind), and the R3a-3
  manifest and the policy facts oracle (amended by hand: its recorder no longer
  exists) gain its one direct `publish` fact. Test:
  `gap_d19_event_publisher_skip::internal_event_publisher_parameters_are_not_flagged`,
  which fails with the old rule ("classified procedure").
- **`alsem batch` time is linear in the number of jobs again** (G14). The write-set
  check that runs before any build (`check_write_sets`) asked, for every job and every
  other job's write, whether the job's workspace read takes that file, and redid the
  workspace's package scope (file-system path resolution) for each pair. 800
  `query effects` jobs on Continia DO spent ~25 s there and 5,488 ran over ten
  minutes before the first job. Each distinct workspace is now resolved once, each
  pair of a workspace and a write asked once, and the read and write-write checks
  look targets up instead of scanning every pair; the first clash reported is the
  pair scan's. Measured on DO (release-fast): 200 jobs 3.1 → 1.7 s, 800 jobs 29.8 →
  4.7 s, 5,488 jobs in one manifest 29.4 s (the 28 × 200-job workaround on 4
  processes: 30 s), every one of the 10,976 output files byte-identical to the old
  binary's. A view's demands also no longer each get copies of all later demands'
  reads (`ViewCx::later_cells`/`later_runs`, another O(n²)): one last-reader table per
  view answers the same question (about 2 s of the 5,488-job run, one run each).
  Guard: `perf_bounds::batch_write_check_is_not_quadratic` (2,000 jobs under 1 s;
  8.8 ms now, 162.6 s with the old check).
- **A failed program build now says why.** `build_context_with` and the
  `LspSnapshot::build_full*` builders returned `Option` and dropped the snapshot
  builder's error, so `--analyze` warned only "the program snapshot could not be built"
  (a BOM or a typo in `app.json` looked like any other failure). They now return
  `Result<_, String>` with the reason, e.g. `snapshot build failed: parse
  <ws>/app.json: EOF while parsing a value at line 1 column 8`, and every consumer
  prints it: the `--analyze` call-graph warning (a missing `app.json` keeps its plain
  "no app.json at the project root"), the `--project` index report, the LSP server's
  per-root build warning (whose text had also lost a line continuation and carried
  long runs of spaces) and the updater's rung-3 rebuild warning. Test:
  `cli_analyze_call_hierarchy_json::unusable_app_json_warning_names_the_builder_reason`,
  which fails with the old fixed message.
- **A UTF-8 BOM in `app.json` no longer empties the program.** VS Code on Windows
  often writes one and the AL compiler accepts it, but `serde_json` rejected it: the
  root `app.json` failed to parse, the snapshot build returned nothing, and
  `--analyze` said only "the program snapshot could not be built" (Continia DO 29.0's
  `app.json` has a BOM). Every `app.json` read now goes through
  `source_text::parse_app_json`, which drops a leading BOM: the workspace inputs, the
  root app id, the model instance id's version, the dependency list
  (`dependencies::parse_app_json`), the compiler golden's `preprocessorSymbols` and
  `mint-goldens`' workspace id.
- **Two batch test helpers no longer fail on a closed stdin pipe.** They write the
  diff text to every command they start, and a command that never reads its stdin
  can exit before the write lands; the write then failed with `BrokenPipe` and
  `cli_batch_contract::batch_equals_standalone` failed at random. A closed pipe is now
  ignored there (any other write error still fails). Proven with a 3 s delay before
  the write: the old code fails with exactly that panic, the new code passes.

- **Digest `--file` and `--changed a.al,…` read paths like `--diff`** (#339). A file
  path may now be relative to the git top level (automatic mode, as #77 reads diff
  paths) or to `--diff-root` (explicit mode), not only to the workspace: run from the
  repository top, `--file Cloud/src/posting.al` resolves like `--file src/posting.al`.
  A path naming a workspace file both ways gives no roots and one
  `{kind: "file-ambiguous", file, candidates}` diagnostic (human:
  `changed-roots: file-ambiguous <file> (candidates: …); pass one candidate as --file,
  or --diff-root <folder> to read paths relative to <folder>`). A `ws:` id names one
  workspace file exactly, case kept, under every root, so a copied candidate picks its
  one file even next to a case-distinct sibling (a file holding no routine is
  `file-unmatched`). A `ws:` id that names no workspace file is read as a path, so a
  workspace folder literally named `ws:Cloud` still resolves under `--diff-root`, as a
  diff path does. `app:<guid>:` inputs are paths, as before. A batch decides the root
  for a file-only job as a standalone run does. Limit: prefix folders compare exactly, case
  included (`cloud/src/posting.al` under `Cloud` stays `file-unmatched`). (Absolute paths:
  #363, above.)

- **d39 no longer reports a record that a later helper saves on every path** (#343).
  Before, d39's `callerPersists` skip counted only the caller's own `Modify` / `Insert`
  / `Rename` after the call. Now a new skip, `helperPersists`, also counts a later call
  that hands the record to a helper (as a `var` argument, or as the receiver of a table
  procedure) whose own body saves it on every path. The check follows the paths of the
  caller's statement tree: an `exit` reached before the save keeps the finding. An exit
  on the `if not C(..) then exit` arm also needs no save when `C`'s body proves it
  leaves the record clean whenever it returns that value (the CDO shape).
  - Effect: the 3 CDO false positives in `CDOSetupData` (`InitRecurringDailyJob`, then
    `InsertJob`) are gone. Base App has 0 moves. No other detector moves.
  - The check fails closed: when unsure it keeps the finding. That includes `try` and
    `asserterror` (in the caller or in a helper), a `[TryFunction]` helper, an
    incomplete parse, an unresolved or interface call, a ternary branch, a reload, any
    whole-record assignment (`Rec := <anything>`), dirt left from an earlier loop pass,
    a bare call to a table procedure while the record is the implicit `Rec`, a call on
    the record that also passes it as an argument, any call other than a builtin that
    does not take the record while the record is an object global, and more than 3
    helper levels. No L4 role summary is trusted for
    a called routine; only its own body counts.
  - Known limit: an event publisher that takes the record by `var` between the call and
    the save keeps the finding, because a subscriber may reload or replace the record.
    This is why the 5 Base App candidates stay reported.
  - A helper that exits early (`if IsHandled then exit;`) before its save also keeps
    the finding.
  - The incomplete-parse guard has no fixture test: a fixture with a parse error would
    also move other detectors and the L2 corpus.
  - Tests: `tests/cli/cli_d39_helper_persists.rs` over `tests/fixtures/issue-343/ws-helper`
    (36 shapes, 29 expected rows) and `walk_paths` unit tests. The in-memory field
    `PCFNNode.path_hint` changes the hash of 988 distinct routine keys (1013 snapshot
    entries; overloads share a key) in `l2_features.snapshot` (regenerated; nothing
    serialized changes). The fixture-root tripwire counts 47
    `tests/fixtures` app dirs (was 46).

- **Digest `--diff`: a file that is not AL source gets its own kind, `diff-file-not-al`**
  (#353). Until now a non-AL file that a diff changed, added or listed in an `Only in`
  line (`app.json`, `.xlf`, `LICENSE`) was reported as `diff-file-unmatched`, so a
  consumer counting unmatched AL files counted it too. A deleted one was
  `diff-file-deleted`, and binary or mode-only sections were not reported at all (still
  true). A diff path counts as AL when it ends in `.al` in any case
  (`source_text::has_al_extension`, the test workspace discovery uses). A non-AL record
  makes no roots and gives one `{kind: "diff-file-not-al", file}` diagnostic (human:
  `changed-roots: diff-file-not-al <file>`). A rejected hunk header keeps its
  `diff-parse-error` too. A rename from an AL path to a non-AL one is `diff-file-deleted`
  on the old path. A copy to a non-AL name is `diff-file-not-al` on the new path, since
  it deleted nothing. A `/dev/null` → `/dev/null` record stays `diff-file-deleted` on
  `unknown`. An `Only in` path is `diff-file-not-al` only when no workspace file lies
  below it, because it may be a folder. That includes the diff root's prefix and the
  folders above it, such as `Only in .: Cloud` for a workspace at `<top>/Cloud`. This
  narrows the #111 entry's "reported as `diff-file-unmatched`" to AL paths.
  `diff-file-unmatched` now means an AL path with no routine-bearing workspace file, or
  an `Only in` folder that holds workspace files. Limits: the rule reads paths only, so
  a folder named `x.al` reads as AL. An `Only in` folder of workspace files stays
  `diff-file-unmatched`, and its roots are still lost. A folder that only the old tree
  has reads as `diff-file-not-al`. `--file` / `--changed-files` (`file-unmatched`) do
  not change.

- **`digest --format human` lists the changed-roots diagnostics** (#340). Until now the
  human output dropped them, so a run could exit 0 while a diff file or `--file` went
  unresolved and say nothing about it. Each diagnostic now gets one line,
  `changed-roots: <kind> <subject>`, where `<kind>` is the JSON `kind`. The lines come
  after the entries, or after `digest: no changed roots resolved` when there are none. A
  `diff-file-ambiguous` line names its candidates and suggests `--diff-root <folder>`.
  Control characters and bidi or line-separator characters in a path print escaped
  (`\n`, `\t`, `\u{202e}`), so each diagnostic stays on one line and reads as written.
  The `--tests` line stays last. The JSON does not change. Six cli-b human goldens gain
  the line `changed-roots: file-unmatched src/Rec.Table.al`.
- **d35 names a dependency subscriber's own unresolved call sites** (#287). This lifts
  the limit stated in the #265 entry: a subscriber that lives in a dependency app
  (reported at `--scope all`) now gets the same `; unresolved: <callee> (line n)` segment
  as a workspace subscriber, and drops itself from "partly analysed" under the same rule.
  The detector context now also indexes the dependency half of the uncertainty edges,
  keyed by caller (`dependency_uncertainty_edges_by_from`, with its own census row);
  the Primary index and every detector that reads it are unchanged, and single-app the
  new index is empty. Ids, fingerprints, severity and confidence do not change. Limit:
  the confidence cap reads the core summaries and the Primary index, not the dependency
  index, so a dependency subscriber's dependency-half call-edge gaps (its own and its
  callees') do not cap its confidence. Core-summary uncertainties still do (for example
  a parse-incomplete row sharing its id); with none, the confidence is uncapped.

- **A dependency page known only from its symbols now carries its write-surface
  properties (#302).** When a dependency `.app` has no embedded `.al` source, ABI
  ingestion now reads each page's `Editable`, `InsertAllowed`, `ModifyAllowed`,
  `DeleteAllowed` and `SourceTableTemporary` from `SymbolReference.json` into the model,
  as the source path already did. Symbols write these values as `"0"` / `"1"`; `true` /
  `false` are read too, and any other value counts as "not declared". Effects:
  - d39 now reports a pageext over a read-only (`Editable = false` or
    `ModifyAllowed = false`) symbol-only dependency page, with the same finding and
    fingerprint as when that dependency ships its source. Before, such a page counted as
    modifiable, so the read-only rule never fired.
  - Opt-in d64 no longer reports "API page write surface not declared" for symbol-only
    API pages that do declare it. On the pinned CDO workspace with every dependency
    stripped to symbols, all 8 such findings were false positives and are gone.
- **Model: a pageext's implicit `Rec` / `xRec` follows its base page's
  `SourceTableTemporary`, and a declared `Rec` is never made temporary by it (#302).**
  This changes the record temp state in the model, so every reader of it moves: record
  operations, the record variable, and arguments that pass the implicit `Rec` (the L4
  parameter-dependent substitution and the capability cone). Temp-aware detectors such as
  d39 and d3 then skip it.
  - A pageext's implicit `Rec` / `xRec` is now temporary when its BASE page declares
    `SourceTableTemporary = true`. Before, only the pageext's own flag was read, and a
    pageext never carries one. This holds whether the base page is in the workspace, in a
    dependency's source or in its symbols. So d39 no longer reports a pageext over a
    read-only, temporary base page.
  - Only the IMPLICIT record is affected. Before, the rule marked every record named
    `Rec` / `xRec` temporary on a `SourceTableTemporary` page, including a param, local or
    global the routine declared itself with that name. A declared `Rec: Record X` now keeps
    its own temp state, so d3 and d39 report it as they would any physical record. The
    model marks the implicit row (`ModelRecordVariable.is_implicit_rec`).

  Both #302 entries, measured on the pinned CDO workspace (whose page-bearing dependencies
  all embed source), final code against the base: 2,217 findings at `--scope primary` and
  30,006 at `--scope all` on both sides, 0 fingerprints moved, and both JSON payloads
  byte-identical. Neither entry moves a CDO finding. No ABI vector or golden needed an
  update: no golden or ABI vector that existed before this change carries the page
  properties or the shapes above, so new unit and CLI tests (with their own fixtures,
  checked by direct asserts) pin them instead. No Windows confirmation is relevant: both
  entries read facts the code already declares (symbol properties, `SourceTableTemporary`)
  and pass them through the model; neither claims anything new about BC runtime
  behaviour.

## [2.1.1] - 2026-10-25

### Changed

- **Grammar: tree-sitter-al `main` at `940ba71b`** (package version still 4.4.1; was
  `c89c2ecb`). Two grammar fixes are in it. `ac8a8665`: an `#if` tail may have an empty
  `#else` arm (`I := A #if X + B #else #endif;`, tree-sitter-al issue #38), and an
  operand-prefix arm may be a unary operator alone. `f78aa68b`: an operand prefix may have
  an empty arm (`I := #if X a + #else #endif b;`). Each of these shapes was an ERROR
  before. Now it is a `preproc_conditional_expression_tail` or `preproc_operand_prefix`
  beside the value it continues, which the lowerer already skips, so no lowerer change was
  needed. The only `node-types.json` change: `preproc_operand_prefix`'s `operand` is now
  optional and `not` is one of its operators; no named kind was added or removed, so
  `kind_policy` and the 501 named kinds did not move. `CACHE_VERSION_GRAMMAR` is now
  `tree-sitter-al-v4.4.1-940ba71b-native` (same length, so `dry-run.txt` did not move).
  A new lowerer test, `empty_arm_tail_and_prefix_keep_the_value`, pins that every call
  around these shapes stays linked with the right arity; on `c89c2ecb` it fails with no
  call at all, because the whole body was an ERROR. Measured old against new: per-test
  outcomes identical (4,439 run, all pass, 8 skipped, on both sides), zero goldens moved
  (`check-goldens --regen` wrote nothing), and CDO `--program-call-graph-stats`
  byte-identical (0 unknown edges, 0 recovered files on both sides). The pinned CDO code
  does not use these shapes.

- **d11 and d37 no longer report `Rec` in a table or table extension routine** (#299).
  There `Rec` is the receiver: the record the caller called the method on (`Cust.Foo()`),
  or the record the platform or caller fired the trigger for. The caller owns it, as it
  owns a parameter record, which both detectors already skipped. d11 (`Modify`/`Validate`
  with no load) skips the receiver in every such routine, unless the routine itself
  replaced `Rec` with a bare `Rec := Other` before the op. This is ownership, not proof
  that the caller loaded the record. d37 (`Validate` with no persist) skips it when d39's
  owner rule says the owner persists `Rec` (every routine except a table extension
  `OnAfterInsert`/`OnAfterModify`/`OnAfterRename`) and the routine does not put `Rec` in a
  new state after the `Validate`: its own `Get`/`Find*`/`Next`/`Init`/`Copy`/
  `TransferFields`, a `var` helper that loads it, or `Rec := Other`. `Reset` is not a new
  state. A declared `Rec` (a local, or a named return value `Rec`) is not the receiver and
  is still reported. The receiver is a flag on the seeded `Rec` row
  (`PRecordVariable.is_receiver`, not serialized), so a `TableType = Temporary` table or an
  `IsTemporary` entry guard does not hide it. New stats key `callerOwnedRec` on both
  detectors. Measured on this branch (release-fast, findings removed, 0 added, no other
  detector moved): Base App single-app scope all, d11 2321 → 1101 and d37 1400 → 550; CDO
  primary, d11 112 → 15 and d37 12 → 3; CDO all, d11 729 → 249 and d37 163 → 31. Every
  removed finding is a d11/d37 finding on table `Rec` on the base; triage samples were all
  false positives (Base App d11 18/18, d37 18/18, field `OnLookup` 6/6; CDO primary d37
  9/9, d11 13/13). The table field `OnLookup` case relies on a write that was measured as
  persisted on the BC 28.4 Linux sidecar; **a Windows Cronus confirmation is still owed**.
  Known limits. The rule moves the question to the caller, and d11/d37 do not judge a
  method call on a record (the same blind spot they have for parameter records today),
  so these real problems are now missed: a caller that runs a table method on a record it
  never loaded (d11 used to fire inside the method); a method that only `Validate`s `Rec`
  whose callers never persist the record, including a table procedure called only from a
  table extension `OnAfterInsert`/`OnAfterModify`/`OnAfterRename` trigger (d39 does not
  see a method call on a local either). In the routine itself: a reload through a method
  called on the receiver (`ReloadMe()`, which does `Get`) is not seen, so d37 skips that
  `Validate`; a reload that comes before the `Validate` in the source but runs after it in
  a loop is not seen either (d39 has the same limit); a replacement whose right side or
  target is not a bare unquoted identifier (`Rec := GetRec()`, `"Rec" := Other`) is not
  seen as a new state; `Validate` followed by `Clear(Rec)` is not reported, because d37's
  older rule for a call that takes the record and cannot be resolved already hides it, for
  any record; and `Rec := Other` in the other arm of a branch keeps the finding, for d37
  when that branch holds the `Validate` and for d11 when it holds the `Modify` (a
  conservative false positive). Page `Rec`, d21 on table `Rec` and a codeunit `TableNo`
  `OnRun` `Rec` are not changed. `src/engine/l5/detectors/mod.rs` (`is_table_receiver_rec`,
  `table_rec_persisted_by_owner`, `receiver_reset_after`, and `load_point_after` with
  `LoadPointCache`, now shared with d39), `d11.rs`, `d37.rs`, `d39.rs`,
  `src/program/body/ir_walk.rs` (`ir_record_variables`).

- **Digest `schemaVersion` 1.7.0: new `diff-file-ambiguous` changed-roots diagnostic**
  (#77). A diff path that names a workspace file both as written and below the git top level
  (`Cloud/src/posting.al` when the workspace holds both `src/posting.al` and
  `Cloud/src/posting.al`) gives no roots and one `{kind: "diff-file-ambiguous", file,
  candidates}`, the as-written reading's units first, each reading's units sorted. Any
  workspace `.al` file counts, routines or not. `--diff-root` settles it. If such a file
  also has a broken hunk header, both candidates are blocked (#72). Other files still
  resolve, and the run exits 0 when one did. Contract, stated at the `schemaVersion` line: a
  minor bump is additive; `changedRootsDiagnostics[].kind` is an open set (treat an unknown
  kind as a diagnostic, not a parse error); exit 0 does not mean every diff file resolved.
  Consumers that pin digest 1.6.0, such as CentralGauge's `ALSEM_SCHEMAS`, must add 1.7.0.
  Prove's schema does not change.
- **`alsem digest --diff` reads `diff -r`'s `Only in <dir>: <name>` lines** (#111), which it
  ignored before, so a diff that adds or deletes files no longer drops them silently. The
  path is `<dir>/<name>` with one `/` between (`Only in new/: x.al` is `new/x.al`). It is
  looked up like a header path (same normalisation, same workspace file match): a path that
  is a workspace file, such as `Only in ./src: new.al` from `diff -ru ../old .` run at the
  workspace root, makes every routine of that file a root, as a rename with no hunk does.
  Any other path is reported as `diff-file-unmatched` on `<dir>/<name>`.
  `src/engine/l5/diff_parser.rs` (`DiffParseResult::only_in`),
  `src/engine/l5/digest_cli.rs` (`resolve_changed_roots`). Not covered: an `Only in` line is
  read anywhere at the top level, so one in a commit message gives a stray diagnostic, or,
  when it names a workspace file, extra roots with no diagnostic; an `Only in` directory is one unmatched entry, not its files, so tool
  folders such as `.git` or `.alpackages` add noise; a directory name containing `: ` is
  split at the wrong place; and `Only in` misses share the `diff-file-unmatched` kind and
  are listed after the per-file diagnostics.

### Fixed

- **`alsem digest --diff` reads plain `diff -u` / `diff -ru` headers** (#111), when their
  paths are relative to the workspace (run `diff` from the workspace root, or use
  `--label`, or pass `--diff-root`, #77). GNU `diff` writes each `---`/`+++` header as `<path><TAB><timestamp>`, and the
  TAB and timestamp stayed in the path, so every plain-diff file was `diff-file-unmatched`
  and a timestamped `/dev/null` was not seen as an addition or deletion. The header path now
  ends at the first raw TAB, before the `/dev/null` test and before unquoting, so GNU's
  quoted form `"./src/a b.al"<TAB><time>` matches too. Both GNU diff and git C-quote a name
  that holds a TAB, so a raw TAB only ever ends the path (checked on GNU diffutils 3.12 and
  git 2.53.0); a producer that writes such a name raw and unquoted would cut it at that TAB.
  `src/engine/l5/diff_parser.rs` (`extract_path`). Not covered: `diff -ru old new` run from
  a parent folder writes a tree-root folder (`n/src/…`) that resolves only with
  `--diff-root` (#77); `diff -ruN`'s
  epoch-dated deletions are not read as deletions (one reads as a modified file with every
  line deleted); the `a/`/`b/` prefix is now stripped from plain GNU paths too, so a
  workspace whose top folder is literally `a` or `b` loses that segment; and a git name with
  a trailing space still loses it to the existing trim.

- **A call that never runs no longer makes an analysis incomplete (#288).** A
  call or record operation after `exit;` (or after a stop such as
  `Error('text')`) added no fact, but it still counted as a coverage gap and as
  an edge of the capability cone. So d35 reported "Commit may be reachable
  (incomplete call coverage)" for a subscriber whose only gap was a dead
  interface call, and a dead `Codeunit.Run(Id)`, a dead call to a committing
  procedure or a dead `Insert(true)` whose `OnInsert` commits still counted.
  Now every coverage producer (the detector context, the cross-app base, the
  r3a3 projection and the snapshot base) and the cone's typed-edge graph skip
  such a site (`capability_cone::DeadSites`), and d35 names only the gaps that
  remain. A site counts as dead only where today's `unreachable` mark is
  provably sound: its routine has no preprocessor directive, and every bare
  `Error(...)` in it takes the Text form (a string literal, two or more
  arguments, or a Text, Label or Code variable found in AL's scope order, the
  named return value included, with AL's Unicode-aware name equality; a name
  holding an escaped quote proves nothing) and binds to the builtin, not to an
  own `procedure Error` (`ModelRoutine::dead_marks_trusted`, which fails
  closed). A proof that rests on a global variable (or a variable of unknown
  scope) also needs the whole enclosing object free of preprocessor
  directives, because an `#if` around the `var` section can give the name
  another type in another build. Elsewhere dead code still counts, as before.
  Stated limit: d35's confidence cap still reads the L4 summary's
  uncertainties, which include dead sites. No golden moves; on the pinned CDO
  baseline no finding moves.
- **An object split across `#if` arms no longer lends one arm's properties to
  the other arm's routines (#279).** A numbered object's id is its number, so
  `#if A codeunit 50100 "Foo" … #else codeunit 50100 "Bar" … #endif` gives two
  object rows with one id. Finding locations and owner display already read
  the routine's declaring row (#241); the remaining id-keyed readers of "this
  routine's object" took the last row for the id, so a routine of the first
  arm got the second arm's name, subtype, SourceTable, InherentCommitBehavior
  or Editable. Now each reads the routine's own declaring row
  (`DeclaringObjects::of`): policy `object.name` and `root.kinds`, root
  classification, d14, d39 (`page_may_modify`), d50 (cap 4), the
  test-coverage Test-subtype check, the return summaries'
  InherentCommitBehavior, the implicit `Rec`'s table, and the HTML report's
  event-graph labels. d57 (SingleInstance) and d60 (Install/Upgrade) used to
  accept a routine when ANY row of its id qualified; they now test the
  routine's own row. `[HandlerFunctions]` finds a handler only in the test's
  own arm, so the other arm's same-named procedure no longer makes a phantom
  coverage path. d2, d13, d17 and d46 were swapped to the declaring row too,
  with no test that pins their behaviour (d13 and d17 compare the app id,
  which every arm shares, so they do not change). `DetectorContext.objects_by_id`
  is gone (replaced by `declaring`, which d50 now reads too);
  `FingerprintIndex::object` is renamed `object_row_by_id`, for reads every
  arm agrees on (object-scoped, or the object type and key). The retained
  census bucket `context.objects_by_id` is now `context.declaring`. Stated
  limits: a routine whose signature is the same in both arms is still one
  routine id, so readers that look a routine up by id see one arm's answer;
  d57's clearing evidence is still collected per object id, so a `Clear` in
  one SingleInstance arm hides a growing collection in another SingleInstance
  arm (a missed finding, never a false one); a table event's publisher label
  in the HTML report falls back to the last-wins row, so a table split across
  arms is labelled with its last arm's name; the program graph still merges
  the arms into one node with the first arm's name. No golden moves; on the
  pinned CDO baseline no finding moves.

### Added

- **`alsem digest --diff` reads paths relative to the enclosing git top level** (#77). `git
  diff` writes repository-root paths from any folder, so a workspace in a repository
  subfolder (`<repo>/Cloud`) got `diff-file-unmatched` for `a/Cloud/src/posting.al`. The top
  level is the nearest folder at or above the canonical workspace that holds `.git` (a
  folder, or a worktree's or submodule's file), with no depth limit and no `git` command. A
  path is read as written and with the workspace's folder (`Cloud/`) removed; a
  workspace-relative diff still works. The prefix compares folder by folder, exactly, case
  included, on every platform, and is the folder's whole name (a folder named `ws:Cloud`
  keeps its `ws:`). With no enclosing repository, paths stay workspace-relative.
- **`alsem digest --diff-root <dir>`** (#77): the folder the diff's paths are relative to,
  for a workspace outside git or a `diff -ru old new` run from a parent folder. The
  workspace must be inside it (as spelled, so a symlinked workspace keeps its link name, or
  after resolving symlinks); every path is then read below it only. A root that does not
  exist, is not a folder or does not contain the workspace, and a `--diff-root` with no
  diff, are exit 3; a workspace that does not exist is the load's error (exit 1), however
  it is spelled, as in auto mode. In a batch the parent decides the root once and its
  workers use that decision; the root and workspace probes count as the job's reads, so a
  job writing the root file is refused as a conflict. `src/bin/alsem.rs`
  (`decide_diff_root`, `pin_diff_root`), `src/engine/l5/digest_cli.rs` (`DiffRoot`,
  `diff_readings`, `diff_key`).
  Not covered: `--file` / `--changed-files` still take workspace-relative paths only; a
  diff whose prefix differs from the on-disk folder only by case stays unmatched (use `git
  diff --relative`); macOS decomposed (NFD) folder names do not match git's composed ones;
  `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` are not read; human output still shows no changed-roots
  diagnostics; under auto mode a repository-root path outside the workspace still resolves
  when the workspace holds the same relative path (as before); `diff -ru a b` of trees
  literally named `a` and `b` loses `a/`/`b/` from its headers but not from its `Only in`
  lines (#111's prefix strip), so the two halves never both resolve.
- **`alsem digest --include-reads`: table reads as `DB_READ` effects (#246).**
  Opt-in. Each table read site (`Get`, `Find*`, `IsEmpty`, `Count*`, `Next`,
  `CalcFields`, `CalcSums`) becomes a `DB_READ` effect with
  `detail.resourceId` / `resourceDisplay`, under the same coverage, witness
  and dependency-boundary rules as writes. A read reached only through a
  dependency call is a boundary group that stops at the first dependency
  routine. Reads get `detail.tempState` through the same L4 join as writes,
  where L4 holds the operation (about 7% of reads on CDO; see below). A
  `DB_READ`'s `factId` key also names its table, so reads of two tables
  witnessed at one operation keep distinct ids. The document gets `payload.includeReads: true`. Without the flag the
  output is byte-identical (no golden moved). `schemaVersion` did not move for
  it (1.6.0 at the time): `DB_READ` and `includeReads` are opt-in and additive.
  This release ships digest 1.7.0 through #77 (see Changed).
  - **Limits:**
    - One effect per read SITE, not per table. Physical and temporary reads
      of one table are separate effects.
    - A read of an unresolved table has no `resourceId`.
    - A dependency-boundary group has no `resourceId` and no `tempState`. Its
      `resourceCount` is complete, but `resources` names at most 10 tables.
    - `LockTable` is not a read.
    - `CalcFields` reads only the record's own table, not the FlowField's
      source tables.
    - `DB_READ` is **not ordering-graded**: its `guarantees` and
      `scopedGuarantees` are always empty, meaning "not graded", not "no
      label applies". The other effects' guarantees do not change.
  - **Cost on CDO** (pinned `bc3ccb18`, release-fast, `VmHWM`, median of 3,
    flag on against off; full table in
    `docs/measurements/2026-10-25-issue-246-digest-include-reads.md`):

    | shape | CPU-s | peak (KiB) | output bytes |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `d` (`--file $F`) | 127.5 vs 125.5 (+1.6%) | 3,155,088 vs 3,163,188 (−0.3%) | +22% |
    | `h` (`--file $F88`, 88 roots) | 493.4 vs 423.4 (+16.5%) | 3,663,632 vs 3,412,092 (+7.4%) | +21% |
    | `ds` (single-app) | 30.5 vs 30.5 | 732,292 vs 722,476 (+1.4%) | +25% |
    | `Up` batch `[a, d, h, ev, qt]` | 486.0 vs 442.3 (+9.9%) | 4,062,196 vs 3,729,108 (+8.9%) | +21% (d+h) |

    Walls were measured under host load 5–24, so CPU-seconds are the cost
    figure (wall `d` 27.5 vs 27.4 s, `h` 58.4 vs 47.8 s, `Up` 61.0 vs 56.1 s).
    The `Up` peak passed the batch admission row, so a digest job with
    `--include-reads` is its own kind, `("digest reads", X)` at
    16 × 256 MiB = 4,194,304 KiB (`("digest reads", S)` at 3 × 256 MiB, from
    `ds`). A plain digest keeps `("digest", X)` at 15. The worker count does
    not change for any measured shape.
  - **Known `tempState` gap:** on CDO, 1,059 of `d`'s 1,133 reads (21,707 of
    `h`'s 23,248) have no `tempState` and a `temp-state-incoherent`
    (`no-l4-row`) diagnostic. This is not read-specific: the default output
    already carries 772 write effects with the same diagnostic. The
    capability cone reaches operations that the root's L4 summary does not
    hold.
    - Almost all of them (1,047 on `d`) are witnessed at one RecordRef
      `FindFirst` with no resolved table. Such a fact matches a read of any
      table (`fact_equivalent`), so for those effects the evidence line is
      not where the table is read.
    - The count is also inflated by that one RecordRef site.

- **Hidden `--l4-host` LSP flag: an incremental L4 host (#222).** Off by default and
  hidden from `--help`. With the flag, each workspace root, once built, gets a
  background worker that keeps the L4 summaries up to date. After every snapshot swap
  (config-only swaps included) the worker re-solves only the routines a change can reach,
  and seeds every other SCC from the last result. The re-solved set is: an SCC whose
  membership is new, an SCC with a member whose model row changed, an SCC with a callee
  in that set, and an SCC with a callee that came out different. The row covers the
  routine's model rows, its out-edges, call bindings, uncertainty edges, leaf summary,
  shared-event bits and fixed-role flag. The result equals a fresh solve; an oracle
  suite checks this case by case.
  - **No editor output.** The host publishes only to its own status and one
    `debug!` line, `l4-host: published generation <g>: <kind>, seeded <s> of <t>`
    (visible with `--verbose`). The diagnostics recompute is unchanged.
  - **Cross-app only.** The host always analyses the workspace plus the dependency code
    it uses.
  - **What forces a full refresh:** adding, removing or renaming an `.al` file (every
    routine id changes with the file list), any `app.json` change such as a version
    bump, any change to the dependency closure (any `.app` in `.alpackages`, even one
    nothing reads), and a change to the table fields or to collided call sites.
  - **Cancellation.** A newer request cancels a running refresh between phases and
    between SCCs, and a cancelled refresh keeps the last baseline. A complete refresh
    that was overtaken still becomes the baseline but is not published.
  - **A crash in the host ends the server**, in every build: the worker catches a panic,
    logs `l4-host: panicked: …` to stderr and aborts the process.
  - **Trace counters** (with `ALSEM_TRACE`): `host.refresh`, `host.full`,
    `host.sccs_resolved` and `host.sccs_seeded`, per refresh whose solve completed.
  - **Two findings shaped the design.** The solve reads the model rows of its callees,
    not only their summaries, so a caller of a changed routine is always re-solved
    (one hop), even when the callee's summary does not change. And a file add or
    remove cannot reuse anything, because it renames every id.

## [2.1.0] - 2026-10-25

### Added

- **`alsem batch <manifest> [--out-dir DIR]` (#277).** Runs the commands of a JSON
  manifest (`{"jobs": [{"argv": [...], "stdout": ..., "stderr": ...}]}`, or several
  `{"batches": [...]}`); a batch runs in one process. Jobs on one workspace and universe share one
  view: one read of the workspace, one build, one witness pass at the union of the jobs'
  requests, one `det`, and one run per distinct detector set and scope. Views are built
  one after another, and a workspace read is freed after its last view. Every job's
  stdout, stderr and exit equal its standalone run with its stdout off a terminal
  (`analyze`'s `--format auto` is JSON in a batch, whatever the run's own stdout is,
  with one batch or several), with two stated exceptions: a
  view's `log` lines (`RUST_LOG`) are printed once on the run's stderr, and a job's own
  write-error line goes to the run's stderr too. The library's job lines (the L4
  non-convergence line, `graph`'s coverage warning) are replayed in the stderr of each
  job whose standalone run prints them. A job's streams go to
  `DIR/<batch>.<job>.stdout`/`.stderr` unless the manifest names them (relative paths
  against the manifest's directory; `--out` stays relative to the cwd); a missing stream
  directory or `--out-dir` exits 3 before any build. The run prints
  one JSON line per job (`batch`, `job`, `exit`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `files`) and exits 0
  when every job ran, whatever their exits; a job whose own write fails gets its
  command's write-failure exit (analyze 2, else 1). A bad manifest (an argv clap rejects,
  `batch`, `policy explain`, `cache prune`, no command, no job) exits 3 and runs nothing,
  and so do two write targets naming one file (also one job's stdout and stderr), a file
  inside another job's shard directory, a job writing the manifest, and a file one job
  reads (a diff side, `--baseline`, `--renames`, `--policy`, a digest diff, a workspace's
  own files) that another job writes. A job that fails its own validation (a bad
  `--format`, `--shard` without `--out`, a policy that does not load, …) writes only its
  two streams, so nothing it would write is checked, but it keeps the files it reads (a
  `digest --diff foo.diff` that failed because `foo.diff` is absent still clashes with the
  job that writes it), named or not (an auto-detected `al-sem.policy.yaml` that does not
  load still clashes with a job writing it); it is a job of its own exit, never a usage
  error. Paths
  are compared after their deepest existing directory is canonicalized and each `..` is
  taken as the OS takes it (after a symlink, the target's parent), so a symlink, a Windows
  case difference or an 8.3 name hides no clash; a workspace's own files are its
  `.al`/`.app` files in any case, its `app.json` and config files, and the `.app` files of
  every ancestor `.alpackages` the loader reads (the ancestors of the workspace as spelled,
  as the loader walks them), each also at the target of a symlink that leads outside the
  workspace, as the loader follows it; a linked directory (a linked `.alpackages`
  included) is compared at its target, so a new `.al`, `.app` or config file written
  under it clashes too. Every job is validated once, before anything runs:
  whether `digest --changed <value>` names a diff file is decided then, and stdin is read
  then, once, only when a job that passed its validation reads it, as standalone (a read
  that fails is each such job's `failed to read diff from stdin`, exit 3); a closed run
  stdout exits 1. Two or more batches run in worker processes (`alsem batch --worker <b>`, hidden),
  at most `W` at once, started in manifest order: `W = max(1, min(batches, 4, ⌊28 GiB /
  P⌋))`, at most 2 when a job is `policy check`, `P` the largest measured CDO peak of the
  run's job kinds that build a view (`batch::admission::KIND_PEAK_KIB`; a kind with no row
  takes the largest; a job that fails its validation or a
  `diff` of two snapshot files counts for none, nor sets the policy cap). The parent writes
  each worker its batch, its `--changed` decisions, the one stdin read and every file its
  plans read (a digest's `--diff` file, a policy file) on the worker's stdin (a worker never
  opens the manifest, and each such file is read once per run, so a FIFO works; a path
  that is not UTF-8 crosses as raw bytes), forwards each worker's stderr whole line by whole line as
  `[w<b>] …`, gives each worker the trace file `<ALSEM_TRACE_FILE>.w<b>`, and prints the job
  lines in manifest order after the last worker exits; a worker that dies without its lines
  leaves its jobs `"exit": null` with `"worker": "<signal or status>"`, and the run exits 1.
  `alsem batch --help` states the budget's limit (the measured shapes only) and that the
  table is CDO-calibrated. Neither `alsem batch` nor its workers read or set
  `RAYON_NUM_THREADS`; each big-stack pool reports its size in a `pool.threads` trace
  instant. Under `ALSEM_RETAINED_CENSUS=1` each worker, a one-batch run's in-process one
  included, prints `[batch] worker <b> peak_kib=<VmHWM>` (where `/proc/self/status`
  exists). Traces gain `batch.workers`
  (`w`, `p_kib`, `policy_cap`), `batch.worker.start`, `batch.worker.exit`, `batch.driver`,
  `view.<i>`, `view.drop`, `view.teardown`, `view.run`, `job.<i>.<cmd>` and
  `inputs.request_read`; `ALSEM_RETAINED_CENSUS=1` prints `[retained-census] batch.held
  outputs= sides= inputs=` at each view's start, `batch.shared cell=<model|rel|raw|l4|det>
  job_refs=<n>` after its one prepare (each cell one allocation, its bytes the cell's own
  buckets, printed once) and `batch.shared cell=runs bytes= allocs= job_refs=` after its
  computes (each distinct run allocation counted once). Limit: jobs that spell one workspace
  path differently share its read, so a program build error names the first spelling
  (graph's missing-`id` error names the job's own).
  `KIND_PEAK_KIB` holds the step-12 CDO bench's measured rows
  (`docs/measurements/2026-10-25-issue-277-160-step12.md` Part 4b), one per command and
  universe, rounded up to 256 MiB: cross-app 13 steps (3.25 GiB) for analyze, fingerprint,
  prove, events fanout/chains and query touches/effects, 15 (3.75 GiB) for digest, 39
  (9.75 GiB) for policy check, 10 (2.5 GiB) for graph; single-app 3 (0.75 GiB), and 6
  (1.5 GiB) for fingerprint and diff. A manifest without `policy check` derives `W` = 4,
  with it 2. Stated limits (spec 12A-19): a batch whose view holds `policy check` and
  other cross-app jobs peaks at about 1.22 × the policy job alone (the union of the jobs'
  requests; measured 10,056,180 KiB against `policy check`'s 8,273,244), above the 1.15 ×
  bound, reported and not gating; and a manifest path or stream directory that is not
  UTF-8 still fails, because a run's job lines and its worker stream names are JSON
  strings.

- `alsem diff`: a new `rename-overlay-collision` diagnostic (`{kind, from, to}`). It
  fires when a `--renames` entry maps an old id (a routine, object, table, field or
  key) onto a target that is also an id in the old snapshot, and nothing maps that
  target away. The two old ids' facts then share one key. Findings do not change;
  the diagnostic says that they merged. Two entries onto one target are still
  reported as `rename-overlay-overlap` (#237).

### Changed

- A tree read that asks for the primary app's facts now stops the run in release builds
  too: the view's "no tree read asks primary" check is an `assert!`, not a
  `debug_assert!` (#277).
- Tests: `standalone_is_a_batch_of_one` pins `ALCH_DRIVER_VERSION_OVERRIDE` to the
  version the `tests/gate-goldens/batch/one-job/` goldens were minted at (2.0.3), so a
  version bump no longer breaks them: `alsemVersion`/`al_sem_version`, graph's `engine`
  and digest's, prove's and fingerprint's `workspaceFingerprint` all carry it. The pin goes
  to each child process, not the test process, where a concurrent test's standalone run
  read it (#277).
- **#160 step 9: `prove`, `fingerprint --routine` and `fingerprint --inventory-only` are
  cross-app by default** (part of #160). Each builds the model of the workspace plus the
  dependency code it requires, as `analyze` and `digest` do, and reads a tree over that
  cone graph, so behaviour follows calls into dependency code. `--single-app` (new on
  `prove` and `fingerprint`) analyses the workspace alone. Its output is the previous
  output for `prove` and `--inventory-only`. For `fingerprint --routine` two things
  differ: the document's `schemaVersion` is `1.3.0`, and `mayCommit` follows the fix
  under Fixed. `--no-roots-config` applies to the cross-app build too.
  - `prove` is `digest` with one root: a dependency effect counts as evidence, and
    dependency code that has no body, is ABI-only or has an analysis gap keeps the answer
    `unknown`. A must-question answered only through dependency code is `unknown`
    (rule B: a dependency effect is a boundary group with conditionality `unknown`).
    `writes-table:` and `publishes-event:` match a boundary group by every resource in
    it, not only the 10 its `detail` lists.
  - `fingerprint --routine`: inherited dependency facts appear on the routine, and each
    witness path stops at the first dependency routine. A selector never names a
