    dependency routine, and `summary.totalClassifications` counts primary classifications
    only. The query document's `schemaVersion` is `1.3.0`. This is additive: a path can
    carry a `boundary` object (`kind` `call` / `trigger` / `event`, its `cs:` / `op:` /
    `ev:` id, the callsite, operation or event id, and an anchor), and a witness's
    `evidence` is the first path's boundary when a path has one. With `--witness 0`, or
    when no path is found, the evidence is the fact's own operation, which for an
    inherited fact can be inside the dependency routine; this is intended (the operation
    is where the effect happens). The json projection is streamed, so a large document
    is not held twice; its bytes are unchanged.
  - `fingerprint --inventory-only` composes no raw facts: its five keys come from a
    tree with no inherited facts, and cross-app `apps[]` names the dependency apps whose
    identities a primary row references.
  - Stays single-app in this release, whatever `--single-app` says: `fingerprint`'s full
    snapshot (json with no query flag, cbor, cbor.gz, `--shard`), the query forms with no
    `--routine` (human with no flag, `--roots`, `--witness` or `--no-include-inherited`
    alone), and `diff`. A filed follow-up moves them.
- **d35's unknown answer names the subscriber's own unresolved call sites** (#265). When
  the gap is in the subscriber's own body, the root cause, evidence note and fix hint now
  say `unresolved: <callee> (line n)` (source order, up to three, then `+N more`) and
  list only OTHER routines under "partly analysed". The callee is rendered from the
  parsed call as the snapshot's `calleeDisplay` does, so a comment between the receiver
  and the method does not leak in. The receiver is still raw source: whitespace runs in
  it become one space, and a comment inside a receiver expression can survive, on one
  line. CentralGauge's direct repro now reads
  `(interface-open-world; unresolved: Strategy.NextKm (line 11))` instead of
  `partly analysed: ReleaseOnRegistered (Codeunit 50104)`. "Unresolved" means a call whose
  callee set is not closed for this proof (interface-open-world, ambiguous-overload,
  external-target, member-not-found). A site in unreachable code is not named. The
  subscriber stays listed when a gap of its own has no located reachable site in its own
  row, or another row with its id is opaque or parse-incomplete. Limit: a subscriber in
  a dependency app (`--scope all`) keeps the old text, because its own uncertainty edges
  are not on the detector context. Ids, fingerprints, severity and confidence do not
  change.
- **`policy check --no-policy` keeps no raw facts (#277 E12-C5).** No rule reads them, so
  the view's composition no longer keeps every primary routine's raw facts
  (`build.witness_pass` 0, was 1), and in a batch it no longer claims them as a later
  reader, so a policy with rules before it frees them after its own use. Output is
  unchanged.
- **Each workspace read is dropped with its last view (#277 E12-C2).** `diff A B` no
  longer holds A's read through B's build. A `RequestInputs` read (policy, baseline) is
  now timed (`inputs.request_read`) and tallied in a `request_inputs` census bucket
  (E12-C6). The view's own cells are freed in a `view.teardown` span (E12-C3).
- Library: `JobFailure` is now an alias of `JobOutput` (E12-C7); `ViewDemand::one` builds
  a one-side job's demand and `JobOutput::text` a text command's writes (E12-C8);
  `DiffJob::new` takes a `WorkspaceReader` and `policy_plan` a `rules` flag.

- **Errors found before the build win (#277).** `policy check` loads its policy, and
  `fingerprint` checks `--shard` against `--out`, before the model is built. So when an
  invocation has two problems, the stderr text changes: a bad policy and a failing build
  now report the policy error; `--shard` without `--out` and a failing build report
  `--shard requires --out <directory>`; and `policy check --strict` with a bad policy and
  an error-severity analyzer diagnostic reports the policy error, not the diagnostic
  lines (exit 1 either way). Neither case builds a model any more, and a bad policy no
  longer reads the workspace before it is reported. The `--shard`/`--out`
  check also now runs before `fingerprint --strict`'s analyzer-diagnostic gate and before
  its `fingerprint: could not compute modelInstanceId` error: with either of those, a
  `--shard` without `--out` now reports the shard error (exit 1 in every case; only the
  stderr text differs). `diff --renames` keeps its order.
- **`analyze --update-baseline` write failure (#277).** The baseline file is now written
  by the command's output step, before stdout, under the one write-failure rule: a failed
  write prints `al-sem: write error: <path>: <OS message>` and exits 2 (was `al-sem:
  failed to write baseline '<path>': <OS message>`, exit 3). Stdout stays empty in both.
- Library: `InputSet` is now `WorkspaceInputs` (read once per workspace path) and
  `InputNeeds` is `WorkspaceNeeds` (with `union`). The policy file and the baseline moved
  to a new per-command `RequestInputs`. `run_analyze_with_exit` takes the request and
  returns the baseline bytes instead of writing them; `save_baseline` is gone.
- **`analyze`, `digest`, `policy check` and `events` run through one batch driver
  (#277).** Each command is a job (`engine::batch`): the driver builds the view,
  prepares one plan and the job computes off it; its writes are an ordered list that
  a standalone run replays in today's order, so stdout, stderr, exit codes and files
  are unchanged. Two small differences: a validation error line is now written like
  every other stderr line, so when stderr is closed the command exits with its own
  write-failure code (analyze 2, every other command 1) instead of panicking; and the
  trace span `l4_l5.run_detectors` is gone (the detector run is the driver's `prepare`).
  `analyze.total` still spans the whole analyze run, model build included. The trace
  carries a `batch.driver` instant (`jobs`, `views`, `workers`).
- **`query`, `graph`, `prove`, `fingerprint` and `diff` run through the batch driver too
  (#277), and every view is built by one builder (`gate::run::build_view_model`).** Their
  stdout, stderr, exit codes and files are unchanged, and so are their validation errors
  and their closed-stderr exit (as above). `query` reads its view's model and `l4` by
  borrow and keeps its own `Arc` of the graph; before its render it releases the view's
  relation and the cross-app base's prepare-only parts (a new `Cell::Base`), so they die
  where they did before. `graph` gets the cross-app program from the builder
  before any model is built from it. `fingerprint`'s `--shard` without `--out` is a job
  with no view. Library: `impact_graph::export_workspace`, `View::into_query_parts` and
  `AnalysisTarget::build_target` are gone (`GraphJob`, `QuerySubstrate::of(&view)` with the
  test entry `query_view`, and `build_view_model` replace them); `diff_strict_plan` is
  `diff_plan(detectors, strict)`; `R3a5CrossAppBase.rel` is read through `rel()`.
- **`prove`, `fingerprint --routine` and `fingerprint --inventory-only` share their view's
  one pass in a batch (#277 on #160 step 9).** Each is a tree job: `prove` asks its one
  root, the query its selected routines and the inventory nothing; the view composes once
  at the union, and each job's tree is composed over its own subjects, read, and dropped
  before `det`. A batch of the inventory, two queries and a prove gives each job its
  standalone bytes. `fingerprint`'s full snapshot and the query forms with no `--routine` stay on their
  own single-app snapshot. Library: the fingerprint reads are `TreeRead::FingerprintQuery`
  / `TreeRead::Inventory` on a job's `TreeDemand` (prove's gap count is
  `TreeDemand.gaps_in_cone`), `View::take_tree_read` takes a `JobId`, and the
  `program::inputs::InputSet` alias is gone (use `WorkspaceInputs`).
- **`diff ws ws`: both sides share one view (#277).** Two workspace sides that name one
  directory (after `std::path::absolute`, not canonicalised) are now read and built once;
  each side still composes its own snapshot. Output is unchanged. Counters
  (program, combined_graph, cone, summaries_v2, graph_scc, pd_solve, detector_context,
  snapshot, witness_pass, inputs.read): without `--strict` 2, 2, 2, 0, 2, 2, 0, 2, 2, 2
  → **1**, 2, 2, 0, 2, 2, 0, 2, 2, **1**; with `--strict` 2, 4, 4, 2, 6, 4, 2, 2, 2, 2 →
  **1, 3, 3, 1, 4, 3, 1**, 2, 2, **1** (one detector run serves both sides' gates). Also:
  every workspace side is read before the first build, so a `diff` whose old workspace
  side fails now counts the new side's read (`inputs.read` 2, was 1; still no new-side
  build and the same error); the `diff --strict` trace releases the view's cells once.
- **Traces (#277).** A view's post-attach phase now ends when the driver drops the view
  (every command; `diff` ended it per side before), so `peak.post_attach_mb` no longer
  covers a command's writes. Every single-app view build now opens `preflight.fresh_program`
  and `l3.assemble_resolve` (only `analyze --single-app` did), and every cross-app model
  build opens `crossapp.base_total` (only `analyze` did; `graph`'s program-only build opens
  none): `scripts/trace_summary.py` shows those rows for more commands.

- **Grammar: tree-sitter-al `main` at `c89c2ecb`** (D1, a parser state-reduction pass;
  package version still 4.4.1; was `960ed312`). `node-types.json` is byte-identical, so the
  generated vocabulary, `kind_policy` and the 501 named kinds did not move, and no valid
  input parses to a different tree. `CACHE_VERSION_GRAMMAR` is still bumped, to
  `tree-sitter-al-v4.4.1-c89c2ecb-native`: a smaller parse table changes the
  error-recovery trees of broken input, and a cache minted from those must not be reused.
  Measured old vs new: per-test outcomes identical (3,988 run, all pass, on both sides),
  zero goldens moved, the stamp kept its length so `dry-run.txt` did not move, CDO
  `--program-call-graph-stats` byte-identical, and zero recovered files and zero
  `parseIncomplete` routines on CDO on both sides.
- `alsem diff`: rename normalization is one hop, as a rule. A `--renames` target, or
  a paired signature change's new id, is never looked up again as an old id. With a
  user entry `X→T` and an old `T` paired to new `U`, `X`'s facts stay on `T` and old
  `T`'s go to `U`. The 2.0.1 notes called this a limit; it is the intended behaviour,
  because following the chain would put `X` and old `T` on one key (#237).
- `alsem graph`: the node id of a source object without a number, whose name holds an
  escaped quote (`""` in the source), now comes from its logical name, where `""` is
  one `"`. That is the same name the model's object id uses. Such ids change once;
  ids of every other object stay the same (#250).
- `looseFingerprint` for d4, d7, d12, d16, d18, d22, d39–d42, d43, d45, d48, d57, d59 and
  d60 is now built from what each check names as its subject, not cut out of
  `rootCauseKey`. Moving the problem to another routine of the same object keeps it. A
  renamed record variable keeps it too when its table is known (d4, d18, d22, d60), and a
  moved parameter keeps it for d59. Each check still keeps its event, called routine or
  global variable; d43 also keeps the object of the code that raises the event. d39–d42
  findings on different record tables, two primary d45 publishers on one table, d57
  globals named like `op1`, d16 self-calls, and d43 raises of one event from two objects
  no longer share a key. These values change once; `fingerprint` and `rootCauseKey` do
  not (#252).
- Digest, prove and fingerprint witnesses are the shortest paths to the nearest carrier (one
  BFS per root and first hop, CLRS §22.2); printed paths are no longer padded with longer
  ones; conditionality is read over the shortest witnesses; the witness BFS has no state
  limit, and the depth diagnostic is per fact; the ordering engine answers happens-before on
  demand (no change in d47/d49/d51 output). Part of #160 (step 6, D8). The BFS keeps every
  shortest-path predecessor (a DAG of all shortest paths), built once per (root, first hop)
  and shared by that root's facts, in digest and in the fingerprint query alike. A fact's
  witnesses are its distinct projected paths to the carriers at the least distance, plus
  the opaque call-site and op seeds, in (projected length, projected JSON) order, up to the
  caller's cap: an opaque seed and a carrier one hop away now sort by their hop JSON, not
  by raw hop count. `state-limit-exceeded` now comes only from the producer proofs, and
  `depth-exceeded` only marks a fact with no witness whose carrier lies past 64 hops. The
  effect merge keeps the 4 smallest distinct paths instead of every path (same output). The
  witness census line `digest.witness_dags=N nodes=N preds=N` joins `ALSEM_CONES_CENSUS=1`.
- #160 step 6: digest sees dependency effects (one cone graph, #161 digest half). Digest
  (cross-app, the default) now reports what a changed routine does through dependency code:
  effects reached through a call into a dependency app are grouped per call and effect
  type, with the dependency routine named (`enters <App>.<Routine>`), the number of
  resources and up to 10 of them. These groups are reported, not graded: their
  conditionality is `unknown`, and they never carry a must-guarantee. Witness paths stop at
  the dependency boundary. Every printed witness path is a shortest one.

  A group is one digest effect: `detail` is `{"boundary": "<App>.<Routine>",
  "resourceCount": "<N>", "resources": "<r1>, <r2>, …"}` (the first 10 distinct resources in
  resource-id order, each by its display name when it has one); `evidence` is the boundary
  call site (else the firing record operation of a trigger, else the publish site of an
  event), and `viaPaths` are the workspace-code prefixes up to it (`[]` when the root's own
  call is the boundary). A dependency effect behind a workspace subscriber or trigger that
  dependency code reaches also groups at the boundary. A group carries no
  `detail.tempState`. A temporary-record write and a physical write behind one boundary are
  two groups; their class shows only in the `factId` (the key carries it), so in the JSON
  the two differ only by their resources. A boundary call site with several dependency
  targets (an interface dispatch, a multi-candidate call) is one group that names every
  routine it enters, sorted: `"boundary": "<App>.<A>, <App>.<B>"`. A group behind an event
  that workspace code raises into a dependency subscriber is ordered at the call that raises
  it, so it takes part in the may-relations (a pending write at an HTTP call) like a call
  group. The producer proofs' cap counts distinct groups, not raw proofs, so many proofs
  behind one boundary no longer hide a proof through another.

  How: digest resolves its changed roots from the model before the view composes, so the
  view's one composition keeps those roots' raw facts and the digest tree is composed from
  it over the relation's cone graph (no second cone, graph, SCC or producer solve: build
  counters 1/1/1/2/1/1/1/1). The tree's call-site ledger reads the dependency routines' own
  calls too, and a resolved call whose every target is a body-less dependency routine is
  `unfetched-dependency`. The unresolved cone's order is now total: the old key (routine,
  file, line, callee) is unchanged, and the anchor column, then the candidate list, then the
  call-site id break its ties: two dependency rows with no
  anchor, the same routine and the same callee kept hash order, so `--deterministic` output
  differed between runs. The tree is released as soon as each root's effects and
  unresolved cone are read off it, before the detector run. d47/d49/d51 (the ordering
  cell), prove, fingerprint and diff stay on the cut graph; moving the ordering cell is the
  #161 follow-up, and until then its cut composition keeps raw facts for every routine
  (dependency rows included), the stated I5 exception.

  `digest --tests` (#254) builds its coverage graph off the same tree, so it changes too:
  a `[Test]` procedure that reaches a workspace routine only through dependency code (a
  dependency routine that calls it, or a dependency event the workspace routine subscribes
  to) now counts as covering it, and the dependency routines' own unresolved calls count
  toward `testsWithUnresolvedTraversal`. With no resolved root the block still reports every
  workspace test, as before.

  `policy check` reads the same view (Task 3): its one composition keeps the raw inherited
  facts of the workspace (primary) routines only, and the rule engine reads them beside the
  run's summaries. Policy no longer composes a second cone over every routine, dependency
  rows included (build counters 1/1/1/2/1/1/0/1, from 1/2/1/3/2/2/0/1). Output is unchanged.
  The policy-only `RAW_INHERITED_FACTS` substrate bit is deleted, and a summary's raw
  inherited half is now test-only. A rule that reads inherited facts still fails loudly
  (a panic naming the routine) when an evaluated routine has a summary but no raw
  entry, instead of passing it unseen; `facts: direct` rules never read that half.
- **d39 decides who persists an implicit `Rec` by an owner rule** (#272). It used to
  skip only a table-level OnInsert/OnModify/OnDelete/OnRename trigger
  (`autoPersistTriggerRec`); now that an implicit `Rec` argument binds (see Fixed), d39
  skips it wherever the caller or the platform writes `Rec` after the call
  (`implicitRecOwnerPersists`): any table or tableext procedure or field trigger (the
  caller owns `Rec`), every table and tableext trigger except tableext
  OnAfterInsert/OnAfterModify/OnAfterRename, and a page or pageext procedure or
  OnAction/OnValidate/OnLookup/OnAssistEdit/OnDrillDown/OnNewRecord/OnInsertRecord/
  OnModifyRecord/OnBefore/OnAfterAction/OnBefore/OnAfterValidate on a page (for a
  pageext, its base page) that is neither `Editable = false` nor `ModifyAllowed =
  false`. The trigger lists were measured on the BC 28.4 Linux sidecar through
  TestPage; a Windows Cronus confirmation is still owed, and OnBeforeValidate is by
  analogy. The delete triggers (table OnDelete, tableext OnAfterDelete, page
  OnDeleteRecord) are exempt as moot (the row is gone), not measured.
  d39 still reports `xRec`, OnAfterGetRecord and other page triggers, a read-only page,
  those three tableext triggers, and a routine that reloads `Rec` after the call.
  **Main limit:** a pageext over a dependency page is always exempt, because the model
  carries no `Editable`/`ModifyAllowed` for dependency (symbol-only) pages, so the
  read-only rule never fires for an extension of a Base App page. Known false
  negative, as before: a modifiable page opened in view mode loses the write too, but
  the open mode is a runtime fact.
- **d37 is more conservative at `Rec` call sites** (#272): a `Validate` on `Rec`
  followed by a call that hands `Rec` to an unresolved, ambiguous or arity-mismatched
  callee is now suppressed as unknown, exactly as for a local record. In cross-app mode
  this also suppresses d37 for dependency callers, whose calls have no callee edge in
  the workspace graph (CDO `--scope all`: d37 345 → 163; primary unchanged; measured on
  the final code, identical to the design prototype by fingerprint).
- **d11, d21 and d33 now see helper loads and filters on `Rec`** (#272): a `var` helper
  that loads (d11, d21) or filters (d33) the implicit `Rec` now counts, as it does for a
  local record (Base App single-app: d11 −20, all false positives; measured on the
  final code, identical to the design prototype by fingerprint).

### Fixed

- **An implicit `Rec`/`xRec` passed as a bare argument binds to its known table** (#272).
  On a table, tableext, pageext or page with a SourceTable, `Helper(Rec)` now starts as
  an upgradable binding, so d41 and d42 report it the way they report a local record
  (d40 still skips it). For `Rec` the finding has the same loose fingerprint as a local;
  `xRec`'s loose subject table stays `?` (not resolved, a stated non-goal). The
  `implicit-rec` label is now exact:
  the object must have its own record, and no parameter, local or object global of any
  type may be named `Rec`/`xRec`. An undeclared `Rec` in a codeunit without TableNo was
  labelled `implicit-rec`; it is now `unknown` (the `ws-argument-bindings` l2 goldens
  moved for that one site). A declared `Rec` of any type, scalar included, no longer
  leaves a phantom synthetic `Rec` record row; on a table or page an object-global
  record `Rec` binds `global` with its own table (robustness only: alc rejects such a
  global, AL0155). A codeunit `TableNo` or report dataitem `Rec` keeps its typed
  binding even next to a global `Rec`. An implicit-`Rec` argument on a page over a
  `TableType = Temporary` table is now temporary, as its `Rec` variable already was, so
  d39 no longer reports it there.
- **`digest` is no longer several times slower since #160 step 6** (#289). Step 6's
  proof cap (count distinct candidates after the boundary cut) made the proof walk
  hash each crossed partial path's full candidate key (the projected hops' JSON) on
  every pop, hundreds of millions of times on CDO. The walk now gives each distinct
  key a small number once, when it first meets it, and a pop checks that number in a
  list. The walk's order, its limits and its output are unchanged, and so is the
  cap's rule. A new unit test counts the key hashes on a CDO-shaped fixture (2, where
  the old walk made 1,094).
- **d43 sees a guarded IsHandled dispatch through a member call** (#271). It followed
  bare calls and object runs only, so `Mgr.OnBeforePost(IsHandled)` through a
  codeunit variable, a call on a record or page variable, and `this.OnBeforePost(..)`
  gave no finding; a dependency publisher reached through a variable did not either.
  d43 now also follows `variable-typed-call` edges (the same exact, resolved call as a
  bare one). Calls through an interface stay out on purpose: they are a may-call
  candidate set, which d43 would report as `confirmed`. d43 no longer checks for the
  `dependency-export` edge kind, which is never built.
- #160 step 9 (part of #160):
  - `fingerprint`'s `mayCommit` reads the inherited coverage when inherited facts are
    shown: a routine whose own body is fully analysed but whose cone is not now says
    `unknown`, not `no`. It reads the direct coverage with `--no-include-inherited`.
    One cli-b query golden moved (`ws-txn-d49-pos-modify-runmodal`).
  - A dependency app that ships source but has a body-less routine gets a
    `body-unavailable` gap for that routine, not an app-level `symbol-only-boundary` gap
    (which names only an app with no source). Both kinds still block `prove`. This also
    removes a debug-build panic on a cross-app inventory of such a workspace.
- `alsem diff`: a `--renames` entry for a table field or key is no longer called
  stale (`rename-overlay-stale`, `not-in-old` or `not-in-new`) when the field exists.
  Field and key ids have schema facts but no `identities` row, and only identities
  were checked. An id now counts as present when it has an identity row or is the
  subject of a fact (#237).
- Interface calls whose value provably comes from a non-extensible source enum are now
  a closed candidate set. That means a routine-local interface variable whose every
  write comes from such an enum, in a cleanly parsed routine with no `with`, where
  every implementation the enum maps is a loaded routine. The resolver edge is
  `Complete`, the model's `DispatchMeta` lists the enums in `closed_over`, the
  combined graph emits no `interface-open-world` uncertainty, the snapshot row has
  `openWorld: false`, and `prove`/`digest` see no unresolved-call blocker for it. d35
  therefore no longer reports an unknown Commit for such a call; a Commit in one of
  the candidates is still reported. Routes, shapes and the call-graph histograms do
  not change (byte-identical on CDO). Two outputs show the closed edges: the graphify
  export's `open_world_reason` is empty for them (the edge is `Complete`), and
  `aldump --switch-dump` prints the new `closed_over` field. Enums known only from
  symbols, a dependency implementer outside the model (`--single-app`) and names that
  are not unique in the whole program stay open. Known limit: the candidates are every
  implementer of the interface, so an implementer the enum does not map still counts;
  if it commits, d35 still reports YES (#264).
- `#if` alternatives no longer type code by their first arm: a routine declared in
  two arms that differ only in the return type has no return type in the program
  graph (a call's result is not typed from it), and a table declared in two arms
  keeps the fields of both, so a field declared with two types is not typed either.
  A call site inside two `#if` alternatives of one routine is closed only when it
  is closed in every arm (#264).
- An object without a number, in a dependency that ships only symbols, whose name
  holds two quote characters in a row (`""`) now has the same id in the program graph
  and in the model. Before, the graph id dropped one of the two quotes (#250).
- An `<owner>::<routine>` selector no longer falls back to another object's routine
  (#239). In `digest`, `fingerprint` and `prove`, when the named owner declares no routine
  of that name, the selector is unmatched: digest `selector-unmatched`, fingerprint
  `selector-unresolved`, prove `answer: unknown`, each exit 2. Before, it silently selected
  another object's routine (2.0.1's #78 entry: "the selector matches as before"). An owner
  spelled any way the owner display does not, for example by object number
  (`Codeunit 50101::Persist`), is unmatched too.
  - The object part is either typed (`Codeunit Sel A`, `Codeunit "Sel A"`, `Codeunit "A
    ""B"" C"`), which matches only that full owner, or a bare object name (`Sel A`,
    `"Sel A"`), which matches every owner of that name. So `Codeunit "Sel A"::Persist`
    never selects a `Table "Codeunit Sel A"`. An unquoted bare name whose first word is a
    type word (`Page Management`) reads as typed; quote it to select it by bare name.
  - A bare name two owners share (`Codeunit "Sel B"` and `Table "Sel B"`) is ambiguous.
    The digest diagnostic and fingerprint's human error list both owners as candidates;
    fingerprint's JSON diagnostic has no candidate list, and prove reports `unknown`.
  - The routine part may be quoted too (`Codeunit "Sel A"::"Post Document"`), and so may
    a bare routine selector (`"Post Document"`). One outer quote pair is removed and
    `""` stays, since routine names are shown as written in source (`Post ""X""`). A
    `::` inside quotes does not split the selector. An empty object part (`::Persist`)
    is the bare routine name.
  - The owner fallback that 2.0.3's #240 entry mentions is gone. The escaped spelling
    (`Codeunit "A ""B"" C"::P`) is supported in the object part of such a selector. An
    object whose name is itself quoted (`"""Legacy"""`, shown `Codeunit "Legacy"`) is
    selected by either spelling.
  - `fingerprint --format human` adds one line to an unmatched `<owner>::<routine>` error
    naming the owners that do declare the routine
    (`declared as: Codeunit Sel B::Persist`). The digest diagnostic, fingerprint's JSON
    and prove do not name them.
- An object split across `#if` arms with different names under one id
  (`#if A codeunit 50100 "Foo" … #else codeunit 50100 "Bar" … #endif`) now names each
  routine's own arm as its owner (#241). Before, every routine of both arms showed the
  last arm's name (`Codeunit Bar::P` for `Foo`'s `P`). This fixes the `query effects`
  and `query touches` headers and effect lines, the `query effects` `Object.Routine`
  selector (`Foo.P`) and its ambiguity list, digest, fingerprint and prove
  `objectDisplay` and headers, the `objectName` of `alsem analyze` finding locations
  (JSON, SARIF, HTML, terminal; fingerprints do not change), and the
  `<owner>::<routine>` selector of #239:
  `Codeunit Foo::P` now selects `P`, and `Codeunit Bar::P` is unmatched. The owner is the
  object declaration that contains the routine.
  - Limit: this holds when the two arms' routines have different signatures. A routine
    declared with one signature in both arms is one routine id, so digest, fingerprint
    and prove show one owner for it: the FIRST arm (before, the last). Its selector with
    the second arm's name (`Codeunit Bar::P`) is now the unmatched one, where
    `Codeunit Foo::P` was. In that same-signature case, `query effects` effect lines may
    name the other arm's object.
  - Limit: an `analyze` finding anchored on the object itself rather than a routine
    (d64) still names the last arm.

### Removed

- `aldump --issue160-full-graph-timings`, the measurement-only mode of #160 step 6.

## [2.0.3] - 2026-10-23

### Added

- `alsem digest --tests` (#254) adds a `payload.testCoverage` block. It says which
  changed routines a `[Test]` procedure of the workspace reaches through the resolved
  call graph. Without the flag the document is unchanged (`schemaVersion` stays
  `1.6.0`). With `--format human` it adds one line, for example `test coverage: 6 of
  10 changed routines reached; 11 [Test] procedures considered (partial: …)`. The rules:
  - A test root is a workspace routine with the `[Test]` attribute. A configured root
    kind alone does not make one.
  - `[Test]` procedures and every routine of a `Subtype = Test` codeunit leave the
    count (`excludedTestCode` says how many).
  - The search follows calls, implicit triggers, resolved object runs, every interface
    candidate, event dispatch, and the handlers a test names in `[HandlerFunctions]`.
  - A routine is `covered` when some test reaches it. `reachedFrom` names the test with
    the lowest stable id. `viaEvent` is true when every shortest path from that test
    crosses an event.
  - Every changed root counts, even one the digest has no entry for.
  - Each `uncovered` routine has one `reason` (the first that fits):
    - `declaration-only`: an interface or ControlAddIn method. It has no body to run.
    - `not-in-graph`: a changed root the digest found but has no entry for.
    - `platform-event-subscriber`: it subscribes to a platform event, which no
      routine raises. It is not used when it also subscribes to a workspace event.
    - `dependency-event-subscriber`: it subscribes to an event a dependency raises,
      and no test reaches that publisher. The same exception applies.
    - `no-path`: no test reaches it.
  - `ratio` is covered / changed, and `null` when no production routine changed.
  - `coverage` is `partial` when a routine some test reaches has something the search
    cannot follow. `reasons` lists the codes, and `testsWithUnresolvedTraversal` counts
    the tests that hit one of these:
    - `dynamic-target`, `unresolved-receiver-type`, `unresolved-member`: a call whose
      target is not known.
    - `ambiguous`: a call to one of several overloads.
    - `interface-open-world`: an interface call whose implementations may not all be
      known.
    - `object-run-unresolved`: a `Run` of an object that is not known.
    - `test-page`: a `TestPage` or `TestRequestPage` the routine uses. What it drives
      is not followed.
    - `parse-incomplete`: the routine did not parse fully.
    - `body-unavailable`: a workspace routine with no body.
    - `no-coverage-record`: the analysis has no record for the routine.
    - `unknown-status`: a call status this version does not know.

    `testsCallingDependencyCode` counts the tests that reach dependency code. Its codes
    are `external` and `unfetched-dependency` (a call into a dependency), and
    `dependency-code` and `opaque-dependency` (a dependency routine, with or without a
    body).

  Limits: calls inside dependency code are not seen, so a subscriber to an event raised
  only there is uncovered. Platform events have no publisher to reach. What a `TestPage`
  drives is not followed. A test codeunit's `OnRun` is not a root.
- `al-call-hierarchy --project <ws> --analyze --format json` gains a `test_quality` block
  (#253), after `summary`, so existing keys keep their order. Text and CSV do not change.
  It has three parts. `procedures` holds one row per `[Test]` procedure; its `path`,
  `line`, `object_*`, `procedure_name` and `routine_id` equal that routine's `metrics`
  row. `object_stable_id` is the issue's object key, `<appGuid>/Codeunit/<n>` (the
  internal object id). It is not a prefix of `routine_id`, which uses the colon form
  `<appGuid>:Codeunit:<n>#…`; both are `null` in the same cases. `codeunits` sums the
  rows per test object: one row per `(path, object type, object number)`, so an object
  written whole in both arms of an `#if` is one row (an object with no number is keyed by
  its start line). `workspace` sums all of them. Each row has
  `assert_count`, `assert_count_reachable`, `zero_assert`, `has_asserterror` and
  `are_equal {total, literal_expected, expression_expected}`.
  How it counts: an assert is a call `X.M(..)` whose receiver `X` is declared (local,
  then parameter, then object global; `this.X` looks at globals) as `Codeunit Assert` or
  `Codeunit "Library Assert"`, any method, plus each `asserterror` statement.
  `assert_count` is the test's own body. Both arms of an in-body `#if` count.
  `assert_count_reachable` adds the own count of every routine the test reaches through
  resolved calls (call, `Codeunit.Run`, implicit trigger) in the **same app**. "Same app"
  means the test file's own app root, the deepest folder with an `app.json`. Routines in
  nested apps and in dependencies are not followed, and each routine counts once per
  test. `zero_assert` is `assert_count_reachable == 0`. Without a call graph (no
  `app.json`, or the program snapshot could not be built) both are `null`, and so are
  the sums that include them. With a graph, a test that has no matching declaration in
  it gets its own count (no callees are known), so it does not make the sums `null`.
  `literal_expected` means the first argument of `AreEqual`/`AreNotEqual`/`AreNearlyEqual`
  is a literal (number, text, boolean, date `0D`/`20261023D`, time `0T`, datetime `0DT`,
  BigInteger `123L`), a signed number, an enum/option value or `Database::X`. A `Label`
  or `Text` constant counts as an expression.
  Limits: event subscribers are not followed. Calls inside `with Assert do` are not
  matched, and neither are numeric receivers (`Codeunit 130000`). Unresolved calls are
  not followed. Handlers that the test framework calls are not counted. Interface calls
  follow every implementation. A routine written in two object-level `#if` arms is one
  routine in the call graph: a test split that way counts only its own arm's asserts as
  `assert_count`, but reaches the callees of BOTH arms, and a helper split that way
  counts the asserts of both arms. A root-app call to a routine that a nested app also
  declares with the same object type and number (and signature) is credited to the
  root app's routine: the graph merges the two (program-graph identity, #250).
  On the CDO Test app (139 files): 1844 tests, 3316 own asserts, 3491 reachable, 88 tests
  with no own assert and 58 with none reachable, 1096 of 1528 `AreEqual`-family calls
  with a literal expected value. JSON run time, median of 15 runs, release-fast: 183 ms
  before, 193 ms after. Text and CSV do no extra work.
- `alsem analyze --format json`: every finding gains `looseFingerprint` (#247), a key
  that stays equal when the same problem moves to another routine of the same object.
  `fingerprint` is byte-identical: it is still the same problem in the same routine, and
  baselines still use it. Inline suppression uses neither key (it matches check, file and
  line). `looseFingerprint` is the fingerprint's five parts with the routine name blanked
  and the anchor routine's id (internal or stable form) cut out of the root-cause key,
  together with the one site id minted on it (`/op3`, `/cs1`, `/loop0`, `/u2`). What
  follows that segment stays (d60's `…/loop0/p1` keeps `p1`), and so does a parameter
  position `/p{N}` (d19, d32). When the anchor is not a routine (d64) it equals
  `fingerprint`. It is **not unique**: several findings can share one. So count new
  findings per key: **new = Σ max(0, after(k) − before(k))** over `looseFingerprint`
  values k. To name which findings are new, pair findings equal on both keys first, then
  on `looseFingerprint`; equal `fingerprint` does not imply equal `looseFingerprint` (d48),
  so only that order agrees with the count. Compare two reports only with no
  `--baseline`, no `--limit`, the same `--scope`, `--min-severity`,
  `--detector`/`--preset` and dependency coverage, and the same inline `// al-sem-ignore`
  comments (suppression is always on), or findings drop out before the JSON is written.
  Limits: the count cancels (fix one, add a same-key one in the same object = 0 new), and
  these checks keep a routine-bound part, so a move there changes the key: local names
  (d4, d18, d22, d57, d60), parameter positions (d19, d32, d59, d39–d42), other cycle
  members (d7), the event name (d12), the event (d38), the caller (d43), the loop routine
  (d48; a direct↔transitive move also changes it). d16 keeps the callee, but a self-call
  strips both ids, so every obsolete self-call in one object shares a key. d39–d42 carry
  no table, and two primary d45 publishers in one object exposing one table share a key.
  A local variable named exactly like a site id (`op2`, `cs1`, `loop0`, `u3`) that comes
  straight after the routine id (d22, d57) is stripped with it, so two such variables in
  one object share a key.
  JSON only: SARIF `fingerprints` would merge results with an equal value. The
  `schemaVersion` does not change (the key is additive).

### Changed

- d35 (Commit in an event subscriber) now reports an unknown answer — no Commit found in
  the subscriber or proven in its callees, but call coverage incomplete — at medium
  severity instead of high (#256). A Commit found directly or via a callee stays high.
  Confidence, ids, fingerprints and loose fingerprints are unchanged, so baselines and
  suppressions keep matching. Such findings no longer trip `analyze --fail-on high` or
  show under `--min-severity high`; SARIF reports them as warnings. `alsem policy check`
  is unchanged. On the pinned CDO workspace, 41 of 52 d35 findings (primary scope; 83 of
  162 at `--scope all`) move to medium; primary `bySeverity.high` drops from 577 to 536.
  This supersedes #148's note that the unknown answer keeps severity high.

### Fixed

- An object or table whose quoted name holds an escaped quote (`"A ""B"" C"`) is shown
  by its logical name (`A "B" C`) everywhere (#240, #249): digest and fingerprint
  `objectDisplay`, `query` owners and table names, the identity table, contracts, the
  HTML report, SARIF and finding text. The ids already used the logical name (#83).
  The R0 identity snapshot and the L2 projection name the object the same way.
  - The contract `signatureFingerprint` of such an object, its R0 identity
    `signatureFingerprint` (`aldump`'s R0 dump), and the table
    `schemaFacts.shapeFingerprint` of such a table, change once. `alsem diff` of a
    snapshot made before this fix against one made after reports the contract change as
    `ProcedureSignatureChanged`; its schema pass compares shape fingerprints only for
    fields and enum values, not for tables.
  - Every name the model stores is the logical name, unescaped exactly once where it is
    produced: object and table names, `SourceTable`, `extends`, a record variable's
    table (also the L2 projection's and an event parameter's `tableName`), `TableNo`, a
    report dataitem's table and a `Codeunit.Run` target. A dependency's quoted
    (source-shaped) `SourceTable` / `TargetObject` and its already-quoted parameter
    type (`Record "A""B"`) are unescaped once too; its bare names are already logical.
    So the lookups compare logical with logical.
  - A source reference written with `""` to a dependency object now resolves (it missed
    before: the source text kept `""`, the dependency's symbol name did not), so effects
    and findings on that table can appear. A dependency parameter typed
    `Record "A""B"` binds the table `A"B` (it took `A""B`).
  - A record variable typed `Record "A ""B"" C"` keeps its whole table name; the name
    used to stop at the first inner quote (`A `). A table that is not loaded is
    described by its logical name (`A "B" C (type not loaded)`).
  - `TableNo = "Q ""X"""` (a name ending in an escaped quote) binds `Q "X"`: exactly
    one outer quote pair is stripped (it stripped every trailing quote).
  - Selectors and the policy field `object.name` match the logical name. The escaped
    spelling is not supported, though it may still match through the owner fallback
    of a `<Object>::<routine>` selector until #239 removes it.
  - Limits: an uncertainty edge's `interfaceName` still shows the raw name; it is an
    input to `edgeId`. The program engine's graph names (`ObjKey::Name`, receiver
    type text) stay raw, so the call resolver still compares raw source names with
    logical dependency names (#250).

## [2.0.2] - 2026-10-23

### Changed

- Digest `stableId` values of #71's declaration-only roots change once (#83). With a unique
  object id (see Fixed) the id no longer folds the object name in as a member: it is
  `{guid}:Interface:@ifoo#{hash}`, the shape the dependency side gives the same method. The
  digest schema version does not change. **Upgrade note:** a stored baseline or gate
  snapshot that holds a numberless object id (`…:Interface:0`, `…:ControlAddIn:0`), a
  dependency interface routine id, or a declaration-only id reports those objects as removed
  (critical) and re-added once; re-mint it with this version (see Fixed). Numbered ids are
  unchanged.

### Fixed

- An object without a number now gets a unique object id (#83). Interface and ControlAddIn
  have no number, and a numbered kind whose number does not parse has none either; every
  such object was `…:<Kind>:0`, so two of one kind in one app shared an id. The identity
  table and every map keyed by the id kept only one of them, the contracts carried duplicate
  ids, and the fingerprint object part was shared by them (the identity table and the
  fingerprint are pinned by tests). The key is now `@` + the folded name,
  percent-encoded outside `a-z 0-9` (`…:Interface:@iprocessor`), from every producer: R0, the
  model, the program graph, R1a and the dependency projection
  (`engine::ids::object_key`). Two dependency interfaces without `Id` that declare a method
  of the same signature no longer share routine ids, and a finding fingerprint's object part
  uses the key, not `{type}/{number}`. Numbered ids do not change. The identity table stays
  ordinal and the contracts stay `locale_compare`, so a numbered and a numberless object of
  one kind list in a different order in each. The differential harness now fails on two
  object rows with one id. **Limits:** an object with an empty name gets `@` and can still
  collide; a table whose number does not parse still collides (`encode_table_id`), and d33's
  object-id to table-id join (`engine/l5/detectors/mod.rs`) no longer matches it
  (non-compiling input); a dependency object whose logical name contains `""` gets a
  different id from the graph (`model_object_id`) than from the dependency projection;
  existing ABI/graph object-kind mismatches (DotNetPackage, PermissionSetExtension,
  Profile, Entitlement) are unchanged.
- **`alsem diff` no longer reports a critical `procedure-signature-changed` when a change adds
  an Interface or ControlAddIn (#83, #245).** Both objects had the id `…:Interface:0`, so the
  untouched old one looked changed (named after the new one) when the new file sorted
  last, and the addition went unreported when it sorted first. Now the diff reports only
  the new object's `object-added` (info). **The stable id of an object without a number
  (Interface, ControlAddIn) changes shape** from `{appId}:Interface:0` to
  `{appId}:Interface:@{name}` (e.g. `…:Interface:@repro%20transport`), because the number
  was the only part that told two such objects apart and they have none. A consumer with a
  stored baseline (a fingerprint, gate snapshot or digest) sees those ids move once. The
  snapshot schema version stays 4, so `alsem diff` accepts a pre-#83 baseline (only the
  `alsem-version-mismatch` warning fires), and **the first diff against it reports the old
  `…:Interface:0` object and its routines as `object-removed` / `procedure-removed`
  (critical)**, plus an `object-added` per new id. The remedy is to re-mint the baseline with
  this version. CentralGauge, which reported #245, has no stored baseline yet.
- Lookups of an object by type and number (record typing's numeric `SourceTable`, an
  unresolved `Codeunit.Run(<number>)` target) no longer pick an arbitrary object without a
  number for number `0` (#83).
- `aldump --graphify-export` keys an object without a number by the engine's object key in
  its `al:obj:`, `al:rtn:` and `al:abi:` node ids (`…/interface/@i%20foo#…`). Before, a
  dependency object's `al:abi:` id carried `0`, and the other ids carried a lossy slug, so
  `I Foo` and `I-Foo` (or two dependency interfaces with a same-named method) shared a node
  (#83). The LSP `al-preview:` URI keeps its `Id` segment (`0` for such an object): it is
  wire format, and the object's name is in the `Name` segment.
- **`alsem diff` no longer reports a parameter appended to a `local` or `internal` event
  publisher as critical (#236).** For an `[IntegrationEvent]` or `[BusinessEvent]` publisher that
  is `local` or `internal` on both sides, adding parameters at the END is not a break
  (AppSourceCop AS0025: subscribers bind by name). Such a change now gives no `abi`
  `procedure-signature-changed` finding, and its `events` signature finding
  (`event-publisher-signature-changed` or `event-contract-changed-with-affected-subscribers`)
  is Low instead of Critical. Removing, retyping or flipping `var` on a parameter stays critical,
  as does an append that also changes the event attribute's arguments (e.g. `IncludeSender`),
  and so do `public`/`protected` publishers and `ExternalBusinessEvent`. The rule is **stricter
  than AS0025 on purpose**: a parameter inserted in the middle, or a reorder, is critical here
  too. To see the parameters, a publisher's contract fact in the snapshot gains a `parameters`
  list (e.g. `"var handled: boolean"`); a snapshot made before this change has none, so its
  publisher changes stay critical.
- **`alsem diff` now reports a renamed or reordered event parameter (#236).** The signature
  fingerprint holds parameter types only, so a pure rename (AS0025: breaks subscribers, which
  bind by name) or a reorder of same-type parameters used to give no finding at all. For an
  `[IntegrationEvent]` or `[BusinessEvent]` publisher whose `parameters` list changed, `alsem
  diff` now gives the Critical `abi` `procedure-signature-changed` and `events` signature
  findings. Needs both snapshots made with this version. When both snapshots carry the lists,
  these findings' `details` also hold `oldParameters` and `newParameters`, since their hashes
  and event ids can be equal.

## [2.0.1] - 2026-10-23

### Added

- **`al-call-hierarchy --project <ws> --analyze --format json` reports call-graph and identity data
  per routine (#159).** Every existing field keeps its name, value and order; text and CSV output
  are unchanged (they also skip the call-graph build, so they cost what they did). Each
  `metrics[]` row gains, after `quality_score`:
  - `path`: the workspace-relative POSIX path (`file` stays the base name).
  - `object_id` (the object number; `null` when none is declared), `access` (`local` | `internal`
    | `protected` as declared, else `public`, triggers included), `is_event_subscriber`,
    `is_trigger`.
  - `routine_id`: equals alsem's `stableRoutineId`, so two overloads get different ids. It changes
    when the app id, the object type or number, the routine's name, a parameter type or `var`, the
    return type, or (for a member trigger) the enclosing member changes; matching a changed routine
    across two versions is left to the consumer. `null` without an app id (no readable
    `app.json`), for a file inside a nested app (a folder below the project with its own
    `app.json`: the root's app id is not its own), and, independent of the call graph, for
    Interface and ControlAddIn members (signatures; `alsem digest` does mint a `stableId` for
    them, this field does not), object kinds alsem gives no id, and nameless routines.
  - `fan_in` / `fan_out`: the number of DISTINCT callers / callees in the resolved call graph the
    LSP serves. A publisher counts as a caller of its wired subscriber; a publisher's subscribers
    count as its callees. `fan_out` counts distinct targets, not the call-hierarchy panel's rows:
    every candidate of a conditional call counts (an interface call with 3 implementations adds
    3), builtin and unresolved calls never do. The panel also hides a caller it cannot locate
    (a symbols-only dependency publisher), so `fan_in` can exceed its row count. `null` (never
    `0`) when there is no graph for the row: the graph could not be built, or the row has no
    matching declaration; also `null` for Interface and ControlAddIn members, which are never a
    call target.

  `findings[]` gains category `unused_procedure` (severity `info`), appended after every existing
  finding, for exactly the procedures the LSP's `unused-procedure` diagnostic reports (the same
  rule and code), behind the same `unusedProcedures` setting; `summary` does not count them.
  Each carries an extra `path` (workspace-relative), so two files with the same base name are told
  apart; existing findings have no `path` key. A subscribed but never raised publisher has
  `fan_in: 0` and is not unused (the rule counts its subscribers). When the graph cannot be
  built, one warning with the reason goes to stderr (`no app.json at the project root`, else `the
  program snapshot could not be built`), `fan_in`/`fan_out` are `null`, and no unused procedure is
  reported, so their absence is then no evidence.
  The graph uses `--dependency-source` (default `embedded`, as the LSP; measured on a small
  workspace with the Microsoft Base Application in `.alpackages`: about +2.5 s and ~565 MB per
  run, or +1.2 s and +160 MB with `--dependency-source symbols`). Dependencies are read only from
  `.alpackages` folders (the workspace's own, then each parent's up to the git boundary); to use
  a symbol store kept elsewhere, make `<ws>/.alpackages` a symlink to it. Without the dependency
  `.app`s, every subscriber to a dependency event is reported `unused_procedure` with `fan_in: 0`,
  exactly as in the editor.
  `analysis::analyze_project` is the library entry point. It shares the LSP's unused rule and its
  caller grouping (`lsp::handlers::incoming_callers`, now also behind the call-hierarchy panel),
  and the L2 projection's stable-id helpers (`stable_object_id_ir`/`stable_routine_id_ir`).
  `program::model::workspace` and `engine::snapshot` still compose `stableRoutineId` on their
  own; the `--analyze` test pins its ids to `alsem fingerprint --inventory-only`.
- **An operator-set, time-limited GitHub CI waiver for the issue flow** (`scripts/agentflow`). During the
  2026-10-22 GitHub Actions incident the operator decided to rely on local tests for 24 h. `ci_waiver_until`
  in `.agent/config.json` (an ISO-8601 UTC time, operator-only, never set by the conductor) lets
  `merge-gate`/`merge` accept a PR whose CI is not green, but only before that time and only when the
  attestation records every required local gate (`ci-steps-all`, `check-goldens-coverage`, `check-goldens`,
  and `cdo-gate` unless docs-only) at exit 0. Both commands then report `ci_waived: true` and the deadline;
  `merge` posts a PR comment saying CI was waived and records `ci_waived_until` in its merge record. An
  expired or absent waiver changes nothing, a malformed one is a `ConfigError`, and a `closes_by: ci-wait`
  register entry still needs its green `ci-wait` record.
- **A daily grammar-drift check** (`.github/workflows/grammar-drift.yml`). It compares tree-sitter-al
  `main`'s `node-types.json` with the committed `node-types.sha256` and, on a mismatch, opens one
  `grammar-drift` issue (none if one is already open) with an Acceptance section, so the grammar bump lands
  as its own PR instead of turning every PR's CI red. It sees vocabulary changes only, not shape changes
  that keep the vocabulary. It can also be run by hand (`workflow_dispatch`).
- **#160 step 8 (#220): the snapshot says which analysis it holds, and whose each row is**
  (spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-22-issue-220-roles-snapshot-schema-4-design.md`).
  - A new header, `analysisUniverse` (`"single-app"` or `"cross-app"`), right after `generatedAt`.
    Every command still writes `"single-app"`; a cross-app snapshot comes with step 9.
  - A `role` (`"primary"` or `"dependency"`) on every `apps[]` row and every analysis-gap row.
  - Key classes in code (`SNAPSHOT_KEYS`, `REFERENCES`, `NON_REFERENCE_FIELDS` in
    `snapshot_full`): each top-level key has a class that says which of its rows a cross-app
    snapshot keeps, and each field that names another row (an identity, an operation, a call
    site, an edge, a frame or an app) is listed with what it names. A cross-app snapshot keeps the
    workspace's own rows plus every row they refer to. `closure_violations` reports any kept
    reference that points at a row that was left out; it is a test-time check only: no command
    calls it, so nothing checks a snapshot's references when it is written or read.
  - A new fatal `diff` preflight diagnostic, `analysis-universe-mismatch`, for two snapshots of
    different universes.

### Changed

- **#156: snapshot routine contract facts carry `routineKind`, and field schema facts carry
  `name`.** Both keys are additive, so the schema stays 4 and an older snapshot without them
  still diffs (field findings then show the stable id, as before).
- **#220: snapshot schema 4.** `schemaVersion` is now 4. A schema 3 file is refused when it is
  loaded, with the remedy: re-create it with `alsem fingerprint`. The 12 vendored `diff` inputs
  were upgraded by hand (three edits each) and every diff output stayed byte-identical. The
  routine-inventory document is version 1.2.0: `apps[].role`, `payload.analysisUniverse`, and a
  cross-app `routineInventory` that lists the workspace's own routines only.
- **#220: `alsem diff` refuses inputs it cannot compare.** A file with no `analysisUniverse` or an
  unknown one, an `apps[]` row with no `role` or an unknown one, or a non-empty `apps[]` without
  exactly one `primary` row is refused at load (exit 1), and so is a file whose `apps` is missing
  or not an array. A dependency shard gets the hint "diff the full snapshot or the primary shard".
  An empty `apps[]` (no `app.json` id) still loads. The app-identity check compares guids
  case-insensitively, so a guid whose letter case changed is the same app.
- **#220, a behaviour change: a fatal `diff` preflight now exits 1.** Before, `app-identity-mismatch`
  and `alsem-version-mismatch` under `--coverage-policy strict` printed their diagnostic and exited 0, so
  CI could not see the refusal. The exit 1 comes before the coverage and `--fail-on` gates; the
  printed output is unchanged.
- **#220: one role rule.** `Model::role_of_app` (and `role_of_stable_id` for readers that hold
  only ids) decides whether a row is the workspace's own or a dependency's, comparing app guids
  case-insensitively. The per-site comparisons spec §3.1 lists now call it; the readers of
  `dep_routine_ids` (entry points, transaction spans, event flow) read the set the rule builds,
  and d1's all-primary anchor map is kept on purpose (spec §3.1). Analysis gaps for dependency
  rows are now derived (the Rust port had always stubbed them off): a cross-app snapshot keeps the
  gaps of dependency code the workspace can reach. A dependency routine that lost its body to a
  parse error gets its `parse-incomplete` gap and does not mark its app as symbol-only.

- #160 step 11b: routine identity corrections, `RoutineIx` re-keying, and one rule for rows
  that share one routine id (part of #160; spec
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-22-issue-160-step11b-routine-rekeying-design.md`). In the
  reports the identity runs compare (`alsem analyze`, SARIF and JSON, on CDO and on every
  fixture dir, both universes and both scopes, plus the CDO call-graph histogram) the only
  output change is: in each cross-app CDO report, 14 `d9-transaction-span-summary` results
  say "publishes N event(s)" with N one higher. No golden moved. Cross-app `digest` and
  `fingerprint` were not compared on CDO (spec §8): for routines whose cone reaches
  `PageManagement` they may carry the same extra event. Identity runs and census:
  `docs/measurements/2026-10-22-issue-160-step11b.md`.
  - **The corrections (stage C).** Each reads a row's true node (`RowNodes.node_of`): J2
    still looks a node up by its declaration anchor, but keeps only a row at that anchor
    whose node IS that node; the adapter's caller check compares the row's node with the
    edge's caller (it compared their declaration anchors); the event graph maps a
    subscriber row to its node (J5's span map is gone). The first
    `#if` arm of the Base Application's `GetPurchaseHeaderPageID` now gets its 5 program
    edges (they were `Unknown(NoProgramSite)`), and one of them raises
    `OnAfterGetPurchaseHeaderPageID`: that is the 14 `d9` moves. `RowNodes.decl_anchor`,
    `j5_node` and `RowNodes::build`'s `edges`/`demand` parameters are deleted.
  - **The re-keying (stage A, byte-neutral).** `RoutineIx` (a row's position) is stored in
    `CallEdge.from_ix`; the L4 interner's index is renamed `SolveIx`. The carrier is split:
    the relation holds a `PrimaryGraph` and the Cone payload apart. The rule-bearing producers
    emit per row, and `program/model/projection.rs` turns their per-row output into the
    per-id input every computation takes (the cone, the solve, the event graph and the spans
    stay per id). Every union payload type is `Ord`.
  - **The one rule (stage B).** Only ids with two or more rows change. Set-valued inputs are
    the full-value union of the rows' values (equal items collapse, unequal ones are all
    kept, ordered by today's sort key and then the total order); coverage takes the least
    complete status and the sorted union of reasons; flags are OR-ed. Single-valued lookups
    take the LAST OWNING row per key, and every piece of one key comes from that row: a call
    site's edge and bindings, an operation's order and scope frame, a parameter's role.
    What changed, point by point:
    - direct facts, coverage and leaf/base summaries (R2a/R2b/R2c, #13): the union (a
      summary's uncertainties ordered by `uncertainty_key`, then the full value);
    - the collided edge and uncertainty lists (class U): ordered by full value, equal items
      collapse; one interface uncertainty per call site, from its last owning row (R1b);
      a collided id's interface site counts each implementer once (R1c);
    - the per-site consumers read one pick (`site_pick`): d37 (over the row's OWN call
      sites: another arm's sites are never "after" this row's `Validate`; a site whose
      LAST owning row is another row reads as unknown, since its callee and bindings
      are that row's),
      `compose_roles_only` (over the id's owned call sites) and the role walker's call
      transfer (`cfg_walker`); R9 `resolved_call_edge_by_callsite` takes the owning row's
      edge;
    - a publisher's event dispatch is its LAST row's, an empty one included (a bodyless
      last row no longer takes an earlier row's dispatch);
    - events: one publisher symbol per distinct value (R4b); a subscriber id emits the
      union of its rows' distinct nodes' subscriptions, ordered by full value (R4; equal
      to before when its rows share one node, as every CDO and corpus group does);
    - `CombinedGraph.nodes` holds each id once, so the reverse call graph, r3a1, d2 and
      the cone list an id once; commits and checked-run seeds are unions, each seeded from
      a row that has it (#14, #16), and that row's own guard frame decides the seed's
      requirements; a span's pending writes count a collided seed row's own sited facts
      only; a temp proof of an event parameter needs every raise, read (and checked
      resolved) at its own row, and rewrites every subscriber row (#17);
    - one copy per distinct value: root classifications (`resolve_target` no longer reads
      two rows of one id as "ambiguous"; a roots config leaves the entries of an id it
      does not name as they are), the snapshot's call-site evidence (ordered by full
      value), d1's seeds (an equal copy collapses; the arms' unequal seeds are both kept);
      one per id: the snapshot's capability facts and coverage;
    - single-valued per id or key, from the LAST owning row: the classification lookups
      (d50/d51, policy `routine.rootKinds`), the dependency order index's entries (each
      op/call site with its own row's frames) and return summaries, the snapshot's
      call-site resolutions (display, `underAsserterror`, `resultConsumed` and the
      representative edge from one row) and its operation index, whose orders name frames
      of the id's one frame table (every row's frames, shifted per row; rows with equal
      frame tables share one block, so equal rows' evidence still collapses), `OperationJoin`
      (`query effects` origins); policy evaluation (class P: one evaluation per collided
      id, through its LAST row, because policy findings are keyed by routine id; the
      facts it reads are the id's unioned summary, but its row-level fields
      (`routine.accessModifier`, `routine.kind`, the finding's anchor) are the LAST
      row's, so an earlier arm's distinct row-level fields never match a rule).

    What deliberately stays: single-row ids (passed through untouched); guard frames (class
    G: the cone reads the last row's frame per id, and so do a span's callers; a defect is
    filed for step 6); the detectors that pick their own row (class R: d1
    reach/dataflow/cohort, d2, d3, d13, d18, d47, d49, d51 and the gate's `kept_ids`); the
    cone, the solve, the event graph and the spans stay per string id. Census counters of
    the event graph count per (id, node). Two stated limits, neither with a CDO witness (CDO's
    2 collision groups have equal facts at every point): within one collided id, order and
    position comparisons between entries of different arms (the dependency order index's
    `order_id`s, the snapshot's operation index) are not meaningful; and readers of the
    snapshot's call-site evidence (`unresolved_cone`, `digest`, `ordering_engine`) pick a
    collided site's copy by value, since the evidence carries no row. The cone's
    `CapabilityFact`, `CapabilityExtra` and `ValueSource` now derive `Ord`.
  - Epic amendments 11B-1 to 11B-8 (spec §9).
- **Grammar: tree-sitter-al `main` at `960ed312`** (B7b-2, "#if groups inside expressions";
  package version still 4.4.1; was `4d75846c`). The `node-types.json` hash guard had made CI
  red. 500 -> 501 named kinds, no field name added or removed. The new
  `preproc_conditional_operand` (an `#if` group in place of a whole operand, one `operand`
  per arm) is `Structural` and the lowerer reads one arm of it; tails and prefixes now also
  sit beside the value of an argument list, a list literal and a parenthesis (see Fixed).
  `CACHE_VERSION_GRAMMAR` is now `tree-sitter-al-v4.4.1-960ed312-native`. Measured old vs
  new: per-test outcomes identical apart from the two new lowerer tests (3,597 -> 3,599, all
  pass), zero goldens moved, the stamp kept its length so `dry-run.txt` did not move, CDO
  `--program-call-graph-stats` byte-identical (SHA-256 `c032c8db…94ef`, as at `4d75846c`).
- #160 steps 10 + 11a: the adapter pairs call sites by key, and routine identity is recorded
  once at assembly (part of #160). Output is unchanged: no golden moved, and on CDO the SARIF
  (both scopes, cross-app and single-app) and the call-graph histogram are byte-identical.
  Measured on CDO (server1, `release-fast`, 5 runs a side): cross-app `analyze` drops from
  26.9 s to 18.6 s, the join span `b3.adapter.join` from 8,381.6 ms to 90.3 ms, and the kernel
  peak from 3,219 MB to 3,070 MB; single-app is unchanged within noise. Numbers and bounds:
  `docs/measurements/2026-10-22-issue-160-steps10-11a.md`.
  - **The key join (step 10).** A model call site and a program edge now pair by
    `SiteIx = (FileIx, expression index)`: the resolver stamps it on each call-site edge
    (`ClassifiedEdge.site`, with `fires` for a record op), and the body walk records it per
    site (`ModelRoutine.file`, `site_exprs`). `FileIx` comes from one file table on the
    `ProgramContext`, keyed by app and path. The span join (J1), the source `texts` map and
    the op-name parse (J4, now the resolver's `fires`) are deleted, with `site_links.rs`.
    A debug assertion checks that every accepted pair has the same span on both sides. The
    LSP's per-file re-resolve passes no file and stays unstamped. The site keys are freed
    at the attach, after the join.
  - **`RowNodes` (step 11a).** Built at the end of assembly and dropped at the attach: each
    row's true node (`node_of`), the program declaration anchor of every caller the join reads
    (`decl_anchor`, for the caller check), and today's J2 and J5 answers (`j2_row`,
    `j5_node`). The caller check, the callee-row lookup and the event graph read them; the
    per-use `by_decl` map, the surface lookups and the event graph's span map are deleted.
    J2's cross-node alias and J5's two mapping gaps are kept as recorded answers, so the
    output does not move; correcting them is step 11b's. J5 answers for event-subscriber
    rows only, the only rows the event graph reads.
  - **The cross-app census counts only callers the model holds** (10A-2): a dependency
    routine the workspace does not demand is no longer a lost site. The cross-app loss gate
    on CDO is exactly the known residual (18 XmlPort record ops the body walk misses, 5
    `caller_mismatch` sites of one `#if`-split routine, their 23 fallback sites).
  - **Census.** A `[retained-census] collision …` line per model (rows sharing a string id,
    split by node and role, plus `j2_alias_nodes` and `j5_compat_rows`: event-subscriber
    rows whose recorded J5 answer is not their true node), and four new
    buckets: `program.edge_site`, `program.file_table`, `program.row_nodes`,
    `model.site_exprs`.
  - Amendments to the epic: 10A-1 (`SiteIx` is a key, not a dense index), 10A-2 (the
    demand filter), 10A-3 (the CDO gate asserts the residual), 10A-4 (bounds on
    `b3.adapter` and `analyze.total`, kernel peak RSS), 10A-5 (byte identity is read on the
    converted calls), 11A-1 (one claim), 11A-2 (`RoutineIx` is the row position), 11A-3
    (J2/J5 answers recorded, wrong ones included), 11A-4 (the L4 interner's `RoutineIx`
    keeps its name).
- #160 epic spec: two owner-approved changes to the delivery plan (2026-10-21; part of
  #160). Step 11 splits into 11a (routine identity, the two declaration joins, a collision
  count; output unchanged) and 11b (re-keying by routine and the one rule for routines that
  share a string id). Steps 10 and 11a land together as one issue, one spec, one review
  panel, one benchmark and one PR, because both edit the same adapter code and 11a would
  have to rebase on 10 anyway. Steps with no speed target (11a, 11b, 5, 8, 13) run no
  benchmark, only `cdo-gate` and the CDO byte-identity check (SARIF, call-graph histogram),
  and a "reported, no bound" benchmark part in a speed step runs 3 rounds of only the
  commands the step touches. Step 11's `by_decl` speed bound is withdrawn: deleting that
  phase made the bound empty. Estimated saving: about 1 h 50 for the merged claim and about
  1 h of benchmarks across the epic. Recorded in the epic's §9, I6, E-rows and Decisions
  45, 57, 58.
- #160 step 7b: closed-class sets and a fold memo (part of #160). The capability cone builds each
  routine's derived row (the five presence flags and the four id lists the detectors read) with
  less repeated work:
  - A singleton (a routine in no call cycle) used to build a `best` map over every entry of
    every callee cone, only to fold the survivors. It now folds one memoized row per distinct
    callee Cone-SCC. That row is the fold of the callee cone's CLOSED entries (those with no
    boolean-parameter guard). It is built at first read and freed with the cone. The guarded
    (open) entries still go through `substitute_entry` per call edge and are folded one by one,
    and so are the routine's own entries. Under `DerivedOnly` (`analyze`) no `best` map is built.
  - A recursive SCC's set is folded once per SCC; each member ORs that row in, then folds its
    own entries.
  - This holds in every mode that wants derived rows. The raw output (`RawOnly`, and the raw half
    of `Both`) is unchanged, and no golden moved.
  - Amendments to the epic: 7B-1, the memo key is the callee Cone-SCC, and there is no
    `FactKeyInterner` or hash-consed `SetArena` (measured net gain about 131 ms); 7B-2, the
    bounded timer is `singleton + bfs_fold`; 7B-3, the cone-span bound subtracts both bands;
    7B-4, X is derived at this step's base, `afd5d88f` (X = 4,382.1 ms, a projection).
  - Census (`ALSEM_CONES_CENSUS=1`): the `singleton:` line drops `fold=` and gains
    `memo= row= open= own=`. A new `closed:` line carries `memo_builds`, `memo_reads`,
    `memo_entries`, `scc_set_folds`, `singleton_scans` and `memo_live_max`. The
    `singleton calls:` and `singleton pop:` lines are now counted only where a singleton scans
    `best` (the raw half), so they read 0 under `analyze`.
  - The test-only `RecursiveMembership::PerMemberWalk` (step 7a's oracle) is deleted in this
    step. T7'/T8' replace T7/T8 and compare `DerivedOnly` with the fold of a streamed `RawOnly`
    composition, so they survive step 6's removal of `Both`.
  - Measured on CDO (`docs/measurements/2026-10-21-issue-160-step7b.md`): `singleton + bfs_fold`
    5,473.8 → 1,056.7 ms; `context.capability_cones` 11,601.5 → 6,365.4 ms (medians of 5
    interleaved rounds, parent `fd77939d`, head `f3ccb89c`). Both bounds are met and neither
    is void. SARIF is byte-identical in both scopes and the histogram SHA is equal. Cross-app
    `policy check` is 13.3 s faster (107.1 → 93.8 s).
- `/issue` (flow speed-ups, P1): findings-register marks are scoped to what changed. Each
  entry carries an `anchor` (the file and lines, or the fix commit, its fix lives in) and an
  `anchor_hash`; an edit resets only the marks of entries whose anchor lines changed, plus
  the entries its commit message names. The old field was one `hash` over the whole Design,
  so every edit reset every mark (#190: 7 resets of up to 31 entries). A conductor
  convention for now: the executor never read the old hash and does not read the anchors.
  After step 11's rebase the conductor re-points every `fix_commit` and commit anchor to
  the rebased SHA (from `git range-diff`), and a later round's fix diff across a rebase is a
  range-diff.
- agentflow (flow speed-ups, P3): a `minor` register entry whose fix touches only
  gate-inert prose and the evidence files closes on the raising reviewer's `accepted`;
  the other reviewer's mark is `accepted-by-rule`, and a `re-raised` still reopens it.
  `attest` and the handoff check count `accepted-by-rule` only when the entry is minor and
  not blocking, its `source` fills exactly one review slot (a stand-in's name under
  `--substitute`), that slot is `accepted` and the rule mark sits in the other one, and
  its `fix_commit` is a full SHA on the branch (after `B`) whose own diff touches only
  those paths; anywhere else, including an entry raised outside the two slots (the
  code-review skill, a task reviewer, a proof), the entry fails. In 3 of 3 runs a final round existed only to confirm a wording fix. 2 new tests
  (12 cases) in `test_cli_flow.py`.
- agentflow (flow speed-ups, P9): new `grant --issue N --key spec_rounds|final_rounds
  --n <k> --by <name>`, for the operator, raises one panel-round cap of the run holding
  issue N, with a `budget-grant` audit line written first. It refuses every other key
  (`key-not-grantable`, `ci_fix` included), `--n` below 1, an issue no lease names and a
  call carrying a run id; it allows a live lease, since the run it extends is live. A
  call without a run id is not stopped in code, so for `grant`, as for `unblock`, the
  prompt is the guard. `charge` and `grant` now hold a per-run `budget-<run>`
  mutex, so neither loses the other's write. A budget written before grants existed still
  loads. #190's sixth spec round was recorded outside the budget. 4 new tests.
- agentflow (flow speed-ups, P2): a findings-register entry whose only remaining work is
  a record written after the panel takes `disposition: fixed` with
  `closes_by: {kind: gate|attest|ci-wait, key}`, and the executor checks the record
  instead of a later round re-marking it. `attest` refuses an unknown kind or key, a
  non-`fixed` entry, a red or absent attested gate, a gate key `attest` does not itself
  require (only `ci-steps-all`, both `check-goldens` keys and `cdo-gate`), and an `attest` key outside
  `B`/`H`/`final_head`; `merge-gate` holds a `ci-wait` entry (`closes-by-unmet:<ids>`)
  until the latest `ci-wait` record is green on the final head (exit 0, not timed out,
  supervised, and the real `gh pr checks <pr> --watch` command). The attestation lists
  them under `closed_by`. On #190 such entries forced a final round after step 11.
  3 new tests (12 cases) in `test_cli_flow.py`.
- agentflow (flow speed-ups, P8): new `ci-rerun --pr <pr>` reruns the latest `ci.yml`
  run on the PR head without a new head or attestation: only the failed jobs of a red run,
  the whole of a green one. It is guarded like `push-branch` (dry-run, HALT, fence), fails
  closed on a run that is missing, unfinished or of another conclusion, and appends a
  `ci-rerun` record (with the head's running `count`) to `gate-runs.jsonl`. A second rerun
  of a red run on one head is refused (`rerun-already-used`); green reruns stay allowed. `/issue` step 13: a red CI whose every failing
  test the diff cannot reach is a flake, rerun once with no `ci_fix` charge; a second
  failure is `blocked ci-flaky:<test>`. On #111 a flake spent the one `ci_fix` and blocked
  the issue after 45 min with no defect. 4 new tests (8 cases) in `test_cli_flow.py`.
- `/issue` (flow speed-ups, P11): a bounded issue whose plan has at most two tasks skips
  the per-task sonnet reviewer; the implementer's proofs and the final panel are its
  review. Architectural issues and plans of three or more tasks keep it. On #111 and #190
  it found only minors; on #160 (architectural) it found an important gap early.
- `/issue` (flow speed-ups, P6): step 11 (rebase and the full gate set) starts in the
  background as soon as final round 1's fixes pass the task gate, while round 2 runs,
  instead of after convergence. A later fix outside the gate-inert prose discards that run
  and step 11 runs again; gate records are keyed by tree, so a discarded run cannot be
  attested. An issue with a CDO bench still waits for the panel and the bench. In 2 of 3
  runs every round after the first was prose only (~10 min saved per issue).
- `/issue` (flow speed-ups, P4): a probe reproduces the acceptance's own invocation (the
  same `ci-steps` step, parallelism, profile and core count). When the acceptance names
  the CI runner, step 3 may push one throwaway probe commit to a draft PR opened there,
  and the Design says which acceptance items the measured hardware can meet before the
  spec panel sees it. On #190 a serial probe of a parallel CI test, and runner variance
  found after the design, cost one spec round, two amendments and ~1 h.
- `/issue` (flow speed-ups, P5): every "if the measurement shows X, go back to design"
  rule in a spec or bounded design states its fallback, which the spec panel reviews with
  it. Firing it then needs no new round and no operator decision; the operator is asked
  only when no fallback fits, with a stated default after 15 minutes. On #190 a bare
  "back to design" cost ~30 min of operator wait and one spec round.
- `/issue` (flow speed-ups, P10): a later panel round's briefing carries only the fix diff
  and the ids to mark, in the reviewer's round-1 thread; the ledger, the full register and
  the previous reviews are not re-sent. Diff-only rounds took 1-2 min on #190 and #111,
  full-context rounds 4-13 min.
- **CI runs in two parallel jobs.** `test` (fmt, lint, gen-syntax, the test suite) and `release` (the
  release build and `perf_bounds`) now run side by side instead of one after the other. The steps took
  ~6.5 min in a row (run 39625785855: Lint 32 s, Test 100 s, Build 202 s, Perf 41 s); the wall time is
  now the slower job's. Each job keeps its own dependency cache. The flow's merge gate needs every check
  of the `CI` workflow green, so it covers both jobs unchanged.

- **Grammar: tree-sitter-al `main` at `4d75846c`** (B7b-3; package version still 4.4.1; was
  `8682cb5f`). The `node-types.json` hash guard had made CI red. 499 -> 500 named kinds, no
  field name added or removed; the `target` field of the four move hosts
  (`moveafter`/`movebefore`/`movefirst`/`movelast` modifications) became optional.
  `preproc_conditional_move_args` (a move header whose target or `;` comes from an `#if`
  group) is `Structural`, and the lowerer reads no move modification, so neither needs an
  arm. Shape changes: a `call_statement` no longer holds its `;`, and every bare name in
  statement position is a `call_statement` (`Bar` before `end`/`else`/`until` too, and the
  body of `asserterror Foo;`), which the lowerer now lowers as a parenless call: it skipped
  the bare identifier before. A case group arm may hold `empty_statement` and nested groups,
  and a branch may carry a directive-only group before its `;`. Two lowerer arms (see
  Fixed). `CACHE_VERSION_GRAMMAR` is now `tree-sitter-al-v4.4.1-4d75846c-native`. Measured
  old vs new at the bump: per-test outcomes identical apart from the two new lowerer tests
  (3,584 -> 3,586, all pass), zero goldens moved (the stamp kept its length, so
  `dry-run.txt` did not move), CDO `--program-call-graph-stats` byte-identical (SHA-256
  `c032c8db…94ef`). Limits: only a `call_statement` named `else` is skipped. In a file that
  already has an ERROR, a name the parser recovers in statement position may now be a
  `call_statement`, and is lowered as a call; so is a half-typed name before `end`
  (`begin Fo end`) and a misread or recovered `begin`/`end` (grammar deferred item 43).
  This is deliberate (`bare_name_before_end_lowers_as_call`).

- #160 step 7a: one inherited set per Cone-SCC (part of #160). In
  `compose_inherited_cones`, a recursive Cone-SCC member's derived row is now folded
