  from ONE set per SCC (its fact cone) plus the member's own producer-solve entries and
  its self half, instead of a per-member breadth-first walk. A non-root SCC borrows the
  fact cone the cone already builds; a root SCC gets the same `fact_cone_for_scc` build,
  dropped after its members are emitted. This holds under `DerivedOnly` (`analyze`)
  and `Both` (policy's raw build); the per-member walk now runs only for the raw half
  (`RawOnly`, `Both`), whose output is unchanged. `fold_row` is not part of 7a (spec
  D7a-2). Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-20-issue-160-step7a-scc-membership-design.md`.
  - **Headline.** On CDO (`cdo_ws`, cross-app `analyze`, server1, `release-fast`,
    parent `d37e8634` against head `7bb9f90c`, 5 interleaved rounds per side) the cone
    span `context.capability_cones` drops from 18.8 s to 10.1 s (median 18,782.9 →
    10,104.4 ms, −8,678.5 ms, head lower in 5/5), and the per-member walk no longer
    runs (`bfs_walk` 8.3 s → 0).
  - **Byte identity.** No golden moved in any commit. On CDO the SARIF is
    byte-identical at `--scope primary` and `--scope all`, the
    `--program-call-graph-stats` SHA-256 is `c032c8db…` on both sides (as at step 4),
    and the retained `context.cone_derived` (65,273,122 B) and `context.summaries`
    (36,400,882 B) are equal on both sides. Numbers:
    `docs/measurements/2026-10-20-issue-160-step7a.md`.
  - **The old path is test-only.** `RecursiveMembership::PerMemberWalk` is
    `#[cfg(test)]`; it is the oracle of T7 (fixtures) and T8 (CDO, in
    `scripts/cdo-gate`). It is deleted by step 7b's last commit once 7b's CDO oracle
    passes; if 7b is dropped, by the next step that edits `compose_inherited_cones`
    (step 6 at the latest). (Deleted in 7b.)
  - **Census.** A new `cone_scc:` line after `compose:` (recursive SCCs, members all
    and emitted, roots, self-loops, max, size histogram, member walks, own entries,
    sets borrowed and built, set entries, `walk_total`), fed from a per-call
    `ComposeStats`, ending with the oracle classes (`own_entry_members`,
    `with_successor`, `with_guarded_successor`) that T7 and T8 now read from the
    same stats instead of recomputing them. `bfs_walk` now holds each set's build or borrow plus the member
    walks that still run; `walk_total` holds the member walks only (0 under
    `DerivedOnly`). `BFS_PICKS` is 0 under `DerivedOnly`. `MERGE_CALLS` and
    `MERGE_TIEBREAKS` rise by the root-set builds' merges (none on CDO, which has no
    recursive root). `direct=` covers the per-routine direct-fact loop only, as at
    step 0.
  - **M3 deferred to step 6.** The Cone pair joins `ExecRelation` at step 6, its
    second permanent reader (spec §4.6).
  - **Coverage limits.** CDO has no recursive ROOT SCC, so the root-set build never
    runs on CDO: root recursive SCCs are not oracle-checked on CDO (roots 0). The
    build is covered by the hand graphs, whose recursive SCCs are roots in T1, T2,
    T3, T3b, T4, T5, T6(a), T10 and T11 (T2's break, an empty root set, is the one
    that targets it), by T7's 4 fixture roots per mode, and by the census CLI test
    (`census_cone_scc_line_counts_the_recursive_sccs`). T7's 249 fixture dirs reach
    only multi-member SCCs (4) and roots (4) per mode, so T8 on CDO is the only
    real-code oracle for SCCs with successors (64), guarded successors (11) and
    own entries (671 members); the hand tests T1, T3, T3b and T4 cover them in small.
    `tests/gap` keeps its scenarios inline and cannot call the lib oracle (the step 3
    deviation). The plan's test "a root SCC with no emitted member" cannot occur:
    Tarjan starts only from `nodes`, so an SCC with no member in `nodes` is always
    reached from outside and is never a root.
    `scc_set_none_for_an_scc_with_no_emitted_member` pins the non-root case instead.
  - **Speed.** The stop rule (§6) passed on server1 before the switch. A7a.4 met: head
    `bfs_walk` median 0.0 ms ≤ 1,000 ms. A7a.5 met and not void (void check 6,745.7 ≥
    1,808.6): the cone saving 8,678.5 ms ≥ 5,841.4 ms (amendment 7A-1), and ≥ 6,745.7
    ms in the literal form. `bfs_fold` (reported) 747.1 → 394.4 ms. Reported, no bound:
    `analyze --single-app` wall 3.8 s on both sides (+0.1 s, inside the 0.5 s band);
    cross-app `policy check` (`Both`, which folds the set and still walks) 85.0 → 76.9 s,
    head lower in 5/5, so `Both` has no regression. Polled RSS unchanged within the band
    (693.3 / 699.1 MB and 13,806.9 / 13,816.1 MB).
- #160 step 4: one execution relation per view. `ExecRelation`
  (`src/engine/l4/exec_relation.rs`) is built once from one split of the calls:
  workspace callers' calls plus every event dispatch (the Primary payload, in
  `edges_by_from` / `edges_from_order` / `uncertainty_edges`), and every typed edge,
  the dependency code's own calls included (the Cone payload, `typed_edges`), with
  its SCC computed in `new`. Before, the cross-app base built the graph twice and ran
  its own Tarjan, a single-app context built its own graph, and `build_l4` ran a
  Tarjan when nobody handed it one. Now the cross-app base holds the relation
  (`R3a5CrossAppBase.rel` replaces `graph`, `combined_scc`, `event_graph` and
  `nodes`), the view's cell is `Cell::Rel` (single-app built by `prepare`, cross-app
  the base's), `build_detector_artifacts` and `build_l4` take the relation, and the
  cone takes only the typed edges (`&[TypedEdge]`, so it cannot read the Primary
  payload). The r3a5 projection reads the relation and the model's own event graph.
  The snapshot stays on its own legacy-cut graph until step 6.
  - **Byte identity.** No golden moved. The CDO detector baseline and the
    `--program-call-graph-stats` histogram are unchanged (CDO `bc3ccb18`, parent
    `c554b704` against head `0729f7f7`, `release-fast`): findings 2277 → 2277 at
    `--scope primary` and 30712 → 30712 at `--scope all`, no detector changed,
    fingerprints 0 added and 0 removed; histogram SHA-256 `c032c8db…` on both
    sides; SARIF byte-identical in both universes. Numbers:
    `docs/measurements/2026-10-20-issue-160-step4.md`.
  - **Dependency uncertainty kept.** The dependency half's uncertainty edges,
    dropped before, are kept in `rel.dependency_uncertainty`. Nothing reads them
    yet (step 5 decides); they stay out of the Primary payload, the detector
    context and the L4 solve.
  - **Counters.** `build.combined_graph` drops by one in every command that builds
    a cross-app base, since one relation counts one build: analyze cross-app 2→1,
    `analyze --detector d47-…` 3→2, digest cross-app 3→2, events, policy check and
    query cross-app 2→1. `build.graph_scc` moves in no row pinned before this
    step. One case gains a Tarjan: a single-app plan that fills the relation but
    no `l4` (`analyze --single-app --detector d47-…`) now runs the relation's
    (`scc` 2, newly pinned by `analyze_single_app_d47`; 1 before by the same
    rule, a value no test ever pinned). The step 0-2 child
    spec's §4.4.8 restates the table "after step 4". A new counter case,
    `analyze_cross_app_with_a_dependency_half`, pins the one-build count on a
    workspace whose dependency half is not empty (the other cross-app rows'
    dependency makes no call, so their half is empty).
  - **Spans, census, cells.** New span `rel.build`; gone
    `context.event_combined_graph` and `context.core_scc_tarjan`;
    `crossapp.base_graph` / `crossapp.base_artifacts_facts` renamed
    `crossapp.field_index` / `crossapp.base_facts`. Census buckets `rel.graph`,
    `rel.scc`, `rel.dependency_uncertainty` replace `base.graph`,
    `base.combined_scc`, `base.event_graph`, `base.nodes`, `context.graph` and
    `l4.scc`. On CDO the renamed graph and SCC buckets keep their bytes
    (cross-app 26 294 162 B and 4 590 120 B, single-app 6 349 073 B and
    794 455 B); `base.event_graph` (2 830 824 B) and `base.nodes` (3 324 090 B)
    are gone and `rel.dependency_uncertainty` is new (77 904 B cross-app, 0
    single-app), −6 077 010 B net cross-app. The `view.release` trace instant names `Rel` where it
    named `Graph`.
  - **Single-app SCC lifetime.** The single-app SCC is now built before the det
    fill's cone and lives in `Cell::Rel` until it is released, longer than `l4`
    held it (through the cone walk; in `events --single-app` and `policy check
    --single-app` until their last release). About 0.8 MB on CDO, bounded by three
    single-app peak bounds, all met on CDO (5 interleaved rounds, band 3 % of
    each metric's parent median): `analyze --single-app` process 578 → 577 MiB,
    post-attach 297 → 296; `policy check --single-app` 576 → 577, 455 → 458;
    `events fanout --single-app` 575 → 576, 297 → 294; stdout equal. Reported
    cross-app peaks are flat or lower: `analyze` 2835 → 2834 / 2139 → 2136,
    `digest` 2837 → 2835 / 2160 → 2118 (post-attach lower in 5/5; the deleted
    transient copies of the calls, not in the retained census).
  - **Tests.** New: three behaviour pins on the base code (a dependency caller of
    a dependency publisher stays out of the subscriber's reverse graph and commit
    span, and a dependency `local` helper is never proven temporary; d17 samples
    the first caller in emission order; dependency uncertainty stays out of
    Primary and is kept), and a per-field parity oracle against today's cross-app
    recipe on 249 corpus app dirs plus two inline fixtures (both models each) and
    CDO. The
    oracle first ran against a COPY of the assembler (independent code, with two
    assembler-internal mutations caught), then `build_combined_graph` was made to
    delegate to the one assembler after a text-identity check. Rewritten with the
    code: the census and release-order counter tests (`rel.*`, `Cell::Rel`), the
    SCC-sharing test (`base.rel.scc()`), and `build_l4` / `build_detector_artifacts`
    call sites. The relation's fields are private (readers name their rule through
    `primary()` / `cone()` / `scc()`), the cross-app base splits the calls by move
    (no `CallEdge` held twice), and the `rel.*` census buckets print where the old
    `base.*` / `context.graph` buckets printed.
- #160 step 3: the capability snapshot and `project_r3a3` no longer run an L4
  solve to get their call-site-local coverage reasons. Before, each snapshot base
  (and each `project_r3a3`) ran its own `compute_summaries_v2` over a fresh Tarjan
  SCC and kept only the four call-site-local uncertainty kinds (`ambiguous-overload`,
  `member-not-found`, `external-target`, `interface-open-world`). Those kinds never
  move from a callee to a caller, so a routine's set is exactly its own uncertainty
  edges'. Now one pass over the combined graph's uncertainty edges
  (`callsite_local_coverage_reasons`) gives the same reasons for every workspace
  routine. It filters with the
  solver's own `is_callsite_local_kind`, so the solver's propagation filter and the
  coverage kinds are one list on purpose. No output changes: r3a3, cli-b and r4f
  goldens are unchanged, and CDO's ratchets and histogram are unchanged.
  - **Proof.** The old solve-and-fold stays as a test-only oracle. The new scan
    equals it per workspace routine, with no extra key, on every app dir (at any
    depth) under `tests/r0-corpus` (217), `tests/fixtures` (29),
    `tests/r3a4-fixtures`, `tests/r3a5-fixtures` and `tests/r2-5b-fixtures` (1
    each), each over both its single-app and its cross-app model (the cross-app
    commands build the snapshot over the latter, whose routines include the
    dependency routines with bodies), plus an inline fixture, a forced roles cap,
    and CDO in both modes (5479 routines single-app, 31656 cross-app). The inline
    fixture puts each kind in a non-recursive routine, a self-loop and a
    two-member cycle, because the inputs miss those cells. On CDO every recursive
    cell is 0 single-app, and only a few are not 0 cross-app:

    | kind | single-app: non-recursive | self-loop | multi-member | cross-app: non-recursive | self-loop | multi-member |
    |---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
    | ambiguous-overload | 18 | 0 | 0 | 119 | 1 | 5 |
    | external-target | 393 | 0 | 0 | 19 | 0 | 0 |
    | interface-open-world | 15 | 0 | 0 | 149 | 0 | 19 |
    | member-not-found | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

  - **Gap deviation.** `tests/gap` keeps its scenarios as inline AL strings inside
    the integration crate, which a lib test cannot reach, and an integration test
    cannot call the test-only oracle. The 32 app dirs under the four fixture roots
    and the inline fixtures stand in for it.
  - **Counters.** Each snapshot builds one `build.summaries_v2` and one
    `build.graph_scc` fewer (process totals): `analyze --detector d47-…` v2 1→0,
    scc 3→2; `digest` (cross-app and `--single-app`), `prove` and `fingerprint`
    (every mode) v2 2→1, scc 4→3; `diff ws ws` v2 2→0, scc 4→2; `diff ws ws
    --strict` v2 4→2, scc 8→6. The child spec's §4.4.8 restates the table "after
    step 3". `run_digest_empty_diff_builds_no_context` now checks
    `build.snapshot == 0` directly, since `build.summaries_v2` no longer witnesses a
    snapshot.
  - **stderr.** The snapshot's private solve printed a roles-cap non-convergence
    line for its own graph. Commands with no L4 solve lose that line entirely:
    `diff ws ws` without `--strict`, `analyze --detector d47-…` (no `l4` fill),
    `aldump --r3a3-cone-coverage` and the aldump snapshot modes. Commands with an
    L4 solve keep only L4's own line (`build_l4`, now truly the one print site),
    which reports L4's graph; in cross-app commands that is the base's graph, not
    the snapshot's cut graph. The dropped line reported the convergence of roles nothing read: the
    fold read only the four selected kinds, and a cap appends `fixpoint-capped`
    without changing that set.
  - **Census and trace.** The removed solve no longer adds to the
    `ALSEM_SUMMARIES_CENSUS=1` totals or emits a `compute_summaries_v2_phase_split`
    trace instant per snapshot.
  - **Span.** `r3a3.direct_facts` is renamed `r3a3.direct_facts_scan`, since it no
    longer contains a solve.
- `/issue` runs the full gate set (`ci-steps all`, both `check-goldens` runs,
  `cdo-gate`) once per issue instead of after every change: before the final
  panel and after each panel fix it runs only the task gate (`ci-steps task`),
  and the full set runs in step 11, right after the rebase, on the head that is
  attested. A rebase onto a moved `master` adds a final-panel round only when the
  branch's own commits changed (`git range-diff`), a conflict was resolved, or the
  post-rebase gates needed a fix; before, any rebase onto new code added a round.
  On #107 the full set ran 7 times (~15 min each) and two review rounds checked
  only code from other merges.
- agentflow: `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/**/*.md` may change after the attested head
  `H` without a new gate run. No gate reads them (`protect.gate_inert`), so
  `freeze-check` and the post-merge identity check accept them beside the two
  evidence files. `test_no_gate_reads_a_gate_inert_path` scans every Rust source and
  the gate scripts, and fails if anything starts to read them. On #160 step 2,
  final-panel wording fixes in the CHANGELOG and the numbers file moved `H` twice and
  cost two full gate runs.
- agentflow: a gate record's `clean_before` / `clean_after` ignore uncommitted changes
  under `.agent/`, so writing the ledger and register while a gate runs no longer
  refuses the post-merge identity skip (`record-dirty`). A commit during the run still
  voids the record. On #160 step 2 that edit alone made post-merge rerun all its gates.
- `/issue`: the final panel's round 1 asks each reviewer for every finding at once,
  wording and records included; later rounds only verify the fixes. A panel fix that
  touches only gate-inert prose and the evidence after step 11's gates needs no new
  gate run.
- Faster gates (2026-10-20; a survey of the gate logs, then each change measured):
  - **One release build per gate run instead of two.** `cargo build --release` and
    `cargo test --release --test perf_bounds` shared nothing, for two reasons:
    - `[profile.release]` had `panic = "abort"`, which cargo ignores for tests. It is
      gone from `release`; the shipped binaries keep it through a new `release-ship`
      profile, which `build-and-deploy.yml` and `release.yml` now build and upload
      (`target/release-ship/`).
    - `criterion`, a dev-dependency, changed the features of shared crates
      (`zerocopy`, `either`, hence `rayon` and `al-sem`). The benches moved to their own
      workspace package, `al-sem-benches` (`benches/Cargo.toml`), and the root package
      sets `autobenches = false`. Run them with `cargo bench -p al-sem-benches --bench <name>`.

    Measured: the perf-bounds step went from recompiling 30 crates, `al-sem` included
    (5m27), to compiling only the `perf_bounds` test target (45 s).
  - `scripts/ci-steps all` runs the release build in the background while the test
    suite runs, in its own target dir (`target/gate-release`); `perf-bounds` then runs
    alone, so its timings see an idle machine.
  - `scripts/ci-steps task-affected`: `task` with only the tests the changed paths can
    reach (an explicit path map; the lib tests always; an unmapped path runs the whole
    suite). It is the per-task inner loop of `/issue` step 8; the whole suite still runs
    before the final panel and before the merge.
  - `scripts/check-goldens` skips when the tracked tree is exactly one `ci-steps test`
    just passed, the same skip the pre-commit hook makes (`CHECK_GOLDENS_FORCE=1` runs
    it anyway).
  - nextest starts the slow `r3`, `cli` and `r4` binaries first (`priority = 50`), so
    the suite no longer ends on a tail of a few long tests.
  - `scripts/cdo-gate` runs `program_resolve_harness` on 4 threads instead of 1
    (measured on CDO: 17-18 s against 36-38 s; the harness shares one CDO context
    and writes nothing outside regen mode or its own tempdir).
  - CI caches cargo builds (`Swatinem/rust-cache@v2` in `ci.yml`).
  - agentflow: a `bench` run (`agentflow run --name bench -- python scripts/bench_ab.py …`)
    takes every gate slot, so no gate builds beside a measurement. `pr-create --draft`
    and `pr-ready --pr N [--body-file F]` (it replaces the body, scanned like
    `pr-create`'s, then marks it ready); `merge-gate` refuses a draft (`pr-draft`).
  - `/issue`:
    - step 9 opens a draft PR after the first green task gate, so CI runs during the
      final panel; that CI is the Linux check (no ad hoc WSL clone);
    - one CDO bench per issue, after the panel converges, under the `bench` lock;
    - step 8 sends review findings back to the same implementer agent (no cold
      review-fix agent), and two small tasks may share one review;
    - the spec panel's round 1 asks for every finding at once.

- #160 step 2: every `alsem` command builds its detector context and its L4 solve once, through one `View` (`src/engine/session.rs`). Some builds stay outside the `View`:
  - `policy check`'s command-local raw-facts build (step 6 removes it);
  - the fold solve (`compute_uncertainty_coverage_reasons`) that snapshot composition runs on its own: in `digest`, `prove` and `fingerprint`, and in each side of `diff` (step 3 removes it);
  - for a plan with d47, d49 or d51, the whole snapshot that `fill_ordering` composes for the ordering facts, with its own cone, `pd_solve`, Tarjan and fold solve (step 3 removes that snapshot's fold solve; the rest stays).
  - **The pieces.**
    - `View`, `Plan` and `RunKey` hold four cells: ordering, graph, det and `l4`. Each cell is filled once, by `prepare`, never lazily.
    - `L4Analysis` / `build_l4` (`src/engine/l4/analysis.rs`) is the one solve.
    - The detector context splits into owned `DetectorArtifacts` and a borrowed `DetectorContext<'v>`.
    - Ordering facts are a filled slot. A detector that reads them without declaring `ORDERING_FACTS` panics instead of filling them lazily.
    - Cross-app, the context shares the base's graph and SCC instead of building its own.
  - **No output byte moves.** The CDO SARIF, digest, prove, query, fingerprint, histogram and detector baseline are identical.
  - **CDO numbers** (`docs/measurements/2026-10-19-issue-160-step2.md`):
    - `digest` takes 33.8 s instead of 52.7 s: its second, all-detector context is gone.
    - `prove`'s peak is 575 MiB instead of 2235 MiB, and it takes 4.2 s instead of 6.9 s.
      - The peak and 1.7 s of the time come from computing effects for its one root, not for every root.
      - 0.3 s comes from the deleted context.
      - About 0.7 s comes from the deleted private bundle solve; that part has no span, so it is not isolated.
    - analyze's post-attach peak is 99 MiB lower, digest's 380 MiB lower. Their process peak is set during attach (about 2835 MiB) and does not move.
    - `digest --single-app`'s post-attach peak is 11 MiB higher, inside its 3 % bound. The solve's retained output (`l4.bundle` + `l4.scc`, 2.2 MB on CDO) now stays alive through snapshot composition; the rest of the 11 MiB is not attributed.
  - **Commands.**
    - `digest`, `prove` and `events fanout|chains` no longer build a second context with every substrate.
    - `digest`, `prove` and `query` no longer run a private bundle solve.
    - `policy check` keeps its raw-facts build, on the view's graph.
    - `digest` checks for an empty change set (no `--diff` content, files or routines) before any solve: exit 1 with the same message, without paying for a context.
  - **Cross-app analyze failure.** A failed cross-app `analyze` build is classified from its own result; no second, single-app build runs.
    - When the program build fails, the failure line carries that build's error. Before, if the single-app rerun succeeded, it said `the cross-app model could not be built`.
    - When the model assembly fails, analyze gives the empty output with the `coverage could not be verified` warning (exit 0), as a single-app assembly failure always did. Before, a succeeding single-app rerun turned it into the `could not be built` failure.
    - `digest`, `events fanout|chains`, `policy check` and `query` now add the program build's error to their `the cross-app model could not be built (--single-app analyses the workspace alone)` line, as `: program engine build failed: <error>`. Before, they dropped it. An assembly failure keeps the bare line.
  - **The non-convergence warning** (`warning: summarize: Summary fixed-point did not converge for SCC [...]`) has one print site per solve, `build_l4`, plus the snapshot fold's own.
    - So a capped SCC prints fewer duplicate lines: digest and prove print 2 instead of 4, events and policy 1 instead of 2.
    - `aldump --r3a2` and `--r3a5-cross-app-summary` no longer print it.
    - No CDO SCC caps, so no CDO output moved.
  - **Retained census** (`ALSEM_RETAINED_CENSUS=1`):
    - new `l4.bundle`, `l4.scc` (only when `build_l4` computed the SCC), `l4.summarize_diagnostics` and `l4.warnings` buckets;
    - `context.db_effect_bundle` becomes `l4.bundle`;
    - cross-app, `context.graph` is not printed, because the base's bucket counts the shared graph;
    - `base.injected_typed_edges`, `base.upgraded_bindings` and `context.ordering_source` are gone.
  - **Trace.**
    - `digest.tx_context_map` and `prove.tx_context_map` are gone.
    - `context.build_total` / `crossapp.context_build` now also open on the `View` paths.
    - New instant event `view.release`: one per cell a `View` releases, named by the cell.
  - **Library API.**
    - `build_detector_context` returns an `OwnedContext`; read the context with `.ctx()`.
    - `assemble_and_resolve_cross_app_program` returns `Result<_, CrossAppFailure>` instead of `Option`.
    - `R3a5CrossAppBase.graph` / `.combined_scc` are `Arc`s, and its `injected_typed_edges` field is gone. Those edges were a second copy of what `graph` holds, about 16 MB on CDO.
    - `R3a5CrossAppBase.upgraded_bindings` is gone: it was a second copy of `resolved.calls.upgraded_bindings`, about 15.5 MB on CDO. A cross-app `build_l4` reads the base's `field_index` (through `CrossAppInputs`) instead of building its own.
    - `DetectorOutput` derives `Debug, PartialEq, Eq`; the superset-mask parity test compares the whole output.

### Removed

- #160 step 2: `effect_query_cli::build_db_effect_bundle`, `cross_app_db_effect_bundle`, `QuerySubstrate::from_cross_app_base` / `from_resolved`, `run::analyzer_diagnostic_lines`, and `digest_cli` / `prove`'s `compute_tx_context_map`. Each was a second build of something the `View` now builds once.
- The unused `salsa` dependency and its 23 `SalsaValue` derives in `src/engine/l4` (#221). Byte-neutral; `Cargo.lock` drops 15 packages.

### Fixed

- `alsem digest`, `alsem fingerprint` and `alsem prove` now name the object that owns each
  routine, for example `Table Customer` or `Interface IFoo` (#78). Before, `objectDisplay` was
  always `""` in all three (digest `routine.objectDisplay`, each fingerprint block, the prove
  document), and the fingerprint human header printed `::Name`. The cause: digest and
  fingerprint split the snapshot's routine name at `::`, that name never holds the object, and
  prove copied digest's result. All three human headers now print `<owner>::<routine>`, or the
  bare routine when the owner is unknown, through one shared rule. The owner now comes from the
  model, with the same rule `alsem query effects` uses (`"<ObjectType> <ObjectName>"`). It does
  not come from the snapshot's identity table, which is not a safe object-name map: every
  Interface and ControlAddIn in an app shares one object id there, so they would all get one
  name, and a tableextension stub can overwrite the name of the real table with its own number.
  An Interface or ControlAddIn method takes its owner from its own declaring object. The routine
  display is now the snapshot name unchanged, so a name that contains `::` is no longer cut.
  Inherited limit: two model objects with the same internal id (for example `#if`/`#else`
  declarations of one type and number under different names) show one surviving name, as
  `query effects` already does.
- A routine selector copied from one of those headers, `<owner>::<routine>` (for example
  `Codeunit Sel A::Persist`), now selects only that owner's routine in `digest`, `fingerprint`
  and `prove` (#78). Before, the object part was ignored, so a routine name two objects
  declare was ambiguous. When no matched routine has that owner, the selector matches as
  before. An ambiguous selector's candidates now print `<owner>::<routine>` too (the digest
  `candidates` list and fingerprint's error lines), and `query effects`/`query touches` build
  their headers with the same rule. The owner lookup no longer builds a full routine join or
  one string per workspace routine; it builds the owner of each id it is asked about.
- LSP watcher: each root now watches its root `app.json`, its workspace `.al-sem.json` (reloaded live), and the ancestor `.alpackages` folders the loader reads, registered before the first build; folder renames and moves, and files replaced without their own event, are reconciled; an overflow or a replaced root re-arms the root's watch, re-syncs the caches and reloads the config. Stated limits: an edit to the global `~/.al-sem/config.json` and a `.git` created or removed at the root or an ancestor still need a server restart; a file replaced without its own event by one with the same length and modification time (and, on Unix, the same file id) is not re-read; a path whose watch cannot be registered is seen only once a 5 s retry succeeds; on Windows a folder event walks that folder's subtree (#221).
- LSP updater: a `.al` file renamed, moved or replaced, a folder renamed, moved in or out, or replaced, and a `FileRemoved` for a file still on disk are reconciled from disk instead of leaving stale or missing declarations; a `.al` under `.alpackages`, `.snapshots` or `node_modules` no longer triggers a full rebuild (#221).
- **#156: `alsem diff` reported private changes as ABI breaks, and a changed signature as two
  findings.**
  - A `local` or `internal` procedure, and any trigger (object, field or action), is no longer
    part of the ABI: adding, removing or changing one gives no `abi` finding. Event publishers
    stay ABI even when `local` or `internal`, because dependent extensions can subscribe to them
    (AppSourceCop AS0025): `[IntegrationEvent]`, `[BusinessEvent]` and `[ExternalBusinessEvent]`
    (any case). `local` → `public` on the same procedure is now a `procedure-added`.
  - A procedure whose signature changed is now ONE `procedure-signature-changed`, not a
    `procedure-removed` (critical) plus a `procedure-added`. Old and new are matched by object,
    name and ABI status, only when exactly one old-only and one new-only routine carry that name
    (unchanged overloads don't count). If two overloads change at once, the diff reports removed +
    added as before. A routine whose ABI status changed with its signature is not matched: public
    `Foo` removed + local `Foo` added stays a critical `procedure-removed`. A repeated snapshot row
    (same stable id twice) counts once. Capability, permission, coverage and subscriber-induced
    findings now follow the routine (the new id) instead of showing up as gained on the new id
    and lost on the old one. Such a pair is not a rename: there is no "renamed from" note and no
    `oldOriginalStableId`, and `renamesApplied` still counts only overlay entries. For an `abi`
    finding the old id is `<object>#<oldSignatureHash>`.
  - Old ids read from event declarations are now normalized through the rename table, the user
    overlay included, at three places. This removes a false `event-subscriber-induced-capability-gained`
    for a paired or renamed subscriber, and puts a removed publisher and a subscriber-induced
    finding on the renamed/paired subject.
  - `table-field-added` (and the other field findings) show the field's name in
    `subject.displayName` instead of its stable id.
  - Limits: an `internal` procedure called by an `internalsVisibleTo` friend app gets no `abi`
    finding. Object-level `Access = Internal` is not visible, so a public procedure in an
    internal codeunit stays ABI. When a pre-fix snapshot (no `routineKind`) is diffed against a
    new one, a trigger present only in the old snapshot is still `procedure-removed`. A
    `local`/`internal` `[IntegrationEvent]` or `[BusinessEvent]` publisher that drops its
    attribute gets no `abi` finding; the events pass reports `event-publisher-removed` (medium).
    An `[ExternalBusinessEvent]` publisher that drops it gets no finding at all (the model does
    not treat it as an event publisher, so there is no event declaration to lose). A routine in
    new that is a user overlay target is never auto-paired, and an old id the overlay maps to a
    target missing from new stays a removal. Rename normalization is one hop: with overlay
    `X → T`, an old-only routine whose own id is `T` can still be auto-paired to a same-name `U`,
    and `X`'s facts then stay on `T` rather than following on to `U`.
- **#220: shards and the `diff` preflight took the first `apps[]` row as the workspace's app.**
  That held only while `apps[]` had one row. Both now read the row whose `role` is `"primary"`.
  A shard is now closed over identity, operation, call-site and edge references: it also keeps
  the rows of those four kinds that its own rows refer to (repeated until nothing new is added,
  in the full snapshot's order; an anchor's internal routine id is mapped through the model).
  Frame and app references are not closed, as before: a shard carries no frame tables, and the
  analysis gaps it copies may name apps it has no `apps[]` row for. A shard matches its app's guid
  case-insensitively, so an upper-case guid in `app.json` gives the same shard. No committed shard
  golden moved beyond the schema-4 header and `role` changes.
- **#160 step 5: one coverage policy** (part of #160; #161 part 2). The detector context
  (`det_cone_inputs`) and the cross-app base (`build_cross_app_base`) now fold the four
  call-site-local uncertainty kinds (`ambiguous-overload`, `external-target`,
  `interface-open-world`, `member-not-found`) into each routine's direct coverage, from both
  uncertainty halves (`ExecRelation::uncertainty_all`: the Primary half, then the dependency
  half), per row before the collided-id projection. Until now only the r3a3 projection and
  the snapshot base folded them, so a routine making an ambiguous or open-world call read as
  `complete` coverage to every detector. Readers that can now move: transaction spans and
  d9 (a span reaching such a routine is incomplete), digest's and prove's
  `transactionContext` (`unknown` where it was known), d35 (new UNKNOWN "may be reachable"
  findings, longer reason text), d45's coverage text, `events fanout`'s
  `capabilityComposition` and `--coverage-policy strict`, and the policy gate under
  `requireCoverage: complete`. The bundled policy uses `partial`, which fails only
  `unknown` (`passes_coverage_gate`), and the fold never writes `unknown`, so it cannot
  move; on CDO its `policy check` output is byte-identical to the parent's. d2 can
  lose a finding when its 500-node walk budget is spent on a newly entered branch (pinned
  by T9). No existing golden moved. The test-only L4-solve fold
  `compute_uncertainty_coverage_reasons` is deleted with the three tests that pinned it (the
  fixture and CDO oracles, both through the helper `check_oracle`, and the roles-cap
  oracle): their "scan equals the solve's fold" claim has no second side any more.
  **Stated limit until step 6:** cross-app, a dependency routine's L4 summary is solved over
  the Primary payload only, so its own four-kind calls never reach its `uncertainties` or
  `hasUnresolvedCalls`. Its folded coverage now names them (`partial`), so the r3a5
  projection (`aldump --r3a5-cross-app-summary`) prints such a routine as `partial` with
  empty `uncertainties`. The summary gap predates step 5; step 6's dependency solve
  closes it. Pinned by T1-T9
  (`detector_context_step5_tests.rs`, `tests/cli/cli_step5_coverage_fold.rs`), each proven
  to fail with its producer's fold broken. Epic amendments 5-A1 to 5-A8 (spec
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-22-issue-160-step5-coverage-policy-design.md` §9): the
  reader list, the policy proxy, the snapshot keeping its cut-graph fold until step 6, the
  two kept fields with one chained accessor, the deletion moved here, the new fixtures, no
  golden predicted, and the triage gate on the default mode at both scopes.
- **The lowerer reads the `960ed312` grammar's expression `#if` shapes** (see Changed). An
  operand group (`1 + #if X Foo() #else Bar() #endif`, or a callee
  `#if X Foo #else Bar #endif (1)`) lowers as its first arm a build can take
  (`conditional_list_arm`, the positional-list policy; a union is no build), with a
  `SyntaxIssue` because the other arms' calls are not lowered. It was an `Unknown`, which
  links no child, so every call in every arm was lost. A `preproc_operand_prefix` beside an
  argument, list element or parenthesised value is skipped like a tail already was: it
  counted as an extra argument (`Baz(#if X 1 + #endif Qux(), 2)` had arity 3) or hid a
  parenthesis's value. Pinned by `operand_group_lowers_its_first_arm` and
  `operand_prefix_takes_no_value_slot`, both proven to fail with the change removed. Limits:
  the arm is chosen without the routine's build guard (like key field lists), and the
  operands of tails and prefixes are still not lowered.
- agentflow (pre-existing): post-merge's verification worktree built into the main
  checkout's `target/` from a new path per merge (`../al-sem-verify-merge-<sha12>`). Test
  binaries bake `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` and cargo reuses a binary whose Rust sources
  did not change, so after #190's post-merge (merge 81e858ac) the checkout's own
  `ci-steps all` and `cdo-gate` ran binaries resolving fixtures under the deleted verify
  tree (37 lib failures in `cdo-gate`). The next post-merge of a fixtures-only merge would
  have done the same in the verify tree: a false red, and a revert of a good merge. The
  merge and revert checks now share ONE fixed path, `../al-sem-verify-tree` (post-merge
  runs one at a time under the merge lane, and the merge tree is gone before the revert
  tree is made), and build into their own cache, `<root>/target-verify` (gitignored;
  `AGENTFLOW_VERIFY_TARGET_DIR` and `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` still override it).

- agentflow (pre-existing): `Git.changed_files` now passes `--no-renames`. With git's
  rename detection a `git mv src/x.rs docs/x.md` listed only `docs/x.md`, which is
  gate-inert, so a code file moved into `docs/` passed `freeze-check`, the post-merge
  identity check, `check-diff`'s protected-path check and the P3 prose check as prose.
  Both paths are now listed. Tests: `test_mergeops.py` (freeze check) and the P3 refusal
  list in `test_cli_flow.py`.
- agentflow (pre-existing): `finish --outcome handoff` measured the handoff's `files` from
  the shared checkout's local `master`, which lags while another session's merge waits for
  its post-merge, so `files` could carry that merge's files too. It now uses
  `merge-base origin/master <sha>`, for `files` and for the P3 prose check alike.
- **`perf_bounds`'s timing tests run one at a time and judge the minimum of their samples**
  (#190; `tests/perf_bounds.rs`). Why: CI runs the binary's tests side by side on a 4-core
  runner, so one test's samples were timed while another test was building or solving, and
  ten gates judged the median of their samples. PR #187 failed twice this way
  (`compute_summaries_v2`, medians 231.8 / 243.0 ms against a 230 ms bound, minima ~150 ms)
  on a change that never reached that code. Now every timing test takes one shared lock
  first, so they run one at a time, and every gate compares the minimum of its samples with
  its bound. A new test reads the file and fails if a timing test does not take the lock, or
  if it cannot check one. Under nextest, where each test is its own process, a `perf-bounds`
  test-group in `.config/nextest.toml` runs them one at a time instead. No bound changed.
  Under the lock, two CI runs measured a `compute_summaries_v2` solve made 3x heavier at
  179.87 ms (run 39625785855) and 248.21 ms (run 39635284889, AMD EPYC 7763, 1x 86.52 ms):
  the two runs differed ~1.4x (the first run's CPU was not recorded). So the 230 ms bound
  catches a 3x slowdown only on runners as slow as the EPYC 7763; on the faster runner and
  on the dev machine an exact 3x passes. The two runs do not establish a robust portable
  bound (one in 173-180 ms, over 2x the slow run's 1x and under the fast run's 3x, fits both
  with ~1-3% margin). A speed-independent ratio gate is
  the follow-up.
- **The lowerer reads two new shapes of the `4d75846c` grammar** (see Changed;
  `crates/al-syntax/src/lower/mod.rs`):
  - A `preproc_split_case_extended` arm may hold a nested `preproc_conditional_case`
    with whole branches in it. The arm read only its direct `case_branch` children, so
    such a branch was dropped with its calls; the arm is now read like a case group's.
    So a `case_else_branch` in such a nested group (it parses clean) becomes the case's
    else, first-match-wins; before, it was dropped.
  - A split terminator (`if C then Bar #if X ; #endif else Baz;`, valid AL) leaves the
    `else` as `(call_statement function: (identifier))` (grammar deferred item 43). It
    was lowered as a call to `else`; it is now skipped, and `Bar` and `Baz` keep their
    calls.
  Tests `split_case_extended_nested_group_branch_is_kept` (also an `#else` arm with a
  branch and a nested group of `;` items), `split_case_extended_nested_group_else_is_the_case_else`
  and `split_terminator_else_is_not_a_call`: each fails when its arm is broken and passes
  after the revert.

- **Nested `#if` case groups no longer recurse without a bound.** `collect_case_branches_in`
  recursed once per nested `preproc_conditional_case` or `preproc_split_case_extended`
  arm with the depth unchanged, and only statements and expressions checked
  `MAX_LOWER_DEPTH`. Each nested level now adds one to the depth, and past the budget the
  lowerer records a `SyntaxIssue` and drops the deeper branches.
  `deep_nested_case_groups_degrade_instead_of_overflowing_small_stack` (300 levels, 1 MiB
  stack) fails with the check removed and passes with it.

- agentflow `post-merge` no longer reads a missing CDO workspace as a red gate. On
  #107 it ran without `CDO_WS`. `cdo-gate` stopped at its usage error (exit 2),
  and the executor counted that as a regression. It tried to revert a green
  merge; the revert failed the same way, so nothing was pushed. `post-merge` now
  refuses with `cdo-ws-unset` before it opens the verification, as `preflight`
  already did. A new `cdo_ws` key in `.agent/config.json` names the pinned
  workspace once, and every executor call uses it whatever the shell exported.

## [2.0.0] - 2026-10-19

A major version, because some changes break existing users. Each one is described in full below:

- **Library API** (#160 step 1b): `build_cross_app_program` is gone (use
  `ResolvedProgram::build`), and `attach_program_calls` now takes `(rows, program)` and
  returns `(Model, ProgramMeta)`. `site_census`, `SiteLinks::build` and
  `resolved_calls_from_program` take an `EdgeView`. `cross_app_demand` and
  `Histogram::of_edges` take iterators.
- **Analysis results** (#100): `Record.TestField` is no longer a table `read`.
  `alsem diff` of an older snapshot against a new one therefore reports
  `CapabilityLost` for each read that was removed. `Rename` and `LockTable` now
  produce table facts (op `rename` / `lock`), and a policy on `resourceKind: table`
  with no `op` filter now matches them.
- **Exit code:** `alsem analyze` exits 2 when it fails to write its output.
- **Diagnostics:** `C1_CONE_CENSUS=1` is replaced by `ALSEM_RETAINED_CENSUS=1`, and the
  trace span `r3a3.calls_graph` is split into two.

### Added

- `scripts/bench_ab.py`: an A/B bench of two binaries in interleaved rounds (side
  order flips every round). It records wall clock, the psutil peak, the trace's
  `peak.process_mb`/`peak.post_attach_mb` and a stdout hash per run, and its
  `summary` mode prints medians, bands and "B higher in k/n pairs" per command.
  It replaces the one-off bench scripts that every measurement task rewrote.
- `scripts/trace_summary.py --compare '<A glob>' '<B glob>'`: per-span medians,
  bands, B − A and the pair count across two sets of traces, runs paired by round.
- #160 step 0, the measurement harness (diagnostic only; no output byte moves):
  - Build counters in the trace (`build.program`, `build.combined_graph`, `build.cone`,
    `build.summaries_v2`, `build.graph_scc`, `build.pd_solve`, `build.detector_context`,
    `build.snapshot`, `build.ordering_facts`), pinned per command and universe by
    `tests/cli/cli_build_counters.rs`.
  - Cone-census timers under `ALSEM_CONES_CENSUS=1`: the BFS walk and fold apart
    (`BFS_WALK_NANOS`, `BFS_FOLD_NANOS`, `BFS_PICKS`), the singleton scan split by entry
    class (`closed_entries=`, `open_entries=`, `own_entries=`; the old `cone_entries=`
    counted all three), `PD_SOLVE_NANOS`/`PD_SOLVE_CALLS`, the signed `COMPOSE_REST_NANOS` remainder,
    and the pd-solve bytes split into arena and working set. New trace spans
    `digest.tx_context_map`, `prove.tx_context_map`, `b3.adapter.join`,
    `b3.adapter.by_decl`, `b3.adapter.convert`, `r3a3.clone_inputs` and
    `r3a3.graph_build`. The last two replace `r3a3.calls_graph`, which covered both
    the snapshot base's input clones and its graph build: old `r3a3.calls_graph` =
    `r3a3.clone_inputs` + `r3a3.graph_build`.
  - The post-attach phase peak: `alsem` opens `pt::run("alsem")` and emits
    `peak.process_mb` and `peak.post_attach_mb` (Windows; 0 elsewhere), also when
    `ALSEM_TRACE_EXIT_AFTER` ends the run early. `peak.post_attach_mb` is the maximum
    over every model's post-attach phase (`diff` ends each side's phase when that side's
    model is dropped). Only a binary that opens `pt::run` starts the sampler.
  - The retained byte census under `ALSEM_RETAINED_CENSUS=1` (`src/engine/census.rs`):
    one `[retained-census] bucket=… bytes=… allocs=… kind=exact|shallow` line per program,
    model, base, context, snapshot and arena structure, with `census_hook` marks so
    `census-probe retained <ws>` gives the live heap at each bucket point (its own mode,
    so `census-probe model`'s phase peaks are not skewed by the marks). d47's ordering
    cell is counted when it is filled. The cross-app base charges the model it keeps
    (`base.resolved.rows`) beside the replacement calls (`base.resolved.calls`).
  - `aldump --issue160-full-graph-timings <ws>`: the snapshot's cone, pd-solve and derive
    cost, and its raw inherited facts (count and bytes), over the cut graph and the full
    graph (measurement only; deleted at step 6).
  - The step 0 CDO numbers: `docs/measurements/2026-10-18-issue-160-step0.md`.
- #160 step 1, the frozen `InputSet` (`src/program/inputs.rs`): every `alsem` command
  that builds the program reads its workspace inputs once, at the start, and every
  later reader reads that one set. It holds `app.json` and the `app.json` walk, the `.al`
  walk and texts (with the nested-app flag), `roots.config.json`, the coverage yaml, the
  policy request and file, the baseline file, the dependency closure, the snapshot hash
  rows when asked for, the driver version and the model-instance id. Two reads stay
  outside it by design: the dependency `.app` files themselves (the set holds the list
  and the hash rows, the loader still opens each `.app`), and `policy explain`, which
  builds nothing. `InputSet::read` charges the trace counter `inputs.read` (1 per
  command; `diff ws ws` reads one set per side) and is timed by the span `inputs.read`.
  `analyze` checks `--preset` / `--detector`, and `fingerprint` its `--inventory-only`
  combinations, before the read. `analyze --format json` takes `alsemVersion` from the set.
  `tests/common/unreadable.rs` makes a file or folder unreadable for tests.
  The step 1 CDO numbers: `docs/measurements/2026-10-19-issue-160-step1.md`.

### Changed

- agentflow can keep build output off the worktrees' drive: `target_root` in
  `.agent/config.json` (default empty: unchanged). `make-worktree` then makes the issue
  worktree's `target/` a junction into `<target_root>/<worktree name>` (still one build
  folder per worktree, so two runs never share one, #60), and `cleanup` deletes that folder
  with the worktree. The disk guard follows the builds: the worktrees' drive keeps only
  `min_free_gb`, and `reserve_gb_per_run` per live run is asked of the target drive
  (`disk-free:targets:<n>GB` in `preflight`, `disk-low:targets:…` on `claim`, and
  `target_free_gb` / `target_required_gb` in the payload).
- Gate speed-ups (spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-gate-speedups-design.md`):
  - `agentflow run` records every gate run in `<run dir>/gate-runs.jsonl`: gate, exit code,
    HEAD, tree, clean before and after, `rustc`, grammar commit and dirt, and the CDO
    workspace identity (path, commit, dirt, a hash of every dependency `.app`) for `cdo-gate`.
  - `agentflow post-merge` skips its gates when the merge is provably the gated tree: this
    run's merge (never a recovered one), a green attestation, the squash on the attested base,
    the merge tree equal to `final_head`'s, only evidence files after `H`, no earlier
    post-merge stop on the merge, and a green, clean record for each gate on `H`'s tree, with
    post-merge's own command, in the same environment (a record whose tree or environment
    moved while the gate ran names neither). Any doubt runs the gates as
    before. The payload carries `verified_by` (`identity` | `gates`) and `identity_refused`
    (every reason a skip was refused); `--full` forces the gates. It used to take 15–28 min
    per merge.
  - `scripts/ci-steps test` and `scripts/check-goldens` run on cargo-nextest (doc-tests still
    on `cargo test --doc`); both fail with a clear message when nextest is missing, and CI
    installs it. Measured 2026-10-18, warm tree, two runs each, same test counts (3430 and
    876): `ci-steps test` 46–50 s against 81–104 s; `check-goldens` 27–31 s against 64–80 s,
    at ~0.3 GB more peak memory (1.5 vs 1.25 GB). `scripts/cdo-gate` stays on `cargo test`:
    nextest took 97–112 s against 72–84 s, because it runs one process per test and the
    harness rebuilds its shared CDO context in each.
- A failed write of a command's output (stdout or an `--out` file) prints one text on
  every command, `al-sem: write error: <stdout|path>: <OS message>`, through one writer
  in `alsem.rs`. `analyze` now exits 2 on it (on a closed pipe it aborted before); every
  other command keeps exit 1 (before, with four different texts). The message goes
  through the stderr writer, so a closed stderr does not turn the exit code into a panic.
- #160 step 1b: the program build is one `ResolvedProgram` (`src/program/resolved.rs`):
  the build's facts (`ProgramMeta`) apart from its body (`ProgramBody`), with the
  resolver's edges (the workspace's routines, plus the event-flow edges of publishers in
  every app) and the dependency bodies' call-site edges kept as two sets and read in
  that order through one `EdgeView` (both sets private to `resolved.rs`).
  `build_cross_app_program` is replaced by `ResolvedProgram::build(inputs, scope)`: a
  `ProgramScope` (`Workspace`: the Summary profile, no dependency call-site edges; `CrossApp`:
  `FULL` plus every dependency body resolved) states what is resolved, not only what is
  kept, and the program records it. The body is not optional: `alsem graph` borrows the
  program, and `attach_program_calls(rows, program)` consumes it and hands back the
  `ProgramMeta`, so a second reader after the release is a compile error, not a panic,
  and analyze's single-app arm moves the build's coverage instead of cloning it.
  `alsem graph` reuses that program build (`CrossApp`, then `export_from_program`, which
  returns an error for a `Workspace` program instead of a graph without dependency
  edges), and its projection reads both edge sets through the `EdgeView`; its output is
  byte-identical. `aldump --compiler-oracle` builds the same way (`Workspace`, or
  `CrossApp` under `--all-apps`); without `--all-apps` that is the Summary profile
  where it was `FULL`, and its CDO report is byte-identical in both modes. The scope is
  readable only (`ProgramMeta::scope()`). Library API: `build_cross_app_program` is
  gone; `attach_program_calls(inputs, rows, ctx, report, coverage) -> Model` is now
  `attach_program_calls(rows, program) -> (Model, ProgramMeta)`; `site_census`,
  `SiteLinks::build` and `resolved_calls_from_program` take an `EdgeView` instead of a
  `&ProgramReport`; `cross_app_demand` and `Histogram::of_edges` take any iterator of
  edges instead of a slice. A `ResolvedProgram`'s meta and body are read through
  `meta()` / `body()` only, so one build's meta cannot be swapped onto another's body. The retained census gains an `inputs` bucket (the
  command's `InputSet`, 5.30 MB on CDO), `program.snapshot_texts` now counts the
  dependency units only, and `program.report` still counts the coverage contract's
  `missing`/`extra` and the recovered files. No output byte moves. The CDO numbers:
  `docs/measurements/2026-10-19-issue-160-step1b.md`.
- `C1_CONE_CENSUS=1` is replaced by `ALSEM_RETAINED_CENSUS=1`; the old
  `[C1_CONE_CENSUS]` report is gone (its structures are covered by the `context.*`
  buckets).
- The cone census report (`[cones-census]`) prints once at process exit, with the
  process total of every cone the command composed (the snapshot's included), instead
  of at the end of the detector context's cone block.

### Fixed

- #160 step 1: no `alsem` reader goes back to the disk after the program build. The
  model id, roots config, program-file selection, coverage projection, inline
  suppressions, pr-summary's app registry, the snapshot hash rows and
  `workspaceFingerprint`, `policy check` and `--baseline` read the command's
  `InputSet`, so a workspace file edited, added or removed during a run can no longer
  give one command two views of the workspace (pinned by
  `tests/cli/cli_inputs_frozen.rs`). A dependency `.app` replaced during a run still
  can: its hash row is read with the set, its contents by the loader.
  With `--update-baseline`, the baseline applied is the one just written.
  `policy check` takes `--no-policy` from the set too (`InputSet::policy_request`), and
  refuses a set read without a policy request.
- #160 step 1: the workspace diagnostics (`No object declaration found in <rel>` and the
  provider rows) read the program build's list of files that parsed to no object
  (`FreshCoverage::files_without_object`) instead of walking and parsing the workspace a
  second time. When the build fails, no fallback parse runs, so those rows are absent.
- An event publisher's parameter roles now include what its subscribers do to a `var` record
  parameter (#107). Before, a publisher (whose body is empty) looked like a no-op to every
  routine that raised its event, so a subscriber's `Modify`, `Validate`, `Get` or `Copy` never
  reached the raiser's roles or the detectors that read them (d37, d39, d40, d41, d42 and their
  load points). Spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-19-issue-107-publisher-roles-subscribers-design.md`.
  - One subscriber that always runs gives the publisher exactly what a direct call to that
    subscriber gives. Two to four subscribers are composed over every order of those that
    always run and every subset of the optional ones; more than four, or a subscriber that
    cannot be seen, makes the publisher behave like an unknown callee. A visible subscriber
    with no body or no role is opaque in its run, and makes the publisher's required entry
    fields `unknown`. Two edges to one subscriber are one subscriber: isolated if any edge is,
    and optional if every edge is or if it is isolated.
  - A subscriber that may not run (manual binding, a license/permission condition in ANY build
    reading, or an isolated event) still contributes its MAY facts (persists, validates, may
    mutate), but never adds or removes a load a caller treats as proven: its load facts
    (`loadsFromDbParam`, `copiesIntoParam`, `initialisesParam`) go `yes -> no`, and an
    `unknown` stays `unknown`. An edge that is not `resolved` makes the whole dispatch unseen.
    The effect on the record's state of an isolated subscriber is not followed.
  - A publisher whose event id another publisher also raises (overloads share one event id,
    and the engine does not keep which overload a subscription selected) dispatches as unseen:
    every presence and path fact of each record parameter is `unknown`, like an unknown callee.
    So a subscriber that selected the other overload adds nothing, not even a MAY fact such as
    a `Reset` that d41 would report.
  - Event-subscriber parameters bind to the publisher's by name in one place
    (`event_param_names_match`), quotes ignored; `pd_solve::carry_reqs` used a second copy that
    did not trim quotes.
  - Source-bearing dependency publishers (cross-app) gain the presence facts of their
    subscribers, workspace subscribers included; their path facts stay `unknown` (#70).
    Symbol-only dependency publishers are unchanged.
  - A roles SCC that hits the iteration cap now publishes the opaque role for its members,
    except `fixed_roles` members, which keep their base roles with every dispatched
    parameter's presence facts `unknown` (their dispatch was folded from an unconverged round).
  - Model event edges (`EventEdge`) carry `conditional` (from the subscription's conditions in
    any build reading) and `mixed_readings` (census only); the combined graph's
    `event-dispatch` edges carry `DispatchMeta { conditional, isolated }`, with `isolated` from
    the event's `EventSymbol`. Neither is projected. The summaries
    census (`ALSEM_SUMMARIES_CENSUS=1`) splits exact parameters into walker and
    `fixed_roles` publishers and counts dispatch sequences once per walk.
  - Goldens: r3a2 summary-core roles of event publishers and their raisers, and d40/d42
    skip-reason counts in `cli-a`; no finding added or removed by the fixtures.
- A routine can carry several readings of one event attribute, one per `#if` build path
  that reads an `#if` group inside the attribute's arguments (since #80). The program
  engine now uses every reading, not only the first (#104):
  - **IncludeSender** is the union of the readings: `true` when any reading is `true`,
    `false` only when every reading is `false`, otherwise unknown. A subscriber that
    captures the extra `Sender` parameter now binds when only a later reading passes it
    (it was orphaned before). One helper (`event::union_include_sender`) holds this rule
    for both per-build readings and `#if`-duplicated publisher routines (#103).
  - **Subscriptions**: readings of one `[EventSubscriber]` that name the same event are
    one subscription and one event-flow edge (they were one per reading). The key is the
    resolved publisher object, so a publisher named by name in one reading and by number
    in another is one key; the element counts only for a platform field/action event,
    where each element is its own event. A skip flag (`SkipOnMissingLicense` /
    `SkipOnMissingPermission`) stays on the merged edge only when every reading sets it.
    The merge happens where subscriptions are wired (`SubscriberIndex::build`) and applies
    to any entries of one routine that name one event, duplicate attributes included, so
    it also gives one edge for two `#if` arms of one routine that subscribe the same event
    with different skip flags; the routine's own subscription list is unchanged.
  - **Isolated** is read from every `IntegrationEvent` and `BusinessEvent` reading: an
    event is isolated (an isolation barrier) when ANY reading is isolated, also when
    another reading of the other publisher kind says it is not. This arises only across
    builds, since AL allows one publisher attribute per build.
  The `IncludeSender +1` preflight diagnostic
  (`count_unknown_include_sender_plus1_subscribers`) can move either way on a publisher
  with several readings; binding is unaffected where it rises. `InternalEvent`'s
  `Isolated` argument is still not read.
- `Record.TestField` is no longer a capability `read` (#100). It checks the value the
  record variable already holds in memory and issues no query; the engine already
  classified it state-only. Its table `read` facts are gone from `--r4f-snapshot`, the
  r1a/r3a3 projections and `alsem fingerprint`, and where a `TestField` was a routine's
  only read of a table, its required `TableData R` row and fingerprint `R` letter go
  too (where another read survives, that read becomes the witness). Effects:
  - `alsem diff` of a snapshot made before this change against one made after reports
    `CapabilityLost` for each removed read.
  - A user policy matching capability `op: read` matches fewer facts.
  - d44 (event multi-subscriber overlap) loses a read-after-write finding when the
    reader subscriber's only read of that table was a `TestField`. Measured on CDO:
    one removed at `--scope all` (Sales Header on `OnBeforePostSalesDoc`), none at
    `--scope primary`; 46 required `TableData R` rows removed.
  - d1/d2 prune a callee whose cone no longer touches a table; a callee that only did
    `TestField` is now pruned, which can free walk budget and ADD a d2 finding that
    the budget used to cut off.
  - Residual (stated, not modelled): under partial records (`SetLoadFields`), touching a
    field that was not loaded makes the platform re-read the row (JIT loading). That
    holds for any field access, and no field access is modelled as a read, so where the
    platform loaded the record (a page's `Rec`, a table trigger's `Rec`, a report
    dataitem), a read and its `TableData R` need can go unreported.
- `Rename` and `LockTable` now give table capability facts, op `rename` and op `lock`
  (#100). d1 and d2 skip callees with no table fact, so a callee whose only database ops
  were `Rename`/`LockTable` was never walked; it is now, which can add d1/d2 findings.
  `Rename` still maps to no permission letter (#9), and neither op makes a permission
  row, digest effect or diff gain. They show in `--r4f-snapshot`, in `alsem fingerprint`
  (a `Rename`/`LockTable`-only routine gains a table family with no permission line), as
  `CapabilityLost` when such a fact disappears between two new snapshots, and in
  policies: `CAPABILITY_OPS` accepts `rename` and `lock`, and a predicate on
  `resourceKind: table` with no `op` filter now matches them (the bundled
  `policy-default.yaml` behaves as before).
- d2 prunes callees on its own presence bit, `TOUCHES_PHYSICAL_TABLE` (#100): set for a
  table fact unless it is a known-temporary non-read. Every read sets it (a temporary
  record's FlowField is still computed against physical tables), so a branch that only
  writes, renames or locks temporary records no longer spends d2's 500-node walk budget.
  An incomplete cone still counts as unknown and is walked. d1 keeps `touches_db`,
  because its temporary terminals are deliberate. The bit reads cone facts, which can
  disagree with d2's own terminal filter in three stated cases: (e) a routine passes its
  own `Temporary` record to a `var` parameter that is written; the write is temporary in
  that caller's frame, so that path's d2 finding (a false positive) is removed; (f) a
  routine whose complete cone holds only known-temporary non-read table facts, and
  whose physical op is unreachable (the cone drops dead code), is now pruned, so that
  dead op gives no finding (a reachable temporary read keeps the routine walked); (g) a `Rename`/`LockTable`-only
  branch on a virtual/system table is now walked with no terminal (meaningless AL; left
  open).
- One table op map serves L2 and the L4 cone: the cone's pass-through wrapper
  `capability_cone::map_table_op` is deleted and the cone calls `table_commit::map_op`
  directly (#100).

## [1.7.2] - 2026-10-17

### Added

- `alsem events fanout`, `alsem events chains` and `alsem policy check` now load the
  workspace's dependencies by default, the same cross-app model `alsem analyze` builds
  (#70). A workspace subscriber to a dependency event is now reported (single-app saw 0
  events for it), policy rules see a dependency's table names and the facts its code adds,
  and the analyzer diagnostics on stderr come from the cross-app run. Only workspace
  routines are evaluated by policy rules; the dependency routines stay in the model for
  lookup. `--single-app` analyses the workspace alone, as before. JSON output carries a
  top-level `dependencies` statement right after `kind` (`mode` `crossApp` / `singleApp`
  and the loaded `apps`, as `digest` and `query` do since #66); human output starts with a
  `dependencies: …` line when apps were loaded (a fixture that declares `platform` lists
  System and System Application as `missing`); SARIF is unchanged, since no consumer reads
  a statement there. In cross-app mode `events --scope all` also lists events between
  dependency routines only. A workspace without `app.json` fails in both modes with
  `could not compute modelInstanceId`; any other failure to build the cross-app model names
  `--single-app`.
  CDO (`U:/Git/DO-cdo-baseline/Cloud`, release-fast, before = single-app): `events fanout`
  4.5 s → 22.8 s and 188 → 248 events (3 hot, 6 with partial coverage); `events chains`
  4.2 s → 22.2 s, 188 → 248 roots; `policy check` 4.2 s → 24.2 s, 7 → 18 findings
  (`no-commit-in-event-subscribers` 4 → 10, `no-http-from-table-triggers` 0 → 4,
  `install-codeunit-no-business-data-writes` 3 → 4; `routinesEvaluated` unchanged, 5479
  workspace routines). Of the 16 new or changed policy findings, 9 were triaged real and 7
  false positives, none from the cross-app plumbing: 6 come from existing reachability and
  transaction-boundary limits (4 of them a Guided Experience commit that runs only for
  `IsPrimarySetup = true`, 1 a commit an early exit makes unreachable, 1 a commit inside a page
  started non-modally), and 1 from the `* Setup` table-name exemption, which does not cover a
  feature-flag table. `--single-app` output is identical to the old default apart from the
  `dependencies` key. `alsem analyze` findings, `--program-call-graph-stats` and the CDO
  fingerprint are byte-identical before and after this change.
- `CapabilitySnapshot.pd_solution` (not serialized): the producer solve as an arena of
  states and links over the snapshot's typed edges, in stable routine ids (#69 D2).
  `ALSEM_CONES_CENSUS=1` reports the solve's producers, states, links, entries, distinct
  edges and retained bytes (`solve_bytes`: the cone solve plus every snapshot arena, each
  `Vec` and hash table at capacity, shared data counted once; `snapshot_bytes`: the
  snapshot arenas alone), and the solve links that found no snapshot edge.
- A5 oracle: cone/L4 temp-class parity on a matched graph, per producer and reduced
  (`tests/r3/r3_temp_class_parity*.rs`), plus a check that every arena link names the
  snapshot edge of its hop.
- `scripts/sweep-builds [--dry-run] [--days N]`: deletes Rust build output not used for N
  days (default 7) and output from toolchains no longer installed, in the main checkout and
  every `al-sem-issue-*` worktree, through `cargo-sweep` (`cargo install cargo-sweep`). It
  uses age mode, not cargo-sweep's stamp mode, because NTFS updates last-access times up to
  an hour late. The first run cleaned 13.2 GiB. Background: U: filled up for the third time
  on 2026-10-14, which failed #68's post-merge check on a green merge.
- `alsem digest`: Interface and ControlAddIn PROCEDURES are now changed roots. A change
  inside one (or `--file` on its file) gives a "declaration-only" entry: `routine.declarationOnly:
  true`, `effects` and `unresolved` empty, `coverage` status `unknown` with the new reason
  `declaration-only`. It is counted once in `rootsRequested` and `rootsResolved` and adds no
  `DIAG-digest-*` diagnostic. Its `stableId` keeps the `<app>:<Kind>:0#<hash>` shape, with the
  object's LOGICAL name (a quoted `"I""Foo"` is `I"Foo`) folded into the hash, because every
  unnumbered object shares object number 0; two interfaces declaring the same
  `procedure Bar()` therefore give two roots. The method becomes a root, not the routines
  that implement it (#81), and `--routine` selectors do not reach these procedures.
  ControlAddIn `event` declarations are not lowered as routines, so they are not roots.
  Carried on the model as `ModelObject.declaration_only_routines`, which follows the same
  file population as the model's routines. Limit: declaration-only roots are special-cased
  in digest instead of being model routines; the root cause is the model's stale
  Interface/ControlAddIn skip (#82). Pinned by `declaration_only_procedures_are_roots`,
  `interface_object_rows_carry_declaration_only_routines`,
  `quoted_interface_name_is_unescaped_in_the_id` and
  `declaration_only_routines_follow_the_population` (#71).
- `alsem digest`: `routine.anchors` lists every declaration's anchor, in document order, for a
  routine id that has more than one declaration (two `#if` arms with one signature). The key
  is absent when the id has one declaration (#71).

### Changed

- The cold dependency build (`build_dep_nodes`) lowers its peak memory (#84). Before step 2 it
  counts the dependency layer's nodes once: the source summaries' objects, routines and routine
  metadata (already in memory), plus the nodes each SymbolOnly dependency will produce
  (`abi_ingest::abi_node_counts`, which shares one ABI lookup, `load_abi`, with `ingest_abi`).
  It reserves the node lists once to those totals, instead of growing them by doubling, then
  fills them in step 2 and step 2b as before. Counting loads each ABI through the `AbiCache`,
  so the ingest pass loads nothing again. `ingest_abi` sizes each app's lists exactly. The
  overload-preserving routine dedup works in place (`retain_mut`) with no second list, and
  then trims the list's capacity to its pre-dedup length, as the old rebuild did. The graph's
  contents and order do not change.
- Every dependency moved to its newest release, and `Cargo.lock` is now committed so builds
  are reproducible. The trigger: on 2026-10-16 the `zip` maintainer yanked every release
  before 9.0.3 after three extraction advisories (GHSA-4v9h-p7m9-rh26, GHSA-vv5m-jxxh-4627,
  GHSA-4684-h2q9-2vcp), and `zip = "2"` no longer resolved. al-sem never calls `extract`.
  - Major moves: `zip` 2 -> 9, `tree-sitter` 0.26 -> 0.27, `salsa` 0.27.0 -> 0.28.5 (still
    pinned exactly), `lsp-server` 0.7 -> 0.10, `string-interner` 0.17 -> 0.20, `phf`
    0.11 -> 0.14, `notify` 7 -> 8, `dirs` 6 -> 7, `sha2` 0.10 -> 0.11, `hmac` 0.12 -> 0.13,
    `roxmltree` 0.20 -> 0.21, `criterion` 0.5 -> 0.8, and the telemetry set together
    (`opentelemetry`/`opentelemetry_sdk` 0.26 -> 0.33, `opentelemetry-application-insights`
    0.36 -> 0.46, `tracing-opentelemetry` 0.27 -> 0.34, `reqwest` 0.12 -> 0.13, `lru`
    0.12 -> 0.18, plus `opentelemetry-http` 0.33 for the blocking client).
  - Code changes:
    - salsa's `Update` derive is now `SalsaValue`.
    - tree-sitter 0.27 ties `Node::kind` to the tree's lifetime, so `kind_str` reads the
      kind name through one `'static` grammar handle.
    - zip's `ZipFile` takes the reader type, and `name()` can fail. It fails only on a name
      that is neither UTF-8 nor CP437; such an entry is skipped like an unreadable one.
    - `hmac`'s `new_from_slice` moved to `KeyInit`.
    - `sha2` digests no longer format as `{:x}`.
    - The App Insights exporter is built through `SdkTracerProvider`; `service.name` on the
      resource keeps the `cloud_RoleName`.
    - Benches use `std::hint::black_box`.
  - TLS stays on rustls with `ring`. reqwest 0.13's `rustls` feature defaults to
    `aws-lc-rs`, whose C binds `strtol` to glibc 2.38's `__isoc23_strtol`, and the Linux
    release binary then failed the glibc 2.34 floor. reqwest is built `rustls-no-provider`,
    and the exporter installs the `ring` provider.
- `prove`, `fingerprint` and `diff` stay single-app (#70). Their output is a capability
  snapshot, and the cross-app snapshot does not yet follow calls made inside dependency
  code: on a workspace routine that calls a dependency routine which calls another that
  commits, it reports complete coverage and no commit. `prove may-commit` would then answer
  `no`. `diff` compares fingerprint snapshots, so it keeps fingerprint's mode.
- `compose_cone_over_graph`'s `ConeOutcome` carries the producer solve as `pd_solution`
  (`pd_solve::ConeArena`: producers, states, links and a per-routine index; #69 D1).
  A link indexes the arena's table of distinct edges, and a resolved entry borrows its
  first-hop edge from the graph, instead of each owning a clone of the edge and its five
  strings: on CDO `alsem analyze`, 984,412 links share 15,172 edges, and the solve holds
  119.2 MiB (counted at capacity, with `Vec` slack and table overhead). The analyzer drops the
  arena once the cone is built.
- `alsem digest` frees the snapshot (with its solve arena), the ordering entries and the L4
  store as soon as the digest query is done, before the envelope's detector run and the
  JSON projection. CDO digest probe (the first 200 files) peak RSS: 6446..6488 MiB before
  #69, 5297..5333 MiB now; output byte-identical (#69 D1.4).
- `viaPathsTruncated` now also means a non-empty path set is not known to be complete: a
  state or depth limit cut the witness enumeration (BFS or proofs). Such effects can move
  from `conditional` to `unknown` conditionality, ordering chains report `capped`, and
  `alsem prove`'s witness-truncated check (any effect's `viaPathsTruncated`) fires, so a
  prove answer can move to `unknown` (#69 D3). Empty path sets (`terminal-not-found`, `first-hop-not-found`, or a limit hit
  that found nothing) are not folded; they are decided over the proofs and the BFS together.
- `FingerprintIndexesPub` gains `pd_solution`, `typed_edges` and `capability_facts`, and
  `oracle_r3a3_inherited_keys_trace_to_a_direct_producer` accepts an inherited key from an
  ordinary direct fact or from the routine's own solve states, no longer a PD→kt rewrite
  (#69 D3).
- digest/prove `detail.tempState` is a per-operation join filtered to the effect's class
  (#69 D4): each originating operation contributes only its L4 rows in the effect's temp
  class (kt = `known(true)`); one with rows only in the other class contributes all of
  them; one with no L4 row makes the field absent. Each failed operation is a new entry
  diagnostic `temp-state-incoherent` with `factId`, `operationId` and `reason`
  (`no-l4-row` | `class-absent`). digest `schemaVersion` 1.6.0, prove 1.4.0 (additive).
  Goldens moved: the `schemaVersion` line of 21 digest and 19 prove files under
  `tests/cli-b-goldens/`, nothing else. Pinned by `a1b_no_temp_state_incoherence`,
  `a2b_one_effect_per_class` and the two `digest_cli::tests::temp_join_*` unit tests. Every
  `cli_digest_temp_state` test fails on any `temp-state-incoherent` item (the `class-absent`
  fallback would otherwise hide a wrong class from a test that reads the rendered value). The
  text output shows the diagnostic's `reason=` and `op=`. `alsem prove` shows the same
  `tempState` value (one shared builder) but carries no entry diagnostics, so it does not
  show `temp-state-incoherent`, and it does not count it as an incomplete witness: the
  diagnostic is about the rendered `tempState`, which no prove obligation reads (prove still
  treats only `evidence-unavailable`, and `viaPathsTruncated`, as an incomplete witness).
- Measured on the CDO baseline (`bc3ccb18`, release-fast, against master before #69), #69 as
  a whole: `aldump --program-call-graph-stats` is byte-identical (unknown 0). Detectors only
  lose tables, never gain a write: `alsem analyze` cross-app default findings 2292 -> 2293
  at `--scope primary` and 27106 -> 26954 at `--scope all` (d43 -139 +1, d44 -14; d9, d8 and
  d50 `affectedTables` shrink; the opt-in set 399 -> 394 / 418 -> 413, d45 -4 +1, d49 -2).
  Every change is a `Validate`/`Copy`/`TransferFields` no longer counted as a write, a
  write now known temporary, or d45's per-publisher cap letting a hidden table in.
  `temp-state-incoherent`: 0 over 16,764 DB_INSERT/DB_MODIFY/DB_DELETE effects (5,512 roots).
  Cost: peak RSS of `alsem analyze` unchanged (2827..2838 MiB before, 2830..2835 now), the
  digest probe 6446..6488 -> 5297..5333 MiB, wall time +6.5% (analyze) and +4.3% (digest);
  the solve holds 119.2 MiB (analyze) and 186.7 MiB (digest probe), 4.2% and 2.9% of peak.
- `alsem digest --file` / `--diff` find changed roots by routine declaration SPAN: the
  first attached attribute line through the header, `var` section, body and `end;`. Before,
  a routine was matched only through the start lines of the operations and call sites the
  snapshot indexed, so a change on a plain assignment line, a header, a `var` line or
  `end;` found no routine, and a routine with no indexed operation (an empty event publisher,
  a pure function) could never be a root. Now, for `--diff`: an added or changed line touches
  the span that holds it; a deletion touches a span only when the gap lies inside it (so
  deleting a whole routine, or blank lines between routines, blames no neighbour), with one
  narrow exception: a run of deleted lines that is one or more complete attribute groups
  (each starts with a trimmed `[` and runs, over one or more lines, until its brackets
  balance, with nothing else between groups; after a closing `]` only whitespace, another
  group or a `//` comment may follow on its line) right above a span belongs to that routine,
  so deleting its first or only attribute, single- or multi-line, makes it a root. Limit:
  brackets are counted on raw text, so a `[` or `]` inside a string argument can
  misclassify the run. Context lines never count. `--file` takes every routine the
  file declares. Only workspace (`ws:`) routines are indexed. Pinned in
  `tests/cli/cli_digest_changed_spans.rs` (`hunk_on_assignment_line_is_a_changed_root`,
  `every_routine_shape_line_maps_to_its_routine`, `context_lines_do_not_create_roots`,
  `deletions_resolve_by_interior_gap`, `deleting_a_routines_first_attribute_line_makes_it_a_root`,
  `deleting_a_multi_line_attribute_makes_the_routine_a_root`,
  `deleting_a_routine_on_its_attribute_closing_line_blames_no_neighbour`,
  `one_inside_one_outside_hunk`, `rename_with_and_without_hunks`,
  `file_with_only_opless_routines_is_matched`, `file_digest_returns_every_routine_of_the_file`,
  `hunkless_modified_file_takes_every_declaration`, `object_level_hunk_is_outside_routines`,
  `limits_are_pinned`) and `diff_parser::tests::attribute_only_deletion_runs`. Stated limits:
  an `#if`/`#else`/`#endif` line gives no root (pinned by `limits_are_pinned`); an attribute
  separated from its routine by a comment, pragma or `#if` is not in the span (#80, since
  fixed: see Fixed); the
  arms of an `#if`-split procedure header with DIFFERENT signatures share one span, so a
  change in either arm's header line makes both arms' ids roots (a safe over-approximation).
  Object-level changes (global `var`, fields, properties) still map to no routine (#79).
- The changed-root diagnostics have new meanings: `file-unmatched` means the file declares no
  routine at all (Interface/ControlAddIn procedures count); `diff-file-unmatched` means the
  same for a diff path; `hunk-outside-routines` means none of the hunk's changed lines touch a
  span (it still reports the hunk header's range). A file with one hunk inside a routine and
  one outside gives the root and the diagnostic, exit 0; exit 2 still means zero roots.
- `routine.anchor` in `alsem digest` and `alsem prove` is now the routine's declaration
  (`source_anchor` line and column, the original `ws:` file name with its case kept), never
  the first operation or call site inside the body. Routines that had no anchor now have one.
  For an id with more than one declaration, the anchor is the LAST declaration the input
  touched (R2-02): under `--diff` with one arm changed, that arm; with both arms changed, or
  under `--file` or `--routine`, the last declaration, which is the value root-slot routines
  had before. Columns stay UTF-8 byte columns. Pinned by `entry_anchor_is_the_declaration`,
  `duplicate_id_anchor_follows_the_changed_arm` and `mixed_inputs_union_touched_declarations`.
  **Limit for bc-dev-mcp (separate repo, not changed here):** its reader reads only the
  singular anchor and calls `--file`, so for a two-arm id it joins only the last arm when its
  subjects carry an `endLine`. `risk.ts` can stop avoiding `--diff` now, and
  `parseAlSemDigest` should expand an entry over `routine.anchors` (#71).
- Digest `schemaVersion` 1.4.0 → 1.5.0, for the additive `routine.declarationOnly`,
  `routine.anchors` and the `declaration-only` coverage reason. Prove stays 1.3.0: its routine
  reference gains no key, only anchor values can differ, and no prove golden moved. The two
