  (#71).
- `ModelRoutine` gains `declaration_start_line` (the first attached attribute's line, or the
  header line), and `AttributeIr` gains `origin`. `source_anchor` is unchanged (#71).
- Goldens, in two regenerations. Regen #1 (span rule and anchors), 9 files:

- Not fixed by #71, filed as issues: #76 (a `./src/x.al` spelling never matches), #77 (a

### Removed

- The frame-bound parameter-dependent cone entry (`ConeFactEntry.pd`) and its
  singleton-only substitution in `substitute_entry`, which now carries guards only (#69 D1).

### Fixed

- **agentflow: a design marked by reviewer stand-ins can be handed off (#141,
  `scripts/agentflow/cli.py`).** `attest` accepts `--substitute SLOT=REVIEWER`,
  but `finish --outcome handoff` judged the handoff rule against the fixed
  `astra`/`flash` roster and had no such flag. A register whose marks were
  recorded under the stand-ins (`sol`/`opus`) had empty slots on every entry, so
  it was always `handoff-not-ready`.
  - `finish --outcome handoff` now takes the same `--substitute` flags, defined
    once for both commands and validated by the same `_substituted_roster`
    (`bad-substitute`: unknown slot, a slot twice, one reviewer in both slots, a
    malformed spec). Refusals still label and comment nothing and keep the lock.
  - `--substitute` on any other outcome exits 2; a flag accepted and then
    ignored would be a silent no-op.
  - The handoff record stores `reviewers`, and the public comment names the
    stand-ins. The next claim carries `reviewers`; `attest` does not apply it on
    its own, so a mismatched roster fails closed (`register-not-converged`). A
    record without `reviewers` (older than this change) claims as before.
  - `.claude/commands/{issue,orchestrate}.md` and the orchestrator spec say how
    the flags travel from `/issue` to `finish` and to the next attempt's
    `attest`, and the preflight reviewer check now checks the operator's
    stand-ins when a loop uses them.

  9 new tests in `scripts/agentflow/tests/test_cli_flow.py`; the suite is 294
  passed (was 285).

- **agentflow: two processes can write one JSON file safely
  (`scripts/agentflow/{state,lock}.py`).** This is step 2 of the parallel-issues
  design and changes no behaviour of a single run.
  - `write_json` wrote every file through one fixed temp name (`x.json.tmp`). Two
    writers of one file shared that temp file, and one `os.replace` moved away
    the file the other was replacing. Two real processes writing one file 200
    times each failed with `WinError 32` within the first writes. The temp name
    is now unique per call (`<name>.<pid>.<uuid>.tmp`), and a failed write
    removes its temp file.
  - On Windows, `os.replace` onto a file another process has open raises
    `PermissionError`, and so does opening a file while another process
    replaces it. A write and a read now retry that error 40 times, 50 ms apart
    (2 s), then raise. The design asked for 5 retries at 100 ms on the write
    and one on the read; measured with two processes, that still failed about
    1 run in 15, and 2 s failed 0 of 60.
  - `read_json` retries a parse error once. A file that is still bad on the
    retry raises as before.
  - `lock.beat` rewrote `.agent/lock.json` in place, so a reader in another
    process (the conductor, while the supervisor beats) could see half a file.
    Lease rewrites now go through `write_json`. `acquire`'s first write stays
    create-exclusive.

  6 new tests in `scripts/agentflow/tests/test_{state,lock}.py`, one of them with
  two real processes; the suite is 300 passed (was 294).

- **agentflow: shared records are read, changed and written under an OS lock
  (`scripts/agentflow/{state,incidents,discoveries,budget,lock,cli}.py`).** Step
  3 of the parallel-issues design. There is still one issue lock; this only
  stops two processes from losing each other's updates.
  - `state.mutex(ctx, name)` holds an OS file lock on
    `.agent/mutex/<name>.lock` (`msvcrt.locking` on Windows, `fcntl.flock`
    elsewhere). The OS drops it when the process dies, so it never goes stale.
    It waits up to 30 s, then raises `MutexTimeout`. It is not re-entrant, so
    only public entry points take one. It is a no-op under `--dry-run`.
  - `state.update_json` is the one read-modify-write helper: it holds the
    mutex, reads, applies a function and writes. When the function raises,
    nothing is written.
  - Moved onto it: `loop.json` (`loop-tick`, `loop-reset`; mutex `registry`),
    `handoffs.json` (`claim`'s consume and `finish --outcome handoff`; mutex
    `handoffs`), and `incidents.json` (open, outcome, verified, resolve; mutex
    `incidents`). `claim` used to write back the copy it read before its gh
    calls, which dropped a handoff another run wrote in between.
  - `file-discoveries` holds mutex `discoveries` per discovery, from the index
    check through search, create and save, and re-reads the index inside it;
    `reconcile_pending` holds it too. Before, two runs filing one discovery at
    once both searched, found nothing, and both created a public issue. This
    mutex is held across gh calls, so its waiters allow 300 s.
  - Every `audit.jsonl` line is appended under mutex `audit`. `set_halt` still
    lands HALT when that mutex times out.

  11 new tests, 4 of them with two real processes (two loop ticks at
  `issues_done = 2` under `--max 3`, two incidents, one discovery filed twice, a
  mutex held across processes); the suite is 311 passed (was 300).

- **agentflow: settings live in `.agent/config.json` (`scripts/agentflow/{state,cli}.py`).**
  Step 4 of the parallel-issues design. `state.config(ctx)` reads the file over
  the defaults `slots: 1`, `heavy_gates: 1`, `min_free_gb: 40`,
  `reserve_gb_per_run: 30` and `gate_wait_minutes: 180`; a missing file or key
  is the default, so nothing changes until the owner writes the file. It is a
  file, not a flag or an env var, so two sessions cannot disagree. An unknown
  key, a non-integer or a negative value is a `ConfigError`, not a quiet
  default. `preflight`'s free-disk floor now reads `min_free_gb` from it
  (`cli.MIN_FREE_GB` is gone). The other keys are read by later steps.

  7 new tests in `scripts/agentflow/tests/test_{state,cli_flow}.py`; the suite is
  318 passed (was 311).

- **agentflow: one lease per issue (`scripts/agentflow/{lock,state,cli,recovery}.py`).**
  Step 5 of the parallel-issues design. A claim now writes
  `.agent/locks/issue-<N>.json`, create-exclusive, so one issue can never have
  two runs. `lock.acquire` runs under mutex `registry` and refuses
  `run-holds-a-lock` (one run, one issue), `issue-held:<run>` (the issue has a
  lease, live or stale) or `slots-full` (as many leases as `slots` in
  `.agent/config.json`; stale leases count until `recover` frees them).
  `claim` and `unblock` report that code as their `error`, before any gh call.
  With the default `slots: 1`, a claim while another issue is held still fails,
  as before, now as `slots-full`. New: `lock.all_locks`, `own`, `for_issue`,
  `drop`; `lock.read` is a shim (the run's own lease, else the only lease).
  `check_fence(ctx, issue=)` refuses a call that names another issue, and
  `finish` uses it, so `finish --issue 9` under a lease for 8 no longer labels
  issue 9. `claim` bumps `attempts.json` under mutex `registry`, re-read, so two
  claims of two issues keep both bumps. `unblock` runs as `unblock-<6 hex>`,
  takes no slot, and refuses `issue-held`. `recover_stale` removes only the
  stale issue's lease, and only while it still names the stale run. A
  `.agent/lock.json` written by the old code is read as one more lease: its
  owner beats, fences and releases it in place, it holds its slot and its
  issue, and nothing new is written there.

  14 new tests in `scripts/agentflow/tests/test_{lock,cli_flow,cli_units}.py`
  (three real-process claim races, the legacy lease, the issue cross-check);
  the suite is 332 passed (was 318).

- **agentflow: commands read the run's own lease (`scripts/agentflow/{cli,lock}.py`).**
  Step 6 of the parallel-issues design. With slots, a sibling's lease always
  exists, so "a lease that is not mine" no longer means "I lost mine".
  - `run` is supervised when the run owns a lease, refused (`FenceError`) when
    it owns none while any lease exists, and unsupervised only with no lease.
    The gate heartbeat beats the run's own lease.
  - `cleanup` of an issue worktree (`al-sem-issue-<N>-a<k>`) is fenced by issue
    N's lease only; a sibling holding another issue no longer refuses it. A
    verification worktree is still refused while any foreign lease is live.
  - `preflight` lists every lease in `locks` (with `stale`). Its old
    `lock-live:<run>` failure is now `slots-full`, counted on LIVE leases
    only, so a stale lease never stops the tick before `recover`. A new
    `warnings` list says `cargo-target-dir-set:<dir>` when `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`
    is set (every worktree would build into one directory, #60).
  - `status` adds `locks`.
  - `clear-halt` and `resolve-incident` are refused while ANY lease is live.
  - `fetch` excludes every issue with a lease, live or stale, as
    `locked:<run>`, even when its `agent-working` label is missing.

  7 new tests in `scripts/agentflow/tests/test_{cli_flow,cli_units}.py`; the
  `post-merge` preflight test now expects `slots-full`. The suite is 339 passed
  (was 332).

- **agentflow: recovery works on one issue's lease (`scripts/agentflow/{lock,cli,recovery}.py`).**
  Step 7 of the parallel-issues design.
  - `preflight` adds `stale_locks`, every stale lease; `stale_lock` stays (the
    first, or null) for one release.
  - `recover --issue N` recovers issue N's lease. Without `--issue` it still
    works when exactly one lease is stale; with several it exits 2 and lists
    them. A live lease is `lock-live:<run>`.
  - `recover` first steals the lease (`lock.steal_for_recovery`): under mutex
    `registry` it checks the lease is still stale, then makes it live with
    `recovering_by` set and the stale run's id kept. A second session
    recovering the same lease at once gets `lock-live` and leaves it alone.
  - On a merged run, `lock.handover` replaces the stolen lease with the
    follow-through's lease in one write. Before, `recover_stale` removed the
    lease and `cmd_recover` took a new one afterwards, so the issue had no
    lease in between and a sibling could claim it.

  4 new tests in `scripts/agentflow/tests/test_cli_flow.py` (two stale leases,
  a live lease by issue, two sessions stealing at once in two real processes,
  no moment without a lease); the suite is 343 passed (was 339).

- **agentflow: `claim` checks free disk (`scripts/agentflow/{lock,cli}.py`).**
  Step 8 of the parallel-issues design. Required free disk is now
  `min_free_gb` plus `reserve_gb_per_run` for each LIVE run (defaults 40 +
  30: 40 GB for the first claim, 70 GB for the second), measured on the
  worktrees' volume (the checkout's parent, not the checkout). `claim`
  refuses `disk-low:<free>GB<<need>GB` under mutex `registry`, before any
  lease, label or attempt; before, only `preflight` checked disk. `preflight`
  uses the same rule, fails `disk-free:<n>GB` as before, and now reports
  `disk_free_gb` and `disk_required_gb`. A stale lease reserves nothing,
  and `unblock` and the recovery follow-through are not checked. With no
  live run the floor is `min_free_gb`, as before.

  1 new test in `scripts/agentflow/tests/test_cli_flow.py`. The test fixtures
  now report 500 GB free unless a test states its own number, because the
  machine's real free space must not decide a claim test (this machine had
  31 GB free on `C:`). The suite is 344 passed (was 343).

- **agentflow: `claim --loop-max` charges the loop budget with the lease
  (`scripts/agentflow/{budget,lock,cli}.py`).** Step 9 of the parallel-issues
  design. `claim N ... --loop-max M` checks `.agent/runs/loop.json` and
  charges it in the same `registry` critical section that creates the lease,
  and only once the lease file exists. Before, the budget was a separate
  `loop-tick` call, so a claim that then failed had already spent a unit,
  and two sessions at the last unit could both pass a check made before
  either charged. Now an exhausted budget is `loop-exhausted` (no lease, no
  gh call), `issue-held` and the other refusals spend nothing, and a claim
  that rolls back gives its unit back. The budget is shared: `--max-issues`
  is a total across sessions. `loop-tick` stays one release for old prompts;
  without `--loop-max`, `claim` does not touch `loop.json`.

  4 new tests (3 in `test_cli_flow.py`, among them two real processes at the
  last unit; 1 in `test_lock.py`). The suite is 348 passed (was 344).

- **agentflow: one git writer at a time in the shared checkout, and
  `make-worktree` (`scripts/agentflow/{gitops,cli}.py`).** Step 10 of the
  parallel-issues design. The CLI's root `Git` holds mutex `git` around each
  subcommand that writes the shared `.git` (`fetch`, `checkout`, `merge`,
  `update-index`, `worktree`, `branch`, `push`, `rebase`, `revert`,
  `commit`, `add`), never around a read; `push-branch --cwd` shares it, since
  a push from a worktree updates shared refs. A waiter gives up after 600 s
  with `MutexTimeout`. `Git.ff` returned False on ANY error, so a sibling's
  `index.lock` inside `post-merge` read as "master does not fast-forward";
  it now returns False only for git's "Not possible to fast-forward" and
  raises otherwise. New fenced `make-worktree` replaces the conductor's own
  `git worktree add`: it takes the worktree and branch from this run's
  `claim.json`, fetches, and bases the branch on `origin/master` (pinned to
  its SHA, reported as `base`), because the root's `master` can lag a
  sibling's merge. `preflight` no longer fails a root `master` that is only
  BEHIND `origin/master` (it reports `master_behind_origin: true`); a
  diverged one still fails `master-differs-from-origin`.

  5 new tests (2 in `test_gitops.py`, 3 in `test_cli_flow.py`). The suite is
  353 passed (was 348).

- **agentflow: one heavy gate at a time across sessions
  (`scripts/agentflow/{cli,supervise}.py`).** Step 11 of the parallel-issues
  design. A heavy gate (`ci-steps-all`, `check-goldens`,
  `check-goldens-regen`, `cdo-gate`, or any name ending `-on-revert`) runs
  only while it holds one of `heavy_gates` (config, default 1) OS mutexes
  `.agent/mutex/gate-<k>.lock`, so a dying holder frees it and nothing goes
  stale. Light gates (`check-goldens-coverage`, `ci-wait`, anything else)
  never wait. A waiting gate retries every 15 s, beats its run's lease every
  60 s, and, under `run`, stops on HALT (`failure: halted-while-queued`) and
  on the run's wall clock. After `gate_wait_minutes` (default 180) it is
  `failure: gate-queue-timeout`, `exit_code: null`: not a verdict, and the
  child never started. The wait does not count toward the gate's own
  `--timeout`. `run` reports `queued_s`. `post-merge` waits under HALT and
  routes a queue timeout like a gate killed at its timeout (HALT only, never
  the revert); a revert re-run that never got the semaphore counts as not
  validated, so the revert is not pushed. The holder writes
  `.agent/mutex/gate-<k>.json` (run, gate, pid, since) for humans.

  7 new tests in `test_cli_flow.py` (two real processes with 1 and with 2
  heavy slots, light vs heavy names, beat and HALT while queued, a killed
  holder, and post-merge under HALT both timing out and waiting through). The
  suite is 360 passed (was 353).

- **agentflow: one merge at a time, through a merge lane
  (`scripts/agentflow/{lock,cli,mergeops,state}.py`).** Step 12 of the
  parallel-issues design. Two runs that both passed `merge-gate` on base B0
  could both merge, the second onto a base it never tested
  (`--match-head-commit` pins the head, not the base). `merge` now takes
  `.agent/merge-lane.json` (`{run_id, issue, pr, merge_sha, acquired}`) under
  mutex `registry` BEFORE its gate re-check, and refuses `merge-lane-busy`
  (another run with a live lease holds it) or `merge-lane-orphaned` (its
  holder's lease is stale; `recover` moves it on). A gate refusal or a merge
  that fails before GitHub merged gives the lane back; a merge whose commit
  could not be read keeps it. `merge` is now fenced like every other write.
  `merge-gate` reports the same two reasons, read-only. `post-merge` takes or
  keeps the lane before any git call (a free lane is taken, so a merge made
  before this change still verifies; another live holder is refused with no
  HALT and no incident) and frees it only on a clean verdict; every stop keeps
  it until `finish`, which frees it on any outcome. `recover` hands a dead
  run's lane to the follow-through with the lease (`lock.handover`), and frees
  it on `blocked-crashed`. The lane has no heartbeat: it is held while the
  lease of its issue that names its run is live. `cleanup` of a verification
  worktree is now refused only while ANOTHER run with a live lease holds the
  lane (before: any live foreign lease). `status` shows `merge_lane` with its
  state, and the heavy-gate holders' notes as `gates`.

  6 new tests in `test_cli_flow.py` (design tests 21-26, plus post-merge
  refused under a live holder and the crashed-run release); the retained
  verification-worktree cleanup test now hand-states the lane and gains an
  arm for a sibling without it. The suite is 366 passed (was 360).

- **agentflow: prompts and spec for parallel issues
  (`.claude/commands/{orchestrate,issue}.md`,
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-13-issue-orchestrator-design.md`).** Step 13
  of the parallel-issues design, for steps 5-12. `orchestrate.md`: each session
  keeps its run id in `.agent/runs/session-<id>.run-id` and never acts on
  another session's; preflight's `slots-full` / `disk-free` mean "do not claim
  now" (reschedule under `/loop`), and it prints `locks`, the disk numbers,
  `warnings` and `master_behind_origin`; `recover --issue <N>` for ONE of
  `stale_locks` per tick, skipping `lock-live`; the separate `loop-tick` step
  is folded into `claim --loop-max`, with `issue-held` (try the next pick),
  `slots-full` / `disk-low` (stop the tick) and `loop-exhausted` (end the
  loop); the budget is shared across sessions. `issue.md`: the claim check
  reads `locks`; step 1 uses `make-worktree` (from `origin/master`) instead of
  `git worktree add`; heavy gates may queue (`queued_s`, `gate-queue-timeout`
  retried once, `halted-while-queued` is `blocked halted`); a shared-ref
  `git fetch` retries once on `cannot lock ref`; `merge-gate` and `merge`'s
  `merge-lane-busy` is waited out with beats and no budget charge, and
  `merge-lane-orphaned` is `blocked`. The spec's non-goal "parallel issues"
  becomes "up to `slots`", and its Locking, Preflight, Claim, Fencing,
  recovery and cleanup text describe per-issue leases, the mutexes, the gate
  semaphore and the merge lane. The `rebase_regate` cap stays 1: raising it
  (design C11) is the owner's decision.

  The refusal codes the conductor branches on are now named constants
  (`lock.ISSUE_HELD`, `SLOTS_FULL`, `DISK_LOW`, `LOOP_EXHAUSTED`,
  `LANE_REFUSED`; `cli.QUEUE_TIMEOUT`, `HALTED_WHILE_QUEUED`).
  `test_docs_drift.py` gains 6 tests (2 parametrised over the documents): each
  document spells, as a token, the codes its steps branch on, read from those
  constants; and every `merge-lane-<x>` a document names is one the executor
  returns. The suite is 372 passed (was 366).

- d35 (`d35-commit-in-event-subscriber`) no longer says a Commit is reachable when it only could not rule one out (#148). The report asked whether `Page.RunModal` counts as a commit point. It does not, in the engine or in Business Central. The finding came from incomplete call coverage: the subscriber's callee runs a workspace page that declares no `OnOpenPage`, the analyze path records that run as `object-run-unresolved`, so the subscriber's cone is `partial` and its commit answer is UNKNOWN, not YES. d35 reported unknown in the same words as a real `Commit()`. Now:
  - The unknown case has its own title, "Commit may be reachable from event subscriber (incomplete call coverage)". Its root cause, evidence note and fix hint name the coverage reasons (for example `object-run-unresolved`), and then up to three of the cone's partly analysed routines (`; partly analysed: …`, with `, +N more` for the rest). When the reasons are missing, they say `no effect summary`, `coverage unknown` or `incomplete coverage`. The wording does not blame the callees, since the gap can be in the subscriber itself.
  - Its confidence stays `possible`, now capped by the subscriber's own uncertainties (here `cappedBy: ["unresolved-call"]`). d35 therefore declares `CORE_SUMMARIES` as well as `SUMMARIES`.
  - The id, severity (`high`) and default-on status are unchanged, so baselines and suppressions keep matching. A direct `Commit()` or a proven one still wins over unknown, and those findings are byte-identical.
  - The reporter's repro is pinned in `tests/cli/cli_d35_unknown_commit.rs` (RunModal, Commit, neither, a page with an `OnOpenPage`, and Commit plus RunModal), and the substrate-parity test gains an inline d35-unknown workspace.
  - d35's rule description (the SARIF rule text) now reads "Commit reachable, or not ruled out, from an event subscriber", which moves the rule table of the SARIF goldens. No finding in any golden moved. On CDO the d35 findings are byte-identical (11 findings, none unknown).
- A procedure written twice under `#if`/`#else` with the same signature now keeps the event facts of every arm (#103). The program build collapses such copies into one routine node, and it used to keep only the first arm's `[EventSubscriber]` attributes and publisher attributes. A subscription declared only in a later arm was lost everywhere: the call graph, events, cones, digest and detectors. The call-graph stats also classed that event's dispatch as `honestEmpty`, a false "provably no callee", so the `unknown` count could not show the problem. Now:
  - The collapsed survivor holds the union of its copies' subscriptions. The survivor's own entries come first, then each later arm's new entries in document order, with exact duplicates dropped.
  - The survivor is a publisher if any arm is one. Its `include_sender` is true if any publisher arm's is, the same possible-build reading as the subscription union, so a subscriber that takes a `Sender` still binds.
  - Only copies from ONE source file are merged. A routine node now records the file it was extracted from (`RoutineNode::source_unit`, a per-build file index, not persisted and not fingerprinted). One file can repeat a routine only under `#if`, so this covers `#if` arms inside an object, arms whose condition cannot be decided (`#if A or B`), and a whole object declared twice under a top-level `#if`/`#else`. The same routine read from another file keeps the old rule, and only the first file's event facts count, even when the two files hold opposite arms. Aliased overloads and ABI symbol-only rows are also left as they were.
  - The differential route verifier now checks every declaration with the subscriber's full routine id, not just the first one with the same name and arity. It accepts the second arm's route. It still rejects a route that only a sibling overload declares. It now also rejects a route whose id names an existing routine with a wrong signature fingerprint. It still accepts a route when the object or routine name cannot be found at all.
  - The model event graph now emits each edge once per subscriber routine id, not once per `#if` row. It used to give such a routine every edge twice. The `EventCensus` per-subscription counters now count per routine id. `unmapped_subscribers` no longer counts a row whose routine id another row mapped, so a dependency's `#if` duplicate does not read as a lost subscription.
  - A verifier test that built its subscriber id with a wrong literal `sig_fp` is fixed, and gains a twin that would catch the same mistake again.
  - No golden moved. On CDO, the `--program-call-graph-stats` output is byte-identical: no CDO routine has differing event facts across `#if` arms (measured: 28 same-signature groups, all in dependencies).
- A write that a publisher routine inherits from its event subscribers now has a witness path through the subscriber (#98). Before this fix, `digest` of the publisher procedure, and a fingerprint witness of it, showed such a write with `viaPaths: []`, `sourceKind: unavailable`, and a `first-hop-not-found` witness diagnostic. The cause: an inherited fact names its first hop by the edge's call site, or since #96 by its trigger op, and an `event-dispatch` edge has neither. The cone, `prove` and `fingerprint` all saw the write; only the witness was missing. A routine that RAISES the event already had the path, because there the event edge is the second hop.
  - The new `witness_first_hop_event_id` field is set from the first hop's event id, the same way the trigger op is set, and is written as `witnessFirstHopEventId`. Like the op, it appears on the snapshot fact, in the CBOR, in a permission row's `derivedFromCapability`, and in the projected fact, where it uses the stable event form.
  - One helper (`fact_first_hop`) now decides the first hop for all four places that need it: the first-hop match, the proof filter, the "no first hop" check and the proof early return.
  - The match uses the event id alone, so a write that several subscribers make shows one path per subscriber, up to the path cap.
  - A subscriber that cannot reach the write is not searched. The write comes from a subscriber that reaches it, so another subscriber is no witness of it, and an opaque subscriber can no longer appear as a 1-hop boundary path that hides the real one. The candidate targets of one call site are not pruned yet. The same argument applies to them, but they keep their behaviour from before #98, so an opaque candidate there is still reported as a boundary; pruning them too is a recorded follow-up.
  - The goldens moved only by the triaged shapes:
    - the new key on facts whose first hop is an event, including r3a3 and the ws-d8 and d47 snapshots;
    - new event-dispatch paths with source evidence, and the `factId`s built from them, on the publisher entries of the ws-d8 and d47 digests;
    - for the ws-d8 publisher, COMMIT and DB_INSERT ordering guarantees that the witness now makes known (the subscriber inserts, then commits).
  - Still open, recorded separately: the direct `EVENT_PUBLISH` fact on a publisher has no anchor, and an event hop's conditionality is `UNKNOWN`.
- A capped witness is now the prefix of the uncapped witness in reported order (#97). The ordinary witness search used to stop as soon as it had `cap` paths, in discovery order, which follows call-site order; the final sort orders by hop count, then by the hop JSON. So with cap 1 it could keep a path the full sort places second. Now, as the proofs already did (#69), it records the hop count at which it reaches the cap, finishes every path of that length, and lets the sort choose. After the cut no node is expanded, so the extra work is bounded by the nodes already queued at the cut, and pops after the cut are not counted toward the state limit, so finishing the length class cannot turn a witness `incomplete`. The prefix holds when neither the capped nor the uncapped search is `incomplete`. An opaque-boundary diagnostic found after the cut is reported only when its path is kept. `truncated` (and `path-limit-reached`) is now set when the search left a queued node or dropped a possible longer path. So exactly `cap` paths no longer read as truncated when every branch still queued at the cut dead-ends before the cut's hop count, for example when a terminal path sets the cut and a sibling only calls back to an ancestor. This does not hold for every cut: when opaque seeds set the cut at 1 hop, nodes queued deeper than 1 hop still make the witness truncated. The flag stays conservative: an unexpanded node counts as a dropped path when it has an out-edge (at or beyond the cut's depth) or an edge that passes the expansion filters (below it), even when that edge leads nowhere.
- Writes and other effects of implicit table and field triggers now reach their callers in the capability cone, the snapshot, digest, prove and fingerprint (#96). Before, `prove ValidateIt "writes-table:Log Row"` answered **no** for a routine whose `Validate` fires an `OnValidate` that inserts into Log Row, and digest showed no effect for it, although L4's `query effects` already listed the write. The typed edge graph skipped implicit-trigger edges, a byte-parity leftover from al-sem with no stated reason. What changed:
  - **The typed graph** now carries `{kind: "implicit-trigger", operationId, triggerKind, fires}`. `fires` is `always` for Validate/Rename and literal-true RunTrigger, and `maybe` otherwise, including ModifyAll/DeleteAll.
  - **The cone** keys trigger edges and PD links by the firing record operation.
  - **The snapshot** has an `ImplicitTrigger` edge.
  - **Digest** gives the trigger hop its op anchor and makes it conditional from the op's control context and `fires`.
  - **A table or table-extension trigger's `Rec`** now takes the caller's record temp state: it is parameter-dependent on the receiver, bound from the firing operation in L4 and in the cone. So a trigger fired on a temporary record no longer counts as a physical write; before, L4 already reported it as one.
  - **The model** no longer drops the program engine's `ModifyAll`/`DeleteAll` → `OnModify`/`OnDelete` edges.
  - **The caller's guard** on the record operation that fires a trigger now applies to the trigger's facts in the cone, as a guard on a call site does: after `if not Skip then T.Validate(...)`, a caller passing `Skip = true` no longer inherits the trigger's writes. The trigger's own parameter guards are still dropped.
  - **d1** binds a trigger's `Rec` the same way, in its production search as well as in its path resolver, so a loop that reaches a trigger body through a real record is a physical finding, not "(temp state uncertain)".
  - **Digest's ordering** keeps the trigger hop in an effect's call chain, keyed by the firing operation, with that operation's order and `unordered-broadcast` sequencing. Before, the hop was dropped, so a trigger's effect looked root-local and its order inside the trigger was compared with orders in the root: `Noop(); DoCommit(); T.Validate(...)` with an HTTP call in `OnValidate` got a false `EXTERNAL_IO_BEFORE_COMMIT`. The occurrence key of a trigger-first effect now names the firing operation too. A path through a trigger is a `May` edge with its own reason `implicit-trigger-may`, so `EXTERNAL_IO_IN_EVENT_SUBSCRIBER_TXN` still needs a real event on the path.

  CDO's `--program-call-graph-stats` is unchanged. The goldens moved only by the predicted shapes, triaged line by line: r1a, ir-l2, r3a1, r3a2 and r3a3; the r3a1/r3a3 manifest matrices; the synthetic l4 collision fixture, rewritten to the real trigger shape. A trigger-first inherited fact now carries `witnessFirstHopOperationId`, in the JSON and the CBOR snapshot alike, and so does the `derivedFromCapability` of a permission row derived from one.

  **Cost on CDO** (`release-fast`, cross-app, mean of 2 runs on the final code): `alsem analyze` wall time roughly doubles (24.5 → 49.8 s at `--scope all`, 23.0 → 47.0 s at `--scope primary`); a digest goes 32.3 → 80.2 s; fingerprint is unchanged (5.5 → 5.8 s, noise); peak memory is flat (about 2.84 GB). The cause is that the cone now follows Base Application trigger hubs (Gen. Journal Line `OnInsert` → approvals → workflow → posting), which grows the largest SCC from 126 to 479 routines. Every such path is a real may-execute path. d43 findings at `--scope all` grow from 841 to 4573 (real trigger paths, mostly from one Base Application site), and fall from 23 to 5 at `--scope primary`.

- `alsem analyze --format sarif` now describes every detector in `tool.driver.rules`
  (#87). The list was written by hand and held only 21 of the 54 detectors, so a finding
  from any of the other 33 (for example `d19-unused-parameter` or `d34-commit-in-loop`)
  named a rule the document did not describe, and SARIF viewers showed it without a name
  or description. Each detector's rule name and one-line description now live in the
  detector registry, and the SARIF list is built from it, so a new detector cannot be
  left out. The 21 existing rules keep their names and descriptions. The README's
  detector counts are corrected to 40 default and 14 opt-in.
- `alsem fingerprint`, `prove`, `digest`, `events fanout`, `events chains`, `policy check`
  and `diff --strict` (in the lines it prints when its gate fails) now report the dependency
  warnings `alsem analyze` reports (#91): a dependency that is missing, older than
  declared, or unreadable, and a package whose manifest cannot be read. That includes the
  implicit `System` and `System Application` dependencies when their packages are absent.
  Before, only `analyze` showed them, so the other commands gave a
  smaller diagnostics list for the same workspace. They appear in each command's usual place
  (the JSON envelope's `diagnostics`, or `warning: …` lines on stderr), after the workspace
  diagnostics. All commands that build a model now build their diagnostics through one shared
  function, so `analyze`'s output is unchanged. `analyze`'s empty-output path (no model is
  built) still reports only the workspace diagnostics, as before.
- `alsem diff --strict` now does what its help says in workspace mode: when either workspace
  side has an error-severity analyzer diagnostic, it prints both sides' diagnostics to stderr
  (`<severity>: <message>`, old side first; one list when both arguments are the same
  workspace), writes nothing to stdout or `--out`, and exits 1 (#89). Before, `--strict` was
  ignored and the run exited 0. The check runs before the `--renames` overlay is read. A run
  with no error is unchanged, warnings included (they are still not printed). `diff` does not
  read the diagnostics a snapshot file's envelope carries, so `--strict` stays a no-op for a
  snapshot-file side.
- `alsem graph` now rejects an `app.json` without a non-empty string `id` (exit 1,
  `could not compute modelInstanceId`), as every gate-backed command does for that case; before,
  it exported the graph with an empty app id and exited 0 (#73). A missing or unparseable
  `app.json` keeps graph's own error (`snapshot build failed: read|parse …`), which still differs
  from the gate commands' `could not compute modelInstanceId`. The id is checked after the
  program build, so on a large workspace the rejection comes after the build. The LSP and
  `aldump` are unchanged.
- `alsem digest --file` and `--diff` now match a workspace-relative file spelled with `./`,
  `.` segments, a doubled `/` or `\` (#76). Before, `./src/x.al`, `src/./x.al` and
  `src//x.al` gave `file-unmatched` (exit 2), and a diff whose headers name the file
  `./src/x.al` (e.g. `a/./src/x.al`, or `diff -u --label ./src/x.al`) matched nothing,
  because the path comparison only stripped the scheme, turned `\` into `/` and lowercased.
  A trailing `/` is ignored too (`src/x.al/` matches). Plain `diff -u` headers that carry a
  tab and a timestamp are still not parsed: the timestamp stays in the path (a separate,
  pre-existing parser limit). `normalize_input`, the one
  function every digest path comparison goes through (`--file`, diff paths and the set of
  files a malformed hunk header vetoes), now also drops every `.` segment and every empty
  segment except a leading root `/` or UNC `//`. It stays purely lexical. Limits: a rooted
  path (`/src/x.al`) and a `..` segment (`src/../src/x.al`) still do not match, on purpose,
  since `..` after a symlink need not name the parent. The pre-existing `\` -> `/` mapping
  now also drops `.` and empty segments, so on POSIX a file whose name contains a literal
  `\` (e.g. `src\.\x.al`) keys like `src/x.al`; such names are outside this guarantee.
  Diagnostics still echo the spelling the user gave. No golden moved.
- `workspaceFingerprint` now covers the whole dependency closure the loader reads (#70):
  every `.app` in the workspace's own and each ancestor `.alpackages` up to the `.git`
  boundary, from the same discovery the loader and the closure digest use. Before, it
  hashed only `<ws>/.alpackages`, so swapping a package in an ancestor cache did not change
  it. An unreadable package or cache is a `dep-package-unreadable` input keyed by its
  relative path and hashed by its failure category, so a readable package beside it is
  still seen and the value does not depend on where the tree lives. Fingerprints without
  an ancestor cache are unchanged (no golden moved). When two names in one cache reach the
  same package (symlinks), discovery keeps the first name in sort order, not in directory
  listing order, so the key is stable. The closure digest's error names the OS reason
  again, and a cache folder that is not an ancestor's `.alpackages` is an explicit
  `outside-walk` error instead of being keyed as the workspace's own cache.
- A workspace that is itself a repository root (its own folder has `.git`, as a directory
  or a worktree file) no longer reads `.alpackages` caches above it (#70). The loader
  ascended from the parent without checking the workspace's own `.git`.
- A dependency event publisher with subscribers now reaches the cross-app L4 store (#70).
  It was a fixed solver leaf, so its subscribers' writes were missing from `query effects`
  and digest's `tempState` while digest's cone kept them. It is now solved for its effect
  rows, but keeps a dependency leaf's parameter roles (`fixed_roles`), because role
  composition does not walk subscriber dispatches: the five path-sensitive role fields
  (`requiresLoadedAtEntry`, `requiredLoadedFieldsAtEntry`, `mutatesBeforeLoad`,
  `dirtyAtExit`, `currentLoadedFieldsAtExit`) stay unknown, and the body-local ones
  (`persistsCurrentRecord`, `writesFields`, `validatesParam`, …) come from the publisher's
  own body, exactly as for every dependency leaf today. Callers composing through it see
  the same roles as before.
- The lowerer no longer drops an attribute that is separated from its procedure or trigger
  by a comment, a pragma or an `#if` line (#80). Before, any node between `[EventSubscriber(…)]`
  and `local procedure Handler()` (a `// note` line, a `/* … */` block, `#pragma`, `#region`,
  `#define`) cleared the pending attributes, so the subscriber never bound and its effects
  (a `Commit()` in the handler, for example) vanished from every caller of the event. Now:
  - the grammar's extras (comment, block comment, `#pragma`, `#region`/`#endregion`,
    `#define`/`#undef`) never end an attribute run;
  - an `#if` that wraps only attributes gives the routine the attributes of every live arm, and
    an attribute written before an `#if` that wraps the routine reaches each arm's routine. Each
    pending attribute carries the symbols of its build path (its guard). It enters an arm only
    when that arm is live and consistent with the guard, and falls through only when some build
    takes no arm. So `[A] #if X P #endif #if X R #endif Q` gives `A` to `P` and `Q`, never to `R`;
  - a carried attribute's own `#if` argument groups are read under its guard, so
    `#if not X [EventSubscriber(…, #if X 'OnA' #else 'OnB' #endif …)] #endif H` subscribes `H`
    to `OnB` only;
  - one positional list (attribute arguments, key fields) is read with one running context: a
    nested `#if` group and later sibling groups see the literals of the arms already chosen,
    and a self-contradictory arm is never chosen. A choice under a compound condition such as
    `X or Y` records no literal, so it does not constrain later groups;
  - guards are projected onto the symbols that later conditions read, so the number of
    pending paths stays bounded. An attribute that still reaches its routine by more than 64
    distinct `#if` paths in one list is not attached, and a `SyntaxIssue` names it.
  Stated limits: an attribute that reaches one procedure through different `#if` builds is
  attached unconditionally (union-read, as for every undecided `#if`); a procedure written
  twice under `#if`/`#else` with the SAME signature still keeps only the first copy's
  subscriptions (a separate issue); an attribute followed by a `var` section, field, key or
  dataitem is still dropped, as before. Tests: 31 lowerer tests (A1-A11 and
  A13-A23, 22 in all, as A12 is the cli test; plus `fall_through_is_dead_when_an_arm_is_decided_true`
  (A7b), the renamed `attribute_separated_by_comment_is_attached`,
  `projection_sees_spaced_and_upper_case_directives`,
  `guarded_attribute_skips_an_unreachable_split_header_arm`,
  `attribute_arg_group_issue_is_reported_once`, `consistent_rejects_a_contradictory_first_operand`,
  `contradictory_context_in_node_attribute_attaches_nothing`,
  `sibling_groups_under_a_disjunction_are_not_correlated` and
  `attribute_flow_scales_linearly`, which pins that the attribute flow stays linear: each
  pending attribute reads a wrapper's directives, not all its children, and guard joins
  are hashed) and the end-to-end
  `tests/cli/cli_attribute_trivia.rs` (`alsem digest` sees `COMMIT` through every separator
  kind). #71's two "#80 limit" tests now assert the attribute is claimed: a comment-separated
  attribute starts its routine's declaration span. CDO (`U:/Git/DO-cdo-baseline/Cloud`), before → after: `primaryScoped` byte-identical,
  `--dependency-bodies-stats` byte-identical, and `alsem analyze` findings byte-identical at
  `--scope primary` (2293) and `--scope all` (26954). `wholeProgram` total 46317 → 46328,
  `honestEmpty` 28249 → 28258, `resolvedSource` 11566 → 11568, `unknown` 0 → 0. Every moved edge
  is traced in a `--graphify-export` diff. 11 dependency procedures regain `[IntegrationEvent]`
  (Base Application 4, Continia Delivery Network 5, System Application 2), each adding one
  event-flow edge, and 4 regain `[EventSubscriber]`. Two of those subscribers give a
  previously-empty publisher its first subscriber (System `OnCompanyOpen` →
  `System Initialization Impl.Init`, and the `OpenRoleBasedSetupExperience` event →
  `Guided Experience Impl.OpenRoleBasedSetupExperience`), which moves 2 edges from `honestEmpty` to
  `resolvedSource`.
- `alsem digest --diff`: a hunk header that is not a valid `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` line (e.g.
  `@@ garbage @@`, `@@ -8,3 @@`, a combined-diff `@@@` header) was silently ignored, so the
  file looked hunkless and EVERY declaration in it became a changed root, with no
  diagnostic and exit 0. It is now a `diff-parse-error` with a new `file` key naming the
  file, and that file gives no diff-derived roots in any of its records (matched by the
  normalized path; `--file`/`--routine` roots are kept). In a `diff --git` section (and a
  merge's `diff --cc`/`diff --combined` section, now also a section boundary) the lines after
  the bad header, up to the next section header, are skipped: the rejected hunk's body has
  no trustworthy length. A digest with such an error is incomplete for that file; a diff
  whose only file is broken gives no roots and exits 2. An `@@` line before the first file
  section (a patch preamble) is still ignored. Pinned by
  `malformed_hunk_header_gives_parse_error_and_no_roots` and eleven sibling tests in
  `tests/cli/cli_digest_changed_spans.rs`, and `malformed_hunk_header_is_an_error_of_its_file`
  / `git_header_dest_names` / `combined_diff_headers_are_section_boundaries` in
  `diff_parser` (#72).
- `alsem digest --diff`: a git-quoted non-ASCII path (git's default, e.g.
  `"b/src/\303\251.al"` for `src/é.al`) decoded each octal escape as its own character
  (`src/Ã©.al`), so a healthy diff of the file gave `diff-file-unmatched`, no roots and exit
  2. A quoted path is now decoded as git's C quoting: escapes are UTF-8 bytes (`\a \b \f \v`
  added), and a non-UTF-8 name degrades to U+FFFD. An escape git never writes (a `8`/`9`
  digit, or a value above `\377`) is kept as text; it used to be dropped. Pinned by
  `unquote_path_octal_escapes_are_utf8_bytes` and
  `escaped_and_literal_spellings_of_one_file_share_the_veto` (#72).
- `Validate`, `Copy` and `TransferFields` are no longer reported as database writes, on
  temporary and real records alike (#69). They copy or assign values in memory and never
  write the record's own table. The `OnValidate` trigger's own writes are not inherited by
  the caller in the capability cone (the typed graph has no implicit-trigger edges, a
  stated non-goal), so a caller of `Validate` now shows no write for that statement; L4
  still follows the trigger.
  Everything that reads the capability `modify` fact (digest/prove, fingerprints, diff, policy,
  the d43/d44/d45 write sets) inherits this. Goldens moved: 9 `tests/r1a-goldens/` and 9
  `tests/r3a3-goldens/` fixtures plus the R3a-3 manifest matrix (`modify` 134 -> 109).
- The capability cone resolves a parameter-dependent write in every routine's own frame
  through a transitive per-producer solve (`l4::pd_solve`, #69 D1). A write a caller makes
  temporary is graded known(true), a real record known(false), across recursion, cycles and
  root SCCs too; guards on these writes now hold on every typed edge.
  Producers no longer share a cone key with ordinary facts. Before, the cone resolved such a
  write only for a non-recursive singleton caller, and only to known(true): a real-record
  caller kept the callee's `parameter-dependent(0)`, and a recursive or root caller kept the
  write physical. Pinned by `a1c_cone_values_are_frame_correct`, the cone/L4 class-parity
  oracle `a5_cone_l4_class_parity_reduced` (every `tests/r0-corpus` fixture and the #69
  probe) and the `pd_solve` unit tests. Goldens moved: 6 `tests/r3a3-goldens/` fixtures and
  the `ws-d1-multi-caller` cli-b snapshot/fingerprint goldens, every line a real-record
  caller's inherited write going from `parameter-dependent(0)` to known(false) (same nt
  class, so no detector or digest output moved). The gap test that pinned the old limit
  (`recursive_callee_write_through_var_param_stays_physical`) now asserts the opposite
  (`…_forwarded_var_param_is_temporary`).
- Digest witnesses for writes a call site makes temporary keep their evidence,
  conditionality and every via-path through the fact's first hop (#69 D3): the paths come
  from the root's own solve states (proofs), and the BFS and fingerprint share one carrier
  predicate (`is_bfs_carrier`: ordinary direct facts only, same temp class). Before, such a
  write had `evidence: unavailable`, no viaPaths and `ORDERING_UNKNOWN`. A path's identity
  is its edges plus its terminal, so two writes reached through the same calls stay two
  paths. Only distinct proofs count toward the path cap, and a capped proof set is a prefix
  of the uncapped one in the global order. Ordinary BFS paths are still capped in discovery
  order, as before #69, so a capped whole witness need not be a prefix. A routine id
  declared twice (two `#if` arms) is one producer, not two. `alsem fingerprint` takes the
  same proofs.
- `viaPaths` are deduplicated by projected path on an effect's first fact too, not only on
  a merge; equal projected paths keep the least restrictive conditionality (#69 D3).
- A kt and an nt DB effect never share an occurrence id: a kt DB effect's canonical key
  ends in `|kt`, and the class is part of the effect's dedupe key (#69 D3). Golden moved:
  `tests/cli-b-goldens/digest/ws-txn-d47-neg-temp.json`, one `factId` of a temporary
  record's direct insert. Pinned by `a2a_temp_call_site_keeps_its_witness`,
  `a2d_all_paths_and_conditionality_kept`, `a2f_degraded_witnesses_never_share_an_occurrence`,
  `a2g_incompleteness_reaches_consumers` and three `digest::tests` unit tests.
- The ordering engine's physical-write filter now grades a write the way `detail.tempState`
  reports it (#69): a write that is temporary in the reporting routine's frame (through
  recursion, cycles, a guard or a call-site buffer) no longer raises `WRITE_PENDING_AT_UI`,
  and a routine reaching one write with a temporary and a real record gets one effect per
  class. Pinned by `a1a_ordering_filter_agrees_with_temp_state`,
  `a2c_depth_two_proof_real_call_first` and `a2e_recursion_cycles_mixes_guards`.
- `alsem digest --diff` reads each hunk body line by line and stops when the header's old
  and new line counts are used up. Header tests (`--- `, `+++ `, `diff --git`, `rename`) no
  longer apply inside a body, so a deleted line `--- x` or an added line `+++ y` is a change,
  not a new file. An empty line counts as context, `\ No newline at end of file` is not
  counted, and a pure deletion's cursor follows git's `new_start + 1` rule. A hunk that ends
  before its counts are used up (end of input, or a line its body cannot accept) is now
  reported as `diff-parse-error` ("hunk at +N truncated"), which no input could produce
  before; the line that ended it is then read as a normal top-level line. Pinned by the
  `diff_parser` unit tests (`hunk_changes_follow_the_body`,
  `pure_deletion_cursor_starts_after_new_start`,
  `truncated_hunk_is_an_error_with_or_without_final_newline`,
  `header_looking_lines_inside_a_body_are_body`,
  `the_line_ending_a_truncated_hunk_is_redispatched`, `minus_line_past_old_count_ends_the_hunk`,
  `exact_fill_completes_the_hunk`, `no_newline_marker_is_not_counted`,
  `omitted_counts_bound_the_body`) and in `cli_digest_changed_spans.rs` by
  `hunk_body_is_count_bounded`, `bare_header_pair_inside_short_hunk_is_body`,
  `minus_line_past_old_count_ends_the_hunk` and `bare_header_pair_exact_fill_is_complete`
  (#71). The header counts are authoritative, as in `git apply` and GNU `patch`. **Limit:**
  plain `diff -u` outputs concatenated with no `diff --git` line, after a malformed hunk whose
  header promises more lines than its body holds, have the next file's `---`/`+++` pair read
  as body lines while counts remain. When the counts happen to be filled exactly, the next
  file's hunks attach to the previous file and no error is reported
  (`bare_header_pair_exact_fill_is_complete`); otherwise a `diff-parse-error` is reported.
  `git apply --numstat` reads that exact-fill input the same way (one file, 2 added, 3
  deleted), and GNU patch 2.7.6 also reads both hunks as hunks of the first file (#71).
- `alsem digest --diff`: a `+++ ` line opens a file only right after a `--- ` header. A `+`
  line that overran a hunk's new count, re-read at top level, replaced the current file and
  silently dropped its hunks (the changes already read were lost). Pinned by
  `plus_header_without_a_pending_minus_header_keeps_the_current_file` and
  `orphan_plus_header_keeps_the_current_file` (#71).
- `alsem digest --diff`: a hunk header whose line range does not fit in a 32-bit line number
  (e.g. `@@ -1,1 +2147483647,0 @@`) overflowed the body cursor, a panic in debug builds. It is
  now a `diff-parse-error` ("hunk at +N has an invalid line range") and opens no hunk. (#72
  then made it an error of its file: that file gives no roots.) A number too large
  for 32 bits, which made the whole header line silently ignored, gets the same error. Pinned by
  `out_of_range_hunk_header_is_an_error_not_a_panic` and
  `out_of_range_hunk_header_is_a_parse_error` (#71).
- `alsem digest --file dep:<guid>:<path>` selected the dependency file's routines as changed
  roots, because path matching lowercased the `dep:` key on both sides. Only workspace
  routines are selected now; the call gives `file-unmatched`, exit 2. Pinned by
  `dependency_routines_never_become_changed_roots`, in default and `--single-app` mode (#71).
- `alsem digest`, `prove`, `fingerprint`, `events` and `policy check` ran 14 detectors
  (13 of `analyze`'s default set plus opt-in d8), because 20 of the 34 names in a list
  copied at port time matched no registered detector. The 20 were invented names on real
  detector numbers (e.g. `d16-blob-in-loop` for registered `d16-obsolete-routine-call`):
  18 of those numbers are registered DEFAULT detectors, 2 (d17, d45) are OPT-IN. The five
  commands now run `analyze`'s default detector set (40) from the registry, each in its
  existing model mode (digest cross-app by default, `--single-app` single-app; the others
  single-app). Diagnostics output is unchanged on every golden (zero bytes moved in all 8
  `scripts/check-goldens` targets), and the output of the five commands (six invocations:
  events has fanout and chains) on CDO is byte-identical
  before and after. Cost on CDO (`U:/Git/DO-cdo-baseline/Cloud`, release-fast, 2 runs each,
  wall time / peak working set, before → after): digest (cross-app) 31.3 / 24.8 s → 28.3 /
  25.0 s, 2836 / 2828 → 2830 / 2831 MB; prove 7.9 / 7.7 → 8.0 / 7.9 s, ~2070 MB both;
  fingerprint 7.3 / 7.3 → 7.5 / 6.9 s, ~1360 MB both; events fanout 4.7 / 4.6 → 4.4 / 5.3 s,
  events chains 4.3 / 4.8 → 4.4 / 5.5 s, policy check 4.5 / 4.4 → 4.6 / 4.6 s, all ~575 MB.
  Paired time deltas (after − before, run 1 / run 2): digest −3.0 / +0.2 s, prove +0.1 / +0.2 s,
  fingerprint +0.2 / −0.4 s, events fanout −0.3 / +0.7 s, events chains +0.1 / +0.7 s, policy
  check +0.1 / +0.2 s. Two runs per side are too few to call any of these a regression or a gain
  (digest's own before-runs differed by 6.5 s), so the time result is inconclusive. Peak memory
  moved by 6 MB or less (#68).

## [1.7.1] - 2026-10-14

### Added

- **Releases carry standalone `alsem` binaries**: `alsem-windows-x64.exe`
  (Authenticode-signed with `al-call-hierarchy.exe`) and `alsem-linux-x64`
  (glibc 2.34 floor), both built with `--no-default-features`, so without
  telemetry. Tools that fetch al-sem themselves (bc-dev-mcp) can pin a release
  and its asset digest instead of depending on the plugin's copy.

## [1.7.0] - 2026-10-14

### Added

- **`alsem digest` and `alsem prove` say whether a DB_* effect writes a
  temporary record** (#65). Every DB_INSERT/DB_MODIFY/DB_DELETE effect now
  carries `detail.tempState`, with the same values as `alsem query effects`
  (`known(true)`, `known(false)`, `parameter-dependent(i)`, `unknown`). A
  temp-only write is `known(true)`, so bc-dev-mcp can drop it from test-order
  polluters and "writes <table>" risk.
  - **One source of truth.** The value comes from the L4 db-effect store that
    `query effects` reads, built by the same function (the new
    `effect_query_cli::build_db_effect_bundle`, which `QuerySubstrate` now
    calls too) and rendered by the same `temp_state_str`. It is joined to the
    digest effect by the root routine and the operation that each merged fact
    started from. The digest's own cone `temp_state` (which the ordering engine
    still reads) is NOT used: it keeps a helper's `parameter-dependent(0)` in a
    caller that has no parameters, both when the caller passes a real record and
    across a recursive call cycle.
  - **Several values** on one effect (one effect merged from facts with
    different temp states) are sorted, distinct and joined with `,`. Test
    `== "known(true)"` for temp-only; do not parse it as one enum value.
  - **Absent** when the L4 store has no row for any one of the operations the
    effect was merged from. Today that is a DB_MODIFY from
    `Validate`/`Copy`/`TransferFields`, which L4 does not count as a database
    touch. Absence is never turned into `unknown`.
  - Pinned by `tests/cli/cli_digest_temp_state.rs`, which drives
    `run_digest_pipeline` on a hand-written workspace and checks every value
    against `query effects` for the same routine. Discrimination: joining on
    the evidence operation (ViaHelperTemp lost its value), rendering the cone
    `temp_state` (ViaRecursionTemp became `parameter-dependent(0)`), dropping
    the field (TempOnly lost it) and inventing `unknown` for a missing row
    (ValidateTemp) each failed the test; each revert passed.

### Changed

- **Digest `schemaVersion` 1.3.0 -> 1.4.0 and prove 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0** (#65), for
  the additive `detail.tempState`. Prove moves too because its witnesses use the
  same effect shape. Goldens moved: every `tests/cli-b-goldens/digest/*.json`
  and `tests/cli-b-goldens/prove/*.json`, plus the digest `.human.txt` files with
  DB_* effects. Only the version and the new field changed; factIds, canonical
  keys and every other golden family are byte-identical.
  #66 bumps digest to 1.4.0 as well; one bump covers both additive fields.
- `alsem digest` and `alsem prove` now run a second L4 summary solve, the
  same assembly `query effects` uses in the same mode: `build_db_effect_bundle`
  single-app, `cross_app_db_effect_bundle` cross-app (#66). Digest's detector
  context already solves one (`ctx.db_effect_bundle`), but it is not built the
  way `query effects` builds its own, so the two are not guaranteed to be
  equal. Measured cost on CDO (single-app, before #66): about 0.1 s warm.
  `cli_digest_temp_state` checks digest against `query effects` in both
  modes. LIMIT: its workspace has no dependency, so it cannot tell the two
  stores apart.
- **`alsem digest` and `alsem query touches|effects` load the workspace's
  dependencies by default** (#66), the same way `alsem analyze` (cross-app since
  S8) and `alsem graph` do. They build analyze's own cross-app base
  (`capability_cone::build_cross_app_base`): one `FULL` program build, the
  workspace plus the dependency code it reaches, with calls cut to workspace
  callers and each source-bearing dependency routine a fixed leaf. A new
  `--single-app` flag on all three keeps the old workspace-only model. Cross-app
  is the default for three reasons: the issue's consumer (bc-dev-mcp) needs
  dependency tables in the default output; an opt-in flag would leave the default
  silently wrong on every BC workspace; and analyze, graph, digest and query then
  share one mental model. Cross-app digest also runs the envelope diagnostics'
  detectors with the cross-app runner (`run_detectors_cross_app`), the
  combination analyze runs, never the single-app runner over a cross-app model.
- **Every digest and query document states which apps were loaded and how**:
  `payload.dependencies` = `{mode: "crossApp" | "singleApp", apps: [...]}`. The
  `apps` rows are exactly `alsem graph`'s `meta.apps` rows (`appId`, `name`,
  `publisher`, `version`, `source`: `symbolOnly`/`embedded`/…/`missing`), from
  one producer, `program::resolve::full::loaded_apps`, which graph now calls too
  (its golden did not move). `--single-app` states `apps: []`. Human output
  gains one first line, `dependencies: <name> (<source>), …`, only when an app
  was loaded, so a workspace with no dependency reads the same in both modes.
  Additive schema bumps: digest `schemaVersion` 1.3.0 -> 1.4.0, query 1.0.0 ->
  1.1.0. Every digest and query JSON golden moved by exactly the new
  `dependencies` block and the version line; no `.human.txt` golden moved.
- Routine selectors stay on the workspace app. A cross-app model also holds
  dependency routines, so `digest --routine`, `query --from` and
  `query effects --routine` match only the primary app's routines
  (`selector_index::build_selector_indexes` takes the primary guid;
  `effect_query_cli::resolve_routine_selector` filters), and `query touches`
  without `--from` lists workspace routines only. A dependency routine still
  appears as an effect's origin (anchored at `dep:<guid>:<path>`).
- `alsem digest` computes per-root effects for the changed roots only, not every
  reportable root then filtered. Each root's pass is independent, so no output
  changes (the goldens pin it byte for byte); it removes most of digest's former
  peak on a large workspace.

### Fixed

- **A dependency table now resolves in `digest` and `query`** (#66). A write to
  Base Application's `Customer` (table 18) had no `resourceId` and no
  `resourceDisplay` in `alsem digest`, and `alsem query touches --table 18` was
  `unmatched`, because both built the single-app model, which projects the
  workspace's files only. It now resolves to `<appId>/table/18` named
  `Customer`.
- **`query touches --table <number>` matches a table by number.** It accepted
  only an internal id or a name, so `--table 50160` was `unmatched` even for a
  workspace table. The number and the case-insensitive name are now one tier:
  two distinct matches (two apps with table 18, or a table literally named "18")
  are reported as ambiguous with every candidate, never narrowed silently. A
  `tableextension` stub's number is not a table number and never matches.

Cost, measured 2026-10-13 on the pinned CDO baseline (`U:/Git/DO-cdo-baseline/Cloud`,
`release-fast`, warm, best of 3, peak working set; before = master `c057313c`):

| Command | Before | After (default, cross-app) | After `--single-app` |
|---------|-------:|---------------------------:|---------------------:|
| `digest --file CDOIssueDocument.Codeunit.al` | 8.4 s, 2112 MB | 27.1 s, 2828 MB | 6.6 s, 576 MB |
| `query touches --table Customer` | 4.1 s, 577 MB (unmatched) | 17.2 s, 2830 MB (resolved) | 4.2 s, 575 MB |

The cross-app time is the shared base `alsem analyze` already pays (18.5 s of
the digest run: program build 3.1 s, dependency bodies 3.0 s, model assembly
2.4 s, adapter 6.8 s), the snapshot over it (3.5 s) and, for digest, the
cross-app detector context behind the envelope diagnostics (4.7 s, 3.9 s of it
capability cones). The peak is the base's, the same as analyze's. Digest's own
per-root pass fell from 1.47 s to 0.04 s (changed roots only), which is why
`--single-app` digest is faster than before. A faster shared base speeds up
analyze, graph, digest and query together; that is the lever, not a lighter
second cross-app path.

The 3.4x default for `digest` is a deliberate cost, not an oversight. Use
`--single-app` only when the caller needs workspace tables alone; it is then
faster than before. bc-dev-mcp's three uses named in #66 (test-order polluter
prediction, the record-write watch's static writer set, risk ranking) all join
on dependency tables such as Customer, so none of them can switch to
`--single-app` without losing this fix. Their speed-up has to come from the
shared base (its adapter step, 6.8 s, is the largest part).

## [1.6.1] - 2026-10-13

### Fixed

- **Two calls on one line are two sites, and a swap between call sites can no
  longer pass the goldens unseen** (#28). The issue was written against the
  L3-minted CDO goldens, which S9.0d deleted; the defect class lived on in two
  places, and both are closed as far as their oracle allows.
  - **The per-site fixture golden** (`semantic_golden.rs`, used by
    `implicit-trigger-fixture.json`). `GoldenSiteKey` had no column, so two calls
    on one line shared a key, and both mint and comparison merged their targets
    by union: a swap of their targets read as a match. The key is now the site's
    whole span (start and end, line and byte column). The end separates chained
    same-name calls (`X.Foo().Foo()`), which share a start. `callee_fp` is gone
    from the key: it was a `DefaultHasher` value in a committed file, which Rust
    does not keep stable across releases. Mint (`build_golden_from_canonical`)
    and comparison (`assert_against_semantic_golden`) now panic on two edges
    with one key, and `SemanticGolden::validate` refuses a golden that lists a
    site twice. The old column-free reason (L3 counted UTF-16 columns) no
    longer applies: both sides are the fresh resolver. On CDO the span key is
    unique over all 46,317 resolved edges, where 1,703 (caller, line) groups
    hold more than one site. Golden moved: `implicit-trigger-fixture.json`
    (each of its 3 sites gains `col`/`end_line`/`end_col` and loses `callee_fp`;
    targets unchanged).
    The issue's own discrimination proof runs through the real resolver: a new
    fixture, `tests/fixtures/same-line-calls`, puts
    `Codeunit.Run(Codeunit::SLCFirst); Codeunit.Run(Codeunit::SLCSecond);` on
    one line of one caller (one callee text, so one `callee_fp`), with a new
    golden, `same-line-calls-fixture.json` (2 sites). `same_line_calls_swap_is_caught`
    swaps the two fresh targets and requires both sites to come out wrong.
    With the old (line, `callee_fp`) key and union put back, the golden minted
    as 1 site holding both targets and the swap read as 1 paired, 1 match,
    0 wrong; with the span key it reads as 2 wrong.
  - **The CDO compiler audit** (`compiler_golden.rs`). It compared (caller,
    class, target) pairs only, so a resolver that swapped the targets of two
    calls in one routine produced the same pairs and passed. It now also
    compares each agreeing pair's first line with the compiler's (where the
    compiler records one; its `Interface` and `Event` edges carry none). A
    mismatch is a new `Side::FirstLineDiffers` disagreement that a verdict must
    explain. One rule explains it: `RunTriggerFalse`, when the compiler's first
    line is a RunTrigger-false record operation that excluded that trigger and
    the program's first line is later. CDO has exactly 2, both that shape
    (`CDOMailManagement` `Insert()` 180 vs `Insert(true)` 208,
    `CDOEMailTemplateManagement` 1530 vs 1564), now pinned. Loading a golden,
    or auditing one, that lists the same pair twice now panics instead of
    reading it last-wins (pinned at the file boundary by
    `loading_a_golden_file_that_lists_one_pair_twice_is_refused`). No golden
    moved: the stored lines were already there.
  - Comments that still described the deleted `match_sites` matcher and the
    deleted L3-era gates (`cdo_genuine_wrong_is_precedence_adjudicated`,
    `cdo_l3_semantic_audit_no_fresh_wrong`) now say what exists instead
    (`differential.rs`, `tests/program_resolve_harness.rs`,
    `docs/2026-10-04-b3-code-map.md`).
  - **Limit, stated openly.** The compiler graph has no column and keeps only
    the first edge of each (caller, callee) pair. A swap between two calls on
    ONE line, or among later calls to a callee called earlier, leaves the
    compiler's pairs and first lines unchanged, so no check against this oracle
    can see it. CDO has 269 (caller, class, line) groups where more than one
    target first appears on one line (249 with 2 targets, 19 with 3, 1 with 6).

## [1.6.0] - 2026-10-13

### Added

- **`alsem graph <workspace> [--out F]`: the program's call graph for diff-scoped
  test selection** (#63; spec
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-callgraph-export-design.md`). JSONL in the
  `{"t","v"}` envelope bc-dev-mcp's `bcdev_test_select` reads, schema
  `al-sem.callgraph` v1 (a `meta` line first). The graph answers "which routines
  may execute when this one does": the engine's resolved edges (`Direct`,
  `Interface`, `Event`, `Trigger`, and `Run` to the run object's node) plus four
  declaration rules — a run reaches the whole object (its triggers, its extensions'
  triggers, a page's parts, source table, the pages its actions open), a
  `Page`/`Report`/`XmlPort`/`Query`/`TestPage` variable may run its object,
  `[HandlerFunctions]` links a test to its handlers, and a test runs its codeunit.
  Open call sites become bounded hub nodes (`name`, `run`, `record`, `callbacks`
  for symbol-only apps, and the universal `any`); channels no edge shows yet are
  flagged on the node (`hiddenCallers`: `unraisedPublisher`, `unboundSubscriber`,
  `unmodeledRecordTrigger`). Nodes carry their location (`sourcePath`,
  `line`..`endLine`) so changed code joins by location, triggers included.
  Dependencies with source are full nodes; the output keeps only what lies on a
  workspace-to-workspace path. Module `program::impact_graph`; fixture
  `tests/fixtures/test-selection-graph/`; tests `cli_graph_export::` and
  `impact_graph::`; golden `tests/cli-query-goldens/graph.test-selection-graph.jsonl`.
  On the bc-dev-mcp acceptance fixture the `Codeunit.Run`-only `ApplyDecay` now
  reaches its test with no coverage map. DO (release-fast): 9-10 s, 2.1 GB peak,
  24 MB, 31,827 nodes / 79,860 edges.
- **`SiteFacts::open`**: what an open call site may reach (`OpenBound`: a
  procedure name and arity, an object kind, a record-trigger family, or anything),
  set by the resolver for unknown routes, `DynamicOpen` sites, record operations on
  an unresolved table and the catalog builtins that run user code
  (`member_catalog::DISPATCHING_BUILTINS`: `Page.Run`, `Report.SaveAsPdf`,
  `RecordRef.Insert`, `Session.StartSession`, ...). Diagnostic: no edge, histogram
  or golden moves.
- **`ObjectDecl::run_objects`** in the IR: every `RunObject` property value outside
  code (page actions and the like).
- **`full::build_cross_app_program`**: the cross-app program build (FULL, dependency
  bodies merged) that `alsem analyze`'s cross-app model and `alsem graph` share. It
  stops before the demand filter, which stays the model's own step.

### Fixed

- **A call never resolves to a trigger.** `resolve_in_object` took every routine of
  the name as a call candidate, triggers included, so in a table with a field
  trigger `OnValidate` and a procedure `OnValidate()` a call to the procedure became
  a two-route edge that also reached the trigger. AL code cannot call a trigger;
  triggers are now left out of call candidates (they stay reachable by role, through
  object runs and record operations). Found while building `alsem graph` (#63), which
  reads a `Call` route to a trigger as a typed-variable run. Pinned by
  `a_call_never_resolves_to_a_same_named_trigger` (it failed before the fix).

## [1.5.0] - 2026-10-13

### Fixed

- **The lowerer reads four new shapes of the `8682cb5f` grammar** (see Changed;
  `crates/al-syntax/src/lower/mod.rs`). Each was an ERROR before, and without an arm its
  content was lost or wrong:
  - `preproc_conditional_property_value_sequence` (`SourceTable = #if X Customer;
    #endif #if not X Vendor; #endif`): one `ObjectProperty` per arm of every group, as a
    single whole-value `#if` already gives. Without it the whole run, directives
    included, was one property value.
  - `preproc_conditional_implements` (`implements IA, #if X IB, #endif IC`) and
    `preproc_conditional_var_names` (`A, #if X B, #endif C: Integer;`, globals and
    locals): every arm's names, the union the lowerer already reads across `#if`-wrapped
    headers and declarations. Without it the names inside the group were dropped.
  - `preproc_conditional_field_list_items` (a key's field list) and
    `preproc_conditional_attribute_args` (`[EventSubscriber(ObjectType::Table, #if X
    Database::"New", #else Database::"Old", #endif 'OnX', …)]`): these lists are
    positional, so they read ONE arm, the first one the build context does not rule out
    (`conditional_list_arm`; a routine's attributes use the routine's own context, so a
    subscriber that exists only under `not X` takes the `#else` arm). A union of the arms
    is no build at all and would move the event name off `args[2]`. An attribute group
    also records a `SyntaxIssue`. Without the arm a key lost the group's fields, and the
    group was one `Unknown` attribute argument.
  Pinned by five `lower::tests` (`property_value_run_…`, `implements_list_group_…`,
  `key_field_list_group_…`, `var_name_list_group_…`, `attribute_args_group_…`); each
  failed when its arm was broken (the attribute test once with the context dropped and
  once with the arm removed) and passed when restored.
- **Corrected a false claim about zero-width member names (issues #56, #41).** The
  `lower/mod.rs` comments said `modify()` and `action()` parse Clean with
  `has_error()` false. They do not: tree-sitter recovery inserts a hidden MISSING
  keyword under the `identifier` alias, so `has_error()` is true and `ParseStatus` is
  `Recovered` (only the `tree-sitter parse` CLI hides it). `action("")` (empty quoted
  name) is the shape that really parses Clean. The empty-name guard stays. A new lib
  test pins both facts. The older #41 entry below is left as written.
- **Doctrine: measure event detectors in cross-app mode (issue #57).** d43/d44/d45
  now have a real population under default `alsem analyze` (pinned CDO baseline,
  `--scope primary`: 22 / 20 / 153; `--scope all`: 979 / 248 / 153), fixed earlier by
  engine-switch S4.2 + S8.3. `--single-app` still gives none. `CLAUDE.md` and
  `/triage-wave` now say so, and `/triage-wave` names the pinned workspace.

- **`mint-goldens --fixture` minted against `$CDO_WS`.** Without a workspace
  argument it fell back to `$CDO_WS` like a CDO mint, so with that variable set it
  read CDO's app id, matched none of the fixture graph's edges and wrote an empty
  fixture golden (0 pairs). Found by the post-S9 "every regeneration path runs"
  check. `--fixture` now always mints from `tests/fixtures/semantic-golden` and
  refuses a workspace argument; re-minted, the golden is byte-identical to the
  committed one. `select_workspace` is pinned by a test (discrimination: letting
  `--fixture` fall through to `$CDO_WS` fails it).
- **Overload selection follows the compiler where it is proven** (engine-switch
  S9.5c). Probed with alc 18.0.41.45789 and the altool graph (~90 calls):
  - **An exact match beats a conversion.** `I(Integer; Text)` and
    `I(Integer; Code[20])` called with `(Integer, Text)` bind the Text overload;
    an enum value binds `EI(Enum)` over `EI(Integer)`. Until now any rival that
    could take the argument by conversion blocked the pick.
  - **Exact includes the length.** A by-value `Text`/`Code` match is exact only
    when the argument fits: unbounded `Text` or `Text[60]` into
    `TL(Text[50] | Code[20])` is AL0196 in the compiler and stays ambiguous;
    `Text[30]` binds `Text[50]`.
  - **A sole applicable overload binds.** When every other candidate is proven
    unable to take the arguments, the one left binds, `Variant` included:
    `V(Variant | Integer)` with an InStream binds `Variant` (this retires
    Round-1 addendum I5, "never pick the Variant survivor"); `InitNew(...;
    Integer; ...)`/`(...; Code[20]; ...)` with a Text binds Code[20], with a
    Decimal binds Integer.
  - **"Incompatible" is now sound.** It claimed six convertible pairs (Option,
    Char, Byte, an enum into Integer; Guid and Text into each other) were
    impossible. The relation is now built from single-overload calls (AL0133 =
    inconvertible), not from `(Variant | T)` preferences, which mislead: a
    Decimal binds `Variant` over `Integer` yet converts to Integer. The numeric-
    like types (Integer, Decimal, BigInteger, Duration, Char, Byte, Option)
    convert into each other; an enum with Integer/BigInteger/Option.
  - Not attempted: ranking two needed conversions (the compiler binds
    `Code[30]` into `TC(Text | Code[20])` to Text). Those calls stay ambiguous,
    never guessed.
  - L3 had resolved `ws-overload-negatives`' `CallVariant`; the switch had lost
    it. CDO: dependency `ambiguousResolved` 679 -> 459; all 220 sites checked
    against the compiler graph (178 at the exact line, 42 repeat calls on an
    overload the compiler binds from that file), 0 wrong. Workspace unchanged
    (0 unknown / 23).

- **An enum value argument binds its enum overload** (engine-switch S9.5c).
  `T.P("Probe Kind"::Open)` over `P(Enum "Probe Kind")`/`P(InStream)` stayed
  an ambiguous overload: the argument was untyped. It now types as its enum,
  as the compiler binds it (alc 18.0.41.45789 and the altool graph:
  `EN(Enum|InStream)` and `EI(Enum|Integer)` both bind the Enum overload).
  Only a bare qualifier that names an enum: an option value (`R.Opt::A`,
  `K::A`, and a local option variable named like the enum, which the
  compiler lets shadow it) binds `Integer`, so it stays untyped. L3 had
  resolved `ws-overload-enum-discriminator`; the switch to the program model
  had lost it. CDO: dependency `ambiguousResolved` 710 -> 679 (20 of the 31
  sites checked against the compiler graph, all on the Enum overload; the
  other 11 repeat a call the graph records once). Workspace unchanged (0
  unknown / 23).

### Added

- **agentflow: a design that converged at the spec-panel cap is handed to the
  next attempt (#45).** Before, a tick that hit the 3-round spec cap ran
  `finish --outcome blocked`. That label, `agent-blocked`, is on the exclusion
  list, so `fetch` dropped the issue and its finished design waited for a
  human (#19, #20 and #34 were all fixed by hand). Now `/issue` returns
  `handoff <sha>` when the register is handoff-ready. Handoff-ready means:
  - both closed vocabularies hold;
  - no entry is `open`;
  - no blocking entry is `deferred`;
  - every mark is `accepted` or `re-raised`;
  - every entry is `accepted` by at least one reviewer.

  An entry both reviewers re-raised blocks the handoff. `finish --outcome
  handoff --handoff-ref <sha>` re-checks that rule against the register at that
  commit on the claimed branch. It then writes `.agent/handoffs.json` and
  labels `agent-design-ready`. That label is deliberately not excluded, so the
  issue stays eligible. The next claim carries the design as `handoff`, and
  that attempt starts at the acceptance tests. Merge safety does not change:
  the carried register, re-raised entries included, still needs both
  reviewers' acceptance at `attest`. Four more rules:
  - an issue edited since the handoff voids it (`handoff_void: issue-edited`);
  - a rolled-back claim does not consume it;
  - a pre-ratified attempt cannot hand off again;
  - any refusal labels nothing, so the tick falls back to `blocked`.

  13 new tests in `scripts/agentflow/tests/test_cli_flow.py`; the suite is 284
  passed (was 271).

- **An inline builder for the program-backed model** (engine-switch S9.2).
  `program_calls::assemble_and_resolve_inline_program(files, app_guid,
  model_instance_id)` (and `_default`) takes `(relative path, source)` pairs,
  writes them with an `app.json` to a temporary directory and builds the model
  exactly as `alsem analyze` does. Unit ids are `ws:<relative path>`, as in the
  L3 inline builder it will replace in tests (S9.5). A test checks that every
  single-app r0-corpus fixture passed inline gives the same model as built from
  disk.

- **A `cdo` cargo profile for correctness loops.** Optimized, but no LTO, 16
  codegen units and incremental builds. `scripts/cdo-gate` now uses it: after a
  one-line edit the gate took 236 s, against ~375 s on `release-fast` (lib-test
  rebuild 46 s against 133 s; measured 2026-10-07, all 2,201 CDO-gated tests
  green). `aldump` on `cdo` rebuilds in ~1 min and reports the same CDO counts.
  Timing and memory numbers still come from `release-fast` or `release`.

- **Dependency-body unknowns are measured and ratcheted** (engine-switch S9.0e).
  `aldump --dependency-bodies-stats --sites` lists every unknown route in dependency
  code resolved from its own app, with its source line. The CDO test
  `dependency_body_unknown_ceiling_on_cdo` holds their count (6,315 of 431,248 edges on
  2026-10-07) and only moves down. `realUnknownRate` never counted these.

- **The AL compiler's call graph as an independent oracle** (engine-switch
  S9.0b). The AL extension ships `altool graph`
  (Microsoft.BusinessCentral.CallGraph). `altool graph extract-whole --corpus
  <workspace> --corpus <dependency sources> --graph g.jsonl` compiles every app
  together and writes the compiler's own call graph. The new
  `aldump --compiler-oracle <g.jsonl> <workspace> [--all-apps]`
  (`program::resolve::compiler_oracle`) compares it with the program resolver's
  edges, caller->callee pair by pair. Pairs are the granularity both share: the
